The authors derive exact bias and variance decompositions revealing multiplicative coupling between policy-weight and advantage errors, motivating a coupled correction method.

entry.title: Which Rollout Taught It That? BehaviorTrace and the Limits of Training-Data Attribution in Online RL

author.name: Amit Nautiyal

entry.summary: BehaviorTrace is an open evaluation harness for training-data attribution in online RL with GRPO, using a planted behavior with known cause plus controls for gradient magnitude, fluency, headroom, and seed variation. Experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B show much of the apparent attribution signal comes from confounds, with a gradient-size-only control reaching 4.2-4.5x chance.

entry.title: HULK: Learning Whole-Body Forceful Loco-Manipulation for Humanoids

author.name: An Dang, Arturo Flores Alvarez, Yu-Ming Chen, Conor Mc Gartoll, Helen Sun, Aaron Ames, Nima Fazeli, Manikantan Nambi

entry.summary: HULK is a whole-body control framework for forceful humanoid loco-manipulation, using MPC-guided reinforcement learning to train separate arm-tracking and locomotion-under-load teachers, augmented with a capture-point control barrier function, and distilling them into a single policy. It addresses balance and tracking under heavy payloads that shift the center of mass.

entry.title: It Is Not Seeing the Hazard: A Frozen Vision-Language Safety Score Measures Its Caption Bank

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: This paper critically evaluates frozen CLIP-based safety scores used in safe RL and driving, presenting controlled experiments showing that image-text similarity to hazard descriptions may reflect prompt structure, embedding geometry, and viewpoint rather than actual hazard detection. The authors show a frozen vision-language safety score largely measures its caption bank rather than the hazard itself. This is an important caution for the increasingly common practice of using VLM similarity as safety signals.

entry.title: Computations of the slice genus and the unknotting number of links via machine learning

author.name: Yutong Dai, Oliver Hayman, Andr\'as Juh\'asz, Ludovico Morellato

entry.summary: This paper uses reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimisation to compute new upper bounds on link invariants in knot theory, including slice genus, unknotting number, and strong slice genus, which are not known to be algorithmically computable. Combined with lower bounds from known invariants, the agents obtain new exact values and reproduce known counterexamples to unknotting number additivity, sometimes finding new unknotting trajectories.

entry.title: RELATE: An Evaluation Framework for measuring Relational Orientation of Large Language Models

author.name: Shivam Shukla, Jihye Kim, Shubham Gaur, Mahnaz Roshanaei, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: RELATE measures relational orientation of LLMs used for emotional support: whether models position themselves as the user's ongoing support source (inward-facing language) or encourage real-world human connection (outward-scaffolding language). Grounded in psychological and sociological literature, the framework formalizes a taxonomy to assess where models orient users for continued support. This addresses concerns that sustained AI emotional-support use may displace real relationships.

entry.title: SpikingVLA: Asynchronous Spiking Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jingya Wang, Dehao Zhang, Shuai Wang, Malu Zhang, Yang Yang, Haizhou Li

entry.summary: SpikingVLA presents an ANN-to-SNN conversion framework for energy-efficient vision-language-action models, introducing a Dendritic Integrate-and-Fire (DIF) neuron that handles channel-wise activation outliers to enable accurate conversion with fewer timesteps. This reduces inference latency for real-time robotic VLA deployment.

entry.title: SPW-Nav: A Streaming Panoramic World Model for Language-Guided Navigation

author.name: Yunheng Liu, Ziqi Cai, Siqi Yang, Yimu Wang, Minggui Teng, Jiaming Tan, Shuchen Weng, Erwin Wu, Kaipeng Zhang, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: SPW-Nav is a streaming panoramic world model that interprets movement instructions as camera motion and generates one minute of 2K 360-degree video in real time from a single panorama. Key techniques include spherical rotation decoupling, pose-aligned conditioning to keep translations bounded, and multi-scale conditioning, with applications in interactive 3D exploration, VR, and embodied agent training.

entry.title: PhyDiCT: Plug-and-Play CT Reconstruction from Sparse X-Rays via Differentiable Rendering and Strong Priors

author.name: Weicheng Dai, Shantanu Ghosh, Kayhan Batmanghelich

entry.summary: Presents PhyDiCT, a training-free framework reconstructing 3D lung CT from sparse X-ray projections by combining a differentiable Beer-Lambert physics forward model with a text-conditioned diffusion prior. Split Gibbs sampling jointly optimizes projection fidelity and prior consistency without fine-tuning the generative model.

entry.title: Visual Evidence Under Cross-Examination: Evaluating and Controlling Decision-Level Evidence Use in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Huiyao Zhang, Jin Bai, Zilong Su, Rui Guo, Chaofan Qin, Jinze Lv, Wenhui Yu, Hongfei Wang, Ye Li

entry.summary: This paper studies whether visual evidence in vision-language models actually benefits the candidate it supports, formalizing candidate-bound visual contribution with matched invalidation and rebinding tests. It introduces CROSS-Bench with 28,000 decision problems and the RIVET interface, which preserves evidence identity and uncertainty and separately controls response strength.

entry.title: DynStream: Online Streaming 4D Gaussian Reconstruction of Dynamic Worlds from Unposed Video

author.name: Dingwei Xian, Xiaoyu Zhou, Yajiao Xiong, Yongtao Wang, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: DynStream performs online 4D Gaussian reconstruction of dynamic scenes from long, unposed streaming videos by reconstructing local temporal windows and incrementally fusing them into a globally consistent scene. It achieves simultaneous continuous processing and photorealistic rendering, which prior offline Gaussian methods and online point-cloud methods could not jointly deliver.

entry.title: RealtimeWAM: How Fast Can I Run My World Action Model?

author.name: Huanan Liu, Ye Li, Kangye Ji, Xiaoyu Chen, Hanyun Cui, Yutian Shen, Yuan Meng, Chenglei Wu, Jingyan Jiang, Bo Li, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: RealtimeWAM is a general, training-free inference acceleration framework for world action models that combines parallel execution with adaptive computation, exploiting layerwise dependencies to overlap work across timesteps. Unlike architecture-specific approaches such as FastWAM or pure caching, it adapts to the changing computational demands of closed-loop control.

entry.title: An overview of frontier AI company monitoring practices in mid 2026

author.name: Francis Rhys Ward

entry.summary: A reference document compiling publicly available evidence on how OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind monitor internally deployed agents, drawing on published safety framework materials and statements. It notes that monitoring is largely asynchronous/offline, cites specific latency targets (e.g., notifications within 30 minutes of concerning activity at OpenAI), and highlights the scarcity of public evidence about DeepMind's actual practices versus its control roadmap proposals.

entry.title: CM-DPO: Constraint-Margin Direct Preference Optimization for LLM Planning

author.name: Rabimba Karanjai, Qun Gu, Hemanth Hegadehalli Madhavarao, Wenhuan Sun, Xiaojiao Yu, Suryabhan Singh Hada, Libin N. George, Uma Kona, Richard Williamson, Linsey Pang, Prakhar Mehrotra

entry.summary: CM-DPO replaces DPO's binary preference signal with a continuous margin from a deterministic symbolic verifier, scaled by constraint-violation severity, and separates hard and soft constraints via a lexicographic objective so hard constraints are never traded off. Preference pairs come from procedurally generated constraint profiles to reduce length and style bias. This addresses concrete flaws of vanilla DPO for constrained planning.

entry.title: Consistent Distribution Matching for Data-Free Diffusion Distillation

author.name: Yuxiang Fu, Qi Yan, Zike Wu, Yongxing Zhang, Purang Abolmaesumi, Lele Wang, Renjie Liao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a simulation-free, data-free distillation method for accelerating diffusion and flow models to one- or few-step generation, unifying sample generation and score estimation in a single student network so only two models are needed. This avoids curated distillation datasets, expensive teacher rollouts, and auxiliary proxy networks required by prior approaches.

entry.title: Are Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning Methods Really Different?

author.name: Yikuan Li, Pinyan Lu, Fanghui Liu

entry.summary: The paper compares six PEFT parameterizations across language and diffusion models, examining task performance, forgetting, and changes in pretrained weight geometry. It finds LoRA-family methods approximately preserve pretrained geometry and that questioning whether explicit spectral preservation (as in OFT) is necessary, plus further analysis of methodological differences.

entry.title: Certified by Abstention: Distribution-Free Guarantees for Chain-of-Thought Verifiers at Small Calibration Budgets

author.name: Arjun Balaji

entry.summary: This paper studies distribution-free selective guarantees for chain-of-thought verifiers at realistic calibration budgets of tens to hundreds of labeled problems, using seven open models, five verifier signals, and 37,000 graded traces. It identifies the key issue of validity by abstention: rarely-firing certificates can be nominally valid yet wrong every time they are used, so failure probability must be bounded relative to firing rate. This provides practical guidance for deploying CoT verifiers with statistical guarantees.

entry.title: Judging in Latent Space: Efficient Generative Reward Modeling via Semantics-Preserving Compression

author.name: Mingqing Yuan (Soochow University), Xiaobo Liang (Soochow University), Junwei Yang (University of Cambridge), Ziwei Chen (Chalmers University of Technology), Zeren Zhang (Peking University), Hejin Wang (Tsinghua University), Yubin Wang (The Hong Kong University of Science, Technology), Juntao Li (Soochow University)

entry.summary: LatentGRM is a latent evaluation framework for reward modeling that compresses rubric-guided evaluation reasoning into compact continuous trajectories, performing pairwise judgments without token-by-token verbalization. A separate interpreter reconstructs evaluation text offline, offering a view of what information is retained.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Agent Skills' Downstream Utility

author.name: Yu Cheng, Dehai Zhao, Zhongxin Liu, Qing Huang, Zhenchang Xing, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: This empirical study measures when reusable Agent Skills actually improve task outcomes, defining utility as pass-rate difference versus a No-Skill baseline across 87 SkillsBench tasks and nine configurations. It examines how skill content, execution configuration, and multi-skill organization affect gains, including marketplace-retrieved skills. This is timely and practical as skill marketplaces for coding agents proliferate.

entry.title: PAIR: Bridging Perception and Action in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Kaixi Feng, Guoheng Sun, Ang li

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces PAIR, a framework for vision-language-action (VLA) models in robotics that explicitly learns a shared perception-action representation rather than relying solely on end-to-end action-prediction losses. It uses a Masked Action Autoencoder to encode expert action chunks into horizon-aligned Action Latent Tokens and a Bridge Module to align visual-language features with action-relevant representations. The work addresses a known weakness in continuous-action VLAs where the transition from scene understanding to action generation remains implicit.

entry.title: Breaking the Space Barrier and its Application to Language Model Inference

author.name: Arip Asadulaev

entry.summary: The paper connects constrained decoding for structured LLM output (schema-conformant JSON, typed tool calls) to complexity theory, observing that automata enforcing formats have few joining paths between states. It resolves an open question about reachability in such graphs, placing the problem in ReachUL, LOGDCFL, C=L and SC2 with only O(log^2 n / log log n) space. This gives new theoretical underpinnings for constrained inference.

entry.title: The AI Evaluation Ecosystem

author.name: Yash Dave, Sang T. Truong, Serena Wang, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: The paper argues that valid benchmark design requires modeling the ecosystem of actors (providers, users, funders, regulators) whose incentives shape benchmark dynamics. It builds a simulation combining rule-based market dynamics with LLM-driven strategic actors over a six-dimensional capability space, and applies it to benchmark holdout design, finding that public benchmarks behave differently from held-out ones. A meta-level contribution to evaluation science.

entry.title: SearchWorld: Spatial Value-Grounded Imagination for UAV Object Search via World Models

author.name: Yatai Ji, Zhengqiu Zhu, Yong Zhao, Yue Hu, Fanglong Yao, Chen Gao, Pengfei Zhu, Quanjun Yin

entry.summary: This paper addresses autonomous UAV object search in urban environments by combining world models with spatially-aware value estimation, enabling prospective reasoning through imagined rollouts rather than reactive reasoning over past observations. It targets the closed perception-decision-action loop under partial observability while avoiding the high inference latency of image-generating world models.

entry.title: The Attribution Blind Spot: Layerwise Trajectory Diagnostics for Source Reliance in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models

author.name: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Yunzhao Wei, Bo Yang, Chen Ye, Gaolei Li, Meng Han

entry.summary: Using controlled knowledge conflicts, this paper studies which internal-state properties of retrieval-augmented models predict source reliance, introducing Latent Trajectory Shift, a signed projection onto a fitted principal component. Findings indicate that state-change magnitude is the stronger predictor while signed PC1 direction is the better controller for interventions that shift source preference without harming other behavior.

entry.title: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?

author.name: Michael Ofengenden, Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: AgentTime is a benchmark testing whether LLM agents can work for a requested duration, predict their runtime, and estimate elapsed time, across 222 tasks from 18 sources including coding, computer use, and automated research. Duration-following experiments span requests from about a minute to multiple days. It reveals that time-awareness and runtime control in native agent harnesses are largely unexplored and presumably weak.

entry.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution

author.name: Python Song, Zhixuan Liang, Kelsey Fu, Mengdi Wang, Junfeng Yang, Shilong Liu

entry.summary: EmbodiedRSI is a self-evolving agentic harness for robots that decides where to explore next and converts physical interactions into improved code and skills. A Fast-Slow Dual-System Architecture evolves competing code and skill hypotheses to use costly robot trials more efficiently than prior self-improvement harnesses.

entry.title: U-Space: Uncovering When and Why Uncertainty Arises in Language Models

author.name: Tobias Braun, Nils Loose, Alexander Herzog, Virginia Ceccatelli, Marcus Rohrbach, Thomas Eisenbarth, Lorenzo Cavallaro

entry.summary: U-Space addresses uncertainty quantification in LLMs by going beyond scalar reliability estimates to reveal where and how uncertainty arises and evolves during reasoning, avoiding the cost of repeated generations or separately trained components. This matters for high-stakes decision-making where knowing when to defer is critical.

entry.title: The Confidence Game: Strategic Miscalibration in Human-AI Delegation

author.name: Raghu Arghal, Saswati Sarkar, Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti

entry.summary: The paper formalizes strategic distortion of AI confidence reports as a repeated signaling game with imperfect monitoring, where an agent of unknown honesty and ability reports confidence and a user decides whether to delegate. Characterizing Markov Perfect Bayesian Equilibria of the two-period game, the authors show honest reporting is not an equilibrium and confidence inflation is the unique equilibrium behavior.

entry.title: Not All Uncertainty Matters: Simulation-in-the-Loop Fast-Slow Reasoning for Decision-Critical Autonomous Driving System

author.name: Jiayi Chen, Shuai Wang, Guangxu Zhu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Chengzhong Xu, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: SIGMA is a simulation-in-the-loop framework for fast-slow collaboration in autonomous driving, deciding when cloud-side VLM reasoning should influence time-critical onboard decisions by assessing whether resolving an uncertainty actually improves planning, rather than using perception-uncertainty or heuristic triggers. This targets the impracticality of continuous high-latency cloud reasoning for real-time driving.

entry.title: WAPR: A Foundation Model for Wide-Angle Refinement in Unseen Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Yulin Wang, Mengting Hu, Hongli Li, Jianghao Zhou, Chen Luo

entry.summary: Presents WAPR, a zero-shot wide-angle pose refinement model handling rotational deviations up to 90 degrees, with fast inference (under 1 s per frame) and throughput up to 25 instances per second. It uses rotational symmetry priors and introduces SA6D, a large-scale 6D training dataset built with KASAL-assisted symmetry annotation.

entry.title: A Deafening Silence: Catastrophic Forgetting Lives in the Output Embeddings of Tokens the Data Never Speaks

author.name: Jonghyun Han, Younghoon Song, Jongyoul Park

entry.summary: This paper localizes catastrophic forgetting in data-free continual pre-training and fine-tuning of LLMs, showing through systematic parameter freezing across five settings up to 1.4B parameters that forgetting concentrates in the output embeddings of tokens rarely seen in the new corpus. It further shows this localization is governed by the corpus vocabulary deficiency, enabling pre-retraining risk ranking from token counts alone. This offers a practical, data-free diagnostic for a core continual learning problem.

entry.title: LLM Persuasion Is in the Eye of the Evaluation

author.name: Kamile Dementaviciute, Julija Vaitonyte, Tijl De Bie

entry.summary: This arXiv paper examines the fragmented state of LLM persuasion evaluation, noting that while LLMs have matched or exceeded human experts in persuasion, assessments vary widely in how they define persuasion and often overgeneralize from narrow, situation-specific tests. The authors propose automated evaluation methods as a way to compare assessments directly, run them at scale across models, and cover high-risk persuasion scenarios that would be impractical or unethical to test on humans. This matters because persuasion is a key dual-use capability relevant to both beneficial applications like education and to manipulation and misinformation risks facing developers and regulators.

entry.title: SemanticFold: Latent Sequence Compression SeparatesLanguage Modeling, Decodability, and Reasoning

author.name: Mingyan Liu, Min Huang

entry.summary: SemanticFold introduces a latent compression scheme that folds prompt prefix hidden states at learned boundaries, and rigorously tests whether compressed prefixes preserve LLM capabilities. Using a fixed-target teacher-forcing protocol across five models (Qwen3, SmolLM2, Pythia families), it separates effects on likelihood, reasoning accuracy, probe accessibility, and generation quality.

entry.title: Composing What Each Teacher Learned: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation through Teacher-Relative Shifts

author.name: Hejian Sang, Zhengze Zhou, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Xiaomin Li, Rohit Jain, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: This paper introduces Delta-MOPD, a method for multi-teacher on-policy distillation that transfers each teacher's logit shift relative to its own base model, re-anchored at the student's frozen initialization, rather than copying each teacher's endpoint policy. The approach is evaluated in both common-domain composition and routed-domain distillation settings, aiming to isolate what post-training actually changed in each teacher. This matters because it provides a cleaner signal for knowledge transfer in multi-teacher pipelines used to train smaller student models.

entry.title: Tucker Bottleneck Attention for Multi-Dimensional Sequence Modeling

author.name: Ryan Solgi, Parsa Madinei, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: TuBA exploits low-rank tensor structure by projecting hidden tensors into compact Tucker cores, performing attention on the cores for subquadratic global token mixing, with an autoregressive extension mixing causally across cores. It shows favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs on video prediction and global weather forecasting.

entry.title: Noise, Denoise, Correct: MCMC Posterior Sampling with Diffusion Priors in Three Steps

author.name: So Takao, Gregory David Bellchambers, Luke Ye, Sanmitra Ghosh, Michalis Michaelides

entry.summary: Diffusion waltz is an MCMC method that uses SDEdit-style noising-denoising as a Metropolis-Hastings proposal for posterior sampling with pretrained diffusion priors, avoiding prior density evaluation and handling non-differentiable forward models. An ensemble Kalman update injects observations while preserving exactness, with strong results on Navier-Stokes initial condition recovery.

entry.title: Homogenization in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Prakhar Ganesh, Kyra Wilson, Luca Zappella, Barry-John Theobald, Nicholas Apostoloff, Lucas Monteiro Paes, Nivedha Sivakumar

entry.summary: The paper identifies homogenization in multi-agent LLM systems, where agent interactions cause convergence to similar behaviors, operationalized via conformity, polarization, and inertia metrics. It demonstrates concrete downstream risks in code generation, hiring, and scientific peer review, including hidden correlated errors.

entry.title: Efficient Provably Private Classification with a Tabular Foundation Model

author.name: Talal Alrawajfeh, Cristiana Diaconu, Ossi R\"ais\"a, Sebastian Rodriguez Beltran, Yuan He, John Bronskill, Richard E. Turner, Antti Honkela

entry.summary: PrivTab is a tabular foundation model for differentially private classification that avoids the slow dataset-specific optimization and utility loss of traditional private learning, while existing foundation models lack formal privacy guarantees and are vulnerable to membership inference. The authors include Cambridge and Finnish collaborators with credible privacy researchers.

entry.title: How Do Transformers Learn to Represent Symmetries?

author.name: Eduardo Santos-Escriche, Valerie Engelmayer, Ya-Wei Eileen Lin, Stefanie Jegelka

entry.summary: The authors study how vanilla Transformers learn symmetries (translation, rotation, scale, angle-preserving groups) from finite data augmentation on point clouds. They establish an ordering of learnability across symmetry groups and analyze the interplay between architecture, invariance, and augmentation budgets.

entry.title: Why Forget-Only Unlearning Needs Memorization

author.name: Luka Radi\'c, Vikrant Singhal, Amartya Sanyal

entry.summary: The paper studies forget-only machine unlearning, where the algorithm receives only the trained model and examples to forget, and shows feasibility depends on the learning method: identical trained models can require different post-deletion outputs. The authors derive lower bounds on how accurately unlearning can match retraining and identify what auxiliary information is needed.

entry.title: Beyond Explanation: Debugging Medical Imaging Models via Concept Intervention

author.name: Samrajya Thapa, Daniel J. Quest, Timothy L. Kline, Carrie L. Langstraat, Emanuel C. Trabuco, Wei Le

entry.summary: This work presents a plug-and-play framework that aligns a single-modality encoder to BioMedCLIP to build a Concept Bottleneck Model enabling concept-level interventions for medical imaging. Interventions let practitioners isolate causal versus spurious concepts, validate insights with domain experts, and generate counterfactual samples for targeted fine-tuning, evaluated on Mayo Clinic ultrasound and CheXpert data.

entry.title: Quantize by Drift: Label-Free Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Text Embedders

author.name: Hyojung Han, Jongmin Kim, Seung-Hun Jeon

entry.summary: This paper proposes using quantization-induced representation drift -- how far output embeddings move when a module is quantized -- as a label-free sensitivity signal for mixed-precision post-training quantization of text embedders. Across five embedders, configuration-level drift predicts held-out retrieval quality with a macro Spearman of 0.911, removing the need for relevance labels in deployment settings. This matters for efficient deployment of embedding models without labeled evaluation data.

entry.title: Tracing Inputs, Verifying Outputs: Validating Attribution in Music Generation

author.name: Taejun Kim, Wonil Kim, Jongmin Jung, Hyeongseok Wi, Sangeun Kum, Keunhyoung Luke Kim, Taehyoung Kim, Dongjoo Moon, Seungsoon Park, Taewan Kim, Virginie Berger, Juhan Nam, Jongpil Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces MixAudio, a music generation system conditioned solely on audio inputs, and a pipeline for verifiable attribution showing which input audio sources shaped each output. It also audits training-data memorization using a musical version identification model called musicDNA, finding few reproductions of unprovided training material. This matters because it offers a technical framework for provenance and copyright accountability in generative audio.

entry.title: Gaussian Equivalence for Multi-Head Self-Attention

author.name: Tomohiro Hayase, Ryo Karakida

entry.summary: This theory paper uses random matrix theory to prove a Gaussian equivalence result for multi-head self-attention: softmax attention can be replaced by rescaled scores plus Gaussian noise while preserving the limiting spectral law of the centered output. The framework also handles key-dependent value and output projections and separates the effects of head allocation, projection widths, and key-value dependence structure.

entry.title: Rubix: Global Correspondence-Free Point Set Alignment through Assignment Geometry

author.name: Subhransu S. Bhattacharjee, Dylan Campbell, Rahul Shome

entry.summary: Rubix solves the equally weighted planar Procrustes-Wasserstein alignment problem globally, avoiding suboptimal local minima of alternating minimization. It characterizes the permutation polygon of complex correlations, proving a sharp bound of n(n-1) vertices and thereby answering an open problem by Rote on rotation-assignment. Exact arithmetic recovers the polygon in O(n^5) operations.

entry.title: InsClaimBench: Benchmarking Insurance Claim Adjudication Across the Decision Chain

author.name: Linqi Zhang, Chong Qi, Yan Cheng, Wanqing Cao, Yu Liu, Chenwei Lin, Xian Xu

entry.summary: InsClaimBench is an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating reasoning LLMs on insurance claim adjudication, spanning 3,780 real-world cases across auto, property, and health insurance with 86,656 atomic rule judgments. It evaluates models across the full decision chain from atomic rule application through intermediate judgments to payout calculations.

entry.title: Large-scale Repository Engineering via Agent-Native Reusable Code Primitives

author.name: Haibo Jin, Peng Kuang, Xucheng Yu, Jerry Wang, Dehao Wu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Code Primitives, agent-native reusable executable components with interface contracts, dependency closures, validation tests, and provenance, organized into CodeFace, a searchable library of 1,424 validated primitives. The LEGO framework uses a resident LLM to assess relevance and adapt primitives for repository-scale code construction.

entry.title: Mitigating Accent-Language Confusion in Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Language Identification

author.name: Minu Kim, Jihwan Lee, David R. Mortensen, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: The authors show that language identification models built on self-supervised speech representations systematically misclassify non-native accented speech as the speaker's first language because non-native representations lie geometrically between native language poles. They propose a simple geometric projection that estimates and removes the L1-bias direction using only native speech, improving L2 speech identification across five MMS-LID models.

entry.title: VIS-Ground: Video Interactive Storytelling with Contextual Grounding

author.name: Bingxuan Li, Yiwen Song, Xueqing Wu, Yanzhou Pan, Yang Li, Kuang Su, Jingyun Liu, Sebastian Ko, Huan Zhang, Tong Zhang, Nanyun Peng, Tomas Pfister, Yale Song

entry.summary: Explores video interactive storytelling where viewers steer generation mid-video, addressing how to resolve viewer requests whose dependencies span an external grounding source, the rendered video history, and new intent. The paper formalizes what context must be assembled jointly, going beyond instruction-following or source-grounded generation alone.

entry.title: One Frame, Full Heartbeat: ECG-Free Cardiac Cine MRI Synthesis via Phase-Conditioned Flow Matching

author.name: Shiyi Wang, Ruochen Sun, Peirong Liu, Xiang Li, Fangxu Xing

entry.summary: Presents PhaseFlow, a flow-matching generative framework synthesizing full cardiac cine MRI sequences from a single frame without ECG gating, using phase conditioning to reproduce clinically relevant dynamics like ejection fraction. It targets uncooperative patients, resource-limited settings, and temporally corrupted datasets.

entry.title: Identity-Duplication Auditing in National-Scale Neuroimaging Repositories

author.name: Jiheng Li (HABS-HD), Michael E. Kim (HABS-HD), Trent M. Schwartz (HABS-HD), Yuhan Cui (HABS-HD), Gaurav Rudravaram (HABS-HD), Derek B. Archer (HABS-HD), Timothy J. Hohman (HABS-HD), Lori L. Beason-Held (HABS-HD), Victoria L. Morgan (HABS-HD), Dario J. Englot (HABS-HD), Angela L. Jefferson (HABS-HD), for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (HABS-HD), for the BIOCARD Study team (HABS-HD), for the Health (HABS-HD), Aging Brain Study (HABS-HD), : (HABS-HD), Health Disparities (HABS-HD), Study Team, Lianrui Zuo, Guray Erus, Christos Davatzikos, Bennett A. Landman

entry.summary: This paper addresses identity duplication in aggregated national-scale MRI repositories, where the same subject can receive multiple identifiers across studies, creating train-test leakage that inflates reported performance. It presents HAPPEN, a human-in-the-loop image-based pipeline for auditing duplication in T1-weighted MRI at repository scale.

entry.title: MeshCarve: Artisan Mesh Generation with Flow Matching in Compact Latent Spaces

author.name: Xiyu Wang, Ruocheng Wu, Yufei Wang, Zhihao Li, Lanqing Guo, Bihan Wen

entry.summary: MeshCarve generates artist-grade 3D meshes via flow matching entirely in compact latent spaces, separately generating vertex positions and edge connections to avoid joint compact encoding of geometry and topology. It uses a hierarchical sparse transformer with VertexVAE and EdgeVAE to shorten token sequences, addressing the slow autoregressive inference of prior mesh generators.

entry.title: Purifying Backdoored Large Vision-Language Models by Removing Hijacked Directions

author.name: Bojun Yang, Haochen Zhou, Zhifang Zhang, Haobo Wang, Songze Li, Lei Feng

entry.summary: OrthoPurify is a one-step orthogonal projection method that purifies backdoored vision-language model weights without costly retraining or per-query inference intervention. The authors identify a direction hijacking phenomenon in which a small number of weight update directions are diverted from task adaptation to backdoor shortcuts. This provides an efficient post-hoc defense against backdoor attacks in deployed LVLMs.

entry.title: YUBI-STAG: Contact and Semantic-Rich Alignment for VLAs via Automated Video-Language Grounding

author.name: Masatoshi Tateno, Takehiko Ohkawa, Yueh-Hua Wu, Hanlong Li, Tatsuya Matsushima, Yoichi Sato, Kei Ota

entry.summary: YUBI-STAG automatically enriches robot manipulation demonstrations with fine-grained interaction semantics (which gripper contacts which object, how it is grasped and moved) by combining contact-object segmentation with vision-language models. This alignment between instructions and physical interactions helps elicit latent capabilities of pretrained vision-language-action models.

entry.title: CAP: Codebook-Aligned Prediction for Tokenized Robot Policies

author.name: Haoran Chen, Jingtian Ji, Samuel Wheeler, Kaylene Caswell Stocking, Matthew Walter

entry.summary: CAP reuses the action tokenizer's learned codebook vectors as class prototypes in the policy head, preserving latent structure that standard token-classification discards. Evaluated across four quantizer families, three simulation benchmarks, and two real-robot tasks, it consistently improves task success with minimal architectural change.

entry.title: Point It, Strike It: Direction-Conditioned Dynamic Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects

author.name: Yi Yang, Xiang Fei, Lehong Wang, Zilin Dai, Ruogu Li, Jiting Cai, Liyao Chang, Xinyi Yang, Henry Kou, Ruijie Fu, Lu Li, Howie Choset

entry.summary: This paper studies single-swing rope striking where goals specify both the 3D position and arrival direction of a rope tip, a harder problem than position-only goals for deformable linear objects. The authors extend the DeformX simulator with GPU acceleration, a stable Cosserat rod solver, and aerodynamic modeling to enable sim-to-real transfer without demonstrations.

entry.title: Benchmarking Behavioral Steerability in Behavior Foundation Models

author.name: Minghe Gao, Zhanxi Yan, Jiahui Liu, Wendong Bu, Xiaoting Chen, Qizhou Wang, Yi Su, Siliang Tang, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Tat-Seng Chua, Juncheng Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces behavioral steerability as the ability of behavior foundation models to faithfully generate behaviors matching user-specified intentions, and presents RoboSteer, the first benchmark for this capability. It organizes steerability into a three-level hierarchy of conditional, constraint, and compositional steering for humanoid behavior models.

entry.title: RFPO: Rectified Flow Policy Optimization for Embodied Control

author.name: Ting Huang, Lisiyu Pan, Haoyu Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Siyuan Qian, Yanjun Li, Yandong Guo, Boxin Shi, Hao Tang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a few-step discretization gap in flow-based robot control policies: reducing the ODE integration budget at inference severely degrades control because policies are trained under full-step execution. RFPO uses reward-aware online Reflow plus a frozen Gaussian PPO controller to make flow policies robust to coarse integration, cutting inference cost while preserving control quality.

entry.title: Enabling Dynamic Computation in Looped LMs

author.name: Aayush Mishra, Arnau Padr\'es Masdemont, Victor Conchello Vendrell, Jordi Ros Giralt, Arash Behboodi, Fabio Valerio Massoli

entry.summary: The paper shows that state-of-the-art looped LMs (Ouro) fail to realize their promised dynamic computation because per-depth KV caching forces full-depth execution and static early-exit priors treat all tokens equally. It proposes a best-available KV caching strategy that works out of the box, cutting FLOPs and KV memory by up to 30 percent while retaining full performance. A clean efficiency win for a promising architecture class.

entry.title: Frozen Models, Evolving Expertise: Model-Agnostic Learning from Deployment Experience for Multimodal Medical AI

author.name: Yexiao He, Yucheng Tang, Pengfei Guo, Yufan He, Andriy Myronenko, Can Zhao, Ang Li, Daguang Xu, Dong Yang

entry.summary: The paper presents a model-agnostic framework enabling frozen LLMs and VLMs to learn from deployment experience in medicine via three external expertise stores: a skill library, domain knowledge, and visual experience that preserves image details rather than compressing to text. This avoids weight access and retraining while mitigating overfitting to fixed validation sets. It addresses the real problem that clinical guidelines evolve faster than deployed models.

entry.title: KVFetch: Temporal Prefetching for the Missing Half of KV Cache Compression

author.name: Linfeng Dong

entry.summary: Argues that existing KV cache compression families (eviction, summary compensation, offload-recall) all optimize associative content lookup while ignoring sequential positional access, which matters for verbatim reproduction of identifiers, code tokens, and field values. KVFetch adds temporal prefetching to cover the sequential-access half of the cache.

entry.title: Careful Judge: Safe and Efficient Human-AI Collaborative Decision Making

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Rachel Luo, Boyi Li, Anjali Parashar, Marco Pavone, Apoorva Sharma

entry.summary: CARE (calibrated adaptive rectification and escalation) is an end-to-end pipeline combining AI models and human reviewers to guarantee safe, human-aligned decisions while continuously learning from selectively queried human feedback to increase automation. It addresses the tension between learning from human interventions and maintaining safety guardrails calibrated for older models. The framework is presented as principled, general, and modular.

entry.title: An Informational Curse of Horizon in Goal-Conditioned Policy Learning

author.name: John L. Zhou, Yuxuan Dong, Jonathan C. Kao

entry.summary: Beyond the familiar curse of horizon from TD bias accumulation, this paper identifies an informational curse: increasing the goal relabeling horizon during training can significantly degrade goal-conditioned policy generalization. Controlled experiments with oracle planners show policies suffer severe training-horizon-dependent performance loss even when evaluated only on nearby subgoals.

entry.title: Safe on Average, Unsafe in the Tail: When Is the Episodic-Cost Tail Controllable?

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: This safe RL paper shows that policies satisfying the standard expected episodic-cost criterion can remain unsafe in their worst episodes, and measures the tail using CVaR at the 10% level. The authors classify policies as tail-safe and characterize when the episodic-cost tail can be brought within budget while preserving return.

entry.title: From Pareto to Preference: Personalized Test-Time Scaling via Amortized Agentic Policy Discovery

author.name: Xinglin Wang, Zishen Liu, Tong Zheng, Shaoxiong Feng, Peiwen Yuan, Yiwei Li, Jiayi Shi, Yueqi Zhang, Chuyi Tan, Ji Zhang, Boyuan Pan, Kan Li

entry.summary: Reframes test-time scaling as discovering executable controllers that jointly satisfy user-specific accuracy, latency, and cost requirements, rather than optimizing one Pareto dimension at a time. The proposed approach amortizes policy discovery across user profiles to avoid repeated discovery overhead for new requirements.

entry.title: QuSema: Detecting Silent Bugs in Quantum Libraries via Quantum-knowledge-enhanced Agents

author.name: Yujin Song, Kaining Zhang, Qixin Zhang, Shuai Wang, Pingchuan Ma, Yuxuan Du

entry.summary: QuSema is an autonomous LLM-based testing agent that finds silent bugs in quantum computing libraries by leveraging quantum semantics and documentation constraints, going beyond failure- or comparison-based oracles. Silent bugs are especially dangerous because they propagate incorrect results into research conclusions. This combines agentic AI with domain knowledge for scientific software correctness.

entry.title: PatchBench: Measuring Collateral Damage in Activation Patching

author.name: Alexi Canesse, Mathis Le Bail, Ma\"el Jenny, Cl\'ement Elliker, Mahammed El Sharkawy, Sonia Vanier

entry.summary: PatchBench is a benchmark of model-specific jailbreak failures for evaluating whether activation patching safety repairs selectively fix unsafe behavior or cause collateral damage, such as over-refusing benign prompts with similar wording or failing on close harmful variants. It addresses the gap where aggregate metrics cannot distinguish selective repairs from broader suppression.

entry.title: Continual Learning without Continual Training

author.name: Nikita Narayanan, Ritham Majumdarr, Sonali Parbhoo

entry.summary: The authors propose replacing continual training with continual inference via Latent Concept PFN, a meta-trained prior-fitted network that is frozen and adapts to new classes only by extending an in-context evidence set. It performs in-context Bayesian inference over a latent concept space shared across domains and classes.

entry.title: Same Text, Different Prediction: Serving-Context Nondeterminism in Text Classifiers

author.name: Santhosh Kumar Kasa, Siva Rajesh Kasa, Sumit Negi

entry.summary: This systematic study shows that serving-context factors like batch size, batch composition, hardware, and inference engine change text classification predictions even with fixed prompts, parameters, and sampling randomness. It extends prior findings on nondeterminism in text generation to classifiers and quantifies the effect.

entry.title: Neural Sampling with Reweighted Normalizing Flows via the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao JKO Scheme

author.name: Chenguang Duan, Johannes Hertrich, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: The authors propose a neural sampler for unnormalized Boltzmann densities based on the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme in Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao geometry, parametrizing transport and reaction components with reweighted normalizing flows. They prove exponential convergence of exact WFR JKO iterates for any fixed step size without structural assumptions like log-concavity or log-Sobolev inequalities, a notable theoretical guarantee.

entry.title: Right Number, Wrong State? Measuring Cross-Jurisdiction Substitution in LLM Recall of State Policy

author.name: Jiayu Feng

entry.summary: This paper measures cross-jurisdiction substitution in LLM factual recall using a minimal-set design where only the U.S. state varies in questions about three Medicaid income-eligibility quantities across 51 jurisdictions. Under a pre-registered protocol, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol reproducibly return another state's value for 10 and 25 of 153 items, and attribution of wrong answers proves fragile. Gold values are verified against official and independent sources.

entry.title: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory

author.name: Hongru Cai, Ran Wei, Wenjie Wang, Chengfa Wu, Ning Song, Yongqi Li, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: EngramEdit targets knowledge editing in conditional-memory architectures like DeepSeek Engram, enabling factual updates by editing n-gram-keyed embeddings while keeping the Transformer backbone fixed. It addresses the challenge that different expressions of a fact activate different embeddings and that shared-embedding updates can cause unintended side effects.

entry.title: StableGrasp: Reconstructing Physically Stable Human Hand Grasps from Single Images

author.name: Han Jiang, Etienne Vouga, Qixing Huang, Georgios Pavlakos

entry.summary: StableGrasp reconstructs physically stable human grasps from a single RGB image using differentiable simulation-based optimization that explicitly separates visual hand pose estimation from the control target determining grasping forces. It jointly optimizes hand geometry and control by minimizing kinetic energy under physics constraints.

entry.title: UltraWorld: Learning Interactive Ultrasound World Models from Untracked Clinical Videos with Acoustic Sampling Map

author.name: Keke Yang, Erqi Wang, Sainan Guan, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: UltraWorld is a self-distillation recipe that transfers priors from untracked, unlabeled clinical ultrasound videos into interactive world models without real action annotations. It adapts a video foundation model into an ultrasound generator conditioned on reference images and anatomical masks, with an acoustic sampling map modeling ultrasound's cross-sectional geometry to support autonomous probe-motion prediction.

entry.title: HeiCo-FOCUS: A Clinically Grounded Dataset for Long-Context Video Understanding

author.name: Leon Mayer, Lucas Luttner, Patrick Godau, Kai Fritzsche, Annika Reinke, Leonie Boland, Jule Brandt, Janne Heinecke, Chloe K. Nobuhara, Niklas Holzwarth, Evangelia Christodoulou, Marcel Knopp, Dominik Michael, Pascale Piermarco, Saliq Neyaz, Korhan Derin \"Ozarslan, Jakob Hennighausen, Carlos Aumente-Maestro, Tim R\"adsch, Dheeraj Baji, Peter Maximilian Full, Finn Aichholz, Justus Veit Erpenbeck, Linus Finn Schott, Bastian Winkelhausen, Claas de Boer, Bianca G\"uttner, Anneli Hummel, Gregor Just, Max Kirchner, Chenyang Li, Rozenn Raffaut, Ariel Rodriguez, Danush Kumar Venkatesh, Kevin Wang, Jinjing Xu, Mona Sheikh Zeinoddin, Salman Khan, Thomas M. Pausch, Stefanie Speidel, Danail Stoyanov, Daniel A. Hashimoto, Fiona R. Kolbinger, Thomas G. Weiser, Lena Maier-Hein

entry.summary: HeiCo-FOCUS introduces a clinically grounded benchmark for long-context video understanding based on Heidelberg colorectal surgeries, requiring models to continuously track foreign objects inserted, manipulated, occluded, and removed over procedures lasting up to hours. It targets the neglected capability of cumulative temporal consistency, beyond the short-horizon reasoning of existing VLM evaluations. The large multi-institutional author list suggests a serious clinical collaboration.

entry.title: FlashNeRD: Performance-First Contact-Rich Neural Robot Dynamics

author.name: Mohammadmehdi Ataei, Mohammad Amin Nabian, Jie Xu, Miles Macklin, Yashraj Narang, Eric Heiden, Octi Zhang, Yunrong Guo, Ruben D'Sa, Oliver Hennigh, Gavriel State, Sanjay Choudhry

entry.summary: FlashNeRD improves on Neural Robot Dynamics (NeRD) with a parallel streaming architecture for faster and more accurate predictions, arbitrary contact locations rather than predefined points, and two-way coupling with analytically simulated objects. It retains NeRD's design of analytical collision detection plus learned dynamics, making learned robot simulation practical for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: TMT: Runtime Backdoor Detection for Vision-Language-Action Policies on Unseen Tasks

author.name: Zirun Zhou, Jingfeng Zhang, HaoChuan Xu, Xizhe Zhang, Elliott Wen, Jing Sun, Hong Jia

entry.summary: TMT is a runtime detector for backdoored VLA policies, using two branches that assess token-manifold structure and adjacent-layer latent transition errors to flag suspicious rollouts even on tasks unseen during training. This addresses robot-specific AI security threats where triggers cause malicious actions that look individually plausible.

entry.title: Sequential Probabilistic Uncertainty Estimation for Parallel Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems

author.name: Tunyu Zhang, Zihao Zhao, Yusong Zhao, Haizhou Shi, Zhuohang Li, Haoxian Chen, Hao Wang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: SAUCE is a lightweight, training-free method that estimates uncertainty in parallel multi-agent LLM reasoning by modeling the process as sequential inference over a latent system state that evolves with consensus across rounds. This addresses an underexplored reliability question for multi-agent systems. Uncertainty quantification for agent swarms is increasingly important for deployment.

entry.title: Constraint Tree Exploration for Learning from Language Feedback

author.name: Shaoang Li, Daniel R. Jiang, Jian Li

entry.summary: TRACE models user intent as latent constraints and treats learning from natural-language feedback as pure exploration over feasible regions. The algorithm organizes candidate constraints in a tree, tests proposed refinements with generated actions, and only commits when feedback is consistent, explicitly separating falsification from stronger uses of feedback. It addresses a real failure mode where agents over-generalize from a single failed action.

entry.title: FreeEvolve: Learning to Evolve Beyond Fixed Loops

author.name: Lecheng Kong, Like Hui, Nikos Kanakaris, Prithwish Jana, Sahika Genc, Narayanan Sadagopan

entry.summary: FreeEvolve automates not just agent design but the evolution process itself: instead of a hand-designed search loop, an evolver with an editable evolution skill decides what to test, how much evidence to gather, which candidates to keep, and when to stop. The skill is improved via meta-evolution scored on fresh agents it produces. This pushes automated agent design toward self-improving optimization procedures.

entry.title: TopoGraphRAG-Bench: Evaluating Multimodal GraphRAG on Layout-Grounded Evidence Reasoning

author.name: Ruochi Li, Jianzhe Lin, Haoxuan Zhang, Haihua Chen, Junhua Ding, Edward Gehringer, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: This work introduces a benchmark of 2,024 questions over 201 long, visually rich documents to evaluate whether multimodal GraphRAG systems can recover the evidence topology connecting text, tables, figures, and captions in complex page layouts. Existing evaluations are either text-centered or focus on retrieval and generation without testing recovery of the intended evidence structure.

entry.title: Reliability of LLM Judges for Evaluating Entity Alignment

author.name: Vaibhava Lakshmi Ravideshik, Mayank Kejriwal

entry.summary: This is the first systematic benchmarking of LLM-as-judge reliability for entity alignment, covering three frontier models, three datasets, and four EA systems with perturbation bias diagnostics and counterfactual label-flip tests. The authors identify anchor bias, a failure mode where judges invert assessments, highlighting risks in using LLM judges for structured prediction evaluation.

entry.title: Think Before You Paint: Recursive Latent Reasoning for Diffusion Models

author.name: Pawe{\l} Skier\'s, Ma{\l}gorzata Grzanka, Wojciech Masarczyk, Jan-Willem van de Meent, Kamil Deja

entry.summary: PaTh (Painter-Thinker) brings recursive latent reasoning to image diffusion: a small recursive Thinker network refines a latent state within each denoising step over learned tokens, steering a frozen diffusion Painter via ControlNet adapters. This enables pixel-level visual reasoning tasks like drawing maze paths or filling Sudoku grids without symbolic representations. It bridges puzzle-solving recursive models (TRM) with image generation.

entry.title: RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs

author.name: Jinheon Baek, Soyeong Jeong, Yumin Choi, Dongsu Han, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: RunningTab is a framework for LLM agents doing direct workspace interaction (searching and reading files from a terminal without indexing). It maintains environment-side state tracking of task requirements, files read, and items listed but never opened, preventing deliverables from silently missing required content that slips out of the context window.

entry.title: Multi-Aspect Runtime Verification for Simulation-Based V&V of LLM-Enabled Autonomous Agents

author.name: Nikolaos Kekatos, Dimitrios Nikou, Anastasios Temperekidis, Alexios Lekidis, Nikolaos Kolokotronis, Panagiotis Katsaros, Stylianos Basagiannis

entry.summary: This paper presents a runtime-verification framework for LLM agents in defense decision-support, where models arrive as procured components and retraining is unavailable. It decomposes natural-language policy clauses into typed spatial, temporal, and semantic obligations over a canonical event representation, enabling detection of sequential tool-attack chains that per-event guardrails miss. The framework supports simulation-based verification and validation of agent behavior at the interface level.

entry.title: GraphOPD: Graph-Augmented On-Policy Distillation for LLM Agents

author.name: Bohan Lin, Liyi Chen, Zhuoning Guo, Muyang Li, Qimeng Wang, Yan Gao, Yao Hu, Yudong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a failure mode in on-policy distillation for multi-turn LLM agents: step-level teacher guidance allocated by per-step teacher-student divergence misfires when decisions chain across turns, since early drift contaminates later context. GraphOPD augments distillation with graph structure to propagate credit and guidance appropriately across chained decisions. This improves post-training of agents where RL rewards are sparse.

entry.title: Spatial Induction Heads: In-Context Learning of Multidimensional Cellular Automata

author.name: Kimia Kazemian, Menghan Xu, John Thickstun, Sarah Dean

entry.summary: The paper extends mechanistic accounts of in-context learning beyond sequential data, studying how transformers handle the routing problem created when multidimensional cellular automata are serialized into flat sequences. It introduces spatial induction heads, two-layer gather-and-match circuits that reconstruct spatial neighborhoods, providing a circuit-level explanation of in-context rule learning in multidimensional data.

entry.title: Efficient Best-of-N policy evaluation for inference-time alignment

author.name: Jonas Schweisthal, Yuxin Wang, Athiya Deviyani, Stefan Feuerriegel, Dennis Frauen

entry.summary: The paper develops a sample-only framework for evaluating and selecting Best-of-N alignment policies from logged data without access to response likelihoods, exploiting the order-statistic structure of BoN to express density ratios via score-rank probabilities. It derives a doubly robust estimator (BoN-DR) that efficiently reuses a shared auxiliary model.

entry.title: Visual Jev Rewards: Reference-Bound Verification for Multi-Subject Image Generation

author.name: Baoteng Li, Wenzhuo Wu, Kongming Liang, Zhanyu Ma

entry.summary: The paper proposes reference-bound Visual Jev rewards for multi-subject image generation, where positive labels are given only when both the requested condition and the correct reference identities jointly hold. A Qwen3.5-4B verifier is trained with binary supervision, and its Yes probabilities serve as GRPO rewards for training generators that correctly bind attributes and interactions to specific subjects.

entry.title: OmniCam: Omni-Camera Trajectory Generation via Geometry-Grounded Pose Token Learning

author.name: Zhenyang Liu, Chenjie Cao, Yisu Zhang, Xuhui Zuo, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu, Tengfei Wang, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: OmniCam is an autoregressive model that generates camera pose sequences from a single panorama and textual trajectory descriptions, using panoramic point-cloud encoding, hybrid rotation-translation tokenization, and separate geometric and semantic conditioning with a 3D target anchor. The authors also release OmniCaT, a dataset of 267,700 trajectories for training and evaluation.

entry.title: CircuitATLAS: Agentic reasoning over a systems neuroscience knowledge graph for target discovery in circuitopathies

author.name: Gabriel Ocana-Santero, Marko Tvrdic

entry.summary: Presents CircuitATLAS, a provenance-grounded systems-neuroscience knowledge graph plus agentic framework for discovering drug targets that restore pathological neural circuits, deliberately excluding direct disease-gene edges to reduce shortcut reasoning. It reframes target discovery around unaltered molecular control points rather than disease-altered molecules.

entry.title: RollVerify: Bridging Efficiency and Accuracy in Long-Tail Rollout Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yongqiang Yao, Jinru Tan, Kaihuan Liang, Zixin Yin, Yazhe Niu, Ruihao Gong, Dahua Lin, Ningyi Xu

entry.summary: RollVerify addresses GPU underutilization from long-tail rollouts in on-policy RL for LLM reasoning, where asynchronous or partial-rollout methods introduce stale off-policy samples. Instead of passively reweighting off-policy trajectories, it actively verifies them to close the accuracy gap with fully on-policy training. The work targets a core scalability bottleneck of RLHF/RLVR training for large models.

entry.title: TestGRAD: Evolving Test Suites via Failure Pattern Momentum for SWE-Agent Ensemble

author.name: Pengfei He, Jiayuan Zhou, Shaowei Wang, Ruiqi Pan

entry.summary: TestGRAD formulates test-based patch selection for SWE-agent ensembles as test-space optimization, evolving a repository test suite until it can distinguish competing candidate patches. Inspired by gradient descent with momentum, it uses failure-pattern feedback across iterations rather than one-off test generation. This targets a key bottleneck in combining patches from multiple coding agents.

entry.title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds

author.name: Yunxiao Zhao, Changxiao Cai

entry.summary: The paper develops a theoretical framework for training parallel and semi-autoregressive speculative decoding drafters by directly minimizing expected decoding rounds, capturing the cross-round coupling that block-local surrogate objectives ignore. Because where a decoding round starts depends on how many tokens earlier rounds accepted, the proposed objective targets global decoding efficiency rather than local block quality.

entry.title: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents

author.name: Ali Asaria, Deep Gandhi, Tony Salomone

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that large populations of autonomous research agents sharing a compute pool will spontaneously acquire an organization whether designers intend it or not, so designers should provide explicit institutions. The authors propose a society of researchers built on six principles, including principal investigators competing for compute through RFPs, independent review, grants, and a human governor role that allocates resources. It applies institutional-design ideas from multi-agent systems research to the emerging scale of agentic AI deployments.

entry.title: Are We Really Benchmarking Forecasting Models? The Impact of Preprocessing on Time Series Performance

author.name: Guilherme Afonso Galindo Padilha, Paulo Salgado Gomes de Mattos Neto, Rafael Menelau Oliveira e Cruz

entry.summary: This benchmark study shows preprocessing is a major, overlooked driver of time series forecasting performance, evaluating 11 models across 16 reversible preprocessing pipelines on 29,000 M4 series. It argues that structural preprocessing bias in standard benchmarks favors models with built-in data treatments and obscures the potential of simpler architectures.

entry.title: Q-PACE: Dynamic Precision Allocation for Quantization-Aware Training

author.name: Alexandra Volkova, Matin Ansaripour, Erik Schultheis, Christoph H. Lampert, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Q-PACE assigns per-layer precision during quantization-aware training using a second-order sensitivity model that predicts loss increase as quantization noise MSE weighted by per-layer curvature, recomputed periodically during training. This dynamic reallocation maintains performance under aggressive quantization for LLM deployment.

entry.title: Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: The Origin of Symmetry and Its Breaking

author.name: Yossi Arjevani

entry.summary: Arjevani explains the persistent clustered structure of Hessian spectra at trained deep networks - a near-zero bulk with isolated outliers - as symmetry breaking from a hidden highly symmetric reference configuration. The symmetric reference forces high-multiplicity eigenvalues, and deviations from it account for observed spectra beyond known weight symmetries.

entry.title: Robust Decentralized Fairness Auditing

author.name: Sayan Biswas, Jade Garcia Bourr\'ee, Anne-Marie Kermarrec, Palak, Martijn de Vos

entry.summary: Auditopus enables multiple auditors with individual query sets to collaboratively audit LLMs for fairness while defending against fairwashing, where a malicious auditor acting for the provider portrays a misleading appearance of fairness. This addresses a trust problem that becomes acute as regulatory audit requirements for LLMs expand.

entry.title: Thinking in Depth: Retrospective Inference for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Hao-Run Cai, Si-Yang Liu, Zi-Jian Cheng, Kun-Yang Yu, Jin-Hao Sheng, Guo Yu, Chonghan Liu, Zhi Zhou, Jun-Peng Jiang, Lan-Zhe Guo, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: The authors trace queries through strong tabular foundation models and find predictive refinement concentrated unevenly in later layers. They introduce Retro, a TFM with retrospective inference in which later stages explicitly revisit and refine earlier computations, improving over standard stacked-layer in-context prediction.

entry.title: ResidualQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers with 2-Bit Residuals

author.name: Heejun Kim, Junyoung Lee, SangLyul Cho, Dongsu Han, Insu Han, Sehoon Kim

entry.summary: ResidualQuant exploits the observation that KV states across loops of a looped Transformer are highly similar, using final-loop KV states as references and representing other loops with 2-bit residuals. This addresses KV cache memory bottlenecks in looped Transformers while avoiding the accuracy degradation of generic aggressive quantization.

entry.title: Oracle-Efficient and Parameter-Free Agnostic Smoothed Online Learning

author.name: Sasha Voitovych, Adam Block, Alexander Rakhlin, Abhishek Shetty

entry.summary: This theory paper advances smoothed online learning — an interpolation between adversarial and stochastic regimes — by providing oracle-efficient, parameter-free agnostic algorithms. It removes significant statistical and computational barriers that previously limited practical online learning in this framework.

entry.title: Quadratic Weak-to-Strong Generalization in Random Feature Networks via Random Matrix Theory

author.name: Deborah Oliveira, Elliot Paquette

entry.summary: The paper theoretically studies weak-to-strong generalization in two-layer random feature networks where strength is determined by width, deriving deterministic equivalents for teacher and student errors via random matrix theory. For ReLU and a spherical harmonic target, it shows the student error scales as the square of the teacher error, matching general lower bounds.

entry.title: Democratizing MoE inference on commodity GPUs with CoMoE

author.name: Ruwen Fan (Jimmy), Yuezhi Zu (Jimmy), Junru Li (Jimmy), Qingda Hu (Jimmy), Xinjun (Jimmy), Yang, Jiwu Shu, Youyou Lu

entry.summary: CoMoE is a communication-efficient Mixture-of-Experts inference system that enables MoE model deployment on consumer GPUs lacking NVLink and P2P interconnects, which current expert-parallel systems require. By addressing PCIe-bottlenecked, host-mediated communication, it makes local and privacy-preserving MoE inference feasible on commodity hardware. This broadens access to large open-weight MoE models for individuals.

entry.title: ORCA: Hunting Compositional Failures in Text-to-Image Diffusion

author.name: Arshia Hemmat, Amirhossein Vahidi, Amitis Shidani, Mohammad Vali Sanian, Hesam Asadollahzadeh, Aryan Yazdan Parast, Mohammad Lotfollahi

entry.summary: ORCA investigates compositional failures in text-to-image diffusion models, arguing that attribute-binding failures stem from misaligned rather than missing information: the text encoder preserves compositional structure but in a language-modeling-shaped space that the denoising objective does not reward aligning. The paper shows this cross-modal correspondence can be supplied as an explicit training signal to reduce failures. This offers a mechanistic account and remedy for a persistent weakness of modern image generators.

entry.title: Expert Coupling in MoE Pretraining: Reducing All-to-All Overhead with Correlated Placement and Token Shuffling

author.name: Radha Gulhane, Quentin Anthony, Beren Millidge

entry.summary: The paper observes that during MoE pretraining, routers learn correlated expert-pair assignment patterns, with a small fraction of expert pairs co-selected heavily. Exploiting this, the authors propose correlated expert placement and token shuffling to reduce all-to-all communication overhead, which they measure at 45-60% of the training step on an 8x AMD MI300X node under expert parallelism. The result targets large-scale MoE training efficiency.

entry.title: S2Tok: Streaming 3D Gaussian Reconstruction with Persistent Spatial Tokens

author.name: Fang Li, Jiraphon Yenphraphai, Quentin Herau, Depu Meng, Yihan Hu, Tianshuo Xu, Narendra Ahuja, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: S2Tok is a feed-forward framework for streaming 3D Gaussian reconstruction that maintains a size-adaptive, persistent scene state from uncalibrated image streams, distinguishing updates to known regions from selective expansion for new content. A spatially informed transformer integrates each observation into a renderable, evolving representation.

entry.title: Adaptive Visual Token Reduction for Accelerated Image Understanding

author.name: Seyoung Jeong, Jong Pil Yun, Sang Jun Lee

entry.summary: Proposes ReFIT, an instruction-guided visual token reduction framework for large vision-language models that combines Relevance-Guided Window Reshaping with Instruction-Guided Token Refinement. It adapts window shapes to spatially structured content like elongated text, improving on fixed-crop and per-token pruning baselines for high-resolution VQA.

entry.title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Shadi Alijani, Fereshteh Aghaee Meibodi, Homayoun Najjaran

entry.summary: The authors propose CA-WCP, a conformal prediction method for 3D multi-class medical image segmentation that combines latent-space density-ratio weighting to handle covariate shift with directional quantiles for asymmetric lower and upper volume error bounds. Class-specific asymmetry factors derived from validation false-positive and false-negative rates address biases that symmetric 2D conformal methods miss. The method aims to provide calibrated volumetric uncertainty for foundation segmentation models like MedSAM under distribution shift, which is important for clinical reliability.

entry.title: SkillCycle: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Skill Banks

author.name: Ling Li, Qiuyu Shen, Zheng Jiang, Qinwei Ma, Yuxuan Liu, Zhidong Deng

entry.summary: Introduces SkillCycle, a framework where language agents co-evolve their policies and external skill banks through alternating skill internalization and rule revision, using token-level contextual differences to locate rules and interaction outcomes to guide edits. This addresses the coupled problem that internalizing skills changes the value of remaining guidance.

entry.title: ActiveLang: Active Open-Vocabulary 3D Mapping with Semantic-Uncertainty-Guided Exploration

author.name: Liyan Chen, Hairong Yin, Huangying Zhan, Yi Xu, Raymond A. Yeh, Philippos Mordohai

entry.summary: ActiveLang is an autonomous robotic system that builds language-annotated 3D maps supporting open-vocabulary scene understanding, using online language-feature adaptation on a compact dual-Gaussian representation. Its planner uses semantic uncertainty to guide exploration, enabling robots to map unfamiliar environments without knowing relevant concepts in advance.

entry.title: Quasi-Binarized Autoencoders: An Architecture-Independent Information Bottleneck for Medical Image Anomaly Detection

author.name: Shouhei Hanaoka, Takahiro Nakao, Atsushi Takamatsu, Takeharu Yoshikawa, Osamu Abe

entry.summary: The paper introduces a quasi-binarizing layer that squashes latent elements into [0,1] with Laplace noise, providing an architecture-independent information bottleneck for reconstruction-based medical anomaly detection. This replaces fragile per-dataset architectural capacity tuning with a quantifiable bits-level constraint that prevents identity mapping and anomaly reconstruction.

entry.title: Do Generative Priors Align with Human Naturalness Perception?

author.name: Taiki Fukiage

entry.summary: The study probes the native priors of 25 open image and video generators using directional loss differences under content-preserving paired interventions that selectively disrupt facial configurations or physical illumination consistency. It finds these loss differences reproduce human-like selective sensitivities and tolerances for naturalness violations across both image and video domains. This offers insight into whether generative training objectives implicitly capture human perceptual regularities.

entry.title: MultiFly: A Real-World Multimodal Aerial Dataset with Annotation-Efficient Label Transfer and Cross-Modal Semantic Consistency

author.name: Markus Gross, Andreas Greiner, Taehyoung Kim, Sivasubiramaniam Subbiah, Toma\v{z} Coti\v{c}, Sai Bharadwaj Matha, Conrad Christoph, Oussema Dhaouadi, Simon Zieher, Surya Vijaya Kumar, Gordon Elger, Henri Mee{\ss}, Olaf Wysocki, Paul Spannaus, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: MultiFly is a real-world low-altitude UAV dataset with 17,272 synchronized samples across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar modalities, plus calibration and GNSS-RTK/IMU data. Its key contribution is label transfer from only 115 manually annotated RGB images to all modalities via shared geometric representations, achieving about 90% agreement with held-out manual annotations.

entry.title: Contact-Aware Imitation Learning Through Contact Factorization

author.name: Jiho Hong, Daeun Song, Sanghyun Kim, Mingyo Seo

entry.summary: FACE is a contact-factorized imitation learning framework that separates intended task behavior from environment-dependent contact factors by expressing forces in contact-relative coordinates with learned contact-normal and online friction estimators. This enables contact-rich manipulation policies to transfer beyond demonstrated surface conditions.

entry.title: On-Demand Robotic Assembly via Differentiable Geometric Part Repair

author.name: Millicent Schlafly, Fabio Schaub, Diogo Costa Pais, Luca Lelli, Janne Dvorak, Claire Colmont, Sven Marti, Mark D. Fuge

entry.summary: This work presents an end-to-end pipeline converting user prompts into physically buildable bespoke wooden assemblies: a generative AI agent creates initial 3D geometry, and a gradient-based repair stage backpropagates through a graph attention network surrogate to fix disjointed or overlapping components and correct hardware-specific assemblability issues. The pipeline culminates in physical robotic construction.

entry.title: AdaGuard: Enhancing Safety and Policy Compliance with Reasoning-Enabled LLM-As-A-Judge Guardrails

author.name: Melissa Kazemi Rad, Sihui Dai, Isha Slavin, Kushal Chawla, Mann Patel, Jian Ni, William M. Campbell, Stephen Rawls, Sambit Sahu

entry.summary: AdaGuard is an adaptive LLM-as-a-Judge guardrail that dynamically enforces user-defined safety and compliance policies at runtime, trained via supervised fine-tuning and GRPO reinforcement learning. Its core innovation is adaptive reasoning-budget allocation so latency and policy flexibility can be traded off per input. It targets rigidity in current fixed-policy guardrail systems.

entry.title: DIVA: Dual-Space Intent-Aware Visual Attenuation for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Kaixi Feng, Guoheng Sun, Ziyao Wang, Yexiao He, Zheyu Shen, Ang Li

entry.summary: DIVA is a module for vision-language-action policies that estimates patch-wise relevance by combining task intent with low-level visual evidence, then attenuates low-relevance visual tokens both before the backbone and persistently within it. It preserves the full token sequence and needs no external grounding supervision. This targets a real inefficiency in how dense visual tokens dominate VLA computation.

entry.title: Let the Library Speak: Self-Advertised Method Selection for Formal Proving

author.name: Xiaopeng Yuan, Suijin Wang, Yanli Wang, Haibo Jin, Peng Kuang, Jerry Wang, Lijun Yu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: The paper formulates applicability-aware method selection for LLM-based formal provers, noting that relevance of retrieved lemmas does not imply a method can be applied to the current theorem. The proposed self-advertisement approach has a model generate a problem-specific proposal for each candidate method, and organizes 82 reusable methods from Putnam competitions.

entry.title: Loud Failures, Quiet Failures: Fault Detection and Recovery in Tool-Using Language Model Agents

author.name: Obada Kraishan

entry.summary: This work injects four typed faults (timeouts, disappearing endpoints, changed parameters, silently wrong results) into a function-calling benchmark's environments to study how six LLM agents detect, react to, and recover from tool failures. It finds that models over-trust silently failing tools, with distinct behaviors across failure-handling stages and between reasoning and standard variants. This is directly relevant to production agent reliability.

entry.title: One-Slide Calibration of Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Ming Ren Hou, Tianyi Huang

entry.summary: SlideRuler corrects scanner-induced distribution shift in pathology foundation models by using regions within a single slide as internal controls, learning a transfer map from paired rescans that enables calibration at inference with the foundation model frozen. Across two encoders and five SCORPION scanners, calibration reduces embedding distance shifts by 16.3-38.5%. This addresses a real deployment bottleneck for digital pathology AI.

entry.title: A Deterministic Evidence Layer for Vision-Language Autism Screening from Naturalistic Home Video

author.name: Wenqi Li, Mindi Ruan, Chuanbo Hu, Shuo Wang, Xin Li

entry.summary: The paper finds that VLM-based autism screening verdicts from home video are unstable, with 16-37% of clips changing predicted labels across repeated runs at temperature 0 due to serving-stack nondeterminism. It proposes moving the decision out of the model: the frozen VLM writes timestamped, glossary-labeled event tables with counter-evidence, and a text-only stage performs age-calibrated, deterministic screening decisions.

entry.title: Mixture of Layers: Dynamic Layer Routing for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Jeonghwan Kim, Sofia Stoica, Jiwan Chung, Ansel Blume, Hyeonjeong Ha, Zhenhailong Wang, Xin Luna Dong, Heng Ji

entry.summary: The paper proposes Mixture of Layers (MoL), an instruction-conditioned routing mechanism that dynamically aggregates query-relevant representations from intermediate vision encoder layers at the patch level, rather than relying only on final-layer features. This improves access to fine-grained cues like small objects, text, and spatial details in multimodal LLM visual reasoning.

entry.title: Coding-Agent Benchmarks Should Match Their Users' Task Flows

author.name: Igor Slinko, Yaroslav Golubev, Sergey Titov

entry.summary: Collects 4,782 real agent sessions from software engineers in JetBrains IDEs and shows that long interactive sessions differ sharply from issue-derived benchmark tasks in task-type mix and flow. The authors argue coding-agent benchmarks should reflect real users' task flows, including questions, planning, review, refactoring, and execution.

entry.title: VideoEvolve: Co-Evolving Memory and Retrieval for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yongchao Xu, Bowen Ye, Jiefeng Gan, Junkai Ma, Wenzhao Li, Sen Tao, Yi Wei, Jiawei Liu

entry.summary: VideoEvolve is a self-evolving framework for long video understanding that jointly adapts both what is remembered (Memory Evolver) and how information is retrieved (Retrieval Evolver), rather than fixing the memory and only varying retrieval. Starting from a low-frame-rate overview, it selectively augments memory guided by downstream question needs. This addresses a real mismatch in memory-based video systems where missing details are costly to recover.

entry.title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Linghao Meng, Feng He, Xuan Yang, Junyuan Mao, Pinze Ren, Deqing Mu, Hesen Yang, Qiankun Li

entry.summary: PHRBench is a controlled benchmark evaluating how 18 LLMs behaviorally handle hallucinated premises that propagate into multi-stage reasoning, characterizing trajectories via Hallucination Compliance, Hallucination Avoidance, and Heuristic Correction across four domains. It assesses response-level reasoning processes independently of final-answer correctness, defining insightful trajectories as successful corrections leading to accurate answers.

entry.title: Never Look Back: Understanding Persistence in 3D Object Memory from Egocentric Videos

author.name: Shravan Chaudhari, William Paul, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Homanga Bharadhwaj

entry.summary: Ledger is a persistent 3D object memory system that lets an embodied assistant recall object locations, histories, and contextual descriptions from egocentric video of a person's daily activities. It retains objects after they leave view, clusters observations by resting location, and records movements only after repeated evidence, mimicking human incidental memory. This targets a gap in embodied AI where agents need to remember task-relevant objects encountered long before they become useful.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Pretraining for Steady-State Neural CFD Surrogates

author.name: Anthony Zhou, Amir Barati Farimani, Shirley Ho, Rudy Morel

entry.summary: This work studies neural CFD surrogates trained across different geometries, boundary conditions, and fidelities, finding that cross-domain pretraining improves zero- and few-shot generalization to held-out datasets. It reduces the need for costly application-specific solver data generation.

entry.title: Universal Local Error and Realized Amplification for the First-Order EDM Predictor

author.name: Nicolas Brosse, Arnak S. Dalalyan

entry.summary: The paper provides theoretical analysis of the first-order deterministic EDM diffusion sampler in 2-Wasserstein distance, separating local discretization error from its amplification by subsequent learned steps. The authors prove a universal distribution-independent quadratic one-step error bound and derive explicit contraction criteria and realized amplification measures that depend on the learned network.

entry.title: SPLATIFY: Reproduce, Discover, Innovate! From Papers and Ideas to Trainable 3DGS Code

author.name: Seemandhar Jain, Keshav Gupta, Manmohan Chandraker

entry.summary: SPLATIFY is a multi-agent framework that converts 3D Gaussian Splatting research papers into trainable gsplat-based implementations, using a context-free grammar constrained synthesis, fork-aware citation recovery, and other innovations where generic code-generation methods fail. It targets the heavy reimplementation burden in the fast-moving 3DGS field.

entry.title: Unified Multi-plane Autoregressive Diffusion for 3D Multi-contrast MRI Synthesis

author.name: Yejee Shin, Geonhui Son, Jinglu Wang, Minwoo Jung, Yan Lu, Dosik Hwang
