author.name: Gennadiy Savrasov, Maksim Elistratov, Nikita Gavrilov, Albert Garifullin, Oleg Pavlov, Soslan Kabisov, Vladimir Frolov, Anton Konushin, Andrey Kuznetsov, Dmitrii Zhemchuzhnikov

entry.summary: CADFather is an agentic system that reconstructs editable parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes by coordinating complementary tools. A vision-language assistant inspects renders, decides which candidate programs to extend, which proposal tools to invoke, and when to stop, while numerical optimization refines parameters. It addresses a real engineering gap since no single proposal source works across all geometries.

entry.title: Ream: Unfolding Mutual Awareness in Human-Agent Workspaces

author.name: Peiling Jiang, Sangho Suh, Varsha Kishore, Jonathan Bragg, Haijun Xia, Pao Siangliulue, Daniel S. Weld, Amy X. Zhang, Joseph Chee Chang

entry.summary: Ream is a literature-review workspace supporting mutual awareness between humans and AI agents through structured artifacts, bidirectional engagement tracking, and localized visualizations, so users can inspect agent activity and agents can retrieve user histories. Studies with eighteen researchers show the traces help users steer agents and calibrate trust.

entry.title: Learning to Accumulate Knowledge with Mutual Information

author.name: Yuyang Zhao, Lizi Liao, Leyang Shen, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Fuli Feng, Xiangnan He

entry.summary: Knowledge Weaver is an RL framework that trains a model to curate reusable knowledge from agent trajectories into a growing knowledge bank, using mutual-information-inspired feedback to penalize redundant entries. Standard GRPO on task success alone would reinforce generic guidance that duplicates existing knowledge. This targets the open problem of making agent memory increasingly useful as it grows.

entry.title: AI Safety Considerations for Agents With Limited Time to Act

author.name: Leo Zeitler, Jack Richings, Victoria Nockles

entry.summary: The authors prove theoretical impossibility results for agent-agnostic safety guarantees in partially observable environments requiring timely action, via two realistic scenarios (infinite state space and signal mixture). They show that even a perfect agent cannot guarantee safe behavior, arguing that any AI safety or alignment proof must reference the environment and its safety assumptions. This is a caution against architecture-only alignment claims.

entry.title: Autonomous Driving Research Requires a Community-Driven Data Paradigm

author.name: Jinsu Yoo, Zanming Huang, Katie Z Luo, Zheda Mai, Qiyuan Wu, Bharath Hariharan, Mark Campbell, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that the gap between current autonomous driving systems and universal robustness stems from the data paradigm, not just modeling: research relies on a few narrow benchmarks while over 600 datasets from nearly 50 countries remain underused due to fragmentation. The authors propose a community-driven data paradigm to unlock this collective resource.

entry.title: Work While They Sleep: Exploiting Evaluation Latency for Fully Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Gustavo Sutter, Alejandro Comas-Leon, David Holzm\"uller, Hao Wang, Luis Ricardez-Sandoval, Pascal Poupart, Agustinus Kristiadi

entry.summary: This work improves Bayesian optimization for expensive black-box objectives by using the latency of objective evaluations to perform fully Bayesian hyperparameter marginalization via model averaging, rather than fitting point-estimate surrogate hyperparameters. This yields better uncertainty estimates in the low-data regimes typical of costly experiments in science and engineering. The approach turns unavoidable idle time into better inference.

entry.title: Patient, Place, Prior (P$^3$): What Counts as Personalization in Medical World Models?

author.name: Xingrui Gu, Hanxue Gu, Yuxiang Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: P3 is an audit framework asking whether a longitudinal medical forecast genuinely benefits from a specific patient's imaging history, spatial support, and context, versus merely matching population averages. The authors also propose Cancer JEPA, a one-step model forecasting representations of future breast DCE-MRI exams during neoadjuvant treatment.

entry.title: MORA: Modeling Observed Changes for Drift-Robust Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xudong Mou, Tiejun Wang, Rui Wang, Hui Wang, Pin Liu, Tianyu Wo, Xudong Liu, Renyu Yang

entry.summary: MORA is a drift-robust time-series anomaly detection framework that formalizes temporal change disambiguation: deciding whether a local deviation reflects abnormality or evolving context. It reconstructs the same local target from paired short- and long-term views, using the reconstruction gap to measure contextual support and resolve the ambiguity that plagues non-stationary settings.

entry.title: Activation-Aware Weight Tensorization: A Calibration-Time Preconditioner for Tensor-Network LLM Compression

author.name: Alessandro Beatini, Marco Maronese, Emanuele Rodol\`a

entry.summary: AWT is a training-free compression preconditioner that scales each weight matrix by a diagonal activation-derived calibration before tensor-network (TT/TTN) decomposition, correcting the mismatch between weight-space Frobenius error and functional error. Across Llama 3.1 8B, Ministral 8B, and Qwen2.5 7B at 2-6x compression, AWT closes 12-35% of the WikiText perplexity gap of vanilla tensorization under single-operator replacement. It is a practical efficiency technique for deploying compressed LLMs.

entry.title: From Prompts to Trees: Effective LLM-Guided Tree Generation for Few-Shot Tabular Classification

author.name: Yue Qiu, Zekang Du, Yiqun Diao, Bingsheng He, Qinbin Li

entry.summary: The authors propose distilling LLM world knowledge into interpretable decision trees for few-shot tabular classification via a three-stage paradigm: prompt the LLM to generate rules, then organize rules into a tree, avoiding unstable full-tree generation. This combines the interpretability and efficiency of trees with LLM generalization. Results across real-world tabular datasets support the approach.

entry.title: Exact Dynamics and Finite-Sample Trajectory Recovery of Linear Recursive Feature Machines

author.name: Andrew Cheng, Bobak T. Kiani, Yue M. Lu, Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan

entry.summary: The paper gives exact dynamics and finite-sample statistics for linear recursive feature machines in noisy multi-output regression, extending the connection between RFMs and iteratively reweighted least squares to ridge-regularized noisy settings with low-rank teacher targets. This clarifies how representations evolve during feature learning in an analytically tractable model.

entry.title: When Should an In-Context Learner Expand Its Hypothesis Space?

author.name: Weihan Li, Xinlei Chen, Junhao Wu, Tianshi Zheng

entry.summary: This work frames hypothesis-space expansion in in-context learning as a costly sequential decision problem, distinguishing failures due to noise, exceptions, in-family change, or out-of-family structure. It introduces a Structural Revision Environment with exact Bayesian solutions showing revision follows a value boundary dependent on expansion cost and remaining horizon.

entry.title: BoT-GRPO: Efficient Process-Reward RL for Reasoning via Bag-of-Token Aggregation

author.name: Yingxiang Yang, Weihang Xiao, Zhunxuan Wang, Joshua Flashner, Niresh Agarwal

entry.summary: BoT-GRPO extends GRPO to token-level reward models via a length-invariant bag-of-tokens aggregation that weights token rewards by inverse sequence length and computes per-token advantages from weighted group statistics. It is critic-free and aims to accelerate convergence and improve reasoning quality without value networks.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Coordination via Support-Preserving Distillation

author.name: Sangmin Lee, Youngju Na, Chanmi Lee, Sung-eui Yoon

entry.summary: This work identifies a failure mode in offline multi-agent RL where flow-based teachers pair noise with replay targets independently, causing samples between conflicting coordination modes that then propagate to distilled student actors. The proposed MoSDOT method uses semi-discrete optimal transport to preserve mode support during teacher training.

entry.title: Physics-Aligned Electronic Ground-State Learning Improves Generalization

author.name: Eike S. Eberhard, Xaver Kainz, Viktor Kotsev, Abdulrahman Aldossary, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: The authors propose observable-agnostic electronic ground-state descriptor models positioned between ML interatomic potentials and Kohn-Sham DFT in cost, aligning learning objectives with the governing KS-DFT equations via physical constraints. Contributions include an OrthoNormal loss and Grassmann regularizer, showing improved size extrapolation from QM9 to QM40.

entry.title: PoreML: A Data-Driven Framework for Learning Multiphase Flow in Porous Media

author.name: Chunyang Wang, Mingrui Zhang, Yuyan Zhang, Linqi Zhu, Xin Ju, Edo Sicco Boek, Martin J. Blunt, Gege Wen

entry.summary: PoreML is an open-source framework unifying data generation, training, and physics-grounded evaluation for learning multiphase flow in porous microstructures, relevant to CO2 storage and fuel cells. It includes a GPU-native lattice Boltzmann solver validated against analytical solutions to address the scarcity of time-resolved 3D datasets.

entry.title: Slow Beats Fast at the Kesten-Stigum Threshold: Minimax, Fisher-Information and Belief-Propagation Characterizations of the Information-Computation Gap in Sparse Stochastic Block Models

author.name: Soroor Ghandali

entry.summary: This theory paper provides three characterizations of the Kesten-Stigum threshold and the information-computation gap in sparse stochastic block models, using minimax risk, Fisher information, and belief propagation. It connects Bayes rules, polynomial estimators, and low-degree methods into a unified statistical decision-theoretic picture.

entry.title: emg2face: Expressive Facial Animation with High-Density Surface EMG

author.name: Ganidhu Abey, Wendy Greening, Ashika Kamboj, Leonhard Helminger, Abhijeet Ghosh, Karel Petranek, Sergio Orts Escolano, Dinesh K. Pai

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that high-density surface EMG (64 channels at 2048 Hz) can drive expressive facial animation without optical capture, addressing occlusion by VR headsets and privacy concerns. The authors collect forehead and side-of-face EMG signals and map them to facial expressions. This enables realistic avatar facial animation under head-mounted displays where cameras cannot see the face.

entry.title: Unpaired Canonical Correlation Analysis

author.name: Nir Ben-Ari, Ronen Talmon, Uri Shaham

entry.summary: This paper presents Unpaired CCA (UCCA), the first method to learn maximally correlated linear projections without any paired samples during training, by connecting the Quadratic Assignment Problem to CCA theoretically. The approach learns multiview shared spaces when pairing is unavailable or impossible to obtain. This relaxes a strict and often impractical requirement of a fundamental classical method.

entry.title: Global Average Precision for Representation Learning

author.name: Bill Psomas, Mohammad Mahdi, Michalis Thomas, Danda Pani Paudel, Giorgos Tolias, Giorgos Kordopatis-Zilos

entry.summary: The paper introduces Global Average Precision (gAP), an information retrieval metric that ranks all query-candidate pairs in a single list, capturing cross-query comparability that per-query metrics like mAP ignore, plus gSAP, a differentiable surrogate usable as a training loss. This is relevant to systems with a single global decision threshold. The loss plugs into standard representation learning pipelines with the same inputs as InfoNCE-style objectives.

entry.title: Data Reuse in Non-Stationary Learning

author.name: Tomer Gafni, Garud Iyengar, Assaf Zeevi

entry.summary: The authors study online learning in non-stationary environments where an unknown parameter switches abruptly among recurring values, quantifying fundamental tradeoffs in safely reusing past observations. They propose Exposure-Capped Reuse (ECR), a class of anytime algorithms combining online change detection and compatibility testing, showing the tradeoffs resemble a bias-variance dilemma.

entry.title: Derivative Gaussian Processes on a Two-Direction Budget

author.name: Hyunseok Seung, Matthias Katzfuss

entry.summary: This work proposes a derivative Gaussian process surrogate that uses only two directions per observed gradient within a Vecchia approximation. One direction captures the gradient's direct contribution to prediction and the other its indirect contributions via correlations, reducing md gradient coordinates to 2m directional derivatives and achieving O(m^3) dense factorization per prediction target. This makes gradient-informed GPs far more scalable.

entry.title: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation

author.name: Yihao Hu, Yanlin Feng, Naoki Otani, Nikita Bhutani

entry.summary: ARCS introduces structured disambiguation, a paradigm where ambiguity in text-to-SQL user questions is resolved through explicit, constrained interactions rather than free-form clarification dialogue. The paper contributes the first text-to-SQL ambiguity benchmark with naturally occurring, unconstrained user questions. This targets error sources that silently push systems away from user intent in real deployments.

entry.title: Learning to Act with Task Progress: Distilling Small Agents from Compact Teacher Supervision

author.name: Wenxi Gan

entry.summary: Task-Progress Distillation (TPD) trains small agent models offline by pairing each demonstrated action with a compact label describing the current task stage, letting a 1.7B-parameter student score stage-action pairs executed by a deterministic harness. On ALFWorld, the student achieves 72.4% unseen task success with only 404 demonstrations.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Brain MRI Inpainting with 2.5D Unconditional Flow Priors

author.name: Arnela Hadzic, Franz Thaler, Simon Johannes Joham, Martin Urschler

entry.summary: The authors propose a zero-shot brain MRI inpainting framework using 2.5D unconditional flow priors that capture superior-inferior spatial context without full 3D convolution overhead or task-specific conditional training. The method synthesizes healthy tissue in pathological regions to support downstream registration, brain extraction, and segmentation.

entry.title: Controllable Crowd Generation through World-Model Planning

author.name: JunGyu Lee, Jisu Shin, Seunghyun Shin, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: Proposes Ctrl-CWM, a controllable crowd world model that adapts world-model planning with imagined futures to crowd simulation, combining an encoder of human motion dynamics, an actor proposing behaviors, and run-time control supporting new user-specified objectives. It targets robotics, autonomous driving, and urban planning simulation.

entry.title: Gradient-Based Trajectory Optimisation over Continuous Poses for Sparse-View Cone-Beam CT

author.name: Linda-Sophie Schneider, Simon Wittl, Gabriel Herl, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: The authors make every CT source pose a continuous variable optimized by gradient ascent on the scanner's kinematic manifold, combining soft-Tuy plane coverage, a continuous view covariance loss, and an attenuation-aware ray-bundle penalty. This handles multiple scanner geometries and recovers laminar defects invisible to circular orbits in sparse-view cone-beam CT.

entry.title: MOTIF: Person-of-Interest Deepfake Detection Beyond 3DMM Coefficients

author.name: Giovanni Affatato, Sara Mandelli, Paolo Bestagini, Stefano Tubaro

entry.summary: MOTIF dissects which components of 3D Morphable Model representations carry the detection signal in person-of-interest deepfake detection, holding encoder, training corpus, and enrollment protocol fixed. It finds coefficient groups largely redundant, with the shape block alone recovering most accuracy and temporal evolution contributing a bounded amount. This provides actionable insight into what matters for building per-identity deepfake detectors from genuine footage.

entry.title: HarnessIR: Harnessing Multimodal Foundation Models for Universal Real-World Image Restoration

author.name: Xiangtao Kong, Shuaizheng Liu, Rongyuan Wu, Lingchen Sun, Zhengqiang Zhang, Jinxin Zhao, Yuhui Wu, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: HarnessIR is an agentic framework for real-world image restoration that uses a multimodal foundation model as the executor across five stages including perception, diagnosis, and on-demand tool invocation. It critiques sequential tool-calling over single-degradation models, arguing mixed real-world degradations cannot be cleanly undone one at a time. The design aims at universal restoration of complex combined degradations.

entry.title: Position Forcing: Self-Conditioning 3D Generation

author.name: Ziheng Ouyang, Zeqiang Lai, Jiarui Chen, Jiangshan Wang, Yuhao Wan, Jingbo Gong, Xiangyu Yue, Hengshuang Zhao, Qibin Hou, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Position Forcing improves single-stage 3D generative models built on VecSet representations, which must implicitly infer token positions during denoising unlike two-stage methods with explicit positional guidance. The method recovers token positions from the current clean latent estimate, quantizes them at progressively finer resolutions across denoising stages, and uses them as self-conditioning. This strengthens generation quality without a second stage.

entry.title: QuadTok: Quadtree Visual Tokenizer for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Yucheng Mao, Zeyuan Chen, Xiaojun Shan, Xiang Zhang, Divyansh Srivastava, Bingnan Li, Zhuowen Tu

entry.summary: QuadTok proposes a hierarchical quadtree visual tokenizer for autoregressive image generation that dynamically allocates representational capacity to visually intricate regions while keeping homogeneous areas coarse. Compared with a fixed 256-token grid it saves about 10 percent of tokens on ImageNet and 9 percent zero-shot on COCO at comparable reconstruction fidelity. The tree structure also introduces natural causality that fits autoregressive modeling.

entry.title: ScribbleEdit: A Benchmark for Scribble-Only Image Editing

author.name: Jie Ren, Hao Kang, Kai Guo, Yiding Yang, Bo Liu, Liming Jiang, Qing Yan, Zichuan Liu, Yizhi Song, Yue Xing, Hui Liu, Xin Lu

entry.summary: ScribbleEdit is a benchmark with an automated data construction pipeline and evaluation protocol for image editing conditioned solely on scribbles, measuring both intention alignment and spatial accuracy. It reveals that current VLM/LLM-based editing models struggle with scribble-only inputs, highlighting a real interaction gap for creative tools.

entry.title: The Modular CMA-ES: A Framework for Modern Evolution Strategies

author.name: Jacob de Nobel, Diederick Vermetten, Anna V. Kononova, Carola Doerr, Thomas B\"ack

entry.summary: ModCMA is a configurable framework that decomposes the CMA-ES evolution strategy into interchangeable modules, integrating many proposed modifications within a single implementation so their interactions can be systematically studied. This addresses the fragmentation of evolution strategy research where variants are developed and evaluated in isolation.

entry.title: LACE-CRAFT: Robot Co-Design with Actor Inheritance and Blackboard Collaboration

author.name: Yuhan Wen, Jiawei Wang, Qixuan Zhang, Yusen Qin, Lan Xu

entry.summary: LACE-CRAFT couples robot morphology search with policy learning while preserving acquired control experience: LACE resumes the incumbent policy and initializes challenger designs with inherited actor parameters, while CRAFT coordinates morphology, reward, and feedback roles through shared records and a multi-agent blackboard. A generative extension converts generated meshes into editable articulated models.

entry.title: TempoBridge: Language-Guided Tempo Control for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Yeonseo Lee, Hyosup Shin, Guebin Hwang, Sungho Jo

entry.summary: TempoBridge adds how-fast-to-move controllability to frozen VLA policies by extracting tempo cues from VLM representations and aligning them with task progress via a causal phase router, requiring no tempo-labeled demonstrations or base-policy fine-tuning. On LIBERO tasks it raises tempo success rate from 52.6 percent to 89.7 percent.

entry.title: AeroEval: Staged Program and Execution Validation for AI-Generated Drone Missions

author.name: Kautuk Astu, Naina Rabha, Yogesh Simmhan

entry.summary: AeroEval is an agent-assisted middleware for staged validation of LLM-generated drone mission code, combining deterministic program analysis with context-grounded LLM agents to catch violations of user intent, environmental constraints, and mission-level behavior. It improves failure localization over prompt guardrails or simulator-only checks.

entry.title: RoboPrompt: Intuitive Robot Policy Steering with Sparse Human Input

author.name: Yanwen Zou, Chenyang Shi, Guoxuan Xu, Wenye Yu, Wendi Chen, Ye Pan, Cewu Lu, Chuan Wen

entry.summary: RoboPrompt is a lightweight shared-autonomy system that lets users steer pretrained end-to-end robot policies at deployment using sparse intuitive inputs such as drawn traces, target points, and directional strokes, without teleoperation hardware or policy retraining. This addresses the limited zero-shot reliability of imitation-learned policies and the scalability barriers of existing human-correction methods.

entry.title: UltraText Bench: A Comprehensive Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Image Generation

author.name: Deyuan Liu, Yihao Hu, Jingxuan Zhang, Xingying Li, Jun Xie, Jiacheng Liu, Jungang Li, Yu Huang, Xuanyi Liu, Yue Ding, Zecheng Wang, Lei Zhao, Mingda Wang, Zhenglin Cheng, Peng Sun, Tao Lin

entry.summary: Introduces UltraText Bench, a bilingual (English/Chinese) benchmark of 432 human-reviewed prompts for dense visual text rendering across 24 scene categories and three difficulty levels, with structured references for content, placement, and attributes. Evaluation uses a Q-Judger vision-language model to assess generated images against complete references.

entry.title: The Identifiability and Observability of Deep Normalized Attention

author.name: Pranav Venkata Konda

entry.summary: The paper characterizes which parameters of deep unmasked single-head attention are determined by its input-output function, proving the real-analytic case of the Henry-Marchetti-Kohn conjecture including softmax. It classifies exceptional fibers where collapse makes scores unobservable and computes Jacobian decay spectra near simultaneous query/key collapse.

entry.title: Shared Gaussianization: What Gaussian Regularizers Certify About Contrastive Learning, and What They Miss

author.name: Ruoyu Zhao, Yuting Chen, Jinheng Zhang, Zhehao Zou, Tong Che

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes shared Gaussianization—the Gaussianity test underlying SIGReg in LeJEPA—showing it vanishes exactly at aligned uniform minimizers of population InfoNCE and bounds InfoNCE excess risk with a sharp square-root rate and dimension-free constant. It also probes what such regularizers fail to certify about contrastive learning.

entry.title: Executing Causal Structure Learning with Linear-Attention Transformers

author.name: Amartya Roy, Sayar Karmakar

entry.summary: The authors explicitly construct a fixed-weight linear-attention Transformer whose forward pass exactly reproduces one update of a continuous causal discovery algorithm, showing repeated blocks reproduce its optimization trajectory. They prove retaining the algorithm's multiplier between updates is essential for exact execution.

entry.title: PEACE: Covariant learning of nonadiabatic manifolds with parity-resolved Hamiltonians

author.name: Rongzhi Gao, Shuguang Chen, Yang Zhou, GuanHua Chen, Ziyang Hu, ChiYung Yam

entry.summary: PEACE combines a parity-equivariant latent Hamiltonian with a learned electronic connection to model nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, respecting electronic symmetry in light-driven processes relevant to solar energy conversion and photocatalysis. Controlled ablations show complementary roles of symmetry-allowed state mixing and electronic-frame variation, and the model reproduces excited-state population dynamics from first-principles simulations. This advances ML surrogate modeling for quantum chemistry.

entry.title: Flow-of-Thought: A Framework for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Mariia Baidachna, Nicolas Pugeault

entry.summary: Flow-of-Thought integrates visual sketch generation as intermediate reasoning steps mimicking human mental imagery, training coordinate-aware trajectory flow fields on SO(2) group orbits and cumulative shortest paths. Frozen learned dynamics are compared via reconstruction energy across competing generative hypotheses, achieving 100 percent accuracy on Tetris and 99 percent on colored shape tasks under locked tests.

entry.title: A Probabilistic Perspective on Wasserstein-Based Evidential Uncertainty for Out-of-Distribution Segmentation

author.name: Arnold Brosch, Abdelrahman Eldesokey, Michael Felsberg, Kira Maag

entry.summary: The paper provides a probabilistic analysis of evidential deep learning for out-of-distribution segmentation, moving beyond Euclidean objectives by using Wasserstein-based formulations to better calibrate epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. This targets the safety-critical failure of segmentation networks on OOD objects in autonomous driving. It offers an efficient alternative to costly Bayesian methods like deep ensembles.

entry.title: ECHO: Embodied Camera Observations of Human Object Carrying

author.name: Xuefei Sun, Lorin Achey, Kali Hamilton, Alberto Speranzon, Gregory Grebe, Yonatan Bisk, Christoffer Heckman

entry.summary: ECHO introduces contextual object placement as a benchmark task: predicting an object's destination during an observed object-carrying episode, requiring reasoning about environment layout and human habits. The paper presents a dataset with navigable, fully reconstructed scenes, human activity, and ground-truth object destinations, filling a gap where existing RGB-D scans are static and HOI datasets lack scene context. This supports embodied and assistive agents beyond mere object recognition.

entry.title: Adaptive Workflow Intelligence: A Cognitive Architecture for Context-Driven Enterprise Automation

author.name: Sreedevi Pandiyath Viswambaran

entry.summary: This paper proposes AWI, a cognitive architecture for enterprise automation agents organized around a four-layer Perception-Cognition-Action-Reflection loop. It treats reflection as a continuous policy-refinement mechanism and integrates hybrid reasoning with policy-constrained enterprise operations, addressing brittleness of LLM agents and RL under evolving conditions. It matters for practitioners building adaptive, auditable automation in regulated environments.

entry.title: Sigma-Hunter: A Domain-Specific Language Model for Threat Hunting and Detection Engineering

author.name: Kemal Davaslioglu, Sastry Kompella

entry.summary: Sigma-Hunter is a domain-adapted LLM for generating Sigma detection rules for threat hunting, built from 3,635 validated open-source rules expanded into 7,663 instruction-tuning examples with leak-free train/test partitioning. It fine-tunes 7B Mistral and Phi models to avoid common failures of general LLMs like invalid YAML or overbroad logic. A solid applied security contribution with careful dataset hygiene.

entry.title: GeoNatureAgent (GNA): A Framework and Benchmark for Pre-Production Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents on Geospatial and Environmental Tasks

author.name: Gabriel Diaz-Ireland, Diego Prieto-Herr\'aez, Mario Garc\'ia Peces, Javier Vel\'azquez, Benjamin Zaitchik, Devika Jain

entry.summary: GeoNatureAgent provides a fixed sixteen-tool geospatial MCP server and a 103-task benchmark for evaluating tool-using agents against a real, self-hostable environmental API covering Spain and Portugal. Because the tool layer, tasks, and scorer are held constant, the agent is the only variable under test. It fills a genuine gap in pre-production evaluation for domain-specific agent deployments.

entry.title: Trajectory Abstraction for the Science of Language Agent Behavior

author.name: Tianqiang Yan

entry.summary: The paper formulates scientific study of language agents as learning and testing a hierarchy of trajectory abstractions: measuring role- and phase-indexed events, proposing constrained relations, testing stability, then constructing episode-level motifs and repeating. Explicit measurement functions tie each abstraction level back to raw trajectories, with randomized protocol experiments for hypothesis testing. It proposes a methodology for a behavioral science of agents.

entry.title: From Plausible Hierarchies to Useful Taxonomies: Evaluating Agentic Harnesses on Customer Feedback

author.name: Prabhath Chellingi, Raviraja G, Viraj Bagal

entry.summary: This paper asks when LLM-generated taxonomies over customer feedback corpora are actually useful in production, not merely plausible. The authors build six taxonomies over two proprietary corpora and evaluate them with operationally meaningful criteria beyond per-node validity checks.

entry.title: Learning Situation-Conditioned Thinking Policies for Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Hong Su

entry.summary: This paper proposes a situation-conditioned thinking memory framework that distills historical reasoning experience into a lightweight policy predicting what should be thought about in the current situation, while delegating detailed reasoning to the LLM. It targets long-running agents whose memory and context cannot grow indefinitely, covering temporal and spatiotemporal situation evolution.

entry.title: RewardWeaver: Long-Horizon Interactive Learning for Language Agents via Self-Evolving Reward Adaptation

author.name: Hengbo Xiao, Boyao Zhang, Purui Liu, Yuxuan Zheng, Haoran Yin, Haibo Liu, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: RewardWeaver is a self-evolving reward adaptation framework for long-horizon language agents, maintaining a validated capability space with semantically fixed rubrics and adapting which rubrics are emphasized as the policy evolves. This tackles sparse terminal feedback and the mismatch between static process rewards and the policy's current bottleneck. It extends RLVR to long-horizon interactive settings.

entry.title: Transferability and operational reliability of a Prithvi crop classification foundation model under phenological and geographic shift across three continents

author.name: Venkatesh Kolluru, Rajat Shinde, Abdelhak Marouane, Caden Helbling, Deepak Shah, Othneil Drew, Srinivas Kolluru, Iksha Gurung, Manil Maskey, Rahul Ramachandran

entry.summary: Evaluates the Prithvi-EO-2.0 geospatial foundation model for crop classification across 37 events in 12 countries on three continents, finding overall accuracy drops from 0.65 in the US to 0.40 in Europe. Beyond accuracy, it assesses confidence calibration, sensitivity to observation windows, and other operational reliability aspects under distribution shift.

entry.title: RACER: Reflective Agent Coupling Query Interpretation and Tool-Based Retrieval for Frame Selection in Long Video Understanding

author.name: Yiyang Huang, Yitian Zhang, Yizhou Wang, Jianglin Lu, Qihua Dong, Hailing Wang, Huimin Zeng, Mingyuan Zhang, Yun Fu

entry.summary: RACER is a training-free agentic framework for selecting relevant frames in long-video understanding, decomposing the problem into query interpretation by a lightweight video LLM plus evidence-driven retrieval. The paper diagnoses two failure modes in existing approaches: a Query Comprehension Gap in similarity-based methods and an Interpretation-Selection Gap in judgment-based methods. The reflective coupling of these stages improves frame selection for complex queries over long videos.

entry.title: SwarmReconGuard: Black-Box Detection of Distributed Collective Reconnaissance by Individually Benign-Looking Agent Populations

author.name: Vahid Tavakkoli, Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Distributed Collective Reconnaissance, a threat where agentic clients spread low-rate reconnaissance across many identities so each request looks benign, and presents a reproducible black-box benchmark with 440 test runs across 10-10,000 virtual identities. It compares multiple detector families, with Gaussian likelihood-ratio detection achieving strong performance.

entry.title: TutorLoop: Regulating Student Learning Behaviors via Sensor-in-the-Loop Generative Feedback

author.name: Songlin Xu, Xinyu Zhang

entry.summary: TutorLoop is a sensor-in-the-loop tutoring system that uses webcam-derived cognitive-state signals, a deep reinforcement learning agent to choose feedback types over the whole learning process, and an LLM to render feedback into human-like messages. A large-scale user study (N=187) shows an offline-trained model transfers directly to a new learning task.

entry.title: GeoPrior-Mamba: Structured Process Priors with Mamba for Fine-Resolution XCO2 Reconstruction

author.name: Zhao Meng, Yinan Cai, Siru Zhong, Juepeng Zheng, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: GeoPrior-Mamba reconstructs fine-resolution CO2 (XCO2) fields from sparse satellite observations using a multi-directional Mamba architecture augmented with structured process priors induced offline by a language model. Rather than having the LM predict values, it organizes knowledge about biospheric uptake, respiration, and anthropogenic emissions into deterministic priors before training.

entry.title: Correct Answers, Unsupported Findings: Evidence Binding in Forensic Reconstruction of LLM Agent Logs

author.name: Taehyeon Yun, Dongho Kim, Geonwoo Kim, Juyoung Seo, Minseok Hur, Moohong Min

entry.summary: Audits whether LLM readers, when reconstructing LLM-agent actions forensically, can establish which preserved record supports a finding, using 64 mechanically checkable cases from saved AgentDojo Banking executions. It separately measures evidence-grounded findings, justified abstention, and unsupported assertions, showing that citation identifiers do not establish sources unless identifier-to-record bindings are preserved.

entry.title: What Makes Synthetic Hard Negatives Work in Vision-Language Pretraining?

author.name: Nikos Giakoumoglou, Paschalis Giakoumoglou, Andreas Floros, Kleanthis Marios Papadopoulos, Tania Stathaki

entry.summary: Analyzes six representation-space synthetic hard-negative strategies for vision-language pretraining, identifying two failure modes and observing logit-scale saturation with learnable temperature, which fixing the temperature resolves. Based on this geometric analysis it proposes SNAP, an improved hard-negative generation method.

entry.title: Temporal Predictive Multiplicity: Equally Accurate Time Series Models Yield Different Forecast Trajectories

author.name: Emanuele Albini, Francesca Toni, Saumitra Mishra, Francesco Leofante

entry.summary: The paper introduces temporal predictive multiplicity, a framework characterizing disagreement over complete forecast trajectories among time-series models with near-identical accuracy, showing that performance constraints alone admit a broad range of different trajectories. Unlike prior scalar-output analyses, it treats forecasts jointly across horizons. This has implications for model selection and trust in forecasting systems used for decisions.

entry.title: Why Software Engineering Is Indispensable in the Age of Coding Agents

author.name: Alfonso Fuggetta

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that capable AI coding agents make software engineering discipline and professionals more, not less, essential. It identifies three structural LLM properties (probabilistic generation, agnosticism, semantic statelessness) that create a trust gap which can only be filled by methodological, domain, design, and process knowledge. The argument speaks directly to current debates about AI-generated software quality.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Generation of Transparent, Open-Source Multiphysics Models of Electrochemical Devices

author.name: Sebastian Castro, Maya F. Schuchert, Spencer A. McCluskey, Eric W. Lees, Justin C. Bui

entry.summary: The authors show that frontier LLM agents can generate open-source multiphysics continuum models of electrochemical devices, using 1D electrochemical CO2 reduction as a test case. A machine-readable, human-specified harness keeps the governing physics under researcher control while the LLM removes the numerical implementation burden typically requiring proprietary software or expert skills.

entry.title: The Cost of Long Memory: State, Context, and Stability Complexity in Sequence Models

author.name: Yuheng Song

entry.summary: This theory paper proves matching upper and lower approximation bounds on how much state, context, or dynamical criticality a sequence model needs to forecast accurately under algebraically decaying predictive memory. It shows the best r-mode forecast error decays as e^{-Theta(sqrt r)}, so achieving error tau requires Theta(log^2(1/tau)) states or modes, giving precise complexity characterizations for a canonical forecasting target. This formalizes the resource cost of long-range temporal dependence in sequence models.

entry.title: Neighborhood Smoothing for Calibration

author.name: Idan Horowitz, Avigdor Gal

entry.summary: The authors propose graph smoothing as a general train-time calibration principle that encourages similar predictive distributions across neighboring samples in representation space, deriving theoretical bounds linking neighbor divergence to confidence variation and calibration error propagation, and characterizing when smoothing can improve calibration.

entry.title: EDiS: Edge Disjoint Subgraph Sparsification Framework for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Sai Karthik Navuluru, Siddhartha Shankar Das, Franck Dernoncourt, S M Ferdous, Ryan A. Rossi, Nesreen K. Ahmed, Baris Coskunuzer, Alex Pothen, Lakshman Tamil, Mahantesh M Halappanavar

entry.summary: EDiS decouples one-time structural extraction from per-epoch graph composition for sparse GNN training, decomposing a graph into cacheable edge-disjoint subgraphs that are recombined under edge budgets each epoch. This avoids repeated expensive sampling while allowing topology variation during training.

entry.title: Global Exponential Convergence of Two-Layer Linear Network Training

author.name: Stephen Y Zhang, Gabriel Peyr\'e

entry.summary: The authors prove global exponential convergence with explicit rates for wide two-layer linear networks trained in the rich scaling regime, showing gradient flow closes exactly to a finite-dimensional Bures flow of the neuron covariance. Mean-field conservation laws yield uniform spectral lower bounds under a spectral support gap condition, permitting even singular initializations.

entry.title: Closed-Form Noise Calibration Against Membership Inference for Random-Allocation DP-SGD

author.name: Murat Bilgehan Ertan, Marten van Dijk

entry.summary: For DP-SGD with random allocation (each record used once per epoch at a random step), the authors derive a closed-form formula bounding the accuracy of any membership inference attack on the trained model, via chi-square divergence between a Gaussian and a dominating mixture. This replaces numerical privacy accounting search with a one-line noise calibration rule.

entry.title: Dual-QK: Sharp Queries and Flat Keys for Prunable 2-bit KV Caches

author.name: Sunjoo Whang, Jungjun Oh, Minsung Kim, Dongho Seo, Jisu Shin, Gregory Kielian, Hoi-Jun Yoo, Sangjin Kim

entry.summary: Dual-QK resolves a conflict between rotation-based KV cache quantization and query-channel pruning by using paired non-orthogonal query and key transforms, combining 2-bit quantization with key-cache read reduction. Calibrated query and key statistics allow sharp query energy concentration while keeping computational invariance.

entry.title: A Drosophila Whole-Connectome Network Can Learn Human-Designed Cognitive Tasks

author.name: Joonghui Cho, Minchan Kang, Daeshik Kim

entry.summary: The study uses the MaleCNS v1.0 Drosophila whole-connectome as a fixed recurrent topology, learning only one scalar per anatomical edge, and shows 92.77% accuracy on held-out addition versus 67.93% for degree-preserving rewired controls, plus performance on a grounded language task. This suggests biological wiring diagrams carry computational structure beyond evolved behaviors.

entry.title: WxFM-XL: Adapting Univariate Foundation Models to Multi-Station Weather Forecasting

author.name: Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, Rongwen Li, Hongwu Liu, Kenli Li

entry.summary: WxFM-XL adapts univariate time series foundation models (like Sundial and Timer) to multi-station weather forecasting by introducing a cross-station error correlation prior graph that captures station-specific error priors and spatial information. This addresses factors overlooked by existing multivariate extensions of time series foundation models.

entry.title: ProtocolMatch: Protocol-Dependent Model Selection for Scientific Dynamics Forecasting

author.name: Lu Wei, Yufeng Wang, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: ProtocolMatch formulates protocol-dependent model selection for scientific dynamics forecasting, accounting for observed history, rollout feedback, compute budget, and test distribution. On quantum-spin dynamics, model rankings (e.g., causal attention vs recurrence) reverse as training set size grows, and a linear predictor can beat attention models under matched compute.

entry.title: Revisiting Explainable AI through Model-Independent Concept Dictionaries

author.name: Thomas Schnake, Doreen Sch\"oppenthau, Alexander Meyer, Jacques Corbeil, Klaus-Robert M\"uller, Gr\'egoire Montavon

entry.summary: DictXAI defines concepts directly in the input domain via a large overcomplete dictionary of interpretable elements, computing a sparse code of the input and attributing predictions to these interpretable concepts, avoiding reliance on architecture-specific internal abstractions. The author list includes leading XAI researchers Muller and Montavon.

entry.title: Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning for Multichain MDPs: A Hierarchical Decomposition Approach

author.name: Huizhen Yu, Isaiah Heidt

entry.summary: This paper proposes an asynchronous value-iteration-based RL algorithm for average-reward multichain MDPs, using Bather's decomposition to hierarchically partition the state space into communicating subsystems and transient states. The authors prove convergence to optimal gain and gain-optimal policies without model knowledge beyond the transition graph.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Tri-Hybrid Multi-User MIMO Precoding: The Blessing of EM-Reconfigurable Antennas

author.name: Kaijun Feng, Jiaxin He, Hongrui Yu, Zhen Gao, Anwen Liao, Ziwei Wan, Zhaocheng Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose Tri-PNet, a Conformer-based neural network for joint EM-domain, analog, and digital precoding in wideband multi-user MIMO-OFDM systems using EM-reconfigurable antennas. The approach adds an electromagnetic degree of freedom to conventional hybrid precoding, substantially improving spectral efficiency.

entry.title: Learning Transition Kernels of Jump-Diffusion Processes with Conditional Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuzhen Zhao, Yating Liu, Quentin Guibert

entry.summary: The authors learn transition kernels of time-homogeneous jump-diffusion processes using conditional diffusion models trained on trajectory data, establishing non-asymptotic bounds for score estimation error and KL divergence between true and generated path laws. They validate on synthetic benchmarks and real-world data.

entry.title: Closing the Loop on Contrail Avoidance with Satellite Verification

author.name: Spandan Ghose Chowdhury

entry.summary: This work builds a small 8.4M-parameter diffusion model to detect contrails in satellite imagery, a critical verification step for contrail avoidance programs since rerouted flights only count if satellites confirm no contrail formed. The model achieves 0.476 PR-AUC versus 0.414 for a DeepLabV3+ baseline on this extremely sparse, hard detection task. The paper also runs careful ablations identifying which components matter, including resolution effects.

entry.title: Constitution-Guided Watermarking

author.name: Toluwani Aremu, Samuele Poppi, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: Constitution-Guided Watermarking is a framework that selects request-appropriate trade-offs among watermark strength, text quality, robustness, and forgery resistance, rather than imposing a single operating point on all requests. This lets providers preserve wording quality where it matters and ensure attribution robustness where needed. The work addresses real tensions in deploying LLM watermarking at scale.

entry.title: Optimal Regret for Online Market Making with Limit Order Book

author.name: Maria Elena Vischi, Francesco Emanuele Stradi, Alberto Marchesi

entry.summary: The paper improves regret guarantees for online market making under a limit-order-book feedback model where trader valuations are revealed only when no transaction occurs. Against adversarial market prices, it establishes a high-probability regret bound of order sqrt(T), improving the prior O(T^(2/3)) result. Achieving the optimal rate makes this a significant theoretical tightening.

entry.title: Origins of Universal Machine Learning Force-Field Errors in Multicomponent Materials

author.name: Hongwei Du, Dingyang Lv, Baole Wei, Yu Ren, Feng Yu, Xin He, Bonan Zhu, Yongda Huang, Yongheng Li, Jianjun Liu, Siqi Shi, Hong Wang, Ziheng Lu

entry.summary: The paper builds a benchmark of 7,599 multicomponent configurations inspired by high-entropy design and evaluates eleven pretrained universal machine learning force fields against DFT for energies, forces, stresses, and derived properties. Error analysis links failures to training-reference coverage, local geometric heterogeneity, and elemental response. This provides actionable diagnostics for where universal interatomic potentials fail in materials design.

entry.title: Towards Calibrated Probabilistic Forecasts for Events of Interest via Outcome-Conditional Recalibration

author.name: Jakob Benjamin Wessel, Sam Allen

entry.summary: The authors introduce outcome-conditional recalibration, a post-hoc method that recalibrates probabilistic predictions restricted to user-defined regions of the outcome space, such as extreme events. This addresses the problem that popular recalibration schemes can hide miscalibration in outcome regions that matter most for downstream decisions.

entry.title: Safe Meta-Policy Design with Risk Control

author.name: Wenbin Zhou, Michael Lingzhi Li, Shixiang Zhu

entry.summary: The authors address the problem of deciding when to deploy retrained models, planning policy updates to balance expected improvement against the risk of regression. Their offline meta-policy maximizes cumulative value under a budget on the expected number of harmful updates, using historical learning trajectories, a DAG formulation, and dynamic programming. A signal-to-noise analysis characterizes when improvement can be detected.

entry.title: Steering Follows Geometry, Not Labels: Emotion Directions in a Full-Duplex Speech Model

author.name: Pulak Kuli

entry.summary: This paper studies emotion steering in Moshi, a fully open full-duplex speech language model, using mean-difference activation steering with only per-frame vector additions and no retraining. It shows emotion is linearly decodable from the residual stream, but steering effectiveness is governed by representational geometry rather than label structure. The work extends activation steering from TTS and turn-based models to real-time duplex agents.

entry.title: LLM4Impact: Integrating Heterogeneous Information for Scientific Impact Prediction

author.name: Yong Cao, Markus Flicke, Haoyu He, Katrin Renz, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: LLM4Impact predicts the future scientific impact of newly published papers by integrating semantic, graph, LLM, and temporal evidence, injecting graph information into a frozen LLM via continuous prefix tokens. A context-aware gating mechanism adaptively weights evidence sources and a calibration module accounts for their differing predictive roles.

entry.title: EmphTTS: an emphasis-control TTS with reinforcement learning

author.name: Zirui Li, Rech Silas, Lauri Juvela, Tom Backstrom, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: EmphTTS is a non-autoregressive TTS system that applies GRPO to the duration predictor with an emphasis localization reward, enabling direct RL-based optimization of word-level emphasis control. Evaluations show best-in-class emphasis controllability compared to prior approaches.

entry.title: PanoPed: Beyond Bounding Boxes for Sim-to-Real Panoramic Pedestrian Tracking

author.name: Qinfeng Zhu, Weiguang Zhao, Yunxi Jiang, Anh Nguyen, Lei Fan

entry.summary: PanoPed is a sim-to-real benchmark for pedestrian tracking on the full sphere, addressing the limitation that planar bounding boxes cannot fully describe a person's location on a panoramic image. It includes 108,000 synthetic frames across fixed, quadruped, and drone cameras plus 28,002 real frames, and proposes a sextant-inspired representation leveraging the detector's visual query to recover spherical position.

entry.title: StyleFields: Multi-Scale AdaIN-Modulated Implicit SDFs for Coarse-to-Fine 3D Shape Reconstruction and Editing

author.name: Ehsan Garaaghaji, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua, Doruk Oner

entry.summary: StyleFields is a DeepSDF-based architecture enabling controllable geometric style mixing, combining the coarse structure of one object with fine details of another via depth-aware multi-level AdaIN latent injection and coarse-to-fine supervision with progressive depth growth. It achieves content-style decoupling without part labels or adversarial training.

entry.title: trACT: temporal revelation Airborne Camera Trap

author.name: Oliver Bimber, Rakesh John Amala Arokia Nathan, Mohamed Youssef, Vinayak Lal Bhatnagar, Ralf Berger, Klaus Hackl\"ander

entry.summary: Introduces trACT, a lightweight real-time framework for consumer drones that isolates target motion from severe environmental clutter using Temporal Max Pooling over rolling windows plus self-supervised motion anomaly detection, inspired by hovering birds of prey. It targets wildlife monitoring and surveillance under camouflage, vegetation motion, and system latency.

entry.title: From Global Alignment to Local Grounding: Zero-Shot Chinese Character Recognition with Radical Verification

author.name: Yu-Heng Shih, Bing-Chen Wu, Tsz-To Wong, Ting-En Yen, Hong-Han Shuai, Bin-Hua Hsieh, Chien-An Chen, Yi-Ren Yeh, Ching-Chun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes moving beyond single global image-IDS similarity in zero-shot Chinese character recognition by adding local radical grounding and verification, since global matching often retrieves the correct character but fails to rank it first when characters differ in subtle radicals. The method exploits compositional structure and spatial radical layout.

entry.title: Gaussian Material Fields for Volumetric Multi-Energy CT Decomposition

author.name: Jian Lin, Jiancheng Fang, Hongming Shan, Shaoyu Wang, Yang Chen, Qiegen Liu

entry.summary: This work introduces Gaussian material fields, which represent multiple material distributions in multi-energy CT using shared anisotropic 3D Gaussian primitives with independent nonnegative material coefficients. The shared spatial basis with material-specific coefficients enables volumetric material decomposition that preserves compositional and structural differences.

entry.title: SoccerNet-FoulRet: Retrieving Semantically Similar Soccer Foul Videos

author.name: Jacobus Arthur, Ahmad Sait, Batool Hani, Merey Ramazanova, Jan Held, Marc Van Droogenbroeck, Bernard Ghanem, Anthony Cioppa, Silvio Giancola

entry.summary: SoccerNet-FoulRet is the first benchmark for semantic foul retrieval in soccer, where given a query foul the task is to retrieve past fouls that are relevant precedents for refereeing decisions, regardless of visual appearance. It builds on SoccerNet-MVFoul and evaluates zero-shot video and vision-language embedders plus task-specific fine-tuned models.

entry.title: Concentration, Not Uncertainty: Why Targeted Synthetic Data Doesn't Help Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Akshat Dobhal, Sanjay Singh

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether uncertainty-guided targeting of synthetic data generation improves camouflaged object detection under a fixed generation budget. Across 103 training runs and five controls, the authors find that uncertainty-based allocation does not outperform random allocation, and attribute the failure to a concentration effect in targeted regions. It matters because it challenges a common intuition about how to allocate synthetic data resources.

entry.title: Geometry-Supervised Visual Representation Learning for Multi-Phenotype Lesion Interpretation in Medical VLMs

author.name: Hao Wang, Qiwei Zeng, Shuchang Ye, Jinghao Lin, Yuezhe Yang, Yige Peng, Jinman Kim, Lei Bi

entry.summary: This paper addresses the problem that medical vision-language models fail to preserve anatomical hierarchies and relationships among pathological phenotypes because their visual alignment relies solely on semantic supervision without geometric constraints. The authors propose a geometry-supervised representation learning approach for interpreting lesions that require joint assessment of multiple pathological phenotypes. This could improve clinical diagnostic reliability of medical VLMs on complex multi-phenotype cases.

entry.title: When to Unpair: Regulating Pairing Dependence in Medical Visual In-Context Learning

author.name: Cheng Wan, Chenjun Li, Qingyu Zhao

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses over-reliance on individual image-label pairings in visual in-context learning for medical imaging using a test-time derangement that shuffles support labels while preserving the label multiset. The resulting pairing gap reveals that all four released models depend on pairings to varying degrees, exposing spurious support-associated regions, lesion-size biases, and sensitivity to mis-registered supports. The authors propose regulation of pairing dependence to improve robustness.

entry.title: A Review Of Robotic World Models For Dynamic Environments Based On Factor And Scene Graphs

author.name: Marco Giberna, Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas, Jose Luis Sanchez Lopez, Holger Voos

entry.summary: This is a survey of graph-based robotic world models, covering factor graphs for uncertainty-aware geometric estimation and scene graphs for semantic abstraction, with a focus on extending static representations to dynamic environments. It organizes a fast-growing literature that is central to modern robot autonomy and world modeling.

entry.title: geodex: A Library for Motion Planning on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Phone Thiha Kyaw, Ben Wei, Sepehr Samavi, Miguel Angel Rogel Garcia, Jonathan Kelly

entry.summary: geodex is an open-source C++20 library (with Python bindings) for motion planning that respects the intrinsic Riemannian geometry of a robot configuration space, including configuration-dependent metrics, while planning around obstacles. It fills a gap between manifold-optimization libraries, which lack obstacle-aware planning, and general planners, which treat geometry only via flat metrics.

entry.title: SiGNgapore - An Interactive Dataset for Sign-based Visual Navigation

author.name: Nicky Zimmerman, Joel Loo, Zishuo Wang, David Hsu

entry.summary: SiGNgapore is a dataset collected across public spaces in Singapore with RGB, sparse depth, odometry, and IMU data focused on navigational-sign-centric decision making for mapless navigation, including 56 long-horizon missions and over 450 sign-centric scenarios. It supports research on robots exploiting human-designed navigational aids without prebuilt maps.

entry.title: Design optimization of tendon-driven robots considering tendon wrapping and shortcut

author.name: Yuta Sahara, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: This paper formulates multi-objective optimization of tendon-driven arm design, jointly maximizing joint torque and minimizing arm thickness by exploiting tendon wrapping and shortcut effects, solved with NSGA-II. The resulting Pareto-optimal routings reveal non-obvious design patterns and offer practical guidelines for compact high-torque arms.

entry.title: Distributed Motion Planning for Multi-Robot Systems under Topological Constraints

author.name: Gianpietro Battocletti, Dimitris Boskos, Dimos V. Dimarogonas, Bart De Schutter

entry.summary: The authors propose an MPC-based distributed controller that executes braid-based topological constraints for multi-robot coordination, replacing prior generator-by-generator approaches that produced slow, suboptimal trajectories. This enables compact specification of qualitative coordination patterns with improved execution quality.

entry.title: Graph-monotone entrywise guarantees for MLE and Rank Centrality on general comparison graphs

author.name: Yuepeng Yang, Cong Ma

entry.summary: This statistics paper proves high-probability entrywise error guarantees for maximum likelihood estimation and Rank Centrality under the Bradley-Terry-Luce model on arbitrary fixed comparison graphs, with rates governed by the algebraic connectivity of the count-weighted observation graph. The graph-monotone guarantee handles the irregular, heterogeneous sampling common in real comparison data, not just uniform sampling.

entry.title: sk-bench: A Native-First Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Slovak

author.name: Marek \v{S}uppa, Ivan Vykopal, Andrej Ridzik, Kristi\'an Sopkovi\v{c}, Nat\'alia K\v{n}a\v{z}ekov\'a, Jaroslav Kop\v{c}an, Miroslav Bl\v{s}t\'ak, Vikt\'oria Ondrejov\'a, Daniel Hl\'adek, Michal Gregor, Martin Tamajka, Mari\'an \v{S}imko

entry.summary: sk-bench provides a native-first Slovak benchmark with 30 datasets across ten skill categories, introducing eleven new resources including Slovak-adapted instruction checkers, and evaluates 55 open- and closed-weight models under one harness. Findings include a 12.6-point gap between the best open model and proprietary APIs, and high ranking correlation between native and translated data.

entry.title: MIRROR: From Imitation to Internalization in LLM Personalization

author.name: Huayi Lai, Jicheng Yang, Min Yi, Chong Meng

entry.summary: Introduces MIRROR, a self-distillation framework shifting LLM personalization from style imitation to preference internalization by aligning the model's next-token distributions along its own generation trajectories with its reference-conditioned self. This replaces reference-token imitation with reference-revealed on-policy self-distillation.

entry.title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Near-Optimal Offline Attacks on Warm-Start Bandits with Bounded Rewards

author.name: Qirun Zeng, Manhin Poon, Xiangxiang Dai, Qixin Zhang, Jinhang Zuo

entry.summary: The paper studies offline attacks on warm-start bandits where an attacker injects only valid action-reward pairs into pre-deployment history, modeling realistic manipulation like fake reviews that promote a target rather than suppress alternatives. It proves that when the target arm lies near the lower reward boundary, any order-optimal-cost attack on UCB must allocate nonvanishing cost to the target arm, and constructs matching attack algorithms. This is foundational theory for understanding data-poisoning of sequential decision systems.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Key-Layer KV Communication for Efficient Latent Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Dongsen Zhang, Peipei Li, Zekun Li, Wenjun Xu

entry.summary: KITE is a training-free framework for latent communication between LLM-based multi-agent systems that shifts the goal from sender-side KV-state fidelity to receiver-side task sufficiency. It identifies task-relevant key layers to transmit, reducing the communication and computation overhead of existing KV-based latent communication methods that carry redundant internal states. This improves the efficiency of multi-agent LLM collaboration, an increasingly common deployment pattern.

entry.title: ORACLE: Optimizer-Relative Alignment for Constrained LEarning

author.name: Utkarsh Grover, Wyatt Mackey, Kaixun Hua, J. Morris Chang, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: ORACLE reformulates constrained learning by assessing constraint compatibility on the optimizer's realized post-update step rather than the pre-optimizer gradient, using joint endpoint linearization of heterogeneous constraint families and committing corrections only after validation. It is evaluated across eight PDE benchmarks.

entry.title: FedRSPO+: A Heterogeneity-aware Algorithm for Decision-focused Federated Learning

author.name: Konstantinos Ziliaskopoulos, Alexander Vinel, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: FedRSPO+ combines decision-focused learning with federated cross-silo training, using a regularized predict-then-optimize surrogate (RSPO+) to smooth the discontinuous decision map and handle heterogeneity in downstream objectives and feasible sets across clients. This stabilizes client updates and aggregation in polyhedral optimization settings.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Plasticity: PDE Solvers That Reshape Themselves

author.name: Chun-Wun Cheng, Bingcheng Hu, Angelica I. Aviles-Rivero

entry.summary: The paper introduces physics-informed neural plasticity, where PDE solver representations adaptively reshape during training via local enrichment and residual-directed splitting, instantiated as ReCAP. This addresses capacity mismatch in heterogeneous PDE solutions, where fixed representations waste capacity on easy regions and starve hard ones.

entry.title: MUNITE: Unified Multimodal Latent Inference for Any-to-Any Multimodal Generation

author.name: Kyeongmin Yeo, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: MUNITE is a latent-variable framework for any-to-any multimodal generation that unifies encoding and latent generation as conditional inference over a shared latent, within a single conditional flow model. Full observations recover deterministic encoding while partial subsets define conditional latent inference, with modality-specific decoders capturing remaining uncertainty.

entry.title: A Unified Information-Theoretic Approach to Constrained Multi-Fidelity Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Rikuto Matsumoto, Masanori Ishikura, Masayuki Karasuyama

entry.summary: This paper unifies multi-objective, constrained, and multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization by measuring query utility as information gain about the highest-fidelity feasible Pareto frontier, deriving a tractable variational lower bound using under- and over-truncated approximations. This yields a cost-aware acquisition function without separate fidelity heuristics.

entry.title: NeuralBES: A Differentiable, Control-Aware Emulator for Scalable Building Energy Modeling

author.name: Ting-Yu Dai, Takuya Kurihana, Wing Yee Au, Hon Yung Wong

entry.summary: NeuralBES is a differentiable building energy emulator parameterizing an RC-based thermal model with a shared neural encoder that maps static building metadata to physical parameters, balancing EnergyPlus-style fidelity with data-driven scalability. It supports demand-side flexibility applications like load forecasting and shifting across heterogeneous building stocks.

entry.title: Sparsifying Stochasticity, Not Capacity: Partial Stochasticity via Deep Weight Factorization of Prior Scales

author.name: Marius P Linhard, Maurizio Filippone

entry.summary: The paper learns which Bayesian neural network parameters should remain stochastic by applying deep weight factorization to prior scales, fitting the functional prior to a Gaussian process with an MMD objective; parameters whose prior scales fall below a cutoff become deterministic. It provides a linear-time checkable certificate for universal conditional density approximation plus a repair mechanism. This reframes Bayesian network design as selecting which parameters need uncertainty rather than shrinking capacity.

entry.title: Dataset Pruning from First Principles: A Label-Free Linear Programming Approach

author.name: Rodrigo Schuller, Francisco Ganacim

entry.summary: The paper derives dataset pruning criteria from first principles by reformulating unbiased subset selection as variance minimization, ensuring unweighted subset averages recover full-dataset statistics in expectation. The authors characterize a family of unbiased selection algorithms as a high-dimensional polytope with linear variance objectives, avoiding the proximity assumptions of embedding-space geometry methods.

entry.title: Goldsmith: Gold-Loss-Guided Definition Optimization with an Agentic Annotation Harness

author.name: Yihan Li, Hanyi Zhang, Xiaoxi Jiang, Man Guo

entry.summary: Goldsmith is an agentic pipeline that converts a small expert-annotated gold set into a reusable structured annotation definition by treating the definition as a trainable textual object. Candidate definitions are scored with an executable structured loss, and an LLM editor converts high-loss failures into textual-gradient revisions accepted only when measured loss improves. The harness externalizes schema, retrieval, judging, and human review.

entry.title: Finding the Right Balance: Relevance and Diversity in LLM Retrieval

author.name: Guillaume Brouillette (Universit\'e du Qu\'ebec \`a Trois-Rivi\`eres, Trois-Rivi\`eres, Canada), Faustin Kagabo (Universit\'e du Qu\'ebec \`a Trois-Rivi\`eres, Trois-Rivi\`eres, Canada), Usef Faghihi (Universit\'e du Qu\'ebec \`a Trois-Rivi\`eres, Trois-Rivi\`eres, Canada), Nadia Ghazzali (Universit\'e du Qu\'ebec \`a Trois-Rivi\`eres, Trois-Rivi\`eres, Canada)

entry.summary: This study shows that the effectiveness of retrieval diversification in RAG depends primarily on candidate-pool redundancy: it harms clean pools but helps multi-evidence tasks where redundancy causes repeated passage selection. The authors introduce a query-adaptive rule that diversifies only when the effective number of distinct evidence pieces warrants it.

entry.title: OverLay++: Dense-Overlap Layout-to-Image Generation Dataset

author.name: Shivansh Aggarwal, Shresth Grover, Divyansh Srivastava, Haiyang Xu, Bingnan Li, Xiang Zhang, Ethan J. Armand, Chuan Li, Jianwen Xie, Zhuowen Tu

entry.summary: OverLay++ is a large-scale layout-to-image generation dataset with about 500K images averaging 6.6 objects each, 1.67 times denser in annotations than prior datasets, plus object captions over six times longer. It targets the bottleneck that existing training data lacks dense, complex object overlaps and interactions.

entry.title: Spatial Latent Reasoning for Embodied Reference Understanding

author.name: Ling Li, Jianhui Zhong, Wei Liu, Zheng Jiang aand Yuxuan Liu, Jingyu Li, Zhidong Deng

entry.summary: Proposes SLR, a framework for pointing-gesture visual grounding that structures continuous latent reasoning as an ordered sequence of geometric and visual states, starting from a spatial ray state supervised by fingertip position and direction. Parity pooling constructs visual targets by averaging region tokens on interleaved spatial supports.

entry.title: LiG-DETR: Local-in-Global Reassembly in Latent Space for Aerial Object Detection

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Fangzhuo Gao, Juntao Cheng, Ziyi Zhao, Liang Wan, Ruize Han

entry.summary: LiG-DETR tackles aerial object detection where small objects suffer from downsampling while large objects need global context. It acquires high-fidelity local evidence before feature degradation and reassembles it with global representations in latent space within a unified end-to-end DETR framework, avoiding the post-processing of image-slicing approaches.

entry.title: Counterfactual Route Optimization for Gaussian Head Avatar Modeling

author.name: Shikun Zhang, Yong Li, Yiqun Wang, Qiuhong Ke, Cunjian Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes counterfactual route optimization for Gaussian head avatar modeling, which selects optimization directions based on the realized effects of alternative short-horizon update routes from the current training state rather than fixed loss weights or handcrafted schedules. This adaptively handles state-dependent preferences among geometry, appearance, and cross-view consistency objectives.

entry.title: Hard, Yet Reducible: Controlled Forward Transfer for Synthetic Degradation Curation

author.name: Chunming He, Kailai Zhou, Jiaming Zuo, Hanqi Liu, Fengyang Xiao, Youwei Pang, Xiaofeng Liu, Weisi Lin, Xiaoqi Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes the controlled Reducible Degradation Gap (cRDG), a metric for estimating the training utility of synthetic degradations in dense prediction tasks. It uses budget-matched probe trainings from a common checkpoint to isolate genuine generalization gains from confounds like deteriorating clean performance. This gives practitioners a principled way to curate synthetic augmentation data under finite budgets.

entry.title: One-Shot Adaptive Segmentation For Scientific Images

author.name: Tejaswi V. Panchagnula, Allison M. Davis, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents a training-free, one-shot segmentation framework that adapts vision foundation models using a single annotated reference image. It combines DINOv3 representations with background-adaptive feature orthogonalization to suppress artifacts, then uses cosine similarity to localize candidate regions for SAM segmentation. Evaluated on red-blood-cell microscopy, pool boiling imaging, and chest radiography, it improves mean IoU substantially over the strongest baseline.

entry.title: Explicit Geometric Chain-of-Thought for Vision-Language-Action in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xingtai Gui, Yucheng Zhou, Dongqian Guo, Jiahao Gong, Feiyang Tan, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: GeoCoTDrive tackles the mismatch in driving VLA models between 2D semantic reasoning and the precise 3D geometry driving actions require. It follows a think-in-2D-drive-with-3D paradigm: grounding decision-critical 2D regions, retrieving localized 3D priors from a geometric foundation model within those regions, and injecting them into planning. This explicit geometric chain-of-thought aims to improve planning reliability in autonomous driving.

entry.title: GRACE: Generation-aware latent compression for efficient video generation

author.name: Jiyoung Kim, Paul Hyunbin Cho, Jisu Nam, Donghoon Lee, Hyunsung Go, Yeonkyeong Lee, Hansaem Kim, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: GRACE tackles the tension in highly compressed video autoencoders, where higher compression degrades reconstruction and shifting latents away from the distribution a pretrained DiT was trained on forces costly retraining or adaptation. The paper proposes generation-aware latent compression that preserves compatibility with the DiT's learned latent distribution while compressing. This enables faster video diffusion inference with fewer tokens.

entry.title: Lifelong small-object navigation in changing object layouts: a benchmark and method

author.name: Jiagan Huang, Zikun Zhou, Zijian Ni, Hongpeng Wang, Guangming Lu, Jun Yu, Wenjie Pei

entry.summary: The paper formulates LiSoNav-COL, a task where household robots repeatedly navigate to small, occluded, and frequently relocated objects while accumulating and updating scene memory starting from empty. It provides both a benchmark and a method addressing viewpoint seeking, memory reuse, and memory updating after object relocation.

entry.title: Fast Planning for Multi-object Multi-target Throwing

author.name: Zhengming Zhu, Yang Liu, Xiao Gao, Aude Billard

entry.summary: The authors develop a two-stage planner for throwing multiple objects to multiple targets in a single swipe, targeting logistics and warehouse automation throughput. An offline model of the feasible set combines object flight dynamics with robot kinematics and dynamics, enabling fast online generation of feasible throwing motions.

entry.title: Making Task Abstractions Executable: Control-Aware Layout Repair for a Fixed Controller

author.name: Chiyoung Kim, Seungyeon Back, Sumin Shim, Doyoung Heo, Rita Singh

entry.summary: This work compiles task-level requirements (tracking, clearance, actuation) into auditable affine layout constraints and repairs only the continuous spatial coordinates of a task abstraction so that a fixed agent and controller can execute it, preserving event order, timing, and topology. It provides conditional finite-certification and validates with 300 paired rollouts across three tasks.

entry.title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference

author.name: David Broska, Michael Howes

entry.summary: This paper extends prediction-powered inference (PPI) to settings with cluster dependence, providing closed-form standard errors and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for partially labeled clustered data without bootstrap resampling. This matters because PPI's ML-prediction-boosted efficiency claims break down, yielding undercovering intervals, when within-cluster correlation is ignored.

entry.title: Stale, Misattributed, or Late: Where Personal Memory Fails Before Generation

author.name: Haonan Deng, Park Sinchaisri

entry.summary: This paper measures pre-generation failures in personal memory for language agents — stale values, facts about the wrong person, or late retrieval — using Personal Fact Memory as a reference layer. On a controlled revision benchmark, serving only active values of correctly keyed slots eliminated stale exposure, while without update resolution 70.3% of prompts exposed superseded values. It localizes memory failures to construction and retrieval stages before generation.

entry.title: Personalize at Test Time: Learning User Preferences for Image Generation

author.name: Jiamu Bai, Jiaming Hu, Yanhong Wu, Zellux Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes learning personalized reward models for image generation directly from a user's historical preference pairs, compressing hundreds of visual attributes into 50 attribute-anchored dimensions via an autoencoder and training an evaluator on them. This avoids costly manual annotation or VLM-based extraction from interaction histories. It enables test-time personalization of diffusion model outputs to individual tastes.

entry.title: From Pixel to Coding: Evaluating the Figure Reproduction Capabilities of MLLMs

author.name: Zijian Chen, Zhengyu Chen, Bohan Liang, Lirong Deng, Yushuo Zheng, Yanwei Jiang, Qi Jia, Kaiwei Zhang, Wenjun Zhang, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: FigCodeBench is a new benchmark evaluating whether multimodal LLMs can perceive complex visual structures in figures and reproduce them as precise, executable code, unifying visual comprehension and code generation that prior benchmarks test in isolation. It addresses shortcomings of existing visual code-generation benchmarks that use simplified single-environment layouts. This fills a real evaluation gap for unified multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: REFIT: Recognize, Fix, and Test Wearable Sensor Placement Shifts without Labels

author.name: Bangxun Tang

entry.summary: REFIT calibrates frozen activity-recognition models when wearable sensors are worn differently at deployment than in training, identifying axis transform families (reflections, rotations) that best match user statistics to training data and applying the inferred correction without labels or retraining. It also includes a mechanism to test the fixed model.

entry.title: Domain-informed Adaptive Sampling for Generalizable PINNs in Metal Additive Manufacturing via Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Hyeonsu Lee, Jihoon Jeong

entry.summary: The paper provides an empirical-risk-minimization analysis showing process-condition-aware adaptive sampling is strictly better than static collocation sampling for PINN generalization, and proposes conditional flow matching-based adaptive sampling for thermal modeling in metal additive manufacturing. This improves cross-condition generalization of physics-informed surrogate models.

entry.title: Self-attention summary networks for subsurface velocity-model building from common-image gathers

author.name: Shiqin Zeng, Yunlin Zeng, Abhinav Prakash Gahlot, Zijun Deng, Felix J. Herrmann

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multiscale self-attention summary network that compresses high-dimensional 3D common-image gathers into compact embeddings preserving offset-dependent kinematic structure, which then condition a flow-matching posterior sampler for probabilistic subsurface velocity inversion. This turns CIGs from diagnostic artifacts into informative inversion inputs.

entry.title: CHASE: Channel-Aligned Structure Exploitation for Geometry-Aware Model Engineering

author.name: Wei Wang, Wei Jiang, Ziran Liu

entry.summary: CHASE operationalizes Geometric and Spectral Alignment (GSA) across six applications including parameter-efficient finetuning, pruning compensation, model merging, shared KV attention heads, and model compression. Several new methods (CORA, COEC, CORAM, CAGA, SAK) exploit spectral structure for practical model engineering.

entry.title: TR-PTQ: High-Accuracy Integer-Only Transformer Post Training Quantization via Taylor Region Reformulation

author.name: Eliyahu Levy, Adam Teman, Yoni Pugachov

entry.summary: TR-PTQ attributes transformer quantization loss to normalization scale parameters and compounded GELU approximation error rather than low precision, with SoftMax found inherently robust. It introduces a unified integer-only formulation using shared Taylor Region exponential and logarithm primitives, avoiding floating-point fallbacks.

entry.title: Adversarial RL for Port-Scan Evasion: Attacker Feature Visibility in Edge-Deployed IDS

author.name: Logan Andrew North, Priya Sanjay Kaluskar, Shasi Kumar Ramachandran Prabhu, Peilong Li, Suman Saha

entry.summary: The paper uses a Deep Q-Network adversary to study adaptive port-scan evasion against ML-based intrusion detection systems (XGBoost, MLP, 1D-CNN) deployed on a Raspberry Pi, comparing black-box, gray-box, and white-box feature visibility settings. It highlights robustness gaps in IoT IDS evaluation against adaptive rather than static attackers.

entry.title: Reproducible LLM Inference Benchmarking: A Sequential Isolation Protocol for Regression Testing

author.name: Arnold Olympio, Juan Manuel Servera Bondroit, Wael Abdelmalek, Guang Lu, Jo\~ao Carvalho

entry.summary: The paper presents a Sequential Isolation Methodology for reproducible LLM inference benchmarking and regression testing, reducing the coefficient of variation from 15.2 percent to 2.2 percent across six context sizes and eight concurrency levels using vLLM on an A100. Reproducible performance measurement is a chronic pain point for serving systems. The protocol offers a practical standard for comparing inference stacks reliably.

entry.title: Kinetic Langevin Meets Split Gibbs: Accelerated Posterior Sampling for Imaging Inverse Problems with Diffusion Priors

author.name: Dai Hai Nguyen, Duc Dung Nguyen
