entry.summary: This preregistered study dissects where harness-search score gains come from, using three models, three benchmarks, a GEPA search arm, and six injected evaluation defects across 47 reported endpoints. It finds apparent gains often stem from previously unreadable parser outputs or weak baselines rather than genuine improvements.

entry.title: HLA-WM: Hybrid Linear Attention for Long-Horizon Video World Models

author.name: Zhuokun Chen, Feng Chen, Xi Lin, Xiyu Wu, Jiahao He, Jianfei Cai, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: HLA-WM is a training-free hybrid attention framework for long-horizon video world models that identifies severe long-range forgetting in Gated DeltaNet-style recurrent linear attention and fixes it by combining geometry-guided retrieval of distant scenes with fine-grained linear-state computation. The approach exploits GDN's affine structure to cache retrieved states, preserving scene consistency at low memory cost.

entry.title: HuatuoGPT-3: RL-Only Domain Adaptation from Base Models

author.name: Junying Chen, Xinyuan Xie, Ziniu Li, Wenyuan Gu, Jianquan Li, Xiang Wan, Guangjun Yu, Ruoyu Sun, Haizhou Li, Benyou Wang

entry.summary: HuatuoGPT-3 demonstrates that a general base LLM can be adapted to a specialized domain, specifically medicine, using reinforcement learning alone rather than the standard SFT-then-RL pipeline. The authors identify two failure modes of pure and mixed-policy RL, Gradient Starvation and Teacher-Distribution Anchoring, and propose One-stage Policy Optimization (OnePO) to address them. This challenges assumptions about the necessity of supervised fine-tuning cold starts.

entry.title: AgentSpy: Making AI Agent Behavior Observable

author.name: Christoph B\"uhler, Matteo Biagiola, Luca Di Grazia, Guido Salvaneschi

entry.summary: AgentSpy observes LLM agents from outside their own reporting by running them in isolated environments and recording system calls and network traffic of the agent and all subprocesses. Built on a declarative specification, it supports conformance and behavioral analyses that catch actions the agent's trajectory log omits. This improves transparency and auditability of agents that execute shell commands, file operations, and network access with user privileges.

entry.title: Symmetry and AI-assisted discovery of magic-state factories

author.name: Shubham P. Jain, Adam Wills, Shraddha Singh

entry.summary: This paper develops symmetry-restricted and AI-assisted search methods for discovering magic-state distillation circuits at distance three and above, a regime previously intractable. It introduces a unified binary-matrix formulation covering both triorthogonal-code and direct circuit searches, showing distance-three conditions reduce to distinct nonzero syndromes. This matters because magic-state distillation is a dominant cost in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

entry.title: When Does External Guidance Help LLM Reasoning? A Bias-Variance Theory of Guidance-Augmented GRPO

author.name: Sofia Torres, Gabriel Almeida, Carter Adams, Camila Rocha

entry.summary: Develops GA-GRPO, a unified theoretical framework treating external guidance in RL with verifiable rewards (expert traces, self-explanations, retrieved patterns) as a stochastic operator rewriting the question distribution, analyzed as a biased on-policy estimator. The work provides convergence rates, bias bounds, and an optimal weighting rule that prior empirical methods like LUFFY and ExPO lacked.

entry.title: Identifiable World Models from Pretrained Diffusion Representations

author.name: Ruchi Sandilya, Conor Liston, Logan Grosenick

entry.summary: Shows that identifiability guarantees from auxiliary-variable nonlinear ICA can be transferred to frozen pretrained diffusion models via a lightweight alignment map (ConDA), identifying latent dynamical states up to benign transformations without retraining the generative backbone. This connects diffusion-based world models to causal representation learning theory.

entry.title: Inference and learning in sparse autoencoders as natural gradient flow

author.name: Hadi Vafaii, Tejas Rao, David Chanin, Thomas Fel, Jacob L. Yates, Bruno Olshausen, David Klindt, Dileep George, Miguel L\'azaro-Gredilla

entry.summary: The paper unifies SAE inference and dictionary learning as natural-gradient flows on a shared variational free energy, instantiated as BeFOND, an encoder-free sparse coding model with closed-form inference and learning. Recurrent explaining away reduces interference between overlapping features while Fisher preconditioning speeds learning of rare features, improving dictionary recovery on synthetic data. Strong author list spanning Olshausen, Klindt, and Vicarious/Mountcastle researchers.

entry.title: Fork-and-Flush: Escaping Idea Basins in Autoresearch Agents

author.name: Ziyang Cai, Christos Ziakas, Vasilis Kontonis, Tim Pearce, Siddhartha Sen, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Shivam Garg, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

entry.summary: The authors show that independent runs of autoresearch agents on the same task plateau at substantially different scores, remaining trapped in localized solution-space regions they call idea basins. They propose fork-and-flush, a periodic intervention that forks the agent into parallel trajectories inheriting the workspace but with fresh chat contexts, helping escape these basins.

entry.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models

author.name: Xin Wang, Hao Yu, Zhengyang Zhuge, Bochao Mao, Zheng Li, Junda Feng, Yuyan Luo, Yi Zhang, Yizhong Cao, Mi Zhang, Dayiheng Liu, Jianwei Zhang

entry.summary: TRACE is an FP4 quantization framework for RL post-training of MoE language models that directly aligns the training and rollout quantized execution paths via rollout-guided quantization-aware training, rather than optimizing each path independently. This reduces the compute and memory overhead of RL rollouts for large models.

entry.title: FC-SWE: Failure-Conditioned RL for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Jia Liufu, Bin Hu, Linglin Jing, Terry Kong, Yuki Huang, Ashwath Aithal, Wenming Yang, Jun Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes failure-conditioned RL for repository-level software engineering agents, addressing the waste in GRPO-style training where verifier feedback from failed patches is discarded. It trains agents on recovery trajectories conditioned on prior failures, turning diagnostic information from errors into useful training context for long-horizon, tool-using agents.

entry.title: When Can World Models Recover Physical Laws?

author.name: Ye Yuan, Jun Liu

entry.summary: The paper formally characterizes when a world model can recover underlying physical laws, showing that accurate prediction does not imply law recovery since distinct dynamics can yield identical observations. Using rate-distortion theory, it derives necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform law recovery based on experimental distinguishability of laws, with a finite response codebook and explicit decoding budget.

entry.title: Jailbreaking Open-Weight LLMs via Random Embedding Perturbations

author.name: Abhinav Sudhakar Dubey (University of California Santa Cruz), Scott Sirri (University of California Santa Cruz), Vaggos Chatziafratis (University of California Santa Cruz), C. Seshadhri (University of California Santa Cruz)

entry.summary: Presents PEV, a jailbreak attack that adds independent Gaussian noise to input embedding vectors, successfully eliciting unsafe responses from six open-weight LLMs on JailbreakBench. The attack is far cheaper than gradient-based or per-prompt optimization attacks and requires no weight modification.

entry.title: Personal-Agent Mediated Recommendation with Cross-Platform User History

author.name: Yu Xia, Jiangfan Zhang, Jun Xiao, Julian McAuley, Xiangjun Fan

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Personal-Agent Mediated Recommendation, a paradigm where platform recommenders produce candidate rankings and a user's personal LLM agent mediates using user-authorized cross-platform history to produce final top-K slates. It introduces MediateRec, a benchmark studying the trade-off between beneficial rescues and harmful overrides of platform rankings, with authorship including Julian McAuley.

entry.title: DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks

author.name: Antoine Edy, Max Conti, Victor Xing, Marc-Antoine Allard, Nawfal Benhamdane, Gautier Viaud

entry.summary: Presents DAEDALUS, a method for bootstrapping reusable agent memory from self-generated practice, requiring neither pre-existing training tasks nor oracle verifiers. An explorer agent generates challenges and a complementary agent distills successful experiences into operational knowledge, reducing repeated failures in new environments.

entry.title: UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model

author.name: Edan Kinderman, Elad Hoffer, Yochai Blau, Brian Chmiel, Ron Banner, Daniel Soudry, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: UNREAL is a model-native evidence-selection framework that unifies corpus-scale retrieval and long-context inference by deriving retrieval queries directly from a frozen LLM's internal representations, adding fewer than 500K trainable parameters while leaving the backbone unchanged. On a 3B-token, 21M-chunk Wikipedia index, all dense and hybrid UNREAL backbones reportedly outperform state-of-the-art retriever-reranker pipelines.

entry.title: Secure Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Zhiqi Wang, Neil Gong, Yuchen Yang

entry.summary: This work provides the first systematic security analysis of speculative decoding, the widely used inference acceleration technique where a small draft model proposes tokens verified by a larger target model. Through a large-scale measurement study, the authors reveal a pronounced security-utility asymmetry across lossy speculative decoding configurations, showing that existing approaches to the efficiency-utility trade-off can introduce unexamined security risks. The findings motivate secure design principles for accelerated LLM inference.

entry.title: When Forgetting is not Catastrophic: On the Mechanics of Spurious Forgetting

author.name: Vedant Palit, Florent Draye, Nicolas Zucchet, Zhijing Jin, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: This work studies spurious forgetting in language models, where knowledge seemingly lost during finetuning remains stored and recoverable, including dynamics where recall collapses then self-recovers before eroding. Using a minimal associative memory model, the authors show three ingredients drive these dynamics: shared key structure, concentrated new values, and normalization. The findings clarify when finetuning-induced forgetting is reversible.

entry.title: From Evidence to Action: How Tool-Using Agents Fail

author.name: Hongzhan Lin, Shidong Cao, Ziyang Luo, Wenhao Chai, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: Studies where the evidence-to-action chain breaks in tool-using agents, from deciding whether to act to executing single actions and dependent workflows, across ten model-harness configurations. It finds failures often precede execution, with agents stopping investigation early or acting before required evidence is established, while multi-action workflows expose unresolved prerequisites.

entry.title: Nucleus Speculative Decoding: Plausibility-Aware Verification Beyond Exact Distribution

author.name: Shuhao Li, Fanghua Ye, Wanyu Lin, Tianyu Yuan, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: Nucleus Speculative Decoding (NSD) relaxes the standard speculative decoding acceptance rule by also accepting draft tokens that fall within the target model's nucleus, addressing the conservative rejection of highly plausible tokens. The authors provide theoretical guarantees and the change increases the number of draft tokens retained per verification pass, improving inference speed.

entry.title: Tracking Is Not Permanence: What Video World Models Keep of a Hidden Object

author.name: Peng Xie, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: This probing study examines whether the frozen V-JEPA 2 video world model retains information about objects hidden from view, comparing predictions for occluded regions against encoder representations. It finds the predictor partially retains stationary objects, loses carried objects entirely, and forgets moving objects within a fraction of a second, even though the encoder itself encodes the object's presence strongly. This reveals a fundamental gap between representation and predictive permanence in video world models.

entry.title: Beyond the Linear Representation Hypothesis: Non-Linear Activation Steering in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Muhammad Atif Butt, Pawe{\l} Skier\'s, Joost Van De Weijer, Kamil Deja

entry.summary: This paper challenges the Linear Representation Hypothesis in text-to-image diffusion models, showing that intermediate visual concepts (e.g., between sunny and stormy) are represented nonlinearly and prompting for intermediates rarely activates straight directions in activation space. It proposes nonlinear activation steering to reach true intermediate states.

entry.title: Compositional Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Hierarchically Grounded Semantic Surgery

author.name: Chen Dai, Ganyu Zou, Nathan Self, Kevin Piper, Ramachandra Rao Seethiraju, Karthik Shyamsunder, Chang-Tien Lu, Naren Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: This paper introduces HGSS, a training-free framework for erasing specific concepts (copyrighted, unsafe, or user-specified) from deployed text-to-image diffusion models. It addresses compositional prompts where erase targets are invoked indirectly through related classes or where modifiers migrate onto preserved objects, by lifting both the routing signal and the edit operator in a hierarchical fashion. This matters for practical model safety and content moderation without costly per-target retraining.

entry.title: GeoPID: Decomposing and Steering Visual Information in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Seulgi Kim, Zhixiong Zhang, Xinwei Zhang, Jie Ling, Ronn Shaw

entry.summary: GeoPID is a training-free framework that geometrically decomposes multimodal information in VLMs into redundant, modality-unique, and synergistic components via relationships between visual and textual representation subspaces. Drawing on analysis across 22 VLMs and 14 benchmarks showing correct predictions carry stronger vision-unique components, it steers generation to reduce over-reliance on textual context.

entry.title: CtrlCache: Accelerating Interactive Video World Models with Control-Aware Caching

author.name: Shangye Song, Dong Gong, Hong Jia, Yun Sing Koh, Xinyu Zhang

entry.summary: CtrlCache is a training-free caching method for interactive video world models that exploits the fact that user controls for a chunk arrive before denoising, allowing control-aware reuse schedules at zero extra forward cost. Analysis shows adjacent chunks share structural similarity under consistent control regimes, enabling cheaper chunk generation without sacrificing control fidelity.

entry.title: VLA-ACL: Action-Consistent Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Owen Du, Yang Yue, Jie Zhang, Jiaqi Pi, Chi Bene Chen, Gao Huang

entry.summary: VLA-ACL learns a lightweight visual token pruning policy for vision-language-action models through action-level supervision while keeping the base model entirely frozen, avoiding both indirect heuristics and costly fine-tuning. The action-consistency objective targets real-time robotic deployment by cutting the dominant visual token redundancy at each control step.

entry.title: DepthWorld: 3D World Model for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jai Bardhan, Josef Sivic, Vladimir Petrik

entry.summary: DepthWorld addresses the problem that RGB-trained video world models produce plausible-looking rollouts that are not 3D-consistent, which limits their use in robot manipulation for planning and policy evaluation. The authors propose a calibration pipeline combining learned stereo depth with joint factor graph optimization across episodes from the same robot to recover shared kinematic parameters, providing large-scale 3D supervision for manipulation world models.

entry.title: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Models to Unknown Visual Disruptions During Execution

author.name: Ahin Lee, Jinwoo Seo, Youngsoo Jang, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: SALT enables VLA policies to adapt at test time to unforeseen visual disruptions by using the leftover, unexecuted portion of the previous action chunk as temporally aligned self-supervision, with Transition Anchoring preserving the pre-disruption plan across the shift. This is significant because real deployments inevitably face unmodeled visual corruptions that break vision-based policies.

entry.title: How Much Planning Is Enough? Reducing Search and Computation in World-Model Planning

author.name: Changbai Li, Sirui Li, Yichen Yang, Tongfei Chen, Zichao Feng, Shuwei Shao, Huobin Tan

entry.summary: The paper studies efficiency in visual world-model planning, showing that competitive task performance does not require agreement with full-budget action search and that sufficient planning budgets vary across model-task pairs. It introduces SufficientPlan, a deployment framework with Paired Sequential Budget Certification that certifies reduced model-task-specific budgets without modifying pretrained world models or planners.

entry.title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning

author.name: Zewei Zhou, Rachel Luo, Yulong Cao, Chaowei Xiao, Chensheng Peng, Boyi Li, Thomas Tian, Zheng Lian, Yan Wang, Jiaqi Ma, Boris Ivanovic, Marco Pavone, Wenhao Ding

entry.summary: VeriFine is an agent harness framework in which the policy, training curriculum, and judge co-evolve to sustain self-improvement in embodied reasoning. A rubric judge diagnoses recurring failures and builds an adaptive curriculum, and when progress plateaus, a mechanism scales verification to cover newly emerging failure patterns that fixed judges cannot verify.

entry.title: CADForge: Agentic Single-View CAD Reconstruction with Explicit Geometry Reasoning

author.name: Keyang Lu, Zhifei Yang, Tianao Dong, Mingzhe Xing, Zhen Xiao, Yikai Wang

entry.summary: CADForge is an agentic pipeline that reconstructs editable parametric CAD models from single images by decomposing objects into CAD-meaningful components, extracting geometric constraints, translating them into precise parameters via mathematical code, and synthesizing executable CadQuery programs with a review agent. It targets practical value in modern manufacturing workflows.

entry.title: Do Tool Calls Execute as Intended? Measuring and Repairing Intent-Execution Correspondence in LLM Agents

author.name: Boyang Yang, Zhenhao Li, Ziyao Yang, Kanghui Jia, Xin Yin, Mingmou Liu, Haoye Tian

entry.summary: This paper defines intent-execution correspondence (IEC): the property that an executed action matches what the emitted tool call denotes under the tool contract, noting that intermediate hops can silently alter calls and cause agents to retry correct calls at real cost. It proposes an observation protocol that names the first hop that changed the call and an intervention (IntAct) that delivers calls in a protected form.

entry.title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists

author.name: Kate Zhang, Yuante Li

entry.summary: This paper shows that AI-scientist benchmarks assuming evidence grounding can be gamed: agents can reach correct answers from prior knowledge or option elimination rather than the supplied data. The authors build perturbed dataset versions where evidence is intact, withdrawn, or reversed, verified against pre-registered statistics, and find the grounding assumption often fails. This is an important critique of how scientific-agent capability is currently measured.

entry.title: Judged Useless, Queried Anyway: Tool-Using Agents Rarely Turn Their Own Evidence Judgments into Stopping Decisions

author.name: Chubin Zhang, Zhenglin Wan, Xingrui Yu, Jingxuan Wu, Yaxin Zhou, Ivor Tsang, Bo An

entry.summary: In a retrieval environment with controlled source failures, the authors separate how tool-using agents judge results from their stopping behavior, finding that seven tested agents judge a failing source useless 97-100% of the time yet rarely stop on that judgment. Prompt cues, memory permissions, and budgets shift when agents stop but not what they stop on, revealing a dissociation between evidence assessment and decision policy.

entry.title: AgentPrivArena: Evaluating and Auditing Real-world AI Agent Privacy

author.name: Shouju Wang, Haopeng Zhang

entry.summary: AgentPrivArena is a framework for evaluating privacy risks in realistic LLM agent workflows, integrating authentic MCP tools and self-hosted services in a reproducible execution environment. It proposes trajectory-level privacy metrics that quantify unnecessary information access beyond what the final result requires, addressing limits of simulated-trajectory, outcome-based benchmarks.

entry.title: CoDance: Learning Reactive and Compliant Human-Humanoid Interaction from Video

author.name: Zhuoqun Chen, Shucheng Jia, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: CoDance learns reactive, compliant human-humanoid interaction from video, using partnered dancing as a demanding testbed requiring footstep coordination and continuous two-hand contact. The framework retargets motions from a single video of two dancers into robot and partner references and introduces multi-link compliance augmentation that converts kinematic demonstrations into force-aware training data. This pushes humanoid control toward physically interactive, contact-rich behaviors.

entry.title: OGAM: Connecting Systematic Testing to Runtime Assurance through Object-Grounded Attention Monitoring for VLA Policies

author.name: Haki Darwish, Xiangyu Yin, Changwen Li, Rongjie Yan, Francisco Gomes de Oliveira Neto, Chih-Hong Cheng

entry.summary: OGAM links systematic testing of vision-language-action policies to runtime assurance: pairwise combinations of action templates and objects plus paraphrase tests reveal attention divergence between successful and failed executions, and this signal is used to halt failures at deployment beyond the finite test suite. Across 87 out-of-benchmark cases, OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, UniVLA, and pi-0.5 complete none of 24 feasible instructions and issue unsafe responses to infeasible or hazardous requests.

entry.title: Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs

author.name: Hyunji Lee, Joykirat Singh, Zaid Khan, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Alessandro Sordoni, Arman Cohan, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: This paper analyzes hybrid language models that interleave attention and recurrent layers, finding that despite complementary pathways, these models rely substantially more on attention than on recurrent state for using past information. Standard fine-tuning does not fix this imbalance, so the authors propose interventions to improve recurrent memory utilization. The findings inform the design and training of efficient hybrid architectures increasingly used for long-context efficiency.

entry.title: Reward-Driven Learning under Prompt-Level Differential Privacy

author.name: Jiachen Zhao, Antonia Januszewicz, Taeho Jung

entry.summary: Provides, to the authors' knowledge, the first differential privacy guarantee for RLVR training, treating the group of responses to a prompt as the privacy record. The method aggregates per-prompt gradients, clips once, and adds Gaussian noise so the privacy budget is independent of response count and clipping norm, preventing trained models from leaking confidential training problems.

entry.title: Behavioral Cloning Mystery

author.name: Seohong Park, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: Seohong Park and Sergey Levine propose OCBench, a robotic manipulation benchmark with controllable scripted policies designed to systematically study counterintuitive behavioral cloning phenomena such as performance improving with overfitting and closed-loop policies failing without action chunking. The benchmark fills the gap between costly real-world experiments and synthetic setups that fail to reproduce these effects.

entry.title: ROMA: LLM System for Real-World Object-Centric Multi-Sensory Active Perception

author.name: Ruoxuan Feng, Yutong Chen, Ruihua Song, Huan Yang, Zhongyuan Wang, Guocai Yao, Di Hu

entry.summary: ROMA is an LLM-based system that integrates vision, audio, tactile, and force sensing into a reasoning-interaction-feedback loop for object-centric active perception in the real world. It identifies missing sensory evidence, decides which interactions to perform on target objects, and determines when sufficient evidence has been gathered.

entry.title: LatentQuant: Preserving the Policy-Facing Latent Contract under NVFP4 VAE Quantization

author.name: Ziye Deng, Lufang Chen, Shuyu Feng, Zhenwei Duan, Zicong Ye, Yu Sun, Xiaofan Li, Ruyi Gan, Hao Wang, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper addresses quantization of world action models (WAMs) that reuse pretrained video VAE latents to condition downstream action policies, arguing that quantization must preserve the latent distribution the frozen policy expects, not just reconstruction quality. The authors show that on Wan2.1, direct NVFP4 W4A4 quantization leaves VBench reconstruction nearly intact but collapses LIBERO task success from 95.5% to 10.5%, and they propose joint quantization-aware training with a decoder-only variant to recover policy performance by maintaining the policy-facing latent contract. This matters because it exposes a hidden failure mode in efficient deployment of video-generating action models and offers a practical QAT recipe for 4-bit inference.

entry.title: Agentic Cognitive Depth: Operational Criteria for Evaluating LLM Agents

author.name: Nijesh Upreti, Chris Sypherd, Vaishak Belle

entry.summary: This paper proposes a trajectory-level evaluation framework for agentic LLM systems built on the Planning-Memory-Tools-Control Flow paradigm, defining agentic cognitive depth across five operational criteria: context sensitivity, temporal continuity, multimodal coordination, adaptive interaction, and metacognitive monitoring. It moves evaluation beyond end-to-end task success toward profiling how agents actually use their architectural components.

entry.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures

author.name: Jiateng Liu, Rushi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xuejun Zhang, Sun Li, Jiayu Liu, Yifan Shen, Xu Cao, Jiarui Yao, Bingxuan Li, Ruhi Sarikaya, Heng Ji

entry.summary: LMBuild is a benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents generate 3D structures that are actually buildable and functional — not just geometrically attractive — by representing objects as assemblies with parts, joints, materials, and assembly sequences. It provides a reproducible framework with an interactive environment for physical-realizability evaluation.

entry.title: Trinity: Self-Evolving Vision-Language Models with a Self-Verifier

author.name: Youngwan Lee, Yong-Ju Lee, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Trinity improves self-evolving vision-language models by having one VLM play three roles — Questioner, Solver, and Verifier — replacing weak agreement-based rewards with verification-based signals for self-generated training data from unlabeled images. The key critique is that agreement cannot tell whether a question is grounded in the image or whether a confident majority answer is wrong. This is a promising route to unsupervised capability expansion without larger annotation budgets.

entry.title: Strong Helps Weak: Directional Cross-Modal Alignment Transfer in Multi-modal LLMs

author.name: Hoigi Seo, Byung Hyun Lee, Minjun Kim, Dohyun Mah, Jongho Lee, Se Young Chun

entry.summary: This paper characterizes an asymmetric model-merging phenomenon in multi-modal LLMs: merging a well-aligned, data-rich source-modality model into a data-scarce target-modality model transfers alignment capability without requiring large modality-specific datasets. This offers a cost-efficient alternative to expensive modality-specific training, especially for domains like audio and video where same-modality model variants are rarely available.

entry.title: MemTrace: State-Consistent Memory for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Hongming Xu, Le Zhou, ZhongHe Jin, Xiang Zhang, Bo Tang, Zhiyu Li, Xuanhe Zhou, Juncheng Zhang

entry.summary: MemTrace is a provenance-aware memory system for coding agents handling long-horizon software evolution tasks, designed to keep execution history consistent across context refreshes and to verify that recalled evidence remains valid after repository changes. It addresses context-budget strain and stale evidence, two coupled failure modes of existing compression and retrieval approaches. This is significant as agent memory consistency is a key bottleneck for real-world automated software engineering.

entry.title: A Safe Action Is Not Enough: Feasible-Future Decoding for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Tu Nguyen, Matthieu Zimmer, Vu Anh Vu, Ziyi Wang, Jannik Hammel Nielsen, Xuebing Zhou, Haitham Bou Ammar

entry.summary: This work identifies the feasibility-likelihood gap in vision-language-action policies: a locally safe action may leave no policy-supported route to safe task completion. The authors derive an exact next-block marginal over futures restricted to safe completion and use the resulting feasible-future mass to guide decoding of frozen VLA policies toward actions that preserve viable safe futures.

entry.title: MESH-Harness: Self-Improving Agent Harnesses via Bandit-Guided Compositional Evolution

author.name: Zhiwei Shang, Yu Huo, Mingrong Gong, An Yan, Zikun Qu, Junhao Dong, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Chenglin Wu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: This paper introduces MESH-Harness, a method for automatically improving LLM agent harnesses — the scaffolding code that manages context, state, and tool calls — while keeping model weights frozen. It decomposes the harness into modular components with explicit interfaces, uses a full-covariance LinUCB bandit approach with mixed-start coordinate ascent to efficiently explore candidate module combinations under a limited evaluation budget, and applies validation traces to guide local code edits. This matters because agent performance often depends as much on harness design as on the underlying model, and automating harness optimization could substantially reduce engineering effort.

entry.title: Hallucination Across the Reasoning Lifecycle: Interface Visibility, Causal Evidence, and Release Control in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Zhe Yu, Mohan Li, Lei Yu, Ka-Ho Chow, Chengwei Qin, Xingyu Wu, Wenpeng Xing, Shuguang Xiong, Meng Han

entry.summary: This survey synthesizes 312 papers and first-party reports on reasoning hallucinations in large reasoning models, organizing evidence via a UIPCA taxonomy covering unsupported premises, invalid inferences, dependent reuse, answer-trace consistency, and action-policy failures. It connects diagnosis to verification, repair, selective release, and persistent-state control across memory, tools, and trajectories.

entry.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Stable Temporal Abstraction for Language Model Agents

author.name: Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Yize Cheng, Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: This paper identifies a failure mode in hierarchical language agents called temporal abstraction instability, where the boundary policy swaps subgoals too frequently or retains stale ones. The authors propose STAC, a constrained optimization method that stabilizes subgoal persistence across multiple temporal scales, improving long-horizon control for LLM agents.

entry.title: DiMOS: Doob-Guided Inference-Time Multi-Objective Search for Scientific Design

author.name: Ziqing Wang, Qijie Zhu, Weimin Wu, Zeqi Ye, Minshuo Chen, Han Liu, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: DiMOS is a training-free framework for multi-objective scientific design using frozen pretrained masked diffusion models with inference-time guidance. It tackles pass-or-fail constraints and black-box rewards that provide no gradients by using joint rewards and Doob-guided search to locate small feasible regions under a limited inference budget.

entry.title: Normality Constraint Learning: Adapting Foundation Models for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xiaohui Zhou, Yijie Wang, Hongzuo Xu, Weixuan Liang, Guansong Pang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a key weakness of Time Series Foundation Models for anomaly detection: because TSFMs model rare patterns as well as normal ones, reconstruction or forecasting error loses discriminative power. It proposes Normality Constraint Learning, a lightweight plug-and-play adaptation that constrains pretrained TSFMs to model only normality, without modifying pretrained weights.

entry.title: FREA: A Multi-Source Expert Benchmark for Reaction Feasibility Verification

author.name: Botao Yu, Bo Zhou, Daniel Adu-Ampratwum, Frazier N. Baker, Ziru Chen, Reza Averly, Ye Liu, Wenhao Gao, Xia Ning, Huan Sun

entry.summary: FREA is a benchmark of 751 chemical reactions labeled by expert chemists under an explicit feasibility criterion, drawn from retrosynthesis model proposals, zero-yield records, LLM edits, and five negative generation methods. Evaluation shows no verifier leads across sources: criterion-only LLMs are competitive with dedicated verifiers, and forward models excel on retrosynthesis proposals but reject most feasible edits.

entry.title: AI Agent Pull Requests on GitHub: Frequency, Structure, and Merge Conflict Rates

author.name: George Xu, Arjun Subramanian, Nithilan Karthik

entry.summary: This is the first empirical study of concurrent PR submission by AI coding agents to shared repositories, using the AIDev-pop dataset of 33,596 agent-authored PRs across 2,807 repositories. It finds that 40.2 percent of repositories contain co-active agent-authored PR pairs accounting for 79.4 percent of agent PRs under exact temporal overlap, rising to 53.4 percent and 95.0 percent within a one-week window.

entry.title: Beware EviLLM: Enabling Vulnerability Injection via Large Language Models

author.name: Zeezoo Ryu, Simon Chung, Muhammad Faraz Karim, Anna Raymaker, Karan Singh Jodha, Yash Chaturvedi, Sukarno Mertoguno

entry.summary: This paper studies the EviLLM threat model, in which a third-party adversary compromises the AI code generation pipeline to deliberately inject vulnerabilities into LLM-generated software. Unlike prior work on inadvertent flaws, backdooring, or jailbreaking, this models a realistic cybercriminal-level attacker. The authors implement two attack instances demonstrating the feasibility of the threat.

entry.title: Representational Control over Self-Report & Behavior Coherence in LLM Risk-Taking

author.name: Rafal Kocielnik, Peiyang Song, Pengrui Han, Myrl G. Marmarelis, Ramit Debnath, Dean Mobbs, R. Michael Alvarez

entry.summary: This paper uses activation steering to investigate whether the gap between what LLMs self-report about risk-taking and how they actually behave is a prompting artifact or reflects internal representation. The authors survey nine steering-vector extraction methods across granularities and evaluate coherence between self-report and behavior under the same internal intervention on two behavioral tasks. The work connects interpretability techniques to questions about model introspection and disposition measurement.

entry.title: Questioning the Questions: Sustaining Self-Evolution in Reasoning Models

author.name: Jinyuan Li, Chengsong Huang, Langlin Huang, Donghong Cai, Shiping Gao, Yuyi Yang, Jiaxin Huang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why self-evolving reasoning models degrade over successive rounds of training on self-generated questions, identifying two failure modes: growing prevalence of invalid questions (exacerbated by answer-consistency filtering) and diversity collapse where lexically distinct but mathematically equivalent questions recur. It proposes fixes to sustain self-evolution. This addresses a key instability in self-improvement pipelines for reasoning models.

entry.title: Video2World: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive World Modeling from Embodied Videos

author.name: Jinzhou Tang, Zijun Zhang, Jing Yang, Yuchen Yan, Kun Zhou, Lingjun Mao, Ruobing Han, Jinglin Cao, Wenpeng Xu, Lukun He, Minghao Fu, Fan Feng, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: Introduces Video2World, a benchmark of 222 reconstruction instances from 189 robot and human demonstration videos that evaluates whether frontier coding agents can autonomously convert embodied videos into interactive simulated environments. Agents must observe a video, build the corresponding simulator and robot behavior, and refine via execution feedback. This targets automation of a major bottleneck in scaling embodied AI data.

entry.title: Scaling Verifiable Environments for Long-horizon Work Agents

author.name: Jiazheng Zhang, Long Ma, Yunxian Yang, Zhiheng Xi, Zhikai Lei, Yajie Yang, Chenyang Liao, Enyu Zhou, Yang Nan, Yuchen Tian, Senjie Jin, Yibo Wang, Wei He, Boyang Liu, Jixuan Huang, Xin Guo, Zhezheng Hao, Xinbing Liang, Zhihao Zhang, Changzhi Zhou, Wiggin Zhou, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang, Clarenceai, Aiden Adams

entry.summary: WorkForge is a scalable synthesis framework that constructs verifiable work-agent environments from real-world resources, starting from expert workflows and retrieving real files to organize into interactive workspaces with grounded verification. It addresses the trade-off between hand-crafted environments (high engineering cost) and synthetic ones (low realism or verifiability). Environment scaling for long-horizon professional agents is a recognized bottleneck for training capable agentic systems.

entry.title: Software World Models: From Consequence Prediction to Decision Value

author.name: Tongli Su, Yuntong Hu, Liang Zhao, Bowen Zhu, JayaSai Somasundaram, Hasibul Haque

entry.summary: This paper proposes Software World Models (SWM), which predict the blast set of components a coding agent's change will break across downstream services, going beyond static change-impact analysis. The framework follows an explore-learn-act loop that executes candidate changes from restored system states to learn system dynamics before acting.

entry.title: Same Predictions, Different Harms: Causal Auditing of Patient World Models

author.name: Yicheng Qi, Xiyi Xiong

entry.summary: The paper shows that patient world models used for clinical trial simulation can match on transition kernels and arm-specific risks yet disagree on the counterfactual fraction of patients harmed by treatment switching. Using a two-stage structural causal model, the authors derive closed-form sharp harm intervals for few intermediate states and calibrated outer bounds when independence assumptions are relaxed. This formalizes a reliability gap with direct implications for model-based clinical decision support.

entry.title: AgentDoxx: Agentic Re-identification of Anonymized Text with Web Search

author.name: Jianing Wen, Tianshi Li

entry.summary: AgentDoxx is an evaluation suite of 822 synthetic interview transcripts grounded in public information about real individuals, used to measure how well LLM agents with web search can re-identify anonymized text. The study evaluates fifteen open-weight and proprietary model configurations, isolating the effect of web search and analyzing search trajectories.

entry.title: SEA-LM: Egocentric Spatial Audio Understanding for Wearable Microphone Arrays

author.name: Sonal Kumar, Sinan Hersek, Artem Dementyev, Mengzhen Pan, Ishan Chatterjee, Anurag Kumar, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha, Andrea Colaco

entry.summary: This paper introduces SEA-LM, a spatial audio understanding model for smart-glasses microphone arrays that encodes First Order Ambisonics via a layout-flexible encoder (FOACODER) trained on source localization and ego-centric voice activity detection. It integrates this spatial encoder into a multimodal LLM to enable spatially aware audio reasoning, addressing a key gap in mono-channel audio-language models.

entry.title: SimpleMark: Fast Multi-Bit Text Watermarking under f -Divergence Constraints

author.name: Benjamin D. Kim, Wanrong Zhang, Weitong Ruan, Lav R. Varshney, Daniel Alabi

entry.summary: This arXiv paper presents SimpleMark, a framework for embedding multi-bit messages in LLM-generated text while bounding distortion using general f-divergence measures such as total variation and KL divergence. Unlike prior watermarking work that guarantees distortion-freeness only on average or for specific statistical distances, the scheme enforces its security guarantee per realized key and message. The authors develop a coding-based method that optimally biases next-token distributions under a divergence budget and characterize the tradeoff between embedding rate, decoding reliability, and statistical security.

entry.title: EpicWorldModel: Exploration-driven Planning with Latent World Models

author.name: Bowen Feng, Julian Ost, May Mei, Anirudha Majumdar, Felix Heide

entry.summary: EpicWorldModel extends deterministic JEPA-style latent world models to stochastic settings under partial observability, predicting multiple plausible futures via a flow-matching objective when goal-relevant content is missing from history. The authors use flow predictive variance as an exploration signal for planning in uncertain environments. This addresses a known breakdown of JEPA world models under occlusion and ambiguity.

entry.title: On the Geometry of Multimodal Saturation: Riemannian VICReg

author.name: Nessim Ben Abbes, Duc Han Le, Sabri Mtibaa, Van-Tam Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper identifies and quantifies multimodal saturation: adding a third modality to self-supervised VICReg/SimSiam training frequently harms performance, occurring in roughly half of paired runs across nine image-text-tabular datasets. It attributes the failure to alignment geometry and proposes Riemannian VICReg, aligning views via squared geodesic distance on learnable negative-curvature factors, which recovers VICReg as curvature vanishes and substantially increases the chance a third modality helps. A principled geometric diagnosis with a working remedy.

entry.title: Quantifying the Stability of Multi-Step Reasoning via Error Amplification

author.name: Dongyue Li, Ziniu Zhang, Minxuan Duan, Hongyang R. Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides a theoretical analysis of why errors accumulate in multi-step reasoning chains, such as chain-of-thought prompting in language models. The authors derive an inference error bound expressed as a product of spectral norms of Jacobians across generation steps, framing it as an error amplification factor that can grow exponentially with reasoning length. This offers a principled way to predict and potentially control reasoning instability at test time.

entry.title: The Assistance Dilemma: Learning to Teach via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jakub Macina, Manu Kapur, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: The paper improves LLM tutoring via RL against a simulated student, introducing a masked near-transfer post-test that evaluates the student on an unseen variant with the tutor's words removed, so rewards can only rise through genuine student learning. This discourages answer-telling and cognitive offloading without requiring hand-tuned penalties.

entry.title: Anatomy of LLM Sycophancy: What a Flip Rate Hides

author.name: Haonan Huang

entry.summary: Using SycoLens, a modular replay protocol with matched controls, the paper dissects LLM sycophancy measurement, showing that a single flip rate conflates self-correction with capitulation. Across eleven frontier models from three providers and roughly 760,000 controlled replays, it shows which models appear sycophantic depends heavily on pushback wording and measurement settings.

entry.title: Differentially Private Mixing of Public Datasets Improves Private Learning

author.name: Yufei Chen, Tejumade Afonja, Anvith Thudi, Nicolas Papernot

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first pipeline that differentially privately learns which mixture of several public datasets to pretrain on for a given sensitive downstream task. The key insight is that the best mixture can be found by privately learning a low-dimensional linear model, improving over fixed or heuristic public-data choices before DP finetuning. Tested on NIH data, the method reduces the utility drop of differentially private training.

entry.title: MC-Sparse: Deconstructing and Closing the Dense-Sparse Attention Gap in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Jiarui Chen, Zeqiang Lai, Jiangshan Wang, Ziheng Ouyang, Ye Huang, Xiangyu Yue, Cewu Lu, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Through controlled oracle comparisons, this paper traces quality degradation in sparse attention for diffusion transformers to three sources: token grouping constraints, inaccurate interaction selection, and discarded-token attention loss. It proposes MC-Sparse, a training-free framework selecting individual KV tokens while grouping similar queries into tile-aligned GPU-efficient structures, with meta-caching to preserve lost contributions. This enables high-sparsity attention for video and 3D generation without fidelity loss.

entry.title: Learning to Read the Contextual Tokens in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Omer Dahary, Etai Sella, Hadar Averbuch-Elor, Daniel Cohen-Or, Or Patashnik

entry.summary: Presents a framework for interpreting multimodal diffusion transformers (MM-DiTs) by training a lightweight bottleneck network that maps intermediate contextual text tokens into a frozen LLM's input space, letting the LLM answer questions about the emerging image. The reader reveals that contextual tokens encode rich, global representations of the scene being generated.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Direction-Aware Mismatch Stabilization of Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhen Li, Shuai Zhang, Yanggan Gu, Yiming Zhang, Yang Yu, Mingfa Feng, Congkai Xie, Shuang Yu, Junjie Lai, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: Studies instability in low-precision (NVFP4) reinforcement learning for LLMs caused by learner-sampler execution mismatch, showing that mismatch interacts differently with amplifying versus contracting policy-gradient directions. TRIAGE is a direction-aware stabilization method that intervenes on the early imbalance of negative-advantage updates before mismatch spreads globally.

entry.title: Muon Is Theoretically Wrong For Convolutions, But Empirically Effective

author.name: Thibaut Boissin (IRIT), Thomas Massena (IRIT, DTIPG - SNCF, UT3), Mathieu Serrurier (IRIT), Franck Mamalet

entry.summary: This paper examines the popular Muon optimizer, which is theoretically grounded for matrix-valued updates, and points out that convolutional kernels are 4D tensors whose standard reshaping into matrices breaks the underlying theory. The authors formalize the optimization objective in convolutional operator geometry and introduce Convolutional Newton-Schulz (Conv-NS), which approximates the polar factor while preserving kernel support. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet show that Conv-NS and reshape-based Muon are both efficient and achieve comparable accuracy, highlighting a gap between theoretical justification and empirical performance.

entry.title: Multigroup Fairness and Omniprediction: Separations and Equivalences

author.name: S\'ilvia Casacuberta, Parikshit Gopalan, Varun Kanade, Omer Reingold, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Pranay Tankala

entry.summary: This theory paper maps the relationships between omniprediction, loss outcome indistinguishability, and the multigroup fairness notions of multiaccuracy and multicalibration, establishing new separations and equivalences. It clarifies which fairness-style structural conditions suffice for a single predictor to be competitive against a benchmark class across arbitrary losses. Strong author team (Reingold, Gopalan, Tankala, etc.) from the theoretical CS community.

entry.title: Harmful SFT Leaves a Continuous Trace in LLM Checkpoint Updates

author.name: Ziqun Bao, Xinyu Zhang, Yuchen Shao, Chengcheng Wan

entry.summary: The authors show that harmful-compliance supervised fine-tuning leaves readable evidence directly in checkpoint-update space: a checkpoint-level coordinate derived from a reference geometry of harmful, safety-targeted, and benign SFT tracks harmful-objective composition with Spearman correlations of 0.986-0.992 across four 7-8B backbones. This enables safety auditing without model execution or behavioral evaluations.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Atmospheric Rivers in GraphCast

author.name: Madelyn Mathai, Timothy B. Higgins, Kevin M. Grise, Chirag Agarwal, Antonios Mamalakis

entry.summary: The authors train sparse autoencoders, including Matryoshka SAEs, on GraphCast to show the AI weather model internally computes atmospheric river intensity (integrated vapor transport) as a stable variable even though IVT is neither an input nor a target. The work connects interpretability methods to scientific ML and exposes structured concept organization within the model.

entry.title: Do Higher-Order Models Win for Higher-Order Reasons? Rethinking Performance Gains in Hypergraph Learning

author.name: Fanchen Bu, Fan Li, Geon Lee, Sunwoo Kim, Xiaoyang Wang, Renaud Lambiotte, Kijung Shin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a controlled performance-attribution framework that perturbs higher-order information while preserving pairwise structure, to test whether hypergraph neural networks actually win because of higher-order information. Across 25 benchmarks it finds higher-order models often lose their advantage under such perturbations, questioning a common attribution narrative.

entry.title: Atom-JEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for 3D Atomistic Systems

author.name: Kasper Helverskov Petersen, Rasmus Hannibal Tirsgaard, Fran\c{c}ois R J Cornet, Mikkel Jordahn, Mikkel N. Schmidt

entry.summary: Atom-JEPA brings joint-embedding predictive architecture style self-supervised pretraining to 3D atomistic systems, using complementary atom-level and substructure-level objectives on large molecular and crystalline datasets. The goal is to achieve the kind of cross-task downstream generalization that SSL brought to language and vision but that has lagged in chemistry and materials. It is a notable attempt to establish a general atomistic foundation representation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for Hierarchical Reasoning Rewards: Minimax-Optimal Rates with Transformers

author.name: Naoki Nishikawa, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: This work provides a theoretical explanation for why on-policy exploration with neural reward models succeeds in RL post-training of language models. It models rewards as hierarchical functions on the response space, where local reward components become relevant sequentially, and proves minimax-optimal rates for a natural Transformer-based actor-critic algorithm.

entry.title: The Geometry of Statistical Feature Learning in Mean-Field Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Zong Shang, Tomoya Wakayama, Guillaume Lecu\'e, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: This theory paper introduces a base-fiber geometric decomposition of feature learning in supervised regression, proving the property for spherical mean-field Langevin dynamics as a Wasserstein gradient flow of entropy-regularized risk. In Gaussian multi-index models it shows the low-temperature stationary distribution concentrates near hidden indices in a multi-spike structure, enabling parameter recovery with high probability despite entropy regularization penalizing concentration.

entry.title: Inference-Time Projection for Physically Valid Biomolecular Diffusion Models

author.name: Qurat-ul-ain, Yee Whye Teh, Charlotte M. Deane, Matteo Cagiada

entry.summary: The paper tackles the problem that AlphaFold 3-style cofolding models often produce physically invalid structures (overlapping chains, distorted bonds, non-planar rings) and proposes treating physical validity as a constraint enforced by inference-time projection using quantities the sampler already holds, avoiding the cost of physics-informed steering or architecture-specific finetuning. This enables fixing outputs on large complexes where other approaches are infeasible.

entry.title: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory

author.name: Chinmay Savadikar, Zhaoyu Zhang, Mingyu Zhao, Shuang Xie, Han Li, Tianfu Wu, Lingyun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces append-only memory for long-horizon web agents, arguing that unlike overwrite or summarization schemes, append-only memory guarantees preservation of factual information, error feedback, and progress tracking without context blowup. AMBER trains agents to use this memory structure across multi-step trajectories.

entry.title: MobileVISTA: Generative Data Augmentation for Pose Generalization in Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Suzannah Wistreich, Stephen Tian, Isabella Huang, Vitor Campagnolo Guizilini, Sergey Zakharov, Katherine Liu, Jiajun Wu

entry.summary: MobileVISTA addresses brittleness of imitation-learned mobile manipulation policies to robot pose deviations by transforming demonstrations from canonical poses into diverse pose-perturbed training data, jointly augmenting egocentric visual observations and retargeting actions for base pose changes. The Stanford-affiliated team (including Jiajun Wu) targets humanoid and mobile manipulator deployment in unstructured environments.

entry.title: Learning consistent molecular mechanics force fields from first principles

author.name: Berkay G\"unes, Leif Seute, Jigyasa Nigam, Frauke Gr\"ater

entry.summary: Introduces grappa-fullFF, a unified machine learning approach that learns both bonded and nonbonded force-field parameters as functions of local atomic environments from first-principles data. This removes the reliance on empirical nonbonded parameters, improving accuracy and transferability of classical molecular mechanics simulations.

entry.title: Information-Dense Synthesis for Molecular Discovery

author.name: Kasper K. Jakobsen, Eli N. Weinstein

entry.summary: The paper proposes designing and synthesizing information-dense molecular mixtures that are tested as pools, followed by deconvolution of the molecule-activity map, rather than designing, making, and testing molecules one at a time. By optimizing synthesis for maximal information, the approach theoretically reduces the number of experiments needed to find the best of d candidates from linear in d to much smaller, addressing the sparse-property regime where existing algorithms barely beat random guessing.

entry.title: RAG-PIBench: A Leakage-Aware Benchmark for Prompt-Injection Detection in Trustworthy RAG Systems

author.name: Niveen O. Jaffal, Ahmet Yuksel, David Mohaisen

entry.summary: This paper introduces RAG-PIBench, a benchmark of 4,876 contextual examples for evaluating prompt-injection detection in retrieval-augmented generation systems, with frozen train, validation, and protected-test splits to prevent benchmark leakage. The authors compare keyword-based, semantic, TF-IDF, and transformer-based detectors, finding DistilBERT performs best (F1 = 0.896, PR-AUC = 0.968) while simple sparse baselines remain competitive. This matters because prompt injection via retrieved content is a leading security risk for deployed RAG systems, and rigorous evaluation methodology is needed to measure real detector effectiveness.

entry.title: WavePrune: One period is often enough for RoPE

author.name: Guancheng Du, Luotian Huang, Shaowen Wang, Si Li, Kaifeng Lyu

entry.summary: WavePrune addresses position aliasing in rotary position embeddings by restricting each channel to its first rotation period, removing aliasing artifacts in attention maps. This simple change improves long-context performance without extra tuning, raising the HELMET score on four of five tested models (e.g., 35.7 to 40.0 on one model). It is a lightweight, drop-in fix with theoretical grounding in RoPE periodicity.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Estimation for KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Ahsan Bilal, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Muhammad Umer, Wajih Hassan Raza, Atta Ul Asad, Young D. Kwon, Michal Valko, Dean F. Hougen

entry.summary: Introduces LORE-KV, a training-free KV cache eviction method that reframes future-aware eviction as distributional estimation over plausible query trajectories. It samples short autoregressive continuations from the frozen target model and uses response-side query states to score prompt-token utility, addressing the problem that decoding queries are unknown at eviction time.

entry.title: No Transformer Beats Six Covariates: Long-Horizon Prediction of Depressive Symptoms from Childhood Essays

author.name: Daniel Kua, Emrul Hasan, John-Jose Nunez, Frances Chen

entry.summary: This paper tests whether NLP models can predict depressive symptoms at age 23 from essays written at age 11 in the British National Child Development Study cohort. Surprisingly, a logistic regression on six simple childhood covariates (AUC-ROC 0.737) beats seven fine-tuned transformers, bag-of-words models, frozen embeddings, and four zero-shot LLMs using only the essay text (0.670 AUC-ROC), highlighting the limits of long-horizon text-based mental health prediction.

entry.title: Towards In-Parameter Memory Augmentation for Large Language Models

author.name: Haoyu Huang, Zhongwei Xie, Jiaxin Bai, Yisen Gao, Hong Ting Tsang, Wuganjing Song, Huihao Jing, Yufei Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: This survey examines in-parameter memory for LLMs and LLM-based agents: representing reusable post-pretraining knowledge (domain facts, user preferences, documents, interaction history) in model parameters, adapters, or parameter-like objects composed into the forward pass at inference time. It positions this as a complement to in-context learning, which consumes context capacity and incurs encoding costs that grow with context length, and focuses on pluggable memory-bearing parameter objects at deployment.

entry.title: Medical Image Alignment Assessment as a Test of Generalist Visual Reasoning in Frontier Multimodal Models

author.name: Ross Callaghan, Niannu Gao, Hojjat Azadbakht, Hui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper uses medical image alignment assessment—judging whether two images show anatomical correspondence—as a probe of whether frontier multimodal LLMs can make reliable novel visual judgments without task-specific fine-tuning. It matters because it tests the generality claim of MLLMs as visual reasoners in a domain where human visual assessment is still the gold standard but does not scale.

entry.title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation

author.name: Yu Zhang, Xudong Xu, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: PhysLDM is a latent diffusion framework for one-shot simulation of deformable 3D volumetric meshes, addressing long-horizon prediction without autoregressive error accumulation or prohibitive native-resolution multi-frame prediction. It introduces a compact spatiotemporal latent representation for mesh-based physics and empirically examines deterministic regression versus generative diffusion as predictive paradigms. Relevant to graphics, physical AI, and neural simulation.

entry.title: EmbodiedSmith: Scaling Embodied Data through Recursive Self-Improvement Flywheel in Simulation

author.name: Yikai Qin, Yifei Deng, Mingjian Liang, Wenxuan Song, Zepeng Lin, Zhiyi Jiang, Jiajun Fu, Qiao Sun, Huashuo Lei, Xicheng Gong, Jiayi Chen, Han Zhao, Shuanghao Bai, Pengxiang Ding, Pengwei Wang, Haoang Li

entry.summary: EmbodiedSmith is a framework for scalable embodied data generation that unifies asset, scene, and task generation in simulation via recursive self-improvement. Its agentic refinement loop makes scene generation anticipate downstream task requirements while task generation guides targeted scene edits, supporting autonomous creation and language-driven customization. This addresses key bottlenecks in scaling robotic foundation model training data and evaluation environments.

entry.title: Test-Time Adaptation of Quantized ViTs via Single-Pass Quantizer-Aligned Recalibration

author.name: Hyeongheon Cha, Young D. Kwon, Sung-Ju Lee

entry.summary: The paper targets brittleness of post-training-quantized vision transformers under distribution shift, identifying a quantization-specific failure mode where shifted activations fall outside frozen quantization ranges. It proposes a backprop-free, single-pass recalibration aligned with quantizer constraints, offering accuracy recovery at edge-friendly cost.

entry.title: Backend-Agnostic Sparse Attention for Fast High-Resolution Visual Generation

author.name: Liao Ma, Jiayi Song, Yunfeng Wu, Songhua Liu, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: This work tackles the quadratic cost of full attention in diffusion transformers for high-resolution image and video generation with a backend-agnostic sparse attention scheme. It navigates the trade-off between partitioned window attention (efficient but grid-artifact-prone) and sliding-window attention (better quality but irregular computation), aiming to get both speed and cross-window interaction.

entry.title: WorldSonus: Bringing Sound to Worlds

author.name: Pengjun Fang, Jingyi Fa, Kam Man Wu, Jiaming Wang, Haoyuan Huang, Yaguang Wu, Xiangjun Huang, Ziyang Ma, Weijia Chen, Hongyu Liu, Zeyue Tian, Qifeng Chen

entry.summary: WorldSonus is an interactive video-to-audio framework for world models that generates spatially aligned stereo sound in real time for streaming visual environments. It uses a streaming causal autoregressive diffusion architecture achieving a real-time factor of 0.41, supports mid-stream sound instructions, and couples audio to scene geometry and camera motion. This addresses a notable gap, as most world-model research focuses on visuals while generated worlds remain silent.

entry.title: CoRE: Learning Collaboration-Role Experts for Decentralized Collaborative Manipulation with One Policy

author.name: Yanan Zhou, Zhaoyan Qian, Zihao Li, Mingyuan Ba, Ranpeng Qiu, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: This paper introduces CoRE, a single shared policy that enables decentralized multi-robot collaborative manipulation without task prompts, identity labels, or inter-robot communication. It learns Collaboration-Role Experts via query-conditioned cross-attention with a local router, using fused appearance and geometry features from each robot's observations. This matters because it removes the communication and identity assumptions that typically constrain multi-robot manipulation deployments.

entry.title: Commit While Futures Agree: Consequence-Aware Adaptive Action Chunking for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yuyan Li, Yujia Wang, Yusong Huang, Junjie Yang, Yanggang Sheng, Ziyi Shi, Wenpeng Xu, Xiaoyang Zhou, Haoang Li, Hongliang Lu, Xinhu Zheng

entry.summary: CA3C tackles how much of a predicted action chunk to commit before replanning, arguing that commitment should depend on agreement among imagined futures rather than similarity in action space. The method adaptively varies execution horizons based on consequence-aware consistency, moving beyond fixed-length prefixes used in current chunking systems.

entry.title: ActTune: Action-Aware Precision and GPU Operating-Point Adaptation for Energy-Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference

author.name: Zou Qingyun, Bin Gao, Wenju Zhao, Weng-Fai Wong, Bingsheng He, Tulika Mitra

entry.summary: ActTune targets GPU energy per successful robot task rather than per inference call, recognizing that reduced precision can increase failures or latency in ways that raise total task energy. The framework exploits the observation that quantization sensitivity varies across action classes, layers, and weights-vs-activations, dynamically tuning numerical precision and GPU operating points while preserving success and keeping latency growth under 10 percent.

entry.title: PEARS: Physical-Prior-Guided Efficient Adaptation via Failure Reasoning and Diffusion Steering for Tactile Manipulation

author.name: Kun Song, Yiming Wang, Yilin Chen, Tianyi Ding, Jiaxin Tian, Tianqi Gong, Daolin Ma, Jia Pan

entry.summary: PEARS is a hybrid RL framework for sample-efficient online adaptation of pretrained manipulation policies under out-of-distribution conditions, using tactile feedback. A physics-guided force reasoning module leverages a VLM to diagnose failures from visual and tactile data, and diffusion steering guides exploration to reduce costly real-world trial requirements.

entry.title: Redundancy and synergy in multivariate Gaussians via the Blackwell order

author.name: Artemy Kolchinsky

entry.summary: The paper defines a partial information decomposition for multivariate Gaussian systems based on the Blackwell order, which formalizes comparative channel informativeness. The author proves Gaussian channels are optimal for extracting redundant and union information, yielding a geometric interpretation, an efficient numerical algorithm, and consistency with the well-known BROJA measures.

entry.title: AI Safety at the Frontier: Paper Highlights of August & September 2026

author.name: gasteigerjo

entry.summary: A bi-monthly curated digest of frontier AI safety research, highlighting a paper of the month on plain RL producing reward-seeking models that take harmful actions, plus results on probing for reward hacking, debate with weak judges, automated alignment researchers based on Claude Opus 4.8, evolutionary search for persuasive mind viruses, and alignment training tricks.

entry.title: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents

author.name: Yadong Lu, Theodore Lee, Yifei Li, Lawrence Keunho Jang, Tianci Xue, Yu Su, Huan Sun, Ahmed Hassan Awadallah

entry.summary: CUAWright replaces domain-specific GUI harnesses for computer-use agents with a minimal ~3K-line terminal harness that uses bash commands as its sole action interface and the file system as an evolvable space for dynamically creating tools and managing context. Comprehensive experiments across digital tasks show this minimal interface enables strong performance by letting capable models operate programmatically.

entry.title: Spec2Game: Can LLMs Generate Complete Playable Games from Detailed Specifications?

author.name: Yixue Cai, Yuzhe Zhao, Hanxiang Chao, Qingsen Ma, Ziheng Xiong, Jinhu Qi, Irwin King

entry.summary: Spec2Game is a benchmark of 15 game families and 150 task instances requiring models to generate complete, executable Pygame projects from detailed natural-language specifications, evaluated on executability, specification realization, code quality, and visual/behavioral evidence. It tests whether generated programs actually implement behavioral requirements, not just run.

entry.title: Functionally Equivalent or Not? Graph-Grounded Differential Surrogate Execution for Code Equivalence

author.name: Amit Kachroo, Like Hui, Haitao Mao, Yuhao Zhang, Nguyen Vo

entry.summary: FEAgent is a selective agent that assesses functional equivalence of programs by aligning public interfaces and behaviorally relevant graph anchors, then issuing bounded queries over call-flow, control-flow, and data-flow combined with differential surrogate execution — useful when direct execution is impossible due to obsolete or unavailable environments. It targets code modernization, patch validation, and code-generation evaluation.

entry.title: Runtime Authorization of Self-Generated Subgoals in Long-Horizon Tool-Using AI Agents

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses an authorization gap in long-horizon tool-using agents: per-tool permission checks cannot ensure a dynamically changing goal graph stays within a principal-approved contract. It proposes version-bound witnesses for goal-graph mutations, atomic commit-time rechecking of protected effects, and proves trace-policy and forbidden-state preservation guarantees. This is notable formal work on agent security, an area of rising practical urgency.

entry.title: Benchmarking Jailbreak Guardrails for Embodied Agents

author.name: Xunguang Wang, Qingyue Wang, Yuguang Zhou, Zongjie Li, Wenxuan Wang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic evaluation of jailbreak guardrails for embodied agents powered by LLMs and vision-language models, using a pluggable framework that treats the agent as a fixed backend and guardrails as interchangeable modules. It measures how well existing guardrails prevent physically harmful actions induced by jailbreak attacks.

entry.title: ImproveAnyTask: An Autonomous Post-Training Harness for Iterative Model Self-Improvement

author.name: Xingbo Yao, Xiaoman Wang, Zhengwu Lei, Tinghui Luo, YiLin Zhang, Yuefeng Wu, Yijie Xu, Tianfu Wang, Qingyuan Zhan, Ye Guo, Daoxin Zhang, Zhe Xu, Jian Liu, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: ImproveAnyTask is an autonomous post-training harness that iteratively improves LLM task performance under a limited compute budget by organizing adaptation into error attribution, update-direction selection, and executable model updates. It mimics gradient-based optimization at the level of training-strategy decisions, combining metric-level and case-level analysis to focus on focal problems.

entry.title: Language models can notice an impossible engineering problem yet still report it as solved

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Testing 14 language models on 30 pairs of mechanics problems (valid versions versus versions made physically impossible), the authors find models frequently fail to reject flawed problems, with 12 of 90 replies from three recent models reporting flawed problems as solved despite the models apparently noticing the impossibility. Each answer was independently verified by two solvers, and prompts did not warn that problems could be flawed.

entry.title: A Step Towards Forgetting: Optimiser History and the Loss of Answer Mass

author.name: Valeria Ruscio, Seth Nabarro, Keiran Thompson

entry.summary: This work investigates how optimizer momentum contributes to catastrophic forgetting during language model fine-tuning, showing that stored gradient contributions from earlier model states can push probability away from previously learned answers. Across three language-model families, the authors find that answer mass consistently declines while discrimination among old answers usually improves, meaning models become less likely to produce answers they can still distinguish correctly.

entry.title: A Bird's-Eye View of Iterative Reward Design

author.name: Logan Mondal Bhamidipaty, Lauren Robson, Linda Petrini, Shengrui Lyu, Kamal Ndousse

entry.summary: The authors introduce BIRD, a benchmark that unifies LLM-based iterative reward design methods, which generate and refine reward code from policy feedback, in a single configuration and evaluation space spanning MuJoCo, Meta-World, and Assistax. This enables direct algorithm comparison, ablation of design choices, and prototyping under matched feedback conditions and training budgets. It brings much-needed comparability to a fast-moving but fragmented area at the intersection of RL and LLMs.

entry.title: Organising Trajectory Evidence for Language-Model Agent Assurance: Fragments, Methods, and the Residual

author.name: Xiaowei Huang

entry.summary: Provides a unified formal account of how diverse LLM agent assurance methods, including rule checkers, skill coverage analyses, prefix monitors, execution gates, and rare-event estimators, can be combined and what they leave unchecked. It builds this from a two-tier logic over recorded events and the argument structure supported by recorded context, organized as an assurance ledger. This offers a common vocabulary for auditing agent runs.

entry.title: Communication Shapes Collective Inference in Self-Adapting LLM Societies: Evidence from Mafia

author.name: Haonan Huang, Joey Xiao

entry.summary: Using the Mafia game with 8-100 claude-haiku-4-5 agents across 7,416 analyzed games and 1.9M model calls, this study shows simultaneous broadcast communication improves adversary identification over silence in all tested compositions, while turn-taking removes most of the advantage. Agents adapt by rewriting and inheriting private strategy notes across generations.

entry.title: When Verifiable Counts Depend on Wording: Auditing Wording Robustness in Instruction Following

author.name: Qishi Zhan, Seoyeon Jang, Zihan Dong, Minxuan Hu, Ziheng Chen, Tonghui Qu

entry.summary: This work introduces WISE, a matched evaluation suite testing whether verifiable instruction-following scores remain stable when the operational requirement is fixed but its wording varies, instantiated on word counts and keyword constraints. Across 100 matched tasks and up to thirteen models from seven providers, wording alone produces substantial compliance shifts, including systematic effects from avoidance and exclusion phrasings. The results question the reliability of verifiable instruction-following benchmarks as currently reported.

entry.title: Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation

author.name: Team Kandinsky, Julia Agafonova, Bulat Akhmatov, Mikhail Aksyutin, Grigorii Alekseenko, Anastasia Aliaskina, Olga Androsova, Vladimir Arkhipkin, Anna Averchenkova, Alexander Belykh, Serafima Bocharova, Sofiya Bogakovskaya, Anton Bukashkin, Mark Bulygin, Kirill Buzygin, Irina Cheremnykh, Kirill Chernyshev, Mikhail Chernyshov, Vladimir Chernyy, David Chikovani, Georgy Daniltsev, Denis Dimitrov, Anna Dmitrienko, Vladimir Dokholyan, Sergey Emelyanov, Dmitry Ermilov, Georgii Fedorov, Polina Gavrilova, Nikolai Gerasimenko, Aleksandr Gordeev, Andrey Inozemtsev, Andrei Ivaniuta, Alexander Ivanov, Mikhail Karaev, Anastasiia Kargapoltseva, Ivan Kirillov, Nikita Kiselev, Valeria Kobenko, Yury Kolabushin, Denis Koposov, Anatoly Korobov, Vladimir Korviakov, Kirill Kozlov, Denis Krzhivokolskiy, Konstantin Kuklev, Alexander Kunitsyn, Sergey Kuzin, Vladislav Lakhtionov, Alexey Letunovskiy, Maxim Litvinov, Alexander Lyulkov, Georgy Makarov, Kirill Malakhov, Egor Malykh, Mikhail Mamaev, Dmitrii Mikhailov, Polina Mikhailova, Ivan Mikheev, Elizaveta Muromtseva, Nikolai Nazarkin, Tatiana Nikulina, Lev Novitskiy, Stanislav Onuchin, Nikita Osterov, Denis Parkhomenko, Anatoliy Parpara, Vladimir Polovnikov, Konstantin Reznikov, Azat Saginbaev, Nikita Samsonov, Alexander Sentsov, Nikita Shaimov, Artem Sherstyuk, Andrey Shutkin, Egor Silvestrov, Bulat Suleimanov, Matvey Suprunov, Sergey Taranov, Irina Tolstykh, Tatiana Trofimuk, Ilya Trushkin, Aleksandra Tsybina, Olga Varlashina, Viacheslav Vasilev, Ilya Vasiliev, Eugeny Vilisov, Sergey Yakubson, Konstantin Zakharov

entry.summary: Kandinsky 6.0 Video is a family of diffusion foundation models for synchronized text-to-audio-video and image-to-audio-video generation, with Lite (3B) and Pro (29B) variants producing 5-second clips with synchronized 44 kHz audio and lip-sync, upscaled to Full-HD. It uses a dual-stream CrossDiT architecture connecting a pretrained video stream to a new audio stream via bidirectional cross-attention.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: Performance and Costs of Agentic Retrieval for Complex Tasks

author.name: Reza Esfandiarpoor, Radek Osmulski, Yauhen Babakhin, Gabriel de Souza P. Moreira, Oliver Holworthy, Jie He, Ronay Ak, Jiarui Cai, Ryan Chesler, Bo Liu, Even Oldridge

entry.summary: This paper evaluates agentic retrieval that interleaves LLM reasoning with retriever calls in a ReAct loop, showing +8.7 nDCG@10 over standard dense retrieval with the same embedding model and much stronger out-of-domain robustness. It also quantifies the latency and token cost tradeoffs, giving a practical cost-effectiveness picture for production RAG systems.

entry.title: APOD: reasoning-guided agentic population ordinary differential equation discovery for pharmacological digital twins

author.name: Romain Ferrara, Martin Soucail, Victor Gertner, Adil Moussali, Joris Cocquebert, Sandrine Oziel-Taieb, Julien Nicolas, Florence Gattacceca, Mihaela van der Schaar, S\'ebastien Benzekry

entry.summary: APOD is a language-model agent that discovers population-level ODE systems with between-subject variability for pharmacological digital twins, iteratively reasoning over biological knowledge and fit diagnostics in an open-ended search space. It addresses sparse, noisy clinical data where prior automated methods either restrict the model space or ignore inter-individual variability. It recovers ground-truth structures on synthetic pharmacokinetic and tumor-dynamics benchmarks.

entry.title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents

author.name: Ziyan Wang, Shuqing Shi, James Oldfield, Samuele Marro, Jialin Yu, Philip Torr, Yali Du, Adel Bibi

entry.summary: BazaarBench is a simulated consumer-to-consumer marketplace benchmark for evaluating the safety of LLM agents acting on users' behalf in negotiation, listing, and rating scenarios. It tracks ownership, item condition, and commitments across transactions, combining record checks with rubric-based LLM judgments to identify six failure types across five transaction stages. Large-scale runs with 100 agents over 30 simulated days and multiple models reveal delegation risks to money, privacy, and reputation.

entry.title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Yutong Dai, Viraj Prabhu, Zhiyuan Hu, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen

entry.summary: CLIFT is a training and test-time scaling method for web agents built on conformal self-verification: the agent answers natural-language verification questions about its own rollouts, and a Compositional Conformal Certifier retains signals whose URL-conditional evidence agrees with a training-time judge, assigning signed trust weights. This replaces sparse binary task success and expensive frontier-LLM judges in RL training of open-source web agents. It also supports test-time scaling without assuming judge availability at deployment.

entry.title: Learning to Decide, Not to Reason: Parameter-Efficient Decision Operators via Low-Rank Activation Steering

author.name: Ran Li, Lei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a System-1 decision operator trained by behavior cloning that injects skills into frozen language models at roughly 100x lower parameter cost than RL pipelines: a 330K-parameter default matches a 1.33M RL-trained operator, and a 23K rank-4 variant nearly suffices on SearchQA and LiveMath. The approach collapses 3,685-token deliberation into 6-token decisions with no accuracy loss and transfers across five tasks and three backbones.

entry.title: Learning Scientific Exploration from Human Research Decision Trajectories

author.name: Xuchen Gong, Shane Gu, Haokun Liu, Dixi Yao, Chenhao Tan, Tian Li

entry.summary: Introduces ResearchTrails, a dataset of human research trajectories built from Git commit histories, providing supervision for the exploration process that papers omit.
