entry.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design

author.name: Haosen Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: EASER is a reflective agent that bridges literature reasoning and biological sequence generation by steering a diffusion-based generator through learned low-rank property matrices, proposing intervention hypotheses such as anchors and editable positions. It targets the gap where LLMs can devise design strategies from scientific text but cannot reliably implement them for sequences.

entry.title: GraphDecide: Benchmarking System One Models on Graph Tasks

author.name: Xianliang Yang, Yapu Zhang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: GraphDecide is a model-independent benchmark for evaluating choice-based System One models (such as Jev) on graph decision tasks, using structural task profiles, matched graph-text contrasts, and heuristic-proposal controls across fourteen model configurations. Results show that accurate adjacency recognition does not guarantee broader structural correctness.

entry.title: Conditional Rank Allocation for Taxonomy-Aware Medical Language Model Adaptation

author.name: Guangyuan Dong, Ziwei Hong, Xuehao Zhou, Zidong Yu, Bingchen Liu, Kehan Liu, Chuang Liu, Rong Fu, Yuchao Hou

entry.summary: ARBOR is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for medical question answering that selects rank-one components from a shared low-rank basis per question, using a gate that combines question representations with specialty and operation tags. The paper provides an illustrative theoretical separation showing conditional selection can beat fixed low-rank updates, and demonstrates gains with Qwen3-8B across CMB, CMExam, MedQA, and MedMCQA benchmarks.

entry.title: WAMJET: A Harness for World Action Model Acceleration

author.name: Le Chen, Lixin Liu, Jan Schneider, Zeju Qiu, Simon Guist, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Dieter B\"uchler

entry.summary: WAMJET is an agentic harness that accelerates inference of World Action Models for robot manipulation by equipping coding agents with reusable optimization guidance plus measurement and validation tools. It follows a bottleneck-driven workflow where the agent profiles, modifies targeted code, validates, and iteratively refines the acceleration stack while preserving model behavior.

entry.title: The Score Is Not the Structure: Brain Alignment and Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: Saman Rahbar

entry.summary: This methodological critique examines what brain-similarity and cross-lingual transfer scores actually measure, showing that in cross-lingual probing, the probe itself often fails: in four of seventeen languages it performs at chance, so 64 of 272 language pairs were scored with a non-functioning tool, and dropping those pairs substantially weakens the claimed shared-structure relationship. It cautions against interpreting similarity scores as evidence of shared structure between models, brains, or languages.

entry.title: Streaming Multi-Track Timeline Control for 3D Human Motion Generation

author.name: Yangsong Zhang, Anujith Muraleedharan, Rikhat Akizhanov, G\"ul Varol, Fabio Pizzati, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: TimelineControl enables interactive 3D human motion generation where new text instructions arrive during synthesis while ongoing actions continue, such as answering a phone while walking. It combines interval-aware conditioning, causal part-structured representations, and part-aware denoising to coordinate overlapping, independently timed action tracks. This is a meaningful step beyond one-shot text-to-motion generation toward real-time interactive applications.

entry.title: DUET: Co-Evolving Solver and Grader Agents

author.name: Fengyu Gao, Sourav Pal, Austin Z. Henley, Arjun Radhakrishna, Gustavo Soares

entry.summary: DUET addresses the coupled challenge of continually improving agentic workflows and evaluating them: as a solver agent evolves, its failure modes change and a fixed evaluator becomes inadequate. The framework co-evolves a solver agent and a grader agent so that evaluation improves alongside behavior, providing feedback for optimization. This tackles a fundamental problem for deployed agents in technology, finance, and enterprise settings.

entry.title: Scaling of Wireless Foundation Models via Representation Diversity and Multi-Branch Architectures

author.name: Ahmed Mohamed, Ahmed Aboulfotouh, Hatem Abou-Zeid

entry.summary: The paper proposes objective diversity as an alternative scaling axis for wireless foundation models, fusing frozen representations from independent encoders trained with reconstructive, predictive, and contrastive objectives. This preserves more signal information than pure capacity scaling when pretraining data are limited, improving downstream task performance.

entry.title: Maximizing $p$-Mean Social Welfare in the High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types and Few Item Types

author.name: Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni

entry.summary: This theory paper studies p-mean social welfare maximization for allocating indivisible goods with multiplicities encoded in binary, unifying Nash welfare and egalitarian criteria. It proves NP-hardness for every fixed rational p<1 with only two item types, Nash and egalitarian hardness with three item types, and strong NP-hardness with a single agent type and unrestricted item types.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Stress Testing of Overload Monitoring for Resilient Emergency Cellular Networks Using Internet CDR Proxies

author.name: Bilal Hussain, Xiao Tang, Tan Li, Muhammad Azhar, Danista Khan, Fawad Ahmad

entry.summary: Trains a lightweight CNN to detect cellular network overload during emergencies using Call Detail Record aggregates as a privacy-friendly proxy for signaling stress, then stress-tests and adapts the detector with diffusion-synthesized surge patterns. Shows default alert thresholds fail under realistic stress-test conditions.

entry.title: Towards Automatically Pruning Logging Code with Coding Agents: How Far Are We?

author.name: He Yang Yuan, Haonan Zhang, Xin Wang, An Ran Chen, Kisub Kim, Zishuo Ding, Zhenhao Li

entry.summary: This software engineering study examines logging code removal, an underexplored counterpart to logging generation, by mining and validating real-world removal cases from Python and Java repositories. The authors derive 10 removal patterns and 11 removal reasons and introduce LogRem, a 387-case dataset for benchmarking coding agents on automatic logging pruning.

entry.title: PreAct-Nav: Agentic Reasoning Before Action for Urban Navigation

author.name: Jing Xie, Shouwei Ruan, Yubin Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Junwei Yang, Songchang Jin, Dianxi Shi

entry.summary: PreAct-Nav equips frozen embodied navigation policies with anticipatory agentic reasoning for long-horizon urban navigation, anchoring local decisions in persistent predictions about action consequences and future conditions. It aims to translate distant goals into coherent local decisions where linguistic reasoning over transient observations falls short.

entry.title: Direction-Conditioned Policies for Online Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: S K Swaminathan, Damiya Gondha, Theyanesh Eswaramoorthy Rajahkrishnan, Aritra Hazra

entry.summary: Direction-Conditioned Policies (DCP) modify Contrastive Reinforcement Learning by conditioning the policy on direction and distance to selected visited-state waypoints in representation space during online training, then applying the same interface directly to the final goal at deployment without planning. Across nine navigation and manipulation tasks, DCP beats CRL on seven tasks and spends more time near the goal. It exploits the reachability geometry learned by the contrastive critic that raw-goal conditioning ignores.

entry.title: Settling the Computational Complexity of Max-Min Allocation with Ternary Valuations

author.name: Thi Ngoc Anh Vu, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Khaled Elbassioni, J\"{o}rg Rothe

entry.summary: This theory paper settles complexity questions for allocating indivisible goods to maximize egalitarian welfare under ternary valuation classes. It gives a polynomial-time algorithm for additive {p,q}-valuations when p=2, constant-gap hardness for p>=3, an approximation ratio for bi-valued cases, and resolves a conjectured tractability for {-2,0,c} valuations via reduction to maximum-weight perfect matching.

entry.title: IRSTD-Agent: Agentic Infrared Small Target Detection via Zoom-Guided Interaction Learning

author.name: Jiawen Xi, Yu Zhang, Tianyi Zhao, Zhu Liu, Maoxun Yuan, Xingxing Wei

entry.summary: IRSTD-Agent is an agentic framework where a multimodal LLM adaptively decides where and at what scale to inspect an image for infrared small-target detection, using five tools (PROPOSAL, ZOOM, DETECT, DROP, REFINE) to progressively gather fine-grained visual evidence. It targets maritime monitoring and aerial surveillance applications where precise localization of small targets has challenged MLLM approaches.

entry.title: BeliefGraph-JEPA: Structured Latent World Models for Action-Conditioned Time Series

author.name: Yue Li, Kangqi Ni, Zhen Tan, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: BeliefGraph-JEPA is a structured latent world model for action-conditioned time-series forecasting that factorizes driver influence into typed latent-effect states evolving over the forecast horizon. It routes influence to individual targets rather than relying on static relational graphs or implicit direct conditioning.

entry.title: Cut Binary Cross Entropy: Efficient Large-Vocabulary Loss and Gradient Kernels for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Yaoyiran Li, Haowen Ning, Mohamed Hammad

entry.summary: CutBCE is an exact, hardware-accelerated BCE loss and gradient operator implemented in JAX and Pallas for large-vocabulary sequential recommendation, avoiding the O(BNV) memory blowup of dense logits materialization that causes OOM errors. It adapts chunked-loss techniques, previously developed for softmax cross-entropy in LLMs, to the unexplored multi-label BCE setting.

entry.title: Transformer-Based Time-Series Inference of Lindblad Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems

author.name: Julian Guam, Jianqing Liu

entry.summary: Applies a raw time-series Transformer to infer unknown, potentially time-dependent dissipation rates and Hamiltonian parameters of open quantum systems governed by the Lindblad master equation, removing the hand-crafted features of prior work. This is an AI-for-physics contribution showing transformers can perform system identification under decoherence where analytical inversion fails. It matters as evidence that sequence models can invert complex physical dynamics directly from trajectories.

entry.title: Relational Synthesis: Structure-Mediated Concatenative Synthesis for Foley and Retrieval-Augmented Audio Generation

author.name: Keren Shao, Ayaka Kawano, Shlomo Dubnov

entry.summary: The paper introduces relational synthesis, a variant of concatenative synthesis that replaces a target-matching cost with a relational Gromov-like structural cost, enabling generation of novel audio that stays acoustically consistent with a retrieved source without verbatim copying. This simultaneously addresses a Foley production goal and the well-known copying problem in retrieval-augmented neural audio generation. The approach offers a non-neural-network-based angle on the RAG fidelity-versus-copying tradeoff.

entry.title: On Hyperparameter Tuning on the Test Set

author.name: Matteo Fregonara, Tom Viering, Jan van Gemert

entry.summary: This paper empirically quantifies how much performance inflation actually results from tuning hyperparameters on the test set, a practice usually treated as a cardinal sin in machine learning. Using MNIST-1D, CIFAR-10, and GLUE tasks, the authors systematically measure the magnitude of the effect and question how severe the dogma-violation truly is. The findings suggest the inflation is real but its size may be smaller than folklore implies.

entry.title: JLD: Perceptual Distance Through A Jacobian Lens

author.name: Shreshth Saini, Balu Adsumilli, Alan C. Bovik

entry.summary: Jacobian Lens Distance is a new perceptual image distance that derives its geometry from a frozen vision encoder rather than fitted human judgments, making it more robust across resolutions where label-fitted metrics degrade. It uses the encoder Jacobian to combine locality of early patch features with perceptual sensitivity of deeper representations. This targets applications in compression, restoration, and generation.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Objective Evaluation of Modern Text-to-Speech for Turkish Using Speech Quality Assessment Models

author.name: Yunus Emre Ozkose, Alperen Kahraman, Ali Haznedaroglu

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks four modern TTS systems (Chatterbox, CosyVoice, OmniVoice, VoxCPM2) in fine-tuned and zero-shot configurations for Turkish, a morphologically rich lower-resource language, comparing them against a VITS baseline and natural speech. It uses eighteen objective quality metrics spanning learned naturalness predictors and intelligibility estimators. The work matters because TTS evaluation on non-English, morphologically complex languages is under-characterized.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Calibration of Pre-Generation Success Probes for Multilingual LLM Routing

author.name: Andrea Paganelli, Stefano Civelli, Pietro Bernardelle, Gianluca Demartini

entry.summary: The paper examines whether pre-generation success probes, which estimate response correctness from hidden activations, remain reliable across languages along discrimination, calibration, and utility dimensions. Using MATH problems in 10 languages and 8 open-weight models, it compares English-trained probes against language-specific alternatives for cost-aware multilingual routing. The findings inform whether cheap probe-based routing generalizes beyond English.

entry.title: ARO: Aligned Representation learning for multi-Omics data

author.name: Amogh Singh, Yash Shah, Chiara D'Ercoli, Arash Mehrjou, Patrick Schwab, Timothy Jones, Pietro Li\`{o}

entry.summary: ARO learns aligned representations from multi-omics cancer data to reconstruct missing and unpaired modalities, prioritizing practical applicability in incomplete-data settings over large foundation models. It achieves low reconstruction MSE and latent embeddings that support downstream biological reasoning.

entry.title: Topology-Informed Prompt-Conditioned Universal Segmentation of Uterine Structures from Ultrasound and MRI

author.name: Yongheng Sun, Yuexi Gu, Jingwen Sun, Maureen Kohi, Mingxia Liu

entry.summary: TPUS is a unified prompt-conditioned segmentation framework for multiple uterine structures across ultrasound and MRI, using topology-informed constraints and modality prompts to handle heterogeneous appearances, resolutions, and label spaces while avoiding negative transfer. It supports screening and treatment planning for uterine diseases.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Guided Discovery of Weight-Five Bivariate Bicycle Codes

author.name: Juan Cruz-Benito

entry.summary: Building on an earlier LLM-guided program-evolution workflow, the author catalogs 1,142 weight-five bivariate bicycle code proposals, mostly attributable to LLM-generated programs, certifying several CSS realizations with strong parameters such as [[180,4,14]]. It provides exact distance evidence and verified constructions, demonstrating LLM-guided search as a tool for quantum code discovery. This extends AI-assisted discovery into quantum error-correcting code design.

entry.title: TreeWalker: Partial Evaluation for Grouped Tree-Ensemble Inference

author.name: Durmus Karatay, Richard Newman

entry.summary: Presents TreeWalker, which applies partial evaluation to grouped tree-ensemble inference where rows share feature values, walking each tree once per group and skipping constant features and empty subtrees. It works directly on standard LightGBM and XGBoost models without retraining and comes with a structural work decomposition and speedup analysis.

entry.title: Evolving LLM-Generated Features for Interpretable Classification

author.name: Jack Butler, Zainab Afolabi, Nikita Kozodoi

entry.summary: Proposes an evolutionary framework where an LLM generates candidate natural-language binary feature definitions (rubrics), evaluates samples against them, and evolves the feature set guided by classification errors, per-class activation rates, and ablation scores. The resulting features feed transparent classifiers like logistic regression, targeting regulated domains such as credit scoring and medical diagnosis.

entry.title: Ideal Paths for Approximating Logistic Gradient Descent Trajectories at Large Initialization

author.name: Junjie Xiao, Huiwen Jia

entry.summary: Constructs a unique continuous ideal path approximating full-batch logistic gradient descent trajectories under large initialization, using minimum-norm projection rules, going beyond classical implicit-bias results that characterize only the limiting direction. This gives geometric insight into how fine-tuning from pretrained models evolves. Relevant to understanding transfer learning dynamics.

entry.title: Do RUL explanations hold up? Faithfulness and stability of attributions on C-MAPSS

author.name: Manh Hien Nguyen, Ngoc Thanh Nguyen, Isabella Mendoza Cortes, Tam Khuat, Thanh Pham, Nhat Quang Tran, Ushik Shrestha Khwakhali, Loan Do

entry.summary: Trains 1D CNN, LSTM, and Transformer models for remaining-useful-life prediction on NASA C-MAPSS and rigorously audits Integrated Gradients, occlusion, and attention attributions using deletion/insertion faithfulness, noise stability, cross-seed agreement, and within-RUL consistency checks. It highlights evaluation gaps in the XAI-for-predictive-maintenance literature. A useful negative-results and rigor contribution.

entry.title: UnAct: Gradient-Free Unlearning via Targeted Activation Intervention

author.name: Saeed Abdul Muizz, Aayat Rafiq, Iqra Altaf Gillani, Janibul Bashir

entry.summary: UnAct is a machine unlearning method that removes class information from a trained image classifier using only forward passes over a few forget images: it scores late-layer units by their responses to the forget data and attenuates the most responsive connections over repeated rounds, requiring no gradients or labels. This contrasts with retrain-free baselines like SSD/LFSSD that still need backpropagation over the full dataset. It matters for privacy-sensitive deletion requests with limited forget data.

entry.title: Anticipating the Consequences of Curriculum Decisions with Large Language Models

author.name: Octavio Pappalardo, Nathan Herr, Tim Rockt\"aschel

entry.summary: The paper frames automatic curriculum learning as a sequential decision-making problem and identifies a gap between quantities that determine curriculum decision value and the local learning signals typically used to guide them. It investigates whether LLMs, given richer information about the learning problem, can better anticipate the consequences of curriculum decisions, introducing a method combining online learning-progress estimates with LLM-informed prediction. A novel direction of using LLMs as world models for training dynamics.

entry.title: Localized Operator Learning with Adaptive Partition-of-Unity Mixture-of-Expert Networks

author.name: Madison Cooley, Ramansh Sharma, Shandian Zhe, Robert M. Kirby, Varun Shankar

entry.summary: The authors introduce a partition-of-unity mixture-of-experts framework for neural operator learning, where geometry-aware gating networks create smooth spatial partitions blending local expert networks, with a hierarchical architecture called HiRefPOU for DeepONets. They also adapt the same principle to Fourier Neural Operators to add spatial adaptivity for PDEs with sharp interfaces and multiscale structure.

entry.title: Physics-Augmented Graph Transformers for Patch-Antenna Forward and Inverse Design

author.name: Avi Epstein, Snir Nehemia, Haim Suchowski, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: The authors present a physics-augmented graph transformer framework that predicts antenna radiation patterns as signal reconstruction on irregular surface meshes. An auxiliary objective predicting complex surface currents (PAIS) improves multiple GNN backbones at no inference cost, and the framework also supports inverse design.

entry.title: Private Component-by-Component Learning

author.name: Dvir Karni, Eliad Tsfadia

entry.summary: The paper studies differentially private learning of hypotheses specified by k components in the realizable setting, overcoming the problem that approximate component choices can destroy exact realizability. Using LabelBoost and alternating data reservoirs, it achieves only a root-k over epsilon privacy sample overhead relative to single-component active learning.

entry.title: Underscoring the Problem: Why Softpick Fails at Initialization

author.name: Aryan Sood, Jaikaran Singh, Ishaan Bansal

entry.summary: The paper explains why Softpick attention (which removes softmax attention sinks by rectifying scores) fails at scale, reframing the failure as a normalization problem at initialization where denominator rows cause divergent behavior. It proposes a family of operators that independently choose the positive- and negative-shifted denominators.

entry.title: Joint Estimation of Common-Slope Decay Rates and Spatial Amplitudes Using Parameterized Nonnegative Matrix Factorization

author.name: Jeremy B. Bai, Filip Elvander, Sebastian J. Schlecht

entry.summary: Formulates joint estimation of common-slope decay rates and spatial amplitudes from room impulse responses as parameterized nonnegative matrix factorization with the Itakura-Saito divergence. It derives closed-form amplitude updates and a convex decay-rate update via a SAGE algorithm, plus a contribution-weighted variant to accelerate estimation, producing detailed reverberation-time curves without backward integration.

entry.title: Square-Root Regret for Adversarial Multiplayer Bandits without Collision Information or Shared Randomness

author.name: Chenyu Gan

entry.summary: Addresses adversarial multiplayer bandits with multiple labeled players and no collision information, shared randomness, or communication channel, designing a communication and synchronization protocol with a Monte Carlo public constructor. Achieves square-root regret simultaneously for all oblivious reward sequences with high probability after preprocessing.

entry.title: Discovered, Not Designed: Population Evolution for Collaborative and Compute-Intensive Model Discovery

author.name: Bo Peng, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, Mingyi Wang, Yifan Wu, Serena Li, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao

entry.summary: The authors introduce Population Evolution (PE), a hierarchical framework where LLM-driven searches across related training instances share experimental evidence to guide code-change proposals and promotion to larger training scales. For expensive targets, PE screens candidates on small subsets via peer and intermediate evaluations before full-scale training. They also release RMD-Bench to evaluate both transfer and compute-constrained settings on ranking and watch-time tasks.

entry.title: Joint Precision Neural Networks: Task-Aware Dependency and Predictive Learning

author.name: Andrea Cavallo, Samuel Rey, Antonio G. Marques, Elvin Isufi

entry.summary: The paper proposes task-aware learning of precision matrix structures, extending PCA and covariance neural networks by exploiting the inverse covariance, which encodes conditional independencies rather than raw correlations. It addresses the instability of finite-sample precision estimates by jointly learning regularized, task-dependent graph structures alongside prediction.

entry.title: Sampling Allocation of LinUCB: Optimal Design Limits in the Small-Gap Regime

author.name: Yujie Liu, Vincent Y. F. Tan, Yunbei Xu

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes the sampling allocation of LinUCB in the small-gap regime where reward gaps scale as n^{-1/2}, the hard instances underlying worst-case regret lower bounds. Using a mean-field perspective on the empirical sampling distribution, it proves LinUCB's allocation converges to D-optimal experimental designs. This connects bandit adaptivity to classical optimal design theory in the regime where LinUCB is near-optimal.

entry.title: Generative World Models Enable Predictive Control of Laser Melt Pool Dynamics

author.name: Yiyang Yan, Markus Bambach, Mohamadreza Afrasiabi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a generative world model for laser melt pool dynamics in additive manufacturing, predicting evolution from temperature and phase morphology histories under candidate laser actions. Generative latent dynamics capture unresolved melt flow effects, enabling more accurate recursive rollouts than deterministic regressors, and the differentiable learned dynamics support predictive control. This brings the world-model paradigm to manufacturing process control at timescales beyond high-fidelity simulation.

entry.title: Improving Proactive AI Assistance with Hierarchical Procedural Understanding

author.name: Jin-Seop Lee, TaeYeon Won, SeongJun Jung, JungHoon Kim, Boyang Albert Li, Jin-Young Park, Jaehong Yoon, Jee-Hyong Lee

entry.summary: The paper addresses proactive AI assistants that observe user activity and decide when and what guidance to offer, arguing that existing datasets support only fixed-granularity or detection-based proactive understanding. The authors introduce data and methods incorporating hierarchical procedural structure so guidance can adapt to fine-grained task progress and user expertise. This targets a practically important capability for next-generation assistants.

entry.title: Adapting prior-data fitted networks for tabular anomaly detection

author.name: Maximilian Bershtman, Niv Cohen

entry.summary: This work investigates how TabPFN representations can be adapted for tabular anomaly detection under the difficult constraints of no labeled anomalies at deployment and a contaminated reference set that may itself contain anomalies. The authors begin with frozen TabPFN features and study scoring approaches suited to these conditions.

entry.title: Online Control via Counterfactual Tracking

author.name: Yunzong Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies online control of known linear dynamical systems with adversarial costs, introducing counterfactual tracking, which decouples learning from control: an online learner builds a reference trajectory from benchmark policies' counterfactual trajectories and a corrective law steers the system toward it. Charging each reference change its recovery cost reduces the problem to online learning with switching costs, yielding regret guarantees against general benchmark classes.

entry.title: Same Output, Different Gold: Measuring How Reference Choice Moves a Multilingual Benchmark Score

author.name: Parth Kulshreshtha, Shivali Dalmia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: The authors exploit a rare dual-annotation record from a six-language PII benchmark to hold system outputs fixed and swap the gold reference, measuring how benchmark scores move. Score shifts of up to 4.95 F1 points (7.55 in the worst language) show reference choice is a substantial and often ignored source of benchmark variance. This is a valuable methodological caution for interpreting leaderboard differences.

entry.title: Frame-Level Temporal Alignment for Human-to-Robot Visual Adaptation

author.name: Xizhe Zhang, Jingfeng Zhang, Zirun Zhou, Hong Jia

entry.summary: Proposes Frame-Level Temporal Alignment (FLTA), a framework that adapts visual encoders pretrained on human videos to robot manipulation by learning shared task-progress representations without frame-level correspondence annotations. It handles differences in execution rate and non-key frame proportions between human and robot demonstrations using two temporal priors. This improves transfer from abundant human video data to robot learning.

entry.title: All against the machine: the Solo score for rating skill in variable environments

author.name: David Reguera, Xavier R. Hoffmann, Irene P\'erez, Pol Colomer-de-Sim\'on, Miquel Masoliver, Xavier Guardiola, Jan Wedekind, Mari\'an Bogu\~n\'a

entry.summary: Proposes the Solo score, a distribution-free metric for rating individual skill in player-versus-environment settings with heterogeneous tasks, high randomness, and no direct opponents. Each task outcome is mapped to a bounded performance score with zero population mean and variance bounded by 1/3, enabling direct cross-task comparison, with a reshuffling-based significance test. Applicable to games, education, finance, and AI agent benchmarking.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Bregman Douglas-Rachford Splitting for Discrete Optimal Transport

author.name: Yifan Xu, Shiqian Ma

entry.summary: This work develops GPU-accelerated Bregman Douglas-Rachford splitting solvers for discrete optimal transport across three input formats (cost matrix, point cloud, grid-based separable cost), with hardware-aware algorithmic designs. The implementations reportedly achieve state-of-the-art runtime against eight GPU baseline solvers in what the authors call the first cross-solver GPU study.

entry.title: Static Bootstrap Placement for Encrypted Language Model Decoding

author.name: Halil Ibrahim Kanpak, Didem Unat

entry.summary: AR-HE runs the full autoregressive decoding loop of a language model on the server under homomorphic encryption, selecting and consuming tokens without client round trips per token, including server-side bootstrap placement for the growing encrypted state. The client sends one encrypted prompt and remains offline during generation.

entry.title: A Statistical Inference Framework for PMI Estimation and SGNS Word Embeddings

author.name: Zhongqi Fan

entry.summary: This paper develops a rigorous statistical framework for Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) estimation and its connection to Skip-gram with Negative Sampling (SGNS), which implicitly factorizes a shifted PMI matrix. The authors prove consistency, asymptotic unbiasedness, and asymptotic normality of the empirical PMI estimator, derive its variance via the Delta method, and use stochastic approximation theory to obtain a variance decomposition for SGNS-based PMI estimation separating data variance from optimization variance. This addresses a long-standing gap in characterizing finite-sample uncertainty in word association measures that underpin word embeddings.

entry.title: The sublevel Flood bifiltration: towards scalable 2-parameter persistent homology

author.name: Matt\'eo Cl\'emot, Julie Digne, Julien Tierny

entry.summary: The authors introduce the sublevel Flood bifiltration, a new construction that approximates the sublevel offset bifiltration to make two-parameter persistent homology computable on large point sets. They prove stability properties and give efficient computation algorithms. This addresses a major scalability limitation in topological data analysis.

entry.title: Isotropic Gaussian Processes Improve Vanilla Bayesian Optimization in High Dimensions

author.name: Wei-Ting Tang, Madhav Muthyala, Joel A. Paulson

entry.summary: Iso-BO shows that replacing the standard automatic relevance determination Gaussian process with an isotropic one-shared-lengthscale GP improves vanilla Bayesian optimization in high-dimensional, low-observation regimes, with analysis showing the marginal log likelihood depends on ARD lengthscales only through weighted pairwise distances. This is a simple modeling change with controlled comparison against a matched BO pipeline. It challenges the default ARD choice in high-dimensional BO.

entry.title: PhaseMatcher: Autoregressive Phase-Set Identification with Spectral Decomposition

author.name: Zhonglong Peng, Qiuliang Liu, Chang Chen, Geng Zhong, Qi Li, Lihong Wang, Lan Jiang, Shifeng Jin

entry.summary: This paper introduces PhaseMatcher, an autoregressive framework for identifying complete phase sets from powder X-ray diffraction data. It addresses the problem of residual distortion by re-estimating contributions of all previously identified phases using physics-guided spectral decomposition against original observations. This matters for materials science, where accurate phase identification underpins crystallographic analysis.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Convergence Rate of Normalized Gradient Descent under H\"older Smoothness

author.name: Yuki Takezawa, Eduard Gorbunov

entry.summary: This optimization theory paper analyzes the last-iterate convergence of normalized gradient descent for convex objectives satisfying Hölder smoothness conditions, addressing the gap between theoretical analyses (which typically bound the best or averaged iterate) and practical implementations (which return the final iterate). The authors prove an upper bound of O((log^2(T)/T)^((1+nu)/2)) for constant stepsize, showing only a logarithmic overhead compared to best-iterate guarantees, and demonstrate via numerical experiments. This matters because last-iterate guarantees are the practically relevant ones, and the paper clarifies when the known lower bound overhead for nonsmooth cases (nu = 0) can be softened.

entry.title: Inverse Cross-spectral Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series

author.name: Lorenzo Marinucci, Leonardo Di Nino, Gabriele D'Acunto, Paolo Di Lorenzo, Sergio Barbarossa

entry.summary: The paper introduces iCSNNs, graph neural networks for stationary multivariate time series whose graph shift operators are inverse cross-spectral density matrices, encoding frequency-specific conditional relationships between variables. This extends covariance-based neural networks beyond iid settings to capture joint temporal and cross-variable structure.

entry.title: WNet: Discrete Wavelets Transform for Efficient Token Mixing

author.name: Rana Aref Salama, Abdou Youssef, Mona Diab

entry.summary: WNet replaces self-attention in a Transformer encoder with token mixing based on the discrete wavelet transform, offering three attention-free mixers (linear fusion, learned gating, per-token scale selection) plus a hybrid that keeps attention only in the last layer. Receptive-field analysis shows wavelet mixers build multi-scale structure while avoiding quadratic cost. An interesting architecture-efficiency contribution, though results beyond the abstract are not visible.

entry.title: Usage-Modulated Sentiment Representations in Large Language Models

author.name: Hongfei Du, Jiacheng Shi, Yanfu Zhang, Gang Zhou, Ye Gao

entry.summary: This interpretability study tests whether sentiment in LLM activation spaces is captured by more than a single linear direction, examining how usage factors like tone and audience adaptation modulate sentiment representations. Using a controlled paired dataset that holds content fixed while varying polarity and usage factors, the authors analyze Llama, Mistral, and Gemma models, identify a shared sentiment direction, and probe residual structure via erasure and generation-time tone steering. The work contributes to mechanistic understanding of how pragmatic factors are encoded.

entry.title: Adaptive Utilization of Low-Rank Adaptation via Conditioned Gating

author.name: Guang Yang, Changhao Guan, Chao Huang, Yufeng Chen, Kaiyu Huang

entry.summary: U-LoRA improves parameter-efficient fine-tuning by using conditioned gating to learn token-level utilization coefficients along low-rank adaptation directions, rather than applying a shared low-rank update across all tokens. Sequence-level context coordinates and constrains these coefficients. This makes better use of the limited adaptation subspace for heterogeneous tokens.

entry.title: Improving Diversity in LLM Short Story Generation

author.name: Zahra Solati Dehkordi, Vasileios Lampos

entry.summary: DivLM is a two-phase post-training framework for diverse creative short-story generation: continued pre-training on a creative-writing corpus with weight residuals to restore instruction following, followed by RL with a composite reward that maximizes diversity across genre, tone, style, and named entities while preserving quality.

entry.title: Factorized Delayed Streams Modeling for LLM-based Streaming ASR

author.name: Tatsunari Takagi, Kai Washizaki, Atsushi Kojima, Lianbo Liu, Koki Nikaido, Yui Sudo

entry.summary: The paper simplifies LLM-based streaming speech recognition by removing a padding token from Delayed Streams Modeling and proposing F-DSM, which factorizes the waiting probability from the text-token distribution. This removes ASR-specific tokens from the text softmax and lets the large-vocabulary softmax be skipped on waiting steps, improving efficiency with competitive accuracy.

entry.title: PhysMamba: Selective State Space Models as Learned Articulated Body Simulators

author.name: Haochuan Zhang, Sinisa Todorovic

entry.summary: PhysMamba is the first learned articulated body simulator based on selective state space models, predicting full-body next-frame states from position, rotation, and joint-action history without velocity inputs. With CUDA graph compilation, Mamba2 achieves about 9,300 FPS on an H100 while maintaining rollout accuracy under partial observation.

entry.title: VCURF: Virtual Camera-based Uncertainty of Radiance Fields

author.name: Liyan Chen, Nathaniel Burgdorfer, Philippos Mordohai

entry.summary: VCURF quantifies pixel-wise uncertainty for radiance fields (NeRF and Gaussian Splatting) by measuring inconsistencies among renderings from virtual cameras sampled near a target viewpoint. It treats the radiance field as a black box requiring only color and depth rendering, making it applicable to arbitrary models.

entry.title: TRIM-ReID: Duplication-Aware Token Reduction and Modality-Aligned Interaction for Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification

author.name: Wanke Xia, Ruiding Zhu, Xingguo Xu, Zhengbo Zhang, Dongxia Liu, Yuan Jin, Taojie Zhu, Yiting Zhao, Yihang Ding

entry.summary: TRIM-ReID improves multi-modal re-identification across RGB, near-infrared, and thermal modalities by unifying dense feature extraction, duplication-aware intra-modal token reduction, and aligned inter-modal interaction. It targets the problem that globally aligned encoders lose fine-grained identity cues and duplicate tokens add noisy, costly computation.

entry.title: Probabilistic Pedestrian Forecasts from a Handheld Phone: World-Frame Heat Maps, Visual-Inertial Height Drift, and Evaluation without Ground Truth

author.name: Danial Safaei

entry.summary: The paper builds a system forecasting nearby pedestrian positions as world-frame probability heat maps using only a monocular camera and visual-inertial odometry on a handheld phone, trained with NLL loss on trajectory benchmarks. It honestly documents failure modes such as VIO height drift silently rescaling ground positions by large factors and proposes evaluation without ground truth.

entry.title: Robust Tensor Completion via Reflective Convolution Nuclear Norm Minimization

author.name: Weiguo Zhou, Feng Zhang, Wenjin Qin, Jianwen Huang

entry.summary: RCNNM replaces circular shifts with endpoint-nonrepeating reflection in convolutional low-rank tensor completion, avoiding artificial wrap-around neighborhoods for nonperiodic data. The authors establish high-probability exact recovery guarantees under random sampling and sparse corruption, supported by a weighted Gram identity with nonuniform entry multiplicities. This strengthens the theoretical foundations of convolution-based tensor recovery.

entry.title: SPACE-CLIPv2: Decoding Local Geometry from Frozen CLIP for Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Hyun Song, Taewan Cho, Kangmin Kim, Andrew Jaeyong Choi

entry.summary: SPACE-CLIPv2 is a frozen-backbone depth decoder that aggregates fixed local neighborhoods of CLIP tokens, predicting aggregation weights at selected decoder stages and injecting responses via gated residual updates, with a high-pass branch preserving local contrast. It extends prior work showing frozen CLIP features can support monocular depth by addressing how neighboring tokens combine to recover fine structure. Results are reported on NYU Depth benchmarks.

entry.title: Order Matters: Competition-Guided Query Ordering for RNN-Based Object Detection

author.name: Shengjian Wu, Li Sun, Yu Shangguan, Qingli Li

entry.summary: DETRNN is a plug-and-play module for DETR-style detectors that converts unordered object queries into a competition-aware sequence, ordered by confidence and similarity from prior predictions, then refined with an RNN to model intra-decoder competition. The goal is to stabilize training and make predictions more decisive in the absence of explicit de-duplication. This offers a fresh take on the well-known duplicate-hypothesis problem in one-to-one matching detectors.

entry.title: CleanMDM: Clean Motion Diffusion Model for Multimodal Motion Cleanup

author.name: Zhe Li, Shicheng Wang, Bowen Cai, Huan Fu

entry.summary: CleanMDM formulates motion capture cleanup (fixing missing segments, jitter, drift, and contact artifacts) as masked conditional generation with a multimodal motion diffusion model, enabling controllable cleanup inspired by animator workflows — preserving reliable segments and enforcing user intents rather than acting as a black-box denoiser. This matters for making mocap data directly usable in animation and embodied AI pipelines.

entry.title: Deep Prior Learning for Embodied Perception

author.name: Yimou Wu, Jiaxin Guo, Yun-hui Liu, Zheng Li

entry.summary: The authors present VPGGT, a VGGT-based transformer that extends OmniVGGT for embodied 3D perception by making better use of geometric priors such as camera poses, intrinsics, and depth. Key contributions include training with simulated sensor-motivated pose corruptions and a parameter-free prior residual connection that combats prior dilution, a failure mode where model predictions end up less accurate than the priors already available.

entry.title: Difference Feature Map Distillation: Transferring Inter-Sample Relational Knowledge Towards Efficient Transformer-Based Tracking

author.name: Zhicheng Ding, Xinyu Chu, Qing Tian

entry.summary: Presents DFM-KD, a relational knowledge distillation framework for transformer-based visual tracking that transfers inter-sample relational structure rather than point-wise feature differences. The goal is to compress SOTA trackers so they meet the latency and power constraints of autonomous driving platforms.

entry.title: LoDEOT: Low-Dimensional and Efficient Offset Tokens for Building Footprint Extraction from Off-Nadir Imagery

author.name: Kai Li, Zigan Zhou, Zhenyang Li, Hui Shan, Zhe Chen, Yupeng Deng, Zhihao Xi, Yu Meng, Yifan Peng, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: Derives a five-parameter sufficient descriptor for roof-to-footprint offset maps under local pinhole projection and vertical-extrusion assumptions, and uses this structural prior to design a compact 5D offset token replacing high-dimensional instance tokens in query-based footprint extraction. LoDEOT retains accuracy while improving efficiency.

entry.title: MaRO-GS: Mask-Robust Object-Centric Gaussian Splatting from Inconsistent Multi-view Masks

author.name: Eunji Kim, Gahyeon Kim, Gianella Cravioto, Dong-hun Lee, Chaewon Moon, Chae-yeong Song, Sang-hyo Park

entry.summary: MaRO-GS directly optimizes target-object Gaussians from object-masked multi-view images while remaining robust to mask inconsistencies across views, avoiding the computational overhead of reconstructing the whole scene. This addresses supervision corruption caused by unreliable 2D segmentation masks.

entry.title: Anatomy-aware Fine-grained Multimodal Fusion for Laryngopharyngeal Cancer T-Staging Prediction Using CT and Radiology Report

author.name: Xingyue Zhao, Yanzhou Su, Fang Zhang, Zhanghexuan Ji, Yirui Wang, Dazhou Guo, Sibo Ju, Yuehua Cheng, Yuzhen Chen, Ming Feng, Le Lu, Tsung-Ying Ho, Jian Wang, Dakai Jin, Na Shen

entry.summary: This paper presents a multimodal framework for predicting T-staging of laryngopharyngeal cancer from CT volumes and radiology reports, using anatomy-aware constraints and fine-grained cross-modal alignment. It avoids labor-intensive tumor segmentation while capturing organ-specific invasion patterns described in clinical text.

entry.title: Asynchronous Tracking, Optical Communication and 3D Motion Capture using Event-based Sensors

author.name: Ziwei Wang, Angus Apps, Holly Battisson, Iain Guilliard, Timothy Molloy, Robert Mahony

entry.summary: This paper uses event cameras as receivers for optical communication between robots, exploiting their high temporal resolution and low latency. The approach provides directional, spatially localized communication that addresses wireless limitations around source localization, clock synchronization, and broadcast-only signaling, combining tracking, communication, and 3D motion capture.

entry.title: Chance-Constrained Bi-Objective Evolutionary Optimization for the Open-Pit Mining Operational Planning Problem

author.name: Ishara Hewa Pathiranage, Aneta Neumann

entry.summary: The authors formulate open-pit mining operational planning as a bi-objective evolutionary optimization problem with chance constraints on stochastic ore grades, maximizing ore production while minimizing fleet cost. They derive a deterministic reformulation of two-sided chance constraints, avoiding costly sampling or simulation during fitness evaluation.

entry.title: The Quantum Sphere: A Physically Realizable Optimization Benchmark with Provable Linear Convergence in White- and Black-Box Settings

author.name: Ofer M. Shir

entry.summary: This paper revisits a quantum control objective, characterizes its exact local metric geometry, and proposes it as a rigorous benchmark for search and optimization. The author derives an exact representation of the yield gap as a nonnegative linear combination of sin-squared terms, from which a two-sided quadratic sandwich with ratio 4/pi-squared is proven on a certified worst-case region, establishing linear convergence guarantees in both white- and black-box settings.

entry.title: NM-LIO: Multiple LiDAR-Inertial Odometry Addressing LiDAR Measurement Noise Discrepancy

author.name: Gunhee Shin, Seungjae Lee, Minho Oh, Dongkyu Lee, Jaeyoung Lee, Youngwoo Seo, Hyun Myung

entry.summary: Proposes NM-LIO, a multi-LiDAR inertial odometry framework that explicitly models per-sensor measurement noise discrepancies rather than assuming uniform noise across LiDARs. It quantifies each LiDAR's noise and estimates residual uncertainty so the measurement update reflects sensor-specific reliability, improving localization accuracy.

entry.title: GR-LIO: A Local Ground-Aware LiDAR-Inertial Odometry System Using Body-to-Ground Height

author.name: Zhixin Zhang, Yang Song, Liang Zhao, Nathan Shankar, Barry Lennox, Pawel Ladosz

entry.summary: GR-LIO is a filter-based LiDAR-inertial odometry framework that explicitly exploits local ground plane geometry, parameterized by robot orientation and body-to-ground height, within state estimation. Incorporating the ground constraint improves localization accuracy and computational efficiency for ground mobile robots.

entry.title: Benchmarking Generative Trajectory Models for Active-Inference Control

author.name: Yulin Li, Mohsen A. Jafari, Andrea Matta

entry.summary: The paper introduces generative active-inference control (GenAIF), where a generative trajectory model learned from demonstrations supplies both a goal-conditioned policy distribution and an observation likelihood for belief updating. It derives three model requirements and benchmarks diffusion, autoregressive Transformers, CVAEs, and flow-based models against them.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aware Adaptive Corridors with Feasibility-Perturbed Trust-Region SQP for Certified Nonholonomic Motion Planning

author.name: Yang Shi

entry.summary: The paper presents an optimization-based parking planner for car-like vehicles with reverse gear where every solver iterate exactly satisfies discretized dynamics and keeps the full vehicle rectangle collision-free between time samples, using per-interval convex corridors with sweep margins. A feasibility-perturbed trust-region SQP with directional separating half-planes ensures executability even from in-collision initial guesses.

entry.title: Propagating Elevation-Map Uncertainty Through the Contact Maximum in Closed Form

author.name: Ale\v{s} Ku\v{c}era, Karel Zimmermann

entry.summary: The authors derive closed-form moments of the maximum over uncertain elevation-map cells for risk-aware path planning, using Clark's pairwise recursion and Gaussian quadratic-form identities instead of inaccurate first-order propagation or costly Monte Carlo sampling. A one-time calibration on two design traverses corrects residual standard-deviation shortfall, validated on 317 held-out routes. This gives risk-aware planners an efficient, accurate uncertainty propagation tool.

entry.title: MarvisNav: Making Memory Visible on Route Choices for Zero-Shot Object Navigation

author.name: Jincheng Wang, Chi Pui Chan, Wei Zeng, Shuyang Zhang, Jianhao Jiao, Dimitrios Kanoulas

entry.summary: MarvisNav is a zero-shot object navigation framework that renders exploration memory directly onto visual route choices, so the vision-language model sees target-likelihood cues and prior exploration in the same spatial context rather than fusing separate textual or map-based memory representations. This makes the correspondence between memory and route decisions explicit for the VLM. It aims to improve ZSON performance without task-specific training.

entry.title: Differentiable Ternary Temporal Logic Semantics with Polynomial Surrogate Networks

author.name: Ryan Matheu, Sai Sandeep Damera, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: The authors make ternary temporal logic differentiable for use in learning-based control synthesis, using polynomial surrogate networks to quantify semantics that include an Unknown verdict for uncertainty, unlike Boolean temporal logics. This enables gradient-based training of policies under temporal logic specifications while retaining the ability to abstain. It bridges formal methods for robotics with neural policy optimization.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Aware Distribution Matching for Inverse Problems with Unpaired Data

author.name: Thomas Ryckeboer (Thoth), Giacomo Meanti (MaLGA), Julien Mairal (Thoth)

entry.summary: This work targets recovering the forward operator of an imaging system from unpaired data, avoiding the need for calibration hardware or clean/degraded image pairs. The authors identify that distribution matching alone barely constrains operator components that are suppressed in degraded images, and propose a reconstruction-aware criterion that better distinguishes operators that invert differently. This is relevant to computational optics and imaging inverse problems.

entry.title: Regularization and Variance-Weighted Regression Achieves Minimax Optimality in Linear MDPs: Theory and Practice

author.name: Toshinori Kitamura, Tadashi Kozuno, Yunhao Tang, Nino Vieillard, Michal Valko, Wenhao Yang, Jincheng Mei, Pierre M\'enard, Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, R\'emi Munos, Olivier Pietquin, Matthieu Geist, Csaba Szepesv\'ari, Wataru Kumagai, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: The paper extends theoretical guarantees for mirror descent value iteration (MDVI), an abstraction of KL and entropy-regularized RL, from tabular MDPs to linear function approximation. It shows that variance-weighted least-squares regression achieves minimax sample complexity for epsilon-optimal policy identification in infinite-horizon linear MDPs. This bridges theory behind practical regularized RL algorithms and function approximation.

entry.title: Co-Supervised Tree Synthesis for Interpretable Subgroup Identification and Honest Treatment Effect Inference in Randomized Trials

author.name: Evgenii Kuriabov, Zhaoxue Tong, Jia Li

entry.summary: CausalSynthTree is a co-supervised method where black-box causal estimators guide construction of an interpretable tree for identifying patient subgroups with heterogeneous treatment effects in randomized trials. It partitions covariate space into cells, fits conditional average treatment effect models on both observed and synthetic teacher-labeled data, and builds the tree via a treatment-effect disparity criterion. It addresses the tension between black-box accuracy and interpretable, stable subgroup discovery in precision medicine.

entry.title: Anthropic's updated Certificate of Incorporation

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: The author retrieved and summarizes Anthropic's updated certificate of incorporation ahead of a planned IPO, noting that the public benefit mission and Class T governance provisions are unchanged, the board grew from 5 to 7 with the Long-Term Benefit Trust retaining a majority, and several investor veto rights were removed while fifteen new preferred share series were added. This provides primary-source insight into how Anthropic's governance structure is evolving under commercial pressure.

entry.title: Pressure, Context, and Machine Self-Control: A Criminological Test of Reward Hacking in Generative AI Models

author.name: Murat Ozer, Isaac Kofi Nti

entry.summary: This study applies criminological theories (self-control, general strain, anomie, neutralization, routine activity) to reward hacking in generative AI, measuring delay discounting and shortcut willingness across 2,310 conversations and seven models. It finds pressure raised discount rates dramatically and models chose shortcuts far more often under roleplay framing, suggesting responsiveness to conversational context rather than stable model traits.

entry.title: Do LLMs Understand Sequential Structure? A Controlled Study of Inference and Generation

author.name: Jerry Wang, Zhengxiang Wang, Ting Yu Liu, Hsin-Ling Hsu, Yi-Cheng Lai, Tengfei Ma

entry.summary: This controlled study uses two-player Rock-Paper-Scissors interactions and stochastic n-gram continuation tasks to test whether LLMs can recover latent sequential structure beyond surface action frequencies, separating distribution matching from conditional rule following. Results examine whether models identify latent strategies, follow Markov rules, and sustain higher-order conditional dependencies.

entry.title: Do Small Language Models Learn to Negotiate? A Controlled Scaling Study of RL-Trained Sellers

author.name: Pedro Tabacof, Sagar Joglekar

entry.summary: The authors train four Gemma 4 checkpoints (2.3B to 31B parameters) with GRPO on a programmatic utility reward for bilateral multi-issue bargaining and evaluate all arms on 1,152 negotiations against unseen frontier buyers. RL gains over the base model rise from +0.001 at 2.3B to +0.078 at 31B, suggesting small models benefit little from RL fine-tuning for negotiation.

entry.title: Orchestrating Specialized Agents for Trustworthy Enterprise RAG

author.name: Xincheng You, Qi Sun, Neha Bora, Huayi Li, Shubham Goel, Kang Li, Sean Culatana

entry.summary: ADORE is an agentic framework replacing linear RAG pipelines with iterative, user-steered investigation coordinated by a central orchestrator and specialized agents, centered on a structured Memory Bank with explicit claim-evidence linkage. It targets high-stakes enterprise decision settings requiring deep synthesis, traceability, and recovery from underspecified prompts.

entry.title: Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents

author.name: Mincheol Daniel Song, Joshua Ward, Jake Jung, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: Sentinel is a trajectory-derived, classifier-based confidence layer for LLM agents in clinical text-to-SQL settings. It decides at three points whether to stop: refusing unanswerable questions before execution, halting doomed reasoning trajectories mid-run, and withholding untrustworthy answers at delivery, thereby saving compute spent on outputs that must be discarded. This targets the critical reliability risk of autonomous agents in high-stakes healthcare contexts.

entry.title: On Semi-Markov Suboptimality in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bingyun Liu, Yuheng Jing

entry.summary: The paper separates execution and policy suboptimality in hierarchical reinforcement learning, introducing task and execution trees plus a Unified Value Function for HRL and a four-stage Generalized Hierarchical Bellman Equation. Under bounded rewards and uniform termination it establishes hierarchical policy and execution improvement results and characterizes when Markovian guarantees transfer across execution modes.

entry.title: What Does an Observability Foundation Model Know?

author.name: Dhyey Dharmendrakumar Mavani, Rian Atri, Tairan Ji

entry.summary: The paper audits Toto, an observability forecasting foundation model, on the BOOM benchmark using linear probes on its frozen residual stream compared to raw-window baselines and architecture-ablated controls. Cadence and metric type are more linearly recoverable from Toto's residuals than from raw input in every resplit, while domain is nearly tied and other properties reveal what the model encodes versus merely passes through.

entry.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collision-Free Locomotion of an Underactuated Biped

author.name: Jagannath Prasad Sahoo, Saurabh Kumar, Surya Prakash S. K., Samiran Datta, Abhay Dwivedi, Amit Shukla

entry.summary: Presents a hierarchical RL framework for an underactuated bipedal robot (no hip/ankle roll) where a high-level SAC-trained policy issues body-velocity commands from raycasts and obstacle states, tracked by a low-level velocity-conditioned policy with PD-controlled joints. This enables collision-free locomotion around moving obstacles on a platform where any deviation threatens balance. Solid robotics work combining balance-critical control with dynamic obstacle avoidance.

entry.title: Adaptive Expert Guidance for Efficient On-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daniele Affinita, Ming Xu, Rudolf Reiter, Davide Scaramuzza, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: The paper addresses how to balance guidance from a suboptimal expert (a heuristic, controller, or related-task policy) against reward learning in massively parallel on-policy RL like PPO. Existing methods use fixed schedules or extra learned components; this work proposes adaptively calibrating the expert's influence to speed early learning without capping final performance. Target domains include robotics simulation.

entry.title: MercerFlow: Flow Matching in a Kernel-Induced Latent Space for Probabilistic Forecasting

author.name: Ilya Kuleshov, Egor Serov, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: MercerFlow studies how the choice of latent map interacts with the prior in conditional flow matching for time-series forecasting, finding this underexplored relationship matters strongly. It embeds series via an invertible kernel-induced map into a single latent vector so a cheap tabular MLP can replace expensive sequential backbones like Transformers or S4. This yields efficient probabilistic forecasting with data-matched priors.

entry.title: AffordCraft: Scalable Construction of Task-Ready Simulation Assets from Single Images

author.name: Haoyun Yang, Xueyang Zhou, Ziyi Xie, Yongchao Chen

entry.summary: AffordCraft constructs simulation-ready articulated assets from a single RGB image and task instruction by retrieval rather than generation: it locates the object and part, selects a matching articulated asset from a library, and fits it to the image while preserving joints and physics validity. This avoids the instability of generatively predicted parts and joints in simulation. It matters because robot learning in simulation is bottlenecked by asset availability.

entry.title: Proximal Causal Learning under Unmeasured Confounding

author.name: Ying Tang, Yi Wang

entry.summary: PCL-U is a framework that learns proxy variables directly from observed covariates for proximal causal learning, removing the need for pre-specified proxies. Neural encoders decompose covariates into treatment-inducing, outcome-inducing, and shared components using minimax mutual information objectives, with causal estimates obtained via a moment-based risk. Benchmarks show it matches or outperforms existing baselines.

entry.title: Pareto-Improving Adversarial Attacks with Primal-Dual Regularization

author.name: Yang Dai, Longfei Zhang, Wei Tao, Li Shen, Jincai Huang, Qing Tao

entry.summary: The paper argues that the perceived trade-off between transferability and imperceptibility in adversarial attacks is an artifact of fixed-budget evaluation: on the ASR-imperceptibility Pareto frontier swept over epsilon, stronger transfer attacks are already less perceptible at matched success rates. It introduces ST, a plug-and-play stealthy transfer attack using primal-dual regularization to exploit this latent advantage. This reframes how transfer attack progress should be evaluated.

entry.title: GRAM: Correcting Frozen Time-Series Foundation Models via Graph-Retrieved Amplitude Memory

author.name: Xiaoyun Yu, Xiangfei Qiu, Yonggui Huang, Shixiang Tang, Nanqing Dong, Wanli Ouyang, Geguang Pu, Honggang Qi, Jilin Hu, Xi Chen

entry.summary: GRAM improves frozen time-series foundation models by retrieving and correcting forecasts using recurring systematic model bias in prediction errors, rather than the ground-truth futures of similar historical windows which mix transferable signal with sample-specific noise. The graph-based memory approach targets the failure modes specific to the foundation model.

entry.title: How Execution Assumptions Change Short-Horizon Sharpe Rankings: Evidence from a Synthetic Trading Benchmark

author.name: Weicheng Xue

entry.summary: This paper tests whether backtests of LLM trading agents that assume fills at closing price mislead, by evaluating five LLM signal policies and seven classical baselines under six execution settings across 2,462 runs. Rankings under realistic execution stress diverge sharply from near-ideal fills (Kendall tau drops to 0.21 in high-volatility regimes).

entry.title: METRO: Metric-Enhanced Token Routing Operator

author.name: Nodens Koren, Thomas Hofmann, Georgios Kissas

entry.summary: METRO replaces linear compatibility scores in slice-and-process neural operators with a learnable Mahalanobis metric, giving each latent slice an anisotropic local receptive field. This addresses redundancy and entanglement in latent slices caused by isotropic Euclidean clustering or unbounded linear decision regions.

entry.title: Inferring physical fields in coupled systems with unknown parameters from incomplete observations using physics-constrained attentive neural operators

author.name: Shilun Wei, Xiaoqiang Sun, Wei Li, Kejun Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-constrained attentive neural operator framework for full-field reconstruction and parameter identification of coupled physical systems from sparse observations of a single field. A cross-attention encoder maps sensor observations to a grid-conditioned latent representation, decoded by a Fourier neural operator, under unknown system parameters.

entry.title: The Optimization Landscape of Learning Compacted Context Models

author.name: Thomas Villeneuve, Alex Sandomirsky, Charles O'Neill, Max Kirkby, Michael Psenka

entry.summary: The authors study continual learning through KV-cache compaction, where a smaller set of KV vectors must match the behavior of the full cache through a frozen base model. They characterize why optimizing through a frozen model produces a brittle, flat loss landscape, and show that a heavily simplified Perceiver-based architecture matches the performance of more complex compaction approaches. The work connects memory compaction to direct memory manipulation without weight updates.

entry.title: StagQ: Constraint-Driven Multi-Precision Weight Quantization for LLMs

author.name: Zhe Wei, Mengqi Guo, Yuan Yuan, Jiunn Bin Lim, Boyi Pan, Michael Bi Mi

entry.summary: StagQ is a multi-precision weight format for LLM deployment in which a 2-bit group-wise affine base stream is refined by configurable 1-bit planes, so every supported precision is a readable prefix of the same bitstream. Decoding uses metadata shared across precisions with no per-weight lookup, and a sparse side record handles outlier weights the grid serves worst. The design enables serving one stream across a fleet of precision operating points.

entry.title: Pay to Learn, Share to Earn: Incentivized Federated Multi-Player Bandits

author.name: Pavamana K J, Chandramani Singh

entry.summary: The paper studies federated multi-player multi-armed bandits where self-interested players are not assumed to voluntarily share observations; instead, players are rewarded for sharing information and pay costs to buy information from a central server. It proposes an incentive-aware framework that makes collaboration compatible with rational, self-interested participation.

entry.title: Structured Representation Learning for Behavior Cloning: How can we learn to safely control a nuclear power plant?

author.name: Perceval Beja-Battais (CB), Alain Grosset{\^e}te (CB), Nicolas Vayatis (CB)

entry.summary: The paper studies behavior cloning of an expert NMPC policy for load-following control of a pressurized water reactor, a setting where component-level accuracy does not guarantee system-level safety. It proposes a structured architecture that encodes variables from each physical timescale into separate latent spaces before training a controller on the product latent space. Separated embeddings improve accuracy and constraint feasibility on long-horizon rollouts.

entry.title: OCL-PDE: A Generative Framework for PDE Inverse Problems with Observation-Complementary Latents

author.name: Ding Yang, Chuqi Chen, Chang Ma, Yang Xiang

entry.summary: OCL-PDE tackles ill-posed PDE inverse problems with a learned observation-complementary latent that preserves fine-scale information, letting observations guide large-scale structure while the latent supplies complementary detail. The framework combines a physics-aware autoencoder with conditional flow matching, supporting both inverse reconstruction and forward PDE prediction. Experiments show improved reconstruction accuracy and uncertainty handling.

entry.title: Generalizable Neural Downscaling of Earth System Model Wind Fields via Continuous Dynamics Modeling

author.name: Chenxi Yu, Jianan Wei, Hanlin Kong, Hao Sun, Bian He, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: The authors formulate global near-surface wind downscaling as an operator-learning problem on continuous atmospheric fields, developing a neural operator that maps coarse Earth System Model outputs to fine-scale fields across heterogeneous discretizations. This addresses the limitation of existing downscaling methods tied to fixed grids, improving generalization across models with different native resolutions.

entry.title: Masked Privileged-Information Distillation for Multimodal Skin Lesion Classification Under Missing Clinical Metadata

author.name: Anirban Barua, Md Mahir Abrar Khan, Ayman Iktidar, Md. Sajjatul Islam

entry.summary: The authors propose a privileged-information distillation framework in which a multimodal teacher trained on complete metadata supervises a 9.2x smaller student trained with randomly masked clinical field groups, covering the full metadata availability range in one training run. Residual fusion adds metadata as a gated correction to an image-only prediction. This targets realistic deployment where metadata is partially missing and compute is constrained.

entry.title: WASP: Weakly Aligned Spatiotemporal Pairs for Fetal Brain MRI-Ultrasound Learning

author.name: Francesco Correnti, Gabriele Magrini, Marco Mistretta, Niccol\`o Biondi, Pietro Pala, Alessandro Ramalli, Simona Fiori, Andrew D. Bagdanov, Matteo Lenge

entry.summary: Addresses the scarcity of paired fetal MRI-ultrasound data by learning from weakly aligned spatiotemporal pairs, teaching ultrasound-only models to understand fetal brain MRI from limited examples. This exploits the clinical asymmetry where ultrasound is cheap and abundant while MRI is costly but diagnostically superior. A clinically motivated cross-modal transfer approach with real data constraints.

entry.title: One Tile, Multiple Instances: Rethinking MIL for Sparse Diagnostic Evidence

author.name: Runsheng Liu, Cheng Jin, Hao Jiang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: DI-MIL decouples context encoding from instance granularity in whole-slide-image classification by clustering dense spatial tokens from a frozen foundation model within each tile, turning one tile into multiple weighted instance embeddings. As a training-free post-encoding module, it integrates into existing multiple-instance learning pipelines without re-encoding.

entry.title: Moment-Accurate Gaussian Mixtures for Constant-Step Stochastic Approximation

author.name: Xiaoli Li, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes moment-accurate Gaussian mixture characterizations of constant-step stochastic approximation, matching stationary energy with local Ornstein-Uhlenbeck limits and ruling out invisible quadratic tail mass. It yields observable covariances, expected objective gaps, and mean-shift predictions with Wasserstein error bounds of order sqrt of step size. The results strengthen the statistical foundations of constant-step SGD analysis.

entry.title: Dimension-Free Decentralized Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Yuanyu Wan, Lan Xue, Haomin Bai, Tong Wei, Mingli Song

entry.summary: The paper proposes a decentralized algorithm for finding (delta, epsilon)-Goldstein stationary points in nonsmooth nonconvex stochastic optimization that removes the polynomial dependence on problem dimension from both sample and communication complexity, matching dimension-free rates. This improves on prior work whose dimension dependence was a bottleneck in high-dimensional regimes. It is a solid optimization-theory advance for distributed training of non-smooth models.

entry.title: AnchorPose for Geometry-Aware MOF Assembly through Meso-Grained Pose Generation

author.name: Zhonglong Peng, Rui Jiao, Chang Chen, Geng Zhong, Qiuliang Liu, Shifeng Jin

entry.summary: AnchorPose is a generative framework for predicting metal-organic framework crystal structures from building blocks, representing each block via representative atoms and encoding the geometry-dependent, anisotropic effect of rotational errors into the pose representation. This improves on angular-error-based objectives that ignore block geometry. The work matters for AI-driven materials discovery, particularly porous materials for gas storage and separation.

entry.title: How well do routinely collected demographic and clinical variables aid point-of-care lung ultrasound TB classification

author.name: Joshua M. Jansen van V\"uren, Christiaan M. Geldenhuys, Devendra S. Parihar, V\'eronique Suttels, Trevor Brokowski, Ablo P. Wachinou, Mary-Anne Hartley, Rensu P. Theart, Grant Theron, Thomas R. Niesler

entry.summary: The study fuses lung ultrasound images with routinely collected clinical and demographic variables for deep-learning-based tuberculosis screening, targeting resource-constrained African healthcare settings. Starting from a ResNet baseline with AUROC 0.91, the authors compare three fusion strategies, finding simple average-based score fusion effective. The work has direct potential for deployable point-of-care TB triage.

entry.title: Direct Intermediate Initialization for Tilted Diffusion Samplers

author.name: Gregory D. Bellchambers

entry.summary: The paper observes that Gaussian-tilted intermediate distributions in diffusion posterior samplers can be pulled back to clean-space posteriors with weaker conditioning and transported via a Gaussian bridge. For the SMC sampler MCGDiff, this enables initializing at an intermediate time by sampling a softened clean-space posterior and running only the remaining SMC suffix, improving asymmetry-biased sampling balance.

entry.title: Efficient Test-time Adaptation through Candidate Verification and Divergence Shifts

author.name: Seungmin Oh, Seunghun Kang, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: The paper reframes test-time adaptation for vision-language models as candidate verification rather than prediction adjustment, proposing Test-Time Correction (TTC): hypothesize, reconstruct, and correct among top-k candidate labels. This avoids the computational overhead of logit-, prototype-, or cache-based adaptation while handling domain shift.

entry.title: Learning Subject-Specific Anatomical Representations via Manifold Expansion: Application to Accelerated Multi-Contrast MRI

author.name: Ruimin Feng, Wanyu Bian, Albert Jang, Zachary Stewart, Fang Liu

entry.summary: MAX is a subject-specific framework that learns contrast-invariant anatomical representations from a single fully sampled reference contrast to reconstruct accelerated multi-contrast MRI. It tackles the under-constrained separation of shared anatomy from contrast-dependent appearance by expanding the multi-contrast manifold with anatomy-prior constraints.

entry.title: LoopMoEVR: Loop-Based Degradation-Aware Mixture-of-Experts for Unified UHD Video Restoration

author.name: Yucheng Xin, Runci Bai, Yongcong Wang, Guangwei Gao, Jiao Liu, Dianjie Lu, Linwei Fan, Zhuoran Zheng

entry.summary: LoopMoEVR applies a loop-based learning paradigm to unified ultra-high-definition video restoration, using a degradation-conditioned low-rank loop embedding within a mixture-of-experts architecture to handle degraded UHD inputs across domains. The design keeps parameter counts low while maintaining strong regression capability, countering the trend of simply deepening models. It cites looped Transformers and recent frontier models as motivation for the loop paradigm.

entry.title: Prompt and Refinement: Asymmetric Mutual Learning for Infrared Small Target Detection with Noisy Labels

author.name: Yimin Fu, Songbo Wang, Lizhuo Liu, Baicheng Pan, Zhunga Liu, Michael K. Ng

entry.summary: Introduces PAR, a label-noise-robust asymmetric mutual learning paradigm for infrared small target detection pairing a pretrained SAM with a specialist model to handle noisy pixel-level annotations. The design mitigates misleading spurious patterns arising from inherently weak target distinctiveness and expensive expert annotation.

entry.title: A General Pipeline for Dense Illuminant Estimation via Physically Based Synthetic Data

author.name: Luca Cogo, Gianmarco Corti, Simone Bianco, Raimondo Schettini

entry.summary: The authors propose a reusable pipeline that generates pixel-wise dense illuminant chromaticity annotations from physically based 3D-rendered scenes, lowering the data acquisition barrier for learning-based illuminant estimation. By repurposing existing scene collections, it enables systematic dataset creation under controlled lighting.

entry.title: Online Target-less Radar-LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration via Joint Optimization

author.name: Gunhee Shin, Yunsoo Kim, Chanhyuk Lee, Wanhee Kim, Minwoo Lee, Sungwoo Han, Jeongwoo Woo, Hyuntai Chin, Minha Park, Hyun Myung

entry.summary: Presents an online, target-less method for calibrating extrinsics across a full radar-LiDAR-camera rig by jointly optimizing residuals from all sensor pairs instead of composing pairwise calibrations. The joint approach mitigates inconsistency across sensors and handles the sparsity and noise of radar measurements.

entry.title: VICON: Visual-Inertial-Contact based Hand-Object Tracking for Manipulation Datasets

author.name: Yubin Jeon, Uiseong Shin, Hwanchul La, Jaeseong Kang, Hyelim Choi, Yongseok Lee

entry.summary: VICON jointly captures hand and object motion, contact points, and contact forces during manipulation using a visual-inertial-contact tracking framework that remains robust under severe hand-object occlusion. It enables richer human demonstration datasets where contact supervision complements trajectory-only capture.

entry.title: MagServo: Uncertainty-Resilient Hierarchical Magnetic Servoing via Learned Latent Representations

author.name: Yuhan Tan, Yameng Zhang, Pei Liu, Yao Zhong, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: MagServo is a hierarchical learning-based framework for robust 6-DoF magnetic servoing that learns uncertainty-resilient latent magnetic representations via masked reconstruction and captures state-dependent robot-motion-to-magnetic-transition dynamics without analytical magnetic models or Jacobian supervision. The learned dynamics support control directly from latent features.

entry.title: Traversability-Aware Cooperative Path Planning for Human-UGV Casualty Evacuation

author.name: Kristian Dalland, Prithvi Poddar, Souma Chowdhury, Karthik Dantu, Ehsan T. Esfahani

entry.summary: This work formulates joint path planning for a human-UGV team in search-and-rescue casualty retrieval, notably modeling the human as a physical co-navigator with the Pandolf-Santee metabolic cost model and fatigue-modulated speed rather than relegating the person to supervisory roles. The UGV plan is coordinated with the human's mobility constraints and energy reserves. This reframes human-robot teaming as heterogeneous planning including human physiology.

entry.title: Barrier-Shaped Recurrent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Landing on a Heaving Ship Deck

author.name: Ritwik Shankar, Chiranjeev Prachand, Abhishek, Soumya Ranjan Sahoo

entry.summary: The paper trains a recurrent asymmetric actor-critic policy for UAV rotorcraft landing on a heaving ship deck, where the critic sees 6 seconds of future deck height during training while the actor uses only a 17-dimensional onboard-sensor state, trained across 4096 parallel simulations with vision-in-the-loop fine-tuning. Control-barrier-function stopping margins are incorporated at two stages to enforce vertical safety. This combines RL with formal safety filtering for a demanding maritime autonomy task.

entry.title: On the Comparison of Optimizers for Imbalanced Learning

author.name: Cl{\'e}ment Lezane (ANITI), Fran{\c c}ois Bachoc (LPP), J{\'e}r{\^o}me Bolte (ANITI), Jean-Michel Loubes (IMT, REGALIA)

entry.summary: The paper models deep learning training under data imbalance in continuous time, assuming the optimizer only sees aggregate losses without knowing majority/minority group structure. The authors characterize a region where majority losses are optimized regardless of minority structure and bound the time to leave it, showing milder dependence on minority amplitude for sign, spectral, and Newton descent compared to gradient descent. This offers theoretical guidance on optimizer choice for imbalanced data.

entry.title: ROAR: Unifying Runs across Heterogeneous AI-Driven Research Systems

author.name: Leo Y. Lin, Vishakha Ramani, Z. Berkay Celik, Paul Castro, Marquita Ellis

entry.summary: ROAR provides a relational schema and parsing layer to unify and analyze outputs from heterogeneous AI-driven research systems, whose expensive runs are currently fragmented across incompatible formats and isolated teams. It enables cross-system analytics despite differing objectives and scoring functions.

entry.title: Knowing the Store: What a Memory Backend Must Write Down Before an Agent Can Read It
