It provides an analytical failure mode for the Ring topology whose spectral gap decays as Theta(N^-2), implying slower consensus as scale grows.

entry.title: CLARA: Can AI Assess Developmental Appropriateness in Children's Stories?

author.name: Sijing Yin, Zirui Wang, Qian Liu, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: Introduces CLARA, a cognitively grounded framework for assessing children's narrative developmental appropriateness across cognitive, language, and social-emotional dimensions, plus a bilingual Chinese-English benchmark of 1,107 stories with structured annotations. It tests whether AI systems can approximate human developmental judgments at scale, relevant to educational recommendation and literacy research. A well-scoped application of AI to child development assessment.

entry.title: Parallelism or Concession? Concurrency-Aware Procurement Negotiation for Agentic Commerce

author.name: Xiaolin Xu, Donghao Zhu

entry.summary: This paper models a one-unit post-order sourcing problem where an agentic buyer forges parallel negotiations with sellers, jointly choosing the number of negotiators and a price cap under a hard deadline. The model captures per-thread costs, fulfillment loss, and excess-commitment risk from simultaneous agreements, and derives structural results including a geometrically decaying marginal value of extra negotiators. It provides theory for resource-rational concurrent agent negotiation.

entry.title: Few-Shot Prototype Head Adaptation for On-Device ECG Personalization on PSoC~6

author.name: Guilherme Silva, Pedro Silva, Gladston Moreira, Eduardo Luz

entry.summary: The paper proposes prototype-only head adaptation as a lightweight personalization primitive for TinyML ECG arrhythmia detection on microcontrollers, avoiding backpropagation through convolutional layers and optimizer state. A 1-D CNN with about 1,300 parameters adapts via few-shot prototype updates on a PSoC 6 device. This enables patient-specific on-device adaptation under severe resource constraints.

entry.title: MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents

author.name: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao, Qingyuan Liu, Tao Feng, Bohan Liu, Weida Liang, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: MemPilot is a flexible framework that orchestrates on-demand multimodal memory curation for LLM agents under explicit performance-cost-latency preferences, moving away from query-agnostic memory construction. It optimizes when and how memory operations run at runtime, offering control over the tradeoffs that fixed memory schemes ignore. This addresses growing costs and information loss in agent memory systems.

entry.title: Gated Target Propagation for Compositional Generalization in Continual Learning

author.name: Abdel Mfougouon Njupoun, Colin Bredenberg, Blake Aaron Richards, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: GaTaP is a continual learning algorithm using task-specific gating variables learned via a closed-form inner-loop update to selectively suppress or enhance network modules, with parameters trained on a slower outer loop using local difference target propagation signals. Beyond avoiding catastrophic forgetting, it supports recombination of prior knowledge for novel task compositions. Experiments cover class-incremental learning on multilayer networks.

entry.title: KALEIDO: Input-Space Adaptation of a Vision Model for Time-Series Forecasting Through Gated Fold Geometries

author.name: Xiangyu Shi, Qinghua Liu, Sam Heshmati, Zubin Abraham

entry.summary: KALEIDO repurposes an ImageNet-pretrained masked autoencoder for zero-shot time-series forecasting by rendering series as images, and adapts the rendering geometry itself by detecting dominant periods and generating multiple fold geometries. A convex per-position gate fit on validation data combines the inpaintings with the zero-shot output, requiring no temporal pretraining.

entry.title: Usefulness of Quantile-Aware Diffusion Modeling for Highly Imbalanced Tabular Data

author.name: Abu Talha, Peng Liu, Souradyuti Paul

entry.summary: Proposes a quantile-aware diffusion modeling approach for generating synthetic data in highly imbalanced classification settings such as FinTech and healthcare, arguing standard diffusion models with quadratic loss lack sensitivity to rare, extreme values in skewed or heavy-tailed tabular distributions. The method captures tail structure to better augment minority classes.

entry.title: Reachability-Aware Diffusion Policy Optimization

author.name: Hikmet Simsir, Kutay Demiray, Ozgur S. Oguz

entry.summary: RADPO is a model-free method for safety-aware online optimization of diffusion policies, combining predictive first-hit reachability estimation with cumulative-cost budget feedback. It learns a discounted first-hit reachability value that weights sooner cost events more heavily, uses this to shape rewards, and adjusts shaping strength via a dual-like multiplier based on realized costs. No explicit dynamics model is required.

entry.title: Gated Graph Neural Networks for Learning Hidden Independent Cascade Dynamics

author.name: Anubha Goel, Illia Oleksiienko, Mateusz Wilinski, Alexandros Iosifidis, Juho Kanniainen

entry.summary: The paper tackles the inverse problem of estimating per-node spreading probabilities in the Hidden Independent Cascade model from noisy proxy observations, without access to per-node activation times. Gated graph neural networks are used to infer node-level parameters whose count scales with the graph, marginalizing over unobserved spreading outcomes. Applications include modeling information and disease spread on social networks.

entry.title: Bounded Reasoning: Cognitive Hierarchy in Human-versus-AI Cyber Defense

author.name: Zahra Aref, Sheng Wei, Narayan B. Mandayam

entry.summary: The paper studies a sequential cyber-defense game where human or RL defenders face a DQN attacker, comparing human play under reward-only versus reward-plus-transition information structures aligned with Cognitive Hierarchy Theory-driven DQN. It critiques single-score human-agent evaluations by examining how human and automated policies adapt differently over time.

entry.title: Transporting Unsecured Stacked Payloads with a Quadrupedal Robot via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nobuo Namura, Masayuki Hiromoto, Kento Uemura, Hironobu Sasaki, Kanata Suzuki

entry.summary: PAMORT trains a quadrupedal robot to carry unsecured stacked boxes on a torso-mounted board without payload sensors, using a multi-objective RL base policy conditioned on a preference vector over locomotion and payload-stability rewards, with an online weight adjuster adapting preferences from proprioception. This addresses the real trade-off between aggressive locomotion and payload stability on uneven terrain. It is a practical legged-robotics contribution with a clean preference-conditioned design.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Optimization of Workload-Aware Power Delivery Networks

author.name: Oran Hayes, Maria Pantazi-Kypraiou, Athanasios Tziouvaras, George Stamoulis, Anuj Pathania, Shreejith Shanker, George Floros

entry.summary: The paper presents an RL framework for optimizing power delivery networks in VLSI chips, using architectural power traces from system-level simulations to allocate PDN resources according to local current demand. This workload-aware approach avoids the over-provisioning inherent in worst-case conventional design while satisfying electromigration and IR-drop constraints. It demonstrates ML improving chip-level power infrastructure design.

entry.title: KESurv: A Kernel Ensemble Method for Patient-Specific Survival Prediction

author.name: Rahul Goswami

entry.summary: The paper proposes an ensemble for patient-specific survival prediction that combines a Survival Forest master model with base models and a Beran kernel estimator to improve survival curve predictions. Evaluation on four healthcare datasets shows better calibration and discrimination than baselines.

entry.title: The \`{I}r\`{o}y\`{i}nSpeech Text Corpus: 24,905 Curated Yor\`ub\'a Sentences for Speech and Language Technology

author.name: Kola Tubosun, Aanuoluwapo Aremu, Tolulope Ogunremi, Iroro Orife, David Ifeoluwa Adelani

entry.summary: This paper releases the text component of the IroyinSpeech corpus: 24,905 unique, hand-verified, tone-marked Yoruba sentences (42 hours of aligned read speech from 80 speakers) curated as recording prompts, combining adapted openly licensed news material with in-house writing to broaden coverage beyond religious translation. Every sentence was checked for tone-mark accuracy and localized naming conventions. It is a valuable resource for Yoruba speech and language technology.

entry.title: JEV versus LLMs: Accuracy, Cost and Calibration on Seven Political Science Replications

author.name: Matthew DiGiuseppe, Steven Denney

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests claims made for JEV, a commercial System One model that returns decisions and calibrated probability distributions over fixed answer sets, comparing its accuracy, cost, and calibration against conventional LLMs on seven political science replication tasks. It provides an independent assessment of whether the advertised cost/speed/calibration advantages hold. Relevant to social scientists choosing annotation models.

entry.title: Synthetic Cultural Agents from Aggregate Anchors

author.name: Augusto Gonzalez-Bonorino (Department of Economics, Arizona State University, EconLLM Lab), Kseniia Biriukova (EconLLM Lab, Department of Information Systems, Arizona State University), Monica Capra (EconLLM Lab, Department of Economics, Claremont Graduate University)

entry.summary: The paper proposes mapping aggregate preference anchors from the Global Preferences Survey into group-indexed choice policies via DPO on a bank of paired synthetic responses, as an alternative to population prompts for generating synthetic survey responses. Adapters are evaluated on World Values Survey items with country-omitting prompts to disentangle imposed labels from pretrained associations.

entry.title: FlashGaze: Training-Free Multi-Scale Patch Pruning For Efficient Video Understanding

author.name: Ziye Zhu, Yanghao Zhou, Lixing Tan, Jialiang Kang, Shuxuan Li, Xiao Yang

entry.summary: FlashGaze is a training-free method that prunes redundant spatial-temporal patches before ViT encoding in multimodal LLM video pipelines, reducing compute that post-encoding token pruning methods leave untouched. Unlike learned pre-encoding selectors, it requires no auxiliary networks or extra training.

entry.title: Investigating Spatiotemporal Redundancy in Video Transformer for Collision Anticipation

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou

entry.summary: This study analyzes where computation is redundant in video transformers for worker-equipment collision anticipation, using VideoMAEv2-Base on the Nexar Collision Prediction dataset. It examines how collision-relevant information evolves with depth and evaluates spatial and temporal token pruning to cut latency and carbon cost on mobile robots.

entry.title: Analysis of SWIR Imaging Detection Performance Under Adverse Environmental Conditions for Autonomous Driving Systems

author.name: Rohan Mehra, Alexandre Riffard, Yannis Loumouamou, Mathieu Labussi\`ere

entry.summary: This is a systematic comparative study of paired RGB versus short-wave infrared object detection for autonomous driving on the RASMD dataset, finding that RGB is comparable or superior in most scenarios. It also introduces a sensor-dominance mining framework combining multi-model agreement with manual inspection.

entry.title: FloVMos: Optical Flow-based Medical Video Mosaicking

author.name: Jinyang Liu, Sandesh Ghimire, Chaman Singh, Jennifer Dy, Milind Rajadhyaksha, Dana H. Brooks, Octavia Camps, Kivanc Kose

entry.summary: FloVMos is a generalizable optical-flow-based deep learning framework for real-time video mosaicking across diverse biomedical imaging modalities, addressing non-rigid deformation and modality-specific artifacts. It fine-tunes an optical flow model on synthetic data with ground-truth deformation fields to achieve robust pixel-level registration.

entry.title: Real-Time Conformal-Seeded Hybrid Inverse Kinematics for Offset Redundant Manipulators

author.name: Duc Cuong Vu, Van Tung Nguyen, Duc Hai Nguyen, Manh Cuong Nguyen, Vu Trung Tran, Minh Nhat Vu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage hybrid inverse kinematics framework for offset redundant 7-DoF humanoid-class arms, using approximate analytical IK with conformal-calibrated seed selection to warm-start numerical IK on the full kinematic model. This addresses AIK's inexactness for offset structures and NIK's initialization sensitivity while maintaining real-time performance.

entry.title: Unifying Gradient Estimators for Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Tadashi Kozuno, Mark Rowland, R\'emi Munos, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper provides a unifying framework for estimating higher-order derivatives of value functions, needed in meta-reinforcement learning, based on off-policy evaluation. It interprets prior approaches as special cases, clarifies bias-variance trade-offs in Hessian estimates, and introduces new estimator variants implementable with autodiff libraries that improve performance. This reduced the engineering fragility of meta-RL gradient estimation.

entry.title: Marginalized Operators for Off-policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yunhao Tang, Mark Rowland, R\'emi Munos, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This work introduces marginalized operators, a new class of off-policy evaluation operators for RL that strictly generalize multi-step operators like Retrace. The framework enables scalable sample-based estimates with variance reduction and generalizes marginalized importance sampling. Empirical results show gains for off-policy evaluation and downstream policy optimization.

entry.title: The Reported Engagement with AI Level (REAL) Rating: A Framework for Disclosing Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Im\`ene Goumiri, Mayleen Cortez-Rodriguez, Eric Bell, Amanda Muyskens

entry.summary: The REAL Rating proposes a six-tier scale (Levels 0-5) for disclosing the extent of AI involvement in content creation, moving beyond binary human/AI labels and opaque watermarking. It aims to give user-facing provenance clarity across different production workflows.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning VLM for Enhancing AI's Spatial Intelligence: Understanding 3D and 2D Rotations

author.name: Uttamasha Monjoree, Wei Yan

entry.summary: This companion paper to the authors' agentic-CoT study fine-tunes Gemma-4 mixture-of-experts vision-language models on object-rotation datasets and shows significant gains in 2D and 3D rotation prediction over fine-tuned generalist variants. It demonstrates that targeted fine-tuning plus MoE specialization substantially improves spatial reasoning. The work has applied relevance for STEM, medicine, and construction domains.

entry.title: CI-JEPA: A Counterfactual Analysis of Latent Representations in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Mintu Dutta, Ritesh Vyas, Mohendra Roy *

entry.summary: CI-JEPA extends I-JEPA with counterfactual intervention awareness, learning to predict representation changes between original and modified images, and assesses robustness via selective sensitivity to task-relevant semantic changes versus nuisance changes. Experiments on Flowers102 use flower-center occlusion as a case study.

entry.title: CreativeFlow: A One-to-Many Analogical Relation Transfer Method for 3D Asset Generation

author.name: Xuechen Li, Shuai Zhang, Nanxuan Zhao, Qing Chen

entry.summary: CreativeFlow is a text-to-3D generation framework inspired by cognitive science that models analogical divergent thinking to combat creative homogenization in generated 3D assets. It produces relationally similar source-target asset pairs with distinct geometry, and the resulting corpus serves as a dataset and benchmark for relation-aware 3D model training.

entry.title: The GenAI4IDN Benchmark 3.0 - a Public Tool to Assess Generative AI Tools for the Design of Interactive Digital Narratives

author.name: Hartmut Koenitz, Jonathan Barbara, Mirjam Palosaari Eladhari

entry.summary: GenAI4IDN Benchmark 3.0 is the third iteration of an evaluation framework for generative AI in interactive digital narratives, now delivered as a public web app with AI-assisted, blinded evaluation supporting complex media like music, video, and full IDNs. It adds fact-checking and bias detection tasks responding to community concerns from ICIDS 2025.

entry.title: Process Constitutions and Process Stewards: Towards the Next Generation of BPM for Agentic Organizations

author.name: Amin Jalali, Majid Rafiei

entry.summary: This position paper argues that Business Process Management's founding assumption of human actors is depreciating as AI agents execute and adapt organizational work autonomously. It proposes two concepts: the Process Constitution, a machine-interpretable, value-laden specification of admissible agent behavior, and the Process Steward, a governance role for agentic organizations.

entry.title: Proof-Grounded Patient-Specific Clinical Explanations from Knowledge-Graph Reasoning

author.name: Surajit Das

entry.summary: The CKG Clinical Explanation Engine converts patient inference states and disease knowledge from a frozen, training-free clinical knowledge-graph reasoner into typed facts, explicit rule-application traces, provenance-linked conclusions, and policy-licensed recommendations. It carefully separates observed evidence from missing data and partial representation to support auditable clinical decision support.

entry.title: Beyond Private Training: The New Landscape of AI Privacy

author.name: Sean Culatana, Kang Li

entry.summary: Despite a privacy-themed title, the paper formalizes the distinction between output safety and traversal safety in deletion from graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, where deleted embeddings may still be used in distance computations during graph traversal. It introduces TSD-AUDIT for auditing traversal-safe deletion, showing on Faiss IndexHNSWFlat that native filtering leaves distance computations unchanged and that trace-faithful replay detects deleted-vector scoring in all 100 audited queries at a 70% deletion rate.

entry.title: OceanMind: A multi-agent AI system for ocean diagnosis

author.name: Fan Zhang, Weicong Cheng, Yuheng Chen, Hiuseut Kung, Ying Zhang, Aixi Han, Quanjia Zhong, Can Yang, Jianping Gan

entry.summary: OceanMind is a multi-agent LLM system coupling language models with time-dependent 3D ocean states for scientific diagnosis, organized into four stages: query routing, skill-based planning, tool execution, and evidence-based summary generation. Specialized agents interpret requests and construct analysis to support ocean science and environmental hazard management.

entry.title: MAGEFormer: Learning Metric-Consistent Representations for Anisotropic CT Segmentation

author.name: Jiaying Li, Paolo Remagnino

entry.summary: MAGEFormer embeds physical metric constraints into vision transformer representations for anisotropic CT segmentation, addressing the mismatch between isotropic Euclidean voxel lattices and anisotropic clinical acquisition. It introduces Metric-Adaptive Spatial Embedding to calibrate positional frequencies by voxel spacing and Geometry-Constrained Attention to suppress physically implausible correlations, avoiding accuracy loss from isotropic resampling. The result is geometry-aware volumetric segmentation tailored to clinical reality.

entry.title: Attention-Based Surface Representation Learning for Robot State Prediction and Open-Ended Surface Classification

author.name: Oleg Kushnarev, Alexander Belyaev

entry.summary: The authors propose an open-ended terrain classification approach for outdoor robots where new surface classes can be added as trainable vectors, trained via next-state prediction with attention blocks. They report 98.56% accuracy on their own dataset and 94.8% on BorealTC.

entry.title: Neurodiversity-Aware Multimodal Affective Computing for Neurodevelopmental Assessment: From Norm-Referenced Classification to Context-Sensitive Decision Support

author.name: Mateusz Pomianek, Anna {\L}\k{e}\.zniak-Seruga

entry.summary: A conceptual article proposing a testable architecture for neurodiversity-aware multimodal affective computing, arguing that population-relative deviation should not be treated as sufficient evidence of adverse functioning. Explicitly reports no new study or trained system, instead framing a shift from norm-referenced classification to context-sensitive decision support.

entry.title: EasyClassifier: Honest, Reproducible Machine-Learning Classification for Researchers Who Do Not Program

author.name: Ahmad B. A. Hassanat, Ghada A. Altarawneh

entry.summary: EasyClassifier is an open-source Python package that guides non-programming researchers from spreadsheet data to a valid ML classification analysis via plain-language multiple-choice questions. It prevents two common errors, data leakage and selection bias, by making the correct procedure the default, learning preprocessing inside each training fold.

entry.title: DialectSentEval 2026: Arabic Dialect Sentiment Analysis and Swapping Shared Task

author.name: Saad Ezzini, Shadi Abudalfa, Maram Alharbi, Salmane Chafik, Hind Alatawi, Mo El-Haj, Ahmed Abdelali, Osamah Alnahari, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: This paper introduces DialectSentEval, a shared task at ArabicNLP 2026 with two subtasks: multi-class multi-dialect sentiment analysis and a generative sentiment-swap task that inverts polarity while preserving content. It addresses the persistent difficulty of dialectal Arabic in NLP and provides a community benchmark that will likely spur new resources and models for under-served Arabic dialects.

entry.title: Word-Level Text Unmixing via Evidence-Preserving Ownership Routing with Language Models

author.name: Jinglin He, Siyang Jiang, Lixing He, Guoliang Xing, Hongkai Chen

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Word-Level Text Unmixing: recovering original source sequences from an interleaved lexical stream with exact word and order preservation. It proposes EPOR, which decouples source-ownership prediction from reconstruction so a causal LLM routes words to owners instead of generating separated text directly, avoiding omission, duplication, or hallucination. This is relevant to overlapping transcripts, document flows, and concurrent agent streams.

entry.title: On architectural choices for interpretability and thermodynamic consistency in Physically Recurrent Neural Networks in the low-data regime

author.name: M. A. Maia, K. A. Meyer, A. M. C. M. van Gils, I. B. C. M. Rocha, F. P. van der Meer

entry.summary: Studies how decoder architecture choices affect latent space interpretability in Physically Recurrent Neural Networks, introducing a weight normalization constraint that regularizes training in low-data regimes. Case studies show fictitious stress states can align with true microstructure states without explicit supervision, enabling multi-task reuse of microscopic information without extra parameters.

entry.title: LocusRL: Diagnosing LLM Reward and Policy Interventions in Competitive Games

author.name: Chengyu Luan, Bo Xin, Songyan Guo, Yuxiang Zuo, Ahmed Yazdan, Jiahang Li, Yicheng Liu

entry.summary: LocusRL is a diagnostic framework for settings where LLMs intervene in reinforcement learning through both reward design and action selection, connecting controlled reward-policy comparisons with audits of reward judgments, signal delivery, objectives, and executed actions. Using Connect Four training runs across multiple seeds, it traces performance differences to testable explanations and validates corrections via counterfactual replay. It addresses the problem that aggregate returns conceal differing learning mechanisms.

entry.title: Low-Fidelity FDM Spectral Guidance for Neural Eigenvalue Solvers

author.name: Aryan Chaudhary, Manikandan Padmanaban, Jagabondhu Hazra

entry.summary: The paper proposes using a cheap coarse finite-difference method computation as spectral guidance for neural eigenvalue solvers, using approximate eigenvalues as fixed shifts during training to accelerate convergence and improve targeting of desired eigenvalues. This hybrid classical-neural approach avoids the cost of fine-grid classical solvers while mitigating slow neural training (hundreds of thousands of steps) and missed eigenvalues. A pragmatic example of classical-numerics-informed neural PDE solving.

entry.title: Repeated-Measure Leakage, Distribution Shift, and Reliability under Partial Observation in Patient World Models

author.name: Arjun Subramanian

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether patient world models generalize across patients, survive realistic distribution shifts and missing observations, and emit meaningful reliability signals, using digital-biomarker forecasting on the PhysioNet GaitPDB dataset. It benchmarks persistence, ridge, MLP, GRU, Transformer, and JEPA-style predictors, identifying repeated-measure leakage as a key evaluation pitfall.

entry.title: Fast Convergence through Distributed Augmentation for Class-Imbalanced Federated Learning

author.name: Arathi Nair M, J. Harshan, Anwitaman Datta

entry.summary: The paper establishes a formal relationship between minority-class augmentation and federated learning convergence, then proposes DAFL, which determines the minimum augmentation per client-class pair by jointly minimizing augmentation and training time. This avoids the excessive augmentation and slowdowns of heuristic approaches.

entry.title: Compact set-valued deep ensembling in multi-class classification

author.name: Kim-Dung Tran, Dang-Man Nguyen, Vu-Linh Nguyen, Xuan-Truong Hoang, S\'ebastien Destercke, Van-Nam Huynh

entry.summary: The paper proposes compact deep ensembling using Bayesian neural networks and Monte-Carlo dropout CNNs to reduce training and storage burdens of ensembles, producing a representative distribution via statistical distance minimization. This distribution defines Bayes-optimal set-valued (cautious) predictions that are robust across multiple utilities.

entry.title: Delay-coordinate reconstruction and conditional-moment causal diagnostics in stochastic systems

author.name: Jun Ohkubo

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional-moment interpretation of delay-coordinate reconstruction for stochastic systems, where delay vectors reconstruct conditional moments of a future distribution rather than a deterministic trajectory. It connects this view to Fokker-Planck dynamics and moment hierarchies, yielding Takens-like finite-dimensional approximations and causal diagnostics.

entry.title: Feature identification for parameter extraction and defect detection using machine learning

author.name: Yan Guo, Helda Pahlavani, Artem Khachaturiants, Khalid Elsayed, Jakob van de Laar, Erik Simons, Niranjan Saikumar, Hamed Sadeghian

entry.summary: Companion work on ML for semiconductor metrology, addressing critical-dimension parameter extraction from 3D structures across varying layers and nanometer-scale defect detection from low-resolution images in the EUV era. It develops feature identification methods to support automated in-line process control without layer-specific dedicated algorithms.

entry.title: Strategic Multi-Agent Learning for Interpretable Action Valuation of All Players in Football

author.name: Kenjiro Ide, Taiga Someya, Kohei Kawaguchi, Keisuke Fujii

entry.summary: This paper proposes a football action-valuation framework modeling each possession as a finite-horizon dynamic game with all 22 players as autonomous agents, using Markov perfect equilibrium as a motivating solution concept. This captures strategic interdependence, including off-ball movement and defensive positioning, which prior RL methods aggregate at team level or estimate independently. Interpretability is enhanced through additional modeling choices.

entry.title: Two-Point Local Optimality in $k$-Means via Boundary-Point Screening

author.name: Wenlong Lyu, Xujie Xiao, Yuheng Jia

entry.summary: The paper introduces r-point local optimality for k-means, where no reassignment of at most r points decreases the objective, and develops efficient certification for the r=2 case. It proves that improving two-point moves must involve clusters shared by both reassignments and only boundary points can participate, cutting the exhaustive O(n^2(k^2+d)) certification cost. This yields stronger local-optimality guarantees than Lloyd's algorithm with feasible computation.

entry.title: Where Does the Semantic Gain Come From? A Reproduction and Extension of Semantic Knowledge-driven Contrastive Learning for Long-Tailed Recognition

author.name: Sushrut Ghimire

entry.summary: This single-author reproduction study reimplements SKCL, BCL, and ConCutMix in one framework with three seeds per configuration and finds that SKCL, as described, performs 0.56 points below BCL rather than the reported 2.01-point gain, with the apparent advantage coming from an interaction with ConCutMix. The paper demonstrates the value of careful reproduction and multi-seed evaluation. It questions a published claim in long-tailed recognition.

entry.title: JASPER: Special Session on Joint Reliability And Security Assessment of SPlit Computing for Edge Robustness

author.name: Enrico Magliano, Giuseppe Esposito, Amir Hossein Shahdadian, Rama Mounika Kodamanchili, Juan David Guerrero Balaguera, Juan Esteban Rodriguez Condia, Annachiara Ruospo, Roberta Siciliano, Stefano Di Carlo, Maksim Jenihhin, Marco Levorato, Alessandro Savino, Matteo Sonza Reorda, Christian Herglotz, Michael H\"ubner, Mahdi Taheri

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework for jointly assessing reliability and security in split computing, where DNN inference is partitioned between edge devices and cloud servers. It characterizes reliability via neuron-level fault injection (MRAD) and security via feature-map-aware adversarial attacks (ASR), combining them into a Joint Vulnerability Score. This recognizes that hardware faults and adversarial threats interact on shared intermediate representations.

entry.title: MOXIE: Discovering Alternative Explanations for Biomedical Image Classifiers

author.name: Abiha Tahsin Chowdhury, Rahul Dubey

entry.summary: MOXIE is an evolutionary multi-objective framework that searches over segment subsets to return a Pareto front of alternative explanations for biomedical image classifier predictions, rather than a single LIME-style explanation. It uses NSGA-II with four segmentation methods and exposes how segmentation choice shapes discoverable explanations.

entry.title: What Does It Cost to Simulate a Quantum Sentence Classifier? An Energy and Compute Perspective on Near-Term QNLP

author.name: Kishlay Kashyap, Sandipan Ganguly

entry.summary: This measurement study quantifies the classical simulation cost of variational quantum classifiers for SST-2 sentiment classification across a 27-configuration grid of dataset size, qubit count, and circuit depth. The VQC beats its matched logistic regression baseline in only 6 of 27 single-seed comparisons, exposing the compute burden hidden behind accuracy tables in quantum NLP. It offers a sober efficiency and energy accounting for the field.

entry.title: On Learning Optimal Corners in Orthogonal Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Galleries

author.name: Yassin Ben Mansour, Edwin Meriaux

entry.summary: The paper augments the CADENCE algorithm for the Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Gallery Problem with learned corner-selection heuristics that preserve its formal coverage and connectivity guarantees. Two approaches are explored: a CNN scoring grid-encoded candidates and a GATv2 network trained with Deep Q-Learning on a visibility graph. Across 7,500 randomized environments at varying scales, the learned heuristics outperform baseline CADENCE and ISDA baselines in steps to coverage, peak agent count, and agent utilization.

entry.title: Ideological Stance Detection in a Low-Resource Language: Polarization in Bangladeshi Public vs Private University Discourse on Social Media

author.name: Safaruzzaman Shovo, Monowar Islam, Asif Hossain, Sameya Akhter, Md. Shamsul Islam

entry.summary: The paper releases a manually annotated dataset of 4,060 Bengali social media comments labeled for pro-public, pro-private, or neutral stance on the public vs private university debate, with high inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss's Kappa 0.89). It benchmarks classical ML, BiLSTM, BanglaBERT hybrids, and zero-shot LLMs including Claude Sonnet 4, DeepSeek-V3.1, and Llama 4 Maverick on this low-resource stance task. A useful resource for Bengali NLP and computational social science.

entry.title: Towards cross-cultural study of folksong lyrics with machine translation

author.name: Anna Dvo\v{r}\'akov\'a, Anna Aljanaki, Danbinaerin Han, Peter van Kranenburg, Mat\v{e}j Kratochv\'il, Inna Lisniak, Zden\v{e}k Vejvoda, Jan Haji\v{c} jr

entry.summary: This paper enables cross-cultural comparative musicology on lyrics by machine-translating folksong corpora across five languages into a pivot language and applying a pre-trained neural topic model. It examines the relationship between lyrical content and social function within and across languages, opening a research area previously blocked by language barriers. The work demonstrates NLP's value for humanities and social science research at scale.

entry.title: Breaking Bureaucracy: Evaluating open-source LLMs for legal document review

author.name: Farrukh Baratov, Niki van Stein, Suzan Verberne

entry.summary: This evaluation benchmarks open-source generative LLMs on legal natural language inference using ContractNLI and NLI4Wills, motivated by privacy-constrained legal inspectorial workflows requiring local models. Gemma-4 26B, an existing open model released earlier in 2026, performs best at 81.2% accuracy, even beating the supervised baseline on one metric. The study also analyzes invalid output rates and stability across temperature settings.

entry.title: Any-scale Object Detection using Arbitrary-scaled Images

author.name: Kazutoshi Akita, Norimichi Ukita

entry.summary: The authors propose any-scale object detection that uses arbitrary-scale super-resolution to continuously rescale object images instead of discrete multi-scale pyramids. To control false positives from independently processing many super-resolved images, the method predicts scale proposal maps indicating which pixels suit each scale.

entry.title: COMPASS: Comet Object Measurement Pipeline with Automated Selection and Scoring

author.name: Jack Roberts, Canya Lu, Alexis Michelle Lawson, Kaitlyn Holden, Gerald S. Wilkinson, Anne M. Bronikowski, Ritambhara Singh

entry.summary: COMPASS automates comet assay image analysis, a standard technique for quantifying DNA damage at the single-cell level, by combining deep-learning-based comet segmentation with damage measurement and automated, transparent comet selection. It reduces manual effort and improves reproducibility with optional manual review.

entry.title: Lollypop: Camera-to-Motion-Capture Calibration Verification with a Reference Target

author.name: Tianyi Liu, Kevin Harris, Mihika Dave, Kun He

entry.summary: Lollypop is a physical fiducial target combining an ArUco marker with a motion-capture marker constellation so that the visual and tracked centroids correspond to the same physical point, enabling independent verification of camera-to-mocap calibration that may drift after deployment. Experiments show sub-pixel nominal error and sensitivity to controlled errors. This addresses a practical reliability gap for robotics and AR/VR ground-truth pipelines.

entry.title: Riemannian Shape Analysis of the Corpus Callosum in Kendall Space: Aging and Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Olakunle S. Abawonse, Fatou Fall

entry.summary: The paper applies a Riemannian shape-space framework in Kendall space to analyze corpus callosum morphology in aging and Alzheimer's, deriving multivariate geodesic regression with exact gradients and localizing age-related deformation across five anatomical sub-regions on OASIS-1. On a cognitively normal cohort (n=252), geodesic regression outperforms Euclidean alternatives. This offers principled geometric analysis for neuroimaging biomarkers.

entry.title: Gauss-Map Variation for Image Denoising: Geometric Analysis and an Anderson--Accelerated Majorization--Minimization Method

author.name: Haibin Su

entry.summary: Proposes a Gauss-map variation regularizer for image denoising that measures spatial variation of tangent-plane projectors of the image graph, with differential-geometric analysis proving edge and corner preservation properties. Solves the model via a bilinear decomposition and an Anderson-accelerated majorization-minimization algorithm.

entry.title: Benchmarking CLIP for Zero-Shot Face and Periocular Gender Estimation

author.name: Fernando Alonso-Fernandez, Kevin Hernandez-Diaz, Jose Maria Buades, Josef Bigun

entry.summary: This study evaluates CLIP backbones for zero-shot gender estimation from full-face and periocular images, achieving 95.54% accuracy on full faces without task-specific training. It identifies and corrects a male-bias decision boundary in periocular prediction via threshold alignment, and sets a new periocular benchmark on Adience.

entry.title: Image-Based Breast Implant Detection for Mammography Dataset Curation and Near-Real-Time Deployment: Comparing Foundation Models and Task-Specific Convolutional Models

author.name: Vasisht Ishwar, Hari Trivedi, Young Seok Jeon, Beatrice Brown-Mulry, Frank Li, Rohan Satya Isaac, Mohammadreza Chavoshi, Judy Wawira Gichoya

entry.summary: This study compares foundation models (RAD-DINO, MammoCLIP) against task-specific CNNs (ResNet18, lightweight ResNetLite) for breast implant classification in mammography, using the Emory Breast Imaging Dataset. It evaluates performance-feasibility tradeoffs for dataset curation and near-real-time clinical deployment.

entry.title: Evolutionary Giant Tour for CVRP using NSE and ML Heuristic]{Evolutionary Giant Tour approach for CVRP using Node Shift Encoding and Machine Learning repair heuristic

author.name: Souad Abdoune, Menouar Boulif

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem that separates the genetic algorithm's evolutionary search from route construction, adapting Node Shift Encoding to giant-tour representations and benchmarking it against Path Representation and Double Chromosome. It also introduces an unsupervised machine-learning repair heuristic to restore fleet feasibility after crossover or mutation.

entry.title: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions

author.name: Junhoo Lee (KAIST), Injun Baek (Seoul National University), Seungyeon Kim (Seoul National University), Suhyun Jeon (Seoul National University), Minkyu Kim (Seoul National University), Baekseung Kim (Seoul National University), Nojun Kwak (Seoul National University)

entry.summary: RobotUse is a robot agent harness that organizes computation, context, and decisions around specifying and revising physical actions: agents visually select targets and poses while the backend handles geometry, motion planning, and control, with subagents retaining per-subgoal interaction detail. A continual harnessing mechanism lets agents learn from execution by updating persistent context across repeated attempts.

entry.title: TacGELLO: Tactile Contact Feedback for a 3D-Printed Teleoperation Leader

author.name: Younsoo Kim, Sangmin Song, Sarath Kodagoda, Marc Carmichael, Karthick Thiyagarajan

entry.summary: TacGELLO repurposes existing servos in a 3D-printed teleoperation leader arm to provide tactile contact feedback at the gripper and current-based load cues at joints, using AnySkin contact detection. Evaluations across UR3 sessions show low tracking error and reliable tactile onset detection during grasping.

entry.title: Virtual model control for compliant reaching under uncertainties

author.name: Yi Zhang, Daniel Larby, Fumiya Iida, Fulvio Forni

entry.summary: This paper extends Virtual Model Control, previously mostly studied for legged locomotion, to compliant reaching tasks on a force-controlled 8-DoF humanoid arm in environments with obstacles and uncertainty. Six approaches to designing virtual models are proposed and validated in real-world experiments assessing predictability and safety.

entry.title: Budget-Constrained Fault-Tolerant Mutual Visibility for Autonomous Robots under the Mobility Fault Model

author.name: Prakhar Shukla, Animesh Maiti, Shivam Kumar, Subhash Bhagat

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies mutual visibility for swarms of opaque autonomous robots under a budget-constrained mobility fault model, where each robot has a finite movement budget and an arbitrary number may become permanently immobile. The authors design distributed algorithms enabling non-faulty robots to achieve unobstructed visibility of all robots in finite time. This extends classical swarm visibility results to energy-limited, fault-prone settings.

entry.title: Multiagent Evaluation under Incomplete Information

author.name: Mark Rowland, Shayegan Omidshafiei, Karl Tuyls, Julien Perolat, Michal Valko, Georgios Piliouras, Remi Munos

entry.summary: This paper addresses evaluating and ranking learned multiagent strategies under incomplete information, where Elo ratings fail on intransitive interactions and Nash-based methods are computationally intractable outside two-player zero-sum games. It extends the alpha-Rank framework to handle evaluation with incomplete information, relevant to ranking agents in games. This was an influential DeepMind contribution to multiagent evaluation methodology.

entry.title: Neyman-Pearson Classification with Indecisions: Simultaneous Control of Selective Type I and Type II Errors

author.name: Bradley Rava, Bowen Gang

entry.summary: The paper studies Neyman-Pearson classification permitting indecisions, allowing uncertain observations to remain unclassified while controlling selective type I and type II errors within each class. It develops a model-free calibration procedure that unions candidate threshold regions, coupled to a common martingale for validity. This addresses realistic classification scenarios with substantial class overlap where forced decisions cannot satisfy both error constraints.

entry.title: Downsides of a Mandatory Training-to-Internal Deployment Gap

author.name: Avi Brach-Neufeld

entry.summary: The author critiques AI Futures' proposal that AI R&D only be conducted by models trained at least 9 months prior, acknowledging its benefits (delaying sabotage-capable models, a negative internal-public gap, effectiveness in fast-takeoff worlds) but raising a key concern: it would cause capabilities to accumulate without real-world feedback on alignment, breaking the current sequential train-deploy-correction loop. This is a focused policy analysis contributing to compute and deployment-governance debates.

entry.title: Smoothed Gradient Method for Nonconvex Federated Stochastic Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Xinwen Zhang, Peiran Yu, Zhaosong Lu, Hongchang Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a stochastic doubly smoothed gradient method for nonconvex federated bilevel optimization that avoids Hessian and Jacobian computations, relaxes restrictive lower-level assumptions, and reduces condition-number dependence and cross-level learning-rate tuning issues. Convergence guarantees are provided.

entry.title: Learning While Scheduling Jobs under Context-Dependent Service Rates: An Anytime Rate-Optimal Algorithm

author.name: Seoungbin Bae, Dabeen Lee

entry.summary: The paper studies contextual queueing bandits where a learner schedules jobs while learning unknown logistic service rates, measured by queue-length regret. The proposed WISE algorithm achieves rate-optimal t^(-1/2) queue-length regret at every sufficiently large time without horizon knowledge, under weaker assumptions than prior work. This improves on existing guarantees that either decay suboptimally or require a known fixed horizon.

entry.title: Beyond the Parameter Monolith: Reconstructive Memories, Executable Skills, and Residual Assembly for Language Models

author.name: A. Bochkov

entry.summary: This exploratory work investigates FEM-ASM, an architecture separating contextual computation, persistent storage, and deterministic executable skills that contribute typed proposals to a shared LM state reconciled by a residual operator. An attention-free Multi-Mesh prototype learns causal LM but does not reach competitive general capability.

entry.title: The Cost of a Hop: Benchmarking NLIP and A2A

author.name: Ranjan Sinha, Anindita Das, Ashika Anand Babu, Hari Palleti

entry.summary: This is the first controlled performance study of the Natural Language Interaction Protocol (NLIP) versus the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, decomposing latency into message creation, connection, and send phases across three hardware environments. NLIP is 4x to 9.6x faster for lightweight coordination depending on hardware.

entry.title: Teaching a Minimalist Machine to Discover Recursive Programs for Arithmetic

author.name: Dominik Magiera, Christiane Wiebel-Herboth, Frank J\"{a}kel

entry.summary: The Minimalist Machine is an inductive program synthesis framework using a compact relational Prolog subset where recursion emerges when a target predicate is reused within a learned clause rather than via a dedicated metarule. Modeled on cognitive insights and a primary-school arithmetic curriculum, it sequentially acquires concepts from an empty knowledge base.

entry.title: Collective intelligence through aggregation

author.name: Franz Dietrich, Christian List

entry.summary: A theoretical investigation of judgment aggregation for groups making interconnected judgments over binary and multi-valued issues, examining three challenges: inconsistency from reasonable aggregation rules, and related obstacles to coherent collective judgment. It extends classical judgment aggregation theory beyond yes/no questions to variables like economic or climate quantities.

entry.title: BiasFlow: Geometric Monitoring and Backbone Regularization for Spurious Feature Reliance

author.name: Haojin Deng, Zhiping Lin, Yimin Yang

entry.summary: BiasFlow is a hook-based toolkit for monitoring spurious feature reliance in frozen backbones via geometric diagnostics such as class-attribute centroid alignment and within-class centroid separation, paired with a class-conditional centroid-alignment regularization penalty (BFR). The authors are notably candid that their alignment metric is confounded and not a causal measure of feature reliance, and that improvements are shown only on small-scale benchmarks.

entry.title: LoRA Adaptation Strength in Aurora-WRF: Trade-offs in Regional Heavy-Rainfall Forecasting

author.name: Boyan Liu, Xiaoyuan Zhang

entry.summary: A controlled experiment coupling LoRA-adapted versions of the AuroraPretrained atmospheric foundation model to an unchanged 9-km WRF configuration over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, testing five inference-time adaptation strengths against a GFS-driven control. Using 2023 evaluation data with hourly ERA5 precipitation on a fixed verification grid, it characterizes trade-offs in regional heavy-rainfall forecasting.

entry.title: Selective Backpropagation for Efficient Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Eeham Khan, Abdulmoumen Al-Atrash, Ali Ayub

entry.summary: Selective Backpropagation (SBP) is a deterministic parameter-budgeting framework for few-shot class-incremental learning that restricts gradient updates to a pre-allocated subset of network parameters. It aims to bridge the trade-off between compute-efficient fine-tuning, replay-based memory-heavy methods, and exemplar-free approaches that freeze most of the backbone. This allows models to learn new classes from few samples while retaining prior knowledge under tight compute and memory constraints.

entry.title: Agent Reliability Profiles in Financial Services

author.name: Mike Hsu, Medha Bankhwal, B\'eatrice Moissinac, Kevin Werbach, Lukasz Szpruch, Bennett Hillenbrand

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Agent Reliability Profile, a standardized per-agent unit of assurance evidence for agentic AI deployments in financial services. Given the absence of a shared framework for describing, validating, and benchmarking agent reliability, the Profile aims to help financial institutions, vendors, and regulators assess and trust agents at scale. It defines reliability as assurance that an agent stays within intended bounds and operating limits.

entry.title: Dual-Scale Relational Graph Transformers for Ecosystem-Aware Fraud Detection

author.name: Mohsen Nayebi Kerdabadi, Xinrou Li, Yao Xiao, Zijun Yao, Xin Sun

entry.summary: HERMES is a dual-scale heterogeneous relational graph transformer for account-takeover fraud detection in digital banking that jointly reasons over local session-level relational structure and the evolving global state of the fraud ecosystem. This addresses a limitation of production tabular models, which score sessions in isolation, and of prior graph models, which capture only local neighborhoods. The approach aims to improve detection while minimizing friction for legitimate customers.

entry.title: A Unified Dynamics Framework for Reinforcement Learning and Classical Control of a Six-DOF Pipeline-Tracking ROV in NVIDIA Isaac Sim

author.name: Cheng Siong Chin, M. Venkateshkumar, Jianhua Zhang

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline-tracking architecture for a six-DOF underwater ROV in which a single USD scene feeds identical BlueROV2-Heavy dynamics parameters to both a NumPy implementation of Fossen's marine-craft equations and an NVIDIA Isaac Sim deployment applying the same equations as PhysX forces. This eliminates a common sim-to-real confound where RL controllers are trained and evaluated against different physics representations. The Coriolis-centripetal term is treated as the primary dynamics mode.

entry.title: An LLM-in-the-loop RL Framework for Bioinformatics Feature Selection

author.name: Xinyuan Wang, Deepti Agrawal, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a reinforcement learning framework for feature selection in high-dimensional bioinformatics data where an LLM guides exploration with domain-informed advice and supplies hybrid rewards combining data-driven performance with domain knowledge. This treats feature selection as sequential decision-making augmented by LLM guidance.

entry.title: Ramp Metering Control via Hybrid State Deep Reinforcement Learning in Partially Observable Connected Vehicle Environments

author.name: Youcef Mehamlia, Nadir Farhi, Meriem Bouali

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid observation representation combining macroscopic traffic measurements with a two-channel grid encoding of connected-vehicle presence and speed for ramp metering via a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network. Training covers varying CV penetration rates to handle partial observability. It is a solid applied RL contribution for traffic management.

entry.title: LLM-enhanced spatio-temporal learning for grid-level docked bike sharing demand prediction

author.name: Xuxilu Zhang, Francesc Soriguera

entry.summary: Proposes a bike-sharing demand forecasting framework where an LLM converts free-form urban text such as event schedules and transit bulletins into quantified spatial-temporal perturbation fields with interpretable parameters (intensity, spatial reach, temporal profile). This targets non-stationarity that fixed graph structures and historical flows cannot capture.

entry.title: TMAML: Temporal Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Cold-Start Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Wannes Janssens, Matthias Bogaert, Dirk Van den Poel

entry.summary: TMAML adapts model-agnostic meta-learning to cold-start time series forecasting by formulating the problem as few-window learning, enabling fast adaptation from short histories while leveraging static covariates and cross-series information. Standard global forecasting models are not optimized for out-of-train-set generalization from brief histories, which TMAML targets. This matters for domains like retail demand where new series constantly appear.

entry.title: Hamiltonian Metric Learning and Energy-Based Training: A Dissipative Geometric Framework for Optimization

author.name: Sparsho Chakraborty, Mohammad Alamgir, Nishanth M, Akshit Nanda, Ram Prasad Padhy, Sayan Mukherjee

entry.summary: This theoretical work treats parameter optimization as the evolution of a dissipative Hamiltonian dynamical system, with parameters as generalized coordinates, loss as potential energy, and a learned positive-definite metric defining kinetic geometry. From a variational formulation it derives Hamiltonian dynamics with a metric-compatible Rayleigh dissipation law satisfying monotonic energy dissipation.

entry.title: Cross-Time Directional Selection in Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Dhia naouali

entry.summary: The paper measures how the remaining diffusion-sampling steps amplify perturbations at late latent states, comparing perturbations transported from earlier steps against freshly sampled isotropic noise at matched magnitude. Shaped angular gain exceeds matched fresh gain in every trajectory, with paired gain ratios from 1.14 to 2.35 across samplers.

entry.title: LEON: Location Embeddings from OSM Neighborhoods via Hexagonal Graph Masked Autoencoders

author.name: Szymon Soltysiak, Radoslaw Malek, Jedrzej Kusnierz, Milosz Chojecki, Piotr Szymanski, Aleksandra Kawala-Sterniuk

entry.summary: LEON adapts Graph Masked Autoencoders to learn geospatial region embeddings from OpenStreetMap amenity distributions on H3 hexagonal grid graphs, in a self-supervised framework. It is evaluated on EuroSAT satellite classification and geographic prediction tasks like housing prices and crime rates.

entry.title: Sharp Integrality Gaps in Calibration Distance

author.name: Zinan Wang, Xinhao Yang

entry.summary: Sharpens the known offline gap between deterministic calibration distance and its fractional relaxation to a tight worst-case order of Theta(T^(1/3)), with matching upper and lower bounds, and characterizes sparse-sample gaps as Theta(m) in the number of distinct forecasts. Provides both structural results and rational lower-bound constructions.

entry.title: Large Stepsizes Federated Learning on Logistic Regression with Linearly Separable Data: The Case of Heterogeneous Devices

author.name: Hok Fong Wong, Hoi-To Wai, Chung-Yiu Yau

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that FedAvg for multinomial logistic regression on linearly separable data remains stable even with arbitrarily large stepsizes and heterogeneous device update rules. The objective converges to zero at O(1/R) rate, effects of device heterogeneity vanish asymptotically, and objective values become monotonically decreasing for sufficiently many rounds. This extends prior large-stepsize stability results to the heterogeneous federated setting.

entry.title: Rethinking Least-Core Computation in Contextual-Distractor Games

author.name: Hiroshi Kera, Toshinori Yamauchi, Sai Ganesh Nagarajan

entry.summary: This paper examines the least-core as an alternative to Shapley-based game-theoretic attribution, showing that least-core allocations are nonunique and that the choice of payoff selector and coalition sampling materially affects explanations. Experiments reveal that sampling degrades identification of harmful players even when useful players remain well identified.

entry.title: Loss-Invariant Projections as Passive Probes of Learned Representations

author.name: Akshay Chandrasekhar, Pavlo Melnyk

entry.summary: This paper proposes passive probes: fixed, untrained, property-independent random projections applied to representations during training that act as loss-invariant observers. Changes in how much structure these projections can access reflect changes in the representation itself relative to the task, motivated by an analytic example on the sphere. This offers a lightweight tool for studying representation dynamics without trained probes.

entry.title: Parameter Estimation in Machining Dynamics with Regenerative Delay and Nonsmooth Friction using Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Meiyazhagan Jaganathan, Vikram Pakrashi, Aasifa Rounak

entry.summary: The paper develops a multi-domain XPINN framework for nonsmooth delay differential equations, partitioning the temporal domain into subdomains at integer multiples of the characteristic delay and progressively training subnetworks with freezing. Applied to machining dynamics with regenerative vibration and nonsmooth friction, it improves solution reconstruction and parameter estimation over generic PINNs. This is the first demonstration of this training scheme for DDEs.

entry.title: Constrained Goal-directed Planar Graph Generation with Grammar-based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nicolas Hochuli, Lorenzo Miele, Kristina Shea, Tino Stankovic

entry.summary: This work introduces a dataset-free method for goal-directed planar graph embedding generation combining parametric graph grammars with safe reinforcement learning, formulated as a constrained MDP. An action projection maps sampled actions toward state-dependent safe sets, improving constraint satisfaction during training. It targets engineering applications requiring hard structural and geometric feasibility, which existing graph generators poorly support.

entry.title: Beyond the Model: The Critical Role of Data Filtering in Clinical Machine Learning

author.name: Noah Subedar, Colin Campbell, Wenjing Zhang, Dan Perri, Sarah Culgin, Andrew Hamilton-Wright

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that preprocessing and filtering decisions in clinical ML studies can alter dataset statistical structure and artificially change task complexity, and should therefore be treated as part of the scientific method. It calls for explainable, transparent preprocessing pipelines so researchers can understand why filtering choices are made and how they affect results. Source code is released.

entry.title: On the Approximation Relationship between Optimizing Ratio of Submodular (RS) and Difference of Submodular (DS) Functions

author.name: Pierre Perrault, Jennifer Healey, Zheng Wen, Michal Valko

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates a formal equivalence-style relationship between ratio-of-submodular and difference-of-submodular optimization, showing that approximation algorithms for one yield weaker guarantee algorithms for the other and vice versa. It analyzes a Greedy algorithm for maximizing quasiconvex two-variable functions of monotone submodular objectives, recovering RS and DS as special cases.

entry.title: Structured Neural Modeling of Daily Arctic Sea-Ice Concentration Evolution: Physical-Trajectory-Driven Learning and Forecast-Domain Adaptation

author.name: Maqun Zhang, Feng Gao, Wankun Chen, Hui Yu, Yanhai Gan, Junyu Dong

entry.summary: The paper proposes a reanalysis-forecast dual-domain decoupled framework for learning sea ice evolution operators, built on a lightweight physical baseline generating daily trajectories with temporally constrained joint training. It aims to disentangle physical evolution relationships from data errors to create a stable, verifiable forecasting core for daily Arctic sea ice concentration prediction.

entry.title: Adaptive Partitioning Schemes for Optimistic Optimization

author.name: Raja Sunkara, Ardhendu Tripathy

entry.summary: This paper develops optimistic optimization algorithms for black-box functions that learn their own domain partitioning scheme and can use flexible surrogate models such as neural networks. For multi-index functions on a lower-dimensional subspace, the algorithms achieve improved regret scaling relative to the ambient dimension. This targets fixed-evaluation-budget engineering design problems.

entry.title: Homogeneous Semantic Alignment and Hierarchical Expert Routing for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Erjian Zhang, Jiayuan Ma, Liejun Wang, Yikemaiti Sataer, Xiaoming Tao, Zhiqing Guo

entry.summary: Proposes HSA-HER, a two-stage framework for radiology report generation that uses explicit homogeneous semantic alignment and hierarchical expert routing to prevent weak visual abnormality cues from being diluted by massive text priors during decoding. Inspired by cognitive science, it addresses distribution shift between modalities and rigid coupling of heterogeneous information. A targeted architectural improvement for clinical report generation.

entry.title: Does Neural Complexity Improve Health Misinformation Detection? A Leakage-Controlled Cross-Corpus Benchmark

author.name: Mkululi SIKOSANA

entry.summary: Provides a leakage-controlled cross-corpus benchmark of five compact neural architectures, an ensemble, and classical ML baselines for health misinformation detection on COVID19-FNIR and CONSTRAINT, with exact-text duplicate controls, unified preprocessing, and multi-seed repetition. It questions whether architectural complexity actually improves detection once confounds are controlled. A careful negative-leaning empirical study.

entry.title: RepTC: Representation-Aware Optimization for Efficient Traffic Classification on Edge IoT Devices

author.name: Adel Chehade, Edoardo Ragusa, Paolo Gastaldo, Rodolfo Zunino

entry.summary: RepTC is a hardware-constrained strategy for encrypted-traffic classification on edge IoT devices that jointly optimizes network architecture, session length, and header preprocessing. This co-design approach addresses the tension between accuracy, latency, and energy under privacy and bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: A Contrast-Source Inversion Scheme Based on Stochastic Optimization and Plug-and-Play Regularization

author.name: Lingqi Gao, Hakan Bagci

entry.summary: STO-PNP-CSI integrates stochastic optimization and plug-and-play regularization with a Swin-Conv-UNet denoiser into contrast-source inversion for electromagnetic imaging, randomly selecting one contrast source vector per iteration to cut cost and escape poor local minima. The PNP denoiser counters the resulting ill-posedness.

entry.title: Dual Variational Autoencoders for Efficient Sim-to-Real Transfer in Low-Cost Robotic Navigation

author.name: \'Alvaro D\'iez (Department of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, University of Alicante), Fidel Aznar (Department of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, University of Alicante)

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid sim-to-real framework combining domain randomization with feature-level domain adaptation via a dual convolutional variational autoencoder with a shared decoder, trained on 45225 simulated and only 4556 real images. The architecture learns a common latent representation that bridges simulated and real navigation conditions for low-cost robots. It enables vision-based navigation policies on budget hardware.

entry.title: ufakzeka-karar: An Open Turkish Typed-Decision Model with Order-Invariant Option Scoring

author.name: Sait Furkan Teke (ufak AI)

entry.summary: ufakzeka-karar is an open 182M-parameter Turkish decision model that outputs temperature-scaled option probabilities and an expected-error uncertainty signal in a single CPU forward pass, without text generation. Its head scores each option blind to the others, giving order invariance, which a sequential-head or REINFORCE-trained variant failed to achieve.

entry.title: Writing as a Self-Organized Critical Process

author.name: Nikolay Mikhaylovskiy

entry.summary: This paper explains power-law autocorrelation decay in texts via self-organized criticality, analyzing the KLiCKe keystroke dataset to show that both final texts and revision dynamics adhere to power-law behavior with finite-size scaling and restoring dynamics toward a critical manifold. It suggests human writing dynamically regulates semantic correlations toward a critical state. The finding offers a unifying physics-style account of a pervasive statistical property of text.

entry.title: Verifier-Guided Synthetic Augmentation for 3D Human Shape Generation

author.name: Yuexuan Wu, Yang Xiang, Hamid Laga, Dip Das, Anuj Srivastava, Zhengwu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a verifier-guided data augmentation framework for 3D human body generative models, using PCA-based candidate generation screened by skeletal proportions and body-part geometry before retraining a diffusion model. Elastic registration enables scalable screening, and a blinded human study supports the verifier as an effective gatekeeper.

entry.title: OctMesh: A Unified Octree-Hierarchical Framework for Lossless Triangle Mesh Compression

author.name: Shiyu Feng, Xihua Sheng, Lingyu Zhu, Chunyang Fu, Shiqi Wang

entry.summary: OctMesh is a learned lossless mesh compression framework that codes geometry and connectivity on a shared octree hierarchy, exploiting the observation that octree pooling yields parents with either one or multiple children to model edge refinement compactly. It preserves both vertex positions and connectivity, extending octree coding ideas from point clouds to meshes.

entry.title: CGDD-Net: Context-Guided Dynamic Detail Modeling for Retinal Vessel Segmentation

author.name: Xincheng Li, Xiaoqi Sheng, Xinyu Zhang

entry.summary: CGDD-Net is a retinal vessel segmentation network combining fixed-grid convolution with deformable local attention, spatially adaptive multi-kernel gating for receptive-field selection, and dynamic cross-scale detail fusion that reuses a compact eight-channel representation across decoder resolutions. The design balances vascular geometry capture with fine-scale reconstruction. It is a domain-specific architecture targeting fine vascular structures.

entry.title: FrontVeg V2: A Training-Free Software Framework for Foreground-Aware Zero-Shot Plant Trait Segmentation in High-Resolution Images of Trellised Crops

author.name: Abdoul Djalil Ousseini Hamza (IRHS-IMHORPHEN, DPT SPE), Herearii Metuarea (IRHS-IMHORPHEN, DPT SPE), Corentin Lothod{\'e} (IRHS-IMHORPHEN, DPT SPE), Morgane Roth (GAFL), Jacem Ben Hamden (SVQV, BAP), Eric Duch{\^e}ne (SVQV, BAP), Lionel Ley (UE ARBO), David Alletru (UE ARBO), David Rousseau

entry.summary: FrontVeg V2 is an open-source, training-free pipeline for zero-shot segmentation of plant traits in high-resolution trellised crop images, combining monocular depth (Depth Anything V2), SAM3, tiled zero-shot segmentation, and graph-based mask assembly. It supports digital phenotyping via CLI and a Napari GUI.

entry.title: Cross-dataset harmonization for robust endoscopic image analysis

author.name: Romil Imtiaz, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: The authors tackle the domain-shift problem in endoscopic image analysis caused by differing color distributions across endoscope sensors and light sources. They propose a simple reference-based image harmonization method that reduces global appearance differences and improves cross-device model generalization.

entry.title: Robust 2D Traversability Mapping for Construction AMRs via Failure-Mode-Aware Fusion of LiDAR Geometry and Monocular Semantics

author.name: Manoj Karnekar, Om Mandhane, Gautham Ramkumar

entry.summary: This work proposes a real-time multimodal traversability pipeline for autonomous mobile robots on construction sites, fusing LiDAR geometry with confidence-gated monocular semantics on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. The failure-mode-aware design handles hazards like wet mud that LiDAR misses and phantom obstacles such as speed breakers, and the authors release a multimodal dataset.

entry.title: Optimization Geometry of QAOA and Variational Quantum Algorithms

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Ivan Zelinka, Silvie Ill\'esov\'a, Swagatam Das, Martin Beseda

entry.summary: The paper studies how the classical nonconvex objectives arising from variational quantum algorithms (QAOA) can be visualized and characterized to explain optimizer behavior. It distinguishes the number of local minima along sampled directions from endpoint quality, and compares multi-start BFGS against adaptive differential evolution (jSO) under equal function-evaluation budgets, finding that repeated local search explores different basins.

entry.title: Sparse Calibration-Based Personalization of Kernel-Based Gait Phase and Speed Estimation Using Wearable IMUs

author.name: Myeongju Cha, Pilwon Hur

entry.summary: The paper presents sparse calibration-based personalization for kernel-based co-estimation of gait phase and walking speed from wearable IMUs, combining a user-specific baseline from three calibration speeds with a principal-component model of kinematic deviations. Personalized kernels reduced phase error versus population kernels in offline validation and a small online pilot.

entry.title: DNPush: Distributed Nonparallel Pushing Force Control of Multi-Robot Systems for Object Transportation

author.name: Duy Anh Nguyen, Pham Duy Hung, Trung Dung Ngo

entry.summary: DNPush enables cooperative object transport by robots pushing with nonparallel forces and no inter-robot communication, using only local force measurements and a locally expressed desired direction. A reciprocal-sine law regulates force magnitudes and Lyapunov analysis with LaSalle's invariance proves convergence to a unique rotational equilibrium without object models or contact knowledge.

entry.title: A State Based Dispatch Controller for Hospital Delivery Robots with Shared Human and Infrastructure Resources

author.name: Krzysztof Siwek, Aleksandra \'Swietlicka

entry.summary: This work formulates a location-aware dispatch model for hospital delivery robots that couples robot admission to transporter support, shared elevators, charging, and cleaning, evaluated by replaying 33,079 observed hospital requests. Comparative grids of human dispatch, a resource-aware controller, and benchmarks reveal how pickup travel and pooled elevator demand affect realistic transport capacity.

entry.title: Towards Robust Prehensile Manipulation in Open-Ended Environments

author.name: Mathilde Kappel, Mahdi Khoramshahi, Louis Annabi, Fa\"iz Ben Amar, St\'ephane Doncieux

entry.summary: This paper applies Quality-Diversity algorithms to prehensile manipulation in open-ended environments, discovering a wide repertoire of robust grasp configurations that serve as starting points for diverse manipulation trajectories on articulated objects. The resulting behavioral diversity is argued to improve generalization and adaptability for deployment in continuously evolving open-world settings.

entry.title: Mine Your Own vieW: Self-Supervised Learning Through Across-Sample Prediction

author.name: Mehdi Azabou, Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, Ran Liu, Chi-Heng Lin, Erik C. Johnson, Kiran Bhaskaran-Nair, Max Dabagia, Bernardo Avila-Pires, Lindsey Kitchell, Keith B. Hengen, William Gray-Roncal, Michal Valko, Eva L. Dyer

entry.summary: The paper introduces MYOW, a self-supervised learning method that mines neighboring samples within the dataset to serve as diverse prediction targets, rather than relying only on augmented views of the same sample. This across-sample prediction helps overcome nuisance variables and builds richer representations. It demonstrated strong results including applications to neuroscience data.

entry.title: Planning in entropy-regularized Markov decision processes and games

author.name: Jean-Bastien Grill, Omar Darwiche Domingues, Pierre M\'enard, R\'emi Munos, Michal Valko

entry.summary: This paper introduces SmoothCruiser, a planning algorithm for value estimation in entropy-regularized MDPs and two-player games using a generative model. By exploiting the smoothness of the regularized Bellman operator, it achieves problem-independent sample complexity O~(1/epsilon^4), whereas unregularized settings lack known polynomial worst-case guarantees. Entropy regularization is central to modern RL (e.g., soft actor-critic, RLHF objectives), making this relevant to practice.

entry.title: Efficient Mass Matrix Estimation with Gaussian Cooling

author.name: Jake Hofgard, Michael Lindsey

entry.summary: The paper introduces a multistage Gaussian cooling algorithm for preconditioning log-concave, log-smooth distributions whose cost scales logarithmically with the condition number. It sequentially samples well-conditioned distributions to build preconditioners for later stages, providing theoretical grounding for warm-up mass matrix estimation used in MCMC practice. This bridges practical MCMC warm-up heuristics and provable efficiency.

entry.title: Import AI 475: Swarm scaling; Google DeepMind watermarks biology; and the AI science economy

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter covers Toby Ord's analysis of AI swarm scaling as a form of inference-scaling — swarms trade roughly double total tokens for half the wall-clock time, with a diminishing-returns stepping-on-toes parameter — plus Google DeepMind watermarking of biological sequence outputs and commentary on the AI science economy. It is a curated synthesis with editorial analysis rather than original research.

entry.title: Agentic AI with Structured CoT for Enhancing AI's Spatial Intelligence: Visualization and Reasoning of Rotation

author.name: Uttamasha Monjoree, Wei Yan

entry.summary: The authors evaluate the spatial rotation reasoning of GPT-5.6, an existing frontier generative model, using an adapted Purdue Spatial Visualization Test augmented with extra graphical and contextual features. They study how different structured chain-of-thought reasoning strategies affect performance on 3D rotation understanding. The work documents that even advanced multimodal models struggle with spatial rotation reasoning.

entry.title: Language-Conditioned Token and Reasoning Efficiency in Large Language Models: A Paired Cross-Lingual Study Protocol

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: This paper specifies a prospective paired study protocol for measuring how input language affects token usage and reasoning efficiency in LLMs, carefully separating input language, trace language, and answer realization that prior comparisons conflate. The design spans 240 scored items across eight languages, three open-weight checkpoints, three trace-token budgets, and 22 language conditions, totaling 47,520 planned core runs. It is a rigorous methodological contribution for quantifying cross-lingual cost disparities in LLM inference.

entry.title: GFGE: Unifying Explainable AI Methods through an Interpretation Framework

author.name: Jinfeng Zhong

entry.summary: The paper proposes the General Framework for Generating Explanations (GFGE), a unifying framework for explainable AI grounded in the complementary activities of sense-reading and sense-giving. Its Interpret/Explain Schema connects an analyst's interpretation of system evidence, the communicated account, and the recipient's interpretation, operationalized through five roles.

entry.title: polyview: A Python package for multi-view machine learning

author.name: Gwendal Debaussart-Joniec (ENS Paris Saclay, CB), Argyris Kalogeratos (CB, ENS Paris Saclay)

entry.summary: polyview is a scikit-learn-compatible Python package providing multi-view embedding, clustering, fusion, view augmentation, and incomplete-view handling through a unified composable interface. It addresses the lack of actively maintained, unified tooling for end-to-end multi-view workflows in the Python ecosystem.

entry.title: Logit-Aware MIMO AirComp for Distributed Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference over Wireless Edge Networks

author.name: Lyutianyang Zhang, Yunjian Jia, Liu Cao, Dengke Wang, Jinke Ren, Shuguang Cui

entry.summary: This work addresses the communication bottleneck of distributed MoE LLM inference at wireless edges, where an anchor base station must aggregate expert outputs. It proposes a logit-aware over-the-air computation scheme over MIMO channels that accounts for the unequal impact of aggregation errors on LLM outputs, rather than minimizing generic communication distortion.

entry.title: Do Motion Tokenizers for Co-Speech Gesture Generation Encode Gesture Semantics?

author.name: Varsha Suresh, Divij Jain, Jia Liu, M. Hamza Mughal, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: This probing study examines whether discrete motion tokenizers used in co-speech gesture generation encode gesture semantics, testing 19 gesture descriptors from raw motion to abstract communicative function. It finds geometry and handedness are readily decodable but motion category and semantics are only weakly captured, showing reconstruction quality does not guarantee semantic encoding.

entry.title: Dependable AI-Assisted Engineering: A Formal Framework for AI Participation and Assurance in Safety-Critical Workflows

author.name: Puxue Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a formal framework for deciding whether and how AI-generated engineering artifacts should enter safety-critical workflows. Each workflow unit carries a participation and assurance record specifying the requirement, approved formalization, mechanism, fallback, evidence obligations, guarantee, and deployment-readiness status. The framework distinguishes deterministic verification, statistically calibrated admission, human judgment with AI advice, and human adjudication of AI outputs.

entry.title: Agentic Resource Allocation for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Autonomous Materials Discovery

author.name: Robert Robinson, Shakti Prasad Padhy, Sushant Sinha, Sk Md Ahnaf Akif Alvi, Juan Florez Coronel, Brent Vela, Trevor Hastings, Douglas Allaire, Raymundo Arr\'oyave

entry.summary: This work develops an agentic multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework for alloy design under resource constraints, benchmarking strategies for adaptive exploration-exploitation policy tuning at each iteration. Motivated by self-driving laboratories where constraints shift dynamically, it evaluates the approach on a septenary alloy design space. The goal is to navigate enormous design spaces with competing objectives while adapting to changing campaign conditions.

entry.title: Adaptive Operator Selection in Bilevel Large Neighborhood Search for Electric Autonomous Dial-a-Ride Problem under Uncertainty

author.name: Ishara Hewa Pathiranange, Aneta Neumann

entry.summary: The paper addresses the electric autonomous dial-a-ride problem with battery constraints and travel-time uncertainty, using adaptive selection of insertion operators within a bilevel large neighborhood search. It handles both deterministic and chance-constrained variants where travel times are modeled as normally distributed random variables.

entry.title: AutoDP-LLM: Automating Data Pre-processing for Intrusion Detection Systems using Large Language Models

author.name: Bao-Phong Nguyen, Gia-Khanh Pham, Thai-Duong Do, Mai Xuan Trang, Minh-Tuan Le, Xuan-Nam Tran, Huan Vu, Tien-Cuong Nguyen, Vu-Duc Ngo, Thien Van Luong
