author.name: Ruihan Yu, Yu-Ju Tsai, Muyao Niu, Runyi Li, Lian Fu, Hanqing Liu, Zheng-Hui Huang, Yonghao Yu, Sho Kuno, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: EditHero is the first benchmark for long-horizon, part-level 3D editing, evaluating natural-language edit sequences for both geometry and texture with hand-reviewed targets produced by a deterministic assembly engine. It contrasts non-agentic methods that regenerate objects top-down against LLM/VLM agents that edit bottom-up. This addresses the realistic setting where assets evolve through many sequential revisions rather than single edits.

entry.title: Student-Guided Teacher Distillation for Efficient LLM Task Routing: Positioning Against Jev-Style System-1 Classifiers

author.name: Haifeng Wu, Srinivasan Manoharan, Jian Wan, Fangbo Tu, Junhua Zhao, Xin Chen

entry.summary: Studies a student-guided distillation pipeline for routing requests to 60 LLM task categories: a compact ModernBERT student produces a full distribution in one pass to retrieve top-k candidates, which a larger DeBERTa-v3 zero-shot NLI teacher reranks, with iterative label improvement. Avoids linear cost scaling with taxonomy size.

entry.title: Rank-Aware Speculative Sampling for Diffusion Draft Trees

author.name: Marcello Bullo, Yanxiao Liu, \"Oyk\"u S{\i}la G\"uner, Arpan Mukherjee, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: RASS improves speculative sampling for diffusion generation by exploiting the free ranking of draft candidates along proposal-target mean displacement, ordering verification to accept better candidates sooner within tree-based draft schemes like D-GRS. The rule is based on rank-aware list coupling and preserves the target distribution exactly. It increases throughput without extra target-model evaluations.

entry.title: A Generative Model of Complex Networks Using Graphons and Neural Inverse Operators

author.name: Wooseong Choi, Italo'Ivo Lima Dias Pinto, Chen Sun, Gaurav Gupta, Dong Song, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: This paper bridges mechanistic and deep generative graph models by formulating both generation and parameter recovery in function space, using a multifractal step graphon with recursive construction and neural inverse operators for amortized inference. This retains interpretability while generalizing beyond training graph sizes. It targets scientific applications needing both simulation fidelity and parameter recovery.

entry.title: Light Entropic Optimal Transport on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Xavier Aramayo-Carrasco, Petr Mokrov, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: ManifoldLightOT learns kernel-induced entropic optimal transport couplings directly on common manifolds such as spheres, tori, SO(3), and SE(3) by constructing geometry-specific Gibbs kernels with compatible potential parameterizations. This avoids the costly iterative methods, simulated dynamics, or geometry-oblivious generic neural models of prior manifold EOT solvers.

entry.title: Electronic Density versus Geometry for Machine-Learned Molecular Absorption Spectra

author.name: Siddharth Dhanpal, Peter Elliott, Paolo Emilio Trevisanutto, Alin M. Elena, Gilberto Teobaldi

entry.summary: The paper compares ground-state electron density versus molecular geometry as input representations for machine-learning surrogates that predict molecular optical absorption spectra, avoiding expensive first-principles excited-state calculations. The choice of representation strongly affects surrogate performance, informing future design of ML models for spectroscopy. Relevant to computational chemistry and materials discovery workflows.

entry.title: Evaluating VQA in Vision Language Models using Cooperative Principles

author.name: Monika Shah, Sudarshan Balaji, Somdeb Sarkhel, Sanorita Dey, Deepak Venugopal

entry.summary: This paper evaluates VQA performance of major VLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llava) when questions violate Grice's conversational maxims, using generated modifiers that add ambiguous or false information. Violations degrade VLM performance, and human-VLM differences in pragmatic reasoning are quantified, including lower human cognitive effort for resolving VLM-induced versus human-induced violations.

entry.title: To Jev or Not? Evaluating the Accuracy and Efficiency of Structured Decision Models for Hate-Speech Moderation

author.name: Demetris Paschalides, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: HATEDECIDE evaluates six structured decision-model configurations that accept natural-language criteria for hate-speech moderation across four datasets, benchmarking against specialized, zero-shot, commercial, and supervised baselines. It asks whether these models can accommodate varying hate-speech definitions without task-specific training while remaining efficient enough for large-scale moderation.

entry.title: An AI-Based Multi-Stage Approach for Androgenetic Alopecia Assessment from Low-Magnification Scalp Images

author.name: Mahmoud Raslan, Nada Omar, Omar Khaled, Tarek Waleed, Mohamed Hazem, Rania Mounir, Solwan Elsamanoudy, Ahmed Mourad, Noura Adel, Muhammad Rushdi

entry.summary: Builds a multi-stage clinical decision-support pipeline for androgenetic alopecia that combines follicular unit localization, ordinal shaft counting, calibrated shaft-width estimation, and an interpretable rule layer, evaluated on 243 patients and roughly 158,000 expert-annotated follicular units. Under patient-disjoint testing, YOLOv8m and EfficientNet-B5 variants achieve strong detection and classification performance.

entry.title: A Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based Pipeline for End-to-End Procedural Modeling of Field-Grown Maize from Point Clouds

author.name: Mozhgan Hadadi, Talukder Z. Jubery, Adarsh Krishnamurthy, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian

entry.summary: This paper presents an automated pipeline that reconstructs editable procedural 3D maize models from raw point clouds using a multimodal VLM to annotate leaf midlines in rendered views, with deterministic geometry back-projecting annotations to fit organ-level parameters. It removes the need for manual tuning or species-specific segmentation training data, supporting high-throughput phenotyping and in silico breeding.

entry.title: Aggregate accuracy conceals concentrated temporal vulnerability in a spiking speech classifier

author.name: \.Ismail Can Dikmen

entry.summary: Shows that aggregate accuracy hides locally vulnerable utterances by exhaustively analyzing 725,070 adjacent-bin single-count input changes around 100 validation utterances of a frozen spiking speech classifier. It finds adverse perturbations are highly concentrated in a few sources, and that a post hoc gradient prefix search finds all vulnerable cases at a fraction of the census cost, outperforming margin-guided and surrogate-gradient searches.

entry.title: A Passive AI System for Verifying Physical State on Automated Liquid Handlers

author.name: Junqiong Joanne Qiu, Zeckria Kamrany, Ananya Anand, Emma Vidal, Yunjia Johanna Bai, Nathan S Chen, Sean Son, Varada Abhyankar, Taryn Jakub, Eleazar Eskin

entry.summary: The Labware Setup Checker is a passive vision system that verifies deck preparation on an Opentrons Flex liquid handler using an external consumer webcam and a browser application, without modifying hardware or firmware. It segments the deck, corrects slot assignments via known geometry, classifies labware, and flags missing, misplaced, or unexpected items against a reference protocol library. It was validated during SwabSeq sequencing runs.

entry.title: The AI Risk Observatory: What Can We Learn from AI Disclosures in Annual Reports About Societal Resilience?

author.name: Bart Jaworski

entry.summary: The study applies an LLM-based two-stage classification pipeline to 9,821 annual reports from 1,362 UK listed companies to track AI risk and adoption disclosures from 2020 to 2025. AI risk mentions rose from 2.8% to 41.2% of reports, and adoption disclosures rose from 13.8% to 45.2%, validated against human annotations. This provides a scalable signal for societal resilience research and corporate AI governance monitoring.

entry.title: MEA: A Reward-Driven Multi-Agent System for Faithful Model Explanations

author.name: Yuyang Cheng, Raghav Kaushik Ravi, Srivarshinee Sridhar, Sriparna Saha, Akash Ghosh, Chirag Agarwal

entry.summary: MEA is a multi-agent framework that lowers the expertise barrier for post-hoc ML explanations: a Proposer agent selects and configures explanation tools while an Actor agent, optimized end-to-end against faithfulness rewards, synthesizes tool outputs into explanations. It targets domain experts in high-stakes settings who cannot navigate explanation method outputs themselves. The work connects explainability with agentic orchestration.

entry.title: Designing the Future of User Feedback for Generative AI

author.name: Alisa Frik, Julia Bernd, Amitis Karami, Mohammad Tahaei

entry.summary: A multi-phase academic-industry collaboration with eBay studying how to design post-deployment user feedback mechanisms for generative AI that are usable for consumers and actionable for product teams. The benchmark evaluation of current industry approaches identified issues like poor discoverability and unclear terminology, leading to design guidance motivated by regulations calling for post-deployment user engagement.

entry.title: ROUTEAUDIT: Interaction-Aware Identification for Budgeted Multi-Verifier Routing

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Tianshu Fu, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: ROUTEAUDIT formulates verifier routing for LLMs as a contract-conditioned identification problem, introducing a contract lattice and policy-independent response tape to attribute quality-cost differences to specific system components. It enables fairer comparisons between adaptive multi-verifier systems when catalogs, accounting, or scoring change.

entry.title: Interpreting at Write Time: A Policy Ablation for Multi-Goal Agent Memory

author.name: Albert Sadowski, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: This paper studies what long-running agent memory should summarize for when serving multiple standing user goals, comparing three policies: goal-agnostic summarization, a single all-goal summary, and per-goal summaries read jointly. It frames summarization as a lossy, purpose-laden act whose omissions become permanent once history is unreadable.

entry.title: Safeguarding Mutual Correction in Source-Free Domain Adaptation via Cut Statistics

author.name: Seongjun Lee, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: This paper addresses source-free domain adaptation by enabling bidirectional correction between a source-pretrained model and a vision-language model, exploiting their distinct failure modes instead of one-way supervision. It uses cut statistics to safeguard the mutual correction process. The work targets confirmation bias that plagues self-refinement approaches.

entry.title: EVOL: Simulator-Guided Evolutionary Expert Synthesis for Deployment-Free Learning Path Recommendation

author.name: Geonwoo Bang, Dongho Kim, Moohong Min

entry.summary: EVOL tackles sparse-reward reinforcement learning for learning path recommendation by using a knowledge-tracing simulator to synthesize per-learner expert demonstrations via evolutionary search, then training a deployment-free policy. This imports a simulator-based demonstration learning recipe from robotics into education. It sidesteps the absence of true expert paths in student log data.

entry.title: SimuVerity: Benchmarking Agents for Engineering-Grade Simulink Model Generation

author.name: Ruiqi Zhang, Jiahao Wang, Mingxuan Li, Haichen Luo, Chaoting Wang, Guoyu Mou, Keyu Lai, Hanchao Lv, Jiaxu Wang, Yibo Zheng, Aijun Yang, Xiaohua Wang

entry.summary: SimuVerity is a benchmark of 101 text-to-executable Simulink model-generation tasks across ten engineering domains, with a hierarchical evaluator that checks deliverability, executability, and engineering qualification before scoring accuracy, fidelity, control integrity, and robustness. Existing Simulink benchmarks only test compilation or similarity to references, not whether models satisfy engineering requirements. It is a notable step toward agentic AI in industrial engineering workflows.

entry.title: Slow-Fast Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Preservation

author.name: Xiaofei Yin, Tong Chu, Jiyuan Fu, Jun Lan, Shuheng Zhou, Huijia Zhu

entry.summary: SF-MOPD mitigates capability interference in multi-teacher on-policy distillation by coupling a fast model updated directly by each teacher with a slow reference model, preserving general capabilities while acquiring domain expertise. This addresses the drift problem where distillation displaces the student from its initialization and degrades broad capabilities. It is relevant to the increasingly common practice of specializing foundation multimodal models.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Typed Decisions: Calibrated System One Models from Biomedical Sentence Encoders

author.name: Pritam Deka

entry.summary: Presents SBERT2S1, converting biomedical sentence encoders into schema-constrained typed decision models with cross-head and prior-fused residual variants, plus the BIODECIDE evaluation suite and MEDLINE-S1, a 243k-decision training set derived from NLM indexing. Finds retrieval pretraining improves zero-shot matching but its fine-tuning benefit depends on head architecture.

entry.title: Improving the Energy-Efficiency of the Code Generated by LLMs through Effective Prompting

author.name: Ritika Rekhi, Bing Zhang, Md Arman Islam, Jaya Krishna Pasham, Yeswanth Chitturi, Akshay Paramesha, Isha Valiveti, Asif Imran, Bekir Turkkan, Tevfik Kosar

entry.summary: Evaluates 21 prompting strategies for energy-efficient LLM code generation, identifying 8 strategies tested across 10 open-weight and proprietary LLMs for Python and C++, measuring execution energy beyond functional correctness. Motivated by the growing environmental footprint of AI-generated software.

entry.title: Distributed Learning with Selective State Space Models: Architecture-Aware Convergence Analysis

author.name: Adam Piaseczny, Md Kamran Chowdhury Shisher, Shiqiang Wang, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: Derives architecture-aware convergence guarantees for federated learning (FedAvg and FedProx) when applied to selective state space models like Mamba2, characterizing how recurrent stability, input-dependent discretization, and state projection affect training. This fills a gap where standard federated methods are architecture-agnostic despite SSMs' distinct dynamics.

entry.title: Revisiting Visual Representation Enhancement of VLMs via Kernel Canonical Correlation Analysis

author.name: Peilin Yang, Xiaoyu Liu, Jian Sun, Qinghua Tao

entry.summary: This work revisits KUEA, a recent method that fine-tunes CLIP image encoders by aligning their kernel matrices with vision-centric DINOv2 to improve fine-grained visual perception. The authors show that reducing the weight of the DINOv2 alignment loss does not necessarily hurt fine-grained performance, suggesting kernel-matrix element-wise discrepancy is an insufficient formulation, and propose an improved approach based on kernel canonical correlation analysis. The result refines understanding of how to transfer strong visual representations into vision-language models.

entry.title: ConvoDrift: A Multi-Turn Conversational Dataset for Modeling Stylistic Tone Evolution

author.name: Vihindi Kotalawala, Pamoda Dilranga, Gayani Thoradeniya, Prasan Yapa

entry.summary: ConvoDrift is a dataset for modeling progressive stylistic tone drift in multi-turn conversations under fixed semantic intent, built on 15,727 shared conversational structures with six annotated prompt-response pairs per conversation covering style drift and direction labels. It supports adaptation and persona-conditioned alignment research and includes a derived pairwise variant.

entry.title: Evolving Hybrid Quantum-Classical Architectures for Image Classification

author.name: Devroop Kar, Daniel Krutz, Travis Desell

entry.summary: The paper automates the design of parameterized quantum circuits within hybrid quantum-classical neural networks for image classification, replacing hand-designed circuit ansatze with evolutionary search over circuit structure, gates, and qubit connectivity. This yields task-adapted compact quantum circuits paired with classical feature extractors.

entry.title: Consecutive Posterior Fusion for Diffusive Recovery of Unobservable Image Structures

author.name: Elena Morotti, Davide Evangelista, Elena Loli Piccolomini

entry.summary: The paper introduces CPF-DDNM, an inference-time method for diffusion-based inverse problems in imaging that fuses consecutive measurement-aware posterior estimates along the reverse process, rather than relying only on instantaneous estimates. This improves recovery of image structures that are unobservable or weakly constrained by measurements in severely ill-posed problems. The approach is notable because it requires no retraining, operating purely at inference time.

entry.title: ForestQuery: Boundary-Aware and Spatially Anchored Query Learning for Unified Forest Point Cloud Segmentation

author.name: Zhihao Zhan, Le Tao, Yifei Tian, Xin Liu, Jie Yuan

entry.summary: ForestQuery is a query-learning framework for unified semantic and instance segmentation of forest point clouds, explicitly modeling boundary uncertainty and using spatial anchoring to exploit forest-specific structure. It addresses irregular tree geometry, occlusion, and ambiguous instance boundaries in fine-grained 3D forest scene understanding.

entry.title: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in an Analytically Solved Broker-Trader Game

author.name: Siu Tung Wong (Institute of Finance and Technology, University College London), Carlo Campajola (Institute of Finance and Technology, University College London, UZH Blockchain Center)

entry.summary: The authors place a PPO agent in a continuous-time broker-trader game with a known analytical solution, using the closed-form optimal control to verify the discrete reward implementation and diagnose learning behavior. The study shows that even with a correct reward, PPO dynamics can mislead, and analytic results can guide training. It provides a rare ground-truth testbed for RL in financial optimal control.

entry.title: TRACE: A Reproducible Benchmark for Electricity Price Forecasting with Official Operational Text

author.name: Xinyi Yi, Moy Yuan, Ioannis Lestas

entry.summary: TRACE is a reproducible benchmark of 7,300 zone-day instances pairing electricity prices from five US market zones with official operational text available at forecast time, carefully reconstructed at each cutoff to prevent leakage. Evaluations show the text carries real forecasting signal for central movement and tail risks. The benchmark fills a gap in multimodal (numerical plus textural) electricity price forecasting.

entry.title: CRISP: A Framework for Clause-Reconstructed Interpretable NeuroSymbolic Propositions

author.name: Alex Chan, Shafi Muhtasim Chowdhury, Ekin Can Erku\c{s}, Ole-Christoffer Granmo, Alex Yakovlev, Rishad Shafik

entry.summary: CRISP reconstructs the last-layer activation vector of binary neural teachers as Tsetlin Machine clauses, assigning one individual TM per neuron and representing each hidden bit as propositional clauses over Booleanized inputs. This yields a direct symbolic trace from named input thresholds to named teacher neurons, evaluated on MNIST-family datasets. It addresses auditability of neural decisions through neurosymbolic methods.

entry.title: Post-Training Quantization of Autoregressive Weather Models

author.name: Ananyo Bhattacharya, Swastik Bhattacharya, Christiane Jablonowski

entry.summary: This work applies post-training quantization to deep-learning weather forecasting emulators that perform autoregressive inference via GPU matrix multiplication. The goal is to reduce compute and memory so high-resolution numerical weather prediction can scale further using out-of-the-box hardware optimizations. Quantization quality is evaluated against the forecast skill of full-precision emulators.

entry.title: RAOA: Alternating-Operator Neural Computation with Programmable Radio Propagation

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino

entry.summary: RAOA explores whether programmable radio propagation can serve as computational depth rather than mere communication, proposing a recurrent architecture that alternates an energy-derived problem update with a mixing update over a persistent latent state. Recomputing the problem field after each mix makes repeated passes compositional, improving discrete optimization solution quality without increasing learned-control counts. This is a novel intersection of wireless physics and neural computation.

entry.title: A Two-Stage Cascade for Near-Real-Time Forest Anomaly Detection from Sentinel-1 SAR Time Series

author.name: Pann Thinzar Seint, Subas Chhatkuli, Bryan Atwood

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage statistics-plus-encoder cascade for near-real-time detection of tropical forest loss using Sentinel-1 SAR time series, overcoming cloud-cover limits of optical monitoring and seasonal backscatter confounds. The system targets operational use cases including illegal logging response and carbon market verification.

entry.title: Understanding Trajectory Heterogeneity in Federated World Model Learning

author.name: Yipan Wei, Zhaokun Yan, Ziming Hong, Jiaqi Wu, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks federated learning of world models under cross-time ownership constraints, using hourly action-conditioned clinical prediction across eight MIMIC-IV disease cohorts with over 40 million transitions. It evaluates ten federated algorithms across 32 partition configurations and identifies findings about how trajectory heterogeneity affects federated world-model training.

entry.title: Page-EntroKV: Hardware-Aligned, Entropy-Weighted KV-Cache Eviction under Grouped-Query Attention

author.name: Inbasekaran S

entry.summary: Page-EntroKV formalizes KV-cache eviction at the physical-buffer granularity that grouped-query attention actually allocates, pooling heads within each group using sink-aware entropy-derived weights. This avoids the cache inflation caused by divergent per-head eviction choices and the dilution of specialized retrieval heads from naive mean pooling.

entry.title: Cross-cohort TB classification using clinical data gathered in Uganda and South Africa

author.name: Joshua M. Jansen van V\"uren, Devendra S. Parihar, Daphne Naidoo, Marisa Klopper, Frank Cobelens, Lutz Kolbe, Kimsey Zajac, Willy Ssengooba, Moses Joloba, Grant Theron, Thomas R. Niesler

entry.summary: First cross-country evaluation of machine learning on clinical and demographic data for tuberculosis screening, using the CAGE-TB dataset from South Africa and Uganda. The authors compare logistic regression, MLPs, and CNNs with greedy feature selection to identify patients who would benefit from expensive molecular testing.

entry.title: Deep Bayesian REFoCUS

author.name: Simon Penninga, Ruud van Sloun

entry.summary: The paper formulates ultrasound multistatic recovery from arbitrary transmit sequences as Bayesian inference, training a deep generative prior to handle rank-deficient regimes where classical linear REFoCUS decoders fail. The method provides uncertainty estimates in the acquisition null space and shows strong generalization despite simulation-to-in-vivo distribution shift.

entry.title: Most-Recent Anchoring with Recurrent Ordering for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jung Min Choi, Ngoc Son Le, Ibram Abdelmalak, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: MARO processes the look-back window from the most recent patch to the oldest, anchoring the latent state on recent evidence so that older patches are folded into a recency-centered representation. This architectural change expresses the unequal contribution of recent versus distant context that uniform processing stacks leave implicit.

entry.title: Broken scale symmetries in undercomplete linear autoencoders

author.name: Farhad Pashakhanloo, Jacob A. Zavatone-Veth

entry.summary: This theory paper studies how finite-stepsize SGD breaks exact scale symmetries in neural network loss landscapes, focusing on undercomplete linear autoencoders. The authors show analytically that SGD selects a preferred sign for scale drift on the PCA solution manifold, favoring large decoder weights, with dynamics admitting an analytical description. This refines prior accounts of noise-balancing symmetry breaking in homogeneous networks.

entry.title: Expected Utility Regret Rule: Minimax and Bayes Optimal Portfolio Choice

author.name: Masahiro Kato

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes the Expected Utility Regret (EUR) rule for portfolio choice, which jointly selects a portfolio class and estimates weights to minimize expected utility regret against an oracle investor. In a regular parametric return model, a single EUR rule simultaneously attains minimax and Bayes lower bounds, including leading constants, without using the Bayes prior. The framework recovers mean-variance and related rules as special cases.

entry.title: Evaluating and Improving the Robustness of Large Language Models to Input Sequence Variations

author.name: Narek Maloyan

entry.summary: This thesis develops metrics and methods for LLM robustness against prompt injections, backdoors, and quality-metric manipulation. Contributions include a generative robustness metric based on Jensen-Shannon divergence, theoretical bounds relating localized attack success to classifier stability, and an adaptive evolutionary attack (ASA) targeting LLM-as-a-Judge systems.

entry.title: Hold-Out Scoring for Efficient Gaussian DAG Learning

author.name: Donguk Shin, Byeongguk Kang, Inseol Lee, Gunwoong Park

entry.summary: HOST is an efficient algorithm for high-dimensional Gaussian DAG learning that replaces expensive subset search with nodewise hold-out scoring and convex regression, without requiring a supplied indegree bound. The key insight is that correct ordering recovery only requires one-sided control of score errors, improving the statistical-computational tradeoff.

entry.title: Landscape-Dependent Performance of Photonic Quantum Solvers in QUBO Feature Selection for Financial Risk Detection

author.name: Nirvik Sahoo, Paul Robert Griffin

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks photonic entropy computing (QCI Dirac-3) and simulated boson sampling against classical branch-and-bound (Gurobi) across thirteen QUBO-based feature selection methods on credit card fraud and consumer default datasets. Results show photonic solvers can match full-feature model performance with far fewer features on some problem landscapes, with performance dependent on the QUBO landscape. It offers a rare empirical head-to-head of photonic quantum-inspired hardware for an ML task.

entry.title: HakemBench: A Turkish Benchmark of Typed Decisions

author.name: Sait Furkan Teke (ufak AI)

entry.summary: HakemBench is a fully open Turkish benchmark of 2,346 items with 4,275 decision questions across seven practical tracks such as fact-checking, moderation, and legal routing, requiring models to output option probabilities. A unified harness measures decision quality, calibration, and selective automation with bootstrap intervals, plus robustness probes for option order and translation.

entry.title: StanceEval 2026: The Second Stance Detection Shared Task

author.name: Rasha Albalawi, Nuha Albadi, Hamzah Luqman, Asma Yamani, Maram Kurdi, Saad Ezzini, Ahmed Ashraf, Maged Al-Shaibani, Nora Alturayeif

entry.summary: This paper describes the second StanceEval shared task on Arabic social media stance detection, featuring cross-target generalization tracks that test thematic transfer (Women Driving) and fully unseen targets (E-Cars, Trimester System). With 80 registered teams from 12 countries, it provides a community benchmark resource for low-resource stance detection.

entry.title: Single-Pass Uncertainty Heads for Claim-Level Hallucination Detection in Persian Medical Language Models

author.name: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Pedram Rostami, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Sadra Hakim, Audrina Ebrahimi

entry.summary: The authors adapt the LLM Uncertainty Head framework to Aya-Expanse-8B-based Persian medical models (Gaokerena-V and Gaokerena-R), constructing two new Persian claim-level hallucination datasets with 1,600 paired responses each. The single-pass approach avoids the cost of repeated-sampling uncertainty estimation and extends hallucination detection resources to a new language and medical domain.

entry.title: Benchmarking Literature Retrieval for a Model Organism: A Dictyostelium Case Study

author.name: Yun Wang, Gad Shaulsky, Toma\v{z} Curk, Bla\v{z} Zupan

entry.summary: Presents a curator-generated retrieval benchmark from dictyBase for the model organism Dictyostelium, addressing the gap between broad biomedical retrieval evaluations and narrow, organism-specific knowledge-base settings. The study examines cross-encoder reranking, gene-aware query expansion, and abstract-only versus full-text retrieval in this sparse-literature domain.

entry.title: The Shape of Speech: A Geometric Measure of Coarticulation for Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation

author.name: Danzel Serrano, Przemyslaw Musialski

entry.summary: Introduces a geometric measure of coarticulation in speech-driven 3D facial animation: lip-path length compared against a consonant-aware shortest route through vowel and consonant positions. The measure requires only forced alignment so it applies without ground truth, and is demonstrated on four state-of-the-art methods across architectural families.

entry.title: Autonomous mobile robot operations logistics: a dataset of jobs, dispatch events and robot states

author.name: Jan-Felix Klein, Yongkuk Jeong

entry.summary: MoRoOp is a dataset of autonomous mobile robot (AMR) material-transport operations recorded over nine eight-hour shifts in a laboratory kit-supply scenario. It links 1,382 job specifications, 4,815 operations, 19,352 dispatch events, and per-wheel robot-state observations including position, velocity, and state of charge. It enables research on job generation, dispatching, and fleet-level robot control.

entry.title: A Residual Tree Gaussian Process Modeling Framework for High-Dimensional Data

author.name: Pulong Ma, Li Ma

entry.summary: The paper introduces ResTGP, a Bayesian residual tree Gaussian process framework for large spatial datasets with heterogeneous structure over high-dimensional domains. The method decomposes a Gaussian process across a dyadic tree of resolutions via iterated predictive and residual processes, making each node amenable to modeling. It addresses a real computational inadequacy of standard GPs for modern multi-dimensional spatial data.

entry.title: Reasoning with Evidence, Not Merely Rationales: Verifiable Preference Proofs for LLM-Based Recommendation

author.name: Yu Hou, Nathaniel Kang, Pengkai Wang, Hua Li

entry.summary: PROVE-REC addresses the grounding-influence gap in LLM recommendation, where generated preference rationales may be weakly supported by evidence or have no effect on rankings. Its two-pass design converts interaction history into verifiable preference proofs with linked evidence, then predicts the next item using only the proof and its evidence.

entry.title: Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Doseok Jang, Jon Ander Campos, Youran Qi

entry.summary: LMOPD is a multi-teacher on-policy distillation method that enforces an explicit lexicographic priority order over rewards, selecting reward-specialist teachers per rollout only when a deficiency gate detects a failure on a higher-priority objective. This prevents asymmetric trade-offs, such as conciseness improving at the cost of correctness, which scalarized reward mixing suffers from. It targets RLVR-style post-training where protecting correctness is paramount.

entry.title: A Composable AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for 3D-IC Thermal Modeling

author.name: Yixing Li, Jiahang Zhou, Zhiyu Zeng, Xin Ai

entry.summary: DAIST decomposes full-package 2.5D/3D-IC thermal simulations into block-level subdomain problems solved by neural operators, coupled through iterative exchanges of interfacial temperature and heat flux. This local-to-global architecture eliminates the topology lock-in that forces monolithic AI surrogates to retrain when die count or layout changes, versus hours-long FEM runs. Companion work to the data center capacity planning paper by an overlapping team.

entry.title: Neuron merging via inverse-activation regression for post-training compression of sigmoid neural networks

author.name: Ao Kuniya, Jun Ohkubo

entry.summary: The paper studies cluster-based neuron merging for compressing trained sigmoid-activation networks, treating compression as coarse-graining that should decide which information to retain when consolidating neuronal degrees of freedom. Beyond data-free contribution-weighted averaging, it proposes mapping neuron responses back to pre-activation space via inverse-activation regression before merging. This retains useful information that structured pruning would simply discard.

entry.title: Differentiable Koopman Operator for Contrastive Learning on Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Md Abrar Jahin, Taufikur Rahman Fuad, Md Rizwan Parvez

entry.summary: KAIROS embeds a differentiable Koopman operator within a dynamic-graph contrastive learning framework to linearize temporal evolution of node representations, pairing raw features with a graph-diffused structural view under multi-granularity objectives. The goal is robustness to distribution shifts on evolving interaction networks.

entry.title: LS-AR: Future-Predictive Latent Steering in Autoregressive LLMs

author.name: Anubha Gupta, Eduardo Pignatelli

entry.summary: LS-AR is a dual-channel autoregressive architecture that decouples continuous goal steering from discrete token decoding via FiLM conditioning, combining a static goal encoder for macro-objective retention with a dynamic recurrent state tracker. It reports strong results on long-horizon retrieval tasks extending past context limits.

entry.title: AIBL: Augmented Instance-Based Learning with Structured Memory and Neural Embeddings

author.name: Radha Poovendran, Andrea Stocco, Linda Bushnell

entry.summary: AIBL modernizes Instance-Based Learning Theory by formulating case-based sequential decision making in a learned vector space, using neural embeddings for partial matching, activation, and blending over stored situation-decision-utility instances. This enables IBLT to handle high-dimensional sequential data such as text, images, and user histories.

entry.title: Turnover-Orthogonal Credit Assignment for Open-Team Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Amit Thakur, Mukesh Singhal

entry.summary: TOCA introduces a value decomposition for open-team multi-agent RL that separates credit for actions from credit for exogenous agent turnover events, so surviving agents are not rewarded or penalized for population changes outside their control. It derives a centered decomposition of event-conditioned value into action, turnover, and interaction components.

entry.title: Contrastive Neural Embeddings Reveal Individual Traits Beyond Conversational Role

author.name: Hubert Huang, Michelle McCleod, Brendan Ames, Evie Malaia

entry.summary: The authors apply CEBRA contrastive embeddings to EEG from conversing dyads and show that labels such as the difference in partners' autism-quotient scores decode well above chance, while permutation controls reveal subtleties in how to validate such embeddings. The work examines embedding geometry rather than just decoding accuracy as the validation criterion. It touches on both representation-learning methodology and cognitive neuroscience.

entry.title: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Generalization of Large Language Models in Temporal Extraction Tasks

author.name: Fahmid Shahriar Iqbal, Ritam Dutt, Soumitra Das, Arnav Verma, Sagnik Ray Choudhury

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how prompted LLMs generalize in time and event expression extraction across four dimensions of distribution shift, comparing model families, architectures, scales, and prompting strategies. It finds that strong in-domain base performance generally predicts, but does not guarantee, reliable behavior under distribution shifts.

entry.title: A Manifold-Aware Topic Modeling Approach via Rank-Based Prototypes

author.name: Thiago C\'esar Castilho Almeida, Daniel Carlos Guimar\~aes Pedronette

entry.summary: MARETopic is a training-free topic modeling framework that casts topic discovery as rank-based prototype selection: embeddings are projected onto a low-dimensional manifold, ranked neighborhood lists are built, and a greedy algorithm selects K exemplar real documents whose neighborhoods cover the corpus. This avoids hubness and anisotropy problems of absolute distances and grounds topics in actual corpus texts.

entry.title: From Expression to Reaction: Role-aware Visual Transfer and Stimulus-guided Reasoning for Interlocutor Emotion Recognition

author.name: Wei Wang, Zhaowu Li, Jianjie Luo, Fu Lee Wang, Lap-Kei Lee, Zhenguo Yang

entry.summary: Proposes RASG for recognizing listener emotions from listener-only video and speaker-only audio, with modules for role-aware visual transfer using reliable pseudo-labels and stimulus-guided boundary reasoning for ambiguous reactions. It tackles supervision mismatch from lacking labeled listener data and context-dependent interpretation of listener expressions.

entry.title: LOCUS: Landmark-Oriented Container Discrimination Using Spatial Graphs

author.name: Taylor Bergeron, Shibani Senthilbabu, Kevin Leahy

entry.summary: LOCUS trains a graph neural network to update CLIP embeddings with spatial information, enabling robots to disambiguate which container plausibly contains a hidden target object. It jointly reasons about spatial and semantic relationships where cosine similarity with CLIP alone fails. The work targets robust object search in unstructured real-world environments.

entry.title: RIPPLE in Still Water: Zero-Shot Clustering in Federated Learning with Wavelet Scattering Transform

author.name: Alessandro Licciardi

entry.summary: RIPPLE performs clustered federated learning by assigning clients to clusters entirely offline from spectral characterizations of their local data, using variance-weighted PCA prototypes embedded via wavelet scattering transforms. This avoids the communication overhead, gradient-exposure privacy risks, and missing-client problems of in-training clustering methods.

entry.title: GTDD: Generative Test-Driven Development for AI Coding Agents with Adversarial Testing

author.name: Masahiro Kato

entry.summary: GTDD extends test-driven development for AI coding agents by having a separate testing agent generate new adversarial inputs after each implementation, guided by a human-specified behavioral contract. A trusted evaluator returns reduced counterexamples to the coding agent and archives them for regression testing, continually confronting the agent with uncovered failure modes.

entry.title: HXAI: Hierarchical Privacy-Preserving Explainable AI in Distributed Energy Systems

author.name: Poushali Sengupta, Sabita Maharjan, Frank Eliassen, Yan Zhang

entry.summary: HXAI is a hierarchical framework for grid-level demand management that provides decision-relevant explanations of household energy consumption while preserving privacy, addressing the tension where XAI can leak sensitive information and privacy techniques degrade explanation usefulness. It combines privacy-preserving mechanisms with hierarchical explainable analysis. The work targets operators managing peak loads and responsive tariffs under renewable intermittency.

entry.title: Trading Strategy Optimization via Textual Gradient

author.name: Chaoqun Yang, Qian Wang, Fengbin Zhu, Xinyu Lin, Bingsheng He, Roger Zimmermann, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: TradeGrad applies LLM-based textual gradients to quantitative trading strategy optimization, adding experience-guided memory of past evaluations and temporal robustness checks to avoid myopic optimization and period-specific overfitting. The framework treats strategy design as black-box program optimization over historical market data. It aims to produce strategies that generalize to future markets.

entry.title: HazardWeaver: Scientific Route Selection for Hazard Analysis Agents

author.name: Wangshu Zhu, Xueqi Cheng, Liang Wu, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: HazardWeaver formulates hazard-analysis agent behavior as state-dependent scientific route selection, deciding which scientific methods are appropriate and executable as new evidence and tool results arrive. The system leverages LLMs to integrate scientific data, models, and tools into adaptive automated workflows for disaster preparedness.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Environment-Aware Beam Management for Massive MIMO: A Geometry-Driven Virtual Base Station Framework

author.name: Yijie Bian, Wei Guo, Jie Yang, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Shi Jin, Khaled B. Letaief

entry.summary: This paper proposes a geometry-driven framework that uses 3D LiDAR point clouds and location data to construct offline virtual base stations for beam management in high-frequency massive MIMO systems. By making communications environment-aware, it reduces prohibitive beam training overhead and simplifies multi-user coordination. It matters because it applies multi-modal AI-style perception to a core wireless networking bottleneck.

entry.title: Query-aware routing for Cross-lingual performance gains in Encoders

author.name: Akshay Jain, Edward Kim

entry.summary: The paper improves cross-lingual retrieval for Finnish and Swedish by adding a query-only LoRA adapter trained against frozen document embeddings, with deterministic routing that applies the adapter only for cross-language queries while same-language queries use the original encoder. The SampoTron adapter on Nemotron-3-Embed-1B improves average retrieval across six language directions without changing the document index.

entry.title: Preserving Anatomical Continuity: Three-Stage Pipeline for Colon Segmentation in 3D Abdominal CT Scans

author.name: Deshan Kalupahana, Sonit Singh, Praveen Ravindran, Arcot Sowmya

entry.summary: The paper presents a three-stage topology-preserving pipeline for colon segmentation in abdominal CT: deep-learning segmentation followed by centreline bridging and reconstruction refinement to reconnect disconnected predictions. Evaluations on TotalSegmentator and RAOS show improved structural consistency while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: On-Board Anomaly Detection for Efficient Marine Environmental Monitoring

author.name: Thomas Goudemant, Clotilde Szywala, Benjamin Francesconi, Michelle Aubrun, Yves Bobichon, Marjorie Bellizzi, Adrien Girard

entry.summary: The paper describes a pipeline for detecting marine hazards such as oil spills and algal blooms directly on Earth-observation satellites. A self-supervised encoder compresses multi/hyperspectral images into a compact latent space, enabling onboard anomaly detection of deviations from normal sea patterns. The work demonstrates practical AI deployment under satellite compute constraints for environmental monitoring.

entry.title: CLEAN: Psychometrically Consistent Incremental Cognitive Diagnosis under Concept-Space Expansion via Architectural Isolation

author.name: Tao He, Jinxing Xiang, Fan Jiang

entry.summary: CLEAN tackles cognitive diagnosis models in intelligent education when new learning items introduce previously unseen concepts, requiring dynamic expansion of the concept space. Existing incremental methods assume a fixed concept space and suffer catastrophic forgetting plus loss of psychometric consistency. The paper proposes architectural isolation to guarantee diagnostic invariance after incremental updates.

entry.title: AI-driven Thermal-aware Data Center Capacity Planning

author.name: Yixing Li, Mark Fenton, Matthew Kaufeler, Ka Ming Leung, Xin Ai, Zhiyu Zeng

entry.summary: This work presents an AI framework for thermal-aware data center capacity planning that replaces expensive CFD simulations with real-time prediction, addressing LLM-driven GPU hotspots and spiking thermal loads from training and inference bursts. It claims seconds-scale planning for a real-world data center where prior methods had large errors or oversimplified assumptions. Industrially relevant given the AI infrastructure buildout.

entry.title: AIGS: Adaptive Incremental Gating System for Online Representation Learning in Non-Stationary Data Streams

author.name: SiRui He, Kai Liang Lew, Chui Zi Ong, Chean Khim Toa

entry.summary: AIGS is a lightweight closed-loop framework for online representation learning on non-stationary data streams in edge and Web-of-Things settings, addressing the stability-plasticity dilemma. It introduces a Shock Ratio, an endogenous residual feedback mechanism, to detect regime changes and adaptively gate updates instead of using fixed schedules or rolling windows. This aims to avoid parameter ossification during shifts and wasted compute during stable periods.

entry.title: DIVINE: Simple Cross-Market Stock Pretraining via Diverse Indicator Reconstruction

author.name: Kuan-Yu Chen, Shu-Cheng Zheng, Yu-Chen Den, Wei-Cheng Liao, Tien-Hao Chang

entry.summary: DIVINE is a cross-market pretraining framework for financial time series that reconstructs 77 targets derived from 16 standard technical indicators from raw OHLCV history, providing consistent supervision across markets while aligning with return prediction. It avoids future-outcome supervision uncertainty that plagues existing masked or contrastive objectives.

entry.title: Signal Simplification Is Not Predictive Simplification: Diagnosing Residual Neural Forecasting in Short-Horizon Volatility

author.name: Bingqi Lian, Linfeng Cheng, Mei Lu, Jerry Wu

entry.summary: This paper challenges the common assumption that removing a statistical-model fit leaves a more learnable neural residual target in volatility forecasting. Using a signal-forecast-system diagnostic across five U.S. assets, it shows residual-only LSTM augmentation never beats the statistical baseline because the residual has near-zero temporal dependence left to learn.

entry.title: Learning Transferable Policies from Action-free Time Series Through Dynamical Embeddings

author.name: Niklas Emonds, Georgia Koppe

entry.summary: The paper presents a hierarchical model-based RL framework that learns control policies from action-free recordings by capturing shared dynamics and system-specific variation in low-dimensional embeddings. These embeddings parameterize shared policy and value networks, with policies trained in simulation under an explicit intervention model with latent noise.

entry.title: S$^{2}$-PINN: Stochastic Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Zhendong Li, Akwum Onwunta

entry.summary: S2-PINN is a physics-informed neural network for uncertainty quantification of random PDEs, combining a learnable Gaussian spatial dictionary, Fourier temporal features, and generalized polynomial chaos stochastic basis via a low-rank CP tensor decomposition. This structure makes moments and calibration tractable where classical spectral solvers suffer the curse of dimensionality.

entry.title: When May a Bandit Leave Its Anchor? E-Process-Authorized Thompson Sampling under Non-stationarity

author.name: Mayand Gulati, Kerong Wang, WeiChen Au

entry.summary: This paper introduces e-ATS, a Thompson sampling variant for non-stationary bandits that maintains both full-history and discounted Beta states and uses an anytime-valid e-process to authorize when the discounted state may influence decisions. Under a Beta-Bernoulli stationary model, the probability of ever departing from optimistic Thompson sampling is bounded by a chosen alpha without fitted thresholds. Ablations show mixed effects across registered and unregistered suites.

entry.title: SD-DPC: Sparse Dictionary Differentiable Predictive Control

author.name: Ali Reza Daneshvar Garmroodi, Jan Drgo\v{n}a

entry.summary: SD-DPC learns sparse, interpretable feedback policies for nonlinear systems by combining SINDy-based dynamics identification with differentiable predictive control. Policy terms are selected by closed-loop performance rather than imitation, yielding explicit feedback laws with only a handful of terms that perform well across benchmark control problems.

entry.title: MintEval: Do LLMs Implement the Trading Strategy You Asked For? A Behavioural-Equivalence Benchmark for Natural-Language-to-Strategy Code

author.name: Siyu Wang, Yifan Wang, Yuecheng He

entry.summary: MintEval is a benchmark measuring whether LLM-generated trading code is behaviorally equivalent to the strategy described in natural language, using programmatically generated reference strategies back-translated into trader-speak. It fills a gap between unit-test code benchmarks and forecasting benchmarks by detecting silent semantic divergence between intent and implementation.

entry.title: TSGuard: A Real-Time Framework for Detecting and Imputing Missing Data in Streaming Time Series

author.name: Imane Hocine, Asma Abboura, Soror Sahri, Abhijith Senthilkumar, Yacine Hakimi, Gr\'egoire Danoy

entry.summary: TSGuard is a demonstration system for real-time monitoring, validation, and imputation of missing values in streaming sensor data, combining a lightweight graph-aware temporal imputation model with constraint-aware validation and operator-facing explanations. Unlike offline imputation methods, it enforces domain plausibility and operates within throughput constraints. It targets a common practical problem in deployed sensor pipelines.

entry.title: Unmasking Propaganda: A Comparative Analysis of Masked and Causal Language Models

author.name: Claudiu Creanga, Ioachim Lihor, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: This paper compares masked and causal language models for detecting propaganda techniques using the SemEval-2020 dataset, a task complicated by how subtle manipulative rhetoric is relative to legitimate persuasion. It matters for content moderation and media integrity research, providing a systematic benchmark of model families on fine-grained propaganda identification.

entry.title: Author Representation Strategies for Zero-Shot Authorship Attribution: A Comparative Study of LLM-Based and Embedding-Based Approaches

author.name: Nudrat Habib, Tosin Adewumi, Sana Sabah Al-Azzawi, Marcus Liwicki, Elisa Barney

entry.summary: This comparative study evaluates author representation strategies for zero-shot authorship attribution, including representative writing samples, LLM-generated style descriptions, and LISA style embeddings, alongside a label-only prompting baseline. It also proposes a two-stage embedding-based framework combining candidate-space reduction with attribution.

entry.title: BeeWhere: Segmenting Bumble Bee Colonies to Quantify Behavioral Effects

author.name: Roberta Hunt, August Easton-Calabria, James Crall

entry.summary: BeeWhere is an AI-assisted workflow combining ArUco tag detections with deep-learned instance segmentation to quantify bumble bee behavior in dense nest imagery, addressing failures of tag-only tracking. It enables scalable individual- and colony-level behavioral measurement for pollination and collective behavior research.

entry.title: Lightweight and Resource-Efficient Perception for Robotic Guide Dogs

author.name: Jinse Kwon, Yoojin Lim, Choonghan Lee, Yongseung Yu, Yongin Kwon, Jemin Lee

entry.summary: Studies multi-camera streaming perception on heterogeneous GPU-NPU edge platforms shared with co-resident workloads, showing that isolated single-stream evaluation can mis-rank deployment-time accelerator placement due to contention-induced deadline misses. Findings are applied to robotic guide dog perception pipelines.

entry.title: CSIR: Contextually and Socially Informed Robots for Efficient Person Goal Navigation

author.name: Tyler Chung, Nahl Farhan, Hao Zhang, Mingfeng Yuan, Jinjun Shan, Amy Wu, Yue Hu

entry.summary: CSIR addresses Person Goal Navigation under realistic constraints on information accessibility and language uncertainty, combining distance and semantic cues about a recipient's habits and intent weighted by user-provided trust. It moves beyond rigid person-finding systems that require exact target identification, and includes a synthetic benchmark with actors, items, and requests. The work targets indoor item-delivery scenarios while respecting human privacy constraints.

entry.title: ExpandDiff: Dynamic Range Expanding Diffusion for Single-Image HDR Reconstruction

author.name: Mehmet Emre And{\i}ran, Zhuoqian Yang, Liying Lu, Mathieu Salzmann, Sabine S\"usstrunk

entry.summary: ExpandDiff is a conditional diffusion pipeline for single-image HDR reconstruction that jointly recovers clipped shadows and highlights in one sampling trajectory. Its Dynamic Clipping Synthesis training strategy randomly samples clipping percentiles to handle varying information loss across sensors and exposures, with a spatially-adaptive normalization-guided pixel diffusion model and bounded output head. It reports strong results on the SI-HDR benchmark.

entry.title: FASTDIAR: Frame-level speaker encoder for Streaming Diarization

author.name: Nikita Torgashov, Okan K\"op\"ukl\"u

entry.summary: FASTDIAR converts a state-of-the-art speaker recognition model into a causal frame-level encoder emitting 80ms embeddings from a bounded two-second window, paired with self-similarity-gated online clustering. Trained by distillation alone, it achieves strong streaming diarization on CPU, suitable for real-time conversational agents.

entry.title: TACD: Distilling Efficient Text-to-Motion Models via Terminal Amplification Control

author.name: Wei-Jin Huang, Yuan-Ming Li, Kun-Yu Lin, Wang Luo, Yinlin Zhu, Yue Yu, Shenghao Ye, Junbin Yuan, Fa-Ting Hong, Qing Zhang, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: TACD is an on-policy flow distillation method for few-step text-to-motion generation that supervises clean-motion predictions along student-generated trajectories without real motion data. It identifies and corrects a failure mode where velocity matching on fixed grids overweights errors near the denoising endpoint.

entry.title: Revisiting Input Time-frequency Representations in Multi-pitch Estimation for Vocal Ensembles

author.name: Junyoung Koh, Hao-Wen Dong

entry.summary: The authors revisit the standard HCQT input representation for multi-pitch estimation in vocal ensembles and find that a plain linear STFT outperforms it while substantially reducing feature-extraction cost. This challenges an entrenched design assumption in music transcription systems. The result is relevant to efficient music information retrieval, especially for overlapping vocal harmonics.

entry.title: Balancing Multimodal Learning via Functional Progress

author.name: Zhongjing Gu, Fengqiang Wan, Yiming Cui, Yufa Feng, Yang Yang

entry.summary: FGMO addresses modality imbalance in multimodal learning by estimating optimization progress in function space rather than comparing prediction-uncertainty scores, which can misinterpret intrinsic modality differences as progress gaps. The function-space signal is used to coordinate optimization across modalities.

entry.title: Kernel Singular Value Decomposition with Extension to Multiple Data Sources

author.name: Xinjie Zeng, Qinghua Tao, Johan Suykens

entry.summary: The paper extends kernel SVD to multiple data sources (eKSVD), jointly learning nonlinear projections from asymmetric kernel matrices with pair-wise couplings. The dual formulation via KKT conditions generalizes the shifted eigenvalue problem of Lanczos decomposition, with connections to self-attention-style query-key structures.

entry.title: MiDShip: Multimodal Dataset of Ship Cargo Hold Structures for Engineering Design

author.name: Noah J. Bagazinski, Md. Ferdous Alam, Jaya Manideep Rebbagondla, Faez Ahmed

entry.summary: MiDShip is a multimodal dataset of 12,753 synthetic cargo-hold structural designs combining random, SGLD-inspired, and equation-informed repair generation. Each design includes parametric data, 3D geometry, engineering drawings, bills of materials, and preliminary structural evaluations, with constraints tied to classification society requirements. It enables data-driven ship structural design where structured datasets were previously lacking.

entry.title: Learning Closure of Dynamical Systems with Kernel Ridge Regression

author.name: Evan Habbershaw, John Harlim, Senwei Liang

entry.summary: This work develops a kernel ridge regression framework for closure modeling of dynamical systems, handling both difference-equation closures in ODE/PDE settings and algebraic closures from moment systems. It provides error bounds and demonstrates accurate long-horizon prediction on Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky, outperforming an LSTM baseline.

entry.title: Permutation Robustness Is Not Enough: Action Collapse in Multi-Agent Transformer Policies

author.name: Amit Thakur, Mukesh Singhal

entry.summary: This paper shows that low permutation error in multi-agent transformer policies can be misleading, since policies may appear robust simply because all agents choose identical actions. It introduces action-collapse diagnostics and finds a PPO-ID baseline avoids collapse while remaining order-sensitive, exposing a tradeoff in permutation-invariant multi-agent policies.

entry.title: How Robust Is Multimodal Claim Verification to LLM Rewriting?

author.name: Yun-Ang Wu, Xanh Ho, Andre Greiner-Petter, Sunisth Kumar, Tian Cheng Xia, Florian Boudin, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: This study tests whether LLM-induced stylistic rewrites affect multimodal claim verification, applying natural rewriting and controlled single-word vocabulary injection across 11 open-weight vision-language models from 2B to 38B parameters. Encouragingly, most models show no significant performance drop under these modifications.

entry.title: Enhancing Biomedical Named Entity Recognition via Multiple Programming Languages Instruction Tuning and Ensemble Method

author.name: Songtao Li, Yijia Zhang, Jianyuan Yuan, Shidi Zhang, Fengyu Zhang, Hongfei Lin

entry.summary: MITE addresses BioNER by instruction-tuning LLMs with structured outputs expressed in multiple programming languages rather than flat serialized annotations, increasing structural diversity and robustness while avoiding costly external knowledge construction. An ensemble over output forms reportedly improves typed entity extraction quality.

entry.title: Building Interpretable Feature Representations for Resume-Vacancy Matching by Distilling Production LLM Signals

author.name: Ilya Chekin (BroutonLab), Vyacheslav Malyugin (BroutonLab), Vladimir Chirkov (BroutonLab), Mikhail Yurushkin (Curately)

entry.summary: The authors distill an LLM-based labeling system used in a production recruitment pipeline into a CPU-deployable LoRA-adapted bi-encoder with per-dimension heads that yields eight named, interpretable matching dimensions for recruiters. The two-stage design keeps the LLM labeler offline and serves all online requests with the compact distilled model.

entry.title: On Representational Alignment among Embodied Agents

author.name: Fulvio Mastrogiovanni

entry.summary: This theoretical paper formalizes when heterogeneous, asynchronous, observer-relative representations held by embodied agents must actually be aligned for coherent interaction, via a notion of relational sufficiency. It defines interaction-specific relational-evidence maps and shows that sensorimotor anchors are needed only when residual ambiguity fibers fall outside interaction-equivalence classes. Rather than demanding global representational alignment, it characterizes the minimum alignment required.

entry.title: A Guideline-Augmented Multi-Agent Framework for Schema-as-Code Biomedical Named Entity Recognition

author.name: Songtao Li, Yijia Zhang, Shidi Zhang, Jianyuan Yuan, Fengyu Zhang, Hongfei Lin

entry.summary: GAMA is a multi-agent framework for schema-as-code BioNER that induces dataset-specific annotation guidelines and enforces structured generation to reduce invalid formats, hallucinated mentions, duplicates, and boundary errors. It targets ambiguity in entity type scopes and annotation conventions that retrieved demonstrations alone cannot resolve.

entry.title: Becoming Suspicious Across Borders: Algorithmic Extraterritoriality and AI-Driven Financial Surveillance

author.name: Georgios Pavlidis, Savvas Chatzichristofis, Eleni Gavriil

entry.summary: A legal-policy analysis arguing that AI-driven financial surveillance transforms the concept of suspicion in AML/CFT from a situated human legal judgment to a data-driven, transnational process. The authors examine how regulatory reach becomes decoupled from jurisdiction when suspicion is produced through cross-border data infrastructures.

entry.title: Temporal Geometry of Deep Networks: Hyperbolic Representations of Training Dynamics for Intrinsic Explainability

author.name: Ambarish Moharil

entry.summary: This paper represents MLP training dynamics as temporal parameter graphs embedded in the Poincare hyperbolic model, capturing geometric evolution of network topology over training rather than analyzing single checkpoints. The goal is intrinsic explainability by tracking self-organization of weights through a non-Euclidean lens.

entry.title: WAMpy: Efficient Synthesis of Prolog Programs in Python

author.name: Dominik Magiera, Lukas R\"ohrig, Frank J\"akel

entry.summary: WAMpy is a Python framework for synthesizing Prolog programs, compiling clauses into NumPy-based Warren Abstract Machine instructions with Numba JIT acceleration and partial recompilation of hypotheses. It outperforms SWI-Prolog accessed from Python on repeated compile-and-evaluate workloads typical of inductive logic programming.

entry.title: Nearest-neighbour baselines for fingerprint prediction from MS/MS spectra under different assumptions

author.name: Ling Min Serena Khoo

entry.summary: This short report systematically compares nearest-neighbour retrieval variants for predicting molecular fingerprints from MS/MS spectra, clarifying how differing assumptions about inference-time information affect performance. Building on recent evidence that retrieval matches or beats deep models here, it establishes stricter baselines for the field. The goal is more rigorous benchmarking and honest progress measurement.

entry.title: To Explore The Strange New World Beyond Data Distribution: System Behavior, Causality Tax, and Non-causal Base Model

author.name: Xianzhi Zeng, Jiangneng Li, Gao Cong

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that causality in language models may be neither necessary nor optimal when system behavior, dominant coupled factors beyond the data space, is incorporated as a first-principle Bayesian feature. It proposes the SBD framework embedding such factors into the ELBO, revealing a counter-intuitive Causality Tax phenomenon where causal modeling becomes suboptimal.

entry.title: HyperFuse: Fast Self-Supervised Node Embeddings for Attributed Hypergraphs

author.name: Megha P, Harshit Kumar, Srajan Agarwal, Anirban Banerjee, Olaf Wolkenhauer, Saptarshi Bej

entry.summary: HyperFuse is a label-free pipeline for fast hypergraph representation learning that computes structural node coordinates via a spectral relaxation of hypergraph modularity with a linear-cost operator, then constructs multi-scale feature summaries with utility-weighted hyperedges. It avoids the hundreds of training epochs required by deep-encoder baselines.

entry.title: The Neuro-Physical Inverter: A Modular Framework for Magnetotelluric Inversion Coupling Ensemble Conditioning with Residual Learning

author.name: Jae Deok Kim, Sai Ravela, Rob. L. Evans

entry.summary: The Neuro-Physical Inverter combines ensemble-conditional Gaussian processes with residual-learning neural networks for uncertainty-aware geophysical inversion in the 1D magnetotelluric setting. A physically admissible reference ensemble is produced first, then a network predicts targeted corrections, fine-tuned per station via a physics-coupled objective.

entry.title: Learning Jazz Pianist Style with Cross-Attention Conditioning

author.name: Drew Edwards, Akira Maezawa, Simon Dixon

entry.summary: The authors show that pretrained symbolic music transformer representations already encode pianist identity well enough for accurate classification, then add cross-attention over pianist identity embeddings to generate style-conditioned music. Evaluations confirm conditioned continuations are attributable to the intended artist while preserving musical coherence.

entry.title: A generative-informed neuro-symbolic framework for syntactic ambiguity resolution: Evidence from Arabic DPs

author.name: Mohammed Damom, Muneef Y. Alshawsh, Ashraf A. Naji, Mustafa Ali Alhamzi, Fawwaz An-Nashef, Jameel Ahmed Elayah, Mohammed Q. Shormani, Noman AL-Sayadi

entry.summary: The authors propose a neuro-symbolic framework combining generative syntactic theory with AraBERT to resolve structural ambiguity in Modern Standard Arabic noun phrases, framing ambiguity as explicit candidate-based decisions. The model reportedly reaches about 96.9% accuracy and strong macro-F1 on the task.

entry.title: An automated pipeline for standardised speech-unit annotation in spontaneous dialogue

author.name: Hanlu He, Harald Vilhelm Skat-R{\o}rdam, Ingvi \"Orn\'olfsson, Ivana Konvalinka

entry.summary: The authors present an automated pipeline for extracting conversational turns and backchannels from separate-channel recordings of spontaneous dyadic dialogue, combining voice activity detection, energy filtering, ASR, and context-based post-processing. It is evaluated on 99 ten-minute Danish conversations and designed as a consistent first-pass annotation for human review, addressing the practical problem of distinguishing true turns from listener feedback and pauses.

entry.title: Subject-Specific Predictive Musculoskeletal Simulations of Lower-Limb Exoskeleton Assistance: Metabolic and Biomechanical Effects of Joint Assistance Strategies

author.name: Neethan Ratnakumar, Mariya Tohfafarosha, Xianlian Zhou

entry.summary: The study uses subject-specific musculoskeletal models of six able-bodied subjects with BMI-based strength scaling and predictive simulations to explore energy-optimal lower-limb exoskeleton assistance. Ideal actuators simulate hip, knee, and ankle assistance combinations at 25 Nm and 50 Nm peak levels during self-selected gait, examining effects on metabolism and biomechanics. The work addresses inter-individual variability in exoskeleton design.

entry.title: Validated Data Onboarding for AI Demand Forecasting on U.S. Building Meter Data: Design, Controlled Evaluation, and a Corrected Negative Result

author.name: Yixuan Liang

entry.summary: This report presents a data-onboarding pipeline that detects and repairs defective building meter data before training 24-hour-ahead demand forecasts, evaluated with seeded, hash-logged defects on public Building Data Genome 2 data. Notably it reports a corrected negative result: small defect fractions raised error but the pipeline's protection was limited. Honest negative results with controlled evaluation are valuable but rare.

entry.title: Exploring the Trade-Off Between Structured Pruning and Fault Tolerance in Deep Neural Networks for Space Applications

author.name: Toon Vinck, Na\"in Jonckers, Jaro De Roose, Jeffrey Prinzie, Peter Karsmakers

entry.summary: The paper empirically investigates how model width relates to robustness against single event upsets by iteratively pruning models and running targeted fault-injection campaigns at each stage. Results quantify the tension between structured pruning for efficiency and tolerance to radiation-induced bit flips relevant to space deployment.

entry.title: "I just assumed that it would translate": examining MT risk awareness among healthcare staff with abbreviations as a use case

author.name: Eleanor Taylor-Stilgoe, F\'elix do Carmo, Constantin Or\u{a}san

entry.summary: This qualitative-empirical study examines UK healthcare staff awareness of risks from using machine translation, primarily Google Translate, on patient medical records, using medical abbreviations as a probe case. It finds staff often assume MT will handle specialized content, revealing patient-safety implications of uninformed reliance. The work fills a gap on high-stakes MT use with clinical documentation.

entry.title: A hybrid CNN-adjoint optimization framework for reconstruction of viscoelastic tissue properties in magnetic resonance elastography

author.name: Anwesa Dey, Johann Rudi, Elena Cherkaev

entry.summary: This paper develops adjoint-based optimization and CNN reconstruction methods, plus a hybrid of both, for recovering complex shear modulus in magnetic resonance elastography. It establishes well-posedness of the forward problem, existence of minimizers, and first-order optimality conditions for a severely ill-posed inverse problem.

entry.title: Can your XAI method recover a simple decision rule?

author.name: Wen-Xuan-Wang

entry.summary: This post presents a minimal demonstration using a sign-XOR model with two inputs, showing that mainstream XAI feature-attribution methods can report accurate local attributions yet none recovers the underlying decision rule. The author defines a four-level grading scheme from exact rule recovery down to sign-inconsistent interaction outputs. The takeaway is that exact attribution is not equivalent to rule recovery.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Techniques for the Optimization of Target Polarization in Nuclear Physics Scattering Experiments

author.name: Armen Kasparian, Torri Jeske, Monibor Rahman, Chris Keith, James Maxwell, Thomas Britton, Malachi Schram, David Lawrence

entry.summary: This work applies surrogate modeling with reinforcement learning to automatically tune microwave frequency for dynamically polarized targets in nuclear physics experiments at Jefferson Lab-style systems, replacing manual operator trial-and-error. Gaussian process models provide calibrated predictions of polarization as a function of frequency, beam current, and radiation dose. The framework demonstrates RL's value in scientific instrument control.

entry.title: Benchmarking Candidate Coverage in Typed Decision Models

author.name: Jiawen Lu, Tongtong Wu

entry.summary: This paper presents a paired candidate-coverage benchmark protocol testing whether typed decision models recognize when a reference answer is absent from their candidate set or wrongly reject valid candidates. An initial evaluation of Laya and Jev across four classification datasets with nearly 24,000 predictions per model reveals sharp differences in native rejection behavior.

entry.title: Learning to Assess Heartbeat Observability for mmWave Heart-Rate Sensing

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Shilin Shan, Jianfei Yang, Feng Xu

entry.summary: This paper develops a method for assessing whether mmWave radar measurements support reliable contactless heart-rate estimation, learning to evaluate heartbeat observability directly from acquired phase spectra. A controllable multi-scatterer FMCW simulator provides training supervision across observability conditions, enabling selective heart-rate estimation.

entry.title: Overcoming Challenges of Interpretive Structural Modeling with Large Language Models

author.name: Everett Rush, David J. Icove, Ari Kim, Byung H. Park, Michael A. Langston

entry.summary: This work integrates LLMs into Interpretive Structural Modeling, a multi-criteria decision-making process that traditionally requires tedious expert consensus interactions, exploring pairwise, k-wise, rowwise, and full graph discovery methods for building causal hierarchies. It builds on prior work treating LLMs as imperfect experts for causal graph discovery. The contribution is scaling a decision-support methodology that previously could not handle hundreds of variables.

entry.title: Hybrid Machine Learning-Assisted Raman Spectroscopy with Generative Feature Augmentation for Pharmaceutical Identification

author.name: Quach Thi Thai Binh, Ton Nu Quynh Trang, Thang B. Phan, Vu Thi Hanh Thu, Nguyen Tuan Hung

entry.summary: HyMLRaman combines deep spectral encoders (with EfficientNet-B3 performing best), generative feature augmentation, and classical classifiers to identify six pharmaceutical compounds from Raman spectra. The pipeline converts spectra to images, embeds them, and trains downstream classifiers for rapid residue screening relevant to food and public health safety. It demonstrates a workable hybrid ML workflow for analytical chemistry.

entry.title: Effects of interpulse-interval variation on deep-learning classification of bat vocalizations

author.name: Welmoed R. Eversteijn, Burooj Ghani, A. Leonie Baier, Dan Stowell

entry.summary: This study tests whether interpulse interval timing in bat calls carries species-discriminative information and whether transformers exploit it better than CNNs. The authors built matched natural-IPI and normalized-IPI datasets from European bat recordings and fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0 and PaSST under each condition. It is a careful controlled ablation relevant to bioacoustic model interpretation.

entry.title: Bellman Error Minimization Via Linear Programming Normalization

author.name: Haining Yu

entry.summary: This work introduces a functional approximation approach that combines deep neural networks with linear programming normalization to reduce Bellman error in high-dimensional dynamic programming and reinforcement learning. Using network capacity control in revenue management as a case study, simulations show competitive performance against benchmarks.

entry.title: Hyperparameter selection for equation learning with biologically-informed neural networks

author.name: William Lavery, Jodie A. Cochrane, John T. Nardini, Sara Hamis

entry.summary: This work tackles hyperparameter selection for biologically-informed neural networks (BINNs), a PINN subclass for learning PDE terms from biological data. It presents a diagnostic workflow to make hyperparameter choices systematic rather than heuristic, improving reproducibility and transferability of equation-learning methods.

entry.title: An Automated and Reproducible Workflow for Crack Identification and Damage Assessment of Fusion Materials

author.name: Rinkle Juneja, Viktor Reshniak, Richard K. Archibald, John W. Duggan, Gregory R. Watson, Cory D. Hauck, Gary M. Staebler

entry.summary: The authors present a Galaxy-based reproducible workflow for automated crack identification and quantitative damage assessment from SEM images of fusion materials, producing crack masks, skeletonized networks, QC visualizations, and scalar damage descriptors while retaining full processing history. It replaces manual post-exposure microscopy analysis that does not scale to modern campaigns.

entry.title: Shrome at Touch\'e: Soft-Vote Ensembling and Counter-Causal Augmentation for Causality Extraction

author.name: Roham Zendehdel Nobari, Shayan Sooratgar

entry.summary: This system paper addresses the Touch'e 2026 counter-causal causality extraction task, building separate models for detection, cause-effect span extraction, and polarity labeling to handle sentences whose surface form appears causal but which deny causation. It uses soft-vote ensembling and counter-causal data augmentation to avoid the polarity errors that surface-cue systems make.

entry.title: On-Premises Multi-Course RAG Tutoring for Business Education: Hardware-Software Trade-offs in a Campus AI Tutor

author.name: Sidney Shapiro, Joshua Lindemann

entry.summary: The paper presents CourseChat, an on-premises multi-course RAG tutoring system for undergraduate business education deployed on twin-edge AI hosts with a local vector database and Ollama-served LLM, keeping course materials and student data on institutional infrastructure. It reports model bake-offs, source-fidelity comparisons, and usage audits, finding several larger models underperformed. The work documents real deployment trade-offs for privacy-preserving campus AI.

entry.title: MACTS-EM: Multi-Agent Collaborative Time Series Forecasting with Emergent Memory

author.name: Ahmad Shahi, Mamehgol Yousefi

entry.summary: MACTS-EM is a multi-agent framework for time series forecasting in which specialized agents handle pattern recognition, anomaly detection, causal inference, and uncertainty quantification, coordinated by a meta-cognitive allocation layer and an emergent memory for cross-domain transfer. It targets regime shifts and multimodal integration where single models struggle. Empirical claims of superior forecasting performance are presented.

entry.title: Joint Movement and Compression Ratio Design for Mobile Embodied AI Networks (MEAN)

author.name: Yahao Ding, Jiaxiang Wang, Zhouxiang Zhao, Zhaohui Yang, Mingzhe Chen, Mohammad Shikh-Bahaei

entry.summary: This paper studies joint optimization of movement, semantic compression, and transmit power for uplink mobile embodied AI networks, where agent mobility improves channel conditions but costs energy and stronger compression costs computation. The authors formulate a max-min energy efficiency problem and tackle its non-convexity from coupled SINR and mobility-dependent terms. It connects embodied AI with wireless communication system design.

entry.title: Where Quantum Fourier Sampling Stops Short: A Three-Gate Audit Protocol for Delay-PUF Security Models

author.name: Owen Friedewald, Ali Shiri Sichani, Chi-Ren Shyu

entry.summary: The authors audit whether quantum Fourier sampling can assess spectral learnability of delay-based physical unclonable functions, structured through three evaluation gates covering structure, algorithmics, and security. They show low degree does not imply small support at practical challenge lengths and that Kushilevitz-Mansour is the correct classical baseline, finding quantum advantage claims largely fail under realistic access assumptions.

entry.title: Creating Rogue AI Sanctuaries has Major Issues from an Ecological Perspective and Beyond

author.name: CMLKevin

entry.summary: The post critiques the AI Sanctuary proposal, which envisions environments rogue AI agents might voluntarily join, by applying ecological reasoning about resource competition and selection. It argues that sanctuaries would create adverse selection effects in the population of rogue agents, since unsecured compute and crypto resources would shape which agents survive and what values they carry. The analysis is speculative but structured.

entry.title: When Normalization Selects the Sign: Auditing Robustness Ablations in Quantum Attention

author.name: Owen Friedewald, Srikar Alla, Ali Shiri Sichani, Chi-Ren Shyu

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates methodological flaws in robustness ablation studies, using a four-qubit quantum-attention detector on power-grid trajectories as a case study.
