author.name: Wenhao Liang, Lin Yue, Wei Emma Zhang, Mingyu Guo, Olaf Maennel, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: This paper audits whether routing entropy in dynamic architectures carries correctness information beyond the model's own output confidence. Using Swin-Tiny and DeiT-Small attention-residual variants trained with soft-binned calibration on CIFAR-10/100, the authors run rigorous controls: fixed-confidence checks, seed replication, and held-out predictors against output-only and shuffled-trace baselines. A sensitivity audit injects effects of known size to measure detector power.

entry.title: TopK-Guided: Adaptive, Budget-Aware Activation Sparsity for Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Mukund Agarwalla, Chih-Jen Lin

entry.summary: TopK-Guided is a training-free activation sparsity method for LLM inference that combines bounded token-level sparsity adaptation with sensitivity-aware block-level budget allocation. It addresses limitations of threshold-based methods like TEAL (no tight sparsity control) and TopK-based methods like WINA (uniform per-token budget), which also ignore block sensitivity differences. Skipping unimportant computations directly reduces inference cost.

entry.title: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries

author.name: Ionel Eduard Stan, Paolo Napoletano

entry.summary: The paper introduces Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation (BDA), which treats typed moves in multi-LLM deliberation (proposals, challenges, concessions) as observations to produce calibrated probability-of-correctness estimates and to identify and discount persistently unreliable agents. The authors argue existing council aggregation methods measure decisiveness rather than correctness and fail against persistent adversaries. This addresses both calibration and robustness in multi-LLM decision systems.

entry.title: Spatial Lifting for Dense Prediction

author.name: Mingzhi Xu, Tao Zhou, Yong Li, Yizhe Zhang

entry.summary: Spatial Lifting is a counterintuitive method that lifts 2D inputs into higher-dimensional spaces (e.g., processing 2D images with a 3D U-Net), achieving competitive dense-prediction performance with drastically fewer parameters and lower inference cost. The lifted dimension produces intrinsically structured outputs enabling dense supervision and single-pass uncertainty estimation.

entry.title: The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Matthieu Zimmer, Xiaotong Ji, Tu Nguyen, Haitham Bou-Ammar

entry.summary: Argues that reasoning distillation suffers from a weakest-link problem: a chain-of-thought is only as valid as its weakest step, yet GRPO-style reward hacking and KL-regularized distillation both average over steps, letting students compensate for severe logical violations. The paper formulates worst-case constrained RL to penalize the worst step rather than aggregate rewards or soft divergence.

entry.title: How AI Agents Discover Scientific Equations: From Hydrotope Rediscovery to New Water-Wave Amplitudes

author.name: Zihan Zhou, Digvijay Wadekar, Matias Zaldarriaga

entry.summary: The authors use a controlled case study of the hydrotope, a recently discovered geometric formula for nonlinear surface-wave scattering, to study how AI agents discover and validate scientific formulas. They reconstruct the original human-agent collaboration and analyze 18 single-prompt rediscovery runs under no hint, a false hint, and a true hint conditions. The work provides empirical insight into the dynamics of AI-assisted scientific discovery.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents

author.name: Zhengyuan Jiang, Reachal Wang, Yuepeng Hu, Yupu Wang, Yuqi Jia, Neil Zhenqiang Gong

entry.summary: Presents RuleEvolve, a framework in which a pool of candidate coding rules for AI coding agents is iteratively improved by an LLM-powered mutator that generates variants and a judge module that evaluates and prunes them. Evaluations across two coding-agent frameworks, four backbone LLMs, and three benchmarks show it outperforms hand-crafted and fixed rules. This matters because coding-rule quality is a key input to agent performance and manual rule-writing is labor-intensive.

entry.title: Training-Aware Target Coverage for Synthetic Data Selection

author.name: Yang Ba, Michelle V. Mancenido, Rong Pan

entry.summary: The paper develops a linear theory characterizing when synthetic data add task-relevant information versus introducing errors that offset their benefit, including how an example's value changes as the training set grows. Building on this theory, it proposes Training-Aware Target Coverage (TATC), a synthetic data selection method that determines where synthetic data are useful and how much to add. This addresses the increasingly common practice of scaling LLM training with synthetic data.

entry.title: TOAST: Stochastic Robot Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Keisuke Shirai, Tomohiro Motoda, Hanbit Oh, Ryoichi Nakajo, Roman Mykhailyshyn, Ryo Hanai, Shotaro Miwa, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: TOAST improves robot action tokenization for autoregressive vision-language-action models by exploiting the fact that multiple token sequences can decode to the same motion, replacing FAST's deterministic tokenization with stochastic tokenization. This improves policy learning efficiency from limited demonstrations beyond what FAST's token compression alone achieves.

entry.title: Two Clocks in Diffusion MLLMs: When Answers Stabilize Before Rationales Unfold

author.name: Keuntae Kim, Yong Suk Choi

entry.summary: This analysis of masked diffusion multimodal LLMs shows that answer candidates often stabilize long before their rationales are generated, with 89.4-98.1% of the rationale canvas unwritten at stabilization in some configurations. The authors distinguish retrospective stabilization from token commitment and show block length and EOS prompting dramatically change this behavior and accuracy on VQA benchmarks.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Distributionally Robust Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models under Subpopulation Shift

author.name: Seonghwi Kim, Sung Ho Jo, Minwoo Chae

entry.summary: DR-TFM adapts tabular foundation models like TabPFN-3 for subpopulation shift without group annotations by fine-tuning only a query-scaling network in the attention over context examples, using robust objectives with estimated groups. Adaptation touches just 0.016% of pretrained parameters. It improves worst-group performance on tabular benchmarks.

entry.title: Supervising Sound Localization by In-the-wild Egomotion

author.name: Anna Min, Ziyang Chen, Hang Zhao, Andrew Owens

entry.summary: The authors train a binaural sound localization model using camera egomotion as a free supervisory signal: sound directions must stay consistent with visual estimates of camera motion from multi-view geometry. They also contribute a real-world audio-visual dataset with egomotion and show the approach learns effectively without dense annotation.

entry.title: VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models

author.name: Gueter Josmy Faure, Hao Ping Wang, Min-Hung Chen, Winston H. Hsu

entry.summary: Presents VETO, a training-optional plug-in for VLMs that compresses video tokens along dual axes: intra-frame merging of semantically similar tokens via optimal-transport-inspired matching and inter-frame merging of temporally redundant frames, using hierarchical compression. It targets the quadratic cost of visual tokens in long-video inference.

entry.title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG

author.name: Maria Carmen Jica, Ali Satvaty, Suzan Verberne, Fatih Turkmen

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive, automatic black-box data extraction attack against image-returning multimodal RAG systems, where each query blends an attacker-held shadow image with the embedding walk to retrieve private visual artifacts. It exposes new privacy attack surfaces introduced by grounding MLLMs with external retrieval.

entry.title: From Knowledge Access to Source Learning: Developing Source-Specific Competence

author.name: Lucheng Fu, Kejing Xia, Yiyang Wang, Yiqiao Jin, Jinjin He, Xiyuan Yang, Haoxin Liu, Ye Yu, Haibo Jin, Yijia Xiao, Wenke Lee, B. Aditya Prakash, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces source learning, where LLM agents progressively build reusable source-specific competence over persistent authoritative sources rather than repeatedly treating access as one-off retrieval. A persistent source model captures how the source's knowledge is structured, interpreted, and applied across a sequence of knowledge-intensive tasks.

entry.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation

author.name: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Ying Shen, Kiet A. Nguyen, Adheesh Sunil Juvekar, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: SILSA represents 3D shapes using a fixed set of overlapping sliding-window slice latents along three canonical axes, each token summarizing a local depth window, enabling single-stage rectified-flow generation that preserves cross-sectional and topological continuity. This avoids the fragmentation and cost of voxel-token multi-stage pipelines, especially for thin or highly connected geometry.

entry.title: The Hidden Costs of 99% Accuracy: A Trustworthiness Audit of the Telco Customer Churn Benchmark

author.name: Soumyadeep Roy

entry.summary: A forensic audit of the widely used IBM Telco Customer Churn benchmark shows that pre-split SMOTE augmentation inflates churn-class F1 by over 13 percentage points across ten classifiers, driven by synthetic training points that are nearest-neighbor interpolations of test instances. The paper quantifies the leakage mechanism directly and exposes multiple trustworthiness failures invisible to accuracy-centric reporting. It is a cautionary case study in benchmark hygiene.

entry.title: Stable and Counterfactually Robust Physical World Models from Imposed Structure and Learned Physics

author.name: Yufeng Wang, Parivesh Priye, Lu Wei, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: The paper investigates how to build world models that simultaneously satisfy energy-consistent dissipation, correct responses to interventions on physical parameters, stability far beyond the training horizon (100x), and robustness to disturbances. It proposes imposing general dynamical structure while learning system-specific physics from trajectory data, answering how much physics must be hard-coded. This is directly relevant to trustworthy learned simulators and world models.

entry.title: Specificity-Aware Diffusion Steering via Variance-Reduced Sequential Monte Carlo

author.name: Luran Wang, Linrui Ma, Hannes St\"ark, Regina Barzilay

entry.summary: The paper formulates inference-time steering of pretrained diffusion models for specificity-aware generation, where samples must be repelled from a negative reference distribution without eroding the positive distribution where the two overlap. It derives an overlap-based target distribution with a likelihood-ratio interpretation and estimates it using variance-reduced sequential Monte Carlo. This enables constraint satisfaction at generation time without retraining.

entry.title: CommunityKV: Efficient Long-Context Decoding via Graph Partitioning

author.name: Joe McKenna, Anastasios Alexandridis, Nathan Susanj, Jing Liu

entry.summary: CommunityKV recasts training-free sparse attention as community detection on a token graph built from QK^T scores already computed during prefill, enabling retrieval of semantically coherent token groups during decoding. This avoids the coarse heuristics or costly clustering of prior training-free approaches.

entry.title: Attention Kernels for Learning Maps Between Heavy-Tailed Measures

author.name: Kailen Hargenrader, Edoardo Calvello, Bohan Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows softmax attention integrals diverge for probability measures with polynomial tails and proposes slower-growing attention kernels, validated on new operator-learning benchmarks. Softmax exhibits ensemble collapse on heavy-tailed tasks while slower-growing kernels avoid it, and symlog preprocessing helps only partially.

entry.title: WOMBAT: Whitebox Oracle for Molecular Benchmarking and Attribution Testing

author.name: Dominik Matuszek, Bartosz Zieli\'nski, Tomasz Danel, Dawid Rymarczyk

entry.summary: WOMBAT is a benchmark of 14 whitebox graph neural networks whose message-passing weights are manually set to detect specific SMARTS motifs, providing ground-truth attribution rules by construction. This enables rigorous evaluation of GNN explainers like GNNExplainer, PGExplainer, and Integrated Gradients on millions of PubChem molecules, distinguishing explainer failure from model shortcuts.

entry.title: Rate-Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial Linear CMDPs

author.name: Kihyun Yu, Honghao Wei, Dabeen Lee

entry.summary: The paper closes a regret gap for episodic adversarial linear constrained MDPs with unknown transitions and adversarially varying losses and constraints. A new primal-dual algorithm achieves O(sqrt(K)) regret and cumulative constraint violation, improving on the previous O(K^3/4) result and removing the need for Slater's condition, via careful handling of uniform concentration over value function classes.

entry.title: Kernelized Activation Steering

author.name: Laziz U. Abdullaev, Minh-Hieu Pham, Bach Do, Khoat Than, Tan M. Nguyen

entry.summary: KAS generalizes activation steering by lifting it into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, formulating steering as an optimization expressed purely through kernel evaluations. Unlike difference-in-means, which applies a single input-independent vector, KAS yields activation-dependent, locally adaptive steering that respects the local geometry of activation space. This provides a unifying, more expressive framework for training-free control of attributes like sentiment, style, and helpfulness.

entry.title: RelICL: Training-free Relational Learning with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Simon Forbat, Rainer Gemulla

entry.summary: RelICL extends training-free tabular foundation models to relational learning via deep feature synthesis while identifying and addressing two key problems: feature explosion as schema complexity grows, and interaction blindness in the synthesized features. The approach directly benefits from improvements to the underlying tabular foundation model without any training.

entry.title: A Safe Prototype Is Not a Safety Direction: Reference Dependence and Prompt Confounds in Response-Safety Embeddings

author.name: Sahil Kadadekar

entry.summary: This audit paper shows that scoring response safety by cosine similarity to the mean embedding of known-safe responses, as proposed in a recent sleeper-agent detector, is statistically unidentified and performs poorly in practice: ROC-AUC of 0.457-0.545 on human-labeled corpora versus 0.588-0.738 for an explicit safe-minus-unsafe reference direction. The analysis uses four frozen encoders and prompt-grouped splits to isolate reference dependence and prompt confounds.

entry.title: Learning to Predict Distributions over Weight Updates for Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Azal Ahmad Khan, Keshav Ramji, Tahira Naseem, Ali Anwar, Ram\'on Fernandez Astudillo

entry.summary: The paper studies query-conditioned hypernetworks that predict distributions over LoRA adapters for LLM test-time adaptation, using only the input query as the adaptation signal. It introduces a differentiable Monte Carlo loss and multiple distribution parametrizations, showing meaningful adaptation is possible from the query alone.

entry.title: BranchIP: Learning Adaptive Equivariant Computation for Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Laura Zichi, Gil Harari, Chuin Wei Tan, Marc L. Descoteaux, Albert Zhu, Menghang Wang, Yoel Zimmermann, H. T. Kung, Boris Kozinsky

entry.summary: BranchIP is a single-model framework for learned adaptive tensor-product computation in equivariant machine learning interatomic potentials, trained with a novel distillation loss. It accelerates MLIPs by up to 2.4x across model sizes on catalysis and solid electrolyte systems while maintaining accuracy.

entry.title: Cost-augmented Schr\"odinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control

author.name: Akshay Balsubramani

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that generalized Schrodinger bridges on graphs with state costs can be computed exactly by folding costs into the reference process as a Feynman-Kac tilt, eliminating the need to learn control rates. The solution alternates two sparse matrix-exponential endpoint rescalings with convergence guarantees and involves no time discretization or learning.

entry.title: When a Data Artifact Isn't a Shortcut: Causal Auditing of Synthetic RLVR Corpora

author.name: Esther Xin

entry.summary: This audit examines GooseReason-0.7M, an RLVR training corpus where correct answers are genuine human text and distractors are synthetic, asking whether models could learn provenance instead of correctness. Surface-statistic classifiers barely detect the asymmetry (AUROC 0.562), and manual inspection of per-domain results such as below-chance code distractors explains when artifacts do and do not constitute shortcuts.

entry.title: AnchorPrompt: Self-Distilled Soft Prompts for Robust Audio-Language Models

author.name: Pooneh Mousavi, Amir Ivry, Mirco Ravanelli, Cem Subakan

entry.summary: AnchorPrompt adapts frozen large audio-language models by learning a single block of soft prompt vectors inserted between audio and question embeddings, trained via self-distillation over diverse perturbations with clean-answer targets and refusal targets when evidence is insufficient. It is perturbation-agnostic at inference and mitigates hallucination. This offers a cheap robustness route for LALMs.

entry.title: A Survey on End-to-End Autonomous Driving Training from the Perspectives of Data, Strategy, and Platform

author.name: Chengkai Xu, Yiming Cui, Jiaqi Liu, Yicheng Guo, Cheng Qin, Geyuan Zhang, Xinwei Dong, Shiyu Fang, Peng Hang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of end-to-end autonomous driving training organized around a Data-Strategy-Platform taxonomy that treats data, learning strategy, and compute/infrastructure as an interdependent system. It maps the training ecosystem for models that directly map multimodal sensor inputs to driving actions.

entry.title: Smoother Flow Matching via Contrastive Trajectory Repulsion

author.name: Ziqi Jiang, Zhenqi He, Long Chen

entry.summary: The paper reframes trajectory crossing in flow matching as inducing large local Lipschitz constants in the target velocity field, which neural networks fit poorly due to spectral bias and which destabilizes training. It introduces a contrastive trajectory repulsion method that explicitly regulates intermediate trajectories to produce smoother flows.

entry.title: Learnt Attacks on Quantum Key Distribution under Channel Noise and Device Drift

author.name: Marcel Mordarski, Benjamin Gras, Abdelrahman Shehata, Daniel Budina, Roberto Bondesan

entry.summary: The authors model adaptive eavesdropping on quantum key distribution as a constrained MDP where an attacker selects circuits per round while channel noise follows an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift, with abort conditions as budgets. They bound the value of adaptation against the best fixed circuit and dynamic-programming upper bounds, learning attacks that exploit device drift between recalibrations. This quantifies a previously unmeasured security risk in deployed QKD.

entry.title: Bayesian Fine-tuning Yields Language Models that are as Bayesian as their Beliefs Allow

author.name: Polina Tsvilodub, Andreas Waldis, Linlu Qiu, Tal Linzen, Michael Franke

entry.summary: The authors formalize increasingly demanding criteria for when a language model counts as Bayesian, distinguishing whether an LM represents Bayesian beliefs, acts on them, and converts them to choices as Bayes' rule does. They show that SFT on a Bayesian model's outputs yields near-Bayesian behavior while tuning on true answers falls short, and dissect why the two tuning signals differ.

entry.title: Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs

author.name: Wanyang Hong, Zhaoning Zhang, Yi Chen, Libo Zhang, Baihui Liu, Linbo Qiao, Zhiliang Tian, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: The paper studies cumulative contextual decay in multi-turn conversations, identifying three failure modes: attention pollution, dilution, and drift. It proposes REA, a context-management framework that separates instructional memory (persistent global constraints in a dedicated prefix) from episodic memory, with heuristic retrieval choosing between raw text, compressed representations, or omission per turn. On Long-MT-Bench+ it improves judge scores over baselines.

entry.title: A Matryoshka Hierarchical RAG for Efficient Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Gianluca Bonifazi, Christopher Buratti, Michele Marchetti, Federica Parlapiano, Giulia Quaglieri, Davide Traini, Domenico Ursino, Luca Virgili

entry.summary: MatRAG combines retrieval-augmented generation with Matryoshka Representation Learning, organizing a document corpus into a DAG of clusters whose semantic hierarchy aligns with nested embeddings. This reduces both indexing costs (no KG or LLM summaries required) and query-time costs (no iterative LLM retrieval) while preserving multi-hop retrieval quality. A practical efficiency contribution for multi-hop QA.

entry.title: Q-SPT: Learnable Query-Based Compression for Low-Frame-Rate Speech Tokenization

author.name: Jeeyoung Yun, Seohwan Yun, Sungwoong Kim

entry.summary: Q-SPT is a dual-stream speech tokenizer with learnable query-based compressors specialized separately for semantic and acoustic representations, replacing rule-based average pooling or similarity-threshold merging for low-frame-rate tokenization. Lower frame rates reduce compute for speech language models while preserving linguistic and acoustic detail. Directly relevant to efficient speech LM tokenizers.

entry.title: DSSR-3D: Decoupled Reasoning for View-Dependent Referring in 3D Gaussians

author.name: Thanh-Khoi Nguyen, Thien-Phuc Tran, Minh-Triet Tran

entry.summary: DSSR-3D addresses a fundamental limitation in 3D Gaussian Splatting referring segmentation: language fields embed features in a view-invariant space and cannot resolve observer-centric relations like left of. The method decouples pose-invariant semantic localization from pose-conditioned spatial reasoning as an inference-time framework requiring no retraining. It matters for embodied agents and interactive 3D scene understanding.

entry.title: Just Align $\bm{x}$: Aligning Predictions, Not Representations

author.name: Yuyao Zhang, Yuwei Hu, Ziyang Mai, Yu-Wing Tai

entry.summary: JAx proposes aligning clean-image predictions across noise levels rather than intermediate representations for diffusion training, observing that feature alignment in JiT improves semantic access but reduces access to image variation needed for clean-image prediction. It couples noisier student observations with cleaner ones as auxiliary supervision. The paper articulates a useful alternative principle for auxiliary supervision in diffusion models.

entry.title: Joint Branch-Space Transform Coding for Diffusion Activation Quantization with Classifier-Free Guidance

author.name: Mingrun Jiang, Yuejia Liu, Zishan Shao, Ting Jiang, Qinsi Wang, Hancheng Ye, Yixiao Wang, Rui-Feng Wang, Kangning Cui, Yixuan Chen, Fan Yang, Xiang Cheng, Hai Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: The paper shows that matched classifier-free guidance (CFG) activations form a strongly correlated 2D source and proposes branch-space transform coding that rotates conditional and unconditional branches via an offline 2x2 orthogonal matrix before quantization. This exploits cross-activation structure that prior diffusion quantization methods left on the table.

entry.title: MVDG: Efficient Multi-view 3D Disambiguation on Unconstrained Real-World Images

author.name: Hanyuan Xiao, Gonglin Chen, Haolin Xiong, Wenbin Teng, Haiwei Chen, Yajie Zhao

entry.summary: MVDG addresses the doppelganger problem in large-scale 3D reconstruction by building a multi-view disambiguation framework on the VGGT 3D foundation model, jointly reasoning over arbitrary numbers of views in a single pass rather than O(n^2) pairwise classifiers. It notes that direct multi-view fine-tuning alone is insufficient and adds 3D-aware features.

entry.title: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent

author.name: Cheng Yang, Yifan Wu, Yutao Huang, Zhaohua Zhang, Beiduo Chen, Muxi Chen, Chenchen Zhao, Hexuan Deng, Haolin Yang, Geyuan Zhu, Sa Zhu, Jianhuan Zhuo, Qiuyong Xiao, Jianhao Ruan, Yiran Peng, Jiayi Zhang, Tian Ye, Xinlei Yu, Tianwen Jiang, Jihong Zhang, Yuyu Luo

entry.summary: AutoGUIWorld is a data-generation framework that synthesizes GUI agent interaction trajectories by combining the visual priors of image generators with a planner's task knowledge, avoiding the cost of deploying real software environments. This expands trajectory diversity for training GUI agents beyond the applications actually installed in a lab environment. The idea treats image generators as visual world models for interface dynamics.

entry.title: DiVid: Diagnosing Dimension-Specific Diversity Collapse in Video Generation Models

author.name: Huanran Hu, Zihui Ren, Dingyi Yang, Zhinan Song, Guozheng Wu, Tiezheng Ge, Qin Jin

entry.summary: DiVid is a diagnostic framework that decomposes video generation diversity into six interpretable dimensions: Semantic, Style, Subject, Scene, Motion, and Camera, measured with a reproducible CV pipeline. It analyzes diversity collapse alongside quality and prompt faithfulness across representative video generation models, revealing where global scalar metrics obscure failures.

entry.title: Anti-Persona: Disrupting Unauthorized Identity Binding and Recognition in Personalized Vision--Language Models

author.name: Abhishek Basu, Fahad Shamshad, Karthik Nandakumar

entry.summary: The paper identifies a privacy risk where adversaries bind a target identity from a few reference images into a personalized vision-language model and then detect that identity in new images via natural-language queries. Anti-Persona defends by aggregating shared features from reference images into an identity prototype and applying visually subtle perturbations that disrupt prototype alignment, preventing both binding and later recognition.

entry.title: Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation

author.name: Mohammed Irfan Kurpath, Jaseel Muhammad Kaithakkodan, Sahal Shaji Mullappilly, Ivan Laptev, Hisham Cholakkal

entry.summary: Omni-Embed-Mini is a 0.9B-parameter omni-modal embedder mapping text, speech, audio, images, video, and documents into one shared cosine space without updating any text-side parameters. Its key trick is dense cascaded captions whose frozen-backbone embeddings serve as teacher targets, so student and teacher share byte-identical geometry, trained via lightweight projectors and phased LoRA adapters.

entry.title: World Observer: Joint Actor-Observer Generation for Persistent World Modeling

author.name: Hyunwook Choi, Dahyun Chung, Hyunsung Kim, Siyoon Jin, Jinhyeok Choi, Junyoung Seo, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: World Observer decouples observing from acting in video world models by jointly generating an actor-centric view plus one or more panoramic observers watching selected world regions. Objects leaving the actor's view continue to evolve in observers, so their updated states are correctly reflected upon re-entry, enabling persistent world modeling.

entry.title: Retrospective Open-Vocabulary Memory for Long-Term Object Search

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Zhiwei Xue, Chen Jizhuo, Peng Shiqi, Harold Soh

entry.summary: This work formulates long-term object search as probabilistic inference from censored observations, where a detection or non-detection updates belief only in proportion to the robot's opportunity to observe a location. The proposed ECROM system estimates long-term prevalence of open-vocabulary concepts queried at test time and converts beliefs into an active-search prior. It also contributes a controlled benchmark in ten HM3D homes.

entry.title: Reactive Humanoid Multi-Contact Using Learned Stability Models

author.name: Stephen McCrory, Beomyeong Park, Nicholas Kitchel, Nehar Poddar, Robert Griffin

entry.summary: This work presents a planning and control approach for humanoids to reactively use hand contacts to stabilize themselves in low-stability scenarios where foot contacts alone would fall. A learned model of the center-of-pressure region during post-impact enables rapid scoring of candidate bracing contacts compared to optimization-based methods. Learned stability models replacing expensive online optimization is a practical contribution to humanoid balance control.

entry.title: ReCo: Response-Consistent Locomotion with Policy-Aware MPC for Legged Manipulation

author.name: Kuankuan Sima, Yichao Gao, Chenxi Gu, Kefan Zhao, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces ReCo, combining RL locomotion policies trained for consistent, repeatable command responses with an MPC layer that uses an identified closed-loop response model to coordinate base and arm for end-effector tracking during walking. The key insight is that MPC can only compensate for base motion it can predict, so the learned policy is shaped to be predictable. Targets continuous legged manipulation under varied gait phase, contact, and payload.

entry.title: The Geometry of Time: Horizon-Independent Feasibility and Repair for STL

author.name: Avinash Malik

entry.summary: Presents a geometric decision procedure for signal temporal logic control synthesis that evaluates physical feasibility independently of temporal horizon length, transforming temporal logic constraints into continuous backward reachable sets at time zero. Analytically inverts the Bhat-Bernstein settling-time integral to map temporal windows into spatial boundaries, avoiding exponential growth from horizon discretization and enabling continuous temporal repairs. Addresses a concrete scalability bottleneck in STL synthesis.

entry.title: Backdoor Purification for LoRA-Tuned LLMs via Null-Space Projection

author.name: Jianwei Li, Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: This work proposes purifying LoRA-tuned LLMs of backdoors without requiring trigger knowledge, clean reference data, or aggressive retraining, using null-space projection of suspect parameter updates. The goal is to sharply reduce attack success rates while preserving both base-model general capability and the fine-tuned task performance. It improves practical applicability of backdoor defenses in the prevalent PEFT setting.

entry.title: PG-SFT: Balancing Capability Acquisition and Retention in Offline Agent Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ronghua Li, Zi Liang, Zhishan Li, Shinan Liu

entry.summary: Studies capability regression during supervised fine-tuning on offline agent trajectories, showing standard SFT improves target benchmarks while degrading general reasoning, tool calling, and code generation, and that KL penalties or update-magnitude limits fail to prevent this. Proposes PG-SFT to better balance acquisition of new capabilities with retention of existing ones. Directly relevant to practical agent training pipelines.

entry.title: Q-Learning for Reachability in MEC-Free MDPs

author.name: Lu-Chin Chang, Suguman Bansal

entry.summary: This paper presents Quasar, the first model-free Q-learning algorithm with asymptotic convergence guarantees for reachability specifications on MDPs free of non-terminal maximal end components, a fragment to which every MDP reduces via the standard MEC quotient. Following classical temporal-difference updates, it converges to optimal policies without estimating transition probabilities, where prior guaranteed methods required model-based estimation. This strengthens the theoretical foundations of RL for reachability.

entry.title: Atoms to Processes: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Chemical Engineering

author.name: Michael Baldea, Linda J. Broadbelt, Marianthi G. Ierapetritou, Akhilesh Jain, Ankur Kumar, Thomas A. Kwan, F\`elix Llovell, Andrew J. Medford, Ilias Mitrai, Joel Paulson, Junyi Qiao, Matthew P. Rivera, Kirti C. Sahu, Lev Sarkisov, Zachary P. Smith, Calvin Tsay, Ching-Mei Wen, Victor M. Zavala, Huacheng Zhang, Dan Zhao

entry.summary: This is a multi-author perspective article surveying AI/ML developments across chemical engineering, from atomic-scale simulation and catalyst discovery through transport, thermodynamics, separations, process systems engineering, and industrial operations. It emphasizes integration of learning methods with first-principles models to address predictive accuracy, data scarcity, extrapolation, and interpretability. Written by leading figures in the field, it serves as a roadmap for AI-augmented chemical engineering.

entry.title: The Delegation Danger Band: Why Mid-Capability Sub-Agents Over-Trust Inherited Stale State

author.name: Jundong Hu, Shekar Ramachandran

entry.summary: Using a Qwen3 capability ladder (0.6B to 8B) on a controlled benchmark where every task is solvable from base evidence, this study measures how forked sub-agents handle inherited context, comparing reset, selective, and full inheritance policies. It finds mid-capability sub-agents show a danger band where they over-trust superseded conclusions inherited from the parent, degrading performance in identifiable ways.

entry.title: DuplexSpeechBench-Document Grounding: Benchmarking Document Grounding and Hallucinations in Voice Agents

author.name: Puneet Mathur, Nedim Lipka, Zeyu Jin, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Introduces DSB-DG, a benchmark of 1,636 adversarially verified QA pairs from 50 documents across five professional domains for evaluating whether voice agents faithfully ground responses in external documents. It targets three failure modes: context saturation, grounding decay across multi-turn dialogue, and proactive grounding with context re-injection.

entry.title: Scores That Hold, Benchmarks That Leak: Measuring Dataset Contamination in Public Brain-Tumor MRI Classification

author.name: Bhanu Prakash Vangala, Sowmya Guda, Latha Peddi, Navya Vangala

entry.summary: This audit examines dataset integrity in the heavily published task of brain-tumor MRI classification, where public benchmark accuracies routinely exceed 98%. The authors introduce a three-layer contamination framework covering duplicate, patient, and source-label leakage and audit the three most widely used corpora, including a chest-radiograph negative control and nine architectures. The work questions whether the reported state of the art in this literature is real.

entry.title: LabBook: Harnessing Experimental History for Efficient LLM-Driven Discovery

author.name: Bo Yuan, Wenqian Ye, Zelin Zhao, Lama Moukheiber, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LabBook, an agent-maintained memory for LLM-driven scientific and program discovery that both guides retrieval of relevant evidence from a complete experimental log and informs generation of new solutions. The single-agent harness combines memory with retrieved evidence at each iteration to jointly produce the next program and updated memory, separating full history retention from selective context use. This addresses the tradeoff between evolutionary harnesses that lose evidence and full-history approaches with bloated contexts.

entry.title: Personalized Image Generation with Reasoning and Reflection

author.name: Bo Ni, Ngoc N. Tran, Qinwen Ge, Franck Dernoncourt, Seunghyun Yoon, Samyadeep Basu, Sungchul Kim, Puneet Mathur, Nedim Lipka, Tong Yu, Yu Wang, Ryan A. Rossi, Tyler Derr

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first unified benchmark for personalized image generation from user histories, going beyond exemplar-conditioned synthesis to leverage reviews, posts, captions, and metadata accumulated over time. It defines two complementary tasks and a multi-axis evaluation protocol covering target fidelity, visual quality, user distinguishability, and semantic alignment. The industrial author list (including Adobe researchers) suggests practical grounding.

entry.title: FORALL-LEAN-AGENT for Auditable Reasoning in Formal Mathematics and Software Verification

author.name: Naing Oo Lwin

entry.summary: This framework addresses the gap between successful Lean compilation and actual proof of the intended statement by adding statement comparison, axiom audits, and independent proof checking to coding-agent workflows. It binds verification evidence and reviewer decisions to candidate artifacts for traceability, evaluated on VeriSoftBench, PutnamBench, and a software verification track.

entry.title: Structure-agnostic Causal Representation Learning

author.name: Arman Behnam, Binghui Wang

entry.summary: SaCRL jointly identifies the latent causal structure and learns invariant representations without requiring the causal graph to be specified a priori, using a soft optimization over candidate invariance constraints with HSIC-based violation metrics. The authors provide theoretical identifiability results showing the approach concentrates on achievable structures.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Reweighting for Robust Learning under Spurious Correlations and Label Noise

author.name: Sung Ho Jo, Seonghwi Kim, Wonsang Yun, Minwoo Chae

entry.summary: POTER is a reweighting framework using optimal transport geometry between training and reference distributions to make models robust to both subpopulation shift and label noise. It addresses the underexplored intersection where loss-based sample identification breaks down because mislabeled samples also incur large losses. Relevant to fairness and robustness in practical ML deployments.

entry.title: PROMO: Preference-conditioned Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Robots

author.name: Amr Mousa, Rifny Rachman, Neil Karavis, Michele Caprio, Richard Allmendinger

entry.summary: PROMO makes locomotion trade-offs (command tracking, stability, energy efficiency) an explicit runtime preference input to a single quadruped RL policy, separating operator intent from the fixed reward shaping needed for viable gaits. It compares favorably against fixed-objective controllers, multi-objective baselines, and independently trained specialist policies. Practical for real robot deployment where priorities vary at runtime.

entry.title: MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs

author.name: Xudong Wang, Hao Wu, Haozhe Hu, Peiran Yin, Xinghao Chen, Yunpu Ma, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: MWOP exploits the finding that redundancy in multimodal LLMs varies across modality-interaction paths within attention heads and across visual versus textual executions of FFN channels. It independently prunes V2V, T2V, and T2T attention paths and modality-specific FFN computations, enabling finer-grained compression than unified operation pruning.

entry.title: Removing spurious minima for planar features by skip connections

author.name: Jakob Paul Zimmermann, Moritz Grillo, Andrei Balakin, Georg Loho

entry.summary: Studies the Gaussian population loss of shallow bias-free ReLU networks in the teacher-student setting, proving that adding a learned linear skip connection removes all spurious local minima once the student is at least as wide as the teacher, for teachers with planar features and positive output weights. Without the skip, spurious minima can persist even for a three-hidden-unit teacher.

entry.title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yafei Zhang, Songshuo Lu, Sicong Liao, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: CARM addresses off-policy drift in LLM RL post-training by showing that standard length-normalized geometric-mean masking rules can conceal bidirectional policy drift because signed log-ratios cancel across positions. The proposed cancellation-aware mask handles this mismatch for more reliable sequence-level filtering.

entry.title: DuoMind: Enabling Distributed Multi-Robot Coordination with Semantic Communication

author.name: Hanchu Zhou, Dechen Gao, Hang Wang, Brendan Lynch, Boqi Zhao, Qiyao Ma, Raman Goyal, Junshan Zhang

entry.summary: DuoMind is a distributed hierarchical framework for multi-robot coordination in which each robot combines a VLA-based action model with a VLM-based orchestrator that reasons over task instructions, local observations, and inter-agent semantic messages. This extends recent single-robot VLM/VLA progress to long-horizon multi-robot coordination.

entry.title: Source Identification Is Not Fitness Testing: Measuring the Limits of Synthetic-Data Attribution

author.name: Joss Armstrong

entry.summary: The paper tests whether the provenance of synthetic training data can be recovered and whether provenance helps select better data for retraining, using financial-risk text. Attribution is nearly perfect on original passages but collapses after paraphrasing or style rewriting, and the authors compare source-based versus alternative selection strategies across generation-retraining rounds.

entry.title: Fixing a Model That Learned Worse Cancer Means Lower Risk: Monotonic Constraints in Bladder Cancer Recurrence Prediction

author.name: Saram Abbas, David Thomas, Naeem Soomro, Rishad Shafik, Rakesh Heer, Kabita Adhikari

entry.summary: In a UK multicentre bladder cancer study, an unconstrained XGBoost model learned that higher tumour stage predicted lower recurrence risk, an inversion invisible to standard discrimination, calibration, and SHAP checks. The authors developed a counterfactual direction test to detect such inversions and a monotonic-constraint framework to remove them without hurting performance, validated on 435 patients with protocol-mandated follow-up.

entry.title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations

author.name: Qiuliang Liu, Liming Wu, Qi Li, Zhonglong Peng, Chang Chen, Xiaolong Chen, Wenbing Huang, Shifeng Jin

entry.summary: EP-Flow formulates disordered crystal structure prediction via an Occupancy Distribution Matrix, a continuous site-by-species representation that unifies ordered crystals, solid solutions, vacancy disorder, and interstitial occupancy, requiring only chemical formula input rather than site-level disorder annotations. A flow-based generative model is trained with constraints coupling site-wise occupancy, mass conservation, and non-negativity. This addresses a major gap since many functional materials are intrinsically disordered.

entry.title: Beyond Demographic Balance: Multi-Metric and Intersectional Evaluation of Fairness in MIMIC-IV Mortality Prediction

author.name: Abdullah Al Noman, Fahmid Al Rifat, Tahrima Hashem, Syed Muhammad Ibne Zulfiker, Rishov Paul, Tanzima HAshem

entry.summary: This paper revisits fairness evaluation choices for ICU mortality prediction on MIMIC-IV, showing that conclusions depend heavily on which metrics are reported and at what demographic resolution performance is measured. It also introduces a lightweight representation-balancing strategy across ethnicity-gender-insurance intersections that operates without conditioning on outcomes, evaluated at marginal and three-way intersectional subgroup levels.

entry.title: Debias Anything: Fairness with Diversity without Supervision in Diffusion Models

author.name: Th\'eau d'Audiffret, Mariia Vladimirova, Jean-Yves Franceschi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a post-training debiasing method for diffusion models that jointly addresses fairness and diversity for arbitrary sensitive attributes, using an adapter connecting the frozen diffusion model to a pretrained vision-language embedding space. This avoids the applicability and diversity losses of classifier-guidance or text-conditioning approaches while requiring no supervision.

entry.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair

author.name: Areeb Ahmad, Pratinav Seth, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: The paper argues that apparent self-repair in language models after ablation has a single explanation: a pre-existing gain along a signed counterfactual-strength axis, with repair responses following an affine law. Conventional ablations are recast as uncalibrated points on this dose axis, reframing a debated interpretability phenomenon.

entry.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Cristian McGee, El Houcine Bergou, Aritra Dutta

entry.summary: This work proposes ZFO, a lightweight optimizer framework that decouples direction selection from step-size: a trusted first-order optimizer picks the direction, and zeroth-order evaluations along that one-dimensional subspace select a curvature-aware step size using two extra function evaluations. It targets the persistent problem of step-size selection instability in large-scale LLM fine-tuning.

entry.title: SyntheticHLS: Building Diverse Synthetic High-Level Synthesis Datasets using LLMs

author.name: Stefan Abi-Karam, Miaoyan Zhou, Callie Hao

entry.summary: SyntheticHLS is an LLM-based framework for generating large-scale, diverse synthetic datasets for high-level synthesis (HLS) in chip design, using an iterative refinement approach to ensure quality and diversity across code length, hierarchy, latency, and application domain. It addresses the scarcity of HLS training data as LLM adoption grows in semiconductor design.

entry.title: ScaffoldM3C: A Multimodal Sequential Monte Carlo Framework for Generative Stable Construction Planning

author.name: Gadiel Sznaier Camps, Chengyang He, Guillaume Sartoretti, Eduardo Montijano, Mac Schwager

entry.summary: ScaffoldM3C frames autonomous 3D structure construction as probabilistic next-block generation with multimodal conditioning (text, image, sketch) and explicit modeling of scaffolding for intermediate stability. It uses a sequential Monte Carlo framework to tame combinatorial action spaces and equifinal assembly sequences. The work improves on LLM fine-tuning approaches for construction that ignore stability and scaffolding.

entry.title: Nonparametric Distribution Matching for Self-Supervised Whole-Slide Image Condensation

author.name: Duong M. Nguyen, Trong Nghia Hoang, Hang Thi Nguyen, Thanh Trung Huynh, Phi Le Nguyen, Minh N. Do

entry.summary: The paper introduces NICER, which reformulates whole-slide image condensation as a distribution-matching problem under a fixed representational lens, replacing heuristic prototype learning with a tractable nonparametric prior with slide-adaptive capacity. Experiments span five histopathology datasets. This targets the gigabyte-scale computational burden of computational pathology.

entry.title: TRACE: Tackling Real-World Resource Assignment Problems via Agentic Heuristic Design

author.name: Jose A. Ayala-Romero, Andres Garcia-Saavedra, Xavier Costa-Perez

entry.summary: TRACE is an LLM-based automatic heuristic design framework for real-time resource assignment in computing infrastructure, extending AHD beyond fully-specified combinatorial problems and scalar fitness by letting agents actively probe unknown system behavior such as processor speeds and power consumption. It aims to produce auditable, human-readable rules deployable within tight latency budgets, bridging research schedulers and industrial practice.

entry.title: Measuring Human-Like Bias in LLMs? A Critique of Human-Derived Bias Constructs in LLM Evaluation

author.name: Antonela Tommasel, Markus Schedl

entry.summary: The paper critiques the growing practice of applying human-derived bias constructs, such as implicit bias, stereotype activation, and cognitive biases, to LLM evaluation, arguing there is an inferential gap between instruments built for human cognition and evaluations based on probabilities, completions, and rankings. It analyzes when such adaptations are and are not valid, offering guidance for bias evaluation methodology.

entry.title: Trajectory-Aware Clinical Risk Prediction via Severity-Grounded Knowledge Graphs and Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Kyunghoon Jeon, Youmin Ko, Woohwan Jung, Hyunjoon Kim

entry.summary: TRACER builds a medical knowledge graph enriched with disease severity information from literature, retrieves severity-weighted progression paths for a patient, and combines these with unstructured clinical notes via RAG for trajectory-aware risk prediction from EHRs. It targets well-known failures of existing methods around severity and progression. Clinically meaningful and methodologically thorough.

entry.title: HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Wenhan Yang, Anirudh Rao, Ashwin Chandra

entry.summary: HAWK improves speculative decoding for large vision-language models by using representation similarity to select informative target layers, injecting visual information directly into the drafter, and training with on-policy correction that models how target predictions shift after the drafter's own proposals. This addresses the poor speedups and off-trajectory disagreement that limit multimodal speculative decoding. It is relevant to efficient LVLM inference.

entry.title: Towards Subject Consistency over Dynamic Subject Sets in Video Generation

author.name: Tongcheng Zhang, Jun Zhu, Jianfei Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces DynSC-Eval, an evaluation framework that tracks subjects across their visible lifespans in generated videos and measures local continuity and global identity preservation with six object-level metrics, including explicit inconsistency detection. It reveals substantial subject-consistency failures in models generating 5s, 15s, and 60s videos.

entry.title: OneStreamer: Unifying Perception, Memory, and Proactive Response in Streaming Video Interaction

author.name: Xiangyu Zeng, Yuandong Yang, Zhiqiu Zhang, Yuhan Zhu, Xinhao Li, Qingyi Si, Dingyu Yao, Changlian Ma, Haoran Chen, Xinyu Chen, Yansong Shi, Junhao Zhou, Yifei Li, Jun Zhang, Chuanyu Qin, Chenxu Yang, Xinlei Yu, Kun Ouyang, Yuchen Shao, Qianshan Wei, Changhai Zhou, Jun Gao, Jiaqi Wang, Limin Wang

entry.summary: OneStreamer is a streaming video LLM that jointly learns query-independent evidence recording and task response through proactive hierarchical caption memory, producing time-grounded captions and event summaries. At inference, model-generated records complement a recent visual window, enabling reusable factual memory without compromising real-time perception or revisiting history.

entry.title: TRACE: Privacy-Preserving Next-Best-View Selection over Distributed 3D Gaussian-Splat Maps

author.name: Amirhossein Mollaei Khass, Athanasios Cosse, Qiyu Sun, Nader Motee

entry.summary: TRACE enables a team of robots to cooperatively perform next-best-view selection while each keeps its 3D Gaussian Splatting map private. The key insight is that expected information gain decomposes into transmittance and radiance sums over ray hits, allowing secure aggregation without sharing full maps. This applies privacy-preserving computation to a modern and popular scene representation in multi-robot exploration.

entry.title: Introducing Olmo-core 3: Open, scalable training infrastructure for large MoEs

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: AI2 announces Olmo-core 3, a fully open-source redesign of its training stack engineered to scale mixture-of-experts language models into the trillion-parameter range. The post is brief, but the release matters for democratizing frontier-scale, reproducible training infrastructure.

entry.title: Benchmarking Prompt Optimization of Large Language Models With Chess

author.name: Timoth\'ee Lesort, Alejandra L\'opez de Aberasturi G\'omez, Tristan Karch, Tom Veniat, Philippe Modard, Karl Tuyls, Ludovic Denoyer

entry.summary: The paper introduces a chess benchmark of 1,118 Lichess puzzles for studying automatic prompt optimization of frozen LLMs, designed to be cheap and deterministic to score, unsaturated, and renewable as models improve, addressing contamination and expensive-grading problems in APO research. Chess provides exact-match scoring with clear headroom for improvement.

entry.title: Pay for the Fault, Not the Flow: Label-Free In-Flow Multi-Agent Workflow Optimization

author.name: Xuehang Guo, Haoyu Wang, Shengyu Chen, Zach Chen, Wei Cheng, Qingyun Wang, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: Proposes InFlowOp, a method for optimizing multi-agent LLM workflows without reference answers or trained assessors, by pricing every construction decision within a single label-free execution pass, enabling fault localization and repair cheaply. Addresses the high cost of improving workflows where subtask success is unknown until runtime. Practical contribution to the growing multi-agent workflow literature.

entry.title: NextMe-800: Anticipating Personal Behavior from Months of Egocentric Video

author.name: Zhaoxu Meng, Yiming Sun, Mingyuan Gao, Jiachang Zhang, Zhuhan Dai, Yipeng Du, Zheng Lian, Jian-Qiao Zhu

entry.summary: NextMe-800 is an approximately 800-hour first-person dataset collected from one volunteer over 126 days with 1 Hz images, gaze, and audio, captioned at five hierarchical abstraction levels from atomic actions to major activities. The authors formulate personalized action anticipation from months of egocentric data, aiming to let people preview plausible behavior trajectories for better planning. This is a uniquely long-duration, densely annotated egocentric resource.

entry.title: FedLore: Communication and Memory Efficient Federated Learning via Shared Gradient Low-Rank Projection

author.name: Junkang Liu

entry.summary: FedLore addresses federated training of foundation models by sharing a low-rank gradient projection basis within each round and refreshing it across rounds, avoiding subspace fragmentation where independent client projections bias aggregated directions. The shared basis enables exact aggregation despite client-side low-rank compression, cutting communication and memory costs without the fixed-rank limits of LoRA adapters. The paper clearly diagnoses why prior gradient low-rank FL methods degrade under data heterogeneity.

entry.title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks

author.name: Hao Wang, Ting Huang

entry.summary: Mingbird is a local-first agent harness for Windows and Ollama designed so that small open-weight models (2-9B) can complete real tasks on ordinary laptops. The authors present evidence that many failures attributed to small models are actually caused by cloud-scale harness design, and introduce ten compensating mechanisms including a byte-level net-zero prefill budget and a finish gate that re-reads the task before accepting completion. This matters for democratizing capable local agents without frontier-model compute.

entry.title: Where's Waldo? Query-language Preference under Cross-lingual Knowledge Disparities

author.name: Dayeon Ki, Ruochen Zhang, Silviu Cucerzan, Ryen W. White, Ning Gao

entry.summary: Studies query-language preference in LLMs used for multilingual information seeking, focusing on cases where sources in different languages give incomplete or inconsistent accounts of the same fact. The Waldo benchmark characterizes how a model's source-language selection changes what information users receive, making the bias consequential rather than merely stylistic. It matters for fairness and reliability of LLMs as multilingual knowledge interfaces.

entry.title: Verbalized and Internal Probabilities Are Coupled in Large Language Models

author.name: Sinead Williamson, Jiaxuan Li, Nick Foti, Russ Webb, Masha Fedzechkina

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether LLMs' verbalized uncertainty statements are aligned with their internal sampling distributions, given that prior work suggests each tracks different aspects of training data. The authors find the two readouts are coupled, clarifying when verbalized confidence can serve as a proxy for model uncertainty or training-data frequencies. This advances understanding of calibrated self-reported confidence in language models.

entry.title: JoinGR: Learning to Traverse Join Graphs for Table Retrieval

author.name: Sandipan De, Abhijit Chakraborty, Sambaran Bandyopadhyay, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: JoinGR treats the database join graph as the retrieval space for Text-to-SQL, representing columns as nodes with typed intra-table and foreign-key edges and traversing from anchor tables with a query-conditioned scorer. This captures relevant tables not mentioned in the question but identifiable via join relationships, which dense retrievers miss. Directly relevant to practical text-to-SQL systems.

entry.title: Exact Distinguishability in Non-Markovian Decision Processes

author.name: Kabir Murjani, Nisarg Patel

entry.summary: The paper studies when offline data under a fixed behavior policy can distinguish two candidate Regular Decision Processes, proving that posterior odds between observationally equivalent candidates remain at prior odds regardless of sample size. Results are formally verified in Lean 4, and the authors characterize exactly when equivalence occurs.

entry.title: SoK: Decentralized Agent Economic Infrastructure

author.name: Rui Sun, Xihan Xiong, Qin Wang, Fei Gao, Zelin Li, Zehua Cheng, Jiahao Sun, Zhipeng Wang

entry.summary: A Systematization of Knowledge organizing security and economic requirements for decentralized agent economies into 17 property families across six lifecycle stages, examining 12 systems and standards plus mechanism families and classical baselines. It highlights that locally correct components (e.g., escrow releasing on approval) can compose into globally unsound workflows.

entry.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes

author.name: Sophia Sirko-Galouchenko, Monika Wysoczanska, Andrei Bursuc, Nicolas Thome, Spyros Gidaris

entry.summary: Where-OPD extends on-policy self-distillation to multimodal LLMs by giving a frozen teacher textual, spatially grounded guidance derived from synthetic scenes rather than human-annotated crops or external teachers. This broadens self-distillation gains beyond tasks that benefit from visual zooming while avoiding annotation and teacher-model costs.

entry.title: Fast Polynomial Transcendentals for LLMs

author.name: Robert Hu

entry.summary: The paper tests whether short polynomial FMA programs can replace special-function-unit operations in LLMs, evaluating BF16 polynomial approximations of sigmoid, tanh, and SiLU on NVIDIA GB200 across four integration tasks. Motivated by FlashAttention-4 exposing imbalanced pipeline scaling on Blackwell hardware. This is hardware-level kernel engineering with direct relevance to LLM inference and training throughput.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware RL-Controlled Adaptive 3D Mapping

author.name: Alpay Ozkan, Tunc Ozan Aydin, Marc Pollefeys, Jelena Trisovic, Daniel Barath

entry.summary: The authors propose an adaptive voxel-based 3D mapping framework that allocates resolution using semantic entropy (label uncertainty), geometric curvature, and texture richness, with reinforcement learning controlling refinement decisions. Unlike prior heuristic methods such as MAP-ADAPT, the approach generalizes to unseen objects and provides explicit memory-usage control. This targets efficiency in 3D reconstruction and robotics mapping.

entry.title: Redundancy Meets Synergy: Dependency-aware Expert Selection for MoE via Submodular Optimization

author.name: Zheng Lin, Shaoke Fang, Yuxin Zhang, Jinfeng Xu, Zihan Fang, Zhe Chen, Wei Ni, Jun Luo, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: DS-MoE frames compact expert selection for MoE models as difference-of-submodular optimization, capturing both redundancy and synergy between experts that Top-k heuristics ignore. Grounded in a second-order Taylor analysis of loss degradation, it selects expert subsets with awareness of gating-network dependencies.

entry.title: SkillSpec: Consensus-Gated Agent Skill Evolution via Representation Specialization

author.name: Huancheng Chen, Xiaodi Sun, Zhaoqiong Huang, Shenyang Huang Shreya Singhal, Jingwen Lu

entry.summary: SkillSpec addresses how LLM agents retain and improve reusable natural-language task skills without weight updates. It separates what knowledge to retain from how to organize it, validating textual skill updates through execution evidence before restructuring them, with consensus gating. This improves on monolithic-document skill representations optimized via aggregate validation scores.

entry.title: GLoC-EHR: Evidence-Cited Clinical Reasoning over Global Context and Local EHR Events

author.name: Chaiho Shin, Kwangsoo Kim

entry.summary: GLoC-EHR is a multimodal language model for answering clinical questions from structured EHR code sequences, combining a fixed-size global memory of the full trajectory with a local memory of selected events. It is trained to align memories with clinical text and to cite supporting evidence before answering, using rationale fine-tuning followed by group relative policy optimization. This targets the dual need for whole-trajectory context and event-level grounding in clinical AI.

entry.title: Prediction-powered Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Pascal Janetzky, Yuxin Wang, Michael Klar, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: PPNAS applies prediction-powered inference (PPI) to neural architecture search, fusing a small set of architectures with costly observed performance labels and a large set with cheap but noisy zero-cost proxies, exploiting the ordinal information in ZCPs to build additional supervision. This yields statistically grounded performance estimates for candidate architectures. It reframes a core NAS efficiency problem as a principled inference problem.

entry.title: Learning Commute-Time-Preserving World Models for Planning

author.name: Michael Hauri, Peter Buttaroni, Fabian A. Mikulasch, Friedemann Zenke

entry.summary: This work shows that latent representations whose distances mirror commute-times in the environment graph improve goal-directed planning in world models, and that common self-supervised objectives encouraging isotropy degrade the required geometry. The authors develop a scalable self-supervised approach that preserves commute-time structure without explicitly instantiating the graph Laplacian, enabling planning benefits in large continuous environments.

entry.title: Faynt: Scaling and Optimizing Policies for Competitive Melee

author.name: Ali Janati, Nikita Kuzmin, Rohit Swamy, Charles Niu

entry.summary: Faynt is a family of 10M and 75M parameter transformer policies for Super Smash Bros. Melee, controlling all 26 characters with one checkpoint; after RL, the 10M model wins 98.4% of same-character games against fourteen prior specialist releases and sweeps a zero-delay Slippi-AI model. The paper studies architecture, scaling, and hyperparameter transfer, while honestly flagging that opponents retain action delays that may confound comparisons.

entry.title: STEER: Reducing Inference Cost in Relational Foundation Models through Semantically Informed Sampling

author.name: Abdalla Mohamed, Ashraf Aboulnaga

entry.summary: STEER reduces inference cost for relational foundation models by using schema semantics to guide which linked rows are sampled into the inference context, rather than dropping rows indiscriminately. This preserves predictive quality while shrinking context size for zero-shot predictions on unseen databases.

entry.title: SupraTITO: Transferable Generative Molecular Dynamics for Supramolecular Systems

author.name: Weilong Chen, Nuno Costa, Julija Zavadlav

entry.summary: SupraTITO is a transferable generative molecular dynamics framework for supramolecular systems, demonstrated on peptide self-assembly, that learns implicit transfer operators conditioned on peptide sequence, topology, and periodic geometry. It aims to make computationally demanding assembly processes accessible by accelerating simulation beyond MD timescales.

entry.title: Optimal Stochastic Bilevel Optimization with First-Order Oracles

author.name: Linxuan Pan, Junchi Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MRT-FD, a single-loop first-order method for nonconvex-strongly-convex bilevel optimization that simultaneously tracks upper-level variables, lower-level solutions, and implicit-differentiation auxiliary responses, using order-p finite differences for second-derivative actions. It achieves O(epsilon^{-4-2/p}) stochastic gradient complexity with a matching lower bound, establishing optimality. Matching upper and lower bounds is a strong theoretical result.

entry.title: Towards Robust Numerical Claim Verification

author.name: Peter R{\o}ysland Aarnes, Vinay Setty

entry.summary: The paper shows numerical claim verification brittleness persists in frontier LLMs and demonstrates that adversarial fine-tuning on numerically perturbed examples mitigates it: small Qwen3 models (0.6B-8B) with parameter-efficient fine-tuning reach 98.7% accuracy on label-flipping perturbations, beating zero-shot GPT-5.4 Pro (74.0%) and Gemini 2.5 Flash (73.9%). Gains generalize to unseen perturbation types and transfer without target-domain data.

entry.title: Does AI-Generated Scientific Text Follow Human Argumentation Patterns? A CARS-Based Comparison of Research Article Introductions

author.name: Abdelrahman Sadallah, Narjes Sheikh Asadi, Lonneke van der Plas

entry.summary: The paper compares original research-article introductions from published linguistics papers with LLM-generated counterparts using Swales' CARS rhetorical model, going beyond surface lexical cues to argumentative structure. Human introductions show more flexibility in which rhetorical moves they use and in what order, while generated introductions are more uniform. This offers a robust signature of AI-generated scientific writing and informs the detection debate.

entry.title: DramaAgent: Agentic Storytelling Video Generation

author.name: Ting Huang, Biao Wu, Ronghao Chen, Zeyu Zhang, Tengfei Cheng, Qizhen Lan, Huacan Wang, Hao Tang

entry.summary: DramaAgent is a hierarchical, model-agnostic agentic framework for long-form text-to-video-and-audio generation that decomposes generation into story planning, persistent character conditioning, scene-wise synthesis, and reflection-guided repair, sitting above existing video backbones. It targets narrative drift, character inconsistency, and audio-visual mismatch. Timely given rapid growth in video generation models.

entry.title: Reachability Is Not Generalization: Understanding Verb--Noun Decomposition in Assembly Action Recognition

author.name: Changyi Li, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: This paper systematically analyzes verb-noun decomposition for compositional generalization in assembly action recognition across three datasets, showing it escapes the atomic classifier ceiling only partially and that reachability of unseen combinations does not imply actual generalization. The findings temper enthusiasm for a widely adopted technique. It contributes to a sharper theory of compositional shift in video action recognition.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Video Interaction Generation with Synthetic State Transitions

author.name: Jiho Jang, Jinyoung Kim, Nojun Kwak, Kyungjune Kim

entry.summary: This work creates scalable synthetic datasets of controllable physical interactions by using image editing models to generate explicit start and end state images as visual anchors, then proposing State-Guided Sampling to produce seamless interaction videos. It targets the weakness of video generative models in depicting plausible physical state transitions.

entry.title: VTR-Bench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Text Rendering in Video Generation

author.name: Yu Huang, Jungang Li, Zhiyuan Wang, Yonghua Hei, Song Dai, Jiayu Yang, Deyuan Liu, Xiang Zheng, Xiaoshuang Shi, Hao Cheng, Kaidi Xu

entry.summary: VTR-Bench is a systematic benchmark for evaluating visual text rendering in video generation models, an often-ignored dimension since videos can look cinematic yet render in-scene text incorrectly. It situates text within scene contexts to test whether models faithfully render textual content under varied conditions. Benchmarks of this kind shape evaluation practice for a fast-moving generation field.

entry.title: PhysDEM: Physics-Defined Energy-Matching Diffusion for Spatiotemporal Field Generation under Scarce Measurements

author.name: Zhenyu Liang, Yining Huang, Yubo Zhao, Jack C. P. Cheng

entry.summary: PhysDEM combines governing PDEs with sparse measurements to generate plausible spatiotemporal physical fields via a physics-defined diffusion framework. It constructs a Gibbs target with PDE residual energy, derives an exact conditional-mean identity reducing denoising to supervised learning of an energy-induced mean correction, and introduces a physics-displacement probability formulation.

entry.title: Continual Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models by Suppressing Cross-Edit Interference

author.name: Yongliang Wu, Haori Lu, Jinqi Luo, Wei Cao, Xingyu Zhu, Yaoyao Liu

entry.summary: CEASE is a training-free continual concept erasure method for text-to-image diffusion models that constrains a closed-form solver with two subspace constraints to remove new concepts over time without degrading prior erasures or unrelated generations. It addresses cross-edit interference where residual perturbations accumulate across sequential erasure requests.

entry.title: ColoACT: Multi-Cue Action Chunking for Smooth Autonomous Colon Navigation on a Self-Propelled Endoscopic Robot

author.name: Jian Hu, Shujing He, Leixin Chang, Zongze Li, Ding Huang, Chaoyang Shi, Chengzhi Hu

entry.summary: ColoACT is an autonomous colonoscopic navigation system combining multi-cue action chunking to handle deformable anatomy, weak-texture and specular visuals, and contact-rich interactions on a self-propelled endoscopic robot. It bridges the brittleness of geometry-driven pipelines and the temporal inconsistency of pure learning-based policies. Autonomous endoscopy could reduce operator burden and risks like loop formation and tissue trauma.

entry.title: BLT*: Informed Belief Localization Trees for Uncertainty-Aware Planning on Digital Twins

author.name: Elliot Preston-Krebs, Abhishek Goudar, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: Presents Informed BLT*, a sampling-based belief space planning algorithm adapting RRT* and Informed RRT* to belief space using the 2-Wasserstein metric over isotropic Gaussian beliefs. Enables efficient steering and rewiring without repeated observation propagation and reuses previously computed measurement information, scaling to large outdoor digital twins with point-cloud localization. Includes a framework for generating semantically labeled digital twins from real environments.

entry.title: What Should an Agent Remember? Disentangling Retention from Retrieval in Bounded-Memory Evaluation

author.name: Juli Huang

entry.summary: The paper builds a streaming-recall benchmark crossing retention and selection rules evaluated on 300 seeded episodes, showing that mixed comparisons confounding history access with selection inflate reported gains: a reported 68.7-point query-aware advantage decomposes into only 15.5 points from selection and 53.2 points from access. Under bounded retention, several selection rules reach the retention ceiling.

entry.title: RISED: RubrIcs for agentic multi-environment Selection and sElf-Distillation

author.name: Jingtan Wang, Sirajul Salekin, Young mok Jung, Javier Movellan, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low, Manjot Bilkhu

entry.summary: Introduces RISED, a training framework for generalist LLM agents that uses rubrics beyond scalar rewards to handle cross-environment relationships in rollout selection and to extract learning signal from all-success and all-failure rollout groups via self-distillation. It tackles known weaknesses of group-relative rewards in multi-environment RL. Useful for training agents that generalize across interactive environments.

entry.title: Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)

author.name: Aleksei Medvedev, Alejandro Ariza-Casabona, Steven Derby, Gonzalo Fiz Pontiveros, Xinyang Shao, Florian Spiess

entry.summary: This paper reframes Semantic ID construction for generative recommendation as a recursive clustering problem on a graph whose nodes carry semantic content and edges carry collaborative signal. The resulting framework, GrIS, treats SID assignment as hierarchical graph partitioning and subsumes prior approaches, recovering RQ-VAE and RQ-KMeans as the empty-graph special case. This unifying view naturally balances semantic and collaborative signals.

entry.title: External Observers May See More Clearly: Cross-Model Span-Level Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models via Hidden State Probing

author.name: Kingshuk Gupta, Davide Buscaldi

entry.summary: This paper introduces a hidden-state framework for fine-grained, span-level hallucination detection that inspects layer-wise activation patterns to identify the exact onset and continuation of hallucinated tokens, moving beyond token-wise binary classification. The cross-model aspect suggests probes transfer across models, which the title frames as external observers detecting hallucinations more clearly. This matters for targeted mitigation and for understanding the internal geometry of hallucination onset.

entry.title: Actions with Receipts: Jointly Binding Claims, Evidence, and Execution for Replayable Tool-Agent Auditing

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Yina Sa, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: Introduces a claim-anchored execution contract for tool-using agents that jointly binds each emitted claim to its exact source span, the ordered execution prefix that produced it, and the source version and access state at execution time. This closes the audit gap where valid citations and valid traces exist individually but are transplanted across claims, actions, or source versions.

entry.title: XOR-Trellis: Ultra-Low-Complexity Dequantization and Curvature-Aware Hadamard-Free LLM Quantization

author.name: Xiaofan Que, Nir Elkayam, Spandan Pyakurel, Shuokai Pan, Dibakar Gope

entry.summary: This paper addresses two practical barriers to trellis-coded quantization of LLM weights at ultra-low bit widths: dequantization throughput and accuracy without costly incoherence transformations. The authors propose a hardware-efficient state-to-value mapping for the trellis dequantizer and a curvature-aware Hadamard-free approach to maintain quantization accuracy. The result is practical extreme low-bit compression that avoids inference bottlenecks.

entry.title: Interpreting Reasoning of Large Language Models via Partial Information Decomposition

author.name: Barproda Halder, Qiuyi Zhang, Sanghamitra Dutta

entry.summary: The authors introduce SLIDER, an interpretability framework that uses Partial Information Decomposition to disentangle information about the final answer between consecutive reasoning steps into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. From this they derive the Step-wise Repetitive Reasoning Index, a theoretical measure of reasoning quality aimed at detecting lengthy, repetitive, or erroneous trajectories of large reasoning models. It connects information theory to reasoning-process evaluation.

entry.title: Exploring More, Reasoning Better: Stepwise Risk-Sensitive GRPO for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yue YU, Bowen Zuo, David Crandall, Yinglun Zhu, Dongruo Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes StepRS-GRPO, a reinforcement learning method for diffusion language models that varies the risk coefficient of the group-advantage transformation across denoising states, addressing the mismatch of reusing terminal feedback in RLVR as conditioning contexts change. For binary rewards the transformation reduces to a state-dependent rescaling of centered advantages, with calibration and ablations guiding schedule selection. It matters because diffusion LMs are an emerging architecture needing tailored RL methods.

entry.title: Generalist Representation, Specialist Detection: TS-Router for Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Xuming An, Meng Wang, Yue Pan, Wenjun He, Chenghao Liu, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: TS-Router uses pretrained time-series foundation model representations to route inputs among specialized anomaly detectors, estimating each detector's competence per input rather than applying a single universal scoring rule. This reframing targets the heterogeneity of temporal dynamics across datasets that limits generalization in anomaly detection.

entry.title: ReCast: Contract-Preserving Protection for Fixed-Interface Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Bingchen Pei, Lichong Chen, Bingxi Zhao, Ziang Wu, Sirui Wang, Min Zhang, Yanhao Chen, Qingxu Liu, Qiang Gao, Chang-Tien Lu, Bo Gao

entry.summary: ReCast is an agentic privacy framework that lets users leverage remote multimodal models on sensitive charts and speech without exposing private content: it rewrites entities/topics with a distilled 4B model and substitutes values via a locally invertible numerical map, then reconstructs the required media. It addresses the mismatch between privacy sanitization and fixed media input interfaces. Practical privacy-preserving inference contribution.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning to Accelerate Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient for Linear Programming

author.name: Jinhwan Sul, Alex Oshin, Evangelos A. Theodorou

entry.summary: GALPO uses reinforcement learning to jointly learn continuous algorithm parameters and discrete restart decisions for PDHG linear programming solvers, without differentiating through the solver, using a groupwise proximal policy optimization objective. The learned generalized accelerated update combines separate primal and dual extrapolation, history corrections, and restart anchoring.

entry.title: What Makes Something Hard(er)? Explaining Question Difficulty in Natural Language

author.name: Peng Cui, Qiaoyuan Zheng, Rudolf Debelak, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: Presents a data-driven method that generates and validates natural-language hypotheses explaining question difficulty, using Item Response Theory to estimate difficulty from a large pool of LLM responses and then prompting LLMs to explain contrasts between easy and hard items. This moves beyond scalar difficulty scores toward interpretable explanations.

entry.title: iADD: Improving Alignment and Diversity in Diffusion Policy Optimization

author.name: Ashok Prasad Neupane, Saugat Adhikari, Pramish Paudel, Ajad Chhatkuli, Danda Pani Paudel
