entry.summary: Analyzes reward-based post-training of diffusion models (DDPO-style), mathematically showing that only-latter-timestep updates can harm diversity contrary to prior claims, and proposes an incremental Feynman-Kac training method achieving better alignment-diversity trade-offs. Grounded in theoretical analysis of the reverse diffusion process.

entry.title: Task-Adaptive Grounded 3D-Programmers Using 2D VLMs

author.name: Arman Raayatsanati, Sombit Dey, Anna-Maria Halacheva, Jan-Nico Zaech, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: The paper enables 2D vision-language models to operate reliably in 3D by introducing Canonical Coordinate Framing and Task-Adaptive Feedback, which anchor inputs and outputs to a shared Euclidean coordinate system and add iterative grounding feedback. This avoids expensive 3D-native training while solving axis ambiguity and scale inconsistency.

entry.title: Constant-Memory Recall: Learned Associations in a Fixed Matrix State

author.name: Samuel Larson

entry.summary: The paper shows that a small DeltaNet variant with fixed token-specific key biases can store and recall 32 key-value pairings per sequence within only 32 KiB of fixed recurrent matrix state, achieving 99.95% accuracy, with recall robust to long filler contexts. Ablations (zeroing the first memory block) probe where associations live, and parameter-matched Transformer baselines are compared. This bears on the memory-capacity limits of fixed-size recurrent states versus Transformers.

entry.title: MoRA: MoE Pruning via Router Bias Learning and Expert Approximation

author.name: Yushuai Sun, Zikun Zhou, Lin Gao, Jun Yu, Wenjie Pei

entry.summary: MoRA is a structured pruning framework for Mixture-of-Experts models that learns router biases and approximates removed experts to preserve performance while reducing memory footprint from the full expert pool. It addresses shortcomings of prior ranking-criteria and subset-search methods, including ignored routing-behavior redundancy among retained experts. This supports practical deployment of large sparse MoE models on constrained hardware.

entry.title: Denoising Surface: Modeling and Predicting Inference Cost for Diffusion LLM Serving

author.name: Haoyu Zheng, Fangcheng Fu, Binhang Yuan, Yongqiang Zhang, Liang Deng, Hao Wang, Yuanyuan Zhu, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: The paper observes that diffusion LLM inference has a two-dimensional execution structure over output blocks and within-block denoising steps that standard cost proxies (output length, step count) collapse away. It builds a cost model for per-request inference cost to support scheduling and resource allocation in real dLLM serving systems.

entry.title: Localizing Transfer Between Memorization Tasks

author.name: Yimiao Yu, Florentin Guth

entry.summary: Studying transfer between memorization tasks of random input-output mappings, the authors find surprising patterns: equivalent transfer where each pre-training epoch saves about one fine-tuning epoch, and non-equivalent transfer where mismatched pre-training can beat direct training. Ablations localize transfer into a trivial magnitude-driven last-layer effect and a non-trivial representational component.

entry.title: Supervise What Decides Success: Criterion-Aligned Auxiliary Losses for Latent World-Model Planning

author.name: Takumi Hara, Kanata Suzuki

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in latent world models for robot planning: success is judged by physical quantities like end-effector position, but these are encoded in latent states with errors exceeding the success tolerance, so candidate scoring cannot separate success from failure. The authors add an auxiliary loss that regresses success-criterion quantities from encoder and predictor outputs, aligning latent distances with the actual success criterion. Across four latent world models examined, this improves planning reliability.

entry.title: Reusing Past Samples in Proximal Policy Optimization: When and How Does It Help?

author.name: Alessandro Montenegro, Riccardo Venturelli, Marco Mussi, Matteo Papini, Alberto Maria Metelli

entry.summary: This paper provides a systematic study of hybrid sample-reuse strategies that augment PPO with off-policy data, asking when and how reuse helps. Given PPO's status as the de facto on-policy standard and the known instabilities of full off-policy methods, a rigorous characterization of reuse trade-offs fills an important gap.

entry.title: SkillEvoLean: Mutation-enhanced skill evolution for Lean provers

author.name: Kuo Zhou, ZiXion Yang, Lu Zhang

entry.summary: SkillEvoLean applies mutation-enhanced skill evolution to LLM-based Lean theorem provers, enabling skill library improvement even when all sampled trajectories fail by leveraging the verifier's reliable execution feedback. Unlike prior skill evolution methods focused on natural-language reasoning and root instruction files, it also evolves reference knowledge such as mathematical concepts and proving techniques.

entry.title: FastCI: Efficient GPU-Intensive CI for LLM Training Frameworks

author.name: Tianshuo Qiao, Naiqian Zheng, Xiaopeng Liu, Shuguang Wang, Diandian Gu, Xuanzhe Liu, Xin Jin

entry.summary: FastCI accelerates continuous integration for LLM training frameworks by using runtime evidence to select affected tests, pruning tests that execute changed code in equivalent contexts, and prioritizing high-risk tests. It targets the GPU-cost bottleneck that CI has become for fast-evolving training stacks.

entry.title: When Do Intrinsic Rewards Lead to Exploration?

author.name: Scott W. Viteri (Stanford University), Laura Gomezjurado Gonzalez (Stanford University), Clark Barrett (Stanford University)

entry.summary: This paper proposes a formal counterfactual-information criterion for exploration and constructs a single simple environment in which count-based, prediction-error, empowerment, and information-gain intrinsic rewards all have Pareto-suboptimal maximizing policies. The authors explain these failures and establish conditions under which intrinsic objectives do induce informative exploration.

entry.title: Q-MINO: A Minimal-Norm Method for Quantization-Aware Training

author.name: Don Li

entry.summary: Q-MINO replaces the Straight-Through Estimator heuristic in quantization-aware training with a temporal bundle method combining gradient consensus, state-drift regularization, and an alignment constraint, solved via warm-started Frank-Wolfe, to produce stabilized minimum-norm update directions. It targets noisy updates and parameter oscillations in ultra-low-bit regimes, backed by stochastic Lyapunov analysis. This matters for deploying models at extreme quantization levels.

entry.title: PI-AMFM: Permutation-Invariant Learning for Variable-Cardinality AM-FM Mode Decomposition in Biomedical Signal Analysis

author.name: Youngsun Kong, Ki H. Chon

entry.summary: PI-AMFM is a permutation-invariant neural framework for amplitude- and frequency-modulated mode decomposition of biomedical signals that handles a variable number of components without predefined cardinality. It combines a multiscale temporal encoder, a Mamba backbone, and presence estimation with Hungarian-matching-based training.

entry.title: Continual Learning for 6-DoF Grasp Synthesis via Experience and Demonstrations

author.name: Giulio Schiavi, Andrei Cramariuc, Michael Pantic, Roland Siegwart

entry.summary: The paper presents a continual-learning framework for single-view 6-DoF grasp synthesis in cluttered scenes that adapts at deployment via memory in a learned embedding space, updating grasp scores from outcomes and transferring optional user demonstrations to new scenes. It avoids finetuning large parametric models and is validated in simulation and extensive real-world experiments.

entry.title: Beyond Decodability: Do Acoustic Factors Drive Predictions in Speech-Based Alzheimer's Assessment?

author.name: Serli Kopar, Alkis Koudounas, Roshan P. Rane, Sam Gijsen, Paula A. Perez-Toro, Kerstin Ritter

entry.summary: Using controlled noise and reverberation interventions on ADReSSo speech and three SSL backbones, the authors combine layer-wise decoding, input and representation-space interventions, and geometric alignment to distinguish whether acoustic factors are merely decodable from SSL representations or causally alter Alzheimer's predictions. They find acoustic interventions do shift predictions, raising robustness concerns for speech-based clinical assessment. This is an important caution for deploying such diagnostic tools.

entry.title: AI Emulation of Stochastic Sudden Stratospheric Warming with Interpretable Latent Structure

author.name: C. Daniel Boscu, Daniel Hernandez, Fabio Alvarez Ventura, Justin Finkel, Ashesh Chattopadhyay, Pedram Hassanzadeh, Dorian S. Abbot

entry.summary: The authors build a probabilistic deep learning emulator, a ResNet-inspired conditional variational autoencoder, for the stochastic Holton-Mass model of stratospheric variability, which exhibits rare sudden stratospheric warming regime transitions. They analyze the learned latent space and show it develops interpretable structure corresponding to the strong and weak polar vortex regimes, addressing class imbalance for rare events.

entry.title: ARCCS: An Automated Regulatory Compliance Checking System

author.name: Giorgos Filandrianos, Jos\'e Menezes, Chrysoula Zerva, Alessandro Gianola

entry.summary: ARCCS is an end-to-end, regulation-agnostic, agentic system for automated regulatory compliance checking that decomposes raw regulatory text into atomic, traceable requirements and evaluates target documents against them with retrieved evidence, confidence scores, and interpretable justifications. The design decouples compliance assessment from fixed templates or predefined rules, enabling operation across regulations of varying structure.

entry.title: How Robust Are Neural Audio Codecs for African Speech? A Multi-Task Benchmark and the Limits of Perceptual Quality

author.name: Chibuzor Okocha, Christan Earl Grant

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates seven open-source neural audio codecs on three African speech datasets, reporting signal-level quality metrics alongside downstream ASR and speaker verification. Key findings include that only certain reference-based metrics track downstream validity, and perceptual quality does not guarantee task robustness. Important for equitable speech technology evaluation.

entry.title: PhysVista: Benchmarking Physical Intelligence in VLMs via a Perception-Reasoning-Assessment Loop

author.name: Xinge Peng, Yiting Lu, Tianwu Zhi, Wen Wen, Jianzhao Liu, Xin Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: PhysVista is a benchmark evaluating physical intelligence in VLMs through a closed cognitive loop of perception, reasoning, and physical judgment, aimed at diagnosing whether VLMs can assess the physical authenticity of generative model outputs. It addresses fragmented evaluation in existing benchmarks. The benchmark is timely as generative video and image models proliferate.

entry.title: Align Then Reason: A Multimodal Lip-Sync Judge for Dubbing

author.name: Rui Liu, Bhavin Jawade, Haoqi Li, Shivam Mehta, Karan Saxena, Yinghong Lan, Cameron R. Wolfe

entry.summary: The authors present Align Then Reason (ATR), a multilingual lip-sync judge for dubbing quality control that works with only silent video and candidate text. It first establishes monotonic alignment between frame-level lip representations and phonetic units, then reasons over that alignment, addressing temporal insensitivity of existing visual speech recognizers.

entry.title: OptimusMesh: Compact Autoregressive Mesh Generation from Point Clouds via Sparse Latent Pivots

author.name: Mazhar Iqbal, Naoya Chiba, Xuanmeng Sha, Tomohiro Mashita, Yuki Uranishi

entry.summary: OptimusMesh generates compact triangle meshes directly from point clouds using sparse latent pivot conditioning, compressing 2,048 oriented points into only 16 latent pivots. This avoids the dense or over-smoothed outputs and costly post-processing of implicit-representation-plus-extraction pipelines.

entry.title: A Compact Explicit 4D Representation for Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Di Yang, Zhihao Li, Yanhai Xiong, Yufei Wang

entry.summary: Sparc4D is a feed-forward autoencoder that compresses a monocular video with known cameras into a sparse 4D scene state, sharing static features across a clip and using temporally anchored slots for dynamic content. A sparse decoder outputs 2D Gaussian surfels while stored source pixels preserve fine texture via reprojection. It achieves a very compact representation, averaging under 1M 32-bit-equivalent values for a 32-frame clip.

entry.title: Rethinking Memorization Mitigation in Diffusion Models: Reinforcing Text Conditioning

author.name: Hyungjun Joo, Sehwan Kim, Hyeonggeun Han, Sangwoo Hong, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: This training-free method mitigates memorization in text-to-image diffusion models by redistributing cross-attention with Gaussian smoothing and reinforcing content-token contributions while attenuating padding tokens, without extra denoiser evaluations. It shows stronger content conditioning can improve prompt alignment at comparable training-image similarity, with a local analysis explaining when reinforcement preserves shared value information.

entry.title: From Pixels to Policy: A Multi-Agent System for Intervention and Geo-Spatial Decision Support

author.name: Hosam Elgendy, Utkarsh Mall

entry.summary: VIDA-Geo moves geospatial vision from monitoring to intervention: given aerial or street-view imagery, it discovers changes that improve target urban indicators. It couples a black-box indicator model with a generative editing model as an implicit digital twin, orchestrated as a multi-agent system for testing intervention hypotheses and decision support.

entry.title: Latent-Foresight: End-to-End Learning Predictable Representations for Latent World Models

author.name: Efstathios Karypidis, Spyros Gidaris, Nikos Komodakis

entry.summary: Latent-Foresight jointly learns representation and temporal prediction for latent world models operating on Vision Foundation Model features, replacing two-stage pipelines with fixed dimensionality reduction or independently trained autoencoders. By end-to-end shaping the latent space to be predictable, it supports diverse future scene understanding tasks.

entry.title: From Reasoning Failures to Composable Video Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Pengzhan Sun, Junbin Xiao, Ramanathan Rajaraman, Shiu-hong Kao, Angela Yao

entry.summary: This work disentangles the capabilities underlying spatial reasoning benchmarks for vision-language models by comparing predicted and ground-truth spatial context, identifying four recurring error sources such as inaccurate perception and reference-frame errors. Guided by this diagnosis, it introduces CROSS, a training-free library of typed geometric operators that composes to improve video spatial reasoning.

entry.title: UniTrackPLA: Unified Panorama-Language-Action Model for Instruction-Guided Navigation and Dynamic Person Tracking

author.name: Pengfei Qi, Haoran Lin, Sizhuang Chen, Kai Luo, Sirui Zhang, Xinqi Liu, Fei Cheng, Wenrui Chen, Liming Yin, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: UniTrackPLA is a unified panorama-language-action model that handles both instruction-guided navigation and dynamic person tracking, addressing the typical reliance on forward-facing observations and separate task policies. Its Panoramic-Aware Encoding preserves temporal and azimuthal structure of perspective views projected from panoramas, allowing perspective-pretrained visual encoders to process omnidirectional input. A shared vision-language backbone enables unified closed-loop control.

entry.title: EIDA: Execution-Interface Dynamics Adaptation for Real-to-Sim-to-Real Robot Navigation

author.name: Yiwei Qian, Shanze Wang, Qingyuan Hu, Xinming Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: EIDA adapts sim-to-real transfer for navigation by fitting execution-interface dynamics — how velocity commands actually produce motion and feedback on the target platform — from execution data, without reconstructing actuator models. Separate models update simulator geometry and predict velocity feedback observed by the policy, deployed within a lightweight GPU-parallel simulator. Fitted models reduced position and yaw prediction errors on Jackal and Go2 validation sets.

entry.title: TouchTherm: Building Multimodal Digital Twins of Objects for Tactile and Thermal Rendering

author.name: Yitao Zhang (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China), Hong Ying (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China), Haoran Guo (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China), Xiaoying Zhou (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China), Guanyu Chen (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China), Chenxi Xiao (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China)

entry.summary: Presents TouchTherm, a framework for constructing simulation-ready visuo-tactile-thermal object assets from real-world objects, combining structured-light scanning with photometric-stereo normal maps for visual and tactile reconstruction and capturing transient temperature dynamics. Extends object digital twins beyond geometry and appearance to microscale surface structure and thermal interaction cues. Useful for robotic simulation, haptics, and VR.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Refinement and Execution for Learned Driving Planners

author.name: Huaijin Hu, Shanting Wang, Zhongyu Mo, Andreas A. Malikopoulos

entry.summary: Introduces CLRE, a hierarchical receding-horizon framework that refines learned driving planners' outputs in closed loop without retraining or adding learned models. An upper layer solves finite-horizon optimal control trading route progress against interaction with predicted agents, solved from multiple initializations to generate candidates, addressing closed-loop failures like stalling, conflicts, and abrupt braking that open-loop training misses. Relevant to autonomous driving deployment.

entry.title: Gradient-Aligned Pair Selection for Personalized Preference Optimization

author.name: Ruoming Jin, Xinyu Li, Hao Zhou, Jianfeng Zhu, Ruixin Guo, Feodor Dragan, Lei Xu, Haixun Wang, Yang Zhou

entry.summary: The paper formalizes personalized preference learning as a geometry-aligned optimization problem by analyzing first-order interactions between gradients of expected user utility and DPO update directions, showing heuristic likelihood-based pair selection decouples optimization from user utility. It derives gradient-aligned criteria for selecting preference pairs in personalized DPO.

entry.title: ContractRL: Shielded Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Auditable Tool-Call Repair

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Yina Sa, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: ContractRL models verifier-guided JSON tool-call repair as a bounded decision process where the policy observes typed verifier feedback, immutable repair history, and remaining budget, with contract-derived action masks filtering prohibited RFC-6902 operations before a deterministic validator performs transitions. It specifies a contract-constrained group-relative objective covering patch, retry, and abstention decisions to keep repair auditable and minimize the action surface.

entry.title: Before Agents Decide: Epistemic Action in LLM-Based Systems

author.name: Yizhi Liu, Balaji Padmanabhan, Siva Viswanathan

entry.summary: This paper imports the cognitive science concept of epistemic actions — actions taken to improve the evidence base before a decision — into LLM agent design. It argues agent frameworks focus on task completion while neglecting whether evidence is sufficient, present, or in usable form for the next choice. The framing suggests a new design axis for agentic systems.

entry.title: Calibration-risk routing for controlled world-model adaptation

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Liang Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces the Model-Corrected World Model (MC-WM) for model-based RL under simulator-to-target shift, splitting limited target data into fit/selection/calibration partitions and routing to the model family with lower standardized calibration risk. A learned confidence signal weights one-step imagined policy updates without altering physical rewards. Evaluated broadly across 540 run cells in MuJoCo shift settings.

entry.title: CortexBridge: Cortical Alignment of EEG Montages for Foundation Models

author.name: Jiazhen Hong, Xiaotian Zhou, Zihao Ding, Kailong Wang, Yu Wu

entry.summary: Proposes CortexBridge, a lightweight adapter combining EEG features with electrode and atlas coordinates to map arbitrary electrode montages into a shared cortical latent space, enabling frozen EEG foundation models to transfer across layouts. Evaluated on three foundation models across five MOABB BCI datasets, improving 13 of 15 evaluations with up to 13.02% gain on SSVEP classification. Practical fix for a real bottleneck in EEG foundation model deployment.

entry.title: Contrastive Attention Mitigates Spectral Bias in Spiking Transformers

author.name: Xiaoli Liu, Malu Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: The paper shows via multiscale spectral analysis that both spiking neurons and spiking self-attention act as low-pass filters, dissipating high-frequency components and explaining the performance gap versus ANNs. It proposes Spiking Contrastive Attention, inspired by edge detection and differential sensing, to counteract this spectral bias.

entry.title: SpikeMoE: Brain-Inspired Competitive Routing for Flexible Spiking Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Xiaoli Liu, Yujie Liang, Jialin Li, Malu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces SpikeMoE, a framework combining spiking neural networks with mixture-of-experts architectures via a spike-based k-WTA router inspired by competition-inhibition dynamics in the hippocampal CA1 region. The router uses lateral inhibition and refractory periods to select Top-K experts based on discrete spike counts. This bridges biologically plausible event-driven computation with conditional model-scale computation, a novel architectural direction.

entry.title: Continuous Process-Level Evaluation for Evolving Enterprise AI Agent Skills

author.name: Ngoc Phuoc An Vo, Aarya Doshi, Vadim Sheinin

entry.summary: This paper proposes a continuous evaluation framework combining outcome-level and process-level checks to detect behavioral drift in enterprise AI agent skills as tool APIs, models, and specifications evolve. It evaluates tool selection, arguments, execution order, and database integrity using programmatic checks plus a narrowly scoped LLM judge across 240 trials. The work is important because final-output evaluation alone misses process failures in production agent systems.

entry.title: HydroJEV: A one-second, training-free screen for cyber-attack and fault attribution in water distribution networks

author.name: Tianwei Mu, Shengyan Jiang, Mingzhe Yuan, Qing Luo, Min Xiao, Wenhong Wang, Jun Li, Manhong Huang

entry.summary: HydroJEV applies Jev, a training-free judgment model returning class probabilities in about one second, as the first tier of triage for SCADA alarms in water distribution networks, distinguishing cyberattack, physical fault, normal transient, and sensor fault. On a four-class benchmark on the C-Town network, it was compared under sealed pre-registered rounds against rule trees, a supervised classifier, and seven cloud LLMs with only label-free prior correction. This offers critical infrastructure operators a fast, label-free alternative to supervised classifiers requiring rare labelled incidents.

entry.title: STATERA: Hidden Mass Estimation via Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Kinematics using Frozen Temporal Tubelets

author.name: Animesh Varma

entry.summary: STATERA adapts a frozen pretrained video backbone (V-JEPA) with a lightweight temporal tubelet mixer to localize the center of mass of opaque, asymmetric rigid bodies from short monocular videos, where appearance and point tracking are unreliable. The authors also release a HiddenMass Benchmark with 50K MuJoCo trajectories and a physically calibrated 63-sequence real-world test set, showing substantial error reduction over DINOv2-based baselines.

entry.title: Certainty Is Not Just Correctness: Rethinking Token-Level Certainty in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yunfan Zhou, Ye Zhu, Zhihai Wang, Jianguo Yao, Haibing Guan, Xijun Li

entry.summary: A controlled empirical study dissecting what token-level certainty scores in LLMs actually predict, separating two targets: identifying questions a model answers correctly versus distinguishing correct from incorrect responses to the same question. Findings show certainty is better at the former and varies in ways that current certainty-based training and inference methods do not fully exploit.

entry.title: Tokenized Key-Gated Adapter Routing: A Secure Access Control Mechanism Against Private Data Leakage in LLMs

author.name: Mohamed Shaaban, Mohamed Elmahallawy

entry.summary: Proposes Locket, a framework embedding fine-grained, policy-driven access control into LLM generation by training lightweight LoRA adapters, each encoding a distinct access policy such as full reveal, partial PII redaction, or conditional reveal. Keyed entry tokens route requests to the appropriate adapter, addressing the utility-privacy tradeoff in privacy-critical deployments.

entry.title: Deny Without Disabling: Authorization-Paired Evaluation and Control for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yunbei Zhang, Saiyue Lyu, Janet Wang, Yingqiang Ge, Jiang Guo, Jihun Hamm, Chandan K Reddy

entry.summary: Introduces authorization-paired evaluation, which jointly requires blocking prohibited uses and completing authorized uses in multi-agent systems where individually admissible contributions can jointly enable prohibited actions. The FlowReview framework connects object resolution, permission ranking, and deterministic enforcement, reducing denied-commit rates from 86.0% to zero without losing authorized completions in controlled experiments.

entry.title: T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bo-Wen Zhang, Junwei He, Maoqi Liu, Feiran Li, Song-Lin Lv, Wentao Ma, Rongyi Lin, Shuhan Zhong, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: Proposes T2SPO, which converts successful multi-step agent trajectories into step-level supervision by deriving remaining-distance targets from past interactions and training a model to estimate progress. This addresses the sparse-reward problem in agentic RL, where outcome-only rewards give little guidance on which intermediate decisions advance the task.

entry.title: The Life Cycle of a Massive Activation: Stochastic Birth, Weight-Decay-Driven Growth, and Competitive Consolidation

author.name: S. Aaron McClendon, Jorge Gallego-Feliciano, Antonios Saravanos

entry.summary: This work traces the full life cycle of massive activations in transformers, the large-magnitude residual-stream coordinates associated with attention sinks, through training-trajectory analysis and controlled interventions. The authors find that sink-carrying channels vary across seeds but stabilize early, that surrounding channels erode over training concentrating the sink onto redundant carriers, and that gradient attenuation follows the sink token's collective RMS magnitude. This clarifies how scale regulation of these activations works during training.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reason Over Long Horizons? An Empirical Evaluation of Context Strategies for Longitudinal Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Taye Akinrele, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Subash Neupane, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: This study compares five context strategies (Full, Recent, Episodic, Semantic, Hybrid) for longitudinal clinical reasoning on the MedLoCoMo benchmark across four open-weight LLMs, examining correctness, robustness to query-evidence distance, and abstention. Episodic and Hybrid strategies achieve the strongest accuracy while Recent Context degrades most as evidence becomes distant. The work shows that providing more history does not improve reasoning accessibility.

entry.title: How Divergence Becomes Decision Flips in Compressed Language Models

author.name: Beatriz Almeida Felicio

entry.summary: Shows that total variation, not KL divergence, directly predicts the arg-max token flip rate in compressed language models: across 802 compressed and perturbed copies of 19 open models, flip rate tracks total variation at a stable median ratio of about 1.05 with no fitted constant. KL converts into flips only through its square root with a model- and corpus-dependent factor varying fourfold. This gives practitioners a principled way to reason about how compression metrics translate into changed model decisions.

entry.title: Video Generation Models: A Survey of Post-Training and Alignment

author.name: Chaoyu Li, Xiaoyi Gu, Yogesh Kulkarni, Eun Woo Im, Mohammadmahdi Honarmand, Zeyu Wang, Juntong Song, Fei Du, Xilin Jiang, Kexin Zheng, Tianzhi Li, Fei Tao, Pooyan Fazli

entry.summary: This survey systematically covers post-training and alignment strategies for video generation models, addressing challenges unique to video such as error accumulation over time, motion-appearance coupling, multi-objective trade-offs, and limited temporal supervision. It organizes methods that adapt strong pretrained video models to follow human intent, maintain temporal coherence, and satisfy physical and safety constraints without full retraining. The field has moved rapidly from short clips to high-resolution long-duration generation, making such a synthesis timely.

entry.title: Geometric Similarity in VLM Low-Level Vision Representations

author.name: Shao-Jun Xia, Huixin Zhang, Zhen Lei, Anlan Sun, Yuner Zhang, Xiaoyang Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies how vision-language models organize hidden-layer representations for low-level image restoration, comparing autoregressive models and diffusion transformers across 24 low-level tasks in 5 categories. It uses representational similarity analysis to test whether structurally distinct VLM paradigms share a common geometric organization for pixel-level perception, which would enable transferable unified restoration adapters.

entry.title: A Matched-Budget Audit Framework for Recaptioned Image-Text Supervision Distributions

author.name: Giyeong Oh, Junghun Park, Yuhan Bae, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a reusable matched-budget audit framework for recaptioned image-text training corpora, treating a recaptioned dataset as a supervision distribution induced by a captioning policy, captioner, and source corpus. It reports a five-axis profile at a fixed text budget, exposing caption-register artifacts that length-correlated proxies and downstream benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Posterior sampling by source-space MCMC via prior-based few-step transport maps

author.name: Hoang Phuc Hau Luu, Marcelo Hartmann, Zhongjian Wang

entry.summary: This paper develops a generalized Bayesian inference framework for implicit, sample-based priors by transporting the prior into a Gaussian source space using few-step improved MeanFlow maps, then performing posterior sampling there. It provides Wasserstein error bounds between exact and learned posteriors. Useful for test-time guidance with generative models and reward-tilted sampling.

entry.title: When the Judge Acts: Auditing VLM-Guided Image Selection on Culturally Situated Prompts

author.name: Huichan Seo

entry.summary: This paper audits vision-language models acting as judges that select the best image among candidates, moving beyond the standard practice of validating judges via score agreement with human ratings. On 300 culturally situated prompts, a 4B-parameter judge barely outperformed random selection and underperformed a CLIP similarity baseline, exhibited strong position bias (picking the first image in 49% of calls), and changed its selection on 60% of prompts when candidate order was shuffled. The work highlights that VLM judges validated on ratings may still make poor or unstable actual decisions, with implications for culturally sensitive image generation pipelines.

entry.title: PickMoment: Continuous-Time Single-Image-to-Video via Learning Deblurring and Blur-to-Video

author.name: Junseong Shin, Hyeonsu Jo, Daehyun Kim, Tae Hyun Kim

entry.summary: PickMoment reformulates single-image deblurring and blur-to-video generation in continuous time, learning the interval-mean blur over arbitrary exposure sub-intervals with one deterministic model, drawing on a MeanFlow-like average-velocity formulation. It trains with reconstruction, additivity, and additional supervisions derived from the blur integral. A physically grounded improvement over fixed-frame video predictions.

entry.title: Feature Selective Model Collapse in Diffusion Models: Total Replacement versus Fixed-Budget Training

author.name: Hanna Malet, Gabriel Turinici

entry.summary: This arXiv paper (cross-listed) investigates model collapse in diffusion models trained on synthetic data, examining an intermediate regime between two previously contradictory findings: full replacement of real data (which causes collapse) versus accumulation of real data (which can prevent it). The authors study a finite-budget setting where all past datasets and real data are retained but each new model trains on a fixed-size sample from the growing pool, causing the real-data fraction to vanish even though no data is deleted. Experiments on a 2D spiral dataset and other testbeds show collapse is feature-selective, with some model components degrading faster than others under fixed-budget training.

entry.title: When Does a Second Model Help? Cross-Model Review in LLM Verification

author.name: Tae-Eun Song

entry.summary: Using a controlled experiment with 30 artifacts, 150 planted errors, 10 review conditions, and 900 sessions across three reviewer models, this study tests when cross-model review improves LLM output verification. It finds a top-tier cross-model reviewer is not significantly better in F1 than same-model fresh-session review, though the two uncover partly different errors (Jaccard about 41 percent).

entry.title: Permutation-Robust Decision Modeling with Candidate-Independent Block-Causal Attention

author.name: Guy Amit

entry.summary: The paper introduces candidate-independent block-causal attention for decision models that score variable-sized candidate sets serialized in one sequence, blocking cross-candidate information flow so scores depend on the decision problem rather than serialization order. It compares this architecture with standard causal attention and invariant baselines across benchmarks relevant to System 1 components inside generative systems.

entry.title: Can LLMs Reliably Annotate Bioassay Metadata to Improve Data Readiness?

author.name: Laura van Weesep, Riccardo Tedoldi, Jens Sj\"olund, Hossein Azizpour, Susanne Winiwarter, Ola Engkvist, Jon Paul Janet, Samuel Genheden, Juan Viguera Diez

entry.summary: Quantifies critically sparse metadata annotation across PubChem's roughly 2 million bioassays, including 36% missing assay format fields, and tests whether open-source and proprietary LLMs can predict and audit BioAssay Ontology annotations from assay text. The work addresses AI data readiness for molecular property prediction foundation models.

entry.title: From Isolated Feature to Orbits: Discovering Music Concepts via Multi-SAE Alignment

author.name: Liwei Lin, Gus Xia

entry.summary: Argues that interpretability should move from isolated features to structured relations, analyzing a music foundation model by aligning multiple sparse autoencoders to discover concept orbits such as the 12 transpositions of a chord or diatonic systems within keys. This structure-based analysis reveals how tonal concepts are organized in the model's internal space.

entry.title: MoLE: Mixture of Latent Experts for Complementary Visual Reasoning

author.name: Yingcheng Liu, Tianyi Jiang, Yujuan Ding, jiangbo Ai, Xun Jiang, Guoqing Wang, Wei Ye, Yi Bin

entry.summary: This paper identifies a redundancy problem in latent visual reasoning for vision-language models, where multiple latent tokens access the same visual evidence through shared value projections. It proposes MoLE, a Mixture of Latent Experts framework that encourages latent tokens to act as specialized experts extracting complementary visual information.

entry.title: Watch, Infer, Coordinate: Inferring Robot Partner Constraints for Zero-Shot Coordination

author.name: Suyu Ye, Zheyuan Zhang, Vaishnav Tadiparthi, Hossein Nourkhiz Mahjoub, Ehsan Moradi Pari, Tianmin Shu, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Nakul Agarwal

entry.summary: The paper studies whether a helper robot can infer a partner's physical constraints (e.g., from hardware degradation) by observing it coordinate with another robot, then apply those inferred capabilities to coordinate on a new task. The problem is hard because demonstrations reveal what the constrained robot did, not what it could have done.

entry.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars

author.name: Ramazan Fazylov, Stamatis Lefkimmiatis, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: GALA shows that pretrained 3D Gaussian avatar animation can be approximated by a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes, replacing heavy per-frame neural decoding with a shallow MLP coefficient predictor and linear blend. Block-local PCA under a rendering-aware metric and memory budget improves fidelity while reducing memory. This is a meaningful efficiency advance for real-time avatar rendering.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Learning from Multi-Expert Interval Targets

author.name: Samira Alkaee Taleghan, Younghyun Koo, Andrew P. Barrett, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: This paper addresses learning from expert labels that vary between annotators and are reported as intervals rather than point values, treating within-label imprecision and between-expert disagreement as distinct uncertainty sources. Existing approaches typically collapse these signals, and the proposed method aims to learn uncertainty-aware predictions validated against observed expert disagreement. This is relevant for medical and scientific labeling pipelines.

entry.title: Verification Pulses and the Cost of Escaping Wrong Consensus

author.name: Shivam Gupta

entry.summary: This paper models how a fixed external verification budget can push a population out of a self-reinforcing wrong consensus, using an asynchronous binary register framework. It derives minimum-fuel requirements for crossing a basin boundary under peak verification constraints and gives an exact birth-death analysis of relapse to wrong consensus, with an asymptotic critical budget scaling as N log(x0/b) plus a sqrt(N) correction. The work offers a theoretical lens on how verification effort should be timed and targeted in systems prone to collective error lock-in.

entry.title: Bellman-Certified Rounding for Sparse Policy Deployment in MDPs

author.name: Zhaojun Peng

entry.summary: This paper studies how much discounted return can be preserved when continuous policy mixtures in finite MDPs are rounded to sparse, binary policies suitable for deployment under a limited budget of state-level changes. The author derives reusable performance envelopes from a small number of Bellman solves (2d+2), develops curvature-based exchange representations, and proves an unavoidable linear dimension dependence in the guarantee as the budget scales.

entry.title: One-Step Generative Modeling via Training Dynamics Action

author.name: Zhangyong Liang, Ying Huang, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: TDAction reframes one-step generative modeling by choosing transport targets according to the local shared-parameter realization cost of the finite generator, rather than purely distributional motion. This training-dynamics-aware objective aims to make iterative training-time transport actually realizable by the final one-step map.

entry.title: ORBIT-FMIB: Tracking Order-Resolved Epistatic Information Through ESM-2

author.name: Maryam Rahimimovassagh, Ivan Garibay, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: The paper introduces ORBIT-FMIB, combining Walsh-based interaction decomposition with subset-conditioned neural dependence estimation to track higher-order epistatic information across ESM-2 layers, validated on synthetic landscapes and applied to the GB1 fitness landscape. It probes whether frozen protein-model representations retain higher-order interaction information.

entry.title: Beyond Unimodal Bases: Pullback Geometry for Multimodal Data

author.name: Honglei Brinkmann, Lucas Ng, Georgios Batzolis, Mark Girolami, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Willem Diepeveen

entry.summary: This work extends data-driven pullback Riemannian geometry, which typically assumes a unimodal Gaussian latent space, to data supported on mixtures of manifolds. By using a latent Gaussian mixture, the resulting metric keeps interpolation paths in high-likelihood regions even for multimodal data. This yields statistically more meaningful geodesics and nonlinear interpolation.

entry.title: Auditable Algebraic Counting Field for Cryptic-Pocket Detection from Apo Structures

author.name: Shan Yu, Xuening Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a supervised algebraic counting field (ACF) for predicting cryptic ligand-binding pocket residues directly from unbound (apo) protein structures. Its key selling point is auditability: predictions are compiled into integer-weighted lookup tables that can be fully reconstructed from feature values and training counts, without protein language models or template search at inference. This matters for drug discovery, where cryptic pockets are a major target-finding bottleneck and interpretability is often demanded.

entry.title: Mixture-Trained Merging for Unified Multi-Objective Models

author.name: SeongHyeon Kim, Chaeyun Jang, Seungyoo Lee, Jiyeon Ham, Yunju Bak, Boseop Kim, Juho Lee

entry.summary: This arXiv paper addresses the challenge of building a single language model that combines heterogeneous capabilities such as math, code, instruction following, and controllable thinking modes. It argues that both sequential post-training and naive weight-space merging fail because single-objective experts develop incompatible weight-space geometry, and proposes a mixture-trained merging approach to overcome this. The work matters because it targets a practical, widely felt problem in producing unified multi-capability models without capability degradation or mode collapse.

entry.title: IQS-BO: In-Context Query Selection for Bayesian Optimisation

author.name: Luca Geminiani, Nadja Klein

entry.summary: IQS-BO extends in-context Bayesian optimization by amortizing not just the surrogate (as PFNs4BO does) but also the query-selection step itself, positioning between fully amortized FIBO-style approaches and learned acquisition functions over candidate sets. The method pre-trains on synthetic priors so that query selection happens in-context, removing the need for numerical acquisition maximization. This targets the core efficiency bottleneck of expensive black-box optimization.

entry.title: Port-Hamiltonian Neural Networks for Systems with Multiple Asymptotically Stable Equilibria

author.name: Simon Heilig, Jens P\"uttschneider, Mohammad Itani, Asja Fischer, Timm Faulwasser

entry.summary: This paper extends stable port-Hamiltonian neural networks, which normally can only represent systems with a single attractor because their Hamiltonian is a global Lyapunov function, to systems with multiple asymptotically stable equilibria. The authors parametrize the Hamiltonian as a product of Bregman divergences from a single input-convex network and prove local Lyapunov stability plus structural results, including the forced existence of additional non-asymptotically-stable equilibria and boundedness of all equilibria.

entry.title: FedSAP: Federated Learning with Structured Adaptive Partitioning for Multi-Domain Heterogeneous Edge Devices

author.name: Wentao Yue, Tianyou Lai, Hongji Li, Qingyu Mao, Qilei Li

entry.summary: FedSAP is a federated learning framework for heterogeneous edge devices that treats structured pruning as a budget-constrained tri-state channel allocation problem, jointly handling unequal resource budgets and domain-shifted local data. Unlike prior resource-adaptive methods, it decides where retained model capacity should reside and how it should be shared across clients, separating transferable features from domain-sensitive updates during aggregation.

entry.title: Pooling Helps, Learned Weighting Hurts In-Context: Decomposing Group Attention

author.name: Michael Fore, James Mason Inder, Mrishika Nair, Praneetha Vaddamanu, Sharlina Keshava

entry.summary: This analysis paper dissects the group attention mechanism introduced by the Chronos-2 time series forecasting model, separating each head into a V/O pathway (weighted summary projection) and a Q/K pathway (weight selection) via inference-time edits to the attention matrix. It finds uniform pooling helps in 18 of 20 sensor-network configurations while learned Q/K weighting helps or hurts depending on group type and regime.

entry.title: A foundation for systematic analysis of transformers and RNNs for tractography

author.name: Emmanuelle Renauld, Philippe Poulin, Hugo Larochelle, Antoine Th\'eberge, Maxime Descoteaux

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates RNNs and Transformers for iterative diffusion MRI tractography, studying training strategies, input representations, and hyperparameters, and introduces a generation-validation phase enabling streamline-level supervision during training. It provides a methodological foundation for reconciling local diffusion signals with global anatomical plausibility in a medical imaging task.

entry.title: Muon meets Tamed Langevin: Momentum Preconditioning beyond Convex and gradient-Lipschitz Potentials

author.name: Nikolaos Makras, Sotirios Sabanis

entry.summary: The paper introduces non-quadratic kinetic energies yielding an underdamped Langevin system with momentum preconditioning related to Muon-style optimizers, proving invariance of the target Gibbs measure and exponential convergence under nonconvex, non-Lipschitz potentials. The Euler-Maruyama discretization admits uniform-in-time moment bounds without modification.

entry.title: Weighted Data Selection: Sharp Upper-Half and Five-Dimensional Laws

author.name: Zhongxuan Liu, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper proves exact risk laws for weighted data selection in finite weighted least squares with the minimum-norm learner, including the law Gamma_d(n) = 3 - n/d in the upper-half regime and a sharp five-dimensional case. The dataset-level upper bound and sharpness construction are fully verified in Lean 4, providing machine-checked guarantees for data-subset selection.

entry.title: Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Image Regression Models with Application to an Inertial Confinement Fusion Emulator

author.name: Carrie J. Lei-Cramer, Michael S. Jones, Laura J. Wendelberger

entry.summary: This work proposes Adaptive Conformal Prediction using Nearest Neighbors to provide input-dependent uncertainty estimates for black-box image regression models, applied to an inertial confinement fusion emulator. It addresses the need for reliability assessment in high-stakes scientific ML where outputs guide costly experiments. The method is model-agnostic and does not require access to model internals.

entry.title: End-to-End Historical Music Restoration in Latent Space

author.name: Steven Cho, Junghyun Koo, Raphael Lafargue, Tushar Dhyani, Eloi Moliner, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: The paper presents the first supervised end-to-end benchmark for restoring multi-instrument orchestral historical recordings, including a more faithful simulation of the early-20th-century degradation chain and generative deep-learning restoration methods in latent space. This addresses the lack of pre-degradation ground truth that has confined prior work to solo pieces and super-resolution. It matters for audio restoration and for generative audio research generally.

entry.title: Progressive-Resolution Secure Aggregation for Federated Learning

author.name: Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi

entry.summary: The paper formulates progressive-resolution secure aggregation (PSA), a new cryptographic functionality in which clients upload clipped, dithered updates once as nested-lattice digits, and the server can later be granted successively finer resolutions of the aggregate via a non-collusion-protected pad without renewed client participation. This decouples upload from precision release. It offers a flexible privacy-utility tradeoff for federated learning.

entry.title: Block Optimism for Nonstationary Bandits with Latent Linear Dynamics

author.name: Taehyun Hwang, Hyunjun Choi, Heesang Ann, Min-hwan Oh

entry.summary: This work studies nonstationary stochastic bandits where actions influence an unobserved latent state with linear dynamics and bilinear rewards. It improves on prior explore-then-commit regret rates via adaptive block-level optimism, combining a cyclic truncation approximation with optimistic planning.

entry.title: MASkillBlender: Decentralized Whole-Body Coordination for Multi-Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Skill Blending

author.name: Yifan Hu, Luhang Hong, Mingkang Long, Danning Wang, Chengfeng Jia, Rong Su, Junjie Fu, Guanghui Wen

entry.summary: MASkillBlender is a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for decentralized coordination of multiple humanoids in loco-manipulation tasks, building a shared high-level policy over pre-trained single-humanoid skills. It achieves coordinated whole-body behaviors using only task-level rewards, avoiding heavy reward engineering.

entry.title: Zero Flux: Flow-Based Comparison of High-Dimensional Discrete Distributions

author.name: Leyang Wang, Yakun Wang, Song Liu, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: This paper extends a flow-matching-based two-sample test from continuous to discrete distributions via a criterion called Zero Flux, based on local probability fluxes that vanish at the midpoint if and only if two distributions are identical. This addresses the challenge of comparing high-dimensional discrete distributions whose state spaces grow exponentially. It provides a principled new discrepancy measure useful for evaluating generative models of discrete data.

entry.title: Comparing a gradient boosting algorithm to the GOES FDC for wildfire detection

author.name: Asaf Vanunu, Boaz Nadler, Arnon Karnieli

entry.summary: The authors train a CatBoost gradient boosting model on GOES ABI satellite imagery paired with over 300,000 VIIRS fire detections for wildfire detection. Evaluated across five regions, the model beats the operational GOES Fire Detection and Characterization product, with F1 gains of 0.16-0.38, and detected 26 of 51 historical fire events earlier than the operational baseline.

entry.title: DeBERTa-ConPara: Attack-Aware and Deployment-Realistic Detection of AI-Generated Text

author.name: Mohamed Mady, Yupei Li, Johannes Reschke, Bj\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: This paper introduces DeBERTa-ConPara, a detector for AI-generated text that combines attack-aware Unicode preprocessing with a contextual transformer encoder trained across multiple benchmarks (HC3 Plus, M4, MAGE, RAID). A key insight is that preprocessing has opposite effects depending on where it is applied: normalizing the training corpus can collapse adversarial examples into duplicates of clean ones, destroying supervision signal. The work targets realistic deployment conditions including distribution shift and adversarial perturbation.

entry.title: Acmite: Mitigating Gender Bias in LLMs through Concept-Guided Mutual Information

author.name: Tian Lan, Xiaoqing Cheng, Han Zhang, Jiang Li

entry.summary: Acmite is a lightweight debiasing framework that represents stereotypes as structured semantic concepts, uses maximal marginal relevance to select diverse examples, and explicitly models the statistical dependence between outputs and stereotype concepts via mutual information. This moves beyond word-substitution-based debiasing. It enables targeted, context-robust bias reduction.

entry.title: From Rules to Neural Graphs: Scalable Structured Prediction for Patent Prior Art Search

author.name: Nikolai Zenovkin, Sebastian Bj\"orkqvist

entry.summary: The authors replace brittle rule-based parsers with a neural biaffine-attention parser that predicts structured invention graphs directly from patent text for prior art search. A sliding-window local scoring scheme reduces complexity from quadratic to linear in window size, allowing training on short sequences and deployment on documents over 40k tokens. This matters for long-document information retrieval in a high-stakes legal domain.

entry.title: Concept Driven Domain Adaptation: Finding an Abstract Needle in a Haystack

author.name: Haiming Zhao, Tai Wang, Kun Zhang, Xicheng Peng, Zhiyang Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces concept-to-example video retrieval, where abstract curriculum concepts must be grounded in temporally sparse documentary evidence, motivated by science teachers searching for teaching clips. It proposes CDDA, a three-stage framework bridging the gap between abstract queries and observable video events.

entry.title: Semantic RGB--Depth Based Surgical Skill Assessment in Microscopic Stereo Videos

author.name: Jecia Z. Y. Mao, Sue M. Cho, Francis X. Creighton, Deepa Galaiya, Russell H. Taylor, Manish Sahu

entry.summary: This work presents a framework for objective microsurgical skill assessment from stereo operating-microscope videos by fusing sparse metric stereo depth with learned depth via regression, then reasoning over semantic instrument-anatomy interactions in 3D. Existing RGB-only approaches miss the spatial relationships that characterize surgical competence. The work comes from a strong medical robotics group including Russell Taylor at Johns Hopkins.

entry.title: Localisation-Aware Uncertainty for Pretrained Object Detection

author.name: Charmaine Barker, Daniel Bethell, Simos Gerasimou

entry.summary: This paper introduces a lightweight post-hoc evidential meta-model that estimates uncertainty over object localizations while keeping the base detector frozen. It identifies localization-relevant features and uses saliency-guided modification to build a curriculum, training the meta-model with targets that combine localization error, modification level, and prediction instability. Existing uncertainty methods for detectors typically require retraining or repeated inference.

entry.title: Synthetic training for long-tail haemorrhagic lesion segmentation in data-scarce settings

author.name: Yuan Cao, Sumeet Dash, Antonia Zachariadis, Stefanie Schreiber, Katja Neumann, Jose Bernal

entry.summary: This paper proposes a synthetic training framework for segmenting cerebral microbleeds and cortical superficial siderosis without real voxel-level lesion annotations. It procedurally inserts lesion labels using clinical priors on location and morphology, synthesizes realistic images with randomized intensities and Rician noise, and addresses severe class scarcity in medical imaging.

entry.title: Memory-Guided B-Roll Generation from User Video Collections

author.name: Cusuh Ham, Fabian Caba Heilbron, Josef Sivic, Bryan Russell

entry.summary: The paper introduces collection-grounded B-roll sequence generation: given a user video collection, a natural-language directive, and target duration, produce a multi-shot sequence that complements primary footage while preserving characters, settings, objects, and style. MemComposer turns raw footage into structured visual-reference memory used to plan, retrieve, and generate grounded sequences.

entry.title: RASteer: Retain-Aware Activation Steering for Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models

author.name: Yongliang Wu, Haori Lu, Yulun Wu, Jinqi Luo, Xingyu Zhu, Yaoyao Liu

entry.summary: RASteer improves concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models by constructing steering directions that account for retained concepts, since target and retained concepts overlap in representation space and naive steering suppresses non-target content. By disentangling shared components, it erases target concepts while better preserving general generation ability.

entry.title: Surface-volume self-supervised representation learning of brain MRI for genetic discovery

author.name: Tian Xia, Nuo Chen, Zihao Zhu, Huiwen Han, Ziqian Xie, Zhiwen Fan, Degui Zhi

entry.summary: MEVA is a self-supervised framework that jointly encodes voxel-level brain MRI intensities and cortical mesh geometry (curvature, thickness) into shared imaging features for use as phenotypes in genome-wide association studies. Combining mesh and volumetric inputs improves age and sex prediction and enables richer genetic discovery than either representation alone.

entry.title: Spatially Gated Diffusion for Localized Counterfactual Chest Radiograph Editing

author.name: Kamran Ullah Afaq, Basit Raza

entry.summary: This paper builds a latent diffusion editor for chest radiographs that preserves unrelated content while completing requested changes, using an instruction-independent source trajectory mixed with an instruction-conditioned editing trajectory via a learned gate, plus an image-space mask for compositing. On 2,400 MIMIC-derived requests it achieves 93.5% joint validity and 97.4% target completion, modestly outperforming a composition-only control. Counterfactual medical image editing has applications for model auditing and training data generation.

entry.title: Does Continual Imitation Learning Remain Grounded? A Language-Perturbed Benchmark for Robotic Task Retention

author.name: Siddeshwar Raghavan, Ziqin Yuan, Fengqing Zhu, Byung-Cheol Min

entry.summary: This paper introduces a benchmark protocol testing whether robotic policies that retain task performance under continual imitation learning remain actually grounded in language instructions. It constructs meaning-preserving and meaning-changing instruction variants for the LIBERO suites and evaluates representative continual learning methods on LIBERO-Goal. It matters because it exposes whether catastrophic forgetting research measures true language grounding or just memorized scene cues.

entry.title: Query-Conditioned Articulation Estimation from a Single Image

author.name: Abdelrhman Werby, Fabio Scaparro, Kai O. Arra

entry.summary: Presents QueryArt, a model that estimates 3D articulation parameters of unseen objects from a single RGB image, a 2D query point, and camera intrinsics, decoupling articulation estimation from part segmentation. This avoids failure modes from missed detections and incorrect part associations that plague coupled pipelines, and sidesteps metric-3D issues that a single view cannot resolve. Enables robot interaction with articulated objects from minimal observation.

entry.title: Decentralized Safe Path Following for Multiple Quadrotors on Intersecting Paths with Theoretical Guarantees

author.name: Hamza Tariq, Adeel Akhtar

entry.summary: Reformulates transverse feedback linearization as a constrained quadratic program with four equality constraints enforcing path adherence, speed, and heading for decentralized multi-quadrotor path following on intersecting paths. Safety is achieved by relaxing only the along-path speed constraint while keeping path and heading hard, with theoretical guarantees of convergence, path adherence, collision avoidance, and feasibility under stated assumptions. Rigorous multi-agent safety control with proofs.

entry.title: Finite-Data Safety Informativity Under Dynamic Asymmetric Actuation

author.name: Abhinav Sinha, Praveen Kumar Ranjan, Yongcan Cao

entry.summary: This robotics/control-theory paper develops a finite-data safety certificate for systems with model uncertainty and asymmetric input limits, determining whether a control command can enforce a prescribed safety inequality when multiple models are consistent with the observed data. It derives a support formula for the worst-case safety contribution across all data-consistent models. This matters for safe control of physical systems where the model is imperfect and control authority is limited.

entry.title: Evaluating the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act

author.name: Rob Ennals

entry.summary: Rob Ennals analyzes the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act recently endorsed by MIRI, examining whether the bill's drafting achieves its stated goal of banning dangerous-capability AI and restricting advanced AI development to certified institutions. He concludes the bill contains numerous drafting flaws likely to cause unintended negative consequences, even granting the legitimacy of its aims. This is a substantive policy critique relevant to current AI governance debates.

entry.title: R-GroundBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for R-Group Groundingin Markush Molecular Editing

author.name: Xin Wang, Zichuan Ying, Xinna Lin, Junqi Zhang, Hanyi Xiong, Tianyu Gao, Hairong Zhang, Qixiang Hua, Botian Shi, Zhenhailong Wang, Kaicheng Yu

entry.summary: R-GroundBench is a diagnostic benchmark built from real pharmaceutical patent Markush structures, evaluating grounding of variable R-group placeholders across molecular, textual, and chemical information. It includes a multiple-choice VQA track with controlled difficulty and modality splits, filling a gap since existing molecule-language benchmarks only cover fully specified molecules. This targets a core reasoning gap for AI in drug discovery and patent workflows.

entry.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Preference Distributions

author.name: Fan Huang, Minsuk Kim, C. Tyler Diggans, Filippo Radicchi

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes LLM-generated distributions of human preferences across air travel, restaurants, and consumer products, finding that models are self-coherent (top outcomes stabilize under repeated sampling) but wildly discordant across model families and scales, with little consensus even on most-probable outcomes. This cautions against using LLMs as substitutes for real preference data in simulation and decision support. Solid empirical contribution on an underexamined reliability question.

entry.title: Decision Titan: Test-Time Training for Long-Term Memory in Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jude Waide, Robert Lieck

entry.summary: Decision Titan applies the Test-Time Training (TTT) framework, which stores episodic memories in network parameters via gradient descent at train and test time, to offline reinforcement learning for the first time. It targets long-term dependency problems that plague RNNs and quadratic-attention Transformers in sequential decision-making, and analyzes how the memory functions in practice within RL. This extends a technique proven in NLP to a new domain.

entry.title: Random Recursive Models

author.name: Jama Hussein Mohamud, Mirco Ravanelli

entry.summary: The Random Recursive Model maintains a pool of L learned layers and performs T recursive steps by sampling one layer with replacement per example and step, enabling flexible layer reuse beyond fixed layer orders typical of recursive models. On challenging reasoning tasks, RRM matches or exceeds baselines often with 50-75% fewer parameters, and can vary computational depth. It offers a parameter-efficient alternative to scaling model size.

entry.title: A Citation-Grounded Benchmark for Trustworthy Earnings Call Transcript Analysis with Large Language Models

author.name: Yingzhu Zhao, Vlad Pandelea, Han Yuan, Bo Hu, Wuqiong Luo, Li Zhang, Zheng Ma

entry.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating citation-grounded LLM analysis of earnings call transcripts, proposing a numeric evidence evaluation method that reduces dependence on costly expert annotation. It targets groundedness assessment in long-context, long-answer financial analysis settings.

entry.title: Detect, Explain, Interpret: An End-to-End Benchmark for Time Series Anomaly Detection, Explainability and Interpretability

author.name: Roberto Stanzione, Jules Barbe, Magali Parrino, J\'er\'emie Fourmann, Paul Boniol

entry.summary: This benchmark extends time-series anomaly detection evaluation beyond accuracy to include spatial explainability and human-understandable interpretations, providing rich semantic annotations existing benchmarks lack. It addresses the domain-agnosticism of current detectors. Useful for standardizing evaluation of explainable anomaly detection.

entry.title: Multi-Party Backchannel Prediction: a Diagnosis, a Benchmark, and a Ceiling

author.name: Mohammed Hafsati, Ahmed Loughzali

entry.summary: This paper introduces a multi-party backchannel prediction benchmark from the AMI corpus with 682 masked-listener views, 190 speakers, and nearly 19,000 events in a person-disjoint split. It diagnoses that a state-of-the-art dyadic model performs at chance zero-shot on meetings, that acoustic features remain informative via probing, and that listener conditioning fails to generalize to unseen listeners, establishing a performance ceiling.

entry.title: Cog-VADU: A Training-Free Cognitive Reasoning Framework for Video Anomaly Detection and Understanding

author.name: Mohd Ubaid Wani, Sara Atito, Josef Kittler, Muhammad Awais

entry.summary: Reformulates video anomaly detection as sequential cognitive reasoning with a fully training-free framework, using Chain-of-Anomaly-Detection-Thought Prompting to unroll an LVLM into a recurrent reasoning chain across video segments, propagating structured rationales to maintain implicit temporal memory. This improves generalization in open-set scenarios over dataset-specific training approaches.

entry.title: Flowing Faster to Coordinate: One-Step Online Multi-Agent Flow Policies

author.name: Zhuoran Li, Yunzhan Li, Xun Wang, Yihan Du, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Proposes OMAF, an online multi-agent RL framework combining a Transformer-based flow policy that captures complex multimodal coordination behaviors with one-step action generation to avoid costly iterative diffusion sampling. It targets the balance between expressive generative policies and efficient training and execution.

entry.title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)

author.name: Zilin Du, Bowen Yang, Boyang Albert Li

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why naively replacing per-sample weights with a learned selection network destabilizes meta-learning-based data selection for LLM training, identifying weight suppression and reliance on easy features as causes. It proposes TESS, a transferable example scoring and selection method with a modified loss that stabilizes optimization and generalizes to unseen data.

entry.title: Sharp Oracle-Regret Tradeoffs for Projection-Free Online Convex Optimization

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: The paper characterizes the minimax regret for online convex optimization when the feasible set is accessible only via a linear optimization oracle, with limits on total and per-round oracle calls, proving a dimension-free Θ bound of GD·max{√T, T/(1+min{Q,BT})^(1/4)}. The lower bound holds for arbitrary randomized learners. This sharpens understanding of the oracle-call versus regret tradeoff in projection-free methods.

entry.title: Coupling Perception and Reasoning in Federated Multimodal Graph Foundation Models

author.name: Zekai Chen, Xun Wu, Hailin Zhang, Xunkai Li, Yu Liu, Kairui Yang, Muyan Huang, Xuaner Chen, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: This work studies federated adaptation of multimodal graph foundation models, where clients hold private multimodal graphs and cannot share raw data. The authors show empirically that adapting the multimodal encoder and the GNN are not independent, contradicting prior practice of freezing the encoder, and propose a method that co-adapts perception and relational reasoning modules. This yields better federated adaptation than graph-side-only updates.

entry.title: RACE: Residual-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for Neighbor-Rich Time-Series Foundation Model Forecasting

author.name: Hao-Nan Shi, Tong Wu, Chen-Cong Sun, Yuan Jiang, Han-Jia Ye, De-Chuan Zhan

entry.summary: RACE adapts time-series foundation models at test time for neighbor-rich forecasting, where related but nonidentical historical series (e.g., CGM trajectories, web workloads) are available for each query. Rather than costly per-domain fine-tuning, it exploits residual signals and neighbor relevance to improve foundation-model forecasts in a backbone-transferable way. This targets a practical gap between per-series inference and domain adaptation.

entry.title: SimplexUQ: An Evaluation Framework and Benchmark for Conformal Uncertainty on Simplex-Valued Predictions

author.name: Liang You, Hengyu Shi, Dongwen Ou

entry.summary: SimplexUQ is the first benchmark and reproducible protocol for measuring how conformal prediction wrappers allocate coverage unevenly across simplex-valued predictions, comparing existing wrappers rather than proposing new ones. The SimplexTasks-12 suite spans six synthetic regimes and six real tasks including topic mixtures, cell-type fractions, and emotion distributions.

entry.title: Reformulation-Contrastive Learning for Mixed Integer Programs

author.name: Ousema Bouaneni, Mathis Le Bail, Cl\'ement Elliker, Ma\"el Jenny, Sonia Vanier

entry.summary: The paper uses equivalent MILP reformulations, such as integrality-preserving variable changes and redundant constraints, as self-supervision for learning general-purpose representations of MILP variables and constraints. It characterizes valid affine reformulations and builds on equivariant architectures to learn representations robust to formulation changes, aiming to accelerate MILP solvers.

entry.title: Platonic Task Arithmetic

author.name: Junghwan Park, Woojin Cho

entry.summary: The paper hypothesizes that task-specific parameter updates in different architectures are shadows of a shared model-agnostic platonic task vector, and introduces Universal Task Descriptors: architecture-independent matrices recording a task's functional effect that support addition and negation. This extends task arithmetic beyond single models to cross-architecture settings for encoders paired with text encoders.

entry.title: Autoregressive Drillhole Modelling Under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yihao Ding, Daniel Yitian Su, Yiran Zhang, Christopher M. Gonzalez, Wei Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces DrillBench, a benchmark of 49,671 Western Australian drillholes for next-layer lithology prediction and autoregressive stratigraphic generation, framing mineral-exploration drilling as a naturally autoregressive sequence problem. It covers a gradient of distribution-shift settings, addressing a largely unexplored application of the autoregressive paradigm. The work opens a new domain for sequence modeling research with real economic relevance.

entry.title: Learned End-to-End Guidance Schedules for Diffusion Models

author.name: Aneesh Barthakur, Mathias Niepert, Luiz F. O. Chamon

entry.summary: LEEGS learns a time-dependent schedule for the guidance scale in guided diffusion sampling, trained end-to-end by minimizing the guidance function over few sampling steps. This lets diffusion models satisfy requirements while maintaining data quality with fewer sampling steps than constant small guidance scales, reducing computational cost.

entry.title: Evidence-Gated Research: Statistically Controlled Model Adoption in Adaptive Search

author.name: Yifan Guo

entry.summary: Evidence-Gated Research introduces a statistical adoption layer for adaptive model search where each challenger model is frozen before decision evidence is revealed, and anytime-valid evidence (e-values) across predeclared environments feeds an online controller. The procedure controls false discovery rate under explicit conditional-validity and predictability conditions, addressing the path-dependence problem in sequential model adoption.

entry.title: The Curvature of Regret in Contextual Linear Optimization

author.name: Konstantinos Ziliaskopoulos, Alexander Vinel, Alice E. Smith

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that the nonsmooth pointwise regret in decision-focused linear optimization becomes locally quadratic after averaging over the data distribution, and derives the curvature in closed form as a measure on normal fan walls. It provides a tractable one-projection approximation with weak convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Learn the Directions, Normalize the Gains: Post-Training Normalization for LoRA

author.name: Zailong Tian, Yanzhe Chen, Zhuoheng Han, Houfeng Wang, Lizi Liao

entry.summary: The paper identifies adaptation imbalance in LoRA, where a few singular directions dominate the learned update, and proposes LoRA-Norm, a post-training normalization that spectrally rebalances gains while restoring total spectral mass. It requires no calibration data or extra training, preserving learned directions.

entry.title: Neural Fourier Surrogates for Data Reuploading Quantum Neural Networks

author.name: Oliver Knitter, Jonathan Mei, Sang Hyub Kim, Chi Chen, Masako Yamada, Martin Roetteler

entry.summary: The paper proposes Neural Fourier Surrogates (NFS), a classical stochastic neural network that learns coefficients over the same finite Fourier series support as data reuploading quantum neural networks, enabling like-for-like comparisons. Experiments on tabular benchmarks show NFS is an effective classifier and helps clarify the classical-quantum comparison.

entry.title: Tolerance-Based Fairness Auditing: Violation Certification and Sensitivity Screening

author.name: Jie Tang, Chuanlong Xie, Lixing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper develops a unified statistical framework for tolerance-based fairness auditing with two complementary objectives: violation certification, which controls false violation declarations, and sensitivity screening, which prioritizes detecting violations. It answers how to decide whether group disparity exceeds a prespecified tolerance.

entry.title: Universal Byte-Level Encoding: UTF-8/UTF-16 Routing to Reduce Cross-Script Token-Budget Disparities

author.name: Hyunsik Kim, Youngmoon Jung

entry.summary: The paper identifies an encoding floor problem in UTF-8-based byte-level BPE tokenizers, where many non-Latin scripts pay high worst-case pre-merge token costs, inflating cost and shrinking context for multilingual users. Universal Byte-Level Encoding proposes a dual-alphabet tokenizer routing between UTF-8 and UTF-16 representations to reduce cross-script token-budget disparities without penalizing efficient English spans. It addresses multilingual fairness at the tokenization level.

entry.title: Lingtai: What Concept Geometry Reveals--and Does Not Reveal--About LLM Inference

author.name: Jiangang Chen

entry.summary: Lingtai is a training-free concept telemetry layer that projects LLM residual states onto a bank of named concept anchors at each generation step, built without labeled examples or optimization, producing a per-step concept-coordinate signal. Across code generation and grade-school math reasoning, this signal robustly associates with predictive uncertainty, surviving problem-identity and token-position controls.

entry.title: AGO AI Quality Gate: Evidence-First Release Decisions for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Giulio Zeloni, Enrico Lo Conte, Salvatore Rionero, Giuseppe Santoro, Alessandro Rastelli, Fabio Sorrentino

entry.summary: This paper reports on AGO, an industrial quality-gate framework for deciding whether to promote, revise, or block RAG system versions under incomplete evidence and fallible LLM judges. It combines a four-state decision model treating missing data and judge errors as explicit outcomes, layered scoring, a stratified beta-binomial gate quantifying regression risk, and a mandatory meta-evaluation of the LLM judge itself.

entry.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models

author.name: Juan S. Santillana

entry.summary: This paper documents a false-positive tool-use result in Spanish security language models caused by lenient keyword-matching benchmarks, and proposes a ladder of strict but cheap diagnostics including verbatim-reproduction checks and first-token probes that cleanly separate a 661M model with genuine tool use from a 1B model without it. A valuable caution about benchmark gaming in small-model evaluation.

entry.title: Seeing the City or Recognizing the Place? What Street-View Imagery Adds Beyond Existing Urban Data in VLM Urban Sensing

author.name: Kaizhen Tan

entry.summary: The paper rigorously tests whether street-view imagery adds predictive value beyond existing urban data across seven attributes, three VLMs, and multiple public data sources, using image replacement and conflicting-record interventions. Findings show images help for some attributes like building type but are matched by existing records for others like road damage and house prices. This challenges assumptions in the fast-growing VLM urban sensing literature.

entry.title: FORTE: Adaptive Scoring and Exact Keyframe Selection for Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Haifeng Huang, Biyin Xu, Chunsheng Xin, Yang Li

entry.summary: FORTE is a training-free framework for query-aware keyframe selection in long-video QA that adaptively allocates a limited relevance-scoring budget using a Gaussian-process bandit-style strategy, avoiding the fixed-candidate-pool limitation of prior methods. It balances exploration of underrepresented temporal regions with exploitation of promising frames. This improves long-video understanding efficiency for MLLMs.

entry.title: Overcoming Kernel Redundancy for Scaling Logic Gate Networks

author.name: Sejin Park, Hongjae Lee, Changwoo Han, Seung-Won Jung

entry.summary: The paper studies width scaling in differentiable logic gate networks, finding that naive scaling introduces redundancy among logic kernels that limits effective capacity gains. It proposes methods to overcome this redundancy so logic gate networks can benefit from the scaling principles that drive conventional deep learning.

entry.title: STAGE: Subspace-Targeted Affine Generative Erasure for Text-to-3D Models

author.name: Karol Dziekan, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Dawid Malarz

entry.summary: STAGE is a training-free, closed-form framework for concept erasure in native text-to-3D generators. It observes that 3D generators synthesize structured representations directly, so erasure must be stage-aware: shape concepts are removed in the structural stage and material concepts in the appearance stage, with each edit confined to a low-dimensional subspace. Prior closed-form erasure methods assumed the single generative pathway of 2D diffusion.

entry.title: When Text-to-Image Helps Editing: The Effects of Conditioning During Denoising

author.name: Lidia Troeshestova, Alexander Ustyuzhanin, Sergey Kastryulin

entry.summary: The paper studies how source-image conditioning evolves during denoising in unified editing/generation models and finds that source attention can decline across the sampling trajectory.
