Exploiting this, it proposes task switching to text-to-image generation for bounded denoising intervals, improving edit quality across three unified editors and four benchmarks while preserving perceptual fidelity.

entry.title: MapLightning: Online Vectorized HD Map Construction with 1D Map Tokens

author.name: Shen Zheng, Anurag Ghosh, Mani Ramanagopal, Srinivasa Narasimhan

entry.summary: MapLightning replaces dense bird's-eye-view grids in online HD map construction with a compact set of 1D learnable map tokens. A transformer concatenates map and image tokens under full self-attention, then retains only updated map tokens for decoding, enabling accurate real-time vectorized map inference for autonomous driving.

entry.title: HiPhy: Hierarchical Alignment for Physically-Plausible Multi-Principle Video Generation

author.name: Tahira Kazimi, Shubhankar Borse, Munawar Hayat, Fatih Porikli, Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: HiPhy is a reinforcement learning framework that grounds video generation in physical laws, targeting scenes where multiple physical principles must hold simultaneously, such as a balloon rising while steam rises from a pot. Its hierarchical alignment addresses multi-principle interactions that existing single-principle methods ignore.

entry.title: ROWBench: Do Video Models Render What the Program Specifies?

author.name: Zheng-Hui Huang, Guixu Lin, Yu-Ju Tsai, Jian-Kai Zhu, Fengbo Lan, Yu-Lun Liu, Yung-Yu Chuang, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: PROWBench evaluates programmable world models on fidelity to fine-grained, program-specified world events, with 170 programmatically constructed episodes and 600 proxy videos logging entity states and timestamped events, including off-camera ones, as replayable world records. It fills a gap left by benchmarks that only assess visual quality or instruction adherence, relevant to next-generation game engines.

entry.title: Extreme Length Generalization in a Compact Recurrent Architecture for One-Shot Exploration

author.name: Izen Thornton, Aaron Shey, William Su

entry.summary: FRANK is a 507K-parameter recurrent architecture combining tau-gated recurrent modules, content-addressable memory, and a feedforward reflex pathway, evaluated on algorithmic sequence tasks trained at lengths 5-20 and tested out to two million tokens. At 100,000x the maximum training length, 6 of 10 seeds retain 100% accuracy while no baseline configuration does, with statistical significance testing. This addresses extreme length generalization under fixed onboard compute for autonomous one-shot robot missions.

entry.title: When Do Causal World Models Help Modular LLM Agents

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: The paper addresses the gap between observational world models and intervention-time planning for modular LLM agents, showing that observational traces cannot distinguish whether one module authorizes, mediates, or merely correlates with another. It introduces FedCausalCompose, a causal world-model framework where local actions provide intervention-response evidence for cross-module interfaces, and proves an irreducible interventional gap for purely observational models.

entry.title: JusticeAxis: Benchmarking Legal Judgment between Rigid Rule Application and Ungrounded Discretion

author.name: Zhengkai Tu, Mingda Zhang, Zijia Wang, Xiaoying Tang, Jimmy Huang

entry.summary: JusticeAxis is a benchmark of 256 real criminal cases from 18 countries with audio, image, and text evidence, each with three lawyer-written judgments (the recorded one and one per failure mode), formalizing legal judgment as a reference-anchored task tied to both statute and circumstances. JusticeAgent complements it as a harness whose element agents establish facts and weigh them against legal rules.

entry.title: MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory

author.name: Mitchell Piehl, Muchao Ye

entry.summary: MemFit is a long-term memory system for conversational LLM agents that stores each turn verbatim in an append-only store with near-instantaneous LLM-free insertion, indexing turns with segment summaries instead of replacing or compressing them. This avoids the costly LLM-driven write operations of current memory systems while retaining surface-level details. It targets cost and latency reduction in agentic memory.

entry.title: OR for AI That Does OR: Routing LLMs up the Escalator inside the OSCAR Framework

author.name: Jinzhi Bu, Haixin Tang, Huanan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents OSCAR, a framework where a simulator, coder, and reviewer collaborate to translate business descriptions into optimization models, using an offline simulator certified against labeled examples to verify candidate formulations. It studies how to allocate attempts across LLMs of differing cost and capability via routing. Relevant for making LLM-driven operations research trustworthy and cost-effective.

entry.title: Network World Models as Environments for Algorithm Design on Complex Systems

author.name: Rishab Alagharu, Hongji Pu, Zeeshan Memon, Xinyuan Song, Yuntong Hu, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes an action-conditioned network world model that simulates how complex systems (e.g., epidemic spread, influence campaigns) evolve under node-level actions, replacing costly Monte Carlo simulation when scoring candidate intervention algorithms. This enables faster iterative algorithm design on complex systems. Extends the world-model paradigm beyond robotics to networked dynamics.

entry.title: MCRI: A Four-Dimensional Framework for Analyzing and Evaluating Agent Skills

author.name: Zongrui Yang, Li Xintong, Runchen Xu, Zhongsheng Wang, Zhedong Lin, Haoyuan Li, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: MCRI proposes a four-dimensional framework for analyzing and evaluating agent skills, drawing on information gain and behavioral constraint, operationalized as MCRI-Eval using LLM-based assessment. The method is validated on 63,812 public skills from the OpenClaw skill Hub with 58,275 skill-conditioned executions across BigCodeBench, BFCL-Fundamental, and Mind2Web. Scores correlate with community popularity signals and achieve top downstream prediction performance.

entry.title: Homomorphic Advantage Operator: Stabilizing Reinforcement Learning Under Fully Homomorphic Encryption Constraints

author.name: Abid Mohamed Nadhir, Ahmad Al Hanbali, Beggas Mounir

entry.summary: This work addresses the instability that arises when fully homomorphic encryption is applied to deep RL, where polynomial approximations of non-linear operations diverge catastrophically through a recursive error phenomenon the authors call Bellman drift. The proposed Homomorphic Advantage Operator adapts zero-mean centering projections from advantage-based value estimation to prevent divergence. This enables privacy-preserving cloud RL on confidential data.

entry.title: The Cognitive Continuity Test: Verifying Governed State Transitions in Persistent AI Agents

author.name: Jun He, Deying Yu

entry.summary: The Cognitive Continuity Test (CCT) is a policy-relative contract for verifying state transitions in persistent agents, using scoped authority, provenance, deterministic application, semantic predicates, and persistence receipts to distinguish admissibility, violation, and unresolved evidence. An accompanying IdentityLineageBench supports evaluation of transition governance.

entry.title: Partial AUC Maximization from Positive-unlabeled Data

author.name: Atsutoshi Kumagai, Tomoharu Iwata, Taishi Nishiyama, Hiroshi Takahashi, Kazuki Adachi, Yasuhiro Fujiwara

entry.summary: Introduces a method for maximizing the partial AUC (true positive rate within a specified false positive rate range) using only positive and unlabeled data, removing the need for labeled negatives that are often unavailable due to privacy or annotation-expertise constraints. The authors are from an established industrial research group, and the setting targets high-stakes domains like cybersecurity and medical care.

entry.title: LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jaeyun Shin, Hangeol Chang, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Introduces LEGO-OPD, which decomposes multi-teacher supervision in multimodal on-policy distillation by selectively composing factors from a language expert and a grounding expert into a single teacher distribution. This disentangles a VLM's visual grounding signal from its language prior, addressing the tradeoff between improved perception and degraded language reasoning.

entry.title: Code That Works, Environments That Don't: Measuring Environment Reproducibility in AI-Generated Software

author.name: Bhanu Prakash Vangala, Tanu Malik

entry.summary: This paper argues that functional correctness of LLM-generated code overlooks environment specification, the accurate identification of dependencies needed to execute the code. The authors develop an agent protocol for environment specification and a three-layer framework (declared, runtime-installed, and necessary-and-sufficient dependencies) to systematically assess coding agents. The work highlights a practical reproducibility gap in AI-generated software.

entry.title: Learning Transferable Skills using Goal-Conditioned Bisimulation

author.name: Mohammad Amin Abbasfar, Farbod Azimmohseni, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: Proposes an objective for learning action-aware temporal representations with functional equivariance that preserve local temporal structure while remaining robust to layout variation, and builds unsupervised skill discovery on top of this embedding. The approach avoids requiring expert data and improves transfer to previously unseen environments. This matters for reward-free pretraining of general-purpose control policies.

entry.title: On-the-fly Weight Generation: A Hypernetwork Proof of Concept on ARC-1D

author.name: Fabio J. Fehr, Philip Torr

entry.summary: Using ARC-1D as a controlled testbed, this paper shows that individual input transformations can be represented by tiny specialist models whose parameters are generated on the fly by a hypernetwork from a few demonstrations. The generated parameters occupy a structured weight space, and the specialists exhibit partial compositional generalization plus generalization to unseen transformations. Removing explicit task identifiers improved generalization.

entry.title: Distilling Directional Verification

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Sugyeong Eo, Seongtae Hong, Seungyoon Lee, Chanjun Park, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: The paper shows that knowledge distillation from teacher-generated answers can propagate the teacher's directional recall failures, and proposes directional label distillation: the frozen teacher scores candidate answers in the direction it knows best and the best-scoring candidate becomes the student's target. On parent-child fact relations, known-direction scoring yields more accurate labels than generation.

entry.title: When Is Deletion Ordering Tractable? From Update Dynamics to Permutation Structure

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Ziyu Zhao, Yixuan He, Xiaowen Chang Alex Smola

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes when the order of sequentially processing data-deletion requests (e.g., machine unlearning) affects the terminal model, identifying position-additivity and suffix-localization reductions that make the induced permutation objective tractable. Under shared affine updates it characterizes the quadratic assignment structure. Relevant to the emerging field of machine unlearning economics and scheduling.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Control for Skill-Based Smart Manufacturing

author.name: Kay K\"ohle, Darko Anicic, Thomas A. Runkler, Ren\'e Graf

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-agent LLM architecture for flexible manufacturing where each factory module is paired with a dedicated agent and MCP tool server exposing skills via OPC UA, coordinating over MQTT with real-time state grounding. It compares orchestrator, peer-to-peer, and other agent architectures for both offline sequence generation and online fault handling.

entry.title: FedMIX-P: Mixing Local and Global Preconditioners for Federated Vision and Language Model Training

author.name: Junkang Liu

entry.summary: FedMIX-P mixes shared and local adaptive preconditioners at every local federated training step, reducing operator mismatch squared by a factor related to the mixing weight while retaining local adaptation. It provides an O(R^-1/2) stationarity bound for smooth nonconvex objectives with stochastic gradients and partial participation, without requiring local preconditioners to converge.

entry.title: Iterative Policy Refinement through Semantic Rollout Analysis

author.name: Feiyu Gavin Zhu, Qi Xu, Zhifei Deng, Zhigang Hua, Luke Simon, Jean Oh, Reid Simmons

entry.summary: Proposes a closed-loop framework that iteratively refines structured imitation-learning policies by logging rollouts as semantically meaningful tabular data and prompting an LLM to generate diagnostic analysis code, correcting policy suboptimalities without human instruction. Demonstrated on car racing and door-opening tasks.

entry.title: MIRTO: a registration-gated, multiverse-tested evaluation protocol for unsupervised anomaly segmentation in brain MRI

author.name: Negin Kafee Hernashki, Soumick Chatterjee

entry.summary: MIRTO is an evaluation protocol for unsupervised anomaly detection in brain MRI that makes implicit methodological choices explicit, gating comparisons with registration checks, validating thresholds on validation data alone, and repeating comparisons across 15,552 defensible pipelines with paired bootstrap tests. It exposes how fragile standard single-score rankings are to undisclosed evaluation choices.

entry.title: How Far is Adam from Natural Gradient Descent?

author.name: Vihaan Paka-Hegde

entry.summary: The paper analyzes Adam's full update rule, including momentum, as a diagonal empirical Fisher approximation subject to truncation, label substitution, and temporal lag, and measures its geometric deviation from true natural gradient descent across four loss landscapes. Deviation is context-dependent: low in well-conditioned settings but rising significantly under ill-conditioning. This clarifies long-standing geometric questions about the field's default optimizer.

entry.title: Energy Time-Series Imputation with Differentially Private Diffusion Models via Clipping-Aware Objective Conditioning

author.name: Huizhen Huang, Yu Li, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: This work trains diffusion models with DP-SGD for imputing missing measurements in sensitive energy time series, identifying that low-SNR late timesteps under cosine schedules produce gradients that are disproportionately clipped, degrading the retained learning signal. The proposed clipping-aware objective conditioning mitigates this objective-clipping interaction. It contributes to the underexplored intersection of private generative modeling and time-series imputation.

entry.title: M$^2$Weather: A Benchmark for Joint Multi-Station and Multi-Variable Weather Forecasting

author.name: Rongwen Li, Xiao Wang, Mingyang Wang, Hongwu Liu, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: M2Weather is a benchmark for station-based weather forecasting that jointly models multi-station spatial dependencies and multi-variable physical coupling, offering 2,809 quality-controlled stations and five coupled variables at France, Europe, and Global scales. The multi-scale design enables testing whether conclusions about spatial and physical interactions transfer across geographies. It fills a gap created by fragmented datasets and settings in prior station-forecasting studies.

entry.title: The Conflict Between Logic and Memory: Learning Higher-Order Interactions in Shallow MLPs

author.name: Gongyue Zhang, Honghai Liu

entry.summary: This paper dissects when shallow MLPs fit training data versus recover the generating rule, using synthetic tasks that control interaction order and nuisance inputs. It finds sharp optimizer-dependent breakdowns: at order three, SGD, Adam, and Muon reach 96.25%, 50.87%, and 76.82% test accuracy respectively, with Muon reaching 99.21% at higher order, revealing a logic-versus-memory optimization conflict. The results carry lessons for optimizer choice and grokking-style rule learning.

entry.title: IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs

author.name: Pietro Moriello, Pietro Buzzega, Angelo Porrello, Simone Calderara

entry.summary: IrekoGPT converts pretrained LLMs into slimmable models whose width can be tuned at inference time by retaining SliceGPT projection matrices and exposing nested subnetworks. It calibrates layers across multiple compression ratios and corrects downstream layers via gradient-free ridge regression, improving on naive PCA-based slimming for Llama and Qwen models.

entry.title: TrueMuse: A Benchmark for Data Attribution in Text-to-Music Models

author.name: Jiawei Yu, Jian Liu

entry.summary: TrueMuse is a controlled benchmark for evaluating data attribution methods in text-to-music generation, built by fine-tuning three diffusion-based models on curated samples with known inclusion, providing ground-truth attribution targets. It covers four attribution settings and enables rigorous assessment of whether attribution methods actually identify influential training samples.

entry.title: Fully Online Decentralized Learning in Stochastic Games with Unknown Independent Chains

author.name: S. Rasoul Etesami

entry.summary: This paper develops a fully online, decentralized mirror-descent algorithm operating in the dual space of occupancy measures to approximate stationary Nash equilibria in stochastic games with unknown transition kernels and only local observations. It uses a single sample per time step, needs no coverage of the joint state space or synchronized episodes, and achieves canonical O(T^-1/2) fixed-comparator regret under standard assumptions. This advances the theory of decentralized multi-agent learning under weak information.

entry.title: AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models

author.name: Arash Lagzian, Paniz Halvachi, Junming Zhang, Zhouhan Lin, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: AF-Muon removes the AdamW auxiliary optimizer from the standard Muon recipe for tied-embedding language models, using a support-aware finite-difference-style update for the tied vocabulary table while keeping spectral-norm Muon updates for hidden matrices. This eliminates second-moment state for these blocks and treats the mixed sparse/dense gradient structure of tied tables explicitly.

entry.title: MiLoop: Selective Memory Propagation for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Changliang Zhou, Yuanyao Chen, Rongsheng Chen, Zhiyun Lin, Zhenkun Wang

entry.summary: MiLoop is a purely reinforcement-learning-based constructive framework for neural combinatorial optimization that reuses multi-step computation via selective memory propagation instead of rebuilding subproblem representations from scratch at each step. This avoids reliance on solution labels, pseudo-labels, or aggressive search-space pruning used by prior high-performing methods.

entry.title: Inferring Multi-Timescale Neural Dynamics with Switching Linear Dynamical Systems

author.name: Lulu Gong, Yongxu Zhang, Shreya Saxena

entry.summary: The paper develops switching linear dynamical system methods to identify multiple timescales in high-dimensional neural population recordings, addressing the failure of autocorrelation-based approaches to scale or remain reliable when dynamics change with behavior. This enables better recovery of temporal structure in neural activity across behavioral states.

entry.title: Graph Representation via Elements of Discrete Morse and Cobordism Theories

author.name: Jennifer Rozenblit, Chenguang Yang, Yuxin Liu, Yuzhou Chen, Yulia Gel

entry.summary: This paper imports tools from low-dimensional topology, specifically cobordism and discrete Morse theory, to improve graph diffusion models via a pipeline called MG-Diff, with theoretical guarantees. It argues topological structure can reveal hidden structure in data-generating processes beyond conventional topological data analysis.

entry.title: Symmetry Discovery in Quantum Learning: Observable-Level and Task-Level Inference from Finite Measurements

author.name: Zeyu Chen

entry.summary: The paper establishes a finite-measurement theory for inferring symmetry groups in quantum learning, identifying observable-invisible transformations with the stabilizer of a projected state and providing an unbiased shadow statistic with inverse-gap measurement rates. It connects group-theoretic structure to practical quantum learning constraints.

entry.title: Fractional Laplace Neural Operators: Exact Architectures, an Expressivity Frontier at Criticality, and Certified Stability for Memory-Driven Network Dynamics

author.name: Mauricio Herrera-Mar\'in

entry.summary: This theory-heavy paper introduces fractional Laplace neural operators (fLNOs) that embed Volterra resolvent memory dynamics with non-rational Laplace symbols into learned operators, achieving exact representation for commuting excitation-Laplacian pairs. It proves an expressivity frontier: finite rational approximations cannot reproduce non-integer critical asymptotics from branch points. The theory also yields certified stability parametrizations.

entry.title: Crossing the Cyber Divide: Sim-to-Sim and Sim-to-Real Transfer for RL Agents

author.name: Sabrina Saika, Yinuo Du, Aritran Piplai

entry.summary: The paper studies transfer of reinforcement learning cyber-attack agents across heterogeneous simulators, unifying simulator-to-simulator and simulator-to-real transfer as a single state-alignment and action-translation problem. This allows policies trained in one cyber environment to operate in another without retraining. It addresses a real barrier to deploying and fairly comparing RL-based security agents.

entry.title: RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search

author.name: Chuxuan Hu, Hejie Cui, Norman Huang, Shubham Kumar Bharti, Wang-Chiew Tan, Sercan \"O. Ar{\i}k

entry.summary: RPTune targets catalog search for small merchants by coupling learned curation of which catalog items to present in an LLM context with LLM post-training on automatically generated, catalog-grounded data. It shows that full-catalog prompting underutilizes long contexts and that curation plus tuning improves product selection.

entry.title: Training-Free Diffusion Planning with Analytical Local Scores

author.name: Michael Y. Fatemi, Jinhao Liang, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: This paper presents a training-free diffusion-based motion planner that replaces learned trajectory score functions with analytical local scores, removing the need for large collections of feasible demonstrations that make prior diffusion planners map-specific. It targets smooth, goal-directed, collision-free trajectories for path finding and multi-robot motion planning. This improves deployability of diffusion planners in new environments.

entry.title: Metric-Construction Coupling Inflates Measured Synthetic Dialect Recovery

author.name: Hyojung Han (ThakiCloud)

entry.summary: The paper introduces KoDialectBench, a 1,000-item Korean dialect benchmark released as identifier hashes plus scoring code so users reconstruct items from their own licensed copies, sidestepping redistribution restrictions. It finds synthetic-data recovery of real dialect supervision is strongly axis-dependent (91.2% on region identification but 63.7% on comprehension) and shows metric choice inflates apparent recovery on generation tasks.

entry.title: Precision over Scale: A Polish-Silesian Benchmark and a Translation System Outperforming Open-Source and Commercial Models

author.name: Grzegorz Kulik, Miko{\l}aj Pokrywka, Adam Jatowt, Wojciech Kusa

entry.summary: This paper addresses dialectal machine translation for Polish-Silesian, releasing SiLTT, a new testset, and evaluating neural and rule-based systems against BOUQuET and FLORES benchmarks. A rule-based system consistently outperformed strong neural and commercial models on dialectal translation, and a fine-tuned TranslateGemma improved over neural baselines without surpassing the rule-based approach. Resources are released to support further research.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning in Text Classification

author.name: Rey Sanchez Lopez, Eduardo Morales Manzanares, Hugo Jair Escalante

entry.summary: TORA is a geometric routing framework that uses the low-rank structure of LoRA adapters to decide whether to transfer knowledge from the most compatible prior expert or isolate a new task, addressing catastrophic forgetting and negative transfer in continual text classification. Evaluated across 15 benchmarks. It makes adapter reuse principled rather than ad hoc.

entry.title: Do Multilingual Encoders Produce Language-Consistent Semantic IDs?

author.name: Abhinav Bohra, Anuj Bohra

entry.summary: Using Amazon ESCI listings rendered in English, Spanish, and Japanese, the paper shows multilingual encoders place translations measurably apart, with Japanese translations preserving the first semantic ID code of their English source in only 7.7% of cases under English-heavy quantizer fitting. It tests whether multilingual or language-balanced quantization improves SID agreement for generative retrieval. Exposes a concrete failure mode in multilingual generative retrieval.

entry.title: Vmem-$\varphi$: Low-Compute Out-of-Distribution Detection in Spiking Neural Networks from Membrane-Potential Statistics

author.name: Arul Rana, Agrim Tripathi, Shoaib Ahmed Dipu, Md. Shaown Miah, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury

entry.summary: This paper shows that subthreshold membrane potential statistics in spiking neural networks provide a cheap internal signal for OOD detection in event-camera processing, avoiding dependencies on outputs unavailable in detection SNNs. It also introduces Gen1-C, an event-camera corruption benchmark built on the Prophesee Gen1 automotive dataset. The work supports reliable, energy-efficient neuromorphic deployment.

entry.title: Machine Translation for Sign Languages

author.name: Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Anton Pelykh, Edward Fish, Harry Walsh, JianHe Low, Karahan Sahin, Oline Ranum, Sobhan Asasi, Steven Emery, Richard Bowden

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive review of sign language machine translation covering progress from isolated sign recognition to end-to-end translation, including pose estimation, transformers, and dataset efforts. It also discusses linguistic properties of sign languages, evaluation metric shortcomings, and stakeholder considerations for the Deaf community.

entry.title: HierGF: Hierarchical Gaussian Fields via Geometry-perception Message Passing for Sparse-view 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Bi'an Du, Zhimin Zhang, Daizong Liu, Baoquan Chen, Wei Hu

entry.summary: HierGF proposes hierarchical Gaussian fields with geometry-perception message passing to improve sparse-view 3D reconstruction, addressing limited multi-view consistency and missing structure in under-sampled regions. It targets AR/VR, cultural heritage, and robotic application scenarios.

entry.title: Resolving Mixed Single-Photon LiDAR Returns for Foreground-View and Hidden Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Ziting Wen, Runrong Deng, Zili Zhang, Haitao Zheng, Yuecong Xu, Xiaoqiang Ren, Guodong Shi, Kemi Ding

entry.summary: This paper tackles the problem of mixed LiDAR returns caused by partially transmissive surfaces such as screens and covers in robotic inspection. It reconstructs both the foreground and hidden scene from single-photon LiDAR histograms, showing that accurate transient fitting does not guarantee correct geometry when overlapping echoes are ambiguous. The authors frame the ambiguity problem explicitly and resolve foreground-view and hidden-scene reconstruction jointly.

entry.title: CLASP: Continual Low-rank Adapters for Spatially Placed Concepts from One Hypernetwork

author.name: Wojciech Gromski, Patryk Krukowski, Jan Miksa, Maciej Zieba, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: CLASP enables continual personalization of text-to-image diffusion models using a single fixed-size hypernetwork that generates concept-specific LoRA adaptations on demand, rather than storing growing per-concept parameters. The rehearsal-free approach counters catastrophic forgetting while keeping the parameter footprint constant over long concept streams. This addresses scalability limits of existing continual personalization methods.

entry.title: Revisiting Cross-Reconstruction for Generalizable Deepfake Detection

author.name: Bingjian Yang, Shilei Zhao, Zheng Wang

entry.summary: The authors revisit cross-reconstruction approaches for deepfake detection and argue prior methods suppress artifact diversity by excluding artifact representations during reconstruction. They propose an artifact-oriented disentanglement framework that preserves manipulation-artifact cues to improve generalization to unseen forgery generators.

entry.title: MEGA: Object-Level Mesh Extraction from 3D Gaussian Splatting via Spatial Visual Distillation

author.name: Liwei Liao, Yingkui Zhang, Qianqian Tong, Ronggang Wang

entry.summary: MEGA is a segment-then-mesh framework that extracts object-level, watertight meshes from complex 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes. Its Spatial Visual Distillation treats the 3DGS model as a teacher and, combined with mask-guided neural surface reconstruction, addresses the non-watertight surfaces and lack of object occupancy in scene-level mesh extraction methods.

entry.title: A2Z GameSpec-Bench: How Faithfully Can Coding Agents Generate Games from Game Design Specifications?

author.name: Seonho Lee, Wonryeol Jeong, Alberto Cereser, Inha Kang, Hyeonjong Kim, Seungmin Kwak, Dongmin Park

entry.summary: A2Z GameSpec-Bench is a benchmark of 100 long-form Game Design Documents for evaluating end-to-end game development by coding agents, measuring whether generated games satisfy interdependent requirements across game logic, rendering, and player interactions. It addresses the limitation of existing game-development benchmarks that use compact specifications.

entry.title: LensBridge: Frequency-Guided Compound Degradation Adaptation for Lens Aberration Correction and Veiling Glare Removal

author.name: Xiaolong Qian, Zhonghua Yi, Qi Jiang, Kailun Yang, Shuhang Xie, Shaohua Gao, Kaiwei Wang

entry.summary: LensBridge is a two-stage framework that first builds a reusable aberration-correction foundation model from a large-scale Lens Library of point spread functions, then adapts it to compound degradations (aberrations plus veiling glare) using only a few unpaired target observations. This makes realistic optical correction deployable for simplified camera systems. It matters because compound degradation pairs are rarely available for real target systems.

entry.title: Spiking neural networks for streaming qubit readout

author.name: Barry M. Dillon, Aqib Javed, Jim Harkin, Patryk Dabkowski, Benjamin Lienhard

entry.summary: This paper introduces spiking neural network discriminators for superconducting qubit readout, processing measurement windows in successive time chunks so classification scores update as data arrive rather than at window end. The SNNs exploit temporal structure including crosstalk and relaxation events that conventional matched filtering misses, and outperform matched filtering. This connects neuromorphic computing to quantum processor feedback and error correction.

entry.title: Measuring Asset and Scene Reconstruction Effects in Real-to-Sim Robot Evaluation

author.name: Sanya Verma, Luca Cilio, Velissarios Christodoulou

entry.summary: The paper tests whether a carefully authored real-to-sim reconstruction pipeline — metrically scaled object geometry, authored physics, and scene splatting — reduces disagreement between simulated and real robot evaluation scores compared to a default open-source recipe. It builds two simulated versions of a bimanual robot cell and compares score correlation with the real cell. This quantifies how much simulation fidelity actually matters for credible sim-based policy evaluation.

entry.title: Experience-Based Feasibility-Aware Generative Adversarial Imitation from Observation under Embodiment Mismatch

author.name: Yoshiki Takebayashi, Giovanni Perantoni, Hikaru Sasaki, Matteo Saveriano, Takamitsu Matsubara

entry.summary: EF-GAIfO addresses imitation from observation when human demonstrations are infeasible for the robot due to embodiment and dynamics mismatch. It estimates demonstration feasibility from the robot's own experience rather than explicit dynamics models or large exploration datasets, within a generative adversarial imitation framework. This makes action-free human demonstration data usable even across embodiment gaps.

entry.title: Learning a Resolution-Consistent Jacobian Field for Bio-Inspired Rigid-Soft Finger

author.name: Tianyou Liang, Haisen Zeng, Shanjun Chen, YiMing Zhu, Zhongyue Lu, Zirong Luo

entry.summary: Proposes Jacobian Flow Matching, a framework using Conditional Flow Matching to learn a resolution-consistent Jacobian field for tendon-driven rigid-soft dexterous fingers, modeling actuation-to-motion transitions as a dynamical flow. Supports both single-step prediction and continuous rollout via ODE integration, reducing sensitivity to sensor and controller frequencies. Targets the strong nonlinearity of hybrid rigid-soft fingers.

entry.title: GlassGuard: Verified Glass Plane Mapping for Robot Navigation

author.name: Hanwen Guo, Zhengzhi Lin, Yusen Xie, Ji Zhang

entry.summary: GlassGuard tackles the problem that transparent glass surfaces are invisible to LiDAR, causing robots to miss collision boundaries in SLAM maps, while naive reconstruction can wrongly mark traversable space as obstacles. The framework reconstructs planar glass using complementary visual and LiDAR evidence, leveraging a foundation vision model for glass-instance detection, and explicitly optimizes both glass coverage and free-space contamination during verification and global map construction.

entry.title: Multifidelity Formulations for Triangular Transport

author.name: Owen Davis, Daniel Sharp, Youssef Marzouk, Gianluca Geraci

entry.summary: This paper develops multifidelity methods for constructing triangular transport maps when high-fidelity samples are scarce but lower-fidelity data are abundant, using either hierarchical composition across fidelity levels or non-hierarchical monotonicity-preserving corrections. Numerical experiments show the proposed strategies outperform single-fidelity transport. This is relevant for expensive simulation settings like engineering design and uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: What Do Rationales Communicate? A Message-Intervention Study in Role-Specialized QA

author.name: Jiameng Zhang, Hongqiu Wu

entry.summary: This controlled intervention study fixes evidence and candidate answers while varying only the rationale passed from a reasoner to a verifier in multi-hop QA pipelines. It finds faithful rationales add almost no answer accuracy, but corrupted rationales shift verifier support judgments by 10-22%, revealing that rationales act as a new failure surface rather than a capability gain.

entry.title: Auditing Action Settlement in LLM Agent Environments: Order, Progress, and Replay

author.name: Haotian Chen, Bowen Ye, Yuning Zhang, Jingkun Yu

entry.summary: Implements a typed snapshot-settlement contract for concurrent actions in LLM agent environments and audits order sensitivity, useful progress, and replay consistency across five settlement policies in 28,800 exhaustive permutation trials and 2,160 scripted episodes. Finds conservative rejection completes only 31.25% of agents in a six-agent doorway task versus 90.28% for random tickets. Rigorous, unusually thorough systems evaluation of an overlooked concurrency problem.

entry.title: CoEvolve: Construct-to-Edit Visual Grounding with Bidirectional State Refinement

author.name: Dongwei Sun, Yujie Zhang, Bowen Yao, Pei Liu, Jing Yao, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: CoEvolve reframes visual grounding as explicit state construction followed by state editing, rather than a single terminal prediction. Region-Evolution Reinforcement organizes grounding analysis into a progressive semantic-spatial trajectory, making intermediate localization errors measurable and correctable so wrong region choices and imprecise boundaries do not persist into the final box. This improves diagnosability of multimodal grounding reasoning.

entry.title: When the AI Leaves the Tailorshop: Measuring What an LLM Advisor Leaves Behind in Complex Problem Solving

author.name: Robin Welsch

entry.summary: Two preregistered experiments (N=200 in the first) examine what remains after an LLM advisor is withdrawn during complex problem solving in a simulated factory task. AI-supported participants showed greater confidence and subjective understanding, and after withdrawal outperformed controls on some measures, with more frequent alteration of recommendations predicting better unaided performance.

entry.title: No One Architecture Fits All: A Cross-Environment Evaluation of Hierarchical Red Team Agents

author.name: Ayan Javeed Shaikh, Arunesh Sinha, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Ankit Shah

entry.summary: The paper presents a controlled cross-environment comparison of two hierarchical red team agent architectures, RL planner with RL executor versus LLM planner variants, to determine whether observed advantages reflect general decision quality or environment-specific alignment. It addresses the common practice of developing and evaluating autonomous red teaming architectures in a single environment. Findings indicate that no single architecture dominates across settings.

entry.title: Selection-Based Structured Reasoning: Toward Efficient Multimodal Search Agents

author.name: Feiyu Gavin Zhu, Xiaoyu Zhu, Jiqi Yang, Rui Yang, Arnab Kumar Mondal, Yancheng Wang, Xinke Deng, Jean Oh, Reid Simmons, Joerg Liebelt, Xiang Kong, Zhongyu Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces Selection-based Structured Reasoning (SSR), which reformulates agent reasoning as selecting from pre-specified reusable natural-language reasoning candidates scored by likelihood, rather than free-form generation, enabling parallel scoring and lower inference cost. Aimed at small multimodal models where verbose reasoning provides little guidance.

entry.title: EvoGen-Harness: Learning Where and How to Evolve Image-Generation Harnesses

author.name: Jiabin Luo, Yinan Liu, Chunlei Meng, Yufei Guo

entry.summary: EvoGen-Harness is a generator-agnostic framework that evolves the external harness around a frozen text-to-image generator across multiple responsibilities (prompts, routing, workflows) rather than optimizing a single predefined dimension. It introduces Trace, a trajectory-based method to decide where persistent evolution should occur and how to explore the space efficiently given only visual failure feedback. This improves image generation quality without touching generator weights.

entry.title: Analysis of Quantized and Efficiently Adapted Protein Language Models

author.name: Ilan Yaniv Zeisler, Sebastian Clancy, Pouriya Bayat, Saaim Raad, Ivan Kraskov, Matthew Xie, Vivian White, Spencer Perkins, Serena Singh, Sepehr Bayat, Keith Pardee

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates QLoRA (4-bit quantization plus low-rank adapters) across seven protein language models including ESM-2, ProtT5, Ankh, and Profluent-E1. Many model-task pairs retain over 90% of full fine-tuning performance with GPU memory savings approaching 90%, though effects vary by model and task.

entry.title: Sharpen Before You Adapt: Data-Free Entry-State Sharpening for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhanming Zhang, Vinoth Selvendran

entry.summary: The paper proposes preparing LLM checkpoints with data-free training before test-time reinforcement learning, so the policy starts from a sharper state whose self-supervision is less noisy. Across five datasets, this entry-state sharpening improves the efficiency of label-free adaptation regardless of the specific data-free objective used.

entry.title: Low-Budget Active Learning through Entropic Optimal Transport

author.name: Rim Hajal, Mathieu Besan\c{c}on, J\'er\^ome Malick

entry.summary: The paper tackles low-budget active learning, selecting a small coreset from which a model can be trained to high accuracy, a setting relevant when labeling requires costly expert input such as in medical applications. It performs coreset selection in the feature space of a pretrained self-supervised model using Sinkhorn divergence, which yields dimension-free sample complexity results and efficient gradient computation. This connects modern SSL representations with optimal transport theory.

entry.title: QK-Wanda: Coupling Queries and Keys for Unstructured Pruning

author.name: Ivan Ilin, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: QK-Wanda improves LLM pruning by scoring query and key weights jointly via their deletion costs under an unmasked pre-RoPE reconstruction objective, augmenting Wanda scores with information from the opposite projection and sharing a pruning budget. The closed-form, gradient-free scores add minimal overhead (1.3-3.1 percent runtime) and are evaluated across 15 models including TinyLlama and Llama variants.

entry.title: Physics-Refined Spatiotemporal Forecasting on Open-Boundary Hydrologic Graphs

author.name: Haoyang Jiang, Zhengui Wang, Shenghan Gao, Y. Joseph Zhang, Xingquan Zhu, Yi He

entry.summary: This paper analyzes instability in spatiotemporal forecasting on open-boundary hydrologic systems, where unobserved external forcing (upstream inflows, tidal signals) enters the forecast domain and compounds errors in autoregressive prediction. It proposes physics-refined methods for handling missing boundary forcing and propagating it through the domain for long-horizon forecasting.

entry.title: Bellman Meets Lyapunov: Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning via Mastering Chaos

author.name: Tristan Shah, Wooyoung Chung, Volodomyr Makarenko, Juan Wachs, Stas Tiomkin

entry.summary: The paper introduces Forward CIP, an RL-native formulation of Controllable Information Production for unsupervised RL, defined purely by system dynamics without human selection of information variables. The authors prove RL compatibility and demonstrate the objective, which draws on chaos-theoretic quantities, as intrinsic motivation.

entry.title: Paying for Too Many Tokens? Valid and Cost-Efficient Multimodal LLM Annotation with Simple Heuristics

author.name: Zhixi Zhu, Kristina Gligoric

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates cost-saving heuristics for VLM-based video annotation (frame subsampling, image grids, single-modality input) on sentiment and topic classification tasks, assessing accuracy, cost, and preservation of downstream conclusions. It clarifies which heuristics actually save money without invalidating computational social science findings. Practically useful for anyone doing large-scale video annotation.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Guided Handshake: Efficient Human-in-the-Loop Refinement for Surgical-Grade Glioma Segmentation

author.name: Samuel Hart, Ahmad Yahya, Ahmed Karam Eldaly

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid structural-aleatoric human-in-the-loop framework for glioma segmentation that uses uncertainty to route cases needing clinician review rather than requiring manual error hunting. It achieves sub-2.0mm HD95 on curated benchmarks while providing safety-net routing for structural failures. The design reduces clinician cognitive load compared to traditional interactive segmentation.

entry.title: EvenSplat: Coupled 2D-3D Decomposition for Gaussian Splatting under Exposure and Illumination Variation

author.name: Tongyu Wu, Jacob Edwards, Ziteng Cui, Caigui Jiang, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: EvenSplat addresses the entanglement of capture-specific illumination with geometry in 3D Gaussian Splatting by coupling an image-space illumination decomposition with an illumination field carried by the Gaussians. This shared explanation of lighting separates intrinsic scene properties from exposure and illumination variation across views.

entry.title: Ex vivo breach detection using electrical conductivity during robotic pedicle drilling in the spine

author.name: Jorge Andr\'es P\'erez Vel\'asquez, Fran\c{c}ois Teyssere, Thibault Chandanson, Quentin Grimal, Brahim Tamadazte

entry.summary: This study develops robotic pedicle drilling for scoliosis treatment with real-time preventive breach detection using an electrical bioimpedance sensor integrated into the drilling tool, avoiding reliance on ionizing intraoperative imaging and complex registration. A real-time algorithm analyzes bioimpedance signals during drilling to identify abnormal conditions signaling bone breach. Validated ex vivo, it targets precision and complication risk in demanding spinal surgery.

entry.title: Heavy-Tailed Memory Traces in Long-Horizon Language Agents

author.name: Xinyuan Song, Zekun Cai

entry.summary: This paper studies how external memory in long-horizon language agents concentrates on a small core of states while rare states accumulate prediction errors in a long tail. The authors introduce a conservative tail audit showing that concentration is reproducible but policy-dependent, with semantic LLM policies producing truncated-power-law core-tail traces, and propose a Core-Tail World Model as a remedy.

entry.title: Mathematical Transfer in LLMs Follows Reasoning Approach More Than Topic

author.name: Sajad Goudarzi, Samaneh Zamanifard, Seyed Amin Seyed Haeri, Moloud Nasiri, Hamed Rahimian

entry.summary: Using counterbalanced 2x2 designs crossing mathematical topics with reasoning approaches (2,000 and 800 problems), the paper asks whether same-topic or same-approach training data transfers better after fine-tuning. It finds that shared reasoning approach produces greater transfer than shared topic, suggesting training data curation should organize by solution method rather than domain.

entry.title: When Harnesses Lose the Signal: Causal Evaluation of Recovery in LLM Agents

author.name: Shuyao Xiao, Shengling Wang, Xuan Chen, Ke Chao, Ming Cui, Feifei Qian, Chaoyang Mei, Fanlin Meng, Ziming Yu, Junxi Yin

entry.summary: The paper frames harness-mediated error recovery in LLM agents as a causal decision problem, comparing matched execution states with and without recovery to separate rescues from harms and track how recovery value changes over time. It introduces the Causal Intervention Router (CIR), a lightweight pre-recovery policy deciding when intervention is worthwhile, evaluated on long-horizon ALFWorld-style tasks.

entry.title: Ontology-Grounded, Reasoner-Verified Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Reasoning in Scientific AI

author.name: Nishtha N. Vaidya, Stephan Grimm, Thomas Hubauer, Thomas A. Runkler

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline that automatically generates ontology-grounded multiple-choice benchmarks from any sufficiently axiomatized knowledge domain, with both correct and incorrect answer options verified by a standard reasoner. This avoids the scaling limits of manual dataset construction and the self-flaw risk of LLM-generated benchmarks. It targets evaluation of LLM reasoning over structured scientific knowledge.

entry.title: Beyond Answer Confidence: A Controlled Audit of Self-Knowledge in a Black-Box Decision Model

author.name: Sharath M Shankaranarayana, Davor Runje, Jan Jannink

entry.summary: Audits whether calibration reflects genuine self-knowledge in Jev, a black-box decision model, using paired interventions across 15+ datasets and generated task families. Finding: confidence is calibrated on familiar closed-choice tasks but is a poor indicator of missing knowledge, assigning up to 0.80 to a salient option with no answer-relevant information and remaining overconfident beyond knowledge boundaries. Important for anyone using model confidence for abstention or routing.

entry.title: Improving Math Reasoning through Value-guided Informative Search

author.name: Shaohuai Liu, Yuning Wu, Haoran Liu, Enzo Jia, Devin Chen, Kai Wei

entry.summary: Proposes APIVIS, a training-time RLVR framework that adapts finite-budget Gumbel search to chunk-level mathematical reasoning, mixing direct and searched responses in rollout groups so search-induced improvements yield informative relative rewards, plus selective supervision on search-improved tokens. Addresses the issue that diversity from search alone does not guarantee policy improvement. Incremental but competent advance in RLVR for math reasoning.

entry.title: ProtoFlow: Prototype-Guided Flow Matching for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Shibo Feng, Wanjin Feng, Yang Qiu, Deheng Ye, Peilin Zhao, Chunyan Miao

entry.summary: ProtoFlow applies prototype-guided flow matching to multivariate time series forecasting, combining vector-quantized discrete latent representations with non-autoregressive flow matching to avoid exposure bias and training-inference mismatch of autoregressive token generation, while remaining more efficient than diffusion at inference.

entry.title: The AI Assessment Sandbox Configurator: A Framework to Support Technical Assessment in AI Regulatory Sandboxes

author.name: Alessio Buscemi, German Castignani, Daniele Pagani, Maxime Cordy, Jordi Cabot

entry.summary: Motivated by the EU AI Act's requirement that all Member States establish AI Regulatory Sandboxes by August 2027, this paper derives 11 architectural and governance requirements for infrastructure supporting structured technical testing in sandboxes. It presents a configurator framework to address the fragmented tooling ecosystem whose heterogeneous outputs are hard to compare, trace, and reuse. The work bridges regulatory procedure and practical technical assessment infrastructure.

entry.title: VideoEvolve: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Bingjun Luo, Yuhuan Fan, Jialin Guo, Siqi Li

entry.summary: VideoEvolve automatically evolves agent harnesses around frozen video-language models for video temporal grounding, using a Cloze-Structured Harness Representation that preserves stage interfaces while allowing workflows and instructions to evolve. Branch-Guided Harness Evolution preserves promising code branches for continued refinement, replacing manual diagnosis of grounding failures and coordination of workflow and instruction changes. This applies automated harness engineering to a concrete video task.

entry.title: On-Device Named-Entity Recognition: A Deployability Study of Accuracy, Cost, Reliability, and Confidence

author.name: Vinay Kumar Chaganti

entry.summary: A practitioner-oriented comparison of nine on-device NER systems across three paradigms (classical taggers, encoder specialists like GLiNER, and small local generative LLMs) covering accuracy, latency, output validity, and confidence calibration. It addresses how to evaluate NER without human annotation by constructing silver gold labels from cross-family model agreement.

entry.title: BudgetSchemaBench: A Budget-Swept Diagnostic for Schema Context in Text-to-SQL

author.name: Chen Shen

entry.summary: BudgetSchemaBench is an execution-grounded diagnostic for text-to-SQL under schema-context budget constraints, where systems must trade table coverage against serialization detail. It derives relevance labels mechanically from gold SQL, sweeps four budgets over an 80-database catalog, and includes a source-namespace check to reject correct results obtained from the wrong database.

entry.title: Authorization for Self-Modifying AI Agent Populations: Conserving Authority across Replacement, Forking, and Rollback

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes authorization succession for populations of self-modifying AI agents that replace, fork, or roll back identity-bearing software, showing that per-successor authorization fails to constrain the resulting population (siblings duplicating quotas, permissions combining, surviving ancestor cuts). It proposes an external protocol with manifests, lineage invariants, and staged reservation of residual authority.

entry.title: Manifold-Constrained Initial Noise Optimization for Efficient Generative Model Alignment

author.name: Jinho Chang, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Introduces ZeNOVA, a gradient-free method for aligning one-step or few-step generative models by optimizing the initial noise, using annealed soft-value guidance and manifold-constrained hyperspherical Langevin dynamics to overcome instability in black-box reward scenarios. This extends reward alignment to distilled and flow-map generators where first-order gradient methods are inapplicable or inefficient.

entry.title: Faithful Chart Generation for Multimodal Deep Research: Frame-Evidence Co-Adaptation

author.name: Yuxin Yue, Yingchen Zhang, Ruqing Zhang, Jiafeng Guo, Maarten de Rijke, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Addresses numerical fidelity in charts generated by multimodal deep research systems, where visualization plans made before evidence retrieval can demand data that retrieved evidence only partially supports. It proposes frame-evidence co-adaptation so that chart plans and retrieved quantitative evidence are mutually adjusted, ensuring visualized values are grounded in meaning-preserving evidence.

entry.title: Interpretable Synthetic Medical Tabular Data Generation for Clinical Decision Support Using Fuzzy Cognitive Maps

author.name: Michael Vasilakakis (Department of Computer Science and Biomedical Informatics, University of Thessaly, Lamia, Greece), Dimitris K. Iakovidis (Department of Computer Science and Biomedical Informatics, University of Thessaly, Lamia, Greece)

entry.summary: This paper proposes using Fuzzy Cognitive Maps to generate synthetic medical tabular data with explicit causal structure and privacy preservation, addressing the limits of probabilistic and deep generative models that lack interpretability and fail to preserve clinically meaningful dependencies. The approach encodes clinical features as linguistically interpretable fuzzy sets with inter-feature dependencies as FCM edge weights. It targets the growing need for safe synthetic data when real clinical data is restricted by privacy or availability constraints.

entry.title: ALER: Adaptive Learnable Experience Rewriting for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Oleg Shchendrigin, Egor Cherepanov, Aleksandr I. Panov, Alexey K. Kovalev

entry.summary: This paper formalizes two underexplored memory requirements in partially observable RL beyond retention: rewriting (setting decision-relevant content independent of its old value) and experience fusion (transforming old content by an observation-specified rule). The authors count the memory states solutions need, show baselines fail on compositions requiring more states, and introduce ALER, an adaptive learnable experience-rewriting agent. The contribution sharpens what memory in POMDP agents should do.

entry.title: Increasing Width Allows Greedy Layer-wise Training to Rival End-to-End Backpropagation in Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Syon Mansur, Joel Zylberberg

entry.summary: This study investigates the architectural conditions under which locally optimized networks that avoid end-to-end backpropagation can match backprop-trained representations, focusing on self-supervised learning. The authors show that sufficiently increasing network width allows greedy layer-wise training to rival end-to-end backpropagation. This has implications for biologically plausible learning and memory-efficient training alternatives.

entry.title: Jev-IDS: System One Models for Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Paulo Severo, Silvio E. Quincozes, Amanda Dias

entry.summary: JEV-IDS applies a specialized small model (Jev System One Model) to network intrusion detection, serializing flow records and asking binary attack-probability and traffic-category questions under label scarcity. Reported results show the approach is 4.8x faster, 3.8x cheaper, and achieves 1.5x higher novel-attack recall than GPT-5.6 Luna (an established OpenAI model released mid-2026). It targets zero-day detection with constrained outputs.

entry.title: Federated Learning for LLMs over Mobile Networks: Issues and Solutions in the RAN Transport

author.name: Emilio Paolini, Andrea Pinto, Flavio Esposito, Luca Valcarenghi

entry.summary: This paper examines how federated fine-tuning of LLMs creates deadline-sensitive, structured communication workloads over mobile radio access networks, where conventional transport treats correlated model updates as independent flows. The authors analyze this mismatch, which is especially problematic for optical transport provisioning, and propose solutions that exploit the shared structure of updates within a learning round.

entry.title: Managing Context and Communication in Distributed Agentic UAV Swarms

author.name: Andrea Iannoli, Ivan Zyrianoff, Angelo Trotta, Lorenzo Gigli, Marco Di Felice

entry.summary: This paper presents a distributed UAV-agent architecture where each drone hosts a small language model with an event-driven reason-act-observe lifecycle, representing runtime knowledge as structured atomic notes to manage context degradation and communication overhead. It addresses the information-management problem that arises when removing centralized coordinators from language-model-driven swarms.

entry.title: Hob-VL: A Benchmark for Visually Grounded Boolean Reasoning

author.name: Yuzhou Wang, Emile Anand, Ijay Narang

entry.summary: Introduces Hob-VL, a benchmark for visually grounded Boolean reasoning with 6,000 human-verified balanced Yes/No questions, 1,000 generated scenes, 46 labeled photographs, and 1,000 object-identification questions. It tests whether models can compose multiple visual observations and answer logically equivalent questions consistently while resisting misleading local cues.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Schr\"odinger Bridge

author.name: Jinhwan Sul, Panagiotis Theodoropoulos, Vincent Pacelli, Jaemoo Choi, Evangelos Theodorou

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes the Distributionally Robust Schrodinger Bridge (DRSB), which extends Schrodinger bridges — models that learn stochastic transport between two distributions — to remain reliable when the initial distribution shifts at test time. DRSB trains a single controller minimizing a worst-case objective (control energy plus a KL penalty against the target distribution) over an ambiguity set of possible initial distributions, with an exact variational formulation derived. This matters because distribution shift is a common failure mode for generative transport models in simulation, control, and generative modeling applications.

entry.title: GeoLatent: Geometry-Guided Latent Structuring with Routed Optimization for 3D Reasoning

author.name: Yakun Zhu, Yi Bin, Yujuan Ding, Zheng Wang, Pengpeng Zeng, Duo Peng, Jingkuan Song, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: GeoLatent improves 3D spatial reasoning from 2D images by representing position, direction, and global geometry as decomposed spatial latents under geometric supervision, using Common-Residual Geometry Alignment to prevent geometry collapse and routed optimization to make attention use the latents effectively.

entry.title: Reverse Item Response Theory for Sparsity-Robust Ranking in Fragmented Cancer Drug-Response Matrices

author.name: Jung Min Kang

entry.summary: The paper applies reverse Item Response Theory to pharmacogenomics, treating cancer types as latent subjects with resistance ability and drugs as items with evasion difficulty, estimated from 242,036 GDSC2 drug-sensitivity measurements. It outperforms simple averaging in recovering full-data latent rankings under four missingness regimes, including biased sparsity. A thoughtful methodological transfer from psychometrics to computational biology.

entry.title: One Mastery Threshold Does Not Fit All Knowledge Tracing Models

author.name: Xianghui Meng, Yujing Zhang, Jionghao Lin

entry.summary: The authors audit how mastery thresholds in tutoring systems produce inconsistent advancement decisions depending on which knowledge tracing model is used, evaluating six KT models across four datasets and twelve thresholds. They find BKT is insensitive to threshold changes while neural KT models become highly selective at higher thresholds. The paper offers guidance for balancing student performance, practice burden, and equitable advancement across prior-performance groups.

entry.title: MOVE: Multimodal Open-world Verification and Expansion for Graph Learning

author.name: Zekai Chen, Jiayang Xing, Xun Wu, Miao Zhang, Xunkai Li, Kairui Yang, Zhengyu Wu, Xu Wang, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: MOVE addresses open-world multimodal graph learning, where unseen node classes emerge after deployment, by verifying whether existing classes suffice and whether LLM-generated candidate classes are reliable before expanding the label space. The paper empirically identifies three failure modes in prior approaches and proposes a verification-and-expansion framework using multimodal evidence. It improves the trustworthiness of dynamic label-space expansion for deployed graph models.

entry.title: Beyond Diagonal State Space Models: Exact Non-Abelian Group Tracking, Solvability Barriers, and Geometric Physical Manifolds

author.name: Zeyu Jia (School of Biomedical Engineering, Technology, Tianjin Medical University, Medical School, Tianjin University)

entry.summary: This paper analyzes fundamental limitations of selective state space models like Mamba, S4D, and LRU, showing their diagonal transition matrices impose commutativity constraints that degrade optimization on non-abelian structures. It proposes Non-Commutative SSMs lifting state transitions to compact Lie groups (SU(2), SO(3), SO(N)) using closed-form Euler-Rodrigues and Cayley transforms to achieve exact norm-preserving, non-commutative state updates.

entry.title: NEUROTOKEN: Joint Source and Directional AAD with Envelope Decoding via Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson

entry.summary: NEUROTOKEN unifies auditory attention decoding from EEG, previously split into directional classification, regression-based source ranking, and envelope reconstruction, by modeling the conditional likelihood of the attended speech envelope given EEG. It uses conditional flow matching to jointly support source identification, directional decoding, and envelope reconstruction, targeting 1-5 second windows needed by hearing aids and brain-computer interfaces. This is a principled probabilistic redesign of the AAD pipeline.

entry.title: Do Better Scores Mean Better Physics? Physics-Grounded Explanations for Sim2Real Neural Operators

author.name: Somyajit Chakraborty, Xizhong Chen

entry.summary: This paper probes whether lower prediction error in neural operators corresponds to better fidelity in physically relevant flow statistics, using paired CFD and particle-image-velocimetry data for flow over a NACA4418 airfoil. A mean-preserving input intervention shows sensitivity of forecasts to energetic flow regions, while carefully noting its limits as evidence of physical importance.

entry.title: From Task Mixtures to Specialized Experts

author.name: Hojat Allah Salehi, Mehrdad Mahdavi, Andrew Arash Mahyari, M. Hadi Amini

entry.summary: The paper studies federated fine-tuning with compound heterogeneity, where clients hold unknown mixtures of latent tasks over a frozen shared representation. It proves that under squared loss a client's optimal model is a convex combination of per-task optimal models, enabling decomposition of local models into specialized experts.

entry.title: Learning Goal-Reaching Quasimetric Geometry From Finite-Time Reachability

author.name: Daisuke Yamada, Travis Pence, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: ReQRL improves quasimetric learning in goal-conditioned RL by constraining the critic's value gradients through finite-horizon reachability, drawing on state-constrained optimal control. It decouples dynamical reachability from boundary geometry, estimating both from data. On OGBench, it outperforms or matches existing quasimetric and offline GCRL methods.

entry.title: Variational Streaming Flow: Probabilistic Forecasting in Physical Time

author.name: Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, Minseon Gwak, Soon Hoe Lim, Pan Li, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: VSF extends streaming flow, an efficient reformulation of flow matching that learns velocity fields directly in physical time, to probabilistic forecasting by learning a latent distribution over futures. This addresses streaming flow's deterministic limitation, producing multiple plausible trajectories for chaotic or partially observed dynamical systems at lower cost than standard flow matching.

entry.title: SLIM: Simplex-Lattice Interpolation Merging

author.name: Seongcheol Jeong, Masahiro Suzuki, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: SLIM addresses the cost of tuning merging coefficients for model merging by building a quadratic surrogate of aggregate performance on the coefficient simplex using classical mixture-design experiments. Only evaluations of individual experts and equal-weight pairs are needed to fit the surrogate, after which coefficients are optimized without further benchmark evaluations. Experiments on two architectures show competitive merges under tight evaluation budgets.

entry.title: Persistent Depth Ordering amid Shifting Block-Bypass Responses in Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Shengye Tao, Yinzhu Cheng, Haihua Xie

entry.summary: This study probes how depth-dependent intervention responses in language models evolve across pretraining, using single-block identity bypass on fixed teacher-forced contexts across five training trajectories and 11 model-domain combinations. It finds that block-bypass responses retain recognizable depth ordering even as their magnitudes redistribute, with large changes concentrated at particular positions. This distinguishes persistent representational organization from transient training artifacts.

entry.title: Minimax Optimal Regret for Causal Logistic Bandits with Counterfactual Fairness

author.name: Junhyuk Huh, Seoungbin Bae, Dabeen Lee

entry.summary: This paper studies logistic bandits with counterfactual fairness constraints where only factual rewards are observed, showing that a coverage condition is necessary — without it, factually indistinguishable environments force linear expected joint loss. Under a weaker full-rank-style coverage assumption, the authors establish minimax optimal regret with matching lower bounds, improving on prior analyses.

entry.title: Langevin-Informed Transfer Learning: Replacing Target Samples by Black-Box Feedback

author.name: Vladimir R. Kostic, Karim Lounici, H\'el\`ene Halconruy, Timoth\'ee Devergne, Michele Parrinello, Massimiliano Pontil

entry.summary: LITL is a framework for recovering target Langevin dynamics from biased source samples using only black-box feedback, learning the leading spectral structure of the target generator and projected drift via Dirichlet representation learning. It enables kinetic reconstruction in slow collective variables with applications from molecular dynamics to diffusion models.

entry.title: Artifact Annotations Partially Substitute for Per-User Calibration: SAFE-EDA and a Normalization-Controlled Evaluation of Wrist-EDA Affect Recognition

author.name: Haochen Chai, Xinbi Luo, Zining Liu, Fangfang Jiang

entry.summary: This study examines a subtle but important methodological flaw in wrist electrodermal activity affect recognition: normalization statistics computed from a held-out subject's own recording leak information unavailable at deployment time. The authors present SAFE-EDA, a compact CNN pretrained on expert artifact annotations, and show with normalization-controlled comparisons on WESAD that artifact-annotation pretraining partially substitutes for per-user calibration.

entry.title: MECHVAR: Variance-Guided Mechanism Discrimination for Autonomous Machine Learning Experiment Selection

author.name: Yifan Guo

entry.summary: MECHVAR addresses mechanism-ambiguous benchmark gains by formulating sequential experiment selection over candidate mechanisms with posterior-weighted variance maximization for choosing probes. The score is shown to be exactly proportional to the classical Box-Hill criterion under a shared-Gaussian predictive model, admits efficient vectorized rescoring, and links to expected information gain via a local expansion.

entry.title: Sim+Real: Joint Simulation - Experiment Training Improves Balanced Prediction in Physical Systems

author.name: Mahindra Rautela, Alexander Scheinker, Ayan Biswas, Diane Oyen, Nathan DeBardeleben, Earl Lawrence

entry.summary: The paper formulates sim-to-real learning for spatiotemporal physical systems as a multi-objective problem with separate simulation and experimental risks, showing that standard sim-to-exp fine-tuning causes simulation-domain forgetting. Joint training consistently yields more balanced performance across four fluid systems and two model capacities.

entry.title: High-Value Synthetic Supervision for Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of a Compact Japanese Speech Model

author.name: Sidi Chang, Peiying Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents an auditable synthetic data pipeline mapping Japanese care-handoff speech to structured six-field notes, adapting a 1.47B audio model with full fine-tuning and rank-16 LoRA on only 182 synthetic clips. LoRA with about 0.85 percent trainable parameters achieves 97.7 percent of full fine-tuning performance, demonstrating efficient domain adaptation for low-resource, privacy-sensitive speech tasks.

entry.title: Compositional Embedding Architecture for Physical Field Prediction in Componentized Aerospace Systems

author.name: Qineng Wang, Xinrui Zhou, Shuwen Yue, Kangli Bao, Hairun Xie, Yonghe Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a tree-structured factorized compositional surrogate model for spacecraft thermal field prediction that reuses local component representations across configurations, improving accuracy for component counts and combinations unseen in training. This accelerates design screening compared to expensive high-fidelity thermal simulations.

entry.title: Heteroskedastic Canonical Polyadic Tensor Decomposition

author.name: Kyle Ritscher, Carlos Llosa-Vite

entry.summary: The paper introduces heteroskedastic-CP (HCP), an extension of canonical polyadic tensor decomposition that models entrywise noise variability via a low-rank precision tensor, recovered with an alternating block-coordinate ascent method. It retains the leading-order computational cost of CP-ALS. Demonstrations cover synthetic data and an EEG application.

entry.title: VERITYGATE: A Four-Gate Schema-Level Faithfulness Framework and Paired Benchmark for Grounded LLM Narrations over Structured Evidence

author.name: Sachin Gupta

entry.summary: VERITYGATE introduces a four-gate checker for verifying that LLM narrations over structured evidence honor declared evidence IDs, entities, numbers, and claim types, paired with a 900-instance benchmark of grounded-ungrounded pairs. Evaluation of GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3.3-70B, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 reveals high schema-level rejection rates and mixed benefits of a repair pass.

entry.title: The Price of Correlated Tests: How Strict Should a Model Release Gate Be?

author.name: Marco Pollanen

entry.summary: This paper formalizes ML release gating as a design problem: choosing the number of required passing tests to meet a reliability target while retaining good models, using a two-class latent-factor model. It proves that under shared latent correlation, stricter gates always raise reliability, so the optimal gate is the most lenient one meeting the target.

entry.title: PhaseAT: Fourier Phase Adversarial Training for Medical Image Domain Generalization

author.name: Ahmed Sharshar, Asif Hanif, Naveen Kumar Kummari, Mohammad Yaqub, Mohsen Guizan

entry.summary: PhaseAT is a phase-aware adversarial training framework for medical image domain generalization that creates phase-perturbed training views in the Fourier domain while preserving amplitude, forcing networks to rely on spatial organization rather than domain-specific texture. It targets robustness to shifts across scanners, sites, and acquisition protocols. Applied with clinical deployment motivation.

entry.title: Weather-Aware Domain Adaptation for Street-View Weather Recognition

author.name: Hossein Maghsoumi, George Atia, Yaser P. Fallah

entry.summary: This paper proposes WA-ADDA, an adversarial discriminative domain adaptation method for multi-class weather recognition from street-view images, where training data largely comes from mismatched non-street-view sources. The domain discriminator is conditioned on predicted weather to encourage features that are both domain-invariant and weather-sensitive, and the authors assemble a new multi-dataset benchmark with a standardized macro-metric evaluation protocol.

entry.title: A Holistic Assessment of the Carbon Footprint of Noor, a Very Large Arabic Language Model

author.name: Imad Lakim, Ebtesam Almazrouei, Ibrahim Abu Alhaol, Merouane Debbah, Julien Launay

entry.summary: The authors provide a holistic carbon footprint assessment of Noor, an extreme-scale Arabic language model project of up to 13B parameters, going beyond the standard training-only compute reporting. The paper accounts for a broader lifecycle of resource use and argues for more comprehensive environmental impact reporting in machine learning.

entry.title: LawCompass: Navigating from Legal QA to Multi-Agent Deep Research with Grounded Evidence

author.name: Xiaoxia Cheng, Linnan Wang, Jiahao Ma, Zhichuan Ye, Xuemei Zhou, Chuanyu Tong, Bo Jiang, Qing Zhu

entry.summary: LawCompass is an evidence-grounded legal assistant that moves beyond conversational legal QA to multi-agent deep research supporting systematic evidence retrieval, multi-step reasoning, and report-level synthesis. It offers three task functions: Legal QA, Professional Retrieval over statutes and case law, and deeper research workflows. The system targets the gap between consumer legal chatbots and professional legal work.

entry.title: SHAMS: An Audio-Grounded Pronunciation Benchmark for Levantine Arabic

author.name: Ben Sapirstein, Roy Mattar, Guy Mor-Lan, Ahlam Mohamed, Letizia Cerqueglini, Morris Alper

entry.summary: SHAMS is a benchmark of 1,300 utterances from open audio corpora balanced across five Levantine Arabic varieties (Urban and Rural Palestinian, Urban Jordanian, Lebanese, and Syrian), each represented across four aligned tiers: audio, unvocalized orthography, diacritized text, and phonetic transcription. The multi-tier structure supports evaluating diacritization, grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, and related speech-language tasks in a dialectally diverse, non-standardized orthography setting.

entry.title: The Asymptotics of Language Model Alignment with Memory

author.name: Haricharan Balasundaram, V. Arvind Rameshwar

entry.summary: This theory paper extends asymptotic equivalence results between KL-constrained RL and best-of-n alignment from i.i.d. token sequences to sequences with memory, better matching realistic autoregressive LMs. It clarifies when the cheap best-of-n sampling approach provably approximates RLHF-style alignment. A meaningful theoretical refinement.

entry.title: On-Device Commercial Intent Retrieval Under Size, Latency, and Privacy Constraints: A 3 MiB Retrieval System with Typed Egress Boundaries

author.name: Hyojung Han

entry.summary: This work builds a fully on-device commercial intent retrieval system for Korean commerce text under strict frozen constraints: under 3 MiB payload, under 20ms p95 inference, and no raw text or embeddings leaving the device, using a 4-bit quantized distilled embedding table over a 6,020-leaf taxonomy. It carefully reports where the constraints cost accuracy, including a sharp split on queries containing brand names. A disciplined privacy-preserving systems contribution.

entry.title: Where LLMs Fail with Visualization DSLs

author.name: Chang Han, Andrew McNutt, Katherine Isaacs

entry.summary: This study evaluates how LLMs fail when authoring charts in ten JSON-style visualization DSLs across 41 tasks, using rendering checks and qualitative coding of failures. It identifies four recurring failure patterns tied to specific DSL features and derives design recommendations for model-friendly DSLs. The work reframes DSL design from human ergonomics to machine usability.

entry.title: Discrete Annotation, Continuous Preference: Rethinking Supervision for Accurate and Generalizable Aesthetic Image Cropping

author.name: Ziqing Zhang, Xiao Liu, Kai Liu, Jianze Li, Weihang Zhang, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper models human cropping preference as a multi-peaked, continuous field over crop space via a Continuous Preference Field, recovering dense preference landscapes from discrete annotations through peak clustering. This addresses subjectivity and grid-rigidity problems in aesthetic cropping datasets, improving both training and fair evaluation. It reframes supervision design for subjective perception tasks.

entry.title: Watch Your Speech: Text-aware Video-to-Speech Synthesis with Textual Conditioning

author.name: Gunwoo Lee, Yoori Oh, Yoseob Han

entry.summary: WYS tackles the one-to-many ambiguity in video-to-speech synthesis by adding explicit textual conditioning as a linguistic cue, using an attention-based fusion module and a conditional flow matching objective. It improves phonetic accuracy when generating speech from silent talking-face videos.

entry.title: ShelfChange3D: Object-Level 3D Change Detection for Retail Shelf Monitoring

author.name: Lingyi Zhou, Yunke Wang, Mengyu Zheng, Wenbo Wang, Zijian Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: This work formulates retail shelf monitoring as object-level 3D change detection from paired RGB-D observations, identifying changed products and localizing changes with 3D bounding boxes for downstream robotics. The authors release ShelfChange3D, a dataset of 145K synthetic plus 5K real annotated pairs, and ChangeBox, an end-to-end framework that jointly reasons over the paired observations. This brings metric 3D grounding to a task previously handled in image space.

entry.title: FedCKA: Representation-Guided Layer Personalization for Federated 3D Perception Across Driving Domains

author.name: Jolle Verhoog, Ali Burak \"Unal, Holger Caesar

entry.summary: FedCKA addresses federated learning of 3D object detectors for intelligent vehicles under heterogeneous domain shifts like weather, time of day, and location. Rather than relying on predefined layer partitions for personalization, it uses representation-guided selection of which model layers each client personalizes against a shared global backbone. This targets the tension between a single consensus model and locally adapted models.

entry.title: SuperMotion: Source-Preserving Denoising for Text-Driven Human Motion Editing

author.name: Fa-Ting Hong, Peter Wonka
