entry.summary: SuperMotion introduces a source-preserving denoising framework for text-driven human motion editing that explicitly reuses the source motion at every reverse diffusion step. A predicted preservation gate controls per-frame, per-dimension reuse, and a clean-space source anchor blends predicted motion with the aligned source to retain temporal detail that learned-conditioning editors lose.

entry.title: 3DROID: A Renderable 3D Gaussian Dataset with Measured Per-Scene Reliability

author.name: Wonguen Cho, Junhoo Lee, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: 3DROID is a robot manipulation dataset of renderable 3D Gaussian scenes with measured per-scene extrinsic reliability, plus a calibration-aware pipeline anchoring reconstructions to the robot metric workspace. The paper studies how pose conditioning and camera-extrinsic reliability affect feed-forward 3DGS for robotic 3D supervision.

entry.title: DecomVoxel: Harnessing 3D-Native Priors with Guided In-situ Denoising Optimization for Decompositional Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Junfeng Ni, Zirui Zhou, Yixin Chen, Yu Liu, Nan Jiang, Zhifei Yang, Song-Chun Zhu, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: DecomVoxel formulates object completion in decompositional scene reconstruction as guided in-situ denoising optimization that bridges 3D-native generative priors with neural scene reconstruction. It introduces a reformulated epsilon-based distillation loss for stability, targeting high-quality object and background recovery under heavy occlusion where 2D priors suffer multi-view inconsistency.

entry.title: DiDE:Direct Injection with Color-Texture DEcoupling for 3D Stylization

author.name: Tao Wu, Alexandra Gomez-Villa, Senmao Li, Yaxing Wang, Joost van de Weijer, Kai Wang

entry.summary: DiDE is the first training-free framework for disentangled 3D stylization, allowing independent control of color and texture when transferring visual attributes from a reference image onto a 3D asset generated by rectified flow image-to-3D models. It exploits the overcompleteness of the structured latent space with respect to texture to decouple the two attributes.

entry.title: Learning from Failure: Leveraging Unreliable Predictions in Semi-Supervised Real-World Adverse Weather Removal

author.name: Cap Dang Xuan Kiet, Tat-Jen Cham

entry.summary: The paper proposes a student-teacher semi-supervised framework for adverse weather image restoration that preserves failed teacher predictions as informative negative samples in an unreliable database, alongside reliable pseudo-ground-truth positives. This improves generalization to real-world weather-degraded scenes compared to synthetic-supervision-only unified restoration models.

entry.title: GS-PQM: A Parameter-Domain Quality Metric for Compressed Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Pedro Martin, Ant\'onio Rodrigues, Jo\~ao Ascenso, Maria Paula Queluz

entry.summary: This paper introduces GS-PQM, a full-reference quality metric for post-training Gaussian Splatting compression that operates directly in the GS parameter domain rather than requiring rendering of predefined viewpoints. It estimates perceptual quality from parameter-domain distortion errors using a Support Vector Regression model. This addresses a key limitation of existing image/video-based metrics whose scores depend on selected views.

entry.title: HumanoidTTT: Test-Time Capability Reuse for Efficient Humanoid Control

author.name: Jingtai Yang, Yining Wu, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Hao Tang

entry.summary: HumanoidTTT is a framework for test-time capability reuse in continual humanoid control, addressing the challenge that intervening motions change the robot's entry state, making previously successful motions unsafe to replay blindly. It introduces Selective Full-Motion Reuse, which authorizes direct reuse of validated complete motions only when safe, and manages bounded storage by deciding which capabilities to retain. This targets efficient continual deployment.

entry.title: Toward Humanoid Robots in Construction: A Teleoperation Feasibility Study

author.name: Parastoo Ali Pour, David R. Martin, Chang Min Hur, Bo Zhang, Tommy Zhou, Brandon Thomas Lichter, Shane Stanfield, Pramod Khargonekar, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: This study presents an XR-based teleoperation system with pedal locomotion that lets a single operator perform construction tasks on a Unitree G1 humanoid, achieving 100% success on representative tasks like tool transport. Beyond teleoperation itself, the system aims to reduce worker strain and generate high-quality demonstration data for future humanoid autonomy. It offers a practical near-term deployment path for humanoids in a labor-shortaged industry.

entry.title: AFD-CAMLs: Agile Force-Distribution-Aware Planning and Control for Cable-Suspended Aerial Multi-Lifting Systems

author.name: Antreas Kourris, Sihao Sun

entry.summary: The paper proposes a hybrid planning-and-control framework for multiple UAVs cooperatively transporting a heavy payload via cables, addressing uneven force distributions that arise from redundant or ill-conditioned tension-to-wrench allocation. A global planner explores the allocation null space to generate cable-force references that augment a centralized local planner's cost. This improves both agility and force feasibility in aerial multi-lifting.

entry.title: SonarVoxNet: Diver Detection in 3D Bounding Box using 3D Sonar

author.name: Eugene Park, Jiwon Lee, Seyoung Kan, Trung Dong, Xiaomin Lin, Jane Shin

entry.summary: Presents SonarVoxNet, a detector producing full 3D bounding boxes of divers, including pitch and roll orientation, from sparse and noisy 3D sonar returns. Addresses a real gap since commercial 3D sonar preserves elevation but existing detectors assume dense LiDAR-like data and upright targets. Relevant to AUV systems assisting human divers underwater.

entry.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Multi-Input Systems with Joint Capacity Constraints

author.name: Saurabh Kumar, Lohitvel Gopikannan, Shashi Ranjan Kumar, Abhinav Sinha

entry.summary: Develops the AJ-APIR framework for multi-input strict-feedback nonlinear systems under joint capacity constraints where the admissible input set is a coupled subset of individual actuator limits. Uses spectral decomposition of a state-dependent gain matrix to separate commanded input into normal and tangential components relative to the constraint boundary, exploiting constraint geometry rather than enforcing bounds channel by channel. Avoids unnecessarily suppressing admissible control directions.

entry.title: On skew-symmetric distributions and their use in Monte Carlo sampling algorithms: coordinate-free, Gibbs-style and manifold versions of the Barker proposal

author.name: Minh Vu, Samuel Livingstone, Pantelis Samartsidis

entry.summary: This work reviews the Barker proposal, a Metropolis-Hastings MCMC algorithm built on skew-symmetric distributions, and introduces three extensions: coordinate-free variants, a Gibbs-style version that re-evaluates gradients at partially updated coordinates, and a simplified manifold Barker algorithm with improved robustness. Experiments show the Gibbs-style variant improves sampling in challenging targets. This strengthens the toolbox for gradient-based MCMC sampling.

entry.title: Graph-centric agentic intelligence

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: An Amazon Science post tracing the evolution of network/graph intelligence from passive modeling to agentic reasoning, arguing that graph structure is the natural substrate for AI agents doing causal inference, dependency tracking, and root-cause analysis over large-scale network systems. It demonstrates cascaded graph analytics for root-cause identification and links to a companion solution architecture post.

entry.title: From Discovery to Decision: Finite-Budget Recoverability in LLM Voting

author.name: Shaoang Li, Jian Li

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of voting over multiple LLM responses under a fixed call budget, characterizing the discovery-to-decision gap: a correct answer discovered late may lack remaining budget to accumulate plurality support. Derives a sharp recoverability threshold and shows reachable endpoint winners only contract as sampling proceeds. Relevant to test-time scaling and best-of-n inference design.

entry.title: Evaluating Physical Consistency and Plausibility in Generative Scenario Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Manasa Mariam Mammen, Zafer Kayatas, Stefan Wagner

entry.summary: This paper introduces a layered evaluation protocol for generative scenario models in autonomous driving, assessing five layers: kinematic alignment, statistical baseline comparison, latent controllability, activation analysis, and output validation against vehicle dynamics. The goal is to provide formal assurance about physical consistency, addressing the transparency gap that limits use of generative models in safety-critical validation and certification workflows. It complements existing evaluation methods.

entry.title: A Framework for Egocentric and Exocentric Procedural Understanding via Temporal Segmentation and Semantic Abstraction

author.name: Vivek Chavan, J\"org Kr\"uger

entry.summary: The framework converts long multimodal ego/exocentric workplace video into a structured Procedural State Memory (a Work Environment Model) using event segmentation theory-inspired boundary detection from context, location, motion, narration, and gaze signals. Segments become evidence-linked event cards that incrementally update a compact procedural representation, reducing redundant storage and processing.

entry.title: Useful to Whom? Sample Value Is Defined Only Relative to the Learner

author.name: Yangze Liu, Xiao-Long Yin, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: Through controlled coreset-selection experiments that freeze selected subsets and vary only the training learner, this paper shows data value is learner-relative: doubling ResNet-18 width moves the easy-first versus coverage crossover from 57 to 85 samples per class on ImageNet-100, with further interactions between input resolution and capacity.

entry.title: MatrixReward: Reward from Rubric Matrix for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Zihan Shen, Qi Liu, Zixuan Yang, Yiqun Chen, Chenglong Zhao, Xiaozhao Wang, Lei He

entry.summary: Proposes MatrixReward, which builds rewards for open-ended generation from a rollout-by-rubric win-rate matrix obtained by pairwise comparisons of all sampled responses under each rubric. Column spread and cross-column correlations yield data-dependent rubric weights, addressing the information loss of pointwise rubric scoring and merged scalar judgments.

entry.title: Rules Amortize, Pairings Don't: Linguistic Structure Determines What Latent Task Representations Can Replace In-Context Learning

author.name: Gunmay Jhingran

entry.summary: This paper asks which linguistic operations can be amortized out of prompts into latent task representations, given theory showing static vectors fail on high-rank mappings like word-level bijections. The author trains a small 2.6M-parameter network that reads support-set geometry and produces input-conditioned additive updates to the residual stream of a frozen GPT-2-large/XL. Results across eight inflectional directions show rule-like operations amortize while pairing-type operations do not.

entry.title: Beyond Pointwise Error: A Multi-Metric Evaluation of Spatial Climate Downscaling

author.name: Loys Masquelier, Etienne Le Naour

entry.summary: The authors benchmark five spatial climate downscaling methods on ERA5 temperature, wind, and precipitation fields using five complementary criteria including pointwise, structural, distributional, spectral, and gradient errors. Results reveal a systematic trade-off between spatial fidelity and fine-scale variability, showing that metric choice changes which method appears best.

entry.title: MCIR: A Feature Dependence-Aware Explainability Method with Reliability Guarantees

author.name: Poushali Sengupta, Sabita Maharjan, Frank Eliassen, Shashi Raj Pandey, Yan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MCIR-M, a global feature-importance method that conditions each feature's attribution on strongly dependent neighbors to produce stable rankings under multicollinearity, with theoretical reliability guarantees. It addresses instability of SHAP, LIME, SAGE and related methods under correlated or redundant features.

entry.title: FourierQK: Filter Shape, Admissibility and the Leakage-Coverage Law

author.name: Athanasios Zeris

entry.summary: This work studies frequency-collapse attention, which replaces the Q/K dot product with a bandpass-filtered inner product at a learned frequency, and tests five hypotheses about optimal filter shape via controlled ablations on character-level language modeling. Findings include that DC and Nyquist components are actively harmful, confirming that oscillatory bandpass structure is essential. It advances the science of non-dot-product attention mechanisms.

entry.title: Benchmarking System One decision models against trained classifiers and language models for automated decision gates

author.name: Amir Rafe, Subasish Das

entry.summary: This benchmark compares typed decision models (System One models returning probabilities over declared options without text generation, including a hosted model called Jev) against supervised classifiers and generative LLMs on decision-gate tasks under matched conditions. Results show ranking depends on conditions: small trained classifiers are most accurate with task labels, while decision models and generative models differ in zero-shot and workflow settings. It provides an early systematic evaluation of the decision-native model interface paradigm.

entry.title: STCFormer: Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Modeling with Dynamic Cluster Transformer for Station-based Weather Forecasting

author.name: Rongwen Li, Haixin Xie, Mingyang Wang, Hongwu Liu, Kun Fang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, Kenli Li

entry.summary: STCFormer is an adaptive spatio-temporal Transformer for station weather forecasting that dynamically clusters stations according to their local evolution within each temporal patch, rather than sharing a static grouping across the observation window. Its Cluster-Attention mechanism selectively models intra-cluster interactions while retaining global context, and the paper analyzes when selective interactions outperform dense connectivity. It improves on existing clustering-based selective forecasting approaches.

entry.title: Right In-Place (RiP) Convolution: A Simple, General, and Near-Optimal Strategy for Memory-Efficient CNN Inference

author.name: Opegbemi Matthias Busoye, Tolulope Matthew Busoye, Eghonghon-aye Eigbe

entry.summary: RiP convolution generalizes memory-optimal in-place CNN inference beyond the restrictive assumptions of prior work, identifying two failure regimes in the published closed form including silent input corruption and unbounded overestimates. It achieves near-optimal activation memory without the 2x transpose cost of the previous approach.

entry.title: AnyJev Technical Report

author.name: Jiamu Zhang, Tianze Yang, Yucheng Shi, Evan Chen, Zixiang Nie, Kelly Wan, Liangjie Hong, Ninghao Liu, Liang Wu

entry.summary: AnyJev reads typed decisions (probability distributions over fixed options) from a single prefill of an instruction-tuned LLM by restricting next-token distribution to option tokens. It corrects two biases, label priors and positional preferences in the option list, via training-free corrections: dividing out an estimated label prior and averaging log-probabilities over cyclic rotations of the option list.

entry.title: Rethinking the Information Bottleneck: Structured Decomposition under Label-Induced Partitions

author.name: Jingyao Zhang, Yuxuan Li, Lu Han, Ali Anaissi, Nguyen H. Tran

entry.summary: The authors argue that standard information bottleneck regularization, which compresses via a single scalar I(Z;X), conflates label-relevant structure with nuisance variation such as acquisition conditions or subject appearance, particularly harming data-limited domains like medical imaging. They propose a structured decomposition of the IB objective under label-induced partitions that regulates label-relevant and residual information independently. This improves generalization when training data is scarce.

entry.title: Clifford Sheaf Neural Networks

author.name: Kotaro Kamiya, Joel Nicholls

entry.summary: CSNN is an equivariant sheaf neural network for geometric graphs that places a Clifford algebra on each stalk of a cellular sheaf and transports multivector features along edges. The authors characterize the family of admissible restriction maps, showing that naive algebra-homomorphism choices under equivariance (versor conjugation) are expressively weak, and arrive at a K-term sandwich construction whose sheaf Laplacian is positive semidefinite by construction and still mixes grades. This merges geometric deep learning with sheaf theory at a mathematical level.

entry.title: Tight Transition Time Bounds for Separable Logistic Regression at the Edge of Stability

author.name: Haodong Wen, Kaiyue Wen, Jiaye Teng

entry.summary: The authors disprove a conjecture about Edge of Stability dynamics in logistic regression by showing that worst-case transition time from oscillatory to monotone loss decrease scales as Theta((log eta)^{min{n-2,d-2}}), dependent on both stepsize and problem dimensions. This resolves an open question with tight bounds uniformly over dimensions for separable data.

entry.title: Range-GRPO: Policy Optimization via Pairwise Relations among Reward Intervals

author.name: Ryunyi Lee, Kangjun Noh, Somin Kim, Heedong Kim, Kyungwoo Song

entry.summary: Range-GRPO extends Group Relative Policy Optimization for LLM post-training by representing LLM-as-a-Judge pseudo-rewards as conformally calibrated reward ranges rather than point scores, capturing reward uncertainty. The semi-supervised framework combines limited labeled data with unlabeled prompts, using pairwise relations among reward intervals as learning signals.

entry.title: Function-Structured Reinforcement Learning with Executable Verifiers for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Zihan Liu, Xurong Xie

entry.summary: FSG-RL connects subproblem graphs and Python implementations for algorithmic mathematical reasoning, using supervised fine-tuning to learn code generation from function graphs followed by GRPO optimization with answer-gated rewards and span-level credit assignment. The framework includes multi-verifier feedback, optional teacher supervision, and a benchmark curated from GSM8K.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Free-Boundary Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Tan Phuong Dong Le

entry.summary: This work applies Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) in a physics-informed framework to free-boundary PDEs, including obstacle problems and a Stefan problem, using residual-based losses over obstacle constraints, PDE inequalities, complementarity, and boundary conditions. Compared against PINN and residual-network baselines, the KAN solver achieves low L2 and Linf errors while accurately resolving contact regions and moving interfaces.

entry.title: LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them

author.name: Yinheng Li, Justin Wagle

entry.summary: LLM2Jev extracts calibrated categorical decisions directly from next-token probabilities over bracketed numeric identifiers, offering both a training-free inference recipe and a fine-tuning objective with a listwise loss and KL anchoring. It investigates when general LLMs already function as structured decision models versus when fine-tuning is needed. Practical for building LLM-backed decision systems without free-form output parsing.

entry.title: ODDR: One-Step Deshadow Diffusion via Reward Guidance

author.name: Junseong Shin, Kijun Kim, Minseong Kim, Dongjin Kim, Tae Hyun Kim

entry.summary: ODDR is a shadow-removal framework that avoids costly real-world paired data by training a one-step diffusion model, ODD, on synthetic shadows and then adapting it with a reward-guided method called ShadowReward. This yields efficient single-step inference with high-fidelity results and better generalization than annotation-heavy supervised approaches. The reward guidance replaces traditional paired supervision.

entry.title: GenCOPE: Syn2Real Generalized Category-Level Object Pose Estimation for Robotic Picking

author.name: Jian Liu, Wei Sun, Zhenqi Dai, Hui Yang, Jian Xiao, Nicu Sebe, Na Zhao

entry.summary: GenCOPE targets synthetic-to-real generalization for category-level object pose estimation, training solely on rendered synthetic data and deploying directly on real objects for robotic picking. It addresses the synthetic-real domain gap, particularly in texture appearance, by learning domain-invariant representations.

entry.title: Moore, Escher, Penrose: A Conformal Golden Braid

author.name: Sophia Feldman, Assaf Shocher

entry.summary: Building on the conformal power map analysis of M.C. Escher's Print Gallery, the authors use a frozen text-to-image diffusion model to generate new self-referential scenes, noting that prompting alone fails to enforce recursion and post-hoc transformation leaves structures poorly connected. The work connects art, mathematics, and generative modeling.

entry.title: Whole-Body Aerial Grasping and Lifting via Partial Visual Observations

author.name: Jiaye Jin, Rui Jin, Xinhang Xu, Haotian Jin, Ruiyang Liu, Yi Wang, Jiayan Zhao, Kun Cao, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: This work presents a recurrent teacher-student framework that learns a single simulation-trained policy to jointly command flight, arm motion, and gripper closure for aerial grasp-and-lift under partial target observations. A privileged teacher uses RL with a critical-state curriculum exposing acquisition and lifting states before linking them to approach trajectories, then distills into a recurrent visual student. This addresses training coverage and execution-timing challenges.

entry.title: LiDARFlow: Real-Time Panel-Based MAV Guidance in Unknown Environments

author.name: Jo\~ao Machado (ENAC-LAB), Zeynep Bilgin (ENAC-LAB), Matthieu Verdoucq (ENAC-LAB), Murat Bronz (ENAC)

entry.summary: Adapts a panel-based guidance method derived from aerodynamic potential-flow theory to micro aerial vehicles in unknown cluttered environments, building and updating obstacle representations online from onboard LiDAR. The approach generates smooth collision-free guidance vectors and was validated in indoor flight tests for waypoint navigation and directional guidance. Demonstrates real-time onboard obstacle avoidance with purely onboard sensing.

entry.title: Dynamic Spatial Bayesian Machine Learning Model: Applications to Intergenerational Economic Mobility and Geographic Income Inequality in the United States

author.name: Hammed A. Olayinka, Saheed O. Olayemi

entry.summary: The authors introduce DSP-BART-HS, a dynamic spatial panel Bayesian additive regression trees model with horseshoe shrinkage for high-dimensional spatio-temporal data, and apply it to US economic mobility and income inequality. Extensive simulation across nine scenarios shows it matches or beats structural spatial econometrics, non-parametric ML, and small-area estimators. This offers a strong tool for policy-relevant causal-descriptive analysis of geographic inequality.

entry.title: Knowing When to Yield: Grounded Arbitration of User Corrections in Text-Based Embodied Agents

author.name: Yezhou Cheng, Runjia Du, Zeming Liu, Hang Lyu, Zehua Yang, Bojun Lin

entry.summary: The paper formulates grounded correction arbitration as choosing among accepting, rejecting, inspecting the world, and asking the speaker, and implements this as GAVA with observation-bounded evidence and a one-step expected-loss rule. Using 162 checkpoints and 972 paired true/false interventions in ALFWorld, it establishes an evidence contract and reduces interaction cost versus always-verify policies.

entry.title: Grounding Large Language Models in DSGE Simulators for Policy Generation and Forecasting

author.name: Aditya Dubey, Namah Gupta, Vinti Agarwal

entry.summary: Places an instruction-tuned LLM inside six DSGE macroeconomic simulators where it observes economy states, selects bounded policy actions, and receives simulated rewards, tackling long-horizon credit assignment in economic policy. Provides a common Python interface for rollouts, shocks, state cloning, and rolling-horizon simulation. Interesting testbed linking LLMs to formal economic dynamics.

entry.title: Probabilistic Plan Legibility with Off-the-shelf Planners

author.name: Michele Persiani, Thomas Hellstr\"om

entry.summary: This paper extends legible planning to arbitrary PDDL domains without requiring bespoke planners, allowing plans that disambiguate their goals to an observer, and estimates the observer's perspective via a second-order theory of mind connecting planner and observer task spaces. Benchmarks across several PDDL domains show applicability to human-robot teaming.

entry.title: A Verifier Can Leak the Answer: Diagnosability Before Optimization in Closed-Loop Agent Debugging

author.name: Peiying Zhu, Sidi Chang

entry.summary: The paper documents a case where a simulator-grounded verifier leaked the planted fault identity through exact-anchor predicates, making comparisons between exact and greedy debugging algorithms vacuous even though they appeared equally effective. After removing the leaking anchors, real performance differences emerged, arguing for diagnosability audits before optimization studies.

entry.title: Learning to Cover Locally: Graph Neural Combinatorial Optimization under a Hard Information Horizon

author.name: Johannes F. Loevenich, Thies Moehlenhof, Laurin Holz, Maxime Schwarzer, Tobias Huerten, Roberto Rigolin F. Lopes

entry.summary: The paper studies neural combinatorial optimization where each node commits to part of a global solution seeing only its k-hop neighborhood, formalized as local set cover and instantiated on multipoint relay selection in the OLSRv2 routing protocol. The authors prove impossibility results for deterministic selectors with a one-hop-short horizon and train graph neural models under this protocol-imposed information constraint. It connects learning-based optimization to a concrete networking standard with provable hardness structure.

entry.title: WIPSNet: Deep Learning for Paediatric Wheeze Detection from Overnight Impedance Pneumography

author.name: Felix Oury, Harley Day, Karina Mayoral, Ville-Pekka Sepp\"a, Sejal Saglani, Reiko J. Tanaka

entry.summary: WIPSNet is a 3D ResNet applied to stacked continuous wavelet transform scalograms of overnight impedance pneumography for paediatric wheeze detection, improving night-level classification AUC from 0.633 (current clinical EVI readout) to 0.783 on a 15-patient, 60-night cohort. It outperforms Mamba and modern sleep-staging baselines, with peak performance at 32 minutes of temporal context. This could meaningfully improve noninvasive pediatric respiratory monitoring.

entry.title: Learning Linear Systems under Heavy-Tailed Noise: A Non-Asymptotic Analysis from A Single Trajectory

author.name: Xiaomian Yang, Sungho Shin

entry.summary: The paper establishes non-asymptotic sample complexity bounds for least-squares estimation of vector autoregressive models under heavy-tailed noise from a single trajectory, with error rates degrading gracefully in the moment order p. It also provides a unifying analysis extending to sub-exponential and sub-Gaussian noise.

entry.title: Distillation of Tabular Foundation Models into Efficient Predictors

author.name: Minho Jeong, Dooho Lee, Jinmo Lee, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: The paper studies how to distill tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are expensive at inference due to in-context conditioning on labeled data, into lightweight dataset-specific students. Across two TFMs and neural and tree-based students, the authors derive a practical recipe: use the full labeled training set as teacher context and train students only on teacher predictions for the training points.

entry.title: Towards Optimal Policy Improvement

author.name: Yaniv Oren, Viliam Vadocz, Wiktor Zabka, Thomas Evers, Jan Robine, Wendelin B\"ohmer, Matthijs T. J. Spaan, Martha White, Hendrik Baier, Fenghui Yu

entry.summary: This paper defines optimal policy improvement from first principles as producing the best policy attainable in a single update under constraints, showing that optimal improvement on a state set is equivalent to solving an induced MDP. The authors take steps toward optimal greedification under practical constraints, providing foundational analysis for iterative RL algorithms.

entry.title: Reachability-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Impulse Interplanetary Transfers

author.name: Yashdeep Chaudhary, Roberto Armellin, Harry Holt

entry.summary: The paper develops RARL, a reinforcement learning framework for multi-impulse interplanetary trajectory design in which the policy selects intermediate waypoints within reachability-derived ellipsoidal sets, with Lambert reconstruction producing dynamically consistent maneuvers. This connects learned decisions to maneuver geometry for reusable spacecraft trajectory design.

entry.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Japanese LLMs to IME-Related and Typographical Errors

author.name: Ryota Mibayashi, Hiroaki Ohshima

entry.summary: This study evaluates the robustness of eleven Japanese and multilingual LLMs against realistic Japanese-specific typos across five categories including character transposition, homophone conversion, IME conversion, and full-width conversion, applied to JMMLU, JCommonsenseQA, and JamC-QA. The results reveal which perturbation types most degrade performance. It addresses an underexplored robustness dimension specific to Japanese input methods.

entry.title: Code-Switching Spoken Language Identification as Multi-Label Set Prediction

author.name: Shunsuke Mitsumori, Matthew Wiesner, Shigeo Morishima, Shinji Watanabe

entry.summary: The paper formulates code-switched spoken language identification as multi-label language-set prediction and proposes a set generator that directly outputs the languages present, comparing against atomic-pair and score-based baselines on data leakage-prone CS speech that evades monolingual LID filters. The set generator predicts correct language counts on unseen pairs but underperforms oracle Top-k. Useful for curating multilingual speech corpora.

entry.title: EgoRefine: Ego-Referenced Predictive Alignment and Trajectory-Conditioned Reliability-Aware Fusion for Asynchronous Collaborative Perception

author.name: Lingzhao Kong, Yongsheng Zang, Yu Kang, Kailun Yang, Jie Fu, Yukun Zuo, Zhiyong Li

entry.summary: EgoRefine improves asynchronous collaborative 3D perception by predicting delayed cooperative features using the ego agent's current observation rather than only the transmitter's history, and by fusing features with reliability weights that vary spatially. This reduces residual temporal misalignment in vehicle-to-everything perception. It matters for safe autonomous driving with connected agents.

entry.title: Affine-Aligned Atlas for Canonical Gaussian Construction in Video Representation

author.name: Masaya Takabe, Hiroshi Watanabe, Sujun Hong, Tomohiro Ikai

entry.summary: The paper proposes an affine-atlas canonical Gaussian representation for video, where frame-wise affine transforms absorb large global motion such as camera movement before canonical Gaussian construction. This reduces the burden on the temporal deformation model in Gaussian-based video representations.

entry.title: EndoLive: Real-Time Style Transfer for Endoscopic Endonasal Skull Base Surgical Video

author.name: Griffin Hurt, Calvin Brinkman

entry.summary: EndoLive applies real-time style transfer to endoscopic endonasal skull base surgery video so that cadaveric training specimens visually resemble living tissue, including bleeding appearance. This aims to improve surgical training by narrowing the appearance gap between cadavers and live patients.

entry.title: H-SPAR: Hydrodynamic-aware Simulation for Particle Transport and Autonomous Robots

author.name: Navid Zarrabi, Nariman Yousefi, Sajad Saeedi

entry.summary: Introduces H-SPAR, a marine robotics simulator integrating spatially and temporally varying flow fields, Lagrangian particle transport, probabilistic sampling, and ROS 2/Gazebo-based surface vehicle autonomy in a shared simulation. Precomputed flow fields drive both particle advection and current-induced forces during closed-loop execution, enabling joint evaluation of mission cost and sampling performance. Shows current-aware planners like SVF-RRT* achieve substantial cost reductions.

entry.title: AI #188: Gemini Dot Argon

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's regular AI news roundup covering the Gemini 4 Argon rollout at frontier-level benchmarks and 2/10 dollar pricing, OpenAI pulling the would-be GPT-6.1 Astra over alignment failures while shipping GPT-6.1 Sol, Dev Day announcements including Ultrafast mode and the Dots always-on agent, and continued praise of Claude Opus 5.5 as the author's preferred model. It also touches on White House engagement with tech leaders. This is a widely read situational-awareness digest rather than original research.

entry.title: New tool lets users repair AI-generated 3D models, then fabricate them just the way they want

author.name: Alex Shipps | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL, Google, and Northeastern researchers present InstructMesh, a design tool that generates editable 3D models of functional objects like mugs, glasses, and robot parts via prompts, letting users highlight regions to refine before 3D printing. The system addresses the gap that generative models understand appearance but not physical function, enabling what-you-see-is-what-you-get fabrication workflows.

entry.title: Measuring the Microtask Eligibility Gap: When Is an Off-the-Shelf SLM Enough for an Agent Harness?

author.name: Jundong Hu, Shekar Ramachandran

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks whether small language models can handle agent-harness microtasks like auto-approving shell commands, memory writing, and tool selection, using a four-task benchmark with practitioner-defined thresholds and confidence-interval-aware eligibility rules. Sweeping Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 8B, it quantifies an eligibility gap and examines whether quantization closes it.

entry.title: Scientific Agents: Evaluating Profession-Specific System Prompts on Scientific Tasks

author.name: Timothy Kassis

entry.summary: The paper evaluates 503 profession-specific AGENTS.md profiles against four controls (minimal baseline, role sentence, generic rigor guide, unrelated profile) across nine science benchmarks with 4,488 completed items using Gemini 3.8 Flash in the Pi harness. It finds detailed profession-specific prompts raise token cost without a consistent accuracy gain.

entry.title: Comedic Fool's Gold: Reward Exploits and Countermeasures in Conversational Humor

author.name: Sam Larson

entry.summary: The paper studies reward exploits when training language models for conversational humor, showing embedding-based surprise rewards accept word-shuffled replies, audience-model laughter predictions are vulnerable to laughter cues, and normalization across speakers blocks the covered attacks. Three RL runs evaluate training with the resulting rewards.

entry.title: Conflicting Supervision Moves Commitment, Not Capability: A 12.29{\sigma} arrangement effect that is exactly zero under a convention-agnostic score

author.name: Wenhui Chen

entry.summary: This arXiv paper studies what happens when a model is trained on identical problems written under two incompatible but individually correct conventions, asking how the ordering of that training data shapes the model's learned behavior. The author proves a theoretical bound showing that data arrangement and learning-rate schedule act as separate multiplicative factors on the ordering effect, with constant schedules allowing large end-of-training influence while decaying schedules suppress it. The headline empirical finding is a highly significant arrangement effect measured in standard deviations that vanishes entirely under a convention-agnostic evaluation, suggesting the effect concerns which convention the model commits to rather than its underlying capability.

entry.title: Fault-Tolerant Budget Conservation in Distributed Multi-Agent Delegation

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: The paper formalizes fault-tolerant budget conservation for multi-agent delegation, showing that parent-child allocation constraints and distributed escrow do not prevent overspend under lost replies, late effects, duplicate messages, partitions, and DAG lineage aliasing. It proposes quantized resource vectors as exclusive escrow credits moving through a delegation DAG with lineage-bound, idempotency-keyed operation reservations persisted before dispatch.

entry.title: Ontology-Based Contextual AI Evaluations (OB-CAIE) Methodology

author.name: Julie Krugler Hollek, Michael Zargham, Mala Kumar

entry.summary: OB-CAIE is a methodology for more rigorous, reproducible AI evaluations that uses two ontologies: a Domain-Specific Ontology defining what is tested and an Evaluation Process Ontology defining how. It aims to clarify testing coverage, balance human expertise with automation, and improve reproducibility of evaluation environments. This addresses a widely recognized weakness in current AI evaluation practice.

entry.title: Meta-Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Fast Adaptation of Interactive Policies with Applications to Autonomous Driving

author.name: Huiwen Yan, Kyriakos G. Vamvoudakis, Mushuang Liu

entry.summary: The paper extends meta-reinforcement learning to multi-agent systems by modeling MARL problems as Markov games and developing a meta-MARL framework with bi-level optimization for rapid adaptation of interactive policies. This handles tasks characterized both by environment dynamics and other agents' strategic interactions. Applications include autonomous driving scenarios.

entry.title: ABDA-NL: A Natural-Language Scenario Explorer for Argument-Based Reasoning

author.name: Shawn Bowers, Martin Caminada, Haoyang Liu, Bertram Lud\"ascher

entry.summary: Adds a natural-language interface to ABDA, a system for argument-based discussion over ASPIC+ knowledge bases, letting users inspect accepted/rejected/undecided conclusions, explore what-if alternatives, and author new rules in plain English with an LLM translating to formal statements. Deterministic formal reasoning provides correctness guarantees while the LLM bridges language and formalism. A nice demonstration of neuro-symbolic interfaces for explainable reasoning.

entry.title: AbsorbEvo: An Agentic Framework for Autonomous Inverse Design of Microwave Absorbers

author.name: Zhicheng Feng, Yubo Zhao, Xuefeng Yao

entry.summary: An agentic framework translating natural-language performance objectives into microwave absorber designs verified by full-wave simulation, combining LLM reasoning, physics-based prediction, historical feedback, and a candidate evolution strategy mixing directed increments with global sampling. Demonstrates LLM agents accelerating a specialized engineering design loop. A solid example of AI-for-science/engineering applied work.

entry.title: When Does Exercise-Specific Joint Selection Help? An Audit of Evaluation and Control Design

author.name: Haotian Chen, Jingkun Yu, Yuning Zhang, Bowen Ye

entry.summary: This paper audits whether exercise-specific joint selection genuinely improves skeleton-based correctness classification in rehabilitation, analyzing 1,057 repetitions from ten subjects. It shows that reported gains are sensitive to the choice of estimand, aggregation method, and subset structure, with many gains statistically indistinguishable from dimension-matched random feature maps.

entry.title: Questionnaire-Guided Disaggregation of Energy Appliance Use for Domestic Smart Meter Data

author.name: Achal Nanjundamurthy, Rupam Misra, Suzanne Little, Alan F. Smeaton

entry.summary: The paper presents a label-free system that disaggregates 30-minute smart meter data into nine appliance categories by combining event detection for high-power loads with questionnaire-guided estimation, evaluated on UK-DALE, REFIT, and a large Irish dataset of 2,968 consumers. It addresses the gap between coarse billing-grade metering and appliance-level insight.

entry.title: An ontology for cross-sectoral crisis management: core and public health modules

author.name: Aldo Gangemi, Rita T. Sousa, Luigi Asprino, Giorgia Lodi, Andrea G. Nuzzolese, Valentina Presutti, Johannes Gysen, Diana F. Sousa, Luigi Spagnolo

entry.summary: The paper presents the European Crisis Management Ontology (ECMO), a modular OWL ontology for disaster risk reduction and response, with a core module covering hazards, events, exposure, impact, and response measures, and a public health module aligned with SNOMED CT and ICD-11. It demonstrates utility by representing Epidemic Intelligence data.

entry.title: Verify Claims, Not Scores: Evidence-Based Verification of Modular Agents

author.name: Ali Atiah Alzahrani

entry.summary: The paper proposes a claim-specific verification audit for modular agents that plan, act, check, and refine: instead of judging changes by aggregate task scores, the audit scores evidence for each conclusion with four verdicts and an explicit validity boundary, using oracle policies to measure attainable improvement under stated action sets.

entry.title: PRISM: A Category-Theoretic Framework for Measuring and Refining Multimodal Analogies

author.name: Mirella Zeisler, Ojas Shirekar, Mircea Lic\v{a}, Chirag Raman

entry.summary: PRISM is a modality-agnostic framework for measuring and improving relational alignment in multimodal analogies, representing analogies as explicit relational mappings grounded in category theory and instantiating them across modalities with VLMs, evaluated on visual metaphor generation. A pullback score quantifies relational alignment of generated outputs.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Manasa Mariam Mammen, Priyanka Mary Mammen, Zafer Kayatas, Stefan Wagner

entry.summary: This work evaluates five vision-language models (including Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-E4B, and LLaVA-OneVision variants) for autonomous driving robustness under degraded visual inputs from sensor imperfections and environmental conditions. It examines effects on both predictions and confidence calibration, which is critical for safety-critical driving decisions where models must know when their predictions are unreliable. The study contributes reliability evidence for a growing deployment area.

entry.title: Mapping the RAG Landscape: A Four Axis Taxonomy of Efficiency, Defense, Interactivity, and Reasoning

author.name: Meghana Sunil, Shravya V, Shravan Venkatraman, Joe Dhanith PR

entry.summary: This survey organizes contemporary retrieval-augmented generation research into a four-axis taxonomy covering efficiency, defense, interactivity, and reasoning, extending beyond the standard pipeline-focused surveys. It consolidates recent work on challenges such as hallucination mitigation via external grounding, retrieval efficiency, and adversarial robustness. As a survey, its value depends on coverage breadth and the usefulness of the organizing taxonomy.

entry.title: SW-KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with Stieltjes-Wigert q-Orthogonal Polynomials

author.name: Amirhosein Azarpour, Seyyed Moein Kazemi

entry.summary: SW-KAN introduces a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network variant using Stieltjes-Wigert q-orthogonal polynomials defined on semi-infinite domains, resolving the domain mismatch between unbounded inputs and the bounded support of prior polynomial KAN bases. This removes the need for ad-hoc input normalization while retaining the interpretability and efficiency benefits of KANs.

entry.title: Multi-Behavioral Evolved Substrates Through Neuromodulation and Activation Selection

author.name: Romain Claret, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Kilian Stoffel

entry.summary: Using over 10,000 experiments with CPPN-encoded substrates, this paper shows neuromodulation alone cannot overcome an evolutionary search barrier: monotonic activations impose a 75% ceiling on parity tasks regardless of capacity or population size, while gradient descent escapes it. Adding per-node activation selection enables evolved substrates to acquire diverse computational behaviors.

entry.title: Decoding the Disaster: Multi-Task Geospatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models and Crowdsourced Imagery for Disaster Mapping

author.name: Wenping Yin, Fabian Desuer, Ziqi Liu, Naixia Mou, Weijia Li, Pedram Ghamisi, Xiao Xiang Zhu, Hao Li

entry.summary: Introduces GRDisaster, a multi-task framework using vision-language models to understand, geolocalize, and reason over crowdsourced street-level disaster imagery that lacks reliable geographic metadata. It contributes a new benchmark of 26,340 images derived from PhotoMappers and combines VLM reasoning with complementary remote sensing data for emergency response.

entry.title: Proof-Gated Signing: Solver-Checked Transaction Guards that Hold Under State Drift for Onchain AI Agents

author.name: Bravish Ghosh

entry.summary: Addresses state-drift attacks on AI agents controlling crypto wallets, where pre-signing checks (allowlists, LLM reviewers, simulations) describe chain state that an adversary can change before execution. Proof-Gated Signing simulates proposed transactions, verifies declarative value-and-permission policies with an SMT solver across an oracle-uncertainty band, and compiles on-chain post-conditions.

entry.title: Diffusion Editing with Soft Mask: Pixel Level Redo of Image and Video with Adjustable Strength

author.name: Candi Zheng, Yuan Lan

entry.summary: Introduces SoftPaint, a zero-shot sampling method for diffusion models that uses soft masks to enable a continuous spectrum of pixel-level edits from full preservation to complete re-synthesis, via a Langevin-iteration-based sampler respecting per-pixel mask strengths. This avoids expensive pixel-wise annotation while going beyond standard zero-shot inpainting, and extends to video.

entry.title: FAER: Auditable Utility-Aligned Trajectory Replay for Language Model Post-Training

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Tianshu Fu, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: Formalizes the selection-to-learning gap in replay-based post-training, where cached trajectories are ranked by heuristics like confidence or freshness rather than downstream learner utility. FAER provides an auditable full-trajectory replay framework with a learner-aware selector fitted on calibration blocks and an audit contract that freezes observed fields before evaluation labels are joined.

entry.title: Towards Hierarchical Cyber Defense with Large Language Models: From Planning to Execution

author.name: Harshith Doppalapudi, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Ankit Shah

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether frozen, zero-shot LLMs can provide retraining-free control in hierarchical cyber defense, formulated as a controller-agnostic planner-executor hierarchy where the planner selects a subnet to defend and the executor selects actions within it. It examines how performance changes as LLM control extends from planning to execution, addressing the generalization limits of RL-trained defenders across network scales. Results inform where LLM control is most beneficial in the hierarchy.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Augmentation under Covariate Shift: Invariant-Guided Diffusion and Prototype Reweighting

author.name: Hongyu Cao, Xinyuan Wang, Arun Vignesh Malarkkan, Kunpeng Liu, Haifeng Chen, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: The paper defines the Augmented and Weighted Learning under Covariate Shift (AWL-CS) problem, covering scenarios where tabular data is scarce, imbalanced, and drifting between training and deployment. It proposes invariant-guided diffusion for augmentation plus prototype reweighting to steer generation toward downstream task relevance rather than source-distribution mimicry.

entry.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Enhanced Radiometer Image Precipitation Estimation using Conditional Flow Matching

author.name: Victor Enescu, Assaad Zeghina, Matthieu Meignin, Nicolas Viltard, C\'ecile Mallet

entry.summary: Applies flow matching models to unsupervised domain adaptation of satellite radiometer images for precipitation estimation, leveraging deterministic ordinary differential equation components to achieve precise domain alignment where labeled overlapping data is essentially unavailable. Addresses the domain-shift problem unique to satellite instruments.

entry.title: Contingent Exposure Routing for Financial AI: Outage Risk and the Cost of Indivisible Decisions

author.name: Shivam Gupta

entry.summary: This paper formulates how financial AI systems should route exposure during model outages so that failover does not concentrate correlated decision errors, analyzing expected squared price displacement through a market-impact response matrix. It derives an order-one concentration floor for shared backups, exact second moments for randomized routing of indivisible decisions, and rounding and swap-based bounds. It is a theory contribution on systemic risk in AI-mediated finance.

entry.title: OmniMed-Jev: Calibrating LVLM Confidence for Trustworthy Medical Multimodal Decisions via System One

author.name: Luyao Tang, Cheng Chen

entry.summary: OmniMed-Jev reformulates medical decisions in large vision-language models as native decision interfaces over runtime-supplied candidate sets, returning full distributions over mutually exclusive classes, binary findings, or bounded ordered values instead of generated text. This is motivated by decision-native interfaces like Jev and aims to make reported confidence reflect the actual decision rather than next-token probabilities. The design targets calibrated, trustworthy multimodal medical AI.

entry.title: Geometry-Dependent Bounds for Online Non-Monotone DR-Submodular Maximization

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: The paper proves improved first-order regret bounds for adversarial online maximization of non-monotone DR-submodular functions over down-closed convex sets, improving the 0.401 coefficient benchmark to 4/9 with one gradient query per round, plus geometry-dependent refinements and matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Reward as Observation: Learning Reward-Based Policies for Rapid Adaptation

author.name: Morgan Byrd, Maks Sorokin, Robert Wright, Sehoon Ha

entry.summary: This paper proposes conditioning policies only on rewards and actions rather than observations, enabling zero-shot transfer between environments with completely different observation spaces. The authors discuss the feasibility of reward-based policies and demonstrate training across three distinct environments with transfer to new ones.

entry.title: Latent Information Sharing for Accelerating Federated Learning

author.name: Seungjun Lee, Ensieh Khazaei, Dimitrios Hatzinakos, Baturalp Buyukates, Sunwoo Lee

entry.summary: The paper proposes sharing small amounts of hidden-layer activations between clients to directly mitigate data heterogeneity in federated learning, with theoretical convergence guarantees and claimed privacy preservation. Empirically it outperforms established client-drift baselines such as FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedProto, and SplitFed under fixed communication round budgets. Sharing activations rather than parameters attacks heterogeneity at its source.

entry.title: Robust Non-Clairvoyant Scheduling with Classification Models

author.name: Anthony Dugois, Vincent Fagnon, Giorgio Lucarelli

entry.summary: This paper studies non-clairvoyant single-machine scheduling to minimize sum of completion times, a problem with no constant-competitive algorithm, and introduces a learning-augmented robustness framework that uses a classifier's confusion matrix as side information about job classes. It characterizes how algorithm performance degrades gracefully with classifier quality rather than requiring perfect predictions. This exemplifies the learning-augmented algorithms program with an explicit error model.

entry.title: Robust Evidential Learning Through Latent Consistency

author.name: Charmaine Barker, Daniel Bethell, Simos Gerasimou

entry.summary: CLEAR is a lightweight post-hoc method that improves the robustness of evidential deep learning uncertainty estimates against adversarial and out-of-distribution inputs without retraining or altering base predictions. It characterizes group-conditioned latent geometry using held-out calibration data and perturbs inputs at inference to detect poorly supported high-evidence predictions.

entry.title: Let the Heads Talk: Beyond Diagonal Graph Attention

author.name: Riccardo Ali, Alessio Borgi, Mario Severino, Alessio Gravina, Davide Bacciu, Pietro Li\`o, Christopher Irwin

entry.summary: Using quiver representations, the authors isolate the transport primitive in sheaf neural networks and show standard multi-head attention implements only diagonal edge maps, preventing communication across heads along an edge. Allowing off-diagonal entries enables edge-conditioned cross-head communication before aggregation, yielding a generalized attention mechanism.

entry.title: Stochastic Rounding in Low-Precision Transformer Inference: A Variable-Precision Emulation Study of a Small GPT-2

author.name: Yohan Chatelain (Krembil Centre for Neuroinformatics, CAMH, Toronto, Canada), Pablo de Oliveira Castro (Universite Paris-Saclay, UVSQ, LI-PaRAD, Versailles, France)

entry.summary: The paper extends the PRISM rounding library with a variable-precision stochastic rounding algorithm to study whether stochastic rounding or round-to-nearest is preferable at individual operation sites in low-precision transformer inference. It provides a probabilistic forward-error bound for linear projections and site-level empirical analysis on a small GPT-2, showing the answer depends on network location.

entry.title: Sharp Non-Asymptotic Analysis of the Penalized Challenger in $\beta$-EB-TCI for Bernoulli Bandits

author.name: Nam Nguyen, Tuan Quang Dam

entry.summary: The authors provide sharp non-asymptotic stopping-time analysis for the top-two best-arm identification algorithm beta-EB-TCI on Bernoulli bandits, showing the stopping time matches the information-theoretic bound up to lower-order terms in a key regime. They also characterize challenger sampling frequency, identifying what remains open for the original algorithm without forced exploration.

entry.title: Relative Transitions, Not Absolute Destinations: A Transfer-and-Ground Framework for Target-Trajectory-Free Human Mobility Generation

author.name: Yidi Wang, Yunhe Zhang, Bangchao Deng, Dingqi Yang, Pengyang Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies generating human mobility trajectories for cities with no trajectory data, learning relative movement behavior from source cities and grounding it in target-city POI information alone. The framework disentangles reusable movement patterns from city-specific destination structure.

entry.title: On the Relationship between Model Quantization and Model Inversion Attacks

author.name: Rongke Liu, Youwen Zhu

entry.summary: The paper theoretically bounds how quantization changes the mutual information between inputs and prediction-derived categorical variables in neural networks, disentangling informational effects from optimization obstacles for inversion attacks, and analyzes how data characteristics modulate this relationship. It provides a principled account of whether quantization helps or hurts privacy against model inversion.

entry.title: Mean Spatial Frequency Decoupling for Learning-Based Uplink-to-Downlink Covariance Conversion in FDD Massive MIMO

author.name: Melih Can Zerin

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why learning-based uplink-to-downlink covariance conversion degrades as antenna count grows with fixed dataset size: a mean angle-of-arrival phase ramp whose oscillation rate scales with array size. It proposes a mean spatial frequency decoupling fix that restores learned methods' advantage over model-based baselines. This is a focused contribution to FDD massive MIMO channel estimation.

entry.title: Explainable Suicide Risk Assessment on Social Media with Multi-Task QLoRA

author.name: Xuan Zhong Feng, Geoffrey Martin, Hexin Dong, Yifan Peng

entry.summary: This system paper describes an entry for the IEEE BigData 2026 Cup on explainable suicide risk assessment, adapting Qwen2.5-Instruct models with QLoRA and an answer-masked causal objective across three tasks: risk classification, evidence phrase extraction, and factor identification. It combines efficient fine-tuning with clinically relevant explainability outputs. The work is relevant to applied mental-health NLP safety.

entry.title: On Evaluating Quantum Kernel Robustness for Low-Resource Cross-Corpus Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Lisan Al Amin, Lei Zhang, Vandana P. Janeja

entry.summary: The study compares quantum support vector machines against classical SVMs and MLPs for cross-corpus audio deepfake detection using frozen wav2vec 2.0 embeddings under a strict 200-sample budget, with features reduced to four dimensions to match near-term qubit limits. It evaluates robustness across ASVspoof corpora when training and evaluation conditions differ. Findings inform whether quantum kernels offer value in low-resource audio security.

entry.title: FedMAD: Modulation-Aware Directional Aggregation for Federated Learning in Remote Sensing Image Classification

author.name: Bar{\i}\c{s} B\"uy\"ukta\c{s}, Beg\"um Demir

entry.summary: FedMAD is a personalized federated learning framework for remote sensing image classification that separates globally shared representation parameters from client-specific adaptation parameters, using modulation-aware directional aggregation to handle heterogeneous distributions arising from geography, season, and acquisition conditions. It targets collaborative training across decentralized satellite image archives without direct data access.

entry.title: SmoothOperator: Enhancing Representations for Fine-grained Open-set Recognition via Modulated Label Smoothing

author.name: Thiru Thillai Nadarasar Bahavan, Yu Xia, Sachith Seneviratne, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: SmoothOperator improves open-set recognition by replacing uniform label smoothing with a modulation scheme that adapts smoothing per sample based on embedding quality. This refines the compact-and-separated feature spaces that spherical representation learning methods rely on for rejecting unseen classes.

entry.title: Degree-Corrected Joint Matrix Factorization for Multilayer Community Detection

author.name: Alexandra Dache, Manon Rustin, Arnaud Vandaele, Nicolas Gillis

entry.summary: The paper proposes a joint nonnegative symmetric matrix trifactorization method for community detection in multilayer networks, enforcing disjoint communities shared across layers while allowing layer-specific connectivity and degree corrections. This balances consistency across layers with heterogeneity within layers.

entry.title: Optimal Momentum Methods for Stochastic Multilevel Compositional Optimization

author.name: Wei Jiang, Rui Yan, Sifan Yang, Yuanyu Wan, Lijun Zhang, Zechao Li

entry.summary: The authors analyze stochastic optimization of nested compositions of several smooth non-convex functions using only stochastic gradient and function estimates per level. Momentum-based estimators with mini-batching achieve the optimal sample complexity of O(epsilon^-4) for epsilon-stationary points without strong average smoothness assumptions. This closes a gap in the theory of multilevel compositional optimization.

entry.title: Sequential Capacity of Quantum Processes with Finite Memory

author.name: Yibin Wang

entry.summary: The study formalizes how complex a quantum device's responses can become as runtime grows with fixed internal memory, via a notion of sequential response capacity for adaptive testing stages. It proves a tight law relating this capacity to run length and probability resolution, showing capacity grows on the order of K log K, achieved by time-dependent phase rotations on a single qubit with no extra memory.

entry.title: SCM-based Fairness and Faithful Explainability for Legal Document Classification

author.name: Yasmina El Kacemi, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari, Ali Mohammed Mansoor Alsahag

entry.summary: This study examines whether debiasing LegalBERT on the ECtHR alleged-violations corpus also changes the faithfulness of SHAP explanations, using a fairness-regularized variant that penalizes stereotypical warmth and competence representations. It jointly evaluates predictive performance, demographic fairness, and explanation faithfulness across five seeds, an interaction typically studied separately.

entry.title: Evaluating Biomedical Reranking for LLM-Based Question Answering over Longitudinal Clinical Notes

author.name: Maryam Shahbaz Ali, Laura B. Strachan, Caitlin Sherman, Mark Kovler, Eleanor Mackey, Syed Muhammad Anwar

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether biomedical reranking (PubMedBERT dense retrieval, BM25, weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, and MedCPT cross-encoder reranking) improves evidence selection and answer quality in a locally deployed RAG pipeline over long longitudinal clinical records. Evaluation uses 1,000 question-answer pairs from 200 bariatric surgery patients. Reranking measurably improved downstream answer quality in this clinical setting.

entry.title: Yo-ByT5: Efficient and High-Fidelity Diacritic Restoration for Yor\`ub\'a

author.name: Ahmad Samuel Gali (University of Lagos), Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad (Bayero University Kano, Imperial College London)

entry.summary: Yo-ByT5 is a byte-level model fine-tuned from ByT5-small for automatic diacritic restoration in Yoruba, matching the strongest existing model (mT5-base) with roughly half the parameters while achieving better text fidelity. This matters for making Yoruba text usable in downstream NLP. It contributes to low-resource language tooling.

entry.title: From Web(logs) to Web(AI): Questions, Platforms, and Methods across Twenty Editions of ICWSM

author.name: Koustuv Saha, Eshwar Chandrasekharan

entry.summary: The authors analyze 2,139 ICWSM contributions from 2007 to 2026 using topic modeling and textual problem-framing cues, tracing shifts from blogs to Twitter to Reddit, rising governance and harm research cues, and methodological change as AI reshapes online communication. A valuable field-level retrospective at a moment when AI agents are entering social platforms. Useful for understanding where computational social science is heading.

entry.title: Domain generalization and synthetic data in object detection: the enabler, the probe, and the gap

author.name: Elfi I. S. Hofmeijer, Ella P. Fokkinga, Friso G. Heslinga, Klamer Schutte, J\"orgen M. Karlholm

entry.summary: This is an object-detection-centric review of domain generalization, examining synthetic data through three complementary perspectives: as an enabler, a probe, and a gap in current research. It highlights that DG for detection lags behind classification due to localization and multi-scale challenges. It offers a useful roadmap for robustness research under distribution shift.

entry.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Anti-UAV Detection under Controlled Fog Degradation: Fog-Aware Training and Clear-Sky Tradeoff

author.name: Gur Levy Birkental, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari, Ali Mohammed Mansoor Alsahag

entry.summary: The paper presents the first severity-controlled fog benchmark for vision-based anti-UAV detection, applying synthetic fog at ten levels to Anti-UAV300 and comparing a clear-trained YOLOv5m baseline to fog-aware training. It finds sharply non-linear degradation front-loaded at light-to-moderate fog, with large mAP losses, and quantifies the clear-sky tradeoff of fog-aware training. This informs deployment of security-critical drone detection.

entry.title: VoxelSynth3D: Interpretable Volumetric Image-Domain Metal Artifact Reduction with a Paired Synthetic CLINIC-Metal Benchmark

author.name: Amritesh Banerjee, Abdul Basit, Renil Renji Joseph, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: VoxelSynth3D is a training-free, interpretable 3D image-domain framework for reducing metal artifacts in postoperative musculoskeletal CT, combining support masking, normalized tissue synthesis, deviation gating, and edge refinement while preserving implant voxels. The authors also release Synthetic CLINIC-Metal, a controlled paired synthetic benchmark built from no-metal CTPelvic1K volumes. This avoids dependence on raw projections or models that shift across scanners.

entry.title: Beyond Domain-Level Adaptation: Margin-Oriented Semantic-Appearance Interaction Correction for Personalized Federated Vision-Language Models

author.name: Wentao Yue, Qingyu Mao, Tianyou Lai, Ahmed M. Abdelmoniem, Qilei Li

entry.summary: MOSAIC improves personalized federated parameter-efficient fine-tuning of vision-language models by showing that domain shifts vary across semantic classes and only some class-domain residuals harm the image-text decision margin. It constructs margin-oriented corrections that selectively fix damaging residuals rather than treating domains as class-agnostic transformations.

entry.title: Continuous Conditioning of VLAs with Augmenting EMG and Visual Task Descriptors

author.name: Edward W. Staley, Connor O. Pyles, Rahul Hingorani, Frank Camargo, Griffin Milsap, Jared Markowitz, Matthew S. Fifer, Michael Wolmetz

entry.summary: This paper tests whether vision-language-action models can use non-language modalities for task conditioning, introducing an EMG-conditioned VLA using 8-channel electromyography envelopes and a visually annotated VLA using segmentation annotations. On a cube-selection task across three human participants, the EMG-conditioned model matches language conditioning, supporting multimodal task specification.

entry.title: DexPolicy: Scheduled Exploration for Trajectory-Guided Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Siyuan Qian, Yanjun Li, Zeyu Zhang, Yandong Guo, Boxin Shi, Hao Tang

entry.summary: DexPolicy addresses a failure mode in RL for dexterous manipulation where action noise useful for discovering finger-object contacts interferes with precise control, causing PPO runs to stagnate near initial noise levels. It makes exploration scale an explicit annealed function of training steps while holding other training components fixed, and studies PPO, critic-free GRPO continuation, and a flow-parameterized PPO variant. The method refines hand-object trajectories from human video.

entry.title: Beyond Leaderboard Scores: A Deployment-Focused Protocol for Interpretable Tracking Evaluation in Pedestrian-Centric Environments

author.name: Dominik Wojcikiewicz, Diego Paez-Granados

entry.summary: This paper proposes a deployment-focused evaluation protocol for pedestrian tracking that uses shared detections to isolate tracker behavior and evaluates initialization, gap continuation, identity recovery, close-neighbor association, and load-dependent runtime, retaining HOTA as a complementary aggregate. It argues aggregate leaderboard scores give limited insight into when and how trajectories fail. This improves diagnostic power for robots operating among pedestrians.

entry.title: Controllable Stochastic Quantization Encoding for Adversarially Robust Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Yujia Liu, Peiyu Liu, Yajing Zheng, Tiejun Huang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a stochastic quantization encoding method for SNNs that improves adversarial robustness by exploiting the randomness that appears to underlie Poisson encoding's robustness advantage over direct encoding. Unlike prior defenses focused on training strategies, it targets the input encoding stage, an underexplored defense surface. Results are demonstrated on image classification under adversarial perturbations.

entry.title: Real-Time Human-Adaptive Task Allocation for Multi-Human Multi-Robot Supervision

author.name: Seabin Lee, Sujeong Park, Nayoung Kim, Sungjin Park, Haechan Jung, Changjoo Nam

entry.summary: The paper proposes allocating robot supervision tasks across multiple human operators based on their real-time cognitive states rather than fixed supervisory capacity, accounting for workload and fatigue fluctuations. This maintains balanced mental load in scenarios where several operators intermittently teleoperate several robots. It addresses a practical gap in human-robot teaming where static allocation leads to operator overload.

entry.title: Interaction-Stiffness-Guided Basis Allocation in Dynamic Movement Primitives for Efficient Skill Transfer

author.name: Chan Xu, Silu Chen, Dehao Wang, Xiyu Chen, Dexin Jiang, Chi Zhang, Guilin Yang, Chenguang Yang, Zaojun Fang

entry.summary: SC-DMPs extend Dynamic Movement Primitives with adaptive basis allocation guided by a stage-criticality index built from operator-robot interaction stiffness and cross-demonstration trajectory variability. Basis centers are redistributed in normalized time so approximation capacity concentrates on precision-critical task stages. This improves skill transfer efficiency in contact-rich robotic skill learning from human demonstrations.

entry.title: Towards Physical Underwater Robotic Assistance for Scuba Diver Movement in Confined Spaces

author.name: Demetrious T. Kutzke, Junaed Sattar

entry.summary: Introduces RADMCS, described as a first-of-its-kind wearable robot providing thruster-actuated directional guidance to scuba divers, helping them maintain fixed distance from subsea structures in confined spaces. Distinct from prior propulsive-assistance exoskeletons, it targets diver safety near hazards like reefs, drilling instrumentation, or unexploded ordnance. Combines wearable hardware with perception techniques.

entry.title: Gradient-Guided Density Peak Clustering

author.name: Yikun Zhang, Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes gradient-guided density peak clustering (GGDPC), which inserts a gradient ascent step before each nearest-neighbor uphill search to stabilize the density-peak clustering graph in low-density regions. The authors develop stability theory linking the algorithm to the gradient ascent flow of the population density. This improves the robustness and interpretability of a widely used clustering method.

entry.title: Speak Not of Data Inefficiency

author.name: axel_sdq

entry.summary: A LessWrong post challenging the common claim that humans are data-efficient learners compared to LLMs. The author computes that a preschooler consumes tens of terabytes of visual and sensorimotor data by age three and argues that GPT-2 and a preschooler are so different in embodiment, learning signals, and input distribution that data-efficiency comparisons are largely meaningless.

entry.title: Rules to Tools: Executable Checks for LLM Agents in Scientific Computing

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Guojiang Zhao, Chen Xu, Shanshan Zhong, Xiaochuan Li, Ji Zeng, Guolin Ke

entry.summary: R2T supplies prepared executable checks of written scientific requirements for coding agents doing SciCode-style program repair, comparing matched groups receiving either text requirements or callable check implementations. Tool access improves complete repair from 26/30 to 29/30 in one cohort and 13/16 to 15/16 in another, though the larger shared-definition cohort ties and confidence intervals are wide.

entry.title: A Simple Doxastic Deontic Logic for Norm-Guided Decision Making

author.name: Thorsten Engesser, Agata Ciabattoni

entry.summary: This paper introduces a doxastic deontic logic combining conditional norms with multi-agent KD45 beliefs, enabling norms to depend on what agents believe about facts and other norms. It defines the Doxastic Norm Compliance Optimization Problem, where agents minimize weighted norm violations, distinguishing subjective from objective optimization and giving conditions under which they coincide. This provides formal foundations for norm-governed autonomous decision making.

entry.title: Nous: Learning and Certifying Memory Decisions Before Source Calibration

author.name: Pranav Singh

entry.summary: This theory paper separates learning, calibration, and revision certification for belief-based agent memory, proving that learning useful Bayes decisions and certifying their improvement requires Theta(l^-2) records while fixed-precision source estimation requires Theta(l^-4) as persistence vanishes. It concludes memory decisions can improve with quadratically fewer observations than source calibration demands.

entry.title: CAVE-Mem: Boundary-Aware Experience Validation for Memory Search

author.name: Xinyu Li

entry.summary: CAVE-Mem is a training-free framework for long-term memory agents that represents past search experiences as typed intervention operators with applicability, boundary, and utility conditions, allowing an experience to modify a base answer only when boundary conditions hold. This guards against harmful reuse of relevant-looking but contextually mismatched memories.

entry.title: Signal-Noise Factorization Isolates Nuisance Variation into Removable Subspaces

author.name: Sakin Kirti, Joel Zylberberg

entry.summary: Building on recent theory of representation geometry, this paper constructs regularizers that reinforce signal-noise factorization (SNF) and signal-signal factorization (SSF) during training. Experiments on CIFAR-100 show that enhancing SNF improves performance while SSF regularization has different effects, clarifying which geometric properties matter for inference.

entry.title: Repurposing Obsolete Representations for Post-Deployment Adaptation

author.name: Daniel Bethell, Charmaine Barker, Simos Gerasimou

entry.summary: The authors propose Deep Repurposing (DR), a post-hoc framework for adapting deployed models when part of the output space becomes obsolete, estimating latent geometry of obsolete and retained regions and reallocating evidence via an analytic repair map without gradient updates. This avoids costly fine-tuning while repairing both predictions and representations.

entry.title: Effective Resistance and Graph Neural Network Reliability in Tissue-Specific Interactomes

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: This work examines whether effective resistance in tissue-specific protein interaction networks signals which GNN function-annotation predictions to distrust. Across 24 interactomes, the residual signal beyond inverse degree explains additional per-node loss in 19 of 24 held-out networks, even after controlling for entropy, degree, and other difficulty measures.

entry.title: EyeTAG: Eye Trajectory-Aware Gaze Estimation

author.name: Jungmin Lee, Niamat Ullah, Yoseob Han

entry.summary: EyeTAG is a causal multi-frame gaze estimation framework that explicitly models gaze trajectories by feeding back differenced recent predictions as a kinematic token, exploiting translation invariance for subject-invariant motion cues. This reduces jitter and improves temporal consistency over single-frame and appearance-based multi-frame methods.

entry.title: Harnessing Vision-Language Models for Perceptual Quality Assessment and Autonomous Content Adjustment in Augmented Reality

author.name: Elias Rotondo (Duke University), Lin Duan (Duke University), Yanming Xiu (Duke University), Sangjun Eom (Duke University), Conrad Li (Duke University), Maria Gorlatova (Duke University)

entry.summary: From a Duke University team, this paper presents an automated framework using VLMs to evaluate and predict visual fidelity of AR content, replacing costly user studies, and autonomously adjusting content to improve immersion and comfort. It addresses scene geometry constraints, jitter, and temporal instability in head-mounted AR. The work is a practical step toward scalable AR quality assurance.

entry.title: FFBL-Coop: Association-Decoupled Cooperative 3D Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Haoxin Wu, Xiaokai Bai

entry.summary: FFBL-Coop proposes a fuse-first, bind-later framework for cooperative 3D multi-object tracking that separates instance admission from identity management. Confidence-ranked slot allocation and unified representation aggregation decouple evidence integration across agents and time from identity inheritance, reducing compounding errors from cross-view appearance differences and spatial misalignment.

entry.title: In CEM, a World Model Is Also a Proposal Mechanism

author.name: Oliver Obst, Frieder Stolzenburg

entry.summary: This empirical study disentangles the two roles of world models in the cross-entropy method: scoring action sequences and shaping the proposal distribution of future iterations. By rescoring saved candidate pools across four model types on Walker and Cheetah tasks, it characterizes how scoring errors propagate into proposal contraction and search behavior.

entry.title: Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders

author.name: Parthiv Chatterjee, Dhiraj Golhar, Ummesalma Diwan, Sourish Dasgupta, Manjunath Joshi, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: REPAIR addresses the recoverability gap in personalization encoders, where compressed preference states miss evidence still present in the frozen encoder's cached per-timestep representations. It compares cached representations with the current preference state in a learned coordinate space, selects corrective patterns across full history, recent interactions, and bursts, and adds their aggregate correction before the task head. Encoder-host repair reuses existing forward-pass representations, limiting extra cost.

entry.title: Initial condition recovery in nonlinear damped viscous photoacoustic tomography using a convolutional neural network-guided gradient-free optimization framework

author.name: Madhu Gupta, Anwesa Dey, Prapti Tala, Souvik Roy

entry.summary: This work tackles the inverse problem of recovering initial pressure in photoacoustic tomography under nonlinear acoustic propagation and viscous attenuation, proving well-posedness of the forward problem and using a CNN-guided gradient-free optimization for reconstruction. It combines rigorous PDE analysis with a learned initialization strategy.

entry.title: Child-Adapted Structured Phonological Representations for Interpretable Speech Sound Analysis

author.name: Abner Hernandez, Tom\'as Arias Vergara, Andreas Maier, Paula Andrea P\'erez-Toro

entry.summary: The paper adapts PhonoQ-2.0, a model producing structured phonological representations, to child speech using CHILDES-aligned data, comparing three alignment-supervision conditions and two initialization strategies across 1,352 consonant targets from 58 children. Child-speech adaptation improves voicing recognition from 0.922 to 0.972-0.987 macro-F1, with manner of articulation more sensitive to alignment supervision.
