entry.title: A Comprehensive Review of One-Pixel Attack: Research Status, Taxonomy, Applications, Regulation Policy and Future Directions

author.name: Mirza Niaz Morshed, Md. Masudul Islam, Galib Muhammad Shahriar Himel, Md. Aslam Uddin, Hui Liu, Md. Shafiqul Islam

entry.summary: This PRISMA-guided survey synthesizes one-pixel attack research from 2017 to 2026, providing a unified multi-axis taxonomy spanning algorithmic foundations, black-box evolutionary optimization, hybrid and program-synthesis attacks, defenses, interpretability, applications in safety-critical domains, and regulation policy. It consolidates coverage that existing adversarial-attack surveys treat only fragmentarily.

entry.title: Real-Time Whole-Body Safe Motion Generation for Multi-Segment Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots

author.name: Fangju Yang, Siyi Ma, Tonghao Guan, Tingcong Liu, Hang Yang, Zhengqiang Zhang, Jian S. Dai, Ke Wu

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified actuation-space framework for planar multi-segment tendon-driven continuum robots, using an energy-based variable-curvature model with analytical Jacobians for inverse kinematics and safety monitoring. A multipoint control barrier function QP enforces backbone clearance under obstacle motion and actuation bounds, with decision dimension depending only on the number of actuated segments. The model closely agrees with GVS references with small curvature error.

entry.title: From Proposal to Verified Effect: Praxa, an Evidence-Bound Harness for Governed AI Agent Execution

author.name: Stefan G. Creadore

entry.summary: Praxa is an agent harness that explicitly separates proposal, authority, dispatch, verified external effect, and promotion into distinct auditable states using deterministic admission, brokered execution, external read-back, and reviewed promotion. The evidence includes a repository-local audit passing all tests and a small Terminal-Bench pilot, though the authors candidly note that raw transcripts and independent reproduction are unavailable.

entry.title: Build2SPARQL: A Large-Scale Text-to-SPARQL Benchmark Dataset for Building Knowledge Graph Querying

author.name: Wooyoung Jung

entry.summary: Build2SPARQL is a large-scale text-to-SPARQL benchmark for building automation knowledge graphs using Brick and ASHRAE 223P ontologies, generated by a KG-grounded pipeline where SPARQL queries come from validated graph-traversal code and LLMs generate only the natural-language questions. This design avoids LLM-generated query artifacts and controls label quality.

entry.title: Spatial Strategies, Not Actions: Vector-Quantized Geodesics as Tools for LLM-Driven Agents

author.name: Gabriel Turinici

entry.summary: The paper proposes an architecture where an LLM orchestrator uses vector-quantized geodesic trajectories from grid worlds as named tools, associating natural-language behavioral descriptions with each offline and selecting tools online. Low-level control is delegated to primitive actions executing the chosen trajectory. This addresses the critique that LLM agents lack genuine spatial understanding.

entry.title: Cybernetic and Epistemic: A Missing Vocabulary for Trustworthy Agentic Delegation

author.name: J\'er\'emie Lumbroso

entry.summary: A conceptual/position paper arguing the field lacks vocabulary to distinguish cybernetic language (words that coordinate action) from epistemic language (words that coordinate understanding) in AI delegation channels, naming the failure mode of explanation-shaped output calibrated for approval rather than truth. It connects CS-education research on code supervision to AI oversight. Conceptually valuable for thinking about oversight of code-generating agents.

entry.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Personalized Health Checkup Interpretation and Guidance

author.name: HyungJun Kim, Taehan Lee, Soojin Cheon

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-agent LLM system for interpreting personalized health checkup results, mapping multiple intents to task-specific agents that run in parallel and synthesizing outputs. On 120 Korean compound queries with synthetic records, the multi-agent setting improved weighted LLM-judge scores from 1.695 to 1.797 with statistical significance, with consistent gains across multiple judges. The work demonstrates where agent decomposition helps in healthcare question answering.

entry.title: SPHERE: Adaptive VR Indoor Scene Generation via LLM-Enhanced Spatial Preference Learning and Human-in-the-Loop RL

author.name: Hyeonmin Lee, Zheng Wei, Kyungmin Kwon, Jumin Seo, Jiwon Park, Hayoung Oh

entry.summary: SPHERE is a VR framework that turns one-shot 3D indoor scene synthesis into continuous human-AI co-creation by extracting persistent spatial preferences from natural multimodal interactions such as speech and controller edits. It abstracts edits into hierarchical constraints for geometric resilience and uses human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning to update retrieval policies across sessions. This reduces the repetitive, fatiguing nature of immersive scene authoring.

entry.title: A Comparative Explainability Framework for DeBERTa-v3 in Zero-Shot Medical Abstract Classification

author.name: Javier Diaz Esteban-Herreros, David Mu\~noz-Valero, Raquel Mart\'inez-Espa\~na, Jose M. Juarez, Juan Moreno-Garcia

entry.summary: The paper presents a comparative explainability audit of DeBERTa-v3 under zero-shot classification of medical abstracts, addressing the XAI disagreement problem where different attribution methods yield divergent explanations. Five explanation methods (SHAP, LIME, occlusion, Input x Gradient, Attention x Gradient) are standardized and compared over an NLI setup with enriched hypotheses on the Medical Abstracts corpus. It contributes a structured methodology for reconciling divergent explanations in medical NLP.

entry.title: Pushing CPU Speech Synthesis to the Wall: Extreme Inference Tuning under Serverless Architecture and Billing

author.name: Pakorn Nathong, Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: The paper presents billing-aware neural TTS serving on serverless CPUs, optimizing CPU-seconds and GB-seconds rather than throughput or latency, via request-sized concurrent inference and a reclaimable instance lifecycle that releases memory state during idle periods. It highlights how instance-billed serverless pricing changes optimization objectives for model serving.

entry.title: Per-Node Activation Function Evolution in Indirectly Encoded Substrates: Solvability, Limits, and Emergent Diversity

author.name: Romain Claret, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Kilian Stoffel

entry.summary: A companion paper showing that uniform activation functions create hard search limits: monotonic functions fail to solve parity beyond XOR in sparse evolved substrates while a single oscillatory unit suffices at all scales, a gap of search rather than representation. The work evolves the first known solutions to parity on sparse CPPN substrates via per-node activation evolution.

entry.title: TabJoinBench: A Benchmark for Joinable Table Discovery

author.name: Sandipan De, Jin Wang, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: TabJoinBench is a benchmark for evaluating join discovery methods, which identify tables in large data repositories that can augment a query table for tasks like feature engineering and business intelligence. It covers semantic, relational, and hybrid data lake scenarios and introduces composable perturbations spanning structural, representation, and semantic changes with source-specific validation. This enables reproducible, fair comparison where prior work used method-specific benchmarks.

entry.title: Understanding Issues, Causes and Solutions in Open-Source LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Asad Ur Rehman, Syed Mohammad Kashif, Ruiyin Li, Peng Liang, Zengyang Li, Arif Ali Khan

entry.summary: This empirical software engineering study analyzes 22,848 closed issues from 21 open-source LLM-based multi-agent system projects to characterize problems practitioners face, their causes, and candidate solutions. It combines automated and manual analysis to map the practical failure landscape of MAS development.

entry.title: Model validation in machine learning: A scenario-based guide from hold-out splits to nested group cross-validation in biomedical and applied research

author.name: Mehmet Baygin, Sengul Dogan, Turker Tuncer

entry.summary: A tutorial on model validation schemes — hold-out, k-fold, leave-one-out, group-aware, and nested group cross-validation — grounded in biomedical settings like EEG epochs, paired-eye OCT, and multicenter data. Eight controlled scenarios contrast leakage-prone and leakage-safe designs with auditable metrics and a reproducible simulation. Valuable practitioner education for avoiding leakage-induced overoptimism in applied research.

entry.title: Exposing the Cost of Deep Learning Audio Development

author.name: Constance Douwes, Paul Magron, Romain Serizel

entry.summary: Proposes a methodology to estimate the energy cost of the often-overlooked development phase of deep learning (prototyping and experiments) using activity logs from the Grid5000 platform, applied to four audio projects from a research team. Findings show development can cost as much as or more than final model training.

entry.title: Integrating Fairness and Explainability in a Multiple Instance Reinforcement Learning System

author.name: Bente Hinkenhuis, Seyed Sahand Mohammadi Ziabari, Ali Mohammed Mansoor Alsahag

entry.summary: The study combines RL-based multiple instance learning, adversarial debiasing, and preference-conditioned hypernetworks for student-at-risk prediction, where each student is a bag of weakly labeled interactions and an RL agent selects informative instances. It evaluates whether a user-defined preference scalar can continuously control the fairness-accuracy tradeoff. A multidisciplinary integration relevant to responsible AI in education.

entry.title: Metacognitive Reasoning in Energy Based Models using Instance Based Learning Theory

author.name: Tailia Malloy, Prateek Kumar Rajput, Serge Lionel Nikiema, Cleotilde Gonzalez, Tegawend\'e F. Bissyand\'e

entry.summary: The paper explores metacognition in AI: estimating confidence and allocating compute before producing an output, which transformers with LLMs struggle to do. It builds on energy-based models, which natively support interpretable uncertainty and dynamic resource allocation, and incorporates Instance-Based Learning Theory from cognitive science to implement metacognitive reasoning. The work bridges cognitive science theory and energy-based architectures.

entry.title: Quantifying the Impact of Ambulance Ramping: A Multi-Year Analysis of Victorian Emergency Medical Services Cases

author.name: Ayesha Tanveer, Khandakar Ahmed, Assefa Teshome, Oyetunde Gbadeyan, Ziad Nehme

entry.summary: This study analyzes 2.85 million ambulance attendances in Victoria, Australia from 2020 to 2024 to quantify the scale and dynamics of ambulance ramping across the statewide EMS system. Using exploratory data analysis with interval decomposition, Pareto concentration, and cross-correlations over 59 hospitals and 79 local government areas, it characterizes this operational bottleneck at scale.

entry.title: CAGE-NAS: Certified Functional Descent for Efficient Model Growth

author.name: Santiago Florido Gomez, St\'ephane Rivaud

entry.summary: CAGE-NAS formulates the decision of when to grow a progressively trained neural network as an admissibility criterion on functional gradient approximations: the architecture stays fixed while a certified functional gradient descent step is possible, and a function-preserving expansion is triggered when the criterion fails. In a controlled setting with exact certification it produces architectures positioned favorably in the accuracy-cost trade-off. This brings certified, function-space reasoning to progressive NAS.

entry.title: Least-time Gradient Flow

author.name: Alessandro Betti, Marco Gori, Stefano Melacci, Jinwei Zhao

entry.summary: This theoretical work prescribes the speed of gradient flow directly on the risk, making the risk decay follow an exact chosen dynamic, and then studies the regularized problem of minimizing time-to-zero-risk. The authors prove the optimal rate profile is a linearly scaled cycloid with a characteristic 2/3 exponent near zero risk, matching a previously conjectured power law.

entry.title: FedFit: Federated Fine-Tuning of LLMs via Vector-Bank Parameterization and Quantization

author.name: Hang Zou, Chao Zhang, Yuzhi Yang, Yu Tian, Samson Lasaulce, M\'erouane Debbah

entry.summary: FedFit reduces communication overhead in federated LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs by reconstructing adapter matrices from two compact disjoint global vector banks, and resolves the aggregation dilemma between sum-of-products and product-of-sums implementations via an alternating optimization schedule with quantization. This targets the core bottleneck of privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning.

entry.title: System Attribution in LLM Brand Recommendations: Single Responses Identify the System, Aggregated Brand Profiles Do Not Transfer

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: Using 6,475 stored responses from five deployed LLM endpoints on recommendation-style queries, the paper shows a character n-gram classifier can attribute individual responses to the generating system, but aggregated brand-recommendation profiles do not transfer across systems. It also documents practical audit artifacts such as truncated outputs under token caps.

entry.title: Inference for stochastic differential equations driven by weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion using neural networks and the Euler approximation

author.name: J. H. Ramirez-Gonzalez

entry.summary: This paper addresses parameter estimation of drift, diffusion, and noise covariance for stochastic differential equations driven by weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion, using neural networks combined with Euler approximation schemes. It extends statistical inference for SDEs beyond standard Brownian and fractional noise settings.

entry.title: LESS: Lightweight Evolutionary Supernet Search in Minutes

author.name: Aviral Gandhi, Jinglue Xu, Jialong Li, Hitoshi Iba

entry.summary: LESS combines a brief fair hard-path warm-up with discrete CMA-ES search over a supernet, evaluating proposals as decoded hard genotypes after candidate-conditioned supernet updates. On NAS-Bench-201 it reaches 93.189% CIFAR-10 accuracy in about 409 seconds, nearly matching FairNAS at a fraction of the cost.

entry.title: Convergence Analysis of STORM Under Different Geometries

author.name: Wei Jiang, Yibo Wang, Wenhao Yang, Rui Yan, Lijun Zhang, Zechao Li

entry.summary: The authors analyze the STORM stochastic recursive momentum algorithm without the strong average smoothness assumption used in prior work, proving it retains an O(T^-1/4) rate for nonconvex objectives and PL-condition guarantees via an auxiliary-sequence technique. This extends the applicability of variance-reduced momentum methods to broader problem geometries. It complements the same group's compositional optimization paper in this batch.

entry.title: Lower Bounds for Stochastic First-Order Algorithms with Variance Reduction in Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Optimization

author.name: Jiayi Song, Zi Xu

entry.summary: This paper establishes complexity lower bounds for stochastic first-order algorithms in nonconvex-concave minimax optimization, notably allowing algorithms in the lower-bound class to use variance reduction techniques. The results cover objectives with Lipschitz continuous joint gradients over a compact convex dual domain, with accuracy measured via the gradient norm of the Moreau envelope, and extend prior lower bounds that imposed more restrictive algorithmic assumptions.

entry.title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Low-Resource Languages: Adapting Ragas and Comparative Ranking for Romanian

author.name: Claudiu Creanga, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: The paper investigates LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation for RAG systems in Romanian, adapting the Ragas framework with Gemini 2.5 and Gemini 3 and introducing AdminRo-Eval, a dataset of Romanian administrative documents annotated by native speakers. It compares direct scoring, comparative ranking, and granular decomposition across faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance metrics.

entry.title: Typological Alignment of Stack-Based Language Models on Mildly Context-Sensitive Artificial Languages

author.name: Nadine El-Naggar, Tatsuki Kuribayashi, Ted Briscoe

entry.summary: The paper extends simulations of LM learning biases and language typology, testing stack-based LMs on cross-serial dependencies in artificial languages to probe whether architectural inductive biases explain typological frequencies like SOV word order. It connects cognitive theorizing about learning biases to LM architecture design. A niche but rigorous contribution to computational typology.

entry.title: Robust Online Aero-Engine Blade Defect Detection via Dual-Alignment Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Zhaoyang Wang, Haiyong Chen, Dongying Li, Yining Wang, Huapeng Wu, Xinwei Lv, Atik Shahariar

entry.summary: The authors propose ABDD, a test-time adaptation framework for aero-engine blade defect detection that handles domain shifts across production lines and imaging conditions, with a dual-alignment strategy addressing the challenge of sparse defects making pseudolabels unreliable. It targets practical online industrial inspection reliability. The contribution is a well-motivated applied adaptation method.

entry.title: Form and Void: Entangled Composition through an Autonomous AI Agent

author.name: Shiwen Wang, Jian Yang, Xu Wang, Xincan Wang, Weiming Dong

entry.summary: FaV-A is a multimodal agent for generating positive-negative space compositions in images, where two semantic concepts share a common boundary and must be coordinated. Direct single-pass prompting of text-to-image models fails at this, so the agent uses a staged procedural process to achieve entangled composition.

entry.title: MorphoBranch: A Fine-Structure-Preserving Workbench for Morphometric Analysis of Branched Cellular Structures

author.name: Song Zhiying, Ling Hanyi, Wu Junyi, Jiang Yangbo

entry.summary: MorphoBranch is a workbench for morphometric analysis of fluorescence-labeled branched cellular structures like neuronal and microglial arbors, combining a deterministic image-to-graph morphometry engine with an LLM-assisted refinement engine that maps natural-language requests to corrections. It targets preservation of fine, weakly labeled processes that fragment under skeleton-based methods. The human-reviewable design supports scientific credibility.

entry.title: Online Planning for Sparse Ground Target Search from a High-Altitude UAV under Partial Observability

author.name: Ashik E Rasul, Hyung-Jin Yoon

entry.summary: The paper develops online planning for UAV target search from high altitude, where a target may be in view but effectively unobservable due to its small apparent scale. Instead of physically repositioning — restricted by urban airspace rules — the UAV uses camera pan-tilt-zoom to actively gather information under partial observability. PTZ-based active sensing as a flight-regulation-compliant alternative to active navigation is a pragmatic contribution.

entry.title: How many AI agents are running unattended right now?

author.name: Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel

entry.summary: This post provides Fermi estimates of the number of continuously running AI agents worldwide, defining a digital mind as an agent running unattended for over 24 hours, and estimates 300k-1M concurrent agent loops with perhaps 5,000-25,000 in 24-hour-plus unattended stretches. It triangulates from global token usage, Anthropic's reported 30,000 concurrent agents, and OpenAI's reported agent-workdays per researcher. This quantifies a key exposure variable for agentic AI risk.

entry.title: Four Ways to Grow a Classifier and Why One of Them Cannot Learn

author.name: Cagri Temel

entry.summary: This paper analyzes four constructive classifier growth decisions under a fixed protocol and proves that the natural way to deepen a soft decision tree — turning leaves into gates whose children inherit the parent class distribution — yields identically zero gradients for new gates, so the added level can never learn. It provides an exact diagnosis and a fix for this failure mode.

entry.title: From Image Latent Space to Fuzzy Rules: Interpretable Analysis of Gastrointestinal Foundation Model

author.name: Michael D. Vasilakakis (Department of Computer Science and Biomedical Informatics, University of Thessaly, Lamia, Greece), Dimitris K. Iakovidis (Department of Computer Science and Biomedical Informatics, University of Thessaly, Lamia, Greece)

entry.summary: The authors propose a prototype-based fuzzy-rule framework that interprets patch-level features of pretrained foundation models in gastrointestinal endoscopy without fine-tuning, expressing features as prototype similarities classified by human-readable IF-THEN rules. This makes latent representations of safety-critical medical models inspectable. It addresses interpretability requirements for clinical adoption.

entry.title: Simplex vs Timaeus: Round One

author.name: Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel

entry.summary: Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel compares the research agendas of Simplex (developmental interpretability via singular learning theory) and Timaeus (belief-state geometry via computational mechanics), mapping their intellectual lineages to Watanabe and Crutchfield respectively. He contrasts their focus on weight space versus activation space and training versus inference. This clarifies two prominent mathematical approaches to understanding neural networks.

entry.title: Characterizing a Configuration Where Inference-Time PRM-Pruned Fragment Grafting Is Inert: Evidence from Three Reasoning LMs

author.name: Khawaja Murad ul Hassan, Mehran Ebrahimi

entry.summary: This paper isolates PRM-Pruned Fragment Grafting (PPFG), a minimal inference-time intervention that grafts high-PRM prefixes of pruned chains into sibling decoding trajectories, and shows with n=500 and three seeds on MATH500 that it is statistically indistinguishable from independent sampling. The result characterizes an operating point where prior fragment-grafting gains likely depend on compensating ingredients.

entry.title: EviGraph: Proof-Carrying Selective Recommendation over Temporal Public-Service Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Yixi Zhou, Sikun Wang, Lei Fan, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: EviGraph distinguishes critical decision requirements from details that can remain unresolved, letting a language agent link requirements to evidence in a temporal knowledge graph while a deterministic checker certifies whether a recommendation is supported. Evaluation on a bilingual Hong Kong public-service benchmark shows this reduces unnecessary abstention, and interestingly that extra verification can withdraw supported recommendations without improving decisions.

entry.title: When More Data Is Not Enough: The Context-Sufficiency Frontier in Generative AI Personalization

author.name: Merieme Askour, Ayoub Merimi

entry.summary: This paper develops a theory of context sufficiency for generative AI personalization, distinguishing customer evidence (historical behavior) from provider-side context (current situational information). It argues relevance of context to current intent matters more than volume, and identifies four regimes of context sufficiency. The work reframes personalization as a decision problem about when additional context helps.

entry.title: An Educator-Guided LLM Pedagogical Agent for Scaffolded Feedback in Conceptual Database Design

author.name: Sara Riazi, Pedram Rooshenas

entry.summary: The paper presents an LLM pedagogical agent integrated into an ERD editor that grounds scaffolded feedback in student artifacts, assignment requirements, and educator-authored rubrics. Its architecture separates artifact-grounded diagnosis from disclosure-level workflow control, with stateful episodes linked to versioned diagram states. Deployments across three ERD environments demonstrate the approach in real coursework.

entry.title: PPO-HRAP: Proximal Policy Optimization with a Hybrid Regime-Aware Policy for Risk-Controlled Trading

author.name: Duong Hien Chi Kien, Thanh Trung Huynh

entry.summary: PPO-HRAP combines PPO with an interpretable regime prior for trading, blending the learned actor output with a regime-derived target exposure and using a reward mixing log returns, VIX-conditioned drawdown penalties, exposure-deviation terms, and turnover costs to balance upside participation with drawdown control.

entry.title: AVSD-Scenes: A Dataset for Audio-Visual Description of Urban Scenes

author.name: Dhanunjaya Varma Devalraju, Arshdeep Singh, Mark D. Plumbley

entry.summary: The authors introduce AVSD-Scenes, a dataset of 12,291 paired audio-visual scene descriptions for urban environments, built from the TAU Urban Audio-Visual Scenes dataset. Descriptions are generated per modality using Qwen2-Audio-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B, then merged into multimodal captions by several LLMs. The dataset addresses a real gap in jointly grounded audio-visual captioning resources, though it inherits the limitations of synthetic, model-generated captions.

entry.title: Ask a Language Model for Lottery Numbers: Concentration in Repeated Six-of-49 Outputs

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: This paper tests six language model configurations on requests for six random integers from 1-49, finding severe output concentration: effective diversity of 9.9-18.0 versus simulated thresholds around 46.6 for uniform sampling, with modal tickets comprising up to 68% of responses. Physical lottery samples provide a comparison point with far higher diversity.

entry.title: LENS-GRF: Permutation-Invariant Lesion Evidence Network with Gated Residual Fusion for Acne Severity Grading and Multi-Rater Clinical Oracle Analysis

author.name: Muhammad Muhtasim Shahriar, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: Presents an interpretable multi-stage pipeline for four-class acne severity grading that fuses a global Vision Transformer prior with a permutation-invariant lesion-set transformer and gated residual fusion. It reports 80.82% accuracy fully automated on ACNE04 with YOLOv11s, rising to 95.89% with ground-truth lesion annotations, plus a multi-rater clinical oracle analysis.

entry.title: Token Communication-Assisted Collaborative Embodied Artificial Intelligence: Concepts, Framework, and Opportunities

author.name: Peng Yi, Ying-Chang Liang

entry.summary: A position/framework article proposing token communication (TokCom) as a native intelligence interface for collaborative embodied AI, where tokens serve both as compact semantic carriers for inter-agent communication and as inference units for generative foundation models. It outlines how TokCom supports insight sharing, intent alignment, and interactive control among multiple physical agents.

entry.title: One pool, many targets: a conservation layer and what archival data can identify

author.name: Zahra Khodagholi, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: The authors formulate a differentiable equilibrium layer enforcing conservation of a finite guide-loaded RISC pool for CRISPR off-target scoring, with exact implicit gradients and several theoretical results including rank-invariance conditions. They then audit dose-response and cross-context experiments on archival off-target data, finding corrected affinities only weakly associated with outcomes.

entry.title: HADRec: A Hierarchy-Aware Drug Recommendation Framework by Fusing Molecular Knowledge and Electronic Health Record

author.name: Junke Wang, Hongshun Ling, Li Zhang, Jinjing Wu, Tong Shao, Fang Wang, Yuan Gao

entry.summary: HADRec improves medication recommendation by encoding drugs with molecular structure and pharmacological information rather than as discrete tokens, and by exploiting the hierarchical ATC classification system. It uses LLaMA-7B to encode clinical notes for patient representations, fusing molecular knowledge with electronic health records.

entry.title: From Redundancy to Minimality: Fixed-Point-Guided Hierarchical Reduction of Learned Piecewise-Linear Dynamics

author.name: Hiroto Tamura, Gouhei Tanaka

entry.summary: The authors propose training almost-linear RNNs with many ReLU units and then systematically reducing them to minimal piecewise-linear representations via a fixed-point-guided hierarchical reduction of the symbolic transition graph. This sidesteps the unreliability of directly training small-ReLU models while preserving essential dynamical structure learned from time series.

entry.title: ibUMAP: Coherent and Scalable Field Evaluation for UMAP Optimization

author.name: Bin Chen, Yumeng Xue, Patrick Paetzold, Yunhai Wang, Oliver Deussen

entry.summary: ibUMAP replaces UMAP's stochastic negative sampling with a coherent field-based evaluation of attraction and repulsion from a shared embedding snapshot, using a degree-weighted repulsive field summarized by three scalar moments and computed via an interpolation-based FFT scheme. This stabilizes embeddings across reruns while avoiding all-pairs computations on CPUs and GPUs.

entry.title: Generalization in Neural Networks Through the Lens of Magnitude Potential

author.name: Sahel Torkamani, Henry Gouk, Rik Sarkar

entry.summary: The paper introduces magnitude potential, a quantity from metric magnitude theory measuring how well a point is represented by a set, and shows that ratios of class-wise to dataset-wise magnitude potential at the logit layer correlate with generalization-related properties. This provides a new geometric lens on memorization and generalization in trained networks.

entry.title: Multi-Resolution Feature Fusion U-Net for Magnetic Resonance Imaging Segmentation

author.name: Eirini Cholopoulou, Dimitrios E. Diamantis, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: The paper introduces a U-Net variant with a multi-resolution feature fusion module designed to preserve fine-grained detail alongside global context for MRI segmentation across anatomical structures with irregular boundaries and scale variation. It targets improvements over standard U-Net extensions on medical imaging segmentation.

entry.title: PhysicsMate: A Curriculum-Grounded Bengali Benchmark for Secondary Physics QA with Small-Model Adaptation

author.name: Rashid Azraf Jahin, Saadman Sajid, Khan Raiyan Ibne Reza, Sumaiya Tabassum Nimi

entry.summary: The paper introduces PhysicsMate, a benchmark of 1,834 Bengali physics question-answer pairs grounded in the national Grade 9-10 curriculum and a multi-relational knowledge graph, and fine-tunes small models (0.6B-4B parameters) with LoRA. Adaptation yields substantial closed-book accuracy gains across scales (+5.5 to +23.3 percentage points), with node-type analysis showing which knowledge types benefit most.

entry.title: GPEC: Efficient Pre-LLM Gaussian Process Embedding Correction for Cardiac Video Caption Generation

author.name: Arefeh Rezaei

entry.summary: GPEC is a modular, computationally efficient module inserted between the visual projection layer and language model in VideoChat2, learning a residual correction of projected visual embeddings guided by annotation-derived targets for echocardiography captioning. It improves specialized medical video understanding without heavy fine-tuning. The approach is relevant to adapting general MLLMs to medical domains cheaply.

entry.title: RIQE: a NIQE-style reference model for Computed Tomography

author.name: Fabio Mattiussi

entry.summary: The author releases RIQE, a NIQE-style no-reference image quality model fitted on 3,792 full-dose CT slices from 158 patients in a public LDCT collection, with a declared intensity mapping and full reproducibility materials. On held-out patients it correctly ranks reduced-dose reconstructions below full-dose ones in nearly all tested pairs. This provides a radiology-specific alternative to photograph-trained quality metrics.

entry.title: Neuromorphic Pseudo-Random Number Generators with a Low Power Hardware Implementation

author.name: Jafar Shamsi, Navid Akbari, Sonia Sennik, Aaron Gruber, Wilten Nicola

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that chaotic balanced states in spiking neural networks can be harnessed for pseudo-random number generation, constructing a balanced leaky-integrate-and-fire network implementable on low-power FPGAs. It explores whether brain-inspired excitation-inhibition balance can offer favorable trade-offs among randomness quality, power, and bandwidth. Applications include low-power hardware needing unpredictable sequences.

entry.title: IndoorBEV: A Lightweight Real-Time LiDAR BEV Perception System for Indoor Mobile Robots

author.name: Haichuan Li

entry.summary: IndoorBEV is a lightweight LiDAR perception framework for indoor mobile robots that mitigates the trade-off between computational efficiency and vertical geometric information via a height-aware BEV representation with statistical height features and multi-frequency height encoding per BEV cell. It targets cluttered 3D environments under strict latency and memory constraints. This makes BEV-style perception practical for embedded indoor robots.

entry.title: ChunkVLA-AM: Parallel Action Chunking for Vision-Language-Action Robot Control in Additive Manufacturing

author.name: Zhugang Liu, Kaichuang Zhang, Jinman Zhang, Pu Sun, Martha Asare, Jose Hernandez, Maxim Ermolinsky, Efren Saenz, Qi Lu, Jinghao Yang

entry.summary: Deploys OpenVLA-OFT on a FAIRINO FR3 robot in a fixed additive manufacturing workcell, with a data pipeline converting monocular demonstrations into OpenVLA-compatible datasets and runtime eight-step chunks of 7-D actions executed open loop. Demonstrates adapting a VLA model to a new embodiment and industrial setting. An applied case study of VLA deployment in manufacturing automation.

entry.title: Neural scaling laws and evolution of learnable activation functions of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks

author.name: Tilen Cadez, Sanghoon Lee, Kyoung-Min Kim

entry.summary: This paper studies neural scaling laws of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks and how their learnable activation functions evolve as datasets expand. Three KAN variants are evaluated on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and a scientific regression task of estimating magnetic parameters from moire texture images, providing empirical characterization of KAN scaling behavior.

entry.title: Inherited Learning in an Artificial Ecology: How Controls and Update Allocation Shape Benefits

author.name: Xuening Wu, Lei Li, Shan Yu

entry.summary: This work studies when inheriting learned preferences improves collective performance in resource-limited artificial ecologies, addressing how to measure inheritance benefits fairly given that inheritance changes survival, reproduction, and opportunities for further updates. It shows random controls with equal update magnitudes can yield misleading comparisons if they alter different states or stability constraints. This provides methodological rigor for evolutionary learning studies.

entry.title: Predictive Credit: Measuring What Scientific Explanations Add to Experimental Forecasts

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Xueqi Li, Yibo Kong, Dongting Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces predictive credit, measuring what explanations add to experimental forecasts via paired forecasts varying only description, matched explanation, and donor context, with five preregistered checks across Tox21 and OpenML tasks. The frozen v5 credit decision was inconclusive: point-accuracy gains over description alone remained unconfirmed under the preregistered harm and repeatability rules.

entry.title: Generation Provenance Before Behavior Attribution: Auditing Synthetic Speech Research Objects

author.name: Sidi Chang, Peiying Zhu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a generation-provenance substrate for synthetic speech research objects, binding source specification, generated content, quality signals, review lineage, and immutable manifest identity so that model behavior can later be attributed to training data. It audits the substrate on a 113-asset Japanese care-handoff speech pipeline.

entry.title: PyPottery: an AI-powered end-to-end suite for pottery processing and publication

author.name: Lorenzo Cardarelli

entry.summary: PyPottery is an open-source AI suite semi-automating the complete ceramic documentation pipeline in archaeology through four modules: image extraction with handwriting recognition, automatic inking of pencil drawings, semantically-aware vectorization, and automated layout generation. Evaluated on 50 sheets with 240 pottery drawings from the Terramara di Montale site in Italy. It addresses real publication bottlenecks in archaeological practice with a domain-specific end-to-end tool.

entry.title: Bounded-Fidelity Sim-as-Demo-Stage: Mocap Handoff for Governance Benchmarks

author.name: Xue Qin, Simin Luan, Cong Yang, Zhijun Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a design pattern for LLM-driven robot governance benchmarks in which contact physics is deliberately suppressed within bracketed handoff envelopes (using MuJoCo mocap bodies) to prevent simulation noise from contaminating audit-chain evaluations, while preserving full dynamics elsewhere. It reframes sim fidelity as a controllable property rather than an unconditional goal.

entry.title: Legal text classification in Korean sexual offense cases: from traditional machine learning to large language models with XAI insights

author.name: Jeongmin Lee

entry.summary: This study evaluates legal text classification on ten categories of Korean sexual offense precedents, finding that fine-tuned domain-adapted KLUE-BERT reaches 99.3% accuracy, outperforming GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and traditional machine learning baselines. XAI analysis provides interpretability insights into model decisions.

entry.title: Target-Dependent Limits of Causal Repair: A Leading-Log Frontier in a Gaussian Model

author.name: Qinchuan Cheng, Jiaqi Liu, Ruixuan Xie

entry.summary: The paper quantifies the gap between how much a causal predictor could improve and the gain actually realized by a learned repair, in a scalar Gaussian causal experiment with known intervention geometry. The authors show that at the usual 1/k learning scale, every feasible learner incurs a k-squared assessment floor even when oracle potential is estimable faster, and characterize a sharp leading-log frontier in the magnitude-rich regime. The results are theoretical bounds on jointly optimizing a learner and its assessor.

entry.title: Contextual trajectory and incremental contextual displacement: Towards using LLMs to understand dynamic, utterance-specific meaning construction

author.name: Grayson Wycliffe Storer, Julia Witte Zimmerman

entry.summary: The authors construct token-wise incremental trajectories of contextual word embeddings by repeatedly recomputing embeddings as words are added to a sentence, capturing how contextualization evolves as an utterance unfolds. Using garden-path sentences as a test case, these trajectories reproduce known psycholinguistic features of garden-path processing and reliably distinguish them from matched controls. The work connects transformer representations with human sentence-processing phenomena.

entry.title: Don't Waste the Noise: Importance-Guided Perturbation Allocation under Joint Global and Local Constraints

author.name: Melika Shirian, Kianoosh Vadaei

entry.summary: The authors formalize the problem of allocating a shared adversarial perturbation budget across input coordinates under per-coordinate local magnitude constraints. They propose an importance-guided allocation mechanism using a fixed clean-gradient prior to concentrate perturbation on model-sensitive regions, improving adversarial robustness evaluation efficiency.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Discovery of Typed Semantic Links for Ontology Network Construction

author.name: Nouha Hayouni, Sheeba Samuel, Alsayed Algergawy

entry.summary: This paper presents an end-to-end framework for constructing ontology networks by combining DistilBERT embeddings, clustering-based candidate filtering, and GPT-4o-driven iterative prompt engineering to generate typed, justified semantic links. It is applied to a reproduction research ontology network to demonstrate scalable interoperability link discovery.

entry.title: Architecture Without an Architect? Global Governance of Artificial Intelligence in a Divided World

author.name: Simon Chesterman

entry.summary: A review essay by Simon Chesterman examining global AI governance through Matthijs Maas's framework in Architectures of Global AI Governance, focusing on who has the capacity and incentive to create, enforce, and adapt AI rules given fragmented, non-binding international responses. It is a scholarly commentary rather than original empirical research.

entry.title: A First Glance at Jev for Network Traffic Classification: Accuracy, Processing Time, and Cost

author.name: Shenghe Xu, Lifan Mei

entry.summary: This is the first empirical evaluation of general-purpose decision models, exemplified by Jev, for application classification of network flows using only the first ten packets of QUIC traffic on CESNET-QUICEXT-25. General-purpose decision models with few-shot examples reach only 28-35% accuracy versus roughly 70% for Random Forest and Extra Trees trained on 8,000 records, at substantially higher cost per record. The results suggest strong limits of decision-native models on this specialized flow-classification task.

entry.title: Curvature Under Attack in hZACH-ViT: Gauge Symmetry, Boundary Saturation, and Adversarial Failure

author.name: Athanasios Angelakis, Marta Gomez-Barrero

entry.summary: The paper studies how curvature effects in a compact Vision Transformer with Euclidean, Poincare, and spherical prototype heads depend on coordinate scale, logit temperature, and numerical safeguards. Across three MedMNIST datasets, hyperbolic heads show the lowest PGD attack success but also the lowest clean accuracy, with a curvature-scale interaction analysis.

entry.title: Context-Aware Error Mitigation Orchestration for Hybrid Quantum Reinforcement Learning on NISQ Systems

author.name: Bisma Majid, Shabir Ahmed Sofi, Mir Mohammad Yousuf

entry.summary: This paper presents APGEM, an adaptive policy-guided error mitigation layer for hybrid quantum-classical reinforcement learning that dynamically selects among mitigation strategies as noise conditions and training state evolve, rather than applying fixed corrections. Targeting NISQ devices where decoherence and gate errors degrade policy quality, it aims to make QRL training more reliable. This is relevant to near-term quantum advantage in combinatorial optimization.

entry.title: Why Does Train-Validation Separation Emerge? Update-Pressure Density Dynamics in Pretrained Backbones

author.name: Yuchen Li, Mingyu Du, Zongqi Fan, Ken-Tye Yong, Nguyen H. Tran

entry.summary: The authors propose a dynamic structural account of the train-validation gap during adaptation of pretrained models, linking continued fitting to a shift of gradient update pressure from broadly reusable toward narrower support. They introduce fixed training probes that make this structural evolution observable without validation leakage, validated in residual network hierarchies.

entry.title: Compound interpretation is based on analogy

author.name: Tian Shen, Harald Baayen

entry.summary: The authors propose the Compound Analogy Model, a parameter-free method that predicts compound word embeddings by adding constituent embeddings to average shift vectors from compound families. It outperforms the CAOSS model on Mandarin Chinese compounds. This offers a simple analogical account of lexical semantic composition.

entry.title: Is it Possible to Generate Irreversible PolyProtected Templates from Face Embeddings using System-Specific Keys?

author.name: Vedrana Krivoku\'ca Hahn, J\'er\'emy Maceiras, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: This work investigates whether the PolyProtect biometric template protection method can produce irreversible templates when system-specific keys (shared transform parameters) are used instead of subject-specific keys. System-specific keys would enable face identity de-duplication in the protected domain, which conflicts with unlinkability in the subject-specific setting. The question sits at the intersection of privacy, unlinkability, and practical biometric deployment.

entry.title: quARtet Marker: A 3D-Printable Multi-Tag Fiducial for Robust Near-Frontal Pose Estimation

author.name: Araki Wakiuchi, Hikaru Sasaki, Takamitsu Matsubara

entry.summary: The quARtet marker is a 3D-printable fiducial that tilts four AprilTags within one compact flat footprint so that each tag is observed at a non-frontal angle even when the marker faces the camera, restoring perspective cues that single planar tags lose in near-frontal views. All detected corners enter one Perspective-n-Point solve. It is designed for manipulating transparent or reflective labware where flat, graspable faces must remain intact.

entry.title: OpenSpace Lab Solution to the IROS 2026 Indoor Exploration Competition

author.name: Yuxuan Zhang, Dong Li, Zezhou Sun, Yuxuan Xu, Siyu Teng, Yuchen Li, Jianjian Yang, Long Chen

entry.summary: System report from OpenSpace Lab describing their 1st-place single-robot and 3rd-place multi-robot results in the IROS 2026 indoor exploration competition. The framework uses pre-trained map completion predictions for global planning, a remaining-time-based exploration strategy with homing constraints, and utility-based coordination for multi-robot exploration. A useful applied reference for autonomous exploration under time budgets.

entry.title: JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces

author.name: Haoyang Su, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: JevSpawn is a compositional policy connecting natural language task specifications to finite probabilistic exploration, coupling parallel action spawning with feedback-driven branch selection, representation revision, and recovery from retained alternatives, extending Jev-style models that otherwise require pre-specified finite fields. Shared action structure and model prefixes reduce recomputation cost.

entry.title: Two Routes to the Middle: Placement Search and Brain Readouts Converge on Where Continual Learners Should Specialize

author.name: Yuan Huang, Zihan Chen, Runbin Zhang, Hongwei Ding, Changzeng Fu, Shiqi Zhao

entry.summary: The authors study where to place task-specific adapters in vision transformers for continual learning, finding via exhaustive placement search that accuracy peaks at intermediate depth, and independently that brain readouts of visual cortex plasticity also point to intermediate stages. This cross-disciplinary convergence offers both practical placement guidance and a neuroscience link.

entry.title: ALFRED: Requirement-driven development of an open-source mobile manipulator for long-term plant monitoring

author.name: Ciar\'an Miceal Johnson, Christopher Quail, Garry Ellard, Alistair McConnell, Steve Tonneau, Fernando Auat Cheein

entry.summary: ALFRED is an open-source mobile manipulator built from commercial components for repeated observation of the same plants across seasons, featuring a six-DOF arm, LiDAR, RGB-D cameras, RTK GNSS, and IMU on an Ackermann-steered base. It was developed through four builds against six requirements, with released design files and analysis of how robot structure limits arm reach and occludes sensors. This addresses the scarcity of fully open hardware for long-term field datasets.

entry.title: A Structured State Space Sequence Model for Multi-Class Classification of Malware

author.name: Emmanuela Andam, Rana Shaaban, Emanuel Grant, Naima Kaabouch

entry.summary: Applies a structured state space sequence (SSM) model to multi-class malware classification in the context of growing IoT attack surfaces, motivated by the projected 40 billion IoT devices by 2030. The work targets faster, more scalable detection of expanding malware variants.

entry.title: Robust Is Salient: An Informed Adversary Moves the Optimal Signal onto the Salience Pole

author.name: Cris Huynh

entry.summary: Using a forced-choice signalling game abstracted from a party game, the paper shows that when an informed adversary shares the audience's priors, the adversary-robust optimal signal aligns exactly with the salience pole from prior work, differing from the Bayesian optimum on only a small fraction of a 200,000-item pool. Robustness is achieved by shifting entirely from Bayesian discrimination to salience where the coordinate is defined.

entry.title: Feedback Without the Wait: Piloting a Generative AI Practice Platform in a Large Maths Class

author.name: Lili Chen, Gavin Buskes, Yuxin Ren, Chin Tong Leong

entry.summary: This pilot study deploys a generative AI practice platform in a large electrical engineering maths class to provide immediate conversational feedback, resolving the tension between feedback immediacy and human-oversight trustworthiness by practicing on unassessed work. It addresses the practical bottleneck of student-to-demonstrator ratios in large courses.

entry.title: Trustworthy Data- and ML-Ops for Intelligent Transportation Systems and Logistics

author.name: Antonio Emanuele Cin\`a, Giovanni Scodeller, Cecilia Caterina Pasquale, Silvia Siri, Davide Anguita, Fabio Roli, Simona Sacone, Luca Oneto

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive review of Trustworthy DataOps and MLOps in intelligent transportation systems and logistics, identifying literature gaps and discussing key components for improving efficiency, reliability, and decision-making in the domain.

entry.title: AiSearch: Interactive Multi-Modal Search with VLMs

author.name: Ali Koksal, Mei Chee Leong, Vicky Sintunata, Ching Ling Chin, Wee Teck Fong

entry.summary: AiSearch is a multimodal retrieval framework leveraging zero-shot VLM capabilities for natural language search over images and videos, supporting interactive refinement through user feedback and cross-model visual benchmarking to select the best VLM for a task.

entry.title: Temporal-Difference Learning for Dragonchess

author.name: Jim O'Connor, Annika Hoag, Sarah Goyette, Gary B. Parker

entry.summary: This paper studies evolutionary transfer learning and TD-lambda in Dragonchess, a three-dimensional chess variant with unusual board structure and high computational load. The authors re-implemented the engine in C++ enabling 10,000 games with statistical significance testing, and found both adaptive methods outperform all other agents in round-robin play with no significant difference between them. It is a modest but careful empirical study of adaptive heuristic learning in a novel game environment.

entry.title: Signed Lexical Confidence for Risk-Calibrated Intent Routing

author.name: Yezhou Cheng, Zehua Yang, Bojun Lin

entry.summary: Proposes a signed lexical gate for selective intent routing that combines a sentence classifier's logit margin with a sparse lexical model's support or opposition to the predicted intent. A separate binomial calibration stage then picks a deferral threshold for a target risk level. This improves uncertainty signaling for assistants deciding when to act versus defer without modifying the base model.

entry.title: Beyond Pixel Reconstruction: Retrieval-Guided Glyph-Aware Restoration for Low-Resource Manchu Historical Documents

author.name: Ting Huang, Dongdong Wang, Mingqiu Liang, Siyang Lu

entry.summary: Proposes a retrieval-guided restoration framework for degraded historical Manchu documents that incorporates glyph-level structural knowledge rather than optimizing only pixel reconstruction, retrieving relevant glyph exemplars to guide restoration. This preserves the structural identity of Manchu characters despite severe degradation and scarce paired training data.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Anomaly Detection in Railway Systems: A Structured Survey

author.name: Ammar Bouketta, Smail Niar, Hamza Ouarnoughi

entry.summary: A structured survey of deep-learning approaches for railway anomaly detection, organized by a unified taxonomy covering anomaly location, data representation, sensing modality, and temporal characteristics, spanning convolutional, recurrent, attention-based architectures, autoencoders, and GANs. It maps heterogeneous sensor data use from rolling stock and infrastructure.

entry.title: A Shared Taste for Model-Written Text: The Generator-by-Selector Matrices of "AI-AI Bias" Show No Detectable Own-Model Premium

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: A reanalysis of Laurito et al. (PNAS 2025) on AI-AI bias, rebuilding the 5x5 generator-by-selector matrices (21,828 trials) from public per-item counts and fitting a two-way fixed-effects model with an own-model term. It finds no detectable own-model premium, suggesting models share a common preference for model-written text rather than favoring their own outputs.

entry.title: Multi-agent Auditory Scene Analysis: Improved Localization Speed and Robustness by Multi-beamformed Speech Quality Feedback

author.name: Caleb Rascon

entry.summary: This single-author work improves multi-agent auditory scene analysis, where agents perform sound localization, separation, and classification and communicate via feedback loops to correct local errors globally. The paper speeds up optimization of speech source localization by using multi-beamformed speech quality as feedback. It addresses a demonstrated weakness in the optimization speed of prior multi-agent ASA approaches.

entry.title: From Network Intrusion Detection to Blockchain-Backed Endpoint Detection and Response: Mapping the Landscape of Decentralized Detection-and-Response Architectures

author.name: Yahya Shahsavari, Sara Rouhani, Kaiwen Zhang

entry.summary: A Systematization of Knowledge proposing a three-axis taxonomy (detection-system class, blockchain functional role, response-automation maturity) for blockchain-assisted IDS/IPS and EDR/XDR research, correcting prior reviews that conflated blockchain roles and ignored the shift to EDR/XDR architectures. Focused on IoT and IIoT security.

entry.title: Fusion techniques of time frequency-based images to predict the outcome of rTMS depression therapy

author.name: Wael Korani, Md Fahimul Kabir Chowdhury, Mohammed Aledhari, Reza Rostami, Reza Kazemi

entry.summary: The paper proposes two fusion techniques, montage and blending, over EEG-derived time-frequency images plus a lightweight custom CNN to predict patient response to repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for depression. Fusing multiple domains addresses high inter-subject variability and limited single-domain features. Accurate pre-treatment response prediction would have real clinical value for treatment selection.

entry.title: Reliability-aware short-term roll prediction for unmanned surface vehicles via multi-task learning and adaptive centralization

author.name: Kaizhen Li, Xi Zhou, Zihao Wang, Dan Zhang, Jianjian Liu, Xiaowei Li

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-task architecture for roll prediction of unmanned surface vehicles that pairs a regression head with a confidence-quantification head, embedding reliability estimation directly into the prediction pipeline. Reliable roll prediction supports navigational safety and autonomous decision-making for marine robots. The adaptive centralization component coordinates the reliability estimates across the system.

entry.title: Action-On-Item Preference Flow: A Shared Event Schema for Predictive and Generative Personalization

author.name: Parthiv Chatterjee, Kashish Kanjaria, Vashisth Purani, Sourish Dasgupta, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: The paper introduces an action-on-item event schema and the PerTIDE system that lets a single update mechanism maintain user state across heterogeneous histories (movies, news, dialogue) for both predictive and generative personalization. The authors provide theoretical guarantees including invariance to relabeling, bounded state changes, and pooled-training bounds under compatibility conditions.

entry.title: Anomaly Detection and Localization for the Pantograph-Catenary System

author.name: Francesco Vitale, Hangli Ge, Francesco Flammini

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for railway infrastructure monitoring that localizes pantograph-catenary height and stagger measurements by aligning them with nominal GPS coordinates of the route, then applies collective anomaly detection to assess system health. Unlike existing CNN-based video monitoring solutions, it accounts for the train route's geographic location.

entry.title: Loading history and window geometry bound compact-state slip ranking during granular shear startup

author.name: Ruixin Zhou, Boliang Yu

entry.summary: The authors train a compact neural score on granular shear simulations to rank near-slip windows, carefully separating material state, loading progress, and sampling-geometry confounds across 36 training and 18 held-out trajectories. They find ranking above control baselines but transparently report post-event sampling asymmetries that limit the recovery-aware conclusions.

entry.title: Sentence Specificity Scores for Collaborative Technical Documentation: A Domain-Transfer Study

author.name: Rocker D'Antonio, Thomas Benton Townsend, Dimitrios Michael Manias

entry.summary: This study audits sentence-specificity scoring tools on technical documentation and tests whether post-generation specificity scores can select among fixed LLM-generated revisions. It finds that a general-domain predictor and a target-adapted predictor produce divergent corpus orderings across Wikipedia and three technical corpora.

entry.title: Participation-Sensitive Convergence and the Fragment First, Converge Later Pattern in Asynchronous Online Learning: A Topological Analysis Across 22 OULAD Courses

author.name: Hitoshi Inoue, Koichi Yasutake

entry.summary: Using Zigzag Persistent Homology, the authors analyze behavioral clustering in all 22 OULAD courses (over 22,000 learners), showing that topological convergence signals strongly co-vary with active learner counts, i.e., apparent community convergence may reflect dropout rather than alignment. They also identify reproducible fragmentation-convergence cycles around assessment deadlines. This offers a caution for topological learning analytics.

entry.title: The Impact of Processing Parameters on High-Accuracy Measurements in UAV Photogrammetry

author.name: Pawe{\l} \'Cwi\k{a}ka{\l}a, Edyta Puniach, El\.zbieta Pastucha, Wojciech Gruszczy\'nski

entry.summary: This study systematically evaluates how Bundle Block Adjustment parameter settings affect 3D accuracy in UAV photogrammetry, using a full-factorial design of 768 processing variants across ten UAV datasets collected over 1.5 years on a 220-hectare area. It finds substantial accuracy variability, with the best variant reaching roughly 16mm RMSE. The work fills a gap since acquisition strategies are well studied but processing workflow choices are not.

entry.title: Multi-Reference Path Tracking Control for an Agricultural Tractor with Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Marcel Moll, Timo Oksanen

entry.summary: This study develops an NMPC-based path tracking controller for agricultural tractors that incorporates multiple segments of a piecewise-linear reference path directly into the objective function, with methods for selecting viable reference segments. Field tests via the Tractor Implement Management steering interface show 3.45 ms average solver convergence and 6.1 cm mean absolute cross-track error. It is validated on real hardware, not just simulation.

entry.title: The Effect of Gait Stability Based on Two Types of Impact Strategies for Two-Link Walking and Brachiating Robots

author.name: Alan Estrada Flores, Nelson Rosa Jr

entry.summary: Analyzes impulsive dynamics in single-joint, two-link models of walking and brachiating gaits, studying how gait stability and bifurcations change under time-based versus state-based switching of impact dynamics with respect to slope and switching time. A focused theoretical dynamics study on simple gait models. Contributes foundational understanding of switching-strategy effects on stability.

entry.title: FLF’s Epistemic Case Study Competition: Results

author.name: Oliver Sourbut

entry.summary: Oliver Sourbut reports results of the Forecasting/FLF summer competition awarding over 200k dollars for workflows using AI to build reliable, source-grounded knowledge bases. The post explains the motivation, that diligence rather than insight is the bottleneck in epistemic work, and notes continued investment in this area. It summarizes a community experiment in making AI-assisted research trustworthy and checkable.

entry.title: K-Dense BYOK: An Open-Source AI Research Assistant That Runs Locally and Keeps a Hash-Chained Lab Notebook

author.name: Aubrey M. Brueckner, Darshil Patel, Yuhuan He, Timothy Kassis

entry.summary: K-Dense BYOK is a free, open-source research assistant that runs locally on the researcher's machine, supplies scientific procedure libraries and workflow templates, and maintains a hash-chained lab notebook for provenance. Each project is a plain folder so data, code, results, and records remain readable without the application.

entry.title: Streaming algorithms for robust max-min diversification

author.name: Andrea Pietracaprina, Geppino Pucci, Stefano Zanon

entry.summary: This paper improves on a recent coreset-based streaming algorithm for robust max-min diversification, identifying three shortcomings in the prior AAAI23 approach including an offline coreset computation step. The authors propose streaming algorithms that remove these limitations under weaker assumptions, selecting k points maximizing minimum pairwise distance while excluding z outliers.

entry.title: Mixture of Decoders for Diverse Dialog Response Generation

author.name: Wenchao Du

entry.summary: The paper hypothesizes that low diversity in sequence-to-sequence dialog response generation stems from learning a degenerate uni-modal response distribution, and proposes incorporating a mixture of specialized decoders within a conditional variational autoencoder framework. Evaluation on an open-domain chat corpus shows improvements over strong baselines in quality and diversity.

entry.title: Book Review: Obsolete

author.name: PeterMcCluskey

entry.summary: Peter McCluskey reviews Garrison Lovely's book Obsolete, which discusses AI-driven concentration of power alongside existential risk concerns. The review praises the book for defusing tensions between mundane near-term harms and long-term catastrophic risk, while criticizing gratuitous culture-war framing that may alienate some readers. It is useful commentary for those tracking AI risk discourse.

entry.title: Enterprise Representation Simplification (ERS): Reducing Representational Complexity for Enterprise AI

author.name: Terry Dorsey, Kevin Huggins

entry.summary: The paper introduces Enterprise Representation Simplification (ERS) — reducing unnecessary representational complexity while preserving required information — and Enterprise Representation Complexity (ERC), a representation-neutral model with four dimensions for comparing complexity across representation states. It targets how accumulated artifact complexity burdens both human consumers and AI systems in enterprises. This is a conceptual framework for enterprise AI readiness.

entry.title: vFedProtoQNAS: Prototype-Guided Personalized Quantum Neural Architecture Search for Virtual Federated Learning

author.name: Seok Bin Son, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Soohyun Park, Joongheon Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes vFedProtoQNAS, which combines quantum neural architecture search with virtual federated learning: clients search device-specific QNN architectures while collaboration occurs through class prototypes rather than parameter averaging, avoiding semantic mixing of structurally different circuits. This targets heterogeneous quantum devices where a single shared QNN architecture is unsuitable. The approach addresses a real constraint in emerging quantum federated settings.

entry.title: Query-efficient winner prediction in district-based elections

author.name: Koustav De, Debajyoti Kar, Swagato Sanyal

entry.summary: This theory paper studies winner prediction in district-based plurality elections in a query complexity model, where predictions must be made from individual vote queries. It formalizes the margin of victory as the minimum number of vote alterations needed to change the unique winner. The authors derive query-efficiency bounds for predicting election outcomes under this structured model.

entry.title: Judgement in the Age of Jev: From Evaluation Scarcity to Evaluation Abundance

author.name: Richard Hill

entry.summary: A perspective piece prompted by Jev, TypeSafe AI's specialized model for typed probabilistic decisions, arguing that if machine evaluation becomes cheap enough, evaluation itself shifts from scarcity to abundance, changing organizational decision-making. It formulates conditional claims treating the Jevons economics analogy as a provocation rather than an established result. Scholarly commentary on evaluation economics rather than technical research.

entry.title: A Hybrid Approach to Malware Detection: Integrating Few-Shot Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning with Autoencoders

author.name: Emmanuela Andam, Yasir Abbas Zaidi, Abdelali Hadir, Emmanuel Grant, Naima Kaabouch

entry.summary: The paper combines an autoencoder feature extractor with a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) classifier to detect ransomware with few labeled samples. The autoencoder produces compact latent representations intended to improve detection of novel or scarce malware variants.

entry.title: Evaluating Hybrid Quantum-Classical Models for Reduced-Order Brain Deformation Dynamics

author.name: Tao Liu, Ge He, Dongyu Liang, Wujie Wen

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks hybrid quantum-classical architectures against compact classical baselines for reduced-order prediction of brain deformation fields using POD projection. Results show classical networks, particularly a POD-MLP, outperform all quantum hybrids in the tested setting.

entry.title: FACET at WMT 2026 Automated Translation Quality Evaluation Task

author.name: Ahrii Kim, Chanjun Park, Seong-heum Kim

entry.summary: This paper presents FACET, a reference-free system for the WMT26 Automated Translation Quality Evaluation Task that decomposes translation quality assessment into three passes: Fluency, Accuracy, and Consistency, each prompted with only the context its error type requires (e.g., source text for accuracy, target alone for fluency and entity consistency). A single fixed model is prompted three times, and merged error spans produce error spans, quality scores, and error-free labels without any trained components. The authors also submit a variant, FACET-C, that omits the Consistency pass.

entry.title: Dissonant ballerinas and crafty carrots: a comparative multi-modal analysis of Italian brain rot

author.name: Anca Dinu, Andra-Maria Florescu, Marius Micluta-Campeanu, Stefana-Arina Tabusca, Claudiu Creanga, Andreiana Mihail

entry.summary: The paper presents a comparative multi-modal analysis of Italian and Romanian brain rot memes using CRIB, a curated dataset of 240 TikTok videos stratified by language and popularity, examining textual, acoustic, and visual features. It finds popularity is not significantly correlated with textual absurdity, rhyme, or acoustic features, with cultural distinctions emerging in the Romanian-language subset.

entry.title: Can large language models unlock discrete data in ophthalmic diagnostic reports?

author.name: Umair A. Zaidi, An-Lun Wu, Wei-Chun Lin, Thomas S. Hwang, Michelle R. Hribar

entry.summary: The study evaluates GPT-4o-assisted pipelines, comparing schema-constrained structured output versus prompt-only extraction with JSON conversion, on twenty ophthalmic diagnostic PDF reports against reconciled manual ground truth. Schema-constrained extraction achieved very high value accuracy (100% on some report types) with better formatting accuracy, informing clinical data extraction practice.

entry.title: BanglaDial-Abuse: A Corpus-Grounded Dataset for Regional Dialect Identification in Abusive Bangla Text

author.name: Hasin Almas Sifat

entry.summary: This paper introduces BanglaDial-Abuse, a balanced Bengali-script dataset of 1,000 sentences across four varieties (Standard, Chattagram, Sylhet, Barishal) for dialect identification in abusive and hostile Bangla text. The resource was built with a corpus-grounded synthetic procedure capturing regional variation in pronouns, morphology, and spelling conventions. It addresses a gap in regional linguistic coverage for Bangla NLP.

entry.title: Fusing Visual and Textual Representations via Multi-layer Fusing Transformers for Vietnamese Visual Question Answering

author.name: Cong Phu Nguyen, Huy Tien Nguyen, Tung Le

entry.summary: This work addresses the scarcity of Vietnamese visual question answering research by building multi-layer fusing transformers that combine visual and textual representations. It aims to expand VQA capability beyond English and enable practical applications for Vietnamese speakers.

entry.title: ShowerFlex: Achieving Pseudo-Static Balancing in a Continuum Shower Hose

author.name: Zhiyu Ren, Girish Krishnan

entry.summary: ShowerFlex is a highly articulated continuum mechanism using friction-locked ball-and-socket joints and a retractable spring system, designed to provide pseudo-static balancing for an accessible shower hose for seated bathers. It addresses fall risk and independence challenges in activities of daily living for the aging population. This is assistive hardware design rather than AI research, but directly targets a real accessibility need.

entry.title: Classification Based on Association Rules Algorithm for Breast Cancer

author.name: Ali Alsalama, Ahmed Kubba, Ghaith Jamjoum, Zaher Al Aghbari

entry.summary: This paper presents a weighted association-rule-based classification approach for breast cancer detection, built from three algorithms for rule generation, pruning, and prediction, chosen for interpretability by medical professionals. It applies established data mining ideas to an important clinical screening task. The contribution is primarily applied rather than conceptual.

entry.title: Endogenous Alignment Requires Dependence

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: Gordon Seidoh Worley revises his endogenous alignment proposal in response to commenters, arguing that human child-parent alignment begins with a hologenous parent-child system in which infants model themselves as part of a whole rather than as separate agents. He suggests imitation learning and dependence, not reinforcement learning, are foundational to how humans align children. This is conceptual alignment theorizing drawing on developmental psychology.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens

author.name: Ruiyang Si, Jianxin Bi, Shunyu Yang, Rui Ni, Wenbo Huang, Qiang Wang, Shulong Jiang, Duomin Wang, Xiuyu Li, Haiwen Feng, Zhen Dong, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework for VLM-based robot agents that composes robot primitives and VLA policies into Python cells with conditional checks and retries, returning only explicitly requested observations. Evaluated on 700 simulated tasks across LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365 against a tool-calling baseline using the same GPT-6 Astra planner (an existing model released in early September 2026), it improves success rate while cutting token overhead substantially.

entry.title: Multi-Jurisdictional Legal Identity Assurance for Capability Gating: A Design-Science Proposal for Tiered, Reusable Identity Assurance of Natural, Juridical, and Machine Entities

author.name: Walter Kurz

entry.summary: A design-science position paper proposing tiered, reusable identity assurance across legal jurisdictions for humans, organizations, and AI agents, arguing against flat maximum-verification approaches that over-collect and exclude participants. It sketches a framework where verification strength is decoupled from the specific capability unlocked and is portable across institutions.

entry.title: Evasion Attacks: How Adversarial Noise Bypasses ML Classifiers

author.name: Parker Hummel (Minot State University), Ryne Skabo (Minot State University), Muhammad Abusaqer (Minot State University)

entry.summary: This is a reproducible educational study of evasion attacks, showing FGSM and PGD drastically degrade a small MNIST CNN (down to 0.41 percent under PGD) while pre-defined text perturbations cause only modest probability shifts in a fine-tuned DistilBERT spam classifier. It includes a partial bit-depth-reduction defense evaluation and is intended pedagogically.

entry.title: Open Vocabulary Word Recognition From Transcribed Bangla Texts

author.name: Faias Satter, Sk. Md. Masudul Ahsan

entry.summary: The paper addresses handwritten Bangla word recognition, a critical stage of OCR that lacks reliable solutions, by comparing three object detection models including SSD with MobileNetV2 and Faster R-CNN. It targets open-vocabulary recognition to improve overall OCR performance for the Bangla language.

entry.title: Designing for Interpretation Uncertainty: Architecture and Principles for Topological Learning Analytics Dashboards

author.name: Hitoshi Inoue, Koichi Yasutake

entry.summary: The paper presents TopoLA, a dashboard applying Zigzag Persistent Homology to learning management system data, and proposes three design principles for analytics whose interpretation frameworks are still immature: separating measurement from interpretation, graduated disclosure, and explicit acknowledgment of methodological uncertainty. It contributes human-information-system design guidance rather than new algorithms.

entry.title: FiVOS: A Fish Segmentation Algorithm Based on Interactive Video Object Segmentation and Filter Enhancement

author.name: Yuqing Duan, Song Zhang, Shili Zhao, Daoliang Li, Ran Zhao

entry.summary: FiVOS applies interactive video object segmentation with filter enhancement to fish segmentation for aquaculture monitoring, modeling dynamic correlations between video frames that existing deep learning segmentation methods for aquaculture overlook. Better fish tracking and segmentation supports behavior analysis and precise regulation of farming environments. The contribution is an applied domain method.

entry.title: On Social Reality in China

author.name: alkjash

entry.summary: A first-person essay by a Chinese-American rationalist exploring cultural differences relevant to communicating AI safety ideas and rationalist philosophy in China, with the goal of supporting international coordination efforts such as an AI pause. The author draws on anecdotes from immigrant family interactions and Chinese media, flagging generational and cultural roadblocks to messaging. This provides useful context for cross-cultural AI governance outreach.

entry.title: Endogenous Alignment Requires Dependence

author.name: Gordon Seidoh Worley

entry.summary: A follow-up Forum post refining the author's endogenous alignment framework for how AI systems might be aligned analogously to human children, incorporating commenter feedback that imitation learning and hologenous parent-child dependence precede any reinforcement-based alignment in human development. The author argues babies model themselves as part of a parent-child system before becoming independent agents.

entry.title: Introducing "The Commons Problem" - an AI Governance Megagame

author.name: Philip Harker

entry.summary: Philip Harker introduces an AI governance megagame to be playtested in Toronto, in which 30-60 players representing AI companies, governments, militaries, and other factions simulate the future of AI governance over several hours. Inspired by prior AI wargames like Intelligence Rising, the game aims to reveal emergent dynamics of incentive-driven AI development and crisis response. It is a simulation-based learning and foresight exercise.

entry.title: Beyond Affine Transformations: A Soft Dominance Layer for Coordinate-Wise Neural Computation

author.name: Mariano Rivera

entry.summary: This preliminary study proposes the Soft Dominance Layer, an alternative to affine layers where each output unit compares input coordinates with a learnable reference vector and aggregates smooth, differentiable inequality responses controlled by a sharpness parameter. The author examines trainability and threshold interpretability rather than claiming a replacement for affine layers. On single-run MNIST experiments, accuracy reaches 0.9061-0.9173 versus 0.9827 for baselines.

entry.title: Outer Diversity of Condorcet Domains

author.name: Piotr Faliszewski, Jan Jabrocki, Mateusz S{\l}uszniak, Krzysztof Sornat, Stanis{\l}aw Szufa, Tomasz W\k{a}s

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies outer diversity of Condorcet domains, a measure of expected swap distance from a random vote to the closest ranking in the domain. The authors numerically analyze maximal Condorcet domains with few candidates and derive asymptotic behavior for several special domains. It is a contribution to computational social choice theory rather than machine learning.

entry.title: Calibrating Prediction Timeliness Through Multi-Objective Hyperparameter Optimization for Remaining Useful Life Prediction

author.name: Tugrul Cabir Hakyemez, Ener Uras Gokhan

entry.summary: This study treats the hyperparameter optimization objective for remaining useful life prediction as a design variable, comparing single-objective R2 and NASA scoring regimes against a multi-objective NSGA-II formulation across five architectures on C-MAPSS and BackBlaze datasets. The goal is to capture the asymmetric costs of early versus late RUL errors.

entry.title: Towards a Cloud Fog Edge System for Smart Building

author.name: Christophe C\'erin, Mamadou Sow, Fr\'ed\'eric Andr\`es

entry.summary: This vision paper describes a decentralized smart-building system where the building acts as its own data center, learning from real-time sensor data with privacy preservation and data sovereignty, aimed partly at humanitarian contexts. It details a lightweight Kubernetes-like orchestration framework for deploying AI services at the edge. The contribution is a systems vision and early implementation rather than new ML methods.

entry.title: UniBuc at SemEval-2024 Task 2: Tailored Prompting with Solar for Clinical NLI

author.name: Marius Micluta-Campeanu, Claudiu Creanga, Ana-Maria Bucur, Ana Sabina Uban, Liviu P. Dinu

entry.summary: This system paper describes the UniBuc entry for SemEval 2024 Task 2 on safe biomedical natural language inference for clinical trials, using SOLAR Instruct without fine-tuning and section-tailored prompting in zero- and few-shot settings, achieving a consistency score of 0.72 and 14th place.
