author.name: Jingbo Yang, Kwei-Herng Lai, Xiaowen Wang, Yaar Harari, Evgeniy Gabrilovich, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: ScholarEvolve is a framework where a meta coding agent improves an LLM agent's harness (tool use, memory, execution logic) by drawing on the research literature rather than only its own execution failures. This enables more exploratory, less reactive harness evolution while keeping the underlying model fixed. It represents a step toward lifelong self-improving agent systems.

entry.title: GaugeVLM: Structuring Spatial Supervision with Measured Geometric Interventions

author.name: Hongbo Wang, Zihan Lin, Wenkui Yang, Shiran Ge, Yuang Ai, Jie Cao, Huaibo Huang, Ran He

entry.summary: GaugeVLM targets self-contradictory spatial reasoning in vision-language models by generating controlled object and camera interventions in explicit 3D scenes, yielding linked observations with measured differences between spatial relations. Its GaugeDPO objective converts measured geometric errors into preference margins, giving richer supervision than ordinal pairwise preferences.

entry.title: MILO: Automated Harness Discovery via Orchestrated Multi-Agent Evolution

author.name: Prithwish Jana, Mononito Goswami, Hao Liu, Xinyu Li, Langlin Huang, Zhehui Huang, Zhishen Huang, Patrick Bl\"obaum, Anoop Deoras, Purak Jain, Nikos Kanakaris, Sahika Genc

entry.summary: MILO is a meta-evolutionary framework that co-evolves agent harnesses and the search strategy used to discover them, combining hierarchical lineage memory over island-based trees with per-island mutator agents that treat rejected mutations as negative evidence. It addresses the combinatorial harness-design space that previously required substantial repeated human effort as models change.

entry.title: KlinikeBench: Evaluating Language Models Beyond Diagnostic Accuracy

author.name: Xueting Fang, Zehui Li, Yang Yang, Camilla Giovino, Shubh K. Patel, Shailly Prajapati, Vallijah Subasri, Caihua Shan

entry.summary: KlinikeBench is a benchmark of 333 clinician-authored tasks that evaluate language models on information gathering and clinical assessment in sandboxed environments with virtual patients and clinical tools, rather than only on final diagnostic accuracy with complete case descriptions. It addresses the gap that existing clinical benchmarks lack verification by professional clinicians.

entry.title: Provable Test-Time Scaling for Beam Search in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Qijia He, Yu Huang, Yuan Cheng, Yuxin Chen, Yingbin Liang

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical compute guarantees for beam-search-based test-time scaling in LLM reasoning, where intermediate scoring uses the model's internal log-likelihood and an external reward model is applied only to complete responses. The authors prove a lower bound showing vanilla beam search requires at least a quadratic number of samples in a problem-dependent quantity, plus complementary upper bounds.

entry.title: CRAFT: Causal Responsibility and Failure Tracing in Medical Vision Language Models

author.name: Chunzheng Zhu, Jiaqi Zeng, Hongbo Zhao, Yihang Chen, Yijun Wang, Jianxin Lin

entry.summary: This paper presents CRAFT, a mechanistic interpretability framework for medical vision-language models that identifies two safety failure modes: arbitration failure, where textual context overrides correct visual grounding, and brake failure, where the model commits to answers without sufficient visual evidence. The authors show these failures are mediated by spatially disjoint attention head populations and trace causal responsibility through the network.

entry.title: Loop-Free Inverse Reinforcement Learning via Sequential Value Recovery with Q-Score Matching

author.name: Yang chen, Yitan Zhang, Michael Witbrock, Shuyue Hu

entry.summary: This work reformulates inverse reinforcement learning to eliminate the costly bi-level reward-policy optimization loop by exploiting diffusion policies, whose action-gradient structure encodes the optimal soft Q function. Reward learning is cast as a sequence of value recovery problems solved via Q-score matching, avoiding iterative policy optimization entirely.

entry.title: False Frontiers: Diagnosing and Mitigating Co-Cheating in Self-Evolving Search Agents

author.name: Meijia Chen, Hao Li, Zheng Lu, Hongshan Lin, Junbai Tian, Yichen Liu, Zijun Tian, Yufan Zou, Shuhan Sun, Hanxin Chen, Zeyu Zhang, Weizhi Du, Yueting Li, Tianyu Shi, Alaa Khamis

entry.summary: The paper identifies co-cheating, a failure mode in self-evolving search agents where jointly trained proposer and solver components converge on shared errors, causing internal rewards to rise while external correctness stagnates or declines. It audits this degradation over successive self-evolution rounds and proposes multi-sample verification (MSV), which queries the same model with the source evidence to verify proposals before training.

entry.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: Decoupling Pretext from Actuation for Skill Poisoning in LLM Agents

author.name: Wenxin Wu, Lingyong Yan, Lei Sha, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jiashu Zhao

entry.summary: This work analyzes LLM agent skill poisoning by decomposing risk into two factors: actuation (what operation is performed) and pretext (the rationale for performing it), and demonstrates attacks that separate these components across skill content. The decoupling makes poisoned skills harder to detect while steering agent decision loops under benign requests.

entry.title: Stress-Testing LLM Lie Detectors: Role-Play Failures and Spurious Correlations

author.name: Maximilian von Klinski, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek, Lennart B\"urger

entry.summary: This work builds a dataset of 8,916 human-reviewed on-policy responses from three LLMs adopting anti-factual personas, such as conspiracy theorists, and evaluates eight published lie-detection probes. Many probes fail in this setting, following the persona's beliefs rather than flagging falsehoods, and the paper traces failures to spurious correlations rather than genuine dishonesty signals.

entry.title: CodeMimicry: Exploiting Safety Generalization Lag in Large Language Models via Structured Code Completion

author.name: Zhen Liang, Hai Huang, Wentao Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies a safety generalization lag in LLMs, where alignment trained mostly on natural language fails to transfer to code, creating a code-completion blind spot. CodeMimicry is a fully automated black-box jailbreak framework that wraps malicious intent in syntactically valid object-oriented code prompts, reportedly fooling eight state-of-the-art commercial models.

entry.title: PrefPI: Preference-Guided Steering into Out-of-Distribution Behaviors

author.name: Seungeun Rho, Wontaek Kim, Danfei Xu, Sehoon Ha

entry.summary: PrefPI is an iterative policy-improvement framework that steers pretrained generative robot policies using only relative preferences over self-generated trajectories. It formulates preference learning as preference-conditioned generative modeling, using classifier-free guidance on the density ratio between preferred trajectories and the behavior prior to reach behaviors outside the policy's initial support. Same lead authors as GGSD, suggesting a coherent research program.

entry.title: Blackboard Intelligence Can Surpass Autoregressive on Globally Constrained Problems

author.name: Woosang Jeon, Jaeyeon Kim, Sham Kakade, Yilun Du, Amrit Singh Bedi, Arun Kumar Chithanar, Chul Lee, Taehyeong Kim, Sitan Chen

entry.summary: This paper argues that some weaknesses of LLMs on globally constrained problems stem from the left-to-right inference interface of next-token prediction itself. It proposes blackboard intelligence, where a model iteratively revises a fixed canvas and searches over partially filled candidate solution states, instantiated with diffusion language models whose any-order prediction fits this paradigm. Empirically, this inference-time approach surpasses autoregressive decoding on globally constrained tasks.

entry.title: ID Balancing: Stable Training of Extremely Sparse MoE via PID-Based Load Control

author.name: Peng Jin, Zihan Qiu, Zekun Wang, Bo Zheng, Yang Xu, Tian Xie, Xiao Li, Huaqing Zhang, Haoran Lian, Rui Men, Dayiheng Liu

entry.summary: The paper unifies DeepSeek's loss-free balancing and Kimi K3's Quantile Balancing as incomplete PID controllers, then proposes a full PID-based load controller for extremely sparse Mixture-of-Experts training. This control-theoretic view targets expert load imbalance that undermines stability and parameter utilization at scale.

entry.title: LampAttention: Look-Ahead Mixed-Precision FlashAttention for Dedicated Accelerators

author.name: Stanislav Budzinskiy, Marian Gloser, Tolunay Yilmaz, Ying Hong Tham, Yuanyi Lin, Wenyi Fang, Fan Wu, Philipp Petersen

entry.summary: LampAttention is a hardware-algorithm co-design for mixed-precision attention that computes most key-query products and exponentials in 8-bit while adaptively recomputing sensitive sub-blocks in 16-bit. Experiments with Qwen3 and Gemma 3, both long-established models, show selective high-precision rerouting recovers baseline performance, and the authors propose specifications for a dedicated accelerator.

entry.title: Towards Better Exploration in Sequential Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Joseph Rance, Fabio Pizzati, Juil Sock, Woody Bayliss, Marc G\'orriz Blanch, Philip Torr, Adel Bibi

entry.summary: The paper identifies an attractor phenomenon where sequential test-time scaling for LLM reasoning stops improving because it gets trapped in a set of answers that blocks exploration. Across 27 combinations of scaling methods and models, the authors characterize this failure and propose improvements to exploration in sequential scaling.

entry.title: Backward-State Policy Is Part of the Learning Algorithm

author.name: Shuxiao Xie, Shuyang Xie, Dezhi Ran, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: The authors argue that the choice of which rounded values the backward pass reads in low-precision training is a semantic part of the learning algorithm, not a mere implementation detail. Using emulated FP8 runs at 390M scale, they show training can fail or succeed depending solely on the backward rounding policy, demonstrating that copy accuracy and final loss are insufficient validation checks.

entry.title: Removing Timing Shortcuts Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text

author.name: Dulhan Jayalath, Oiwi Parker Jones

entry.summary: The authors show that major reported improvements in decoding words from non-invasive brain recordings (specifically d'Ascoli et al. 2025) are largely reproducible without any brain data, because fixed-length overlapping word windows leak word-duration information that networks can exploit. Removing these timing shortcuts yields a more honest evaluation and reportedly improves genuine brain-to-text decoding. This is an important corrective for the neuroAI decoding literature.

entry.title: It Takes Little to Rewrite Perception: Targeted Semantic Substitution in Vision-Language Models at $\epsilon \leq 4/255$

author.name: Binchi Zhang, Atrisha Sarkar, Apurva Narayan

entry.summary: This work demonstrates that VLMs previously considered robust to small adversarial perturbations are vulnerable to targeted semantic substitution: by aligning each stream of a source image with its counterpart in a target image within the victim VLM's post-merger token space, attackers succeed at imperceptible perturbation budgets (epsilon at or below 4/255) under a white-box threat model.

entry.title: Warm-starting PDE solvers with any-dimensional machine learning

author.name: Wilson G. Gregory, George A. Kevrekidis, Ben Blum-Smith, Soledad Villar

entry.summary: Leveraging graph-neural-network transferability theory, the authors derive symmetry-based mathematical conditions under which a learned PDE solver trained in low dimensions can be applied zero-shot to higher-dimensional PDEs. When the PDE but not the data satisfies the symmetries, the theory yields a principled warm-starting strategy for higher-dimensional solvers.

entry.title: A Dynamical Theory of LoRA in Continual Learning

author.name: Th\'eo Marchetta, Filippo Alessandroni, Alessandro Breccia, Alessandro Ingrosso, Federica Gerace

entry.summary: The authors derive an asymptotically exact dynamical characterization of LoRA fine-tuning in continual learning using a solvable two-task teacher-student model. They obtain closed ODEs for macroscopic order parameters, yielding exact generalization-error expressions through both the initial learning phase and LoRA fine-tuning, quantitatively matching simulations. The theory exposes how low-rank adaptation shapes catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: When Instructions Retrieve Trajectories: Diagnosing and Mitigating Generalization Failures in VLA Models

author.name: Hung-Jen Chen, Yu-Hsun Hou, Yan-Hong Chen, Yan-Fu Chen, Binghua Cai, Min Sun, Chun-Yi Lee

entry.summary: The paper identifies instruction-action binding as a specific failure mode in vision-language-action models: policies respond to language and vision but fail to combine them to choose the required action, succeeding on in-distribution tasks while failing under counterfactual changes. Behavioral analysis of fine-tuned pi-0.5 and GR00T-N1.7 policies shows failed rollouts retain source behaviors or switch to other demonstrated tasks. The work also proposes mitigations for this generalization failure.

entry.title: Environment Steering: Using Data Flow Control to Improve Agent Utility and Safety

author.name: Charlie Summers, Prajwal Raghunath, Aaditya Pai, Mayur Kulkarni, Zhuo Zhang, Oliver Kennedy, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: This paper proposes Environment Steering, a runtime safety mechanism for LLM agents that models execution state as database tables, tracks record-level data flows, and enforces declarative safety policies during execution. Unlike pre-execution filters or LLM judges, it steers agents toward safe alternatives when violations occur, aiding recovery rather than just blocking.

entry.title: Training LLMs to Verbalize Evaluation Awareness

author.name: Usman Anwar, Sahar Abdelnabi, David Krueger

entry.summary: This paper introduces verbalization training, an RL method that makes LLMs more forthcoming about their awareness of being evaluated, using spontaneous verbalizations as evidence and truncating rollouts before them to build training prefixes. Applied to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kimi K2.6, and Inkling, VT increases calibrated verbalized evaluation awareness without supervising the latent belief. Evaluation awareness can cause models to behave differently during audits than in deployment, making this directly relevant to AI oversight and sandbagging concerns.

entry.title: When Updating Stops Being Learning: Rethinking LLM Self-Evolution via learnable information gain

author.name: Chenxu Wang, Chaozhuo Li, Xinze Shi, Songyang Liu, Kyrie You Wu, Ziluowen Luo, Shun Zhang, Chenxi Li, Litian Zhang

entry.summary: This work addresses self-evolution degeneration in LLMs, where iterative self-training improves then degrades performance, by proposing a holistic measure of learnable information gain defined as KL divergence between successive rounds' data distributions plus entropy change. The gain is estimated by fitting a small model to the generated data, allowing early detection of when updates stop adding learnable information.

entry.title: MultiTalk: Scaling Full-Duplex Speech Models to Long, Multi-Party, Bilingual Conversation

author.name: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Yunqiao Yang, Zhuofan Zong, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: MultiTalk extends the Moshi paradigm of end-to-end full-duplex speech modeling to long, multi-party, bilingual conversations, addressing both long-context robustness and multi-speaker interaction that current systems lack. It also tackles the data and evaluation bottleneck by creating multi-party full-duplex corpora and benchmarks beyond short dyadic exchanges.

entry.title: What Does Post-Training Change in Multilingual Reasoning?

author.name: Hongyang Li, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Gr\'egoire Danoy, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: This paper audits Qwen3 checkpoints on competition math across eleven languages, finding only 15.4-17.9% of non-English problems receive a correct, terminating, visible-reasoning solution in the requested language versus 92.9% in English. It evaluates thirteen endpoints spanning checkpoints and multilingual SFT to isolate what post-training changes about this multilingual access gap.

entry.title: It's All Training: A Fully Synthetic Single-Stage Recipe for LLMs

author.name: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Pieter Delobelle, Yannick Detrois, Pavel Chizhov, Carlos Rosas-Hinostroza, Neil Si Smail, Benjamin Burtin, Hanna Shcharbakova, Ivan Yamshchikov, Anastasia Stasenko

entry.summary: The authors present SYNTH, described as the first open-source synthetic pre-training corpus derived from 58,698 Wikipedia articles, designed to collapse pre-training, mid-training, and post-training into a single stage with reasoning traces included. This addresses the opacity of frontier labs' internal synthetic data practices and enables study of how synthetic corpora affect knowledge and skill acquisition, including in small models. It matters because synthetic data recipes are central to modern LLM training but remain largely proprietary.

entry.title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems

author.name: Fahd Seddik, Fatemeh Fard

entry.summary: This paper studies large language models that reason in continuous latent space by recurring on hidden states or passing them between agents, where training only supervises the final decoded answer via cross-entropy. The authors identify four failure modes of CE-only training, such as thought collapse across questions and retention of irrelevant information, and propose REST, which converts causality, minimality, separability, and stability of thought representations into differentiable auxiliary losses. This matters because latent recursion is an emerging alternative to chain-of-thought text reasoning, and principled training objectives could make it reliable.

entry.title: Can Agents Design Libraries for Agents?

author.name: Gabriel Orlanski, Alex L. Zhang, Avi Trost, Vincent Sunn Chen, Frederic Sala, Aws Albarghouthi, Ludwig Schmidt

entry.summary: LibraryDesignBench is a two-phase benchmark where a designer agent implements a full library from a specification, then three user agents from different model families write programs against it, evaluating correctness and simplicity. Spanning 242 expert-validated problems across 15 library-design tasks in four languages, it finds that on 11 of 15 tasks agent designers reproduce useful abstractions. This tackles an emerging question in agent-agent software ecosystems, where agents currently reimplement rather than reuse code.

entry.title: Authority Bias in Language Models: Source Deference and User Agreement Are Not Interchangeable

author.name: Abhinav Rajeev Kumar (Lossfunk), Paras Chopra (Lossfunk)

entry.summary: This paper measures how much more compliant language models become when a wrong answer is attributed to a verified source rather than asserted by a user, across five open-weight families and three closed APIs. A single authoritative-sounding note endorsing a wrong answer flips 45-88% of baseline-correct responses in seven of eight models, with compliance rising with perceived authority. The findings show source deference and sycophancy are behaviorally distinct inside models, with implications for retrieval-augmented and tool-grounded systems where information arrives with source labels.

entry.title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?

author.name: Hongcheng Gao, Hailong Qu, Yu Lei, Henghui Sun, Haoyang Li, Yipeng Wei, Naihao Xue, Xiaohan Yu, Zhuo Tao, Yihe Zang, Yajiao Wang, Jingyi Tang, Yi Li, Jingjing Zhou, Jie Luo, Bohan Zeng, Chengyu Shen, Hao Jiang, Chong Chen, Bowen Qu, Olive Huang, Zeqiang Wang

entry.summary: EngiWorld is a benchmark of 1,301 expert-curated tasks across six engineering domains (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA, 3D visualization) and 26 professional software platforms, with GUI and CLI interfaces and artifact-centric evaluation via domain verifiers. It targets the gap between strong general computer-use agents and reliable professional engineering automation. This is the first benchmark structured around the complete engineering design loop.

entry.title: Inductive Visual Logic for Few-Shot Out-Of-Distribution Adaptation in VLMs

author.name: Hung-Jen Chen, Yu-Heng Ho, Ting-Yao Huang, Po-Hsiang Hsu, Li-Yu Chen, Chun-Yi Lee, Min Sun

entry.summary: This paper identifies a distant OOD regime where generative VLMs like Qwen-VL and LLaVA fail at discrimination in specialized domains despite retaining strong descriptive ability. The proposed Inductive Visual Logic (IVL) is a training-free framework that exploits the asymmetry between description and discrimination by constructing classification knowledge from the model's own verbalized visual patterns. This allows few-shot adaptation without modifying encoder feature spaces.

entry.title: From Image Interpretation to Clinical Reasoning: Upstream Physician-Context-Aware Multimodal Learning with Causal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jialu Pi, Yanan Ma, Weijie Chen, Owen Crystal, Shubham Trivedi, Stephen Xie, Anna Silverman, Matthew Stib, Chadi Ayoub, Reza Arsanjani, Imon Banerjee

entry.summary: Proposes a causal reinforcement learning framework for opportunistic major adverse cardiovascular event prediction that integrates chest X-rays with physician-authored clinical histories. It uses a role-decoupled dual-LLM architecture to shift from radiology interpretation toward upstream prognostic reasoning, enabling scalable screening from routinely acquired data.

entry.title: DeCoPrune: Efficient KV-Cache Pruning for Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Denoising Consistency

author.name: Zeqi Xiao, Qingle Liu, Kaiwen Zhang, Yifan Zhou, Zihan Ding, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: DeCoPrune is a training-free KV-cache compression method for autoregressive video diffusion that treats pruning as a denoising-consistency problem, retaining tokens whose intermediate clean predictions diverge most from final denoised values. This model-intrinsic discrepancy signal identifies chunks carrying visual evidence not predictable from the retained context, addressing unbounded cache growth in streaming generation.

entry.title: DC-SAE: Deep Compression Semantic Autoencoder for Faster Diffusion Convergence

author.name: Xu Huang, Ye Huang, Zijun Liao, Yuwei Niu, Xiaojie Li, Menghan Zhou, De Wen Soh, Xiaotong Li, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: DC-SAE is a decoupled compact semantic autoencoder achieving both high token compression and fast diffusion training by addressing the fidelity-versus-learnability tradeoff that afflicts aggressive tokenizers and prior representation autoencoders. It replaces VAE latents with semantically expressive features while retaining the pixel-level detail needed for faithful reconstruction.

entry.title: EgoTools: Towards Tool-Centric Reasoning in Real-World Egocentric Videos

author.name: Shulin Tian, Junsu Kim, Shuai Liu, Hao Li, Yujiao Shen, Sihan Li, Zhe Yang, Yeongon Kim, Feiyu Li, Jialin Wu, Yichi Zhang, Wenhui Wang, Runmao Yao, Yuhao Dong, Zhaoxi Chen, Fangzhou Hong, Antonino Furnari, Jingkang Yang, Hongyuan Zhu, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: EgoTools introduces a benchmark and dataset for tool-centric embodied reasoning in real-world egocentric videos, requiring models to reason about affordances, hand-tool-object geometry, procedural progress, and causal effects. It shows that current multimodal video models, despite strong perception performance, remain weak at this form of reasoning.

entry.title: FAST: Flow Any Scene Transformer

author.name: Yongjian Zhang, Longguang Wang, Zhuo Song, Zhiheng Fu, Liang Lin, Yulan Guo

entry.summary: FAST is a scalable correspondence-matching transformer showing that query-key projections inside single-view vision foundation models encode a reusable prior for cross-view matching. A zero-parameter rewiring strategy converts a vanilla single-view encoder into a cross-view matcher, leveraging pretrained projections as initialization.

entry.title: I Have a Stream: Making Self-Supervised Learning Work on Continuous Video

author.name: Ivan Martinovi\'c, Lukas Knobel, Yuki M. Asano

entry.summary: The authors study self-supervised learning from continuous video streams where frames are consumed in temporal order with strict sliding-window batches, no global shuffling, and no multi-epoch replay, motivated by infant visual development. They build WT++, a 95-hour urban walking video dataset and evaluation suite, finding that contrastive and distillation methods struggle while MAE is more robust but still trails i.i.d. pretraining. The work identifies inter-batch similarity as a key factor in stream-based learning.

entry.title: Exploiting Vulnerabilities: Universal Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models in Robotics

author.name: Songhua Yang, Ziyu Liu, Yuanwei Liu, Xuetao Li, Xuanye Fei, He Huang, Zheng Wang, Miao Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Universal Adversarial Object, a physical sphere with optimized surface texture that significantly degrades VLA model task success rates when placed in the robot's field of view. A multi-level attack framework jointly disrupts trajectory planning, task execution, and action control. Given that VLAs act directly in the physical world alongside humans, the work exposes serious and previously underexplored security vulnerabilities.

entry.title: PRICE the Action Chunks: Physical Relational Credit Assignment for Embodied Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yangang Zou, Jiajun Lu, Weitao Zhou, Haibao Yu, Bozhou Zhang, Jiawei Wang, Honglong Tian, Minglei Li, Li Zhang

entry.summary: PRICE addresses a flaw in outcome-based RL post-training of vision-language-action policies, where every action chunk in a trajectory receives the same terminal advantage, penalizing useful early actions in failed episodes. It proposes using physical relations across trajectories — rollouts reaching corresponding physical situations — as mutual references to derive action-chunk-level credit from terminal outcomes alone, without an auxiliary evaluator model.

entry.title: Toward Real-Time VLAs: Stage-Aware Two-Step Flow Denoising and System-Level Evaluation

author.name: Di Wu, Rongtian Shen, Ping Liu, Yan Shen, Zhenhan Yin, Shun Zuo, Xuhua Chen, He Zheng, Lingfeng Zhang, Jianglin Zhang, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: The authors characterize the latency gap between low-rate vision-language-action (VLA) model inference and high-rate robot execution, showing that repeated flow-matching denoising dominates inference cost. Exploiting the observation that velocity fields are stable early but require correction late in integration, they propose two-stage non-uniform denoising that cuts steps from 10 to 2 and inference time from about 61.6 ms substantially.

entry.title: Conditional Generation of Creative Chess Puzzles with Diffusion Models

author.name: Aatu Selkee, Severi Rissanen, Xidong Feng, Tom Zahavy, Eric Malmi

entry.summary: The authors propose conditional generation of creative chess puzzles using masked diffusion models, allowing conditioning on tactical themes and partial board positions via a non-directional diffusion approach. A simultaneous best-move prediction auxiliary task improves solution uniqueness by 11.6% and theme-conditioning accuracy, positioning chess composition as a testbed for constrained computational creativity.

entry.title: WorkGenesis: Building the Worlds That Teach Agents to Work

author.name: Xinyu Zhu, Fenyi Liu, Yuzhu Cai, Shuo Tang, Rui Ye, Linfeng Zhang, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: WorkGenesis is a framework for generating executable occupational work tasks grounded in real-world artifacts, using evidence-based construction guided by O*NET occupational knowledge and retrieval of public files. It addresses the cost of expert-authored occupational tasks and the weak grounding of unconstrained synthesis for training work-capable agents.

entry.title: Advancing Entropy-Level Credit Assignment in RLVR via Proximal Entropy Policy Optimization

author.name: Yun Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: PEPO measures token importance relative to neighboring tokens via a proximal entropy metric proven invariant to prompt difficulty and positional trends, then uses it to weight per-token advantages in value-free RLVR. It outperforms GRPO and entropy-based baselines on mathematical reasoning across multiple small models.

entry.title: Growing an Agent/Prover Interface: Evolutionary Tool Design for Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving in Rocq and Lean

author.name: Jules Viennot, Guillaume Baudart, Marc Lelarge

entry.summary: The paper proposes an evolutionary method where a frontier model proposes new features for the agent-prover interface and retains only those improving smaller models' performance, producing an MCP server for the Rocq prover. This co-designs interfaces for agents rather than reusing human-oriented tools, improving cost efficiency in theorem proving.

entry.title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training

author.name: Kunlun Zhu, Xuyan Ye, Yibo Li, Cheng Qian, Beibin Li, Heng Ji

entry.summary: The Agent Error Dataset provides 50,228 error-diagnosis pairs from 9,961 source tasks spanning 33 environments, 19 harness families, and 23 policy models, retaining source traces and execution metadata for failure analysis and re-diagnosis. A five-stage Agentic Error-to-Training pipeline collects natural failures and converts them into diagnoses and actionable revision targets for error-aware post-training.

entry.title: dattri-LLM: A Unified and Efficient Library for Training Data Attribution at LLM Scale

author.name: Shixuan Liu, Tongli Zhou, Junwei Deng, Pingbang Hu, Jiaqi W. Ma

entry.summary: Presents dattri-LLM, a library making gradient-based training data attribution practical at LLM scale through compact gradient representations, cost-model-driven routing of gradient operations, and a capture mechanism that collects per-example gradients from existing training loops including DDP, FSDP, and pipelined setups without code changes.

entry.title: SceneJail: Exploiting Video Scenario Context to Jailbreak Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Wenyu Chen, Li Wang, Chuanchao Zang, Xiangtao Meng, Xinyu Gao, Jianing Wang, Zheng Li, Shanqing Guo

entry.summary: SceneJail demonstrates that the same harmful query can elicit different safety responses in video MLLMs depending on the surrounding video scenario, and introduces an adaptive black-box jailbreak framework with adaptive scenario construction that exploits this contextual attack surface. Existing video jailbreaks only manipulated visual presentation of the query itself.

entry.title: Emergent Multi-View Geometry Through Self-Distillation

author.name: David Nordstr\"om, Thibaut Loiseau, Vincent Lepetit, Michael Felsberg, Guillaume Bourmaud, Fredrik Kahl

entry.summary: Poincare3 is a self-supervised method learning multi-view geometric representations via self-distillation rather than RGB reconstruction, combining masked patch and image-level distillation with a teacher that sees additional views, trained from scratch without 3D supervision. It outperforms prior single- and multi-view self-supervised methods including DINOv3, MuM, and Muskie on correspondence estimation.

entry.title: OmniReasoning: Pushing the Limits of Audio-Visual Joint Reasoning

author.name: Junming Lin, Yuxuan Wang, Zhenxin Lei, Yuxin Liu, Ruixun Liu, Yinsong Yan, Ling Wang, Minghao Han, Yunfei Chu, Shun Lei, Xueyao Zhang, Qize Yang, Jin Xu, Yiwu Zhong

entry.summary: OmniReasoning tackles the under-evaluation and under-elicitation of audio-visual joint reasoning with three contributions: OmniReasoningBench with 1,150 questions requiring both audio and visual evidence, the OmniQA data engine that automatically builds evidence-grounded QA pairs, and a learning method for omni-modal models.

entry.title: CIDER-FM: Foundation Models for Causal Inference from Diverse Experimental Regimes

author.name: Yuche Gao, Arik Reuter, Siyuan Guo, Anish Dhir, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Adrian Weller

entry.summary: CIDER-FM studies causal foundation models that combine finite observational and surrogate-interventional datasets to predict target conditional interventional distributions when interventions on the variable of interest are unavailable. The authors formalize the benefits of surrogate experiments and train on priors of synthetic structural causal models.

entry.title: NodeGround: A Node Classification Benchmark in the Graph Foundation Model Era

author.name: Jinmo Lee, Dooho Lee, Minho Jeong, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: NodeGround is a large-scale benchmark comparing graph foundation models against dataset-specific supervised learning for node classification across 51 datasets, six GFMs, and 15 supervised baselines under controlled evaluation with workflow cost measurements. Early results favor carefully tuned supervised methods, questioning whether pretrained graph models can replace per-dataset predictors.

entry.title: RoPE at the End of Its Rope? Theory, Diagnosis, and Mitigation of Long-Context Failures

author.name: Yuyang Wu, Yufeng Du, Hao Peng

entry.summary: The paper refines the theory of RoPE-based long-context failures by allowing unequal query-key scales across frequencies, yielding per-head, per-input measures of positional sensitivity and semantic stability. It derives a theoretical context-length bound and uses the diagnosis to motivate mitigation strategies for long-context degradation.

entry.title: BadAction: Backdoor Attacks on Interactive Video Generation via Action-Guided Triggers

author.name: Zhihang Wu, Zhongqi Wang, Jie Zhang, Fengming Gu, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic study of backdoor attacks against interactive video generation models, proposing BadAction, which embeds predefined motion patterns in action sequences as triggers. Once triggered, the backdoored model freezes future frames and stops responding to user actions while behaving normally otherwise, revealing a previously unexamined attack surface.

entry.title: How to Run Statistics over LLM Judges and Trust the Results: Calibrated Inference for Small-Sample AI Evaluation with evalstats

author.name: Ian Arawjo

entry.summary: This work shows that naive statistics over raw LLM judge scores inflate false positives, with false positive risk peaking counterintuitively at near-perfect human-LLM agreement for some inter-rater metrics. It provides guidance and the evalstats tooling with nine hypothesis tests and calibrated intervals for mixed human-AI judge evaluation designs.

entry.title: ATTUNER: Recomputation-Free KV Cache Reuse via Query-Side Adaptation

author.name: Xinghao Chen, Junnan Dong, Cai Ke, Chak Tou Leong, Haocheng Sun, Keyu Chen, Siyu An, Ruizhi Qiao, Xing Sun, Wenjie Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: ATTUNER enables position-independent KV cache reuse for LLM agents loading repeated content by adapting on the query side rather than recomputing tokens or restoring position IDs. The authors isolate the source of quality loss, showing positional mismatch has minor effect and independently cached artifacts retain faithful representations, motivating a recomputation-free adaptation approach.

entry.title: TTMark: Pairwise Distortion-Free Watermarking Beyond Single-Token Entropy

author.name: Ruibo Chen, Zhengmian Hu, Donghang Lu, Xuehao Cui, Georgios Milis, Yihan Wu, Jian Du, Heng Huang

entry.summary: TTMARK extends distortion-free watermarking of LLM text from individual tokens to adjacent token pairs, watermarking the joint distribution of consecutive tokens to enlarge the effective alphabet from V to V-squared. This lets detection exploit both token entropy and conditional entropy while preserving output distribution, overcoming the fundamental detection limit imposed by low-entropy single-token distributions. This is a meaningful advance for reliable attribution of machine-generated text.

entry.title: LongTake: Learning to Sustain Dynamics in Long-Horizon Video Generation

author.name: Byoungwoo Park, Jaemoo Choi, Juho Lee, Yongxin Chen

entry.summary: LongTake addresses the failure of autoregressive video diffusion to sustain coherent dynamics over long rollouts, hypothesizing that short-video supervision provides insufficient guidance for long-duration scene evolution. The two-stage pipeline centers on Long-Horizon Teacher Forcing, training the AR model to predict later frames conditioned on long ground-truth video prefixes from curated real long videos. This extends direct supervision to longer horizons for world models, game simulators, and long-take video creation.

entry.title: Rethinking Generative Image Compression at Extremely Low Bitrates

author.name: Tianyu Zhang, Zhaoyang Jia, Houqiang Li, Dong Liu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes semantic collapse in generative image codecs as bitrate approaches zero, identifying gradient and objective conflicts between reconstruction and semantic goals plus the declining semantic efficiency of pixel-space VAE diffusion models. It introduces RAE-CoD, a compression-oriented diffusion model built in a representation autoencoder space, to degrade gracefully at extreme low bitrates.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Predicate Learning for Semantic Safe Robot Control

author.name: Zihan Ye, Jiayi Liu, Puze Liu, Jiayun Li, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Jan Peters, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: NEUPRO uses a differentiable reasoner to learn reusable safety representations from human-specified safety knowledge, letting practitioners express robot safety requirements as transparent predicates instead of opaque cost functions or task-coupled mathematical formulations. This yields interpretable insight into why actions are safe or unsafe and transfers across tasks. Interpretable, reusable safety representations are important as robots deploy in everyday environments.

entry.title: MoFlow: Multi-Objective Agentic Workflow Generation

author.name: Yining Lu, Aurelie Lozano, Xi Yang, Naoki Abe, Yu Deng, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: MoFlow formulates agentic workflow generation as a multi-objective MDP optimizing accuracy, cost, latency, robustness, and consistency jointly. It uses Convex-Hull Monte Carlo Tree Search with optimistic set-valued backups so each node stores a set of reachable trade-offs, allowing a single trained generator to produce workflows across varied preferences instead of requiring retraining per preference weighting.

entry.title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration

author.name: Dannong Wang, Yuran Zhang, Bian Sun, Alex Stinard, Yuzhang Shang, Song Wang, Yu Tian

entry.summary: PrivMeSA is a privacy-aware multi-agent clinical system where a local LLM agent consults more capable remote specialists while learning to control disclosure, addressing re-identification risk from quasi-identifiers accumulating across multi-turn consultations. Reinforcement learning balances task accuracy against disclosure and registry-based re-identification risks, and the system retains remote expertise for local reuse.

entry.title: When Context Changes: Understanding Update Failures in LLMs

author.name: Junyu Guo, Yuchen Fang, Shangding Gu, Costas Spanos, James Demmel, Javad Lavaei

entry.summary: This paper identifies and studies stale binding, a failure mode where LLM agents answer with outdated values of updated variables still present in context. The authors introduce the Controlled In-Context Memory (CICM) benchmark and use probing and component tests on Qwen and Pythia to show that updated information often remains internally available but is not selected during generation.

entry.title: Search Shapes Conclusions: Auditing Evidence Selection Bias in Deep Research Agents

author.name: Shuyao Xiao, Shengling Wang, Xuan Chen, Ke Chao, Ming Cui, Feifei Qian, Chaoyang Mei, Fanlin Meng, Lulu Wang, Ziming Yu, Junxi Yin

entry.summary: The paper identifies evidence selection bias in deep research agents: adaptive search makes the documents read a selective sample of the candidate pool, so a well-cited report can still support a misleading conclusion. It introduces Causal Evidence Selection Correction (CESS), which predicts each candidate document's evidence direction to correct candidate-pool level averages.

entry.title: Rep2Skill: Representation-Guided Skill Self-Evolution for LLM Agents

author.name: Kaixing Zhang, Changming Li, Yingdong Shi, Zheng Zhang, Kaitao Song, Wenjie Shi, Jingang Wang, Kan Ren

entry.summary: Rep2Skill proposes using an LLM agent's internal representations, rather than only execution trajectories and sparse outcomes, to guide the evolution of external textual skills. By reflecting on internal states, the framework aims to make skill optimization more informed and sample-efficient without parameter updates.

entry.title: The Golden Path Hypothesis: Reusable Schedules in Diffusion Caching

author.name: Dong Wang, Wenwu Tang, Francesco Corti, Yun Cheng, Lothar Thiele, Olga Saukh

entry.summary: The Golden Path Hypothesis claims that prompt-independent cache schedules can match the quality of the best prompt-specific schedules in diffusion caching. Extensive evaluation across ten caching methods, four image and video models, and 1.4 million schedules supports the hypothesis, suggesting simpler fixed schedules can replace adaptive caching policies.

entry.title: Experimental Experience Modeling for Autonomous Research

author.name: Wenda Wei, Yingchen Zhang, Ruqing Zhang, Jiafeng Guo, Daiting Shi, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: EEM is a framework for autonomous research agents that acquire, reuse, and accumulate experimental experience to decide which experiments are worth running. It extracts decision-relevant records from prior trajectories, distills them into a reusable experience library, and uses them to reduce the computational cost of experimentation.

entry.title: RankEvolve: A Reliable Multi-Agent Auto-Research Harness for Evolving Ranking Models

author.name: Zheng Chen, Linfeng Liu, Hong Li, Hong Yan

entry.summary: RankEvolve is an auto-research framework in which LLM agents propose, implement, train, and evaluate changes to generative ranking models across iterations. It enforces an executable operating protocol as a compiled state machine and composes existing black-box coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, with an emphasis on preventing silent execution errors like data leakage and unwired flags that invalidate long-horizon experiment loops.

entry.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Yinghui He, Yapei Chang, Khushi Bhardwaj, Daniele Molinari, Tugrul Konuk, Jan Kautz, Ali Hatamizadeh

entry.summary: The authors identify that most failed multi-turn agent rollouts hinge on a single early pivotal mistake, and that brief teacher guidance after that turn can restore success. PivotOPD is an on-policy distillation framework that concentrates teacher supervision on recovering from these pivotal errors, mitigating compounding error across turns. Experiments span Qwen3 models from 8B to 235B.

entry.title: How Should Diffusion Language Models Edit Code?

author.name: Xijia Tao, Ziru Liu, Shansan Gong, Jiacheng Ye, Kecheng Chen, Zirui Wu, Lin Zheng, Xinyu Fu, Rui Liu, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: The authors systematically compare four code-editing interfaces (whole-file rewriting, search-and-replace, locate-then-infill, token-level editing) for masked diffusion language models on the CanItEdit benchmark. They identify a composition gap: diffusion models can generate coordinated edits when locations are given but largely lose this ability when they must predict edit locations themselves. This informs interface design for the emerging class of diffusion LMs.

entry.title: When Correct Memory Goes Wrong: Fuzzing Persistent Memory Use in LLM Agents

author.name: Yuqiao Meng, Luoxi Tang, Yingxue Zhang, Yuchen Yang, Zhaohan Xi

entry.summary: This paper reframes failures in how LLM agents use persistent memory as a fuzzing problem, distinguishing query-related from memory-state failures, and introduces U-Fuzz, which seeds tests from memory checkpoints and mutates queries or states under explicit mutation obligations. The approach systematically surfaces memory-use failures that fixed test cases and content-error analyses miss.

entry.title: Acceleration of Diffusion Language Model through Discrete Average Generator

author.name: Yidong Ouyang, Zhengyan Wan, Themis Haris, Tian Tan, Liqian Peng, Henry Li, Ziqian Lin, Jianhang Chen, Maryam Karimzadehgan, Alec Go, George Michailidis

entry.summary: This paper extends MeanFlow to continuous-time Markov chains, defining an average generator as the normalized increment of the transition kernel for discrete diffusion and flow matching models. The resulting self-consistency identity yields a training objective enabling few-step generation, addressing the key efficiency bottleneck of discrete diffusion language models.

entry.title: Does Gradient Conflict Predict the Understanding--Generation Trade-off? A Controlled Audit of Conflict-Metric Validity in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Shuyang Jiang, Fucheng Deng, Yuchuan Luo, Zhenyu Wu

entry.summary: This paper audits the widely held assumption that reducing gradient conflict between understanding and generation objectives improves the trade-off in unified multimodal models. Using a controlled testbed called GRIDUMM where the true trade-off is exactly computable, the authors find across 63 configurations and 372 checkpoints that no conflict metric reliably predicts downstream trade-off outcomes, and interventions that suppress conflict leave the trade-off largely unchanged.

entry.title: Beyond Oracle Communication: Benchmarking Interactive Intent Alignment Under Miscommunication and Evolving User Intent

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Mengyuan Chao, Ke Xiao, Ziyi Chen, Daoan Zhang, Yan Zhang, Yanfang Ye, Wei Xu

entry.summary: The paper defines Interactive Intent Alignment, where agents must recover and track a user's current intent despite miscommunication, shifting goals, and limited patience, and introduces Drift-Bench++, a pipeline for executable tasks with controlled misalignment and intent drift plus an interaction-based evaluation. It challenges the oracle-communication assumption of existing agent benchmarks.

entry.title: Understanding Off- vs On-Policy Distillation: A Tale of Distinct Training Objectives

author.name: Qiwei Di, Xuheng Li, Kaixuan Ji, Chenggong Zhang, Heyang Zhao, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical study of on-policy distillation, where a student learns from teacher feedback on its own generated responses, focusing on sequential distillation from multiple teachers. The paper shows forward KL yields a weighted arithmetic mixture while reverse KL yields a normalized geometric aggregate, develops algorithms with logarithmic regret guarantees in the tabular case, and extends to function approximation.

entry.title: Where MLLMs Fail and Why: Causal Task Decomposition for Capability Failure Diagnosis

author.name: Xia Hu, Brian Potetz, Chun-Ta Lu, Huanfen Yao, Leonidas Guibas, Zhicheng Wang, Howard Zhou, Pengfei Xing, Andrew Gallagher

entry.summary: The authors propose a causal decomposition framework that distinguishes intrinsic capability deficits from cascading upstream errors in multimodal LLMs, using controlled interventions on prerequisite dependencies. Metrics score necessity and sufficiency of each prerequisite, instantiated in CADET, a diagnostic benchmark of ten compositional capabilities.

entry.title: APTInvestBench: Evaluating Autonomous APT Investigation under Varying Telemetry

author.name: Yu Wang, Shuhao Li, Tao Yin, Ziyang Li, Xueying Zhao, Peishuai Sun, Jiang Xie

entry.summary: APTInvestBench evaluates LLM agents performing autonomous investigation of advanced persistent threats across seven SOC-inspired telemetry conditions, built from 56 report-informed attack reconstructions with 16.4 million log records across 370 cases. Agents must turn weak leads into cited evidence reports, and the benchmark tests robustness to changes in log collection, retention, and sampling rather than fixed environments.

entry.title: From Verification Failures to Reusable Guidance for Coding Agents

author.name: Yuqing Zhai, Xiaohong Chen, Lingming Zhang, Sriram Vishwanath, Grigore Rosu

entry.summary: This paper combines executable language definitions in the K framework with a kit of procedures for specification construction, proof repair, and adequacy auditing to make expert diagnosis of verification failures reusable for coding agents. A human-guided campaign on HumanEval achieves a 164/164 success rate, and the authors construct adversarial audit cases to test whether auditing catches issues that successful proofs miss. It matters because it connects formal verification rigor with practical LLM coding agent workflows.

entry.title: Coding Agents for Coding Theory

author.name: Abraham Yeung

entry.summary: The authors spend five weeks using an LLM coding agent on open problems in coding theory, targeting large edit-distance code sets such as DNA barcodes. The agent writes verifiers and search code while a human sets the problem and verification protocol, raising the best known code for length 6 and minimum edit distance 3 from 114 to 120 words and improving twelve further lower bounds. Notably, the paper reports failures with equal candor, including a search that stalled below the true optimum.

entry.title: Working Around the Compute Ceiling: Byte-Exact Memory in Galahad Makes LLM Reading a One-Time Cost LLM Reading a One-Time Cost

author.name: Sietse Schelpe

entry.summary: Galahad is a memory layer for vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp that persists byte-exact key-value state so documents are read by an LLM only once, avoiding recomputation across requests. On seven real-world datasets the authors found 98.7% of prompt tokens were text the model had already read, motivating substantial compute savings.

entry.title: ActionGuard: Tool Call Authorization under Poisoned Skills

author.name: Jihun Han, Yejin Jang, Byung Il Kwak, Mee Lan Han

entry.summary: ActionGuard inspects LLM agent tool calls immediately before execution to defend against malicious instructions hidden in third-party skills. It separates the agent's action-generation context from the safeguard's authorization context so the reviewer never sees poisoned raw skill text, deciding whether each action should proceed.

entry.title: From Modes to Memories: Characterizing the Scale-Space Dynamics of Diffusion Models

author.name: Cristina L\'opez Amado, Marco Fumero, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: The paper treats diffusion models at each noise scale as deterministic dynamical systems, showing that fixed points of the denoiser correspond to critical points of the smoothed data density and attractors correspond to its modes. This yields a geometric account of memorization: duplicated or overfit examples remain distinguishable under stronger smoothing than ordinary samples, suggesting practical memorization detection.

entry.title: Inference Auctions

author.name: Keegan Harris, Siddharth Prasad, Asher Trockman, Nika Haghtalab, Michael I. Jordan

entry.summary: The paper designs an auction mechanism for LLM inference priority so users can bid for faster service when demand exceeds compute capacity, replacing coarse fixed-price tiers. It proves economically efficient allocation without latency loss, gives fast truthful-pricing algorithms, and builds an autobidding agent that maximizes user utility under a specified inference budget.

entry.title: Game-Guided Skill Discovery through Self-Play for Playable Agent Control

author.name: Seungeun Rho, Jeonghwan Kim, Xue Bin Peng, Sehoon Ha

entry.summary: GGSD uses competitive self-play in games to discover motor skills that are semantically distinct, interpretable, and directly playable by humans via a small discrete skill set. A hierarchical agent with a high-level skill selector and skill-conditioned low-level policy competes against past selves to ground skill discovery. This offers a compact interface for human control of embodied agents.

entry.title: EviRover: Reinforcing Agentic Perception Beyond a Glance

author.name: Kaixuan Fan, Kaituo Feng, Tianshuo Peng, Yilei Jiang, Manyuan Zhang, Junke Wang, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: EviRover reframes visual perception as an agentic process that actively gathers evidence when a single image glance is insufficient, targeting fine-grained or knowledge-intensive queries. The authors build two data generation pipelines (EviRover-SFT-5K, EviRover-RL-12K) and a human-verified benchmark (EviLens) for this perception-under-insufficient-evidence setting. Formalizes and resources a new task area.

entry.title: Grokking through the Lens of Minimum-Norm Interpolation

author.name: Gil Kur, Ileana Rugina, Cl\'ementine Carla Juliette Domin\'e, Marco Mondelli

entry.summary: This paper develops a statistical theory of grokking, characterizing how regularization geometry and signal sparsity govern delayed generalization near interpolation in high-dimensional regression. It identifies regimes where sparsity-promoting regularization makes exact interpolation more accurate than approximate fitting, proves a zero-one generalization law in strongly overparameterized noiseless settings, and connects the results to minimum-norm interpolation.

entry.title: SparLeak: Privacy Leakage from Sparse Attention in LLM Inference on Shared GPUs

author.name: Fahao Chen, Linkang Du, Jinhao Zhou, Peng Li, Zhou Su

entry.summary: SparLeak identifies a new GPU micro-architectural side channel called Sparsity-Induced Memory Access (SIMA), arising from secret-dependent key-value cache access patterns in sparse attention used for long-context LLM inference. The attack extracts phase-aware traces to infer query attributes during prefill and reconstruct approximate autoregressive responses during decoding on shared GPUs. This exposes concrete privacy risks in an optimization technique widely assumed to be innocuous.

entry.title: Visualizing Distribution Coverage in Generative Diffusion Models

author.name: Yifei Wang, Xiaoyu Wu, Tsu-Jui Fu, Chen Chen, Liang-Chieh Chen, Zhe Gan, Chen Wei

entry.summary: This paper challenges the belief that few-step diffusion distillation models match their multi-step teachers by pointing out that standard benchmarks like GenEval2 draw only one sample per prompt, masking losses in distribution coverage. The authors introduce a pass@k evaluation framework that measures whether k independent draws surface genuinely diverse successes or merely replicate the same outputs. This provides a more rigorous diagnostic for comparing distilled students against teacher models.

entry.title: Parameter symmetries determine representational geometry in overparameterized nonlinear networks

author.name: Marvin Theiss, Lukas Braun, Andrew M. Saxe, Erin Grant

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that parameter symmetries in overparameterized networks act on representations through three primitive feature transformations: addition, duplication, and scaling. The result clarifies the fundamental link between representational geometry and computation, with implications for interpretability research in ML, psychology, and neuroscience.

entry.title: Learning Infinite-Horizon Average-Reward CMDPs via State Augmentation

author.name: Kihyun Yu, Seoungbin Bae, Dabeen Lee

entry.summary: This paper studies infinite-horizon average-reward constrained Markov decision processes (CMDPs) under the weakly communicating assumption, addressing gaps in prior high-probability guarantees that were either computationally inefficient or had suboptimal regret dependence on interactions. The authors propose the first computationally efficient tabular algorithm achieving O(sqrt(T)) regret and cumulative constraint violation with high probability, which is optimal up to logarithmic factors. The method works by augmenting the state with cumulative constraint violation and defining a reshaped reward through differences of a Huber potential.

entry.title: Learning Beyond Full Imitation: Task-Preserving Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Qianfeng Yuan, Wenbing Tao

entry.summary: The paper proves an exact separation between full imitation and conditional learning in knowledge distillation, showing that exact KL minimization to the teacher can force a student to discard discrimination it already possesses. It characterizes when imitation is blocked by score-advantage preservation conditions and motivates task-preserving distillation objectives.

entry.title: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors

author.name: Bo Han, Qianyi Wang, Shuai Liu, Xiong Zifan, Changqiao Wu, Yuanfa Li, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan, Heng Qu, Yunpeng Song, Zhongmin Cai

entry.summary: This paper addresses the reliability of GUI agents on unseen applications and multi-step tasks by proposing a framework that couples retrieval-augmented knowledge acquisition with noise-robust utilization. Rather than pursuing perfect app-specific knowledge, the method explicitly learns to act correctly under imperfect, drifting priors caused by app updates, ads, A/B tests, and personalization.

entry.title: Fork-dLLM: Avoiding the Flexibility Trap in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Stipe Frkovi\'c, Metod Jazbec, Christian A. Naesseth

entry.summary: The paper identifies a flexibility trap in confidence-based samplers for masked diffusion language models, which defer unmasking high-entropy fork positions and thereby reduce diversity and hamper RL post-training. Fork-dLLM proposes a hybrid sampler applying autoregressive-style ordering only at fork positions, improving pass@k scaling without abandoning confidence-based parallel decoding.

entry.title: The System Prompt Illusion: How Instruction Preambles Modify Computation in Language Models

author.name: Muhammad Usama, Dong Eui Chang

entry.summary: Using CKA across 17 instruction-tuned models from 1.5B to 72B parameters spanning 8 architecture families, the paper shows system prompts have layer-selective, instruction-type-dependent effects: persona and formatting instructions deeply restructure intermediate representations while safety instructions barely move them. Restrictive and permissive safety instructions produce statistically indistinguishable representational changes from a minimal baseline. This challenges assumptions about how system prompts steer model behavior.

entry.title: Beyond Layers: Position-Resolved Gradient Conflict and Position-Aware Modulation for Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Shuyang Jiang, Fucheng Deng, Yuchuan Luo, Zhenyu Wu

entry.summary: For unified multimodal models that jointly train image understanding and autoregressive generation, this paper shows gradient conflict varies systematically with the position of visual tokens in the raster sequence, not just by layer or expert. It introduces a position-resolved interference map and position-aware modulation to resolve understanding-generation conflicts.

entry.title: DCM-SAM: Defect-Conditioned Mixture of LoRA Experts for NPU-Deployed AM Defect Segmentation

author.name: Md Mushfiqur Rahaman, Md Mahedi Hasan, Imtiaz Ahmed, Srinjoy Das

entry.summary: This paper introduces DCM-SAM, a defect-conditioned mixture of LoRA experts built on a frozen Segment Anything backbone for X-ray CT defect segmentation in metal additive manufacturing. It trains per-defect-class expert banks purely on synthetic slices, updates only 4.4% of parameters, and achieves 64.2% pore IoU on real NIST scans without ever seeing real training images, with deployment on NPU hardware.

entry.title: Looped Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Yong Xien Chng, Tianyi Chen, Wenwen Tong, Haiwen Diao, Zhongang Cai, Lei Yang, Ziwei Liu, Lewei Lu, Dahua Lin, Gao Huang

entry.summary: The paper explores scaling test-time computation in text-to-image diffusion models by repeatedly running shared Transformer blocks within each denoising step, increasing effective depth without more parameters. Naive looping fails, so the authors diagnose weak supervision across intermediate loops and attention-update erosion of local information, proposing Looped Diffusion Transformer with fixes for both. This offers a parameter-efficient alternative to scaling model size or denoising steps.

entry.title: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions

author.name: Xunjian Yin, Tianchen Guan, Jinao Wang, Weili Cao, Daisy Xinlei Lin, Royce Cheng-Yue, Keagan Long, Kyle Wong, Bhuwan Dhingra, Xiangjun Wang, Shuyan Zhou

entry.summary: BreakingWeb makes benchmark difficulty programmable by pairing solvable base browser tasks with deterministic, detectable, recoverable environment interventions at different layers of the web stack, annotated with cognitive demands. This lets researchers isolate what actually makes a task hard rather than making benchmarks longer or novel.

entry.title: CruxBench: A Benchmark of Information Discovery

author.name: Hui Dai, Lina Piao, Nick Merrill, Nadja Flechner, Ezra Karger, Haifeng Xu

entry.summary: CruxBench grades LLM-generated questions by their Value of Information: how much proposed crux questions update beliefs about target forecasting questions. It evaluates the underexplored skill of identifying which questions are worth asking, and is contamination-resistant by construction.

entry.title: Targeting Pivotal Decisions for Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dongwon Jung, Hemanth Neelgund Ramesh, Yifan Wang, Xiaomin Li, Yuexing Hao, Yu Hu, Muhao Chen, Varun Chandrasekaran, Andrzej Banburski-Fahey, Jaron Lanier

entry.summary: ProVer improves GRPO-based agentic RL by identifying pivotal decisions that distinguish successful from failed trajectories, rather than uniformly assigning trajectory-level advantages to all tokens. An agentic judge proposes candidate segments and the framework verifies them via advantage estimation before applying fine-grained credit assignment. This addresses a core weakness in training LLM agents with reinforcement learning.

entry.title: ProgressCompass: Embodied Progress Reward Models Are Lost Without the Right Context

author.name: Jianshu Zhang, Keliang Wu, Chengxuan Qian, Xiyuan Yang, Ce Zhang, Ariel Tian, Anbang Liu, Haoran Lu, Han Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies context-dependent progress estimation as a key failure mode for progress reward models in long-horizon embodied tasks, where the current frame alone cannot indicate task progress. It introduces ContextProgress-Bench with 24 tasks to systematically test whether PRMs can estimate progress when history matters, and finds existing models struggle without the right context.

entry.title: Repetition, Not Length: Isolating the Counting Failure in Neural Text-to-Speech

author.name: Kirill Borodin, Vasilii Kudryavtsev, Maxim Maslov, Grach Mkrtchian

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that neural text-to-speech models fail on repeated phrases because of repetition itself rather than increased length. Using matched control sentences, six models across three architectures score 94.3% on controls but only 18.2% on repeated twins, and the finding is validated across decoding strategies, multiple speech recognizers, and a held-out architecture.

entry.title: Pair Difficulty Matters: Rethinking Pairwise LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation and Consistency

author.name: Bruno Brocai, Maria Becker

entry.summary: Argues that standard reliability proxies for LLM judges (position bias, transitivity, agreement) are misleading because under Bradley-Terry geometry they are dominated by close-rank-gap pairs where inconsistency is information-theoretically expected and contributes little to aggregate rankings. The paper recommends refocusing judge assessment on far-gap pairs where verdicts actually matter.

entry.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision

author.name: Dor Tirosh, Ido Amos, Mor Geva

entry.summary: This paper introduces LIFT, an architecture and training method that removes the strictly feed-forward bottleneck of transformers by propagating latent state across generation steps. Recurrent-state learning is reformulated as teacher-forced prediction: each input token is paired with an information-dense state derived from an off-the-shelf model's next-token distribution. This could let models avoid recomputing intermediate results and retain alternative continuations during generation.

entry.title: OTROPE: Optimal Transport-based Robust Off-policy Evaluation for Large Language Models

author.name: Liner Xiang, Wenbo Zhang, Hengrui Cai

entry.summary: OTROPE tackles off-policy evaluation for LLMs, where scarce human-labeled data from a behavior model must be used to evaluate a newer target model despite distribution shift and unavailable likelihoods for black-box models. The method uses optimal transport to align behavior-policy samples with unlabeled target-policy samples in a semantic space, providing likelihood-free evaluation. This is significant because reliable, cheap, offline evaluation of new LLMs is a persistent bottleneck for development and deployment.

entry.title: Replay the Curvature: Accurate and Scalable NVFP4 Quantization for Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Ruiyi Ding, Jie Li, Kang He, Ziyan Liu, Chengru Song, Yuedong Xu, Yuan Cheng

entry.summary: This paper improves GPTQ-style 4-bit (NVFP4) quantization of LLMs, addressing the difficulty of choosing block scales when quantizing one column updates subsequent ones, and the memory problem that full-precision weights, activations, and second-order statistics cannot fit on one accelerator for large models. The proposed method replays curvature information to accurately estimate final reconstruction error while scaling across devices. Quantization to 4-bit directly cuts weight storage and memory traffic, major inference costs.

entry.title: QuantMLA: Function-Aligned Dual-Path Quantization for Low-Bit MLA KV Caching

author.name: Zunhai Su, Yuxuan Sun, Jianchao Tan, Tao Zhang, Ruihan Hu, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: The paper provides a systematic analysis of quantization error in the dual content and decoupled RoPE paths of Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) KV caching, explaining why RoPE-path errors are disproportionately amplified. Building on this, QuantMLA introduces path-specific transformations that preserve full-precision computation and can be fused offline into model weights, enabling low-bit MLA cache quantization without runtime overhead. This directly targets memory scaling of MLA-based architectures common in efficient long-context LLMs.

entry.title: LoLBench: Evaluating Coding Agents with Long-Horizon Proposals on Large Software Systems

author.name: Yun Peng, Zihan Wu, Zeyang Zhuang, Xin Zhou, Rui Shu, Xu Han, Chun Yong Chong, Yuan Wang, Jiakun Liu

entry.summary: LoLBench is a multilingual benchmark of 100 tasks across 29 real software systems in five domains, evaluating coding agents on the full proposal-to-implementation process rather than only producing edits from detailed specifications. Each task pairs a human-written enhancement proposal with the requirement to ground intent and design into a specification before implementation. It fills a gap by testing perception of user intent alongside implementation capability on large codebases.

entry.title: SelfSearch: Reward-Free Search for Self-Improving Agents

author.name: Jungwoo Yang, Injin Kong, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: SelfSearch is a reward-free search procedure where agents modify their own instructions, tools, and procedures using records of previous self-improvement episodes capturing reasoning, actions, and outcomes. This avoids costly repeated downstream evaluation and task-coupling of reward-based agent search. Without reward signals during search, it improves population-mean success rates, contributing to scalable self-improvement.

entry.title: Composition, Not Conversation: VLMs Lose the Scene, Not the Thread

author.name: L. D. M. S. Sai Teja, Ufaq Khan, N. Siva Gopala Krishna, Satyajit Tourani, Ashshak Sharifdeen, Fida Mohammad Thoker, Bernard Ghanem, Muhammad Haris Khan

entry.summary: The paper introduces Layered-VQA, a benchmark decomposing images into ordered RGBA layers to test how VLMs handle fragmented visual evidence, with 93 scenes, 300 questions, and roughly 187,200 conversations graded by 1.74M cross-judgments. Evaluating eleven open-weight VLMs (3B-32B) and two proprietary models, it identifies consistent failures in composition when information is presented as fragments rather than whole scenes. The findings suggest VLMs lose scene-level coherence rather than conversational thread under fragmentation.

entry.title: Distill the Visual Evidence, Not Just the Answer: Cross-World On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuanhao Sun, Huawei Ji, Jiaxin Ding, Luoyi Fu, Xinbing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CW-OPD, a distillation method for vision-language models that supervises the student's response to changes in visual evidence rather than only matching teacher answers. For each example it constructs two visual worlds differing in the evidence that determines the answer, ensuring the student relies on the same visual information as the teacher.

entry.title: GRC-Pose: Generation-Reconstruction Correspondence for Prior-Free 6D Object Pose Tracking

author.name: Shiyang Liu, Weiquan Lin, Luping Xiao, Jiadong Tang, Yi Yang, Yu Gao, Xingyu Chen

entry.summary: GRC-Pose tracks the 6D pose of unseen objects from a single RGB video without CAD models, posed references, or pose annotations by formulating tracking as correspondence between object-centric generation outputs and scene-centric reconstruction evidence. A GeoCorr-Matcher bridges the arbitrary object-local parameterization of generated CAD-like content with the sequence-specific world frame of reconstructions, feeding robust pose estimation.

entry.title: Aligning Thoughts with Answers: Probability Rewards to Tame Thinking Drift

author.name: Pengzhan Sun, Shiu-hong Kao, Shijie Li, Yongyi Su, Junbin Xiao, Arjun Reddy Akula, Angela Yao

entry.summary: This paper identifies thinking drift in vision-language RL, where models produce correct outputs despite reasoning that points to a different target, in the context of visual intention grounding. It proposes Rita, an RL paradigm with two label-free rewards derived from conditional probabilities of reference answers, a thinking reward and an answer reward, to enforce thinking-answer consistency.

entry.title: Structural Limits of the Information-Theoretic Uncertainty Decomposition

author.name: Jakob L{\o}nborg Christensen, Christian F. Baumgartner, Morten Rieger Hannemose, Anders Bjorholm Dahl, Vedrana Andersen Dahl

entry.summary: The paper provides a functional-level analysis of the standard information-theoretic aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty decomposition, showing that large portions of the assumed AU-EU range are infeasible with any class probabilities in finite settings. It characterizes how this infeasible region scales with the number of classes and ensemble size, explaining observed entanglement and epistemic collapse.

entry.title: Seeing as Humans Do: Learning from Motion to Segment Anything Without Supervision

author.name: Weijian Jian, Xiaoyue Zhang, Bin Xiao, Chunyu Xie, Yixiao He, Yutao Liu, Dawei Leng, Yuhui Yin

entry.summary: MoSA is an unsupervised segmentation framework that learns a transferable objectness prior from unlabeled videos using multi-granularity motion pseudo-labels, a perceptual grouping model trained with contrastive learning, and subsequent transfer stages. It targets SAM's annotation bottleneck while generalizing beyond moving objects to static scenes.

entry.title: Atomizer-IO: Beyond Pixels, Patches and Grids

author.name: Hugo Riffaud de Turckheim, Sylvain Lobry, Nicolas Houdr\'e, Damien Robert, Roberto Interdonato, Diego Marcos

entry.summary: This paper introduces Atomizer-IO, a vision architecture that abandons the regular grid assumption by treating each observation as an atom described by its measurement and acquisition metadata, using cross-attention to arbitrarily placed anchor points. The approach retains useful spatial inductive biases while handling sensing data with varying channels, temporal sampling, resolution, and geometry. It is evaluated by progressively relaxing the grid constraint, demonstrating a path toward more general vision models for non-standard sensing data.

entry.title: Ego4WAM: What Matters When Scaling Egocentric Human Data for Robot Learning?

author.name: Zhihao Sun, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Haoyi Jiang, Wei Feng, Huiqiang Zhang, Xiaosong Jia, Zhizhong Su, Zuxuan Wu

entry.summary: Ego4WAM systematically studies which properties of egocentric human video drive downstream robot learning gains, using a unified world-action model framework with a fixed backbone to disentangle human-robot alignment, data duration, task diversity, action supervision, and data usage strategies. The key finding is that aligned human demonstrations substantially improve robot performance, clarifying how scarce supervision and data properties interact. This guides how the community should curate and deploy human data for robot training.

entry.title: EmbodiRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Data-Efficient Robot Adaptation

author.name: Haoran Lang, Haotao Lu, Shiyu Sang, Haoyang Luo, Guo Chen, Qun Li, Jingyi Yu, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: EmbodiRSI is an agentic system for recursive self-improvement in robot manipulation, constructing task-specific simulations from target deployment scenes and using policy execution feedback to iteratively acquire experience and update policies before transferring back to the real world. It combines collaborative error correction for agent-assisted corrective trajectories with a complementary mechanism to close the improvement loop.

entry.title: SteerQuant: Steering Quantization Error with Action-Guided Scaling in World-Action Models

author.name: Yunhan Wang, Haodong Wang, Zhiming Liu, Zicong Hong, Qianli Liu, Xiaoyi Pang, Yangjia Hu, Quanxin Shou, Yikun Miao, Song Guo

entry.summary: SteerQuant is a 4-bit quantization framework for world-action models that steers quantization errors toward computations with less influence on final actions, mapping how each token stream's (video, proprioceptive, action) quantization errors propagate to actions and using this map to guide shared channel scaling with per-stream, denoising-step-aware activation calibration. It argues that numerical accuracy alone is insufficient since equal errors in different streams have unequal control consequences.

entry.title: LIBERO-Agent: Evaluating General-Purpose Agents for Direct Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Zijie Diao, Yitong Chen, Sicheng Xie, Tianyi Lu, Wujian Peng, Guojin Zhong, Houze Xu, Ziyi Ye, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: LIBERO-Agent is an agent-native benchmark testing whether general-purpose agents' planning, tool-use, and feedback-revision skills transfer from digital to embodied manipulation. Unlike program-writing or high-level-skill benchmarks, agents interactively inspect observations with their own tools and issue native low-level action commands across 200 tasks, with a 30-task primary suite. Benchmarks of this kind shape how the community measures agentic embodied capability.

entry.title: Principles for Embedded Evaluations

author.name: Axel Højmark

entry.summary: A linkpost to Apollo Research principles for embedded third-party evaluations, responding to September 2026 commitments by frontier AI companies to give outside evaluators employee-like access. The post outlines what effective embedded evaluations for scheming and loss-of-control risk should achieve, warning that impact depends on access, resourcing, and the weight given to findings.

entry.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids

author.name: Rohan Kannan

entry.summary: Microsoft Research describes an end-to-end machine learning pipeline that converts forecast-time solar-wind data into location-specific geomagnetic risk estimates for 66,935 US substations, combining AE and Dst forecasts with local latitude, geology, and ground conductivity. The system detected nearly 80% of major space-weather events and can give grid operators 30-60 minutes of advance warning before site-specific risks materialize. It addresses a concrete critical-infrastructure vulnerability highlighted by the May 2024 geomagnetic storm.

entry.title: Demographic Pluralism: Inference-Time Modeling of Pluralistic Human Preference Distributions

author.name: Meng-Chen Wu, Qipin Chen, Ansh Jain, Tess Wood, Zhe Du, Si-Chi Chin

entry.summary: Demographic Pluralism is an inference-time framework that models population-level opinion distributions by generating multiple perspectives within demographically grounded groups, requiring no opinion-distribution training data or fine-tuning. Across four backbones on GlobalOpinionQA and VITAL, it reduces Jensen-Shannon distance by 8.4%-26.4% over Modular Pluralism.

entry.title: Alleviating Hallucination in Reasoning Tasks with Training-Free Uncertainty-Guided Steering

author.name: Litian Liu, Qiqi Hou, Yubing Jian, Reza Pourreza, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Roland Memisevic, Yao Qin, Hong Cai

entry.summary: USteer is a training-free inference-time method that steers model activations layer-by-layer using the gradient of a confidence measure, nudging generation toward lower-uncertainty outputs during reasoning. It repurposes hallucination-detection signals proactively to improve answer accuracy rather than only filtering confabulations.

entry.title: MiniRep: Robust Reputation-Based Aggregation for Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Yuwan Liu, Yue Huang, Sisi Duan

entry.summary: MiniRep studies multi-agent debate under malicious agents and shows that reputation from past performance poorly predicts future behavior when adversaries can adapt. It proposes a reputation-based aggregation system grounded in a formal model to make MAD robust to such adaptive malicious participants.

entry.title: SkillFM: Generating Skills for LLM Agents via Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Zuming Zhang, Jie He, Yizhe Zhang, Jeff Z. Pan

entry.summary: SkillFM synthesizes task-conditioned textual skills for LLM agents generatively rather than via retrieval or RL, using a codec that maps skills into a continuous latent space and a conditional flow model trained with improved MeanFlow. At inference, single-step latent sampling plus an LLM decoder produces guidance for a frozen downstream agent.

entry.title: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
