author.name: Xinhao Yang, Wenhao Wu, Ning Lv, Yanshen Ding, Zhenhong Sun, Daoyi Dong, Chunlin Chen, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces T3DP, a Text-to-3D Policy framework that improves fine-grained alignment between language instructions and robot manipulation behaviors. It addresses unseen specification generalization, where language specifies behavioral variations such as target position or articulated state that were absent from training demonstrations.

entry.title: Community-Driven API and AI Writer Design for Openly Scaling Community Notes

author.name: Brad Miller, Jay Baxter, Jiansong Chao, Keith Coleman, Sophie Hilgard, Daniel Ortiz

entry.summary: This paper by the Community Notes team presents the design, operation, and impact of the AI Note Writer API on X, which since late 2025 has let AI propose notes while users, not the platform or AI, control visibility. It analyzes interactions between AI- and human-generated notes across topics, showing how explicit note requests shape the AI's post feeds.

entry.title: On the (In)effectiveness of AMR Augmentation for Large Language Models

author.name: Hoa Quynh Nhung Nguyen, Jacopo Staiano, Michael Sullivan

entry.summary: This reproduction study finds that previously reported downstream gains from Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) augmentation likely stem from specific experimental settings rather than genuine benefit. Using a unified hyperparameter-selection protocol, text-only baselines match or exceed AMR-augmented models, and a perplexity-based probe shows AMR adds little relational knowledge beyond what LLMs already encode. A valuable negative result for the semantic-parsing augmentation literature.

entry.title: Learning to Plan from Random Exploration

author.name: Deqian Kong, Guangyan Sun, Sheng Cheng, Sirui Xie, Bo Pang, Jianwen Xie, Tony Geng, Caiwen Ding, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that experience from random exploration can support long-range planning without policy-improvement training. The authors analyze random walks to characterize what temporal relations encode at different horizons (geodesic geometry at short horizons, regional connectivity at longer horizons), and learn these relations with a conditional energy-based model trained via noise-contrastive estimation on unlabeled observation pairs, which a planner then queries at multiple horizons.

entry.title: SparseEngine: Sparse-First Inference Engine

author.name: Jitai Hao, Quansheng Gu, Qiang Huang, Jun Yu

entry.summary: SparseEngine is a sparse-first LLM inference engine that lets sparse attention methods control their own KV-cache representations while sharing common serving infrastructure via a lifecycle contract. It supports 15 sparse-attention methods across four categories and introduces Chain Cache for cross-request state management, addressing integration friction that has limited sparse attention adoption.

entry.title: Robustifying Asynchronous SGD via Soft Throttling

author.name: Kaoru Otsuka, Maxime Meyer, Yuki Takezawa, Makoto Yamada, Anastasia Koloskova

entry.summary: The paper introduces Throttle, a Byzantine-robust generalization of asynchronous SGD that exponentially down-weights updates from faster clients by a factor q, unifying asynchronous SGD (q=1) and synchronous robust SGD (q to infinity) as special cases. The authors provide convergence-rate theory and show the mechanism also addresses stragglers empirically.

entry.title: Certification-Based Differentially Private Learning

author.name: Mihnea Ghitu, Matthew Wicker

entry.summary: This paper extends formal-methods-based tighter privacy analysis beyond private prediction in classification, generalizing abstract gradient training to continuous regression and introducing Abstract Gradient Sampling (AGS). AGS reduces learning to a reachability problem over parameter space, enabling reachability-based privacy certification for parameterized models.

entry.title: Learning Functional Subspaces for Neural Network Compression

author.name: Massimo Bini, Anders Christensen, Stephan Alaniz, Judah Goldfeder, Ole Winther, Yann LeCun, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: The paper introduces Learnable Subspace Projections (LSP), which learn end-to-end which low-rank subspaces to discard per layer, replacing local closed-form criteria that ignore cross-layer error propagation. This prevents error compounding at high compression ratios in transformer compression.

entry.title: Distribution Matching Distillation for Continuous Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Paul Le Van Kiem, Dario Shariatian, Umut Simsekli, Alain Durmus

entry.summary: The paper develops distribution matching distillation to cut the number of network evaluations needed by continuous diffusion language models, exploiting the student's probabilistic token outputs. It proposes two methods under a unified reverse-KL formulation: Simplex-DMD with continuous relaxations and pathwise gradients, and Reinforce-DMD with categorical sampling and a learned density ratio. This addresses a key efficiency bottleneck for parallel token generation.

entry.title: Privacy in Personalized AI Is a System Property, Not Just a Model Property

author.name: Guillaume Salha-Galvan, Jiaying Xu

entry.summary: A position-style paper arguing that privacy in personalized AI (assistants, recommenders) must be evaluated at the system level rather than per model, since user information flows across components and over time. The authors identify four interconnected privacy-risk channels and propose four requirements for system-level privacy evaluation.

entry.title: RSIGame: Autonomous Agentic Game Development with Recursive Self-improvement

author.name: Wenyi Wu, Minghao Fu, Jieyu You, Kun Zhou, Siqi Liu, Aayush Salvi, Yiheng Lin, Ce Zhang, Xiaohan Lan, Jiahui Zhu, Yujie Zhong, Qi She, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: RSIGame is an autonomous agentic framework for game development organized into local explore-diagnose-improve loops and global refinement loops, designed to avoid overfitting to a small test set during iterative game improvement. It performs evidence-grounded revision with an evolving issue repository, targeting reliable improvement of LLM-generated games beyond a merely playable version.

entry.title: HAPMoE: Heterogeneity-Aware Automatic Parallelism Planning for Mixture-of-Experts Models Training

author.name: Mengyuan Fan, Peizhuang Cong, Zixiao Huang, Si Xu, Tong Qiao, Yanghao Li, Jing Yang, Tong Yang, Quanlu Zhang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: HAPMoE addresses automatic parallelization for training mixture-of-experts models on heterogeneous compute clusters, a combination existing approaches handle only separately. As MoE architectures dominate large-model training and accelerator diversity grows, joint treatment of model and cluster heterogeneity is increasingly important. The system derives efficient parallelism strategies automatically at low cost.

entry.title: STARS: From Spatiotemporal Dynamics to Social Representations in Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Nathan Tsoi, Michael J. Munje, Tejas Oberoi, Rishab Maheshwari, Pengen Zheng, Tanush Chauhan, Peter Stone, Joydeep Biswas

entry.summary: STARS is a systematic benchmark evaluating whether vision-language models can understand complex social navigation scenes, including spatiotemporal relations among agents and human intentions, which underpin safe and socially compliant robot navigation. From an experienced group including Peter Stone and Joydeep Biswas, it fills a gap left by prior works that used VLMs in social navigation without systematic evaluation.

entry.title: $\tau$-Multilingual: Benchmarking Voice Agents Across Languages

author.name: Soham Ray, Edgard dos Santos Paiva, Ruben Valenzuela, Karthik Narasimhan, Keshav Dhandhania, Victor Barres

entry.summary: This benchmark extends tau-Voice to Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Hindi, Korean, and Mandarin with native-speaker review, evaluating 4,500 full-duplex calls across five voice configurations. Korean and Mandarin lag English by 14.7 and 8.4 task-completion points with distinct failure modes, and Grok leads task completion while scoring lowest on generation quality.

entry.title: PADM\'E: Preference Alignment Data Synthesis for Meta-Evaluation of LM Agent Evaluators

author.name: Cheng Chang, Yining Mao, Peng Qi

entry.summary: This paper addresses meta-evaluation of LM judges that score agentic trajectories, reformulating the problem as judging whether human and LM evaluator preferences align rather than comparing absolute scores. It introduces PADM'E, a data synthesis method for generating reliable criterion-based preference data, avoiding costly human collection and recursive trust issues with LM meta-evaluators. This matters for building trustworthy automated evaluation pipelines for agents.

entry.title: Generating Edit-Inducing Questions for AI Research Manuscripts

author.name: Sebastian Joseph, Zichao Wang, Jennifer Healey, Alexa Siu, Junyi Jessy Li, Ani Nenkova

entry.summary: The authors evaluate whether LLMs can generate questions whose answers would improve a paper draft, using paired ICLR and NeurIPS submission and camera-ready versions. GPT-generated questions lead to more extensive edits and broader content coverage than human reviewer questions, but a smaller fraction are genuinely edit-inducing, and long-context attention can degrade reasoning-model question quality.

entry.title: Traverse: Learning When to Remember, Reset, and Redirect for Long-Horizon Web Search

author.name: Jingyuan Ma, Lynx Aster, He Zhang, Siyao Song, Weijie Yuan, Zhe Zhang, Kai Jia, Zhifang Sui

entry.summary: Traverse is an autonomous long-horizon web search harness where the agent manages its own process through Rubric, Answer, and Verify states, using a Seal Memory tool for active context management. Training this with reinforcement learning risks a Seal Collapse pathology, which the paper characterizes and addresses for stable training.

entry.title: E-MoE: Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts for Non-Factorized Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Arseny Ivanov, Alexander Kolesov, Alexander Korotin, Ivan Oseledets, Mikhail Goncharov

entry.summary: Proposes E-MoE, which builds the reverse process of masked diffusion language models as a mixture of factorized distributions over a discrete shared latent derived from MoE expert-routing decisions, avoiding the posterior collapse of continuous-latent VAE approaches. This targets sample quality in the few-step regime where diffusion decoding is fastest relative to autoregressive generation.

entry.title: Sage: Formalization with Semantic Correction

author.name: Thomas Hirtz, Farzad Jafarrahmani, Abdelmouksit Sagueni, Xiang Zhou, Wenping Deng, Liang Zhang

entry.summary: Sage is an agentic framework for autoformalization that addresses the illusion of rigor, where Lean 4 statements type-check but silently drop hypotheses or introduce vacuous truths. It replaces monolithic translation with a four-stage decomposed generation pipeline plus a dual-signal semantic correction loop combining compiler diagnostics with multi-dimensional semantic checks. This targets a critical data bottleneck for neural theorem provers.

entry.title: Adapting Context Compression for Long-Horizon Agents with Counterfactual Continuations

author.name: Guanghui Min, Liang Wu, Mingjia Shi, Yinhan He, Mayank Darbari, Liangjie Hong, Chen Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies context compression for long-horizon agents, finding that compression degrades execution reliability before solvability and that severe degradation concentrates at isolated compression events, demonstrated via matched counterfactual continuations from identical agent states. Building on this, the authors propose PAIR, a prompt-adaptation method that isolates individual compression effects using interventional comparisons. It matters because compression quality is ultimately judged by downstream agent execution, which prior comparison methods could not cleanly measure.

entry.title: Reconstructing the Vocal Tract with Differentiable Acoustic Simulation

author.name: Eric Ming Chen, Jin Woo Lee, Vincent Sitzmann

entry.summary: The authors build a differentiable, GPU-accelerated acoustic simulator of the vocal tract that synthesizes speech by propagating sound through an acoustic tube model, and use its gradients to solve the inverse problem of reconstructing vocal tract shape from produced sound. Key contributions include a frequency-domain formulation 70x more GPU-parallelizable than finite-difference schemes and techniques making gradient descent succeed on a notoriously non-convex inverse mapping. This is technically impressive work with applications in speech science and production, with MIT-affiliated senior authorship.

entry.title: Seeing What Should Be Heard: Diagnosing and Repairing Cross-Modal Shortcuts in Omni-Modal LLMs

author.name: Yueran Ma, Ronghao Lin

entry.summary: The authors uncover a pervasive cross-modal shortcut in omni-modal LLMs: when answering audio-related questions, models rely on accompanying images as much as or more than the audio itself, exploiting redundant evidence. They introduce the Factorized Modality Diagnostic, which swaps audio and images across samples to isolate each modality's causal contribution, and propose repairs to enforce modality-following. The work exposes a reliability flaw relevant to multimodal evaluation and deployment.

entry.title: Harness Evolution as Learning: Approximation, Generalization, and Optimization Limits of Self-Improving Personal Agents

author.name: Zeyu Gan, Zixuan Gong, Yong Liu

entry.summary: The paper frames harness engineering for personal LLM agents (context, memory, tools, execution layers) as a learning problem and studies approximation, generalization, and optimization limits of self-evolving harnesses with the base model fixed. It investigates harness architecture, scale, and self-evolution algorithms, giving a theoretical account of when harness improvement can substitute for model improvement. This provides an early conceptual foundation for the fast-moving area of agent scaffolding research.

entry.title: Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training

author.name: Hongyang Li, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Said Mammar, Gr\'egoire Danoy, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: The paper pushes back on the trend of critic-free RL post-training, showing that critic-based RL instability in long chain-of-thought reasoning is largely an optimization artifact controllable via small, low-variance policy updates. It then demonstrates that a well-trained critic estimates the posterior probability of eventual success from later trajectories, enabling reward-free policy optimization for efficient long-horizon reasoning. This recasts the discarded critic as a valuable asset for post-training.

entry.title: FOCUS: Training-Free Decision-Preserving Context Compression for LLM Agents

author.name: Shantanu Dixit, Anson Bastos, Xuchao Zhang, Chetan Bansal, Saravan Rajmohan

entry.summary: FOCUS recasts agent context compression as causal decision preservation: it asks which past interactions causally shape future decisions and prunes accordingly, in a training-free manner conditioned on the evolving test-time trajectory. This contrasts with prior methods that learn compression policies offline via contrastive guidelines or distilled compressors. It reduces quadratic inference cost growth from accumulating interaction histories while preserving agent decisions.

entry.title: Storage Is Not Strategy: State-Conditioned Support Control for LLM Unlearning

author.name: Tianhao Qian, Ziming Hong, Chongyang Gao, Kezhen Chen, Lixu Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues that parameters most associated with a target fact are not necessarily the best to update during LLM unlearning: a storage-localization score achieves 0.981 AUROC yet agrees with the best intervention on only 17/36 targets while LoRA wins 35/36. The authors introduce Intervention Score, which ranks editable parameter groups by the predicted effect of the actual unlearning update including collateral damage. This reframes unlearning parameter selection around intervention efficacy rather than knowledge storage.

entry.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering

author.name: Jaewoo Jung, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jisang Han, Mungyeom Kim, Minkyeong Jeon, Heeseong Shin, Wonjun Moon, Federico Tombari, Daniel Barath, Marc Pollefeys, Seungryong Kim, Sunghwan Hong

entry.summary: Imagine3D-LLM takes an inspiration-from-humans approach to multi-view 3D reasoning in multimodal LLMs: rather than relying on fine-grained geometry cues, the model first roughly identifies common objects across views, infers relative geometry, and imagines the 3D scene before answering. This contrasts with prior work injecting 3D awareness via pixel-level cross-view correspondence or 3D foundation-model features. The approach targets the persistent gap between MLLMs and human spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Audible World Models: Spatially Aware Sound Generation for 3D Worlds

author.name: Duowen Chen, Jinjin He, Gouthaman KV, Sandeep Bangalore Venkatesh, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: This training-free framework adds spatially grounded sound to generated 3D worlds: from a text prompt it constructs a panoramic 3D proxy, separates semantic layers, identifies sound-producing foreground objects and ambient background regions, and synthesizes dry audio per sound label anchored spatially. Sound perception then varies appropriately with listener movement, going beyond text- or video-derived soundtracks that lack explicit source location. It addresses the silent or spatially unaware nature of current world generators.

entry.title: DecoMoE: Decoupling Visual Propagation and Expert Computation for Efficient Multimodal MoE Inference

author.name: Xudong Tan, Peng Ye, Ming Xie, Chenyu Huang, Yaoxin Yang, Jiayuan Fan, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Presents DecoMoE, a two-dimensional structured compression framework for multimodal mixture-of-experts inference that decouples visual propagation depth from expert computation. It exploits the observation that required visual propagation depth varies per input while text-token routing shows concentrated, recurrent expert-importance patterns, cutting attention, routing, dispatch, and expert-MLP costs from long visual-token sequences.

entry.title: Frame Differential On-Policy Self-Distillation for Video Reasoning

author.name: Haiying He, Xin Zheng, Shaoli Hu, Shijun Xiao, Xuanhe Liu, Bing Li, Harry Yang

entry.summary: Presents FD-OPSD, which during RL training transfers useful evidence from dense frame observations to a sparse frame policy for video reasoning. It compares the policy's token-level preferences for the same sampled response under sparse versus dense frames, addressing the cost-quality tradeoff of fixed sparse frame budgets in multimodal RL.

entry.title: UGOD: Uncertainty-Guided Opacity and Dropout for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zhihao Guo, Peng Wang, Zidong Chen, Xiangyu Kong, Yan Lyu, Guanyu Gao, Chenghao Qian, Ziyang Wang, Xinqi Fan, Liangxiu Han

entry.summary: UGOD addresses overfitting in sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by learning a view-dependent uncertainty score per Gaussian primitive via a lightweight prediction head, then using it to modulate opacity so unreliable primitives contribute less during alpha blending. The framework combines uncertainty estimation with a differentiable dropout-style mechanism to prevent erroneous primitives from corrupting novel-view synthesis.

entry.title: Typographic Attack Against VLM-based AI-generated Image Detection

author.name: Eunmin Lee, Jungwoo Kim, Jong-Seok Lee

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates typographic attack strategies against VLM-based AI-generated image detectors across detection-oriented, open-weight, and commercial models, covering both real-to-fake and fake-to-real directions. Findings include that reasoning modes are more vulnerable than direct modes, attacks show directional asymmetry, and larger models achieve higher clean accuracy but also higher attack success rates.

entry.title: Reconstructing the Dynamic World: A Representation-Centric View of 4D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Ziren Gong, Guo Chen, Yongjia Li, Yihua Shao, Fabio Tosi, Stefano Mattoccia, Matteo Poggi, Hao Tang, Fei Ma, Shuyan Li, Ziyang Yan, Nicu Sebe, Ling Shao, Jianfei Cai, Qi Tian, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: This is a survey providing a unified representation-centric taxonomy of 4D scene reconstruction, organizing NeRF- and 3DGS-based dynamic scene methods, their design choices, and evaluation protocols. It aims to systematize a fragmented literature on recovering evolving geometry, appearance, and motion.

entry.title: AssemblyWorld: Rethinking 3D Assembly with General-Purpose Agents

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Yeying Fan, Moitreya Chatterjee, Suhas Lohit, Bernhard Egger, Tim K. Marks, Anoop Cherian, Stephen Gould

entry.summary: AssemblyWorld is an interactive 3D environment testing whether pretrained general-purpose agents can assemble objects via visual interaction without assembly-specific fine-tuning, with agents perceiving parts through 2D renders rather than mesh data and assemblies evaluated geometrically. The accompanying AssemblyWorldBench provides 100 assembly tasks across 80 objects, with optional image or manual guidance. This probes a gap between generalist model capabilities and precise spatial manipulation.

entry.title: Multi-Link Safety Filtering for VLA Policies Around Moving Hazards

author.name: Yatharth Agarwal, Vijay Raghunathan

entry.summary: The paper presents a training-free runtime safety shield for pretrained VLA policies that covers the gripper, wrist, and forearm with five ellipsoids and filters every commanded motion through a barrier program against a keep-out zone fitted from RGB-D perception. Sparse optical flow tracks the hazard's motion without repeated detection, while sharing onboard compute with the policy. This addresses the fact that task success does not guarantee a VLA policy avoids knocking over unrelated objects in clutter.

entry.title: Null-model treatment of the sensory-motor boundary changes an evolutionary connectome comparison

author.name: Gyujeong Park

entry.summary: This paper evolves embodied foraging agents whose brains are a compressed adult Drosophila connectome (FlyWire v783) versus randomized wiring variants, using pre-registered experiments across ten seeds, four ecologies, and 600 generations. It shows that standard null-model randomizations (column shuffles, degree-preserving edge swaps) create implausible sensory-to-motor connectivity far exceeding the real connectome, which can distort evolutionary connectome comparisons even though the primary fitness endpoint showed no difference.

entry.title: CEER2: Directional and Tunable End-Effector and Root Compliance for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Xinyuan Luo, Chunyuan Yang, Boyuan Chen, Xianyi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper presents a compliance control framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that allows directional, tunable compliance at the end-effectors plus selectable root compliance, so a humanoid can accommodate contact forces in some directions while maintaining task accuracy in others. It addresses the gap between whole-body motion tracking and physical interaction with people or the environment.

entry.title: Function beyond Form: Functional Correspondence for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasp Generation

author.name: Bolin Zou, Wenlong Dong, Mu Ai, Chao Tang, Aoxiang Gu, Lipeng Chen, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: FunCo-Grasp introduces functional correspondence — explicit mappings between structurally different robot hand regions serving similar grasp roles — to enable dexterous grasp generation that transfers across heterogeneous hand embodiments. It aligns each hand to a canonical functional schema, helping models learn transferable grasp knowledge rather than hand-specific interaction patterns.

entry.title: LocoWM: High-Precision Locomotion through World-Model-Guided Residual Adaptation

author.name: Zijie Zhao, Shengqian Chen, Xiaoxu Wang, Han Jiang, Yuanheng Zhu, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: LocoWM is a world-model-guided preactive residual adaptation framework for high-precision legged locomotion, where a base policy handles command tracking and an action-conditioned world model predicts future physical states so a residual adapter can correct actions before deviations become observable. This preactive correction contrasts with purely reactive residual control. It is relevant for robots that must precisely regulate contact-rich physical states while moving.

entry.title: DSDyn-VLA: A Dual-Stream Dynamic Manipulation Framework with Motion Perception, Future Awareness, and Realtime Correction

author.name: Wenhao Li, Xiu Su, Yu Han, Yichao Cao, Shan You, Chang Xu

entry.summary: This paper addresses a key weakness of Vision-Language-Action models: they perform well on static tasks but fail in dynamic environments like conveyor-belt manipulation. The authors identify perception, latency, and control gaps and propose DSDyn-VLA, a Slow-Fast dual-stream framework that combines motion-aware foresighted planning with real-time residual correction of executed actions. It matters because closing these gaps could extend VLA applicability from controlled lab settings to industrial settings with moving objects.

entry.title: Experience-Driven Continual Learning of Terrain Traversability for Quadruped Robots

author.name: Luca Bricarello, Jo\~ao Carlos Virgolino Soares, Alberto Sanchez-Delgado, Fulvio Mastrogiovanni, Claudio Semini

entry.summary: This paper presents a continual learning pipeline where quadruped robots predict terrain interaction outcomes (slip, loading, energy cost) from pre-contact images using a frozen DINOv3 backbone mapped to reliability-weighted proprioceptive indicators, updating predictions as new contacts occur. This lets robots learn how terrain will behave under foot before contact, beyond what geometry and appearance alone reveal. The work addresses safe, efficient navigation over unfamiliar terrain with lifelong adaptation.

entry.title: EWAM: Emergent Depth-Wise Specialization in a Unified Embodied Model -- From Semantic Understanding through Visual Foresight to Action

author.name: Hao Wang, Jiajun Wen, Jingzhi Liu, Shuoshuo Xue, Zhiliang Chen, Min Lin, Yicheng Chang, Xiaoyu Guo, Yukang Zhuo, Zheng Chong, Yunshuang Nie, Jian Zhang, Weijia Liufu, Qingman Wu, Heming Xu, Bingchang Song, Dantong Wu, Zhiyuan Wang, Hang Xu, Jianhua Han, Bokui Chen, Shen Zhao, Rui Li, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: EWAM is a unified embodied model with asymmetric joint attention that lets action tokens read semantic, current-visual, predicted-future, and action information at every layer while perceptual experts retain distinct roles. Without layer-wise supervision, the model develops emergent depth-wise specialization where action queries attend to vision-language features in shallow layers, predicted future frames in intermediate layers, and action information in deeper layers.

entry.title: Confounding Behaviours: Do AI Models Really Sandbag?

author.name: Megha Sharma

entry.summary: A BlueDot Technical Project Sprint audit examining whether observed sandbagging in AI evaluations reflects strategic underperformance or confounders such as instruction following, role-playing, or eval awareness. The audit finds existing sandbagging methodologies are unverified against these alternative explanations and reports on deliberate underperformance experiments.

entry.title: Bench on the Clocktower

author.name: TomTaylor

entry.summary: The authors adapt the social deduction game Blood on the Clocktower into a multi-agent benchmark for deception, coordination, and theory-of-mind capabilities in LLM agents. Comparing current frontier models including GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5, and Claude Opus 5, they find GPT-5.6 Sol performs best, observe coordinated deceptive play by Evil agents that naive Good agents fall for, note a same-provider bias in anonymous play, and observe that Anthropic models almost never self-sacrifice. The testbed is motivated partly by recent multi-agent misalignment incidents.

entry.title: Staying on Task: Testing the Foundations of Long-Horizon Agent Reliability

author.name: Jeffrey Willette, Krishna C. Puvvada, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: The authors introduce Long-Transduction, a controlled diagnostic testing whether models can sustain state-dependent operations like reading, mutating, and outputting context-dependent records over thousands of generation steps. It isolates failure axes such as losing place or inconsistently applying operations as context grows. This is foundational for predicting long-horizon agent reliability.

entry.title: Targeted Retrieval, Compact Representations: How CoT Reasoning Improves Long-Context Counting

author.name: Liang Twist Shan, Tianyu Hu, Hao Yan, Yiqiao Zhong

entry.summary: Using a needle-in-a-haystack counting task across twelve model comparison groups, the authors show that thinking modes improve long-context counting accuracy, especially at larger counts. Mechanistic analysis reveals contrasting strategies: broad attention over multiple needles in non-thinking models versus targeted enumeration in chain-of-thought with compact representations in thinking models.

entry.title: PTNO: Training Neural Operators with Noisy Monte Carlo Estimates for Particle Transport Problems

author.name: Yubo Cao, Xi Deng, Mengqi Xia, Vignesh Gopakumar, Ander Gray, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: PTNO is a neural operator that learns particle transport surrogates for radiative transfer and plasma physics directly from noisy, low-cost Monte Carlo labels rather than expensive converged solutions. It handles high label variance by amortizing across many configurations and addresses high dynamic range, with an author team including Anima Anandkumar.

entry.title: Forensic-Aware Continual Adaptation for Image Forgery Localization

author.name: Chenqi Kong, Song Xia, Anwei Luo, Peisong He, Alex C. Kot, Yuming Fang

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first continual learning framework for image forgery localization, with benchmarks under cross-dataset and cross-content data-evolution protocols reflecting how real forensic data arrive sequentially. Evaluations show substantial degradation of existing state-of-the-art methods, and the authors analyze key failure modes and propose forensic-aware adaptation. It addresses the practical mismatch between static forgery detectors and evolving manipulation techniques.

entry.title: What Pretraining and Midtraining Make Learnable from Rewards?

author.name: Chiwun Yang, Xiaoyu Li

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies how pretraining and midtraining determine what tasks can be learned from rewards alone, characterizing mechanisms that agree on all training rewards yet diverge on held-out answers, and constructing finite sampled Adam paths proving how prediction acquires execution or retrieval capability that rewards then specialize. Experiments with pretrained Qwen2.5 checkpoints support the analysis.

entry.title: FlexRouter: Learning Complementary Model Sets for Flexible LLM Routing

author.name: Wang Wei, Harry Yang, Tiankai Yang, Samyadeep Basu, Hongjie Chen, Andy Zhao, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi, Hoda Eldardiry

entry.summary: FlexRouter is an LLM routing framework that explicitly models model complementarity, optimizing answer coverage (the probability that at least one selected model answers correctly) rather than independently scoring models. This avoids selecting redundant models with shared failure modes and fits verifier-in-the-loop inference pipelines, with a flexible budget formulation.

entry.title: Does Learning Protein Folding Generalize to Broader Reasoning?

author.name: Yong Liu, Zhanpeng Shi, Yizhou Dang, Zhongyue Zhang, Xiaoliang Shi, Zhijian Wei, Shuangjia Zheng

entry.summary: The authors build FoldingCorpus, a protein-derived question-answer dataset, and Fold2Reason, a post-training recipe using both discrete structural answers and continuous 3D geometry decoded from shared representations. They investigate whether learning to fold proteins transfers to general reasoning, achieving strong structure prediction results on FoldBench.

entry.title: RAIM: Robust Aggregation of Inexpensive Models for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Elia Onofri, Roberto Di Pietro

entry.summary: RAIM investigates whether a panel of cheap open-weight judges (4-9B parameters) can be aggregated to substitute for frontier-model judges in faithfulness evaluation, proposing an aggregation scheme robust to correlated member errors that combines cross-fitted stacked logistic regression with an admissibility test. It instantiates the approach with ten judges and quantifies what the substitution sacrifices and when it is worthwhile.

entry.title: CAMOS: Coupled Oscillatory State-Space Model for Multimodal Clinical Time-Series

author.name: Maxx Richard Rahman, Mostafa Hammouda, Wolfgang Maass

entry.summary: CAMOS targets multimodal, irregularly sampled, incomplete clinical cohorts by giving each modality a behavior driven by availability patterns, addressing a proven representational limitation: linear state-space layers with availability-independent transitions cannot represent joint presence or absence of modalities. The model uses coupled oscillatory dynamics and is evaluated on longitudinal clinical data such as ADNI.

entry.title: ShieldCLIP: Selective Safety Alignment for Harmful Content Mitigation in Multimodal Foundation Models

author.name: Tobia Poppi, Silvia Cappelletti, Samuele Poppi, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi, Diego Garcia-Olano, Rita Cucchiara

entry.summary: ShieldCLIP conditions safety alignment of multimodal encoders like CLIP on the observed per-modality safety state rather than on whether a sample is synthetic, preserving safe content while redirecting only unsafe components. It also introduces ViSUv2, a 195k-quadruplet dataset to support modality-aware safety alignment.

entry.title: Correcting CondOT: Exact Finite-Step Sampling in Gaussian Flow Matching

author.name: Ron Levy, Michael Elad

entry.summary: The paper analyzes finite-step sampling error in Gaussian flow matching under explicit midpoint sampling, measuring error via squared Wasserstein distance to the target. It shows the standard conditional optimal transport schedule cancels the leading midpoint error and improves convergence bounds even with unequal step spacing, and derives corrected schedule choices.

entry.title: VirusCascade: Hijacking Collaborative Reflection in LLM-Powered Recommender Agents

author.name: Yurong Hao, Wen Zhou, Guowei Guan, Tiantong Wu, Fuyao Zhang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: The paper identifies a systemic vulnerability in LLM-powered agentic recommender systems where adversarial evidence injected into a single agent is rationalized into a legitimate preference narrative (reflection laundering), written to memory, and propagated to other agents through collaborative reflection. The proposed VirusCascade attack demonstrates this system-wide escalation. It exposes a new class of security risks unique to multi-agent LLM architectures.

entry.title: Linear Recurrent Memory Suffices to Distil a World-Model Policy for Robot Air Hockey

author.name: F. Olivia Fan, Oliver Obst

entry.summary: Studying simulated air-hockey defense under temporary loss of puck tracking, the authors show a DreamerV3 teacher needs memory, then distill it into compact 64-dimensional recurrent policies combining a diagonal linear recurrence with an optional rank-k nonlinear innovation. Surprisingly, the purely linear recurrent model matches both a GRU baseline and the teacher across five matched seeds.

entry.title: When Should LLMs Trust Their Own Revisions? A Risk-Aware Study of Intrinsic Self-Correction

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang

entry.summary: This study tracks correctness transitions between initial and revised answers across 29 open-weight LLMs on BoolQ, GSM8K, and Corr2Cause, showing aggregate accuracy can conceal harmful revisions, e.g., Llama-3.1-8B gains 25.5 points on GSM8K while flipping 19.1 percent of initially correct answers to wrong. It then compares runtime decision policies for when to trust revisions.

entry.title: Rethinking Multimodal Fake News Detection in the Generative AI Era

author.name: Wenbin Shen, Guoxuan Qin, Guangxu Yao, Baodong Wang, Yuanbo Rui, Zhichao Lian

entry.summary: This paper argues that generative AI has changed fake news into hybrid content where native and generated material coexist, and that veracity assessment and AIGC detection have been studied in unhelpful isolation. It introduces Weibo26, a multimodal fake news dataset for the generative era that characterizes how generativity differences affect evidence reliability.

entry.title: VLM Fine-Tuning for End-to-End Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Qingsong Yan, Xia Jiang, Yaoxin Wu, Wen Song, Lu Zhang, Yingjie Zhou

entry.summary: The paper presents a general-purpose vision-language solver for combinatorial optimization that augments textual instance descriptions with input-derived visual representations, trained with SFT followed by verifier-guided RL. Visual inputs contain no gold solutions, yet the VLM improves solution quality over text-only counterparts across multiple CO tasks with a single model.

entry.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization

author.name: Bingchen Yao, Haobo Xu, Haokun Lin, Yichen Wu, Ziyu Guo, Renrui Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Zhenan Sun, Ying Wei

entry.summary: STEPQuant is a spatial-temporal post-training quantization method for the recurrent states of linear attention models, motivated by the observation that quantization errors propagate differently depending on state lifetime (temporal) and key-row position (spatial). By quantizing where errors matter least, the method reduces the memory bottleneck of fixed-size recurrent states under concurrent serving while preserving accuracy. This is practically relevant for efficient inference with linear attention architectures.

entry.title: MARCO: Multi-Round Agentic Reinforcement for Conditional Molecular Optimization

author.name: Shicheng Fang, Yuxin Wang, Zhuo Yang, Xiaohu Xu, Jiahao Lu, Chuanyuan Tan, Tong Zhu, Yining Zheng, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: MARCO is an evaluator-grounded reinforcement learning framework that trains molecular editors on bounded proposal-feedback-revision trajectories, aggregating shaped per-turn rewards into trajectory returns for group-relative policy optimization. Unlike one-shot instruction-following editors, it explicitly optimizes the iterative nature of molecular optimization, evaluated under one-response and multi-response budgets. This applies multi-turn RL to a scientifically meaningful domain with clear practical value for drug and materials discovery.

entry.title: Rational Clarification by Assistive Agents via Value-of-Information Reasoning

author.name: T. Duy Nguyen-Hien, Yee Whye Teh, Wee Sun Lee, Tan Zhi-Xuan

entry.summary: REVOIR frames an assistive agent's choice between acting on an ambiguous request and asking a clarifying question as a value-of-information decision, accounting for downstream impact of uncertainty reduction, the costs of asking versus acting, and the possibility of unsolicited user corrections. This improves on threshold-on-uncertainty heuristics common in clarification research. It targets safer and more helpful clarification behavior in language-based assistants.

entry.title: On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Manuel Madeira, Amitis Shidani, Alice Bizeul, Victor Turrisi, Louis B\'ethune, Bhavika Devnani, Dan Busbridge, Pierre Ablin, Jo\~ao Monteiro

entry.summary: PUMBA is a unified framework for trajectory-aware training of masked diffusion language models that trains the denoiser on consecutive steps of policy-induced trajectories, passes information between steps, and jointly optimizes via backpropagation through time. The paper runs a controlled study of the design space, showing how exact trajectory training and cross-step information flow interact. It addresses the train-sample mismatch and step-isolation limits of MDMs.

entry.title: PAMI: Part Anchored Motion for Text to Human-Object Interaction Generation

author.name: Chuqiao Li, Xianghui Xie, Yong Cao, Andreas Geiger, Gerard Pons-Moll

entry.summary: PAMI generates text-conditioned full-body human-object interaction motion by expressing object trajectories relative to multiple body-part anchors, inspired by the Hough Transform, so body parts vote for object motion. A PamiVAE learns this part-anchored representation, reducing object drift, missed contact, and penetration compared to methods that model human-object couplings implicitly from separate trajectories. This improves temporal coordination between human motion and object dynamics.

entry.title: PARK: Accurate Block Retrieval for Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Yun Dai, Jiarui Wen, Huiping Zhuang, Cen Chen, Ziqian Zeng

entry.summary: Identifies two retrieval mismatches in sparse attention for video diffusion transformers: query-side aggregation mismatch where averaging queries before Softmax loses individual preferences, and key-side clustering metric mismatch where Euclidean clustering misgroups keys. Proposes PARK for accurate block retrieval to reduce quadratic attention cost without quality loss.

entry.title: Uruqi: Learning Spatial Cognition from Visual Experience

author.name: Shichao Li, Meiqi Wang, Fei Su, Zhicheng Zhao

entry.summary: Uruqi targets two atomic spatial capabilities that VLMs still lack, tracking self-motion and mapping the surrounding world during motion, via dense multi-turn supervision over interleaved capabilities within each training episode that mimics a continuously moving agent reasoning as it observes. A synthetic data pipeline scales the approach by generating embodied visual experience.

entry.title: VR-JEPA: Learning Contrastive-State Latent Guidance for Generation-based Video Reasoning

author.name: Zehua Ma, Kun Xiang, Yunshuang Nie, Quanlin Chen, Haoyuan Li, Xiuwei Chen, Jiang Ji, Haijun Wu, Zhenyu Xie, Michael Kampffmeyer, Hanhui Li, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: VR-JEPA aligns the V-JEPA predictor with task-specific reasoning logic to guide how latent visual states evolve during generation-based video reasoning, using localized contrastive state objectives. The goal is to prevent physical and structural inconsistencies in generated reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Skill-Level Memory for Partially Observable Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yansong Shi, Jiange Yang, Xijie Yang, Shaowei Zhang, Yuhan Zhu, Tao Lu, Limin Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces HIDE, a benchmark of 15 tasks for evaluating manipulation policy memory under partial observability, covering repetition counting, historical-state recall, and progress tracking with decision points where identical observations require different actions. The authors also propose SEEK, a framework combining three complementary memory mechanisms to retain and use interaction history.

entry.title: NEXUS: Perceptive Whole-Body Control for Terrain-Adaptive Teleoperation

author.name: Xiangyu Miao, Junsong Wu, Jiyuan Shi, Weiji Xie, Jinrui Han, Xingyi Wang, Weinan Zhang, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: NEXUS enables whole-body humanoid teleoperation across mismatched terrains by combining human motion commands with onboard perception so the robot adapts posture and contacts to its local terrain rather than copying the operator frame by frame. The framework includes a scalable terrain-aware adaptation algorithm to generate the paired motion data across flat and rough terrains that real teleoperation datasets lack.

entry.title: Towards Agile Vision-Based Multi-UAV Flight: Revisiting State Estimation

author.name: Michal Pliska, Matou\v{s} Vrba, Ond\v{r}ej V\'ita, Martin Jirou\v{s}ek, Viktor Walter, Martin Saska

entry.summary: The paper shows that position-only vision-based estimation of neighboring UAV states introduces a fixed structural delay in higher-order state estimates that limits agile multi-drone flight. It proposes integrating tilt measurements from a visual detector to inform thrust direction and benchmarks nine estimators, including a novel linear thrust-constraining Kalman filter formulation. The systematic benchmark and structural-delay analysis are valuable for agile drone swarms.

entry.title: Do VPD's Explanations Aggregate? An Audit of the Released Decomposition

author.name: Tom Angsten

entry.summary: An audit of the released AdVersarial Parameter Decomposition (VPD) decomposition of a 67M-parameter language model, testing whether per-input explanations can be aggregated without changing model outputs. The audit finds that aggregating components from 64 tokens causes output drift comparable to the paper's own 20-step adversary (0.80 vs 0.83 nats), that aggregation harm worsens for similar inputs, and that the labels enable targeted edits that disrupt code predictions while sparing protected text.

entry.title: CARAT: Do Materials LLMs Reason or Recite?

author.name: Jiajun Wu, Jian Yang, Zixiang Ni, Zhenzhu Li, Bin Chong

entry.summary: CARAT probes whether materials-science LLMs reason over crystal structures or merely copy answers printed in their inputs, holding questions and gold answers fixed across eight matched structural views while naming each structural relation in a GraphSpace representation. It finds grounded views beat formula inputs by 17.3 points on the hardest question families and shows GraphSpace beats a plain periodic graph by 19.3 points, while carefully dissecting the sources of that margin.

entry.title: VAmoS Part Deux: Harder, More Realistic Voice-Agent Simulation

author.name: Joshua Meyer, Sahar Shayegan, Ritiz Tambi, Ali Khan, Sun Kim, Victor Shih, Mehdi Jamei, Andi Partovi

entry.summary: VAmoS Energy is a voice-agent benchmark of 100 utility billing and payment calls combining multiple requests per caller, background speech, and impatient customers, with sixteen tools backed by a Stripe billing twin and Apache Fineract loan engine. An LLM-as-a-verifier checks agent actions against explicit requirements, agreeing with a code verifier on 99.1% of checks, and results across fourteen voice agents are reported.

entry.title: EvoSteer: Online Self-Evolving Graph Orchestration via Reference-Anchored Credit Assignment

author.name: Mingda Zhang, Hanwen Zhang, Qiang Huang, Zijia Wang, Pengfei Guo, Yuchen Zhang, Jionghao Zhu, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: EvoSteer introduces online self-evolving orchestration for LLM multi-agent systems, where an orchestrator builds a running team of tool-using agents and repairs failing steps mid-trajectory using execution features and a learned value estimate. It tackles credit diffusion and uncalibrated, never-retired skill admission found in prior post-hoc evolution approaches. The approach could make multi-agent orchestration more adaptive and sample-efficient.

entry.title: Positive Ratings, Hidden Concerns: Employee Voice Disclosure in AI-Mediated Organizational Listening

author.name: Thilo Tamme (Technical University of Munich), Michael Saatkamp (Technical University of Munich), Alma Bonte (Technical University of Munich), Daniel Weiss (LMU Munich), Anton Hantel (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Andrej Levin (Technical University of Munich)

entry.summary: This field study inside a global consulting firm examines what changes when employees disclose concerns to an adaptive AI voice interview paired with a pre-survey, finding 20-41% of sessions showed favorable ratings co-occurring with substantive concerns voiced later. Qualitative analysis shows employees soften or deflect concerns even in AI-mediated channels. It highlights risks that organizational listening via AI masks real problems.

entry.title: Composing Task-specific Agent Harnesses at Test Time with Reusable Primitives

author.name: Peng Kuang, Haibo Jin, Dehao Wu, Feiyang Deng, Xiaopeng Yuan, Jerry Wang, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues that fixed agent harnesses are suboptimal across heterogeneous tasks because mechanisms that help one task can add overhead or distraction to another. It introduces Harness Primitives, reusable components composed at test time to build task-specific harnesses for context gathering, tool invocation, verification, state preservation, and termination.

entry.title: MADBench: Benchmarking the Security of Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Yuwan Liu, Jiaming Zhang, Yue Huang, Sisi Duan

entry.summary: MADBench is a benchmark for evaluating the security of multi-agent debate under diverse attacks, organized into a layered taxonomy following the MAD workflow, including both established and new attack strategies. It addresses the central question of whether debate mitigates or amplifies adversarial influence.

entry.title: ANI: Adaptive Numerical Injection for Unifying Semantic and Arithmetic Representations in Numerical Reasoning

author.name: Jinsung Jeon, Seung-won Hwang

entry.summary: ANI hybridizes text-based tokenization with numerical embeddings (FoNE) via a context-aware gating mechanism that selectively injects arithmetic-precise features into the LLM latent space when semantically appropriate. This addresses the tension between tokenization that fragments numbers and context-agnostic numerical embeddings that ignore semantic roles.

entry.title: Values as Style: Disentangling Values from Semantics with One-Way Mixing for Low-Damage LLM Steering

author.name: Jiale Dai, Hongcan Deng, Liuxian Ma, Xiaoke Niu, Guojie Song

entry.summary: The paper proposes an editable interface on frozen residual states that separates value codes from semantic codes via a one-way semantic-to-value pathway, using stop-gradients, swap consistency, and decorrelation to encourage selective codes. Editing the value code at inference changes normative priorities while preserving facts and task content, improving semantic preservation and reducing benign refusals versus conventional activation edits on two instruction-tuned backbones.

entry.title: FIGS: Evaluating Multi-Turn Sycophancy Without Penalizing Empathy

author.name: Sidharth Pulipaka, Ruta Binkyte, Ivaxi Sheth, Sahar Abdelnabi

entry.summary: FIGS is a benchmark for evaluating multi-turn sycophancy that models sycophancy as emerging organically through user insistence and steering over extended dialogue, while explicitly distinguishing yielding from basic empathy so supportive models are not penalized. This aims to prevent over-correction toward cold, dismissive model behavior.

entry.title: NinaXander: Feasibility and Limits of Composing Frozen Language Models Across Architecture Families via a Shared Latent Space

author.name: Takanori Kotama, Shun-ichiro Hayashi, Daichi Mukunoki, Tetsuya Hoshino, Takahiro Katagiri

entry.summary: NinaXander connects layers of frozen language models from different architecture families (recurrent RWKV-4-Raven-7B and Transformer Tulu-Pythia-6.9b) through a single trained shared-latent adapter, producing composed models that run part of one model then part of the other. Once trained, multiple connection points yield composed variants without retraining. The study examines whether heterogeneous pretrained models can be recombined post hoc.

entry.title: TAGGRAPH: Tag-Augmented Graphs for Graph Retrieval of Agent Persistent Histories

author.name: Yu-Su Chen, Yu-Jung Liang, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: This work presents a controlled evaluation framework for agent long-term memory retrieval built on shared 5W-style conversational memories, comparing localized graph configurations (including AdaptiveGraph with chronological edges and Personalized PageRank) against BM25 and a raw-input external reference. Notably, simpler BM25 and the OpenClaw reference outperform the best graph configuration on LongMemEval-S, tempering enthusiasm for graph-based memory retrieval.

entry.title: Personalized State-Transition-Aware Memory for Clinical Agents

author.name: Maryam Haghifam, Zahra Rajabi, Yizhou Sun, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: STAM is a state-transition-aware memory framework for LLM clinical agents that records patient state changes as new entries arrive, maintaining current information in Active memory and superseded information in History, with a query-dependent gate serving historical memory at read time. This balances tracking current patient state while preserving the history needed to reconstruct treatment trajectories.

entry.title: Differentiable Structure Learning for Cyclic Linear Gaussian Models with Latent Confounders

author.name: Sadegh Khorasani, Ali Najar, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

entry.summary: The paper studies causal structure learning in linear Gaussian SCMs with directed cycles and an unknown number of latent confounders, introducing marginal quasi-equivalence to characterize when distinct causal models share observational distributions. It formulates learning as negative log-likelihood minimization with a complexity penalty counting edges and latent variables, and establishes consistency results.

entry.title: ReGain: Restoring Subject Fidelity in Personalization on Synthetic Images

author.name: Shubhang Bhatnagar, Ishan Bhatnagar, Viraj Shah, Narendra Ahuja

entry.summary: Shows that DreamBooth fine-tuning on synthetic images degrades subject fidelity, producing oversaturated colors and excess high-frequency detail, and traces the degradation to classifier-free guidance dynamics, specifically the angle between conditional and unconditional noise predictions. The proposed ReGain method restores subject fidelity when personalizing on synthetic training images.

entry.title: scTrilemma: Balancing Identity, Invariance, and Fidelity in Single-Cell Representation Learning

author.name: Yunhak Oh, Yoonho Lee, Junseok Lee, Namkyeong Lee, Sang-Yeon Hwang, Yinhua Piao, Hyomin Kim, Seonghwan Kim, Jaechang Lim, Woo Youn Kim, Sungsoo Ahn, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a representation trilemma in single-cell RNA-seq learning: preserving biological identity and state, robustness to nuisance context, and gene-level variation for expression analysis. scTrilemma, a latent-bottleneck VAE, routes expression-derived variation to the embedding, decoder, or prior to balance these competing demands.

entry.title: Adaptive Self-Consistency: From Black-Box Sampling to Distribution-Valued Feedback

author.name: Jingkai Huang, Yunfan Zhang, Will Ma, Weihua Zhou, Zhengyuan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper reframes self-consistency decoding for the grey-box setting where each sampled trajectory reveals the full answer distribution from log-probabilities rather than a single answer. It formulates efficient inference as sequential mode identification with distribution-valued observations, with an adaptive stopping rule characterized asymptotically, cutting sample costs.

entry.title: Sparse-WAM: Accelerating World Action Models via Action-Guided Sparse Imagination

author.name: Xinling Xie, Haodong Wang, Jiazhi Mi, Zhiming Liu, Zicong Hong, Xiaoyi Pang, Qianli Liu, Yangjia Hu, Ying Chen, Zhengyang Yan, Song Guo

entry.summary: Sparse-WAM is a training-free framework that accelerates world-action model inference by selectively retaining future-frame tokens based on action relevance rather than purely visual fidelity during joint denoising. By pruning dense future-frame token computation, it substantially reduces the inference cost of video-based robot control models.

entry.title: RAGScope: A Leakage-Controlled, Cost-Aware Evidence-Gating Protocol for RAG Hallucination Triage

author.name: Zeming Liu, Qibai Chen, Jingtao Zhang, Hang Lyu

entry.summary: RAGScope is a leakage-controlled evaluation protocol for cheap local evidence gates that triage RAG answers into accept, review, or strong-verifier paths, using context-grouped splits, fold-scoped preprocessing, bootstrap intervals, and source-shift stress tests. Its enhanced gate reaches 0.798 AUROC on RAGTruth tasks and outperforms ROUGE-L baselines. It addresses both hallucination routing cost and the pervasive data-leakage problem in hallucination-detector evaluation.

entry.title: In a Streaming World, Should You Stand Still? A Comprehensive Benchmark of Anomaly Detection in Streams

author.name: Magali Parrino, Antoine Ajenjo, Emmanuel Remy, Pierre Stephan, Pierre Senellart, Paul Boniol

entry.summary: This is the first large-scale experimental study comparing streaming anomaly detection methods against state-of-the-art time series anomaly detection models deployed online, addressing the gap that streaming methods originate from outlier detection and are evaluated on weak synthetic benchmarks. It provides clarity on whether incremental streaming methods actually outperform static TSAD approaches in realistic scenarios.

entry.title: Rethinking Multi-Image Re-Representation in Multi-Image Understanding

author.name: Gengyuan Zhang, Xiao Han, Xinyu Xie, Tong Liu, Volker Tresp

entry.summary: The paper studies how multimodal LLMs re-organize visual evidence across multiple images, framing prompted chain-of-thought and agentic tool use as different re-representation strategies. It introduces Mosaic, a harness with ten composable image operations, and MosaicBench, a grounding-focused benchmark, comparing five re-representation settings.

entry.title: PartiCam: Camera Controlled Video Generation with Reward Guidance

author.name: Amine Ouasfi, Runjia Li, Junlin Han, Eric Marchand, Philip H. S. Torr, Adnane Boukhayma

entry.summary: PartiCam is a training-free particle-filtering method for camera-controlled video generation that steers pretrained video diffusion models toward specified camera trajectories at test time, avoiding camera-annotated dataset construction. It stabilizes the exploration-collapse tradeoff that plagues existing sampling-based guidance approaches.

entry.title: D-Scope: Decomposing and Steering Diffusion Transformers with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Xinyue Xu, Jiahao Zhang, Lijie Hu, Peter Hase, Hao Wang

entry.summary: D-Scope is a framework that links SAE-based feature interpretation in diffusion transformers to actual generation control. It uses SigLIP 2 embeddings of highly activating patches as visual centroids to retrieve features without per-feature text annotations, and verifies causal control through spatially masked decoder interventions.

entry.title: Learning from Runtime Feedback through Failure-Bank Self-Evolution for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mingyue Cui, Zheyuan Liu, Yihan Zhu, Zheyuan Zhang, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: FailBank is a four-stage self-evolving framework that converts runtime feedback from a CBF-based safety shield into persistent VLA policy improvement. An observe-only safety module produces counterfactual corrections while the policy stays in control, and outcome-aware admission converts useful proposals into training data, addressing the policy-shield mismatch that otherwise blocks task progress.

entry.title: CoVisco: Codec-Native Vision Encoder with Native Token Compression for Unified Image-Video Understanding

author.name: Yulong Liu, Xiaotian Han, Junyuan Shang, Yuchen Ding, Zhenyu Zhang, Shuohuan Wang, Guibo Zhu, Sirui Han, Dianhai Yu

entry.summary: CoVisco is a codec-native vision encoder that performs token compression natively rather than after dense encoding, combining codec input support with segmented attention to encode long visual inputs in a single forward pass. This avoids dense patch-to-patch interactions across all frames and reduces the train-deploy mismatch in unified image-video understanding.

entry.title: TACTIC: Temporal and Context-Aware LLM Tactical Planning for Roadside LiDAR Attacks

author.name: Yiming Gao, Shaocheng Luo

entry.summary: TACTIC uses a multimodal LLM to coordinate scene-aware roadside LiDAR spoofing attacks under a gray-box threat model, relying only on attacker-owned perception without access to the victim's point clouds. It builds a semantic scene graph from local vehicle states and roadside imagery, then selects and configures attack primitives adapted to the surrounding traffic.

entry.title: ComputerSD: Online Self-Distillation from Real-Time Feedback for Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Yong Du, Tongbo Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Yizhou Liu, Bofan Chen, Tao Jiang, Wenhao Xu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: ComputerSD converts real-time feedback from executed GUI transitions into guidance for on-policy self-distillation in computer-use agents, addressing the sparsity of outcome rewards and the misalignment issues of fixed privileged guidance. A fine-tuned GUI analyzer supplies step-level supervision. A timely contribution to the fast-moving CUA training space.

entry.title: Activation-Conditioned Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhexi Lu, Subhajit Chaudhury, Tejaswini Pedapati, Keerthiram Murugesan, Lei Yu

entry.summary: ACSD improves on-policy self-distillation by constructing a steering vector from activation contrasts between trajectories reaching verified correct answers and all others, applied by a frozen model copy at each prediction position. The student learns from next-token distributions on self-generated prefixes, using outcome verification only for direction construction. Refines the self-distillation approach to reasoning improvement.

entry.title: LeanPolish: Verified Supervision for Lean Proof Compression

author.name: Pauline Bourigault

entry.summary: LeanPolish is a symbolic Lean 4 pipeline that releases over 33,000 accepted local proof edits and about 65,000 same-state failed attempts as verified supervision for language models. The paper reveals that first-success search and teacher-selected evaluation sites create ranking shortcuts, and shows that extending evaluation past the first success removes these artifacts, improving a trained ranker's best-candidate selection from 36.9% to 70.1% on held-out states.

entry.title: Flow Matching under Noisy Latent Structure: Beyond Exact Low-Dimensional Support

author.name: Lifeng Hao, Shaolin Ji

entry.summary: This work establishes finite-sample statistical theory for linear flow matching under a noisy latent-generator model, where data is generated by a low-dimensional Holder map perturbed by ambient Gaussian noise so the target is full-dimensional despite latent structure. The authors construct a spatially regular ReLU velocity class and prove non-asymptotic approximation and estimation bounds whose leading sample-size exponent depends on the latent rather than ambient dimension. This extends theory beyond the unrealistic assumption of exactly low-dimensional support.

entry.title: ReTaCo: Residual-Target Control for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zixiang Ni, Zhuo Hu, Renjie Cao, Weijie Ren, Binqin Shi, Weijia Zhang, Shuheng Cao, Zhicheng Shi, Zhenhao Zhang, Haomin Wen, Zhiyuan Hu

entry.summary: The paper proves that entropy-aware on-policy distillation with renormalized top-k teacher probabilities has a bias: the loss keeps pushing the student's top-k mass toward one even after matching the teacher, so the teacher is not a stationary point. ReTaCo introduces residual-target control to fix this, making on-policy distillation cheaper and more correct.

entry.title: Raw-Routed Mixture of Adapters: A Causal Intervention for Routing Collapse in Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Hung Phan, Thuy T. Nguyen, Minh Ngoc Dinh, Nhat-Quang Tran

entry.summary: The paper identifies normalization-induced routing collapse, a failure where MoE routing entropy drops to zero on instance-normalized time-series backbones because pre-encoder normalization strips statistics routers need. It proposes routing on raw input statistics with a mixture of adapters, supported by a mutual-information decomposition explaining the failure mechanism.

entry.title: A library for differentiable signal processing and machine learning on the sphere

author.name: Thorsten Kurth, Max Rietmann, Mauro Bisson, Andrea Paris, Alberto Carpentieri, Jean Kossaifi, Anima Anandkumar, Christian Hundt, Boris Bonev

entry.summary: The paper presents torch-harmonics, an open-source NVIDIA-backed library providing efficient, differentiable implementations of spherical harmonic transforms and related signal processing and ML methods for data on the S2 sphere. It targets growing ML demand in geophysics, atmospheric science, cosmology, chemistry, and other spherical-domain fields.

entry.title: Predicting Multi-View Rashomon Representation: Can We Learn Where Models Disagree?

author.name: Mingyue Ma, Zongbo Han, Changqing Zhang, Guangyu Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces the notion of Rashomon Representation, where different foundation models encode the same input differently, and proposes predicting such disagreement from a single representation rather than requiring an ensemble. It argues disagreement is a valuable signal for input reliability estimation.

entry.title: Cheap to Draw, Expensive to Trust: Certifying Test-Time Scaling Curves

author.name: Sohail (Neel), Sarkar, Shakuntala Baichoo

entry.summary: This paper studies statistical certification of best-of-k test-time scaling curves, showing that naively certifying all budgets simultaneously with exact binomial designs is prohibitively expensive. It identifies that most variance at a given budget lies between questions rather than within, and develops more efficient certification that focuses uncertainty where it matters. The work makes reported test-time compute claims more trustworthy.

entry.title: Fairness Theatre: Evaluating Post-Hoc Fairness Interventions in Vendor-Controlled Early Warning Systems

author.name: Kelly McConvey, Angelina Zhai, Rebecca Li, Shion Guha

entry.summary: Using real student records from a public Ontario college, this work evaluates six post-hoc fairness interventions on an early warning system under simulated procurement constraints where institutions cannot inspect vendor models. It introduces error-type profiling to show how interventions redistribute false positives and false negatives, interrogating whether post-hoc fixes amount to fairness theatre.

entry.title: Towards Optimal Inventory Control under Censored Demand: A Biased Sample-Average Approximation Approach

author.name: Yuxuan Han, Xiaoyu Fan, Jiawei Zhang, Zhengyuan Zhou

entry.summary: The paper develops a model-based framework for learning base-stock policies in multi-period lost-sales inventory control when demand is censored by stockouts. A new cost decomposition enables a coverage condition under which censored data suffice for sample-efficient learning, and two biased sample-average approximation algorithms achieve near-optimal sample complexity offline and active data generation online. This is a meaningful advance in sequential decision-making under partial observability.

entry.title: Ghost in the Encoder: Decodable Artist Identity Representations in Lyrics-to-Song Generation

author.name: Arhan Vohra, Choenden Kyirong, Laura Ib\'a\~nez-Mart\'inez, Mart\'in Rocamora

entry.summary: The paper shows that a trained lyrics-to-song generation model encodes linearly decodable representations of artist identity from song lyrics alone, demonstrated on ACE-Step 1.5 across 2,000 songs from 100 artists. This mechanistic finding sheds light on how models can imitate specific artists or reproduce training songs. It has direct implications for copyright, attribution, and safety of generative music models.

entry.title: FD-VAD: Semantic Endpoint Detection for Streaming Full-Duplex Speech

author.name: Puneet Mathur, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: FD-VAD formulates semantic endpoint detection in full-duplex voice interaction as a causal audio-language reasoning task, mapping bounded causal audio windows directly to Continue/Stop decisions without ASR. It combines a frozen speech encoder, a lightweight modality adapter, and a parameter-efficiently adapted language model with a last-chunk training objective. This addresses the key turn-taking problem of distinguishing hesitation from completed intent in natural voice agents.

entry.title: Lost in Translation: Measuring the Effect of Non-Native English on End User Performance of Large Language Models

author.name: Yusheng Zhou, Eleanor Lin, David Jurgens

entry.summary: Using FABLE, a controlled dataset of roughly 191,000 prompt variants derived from 174,000 real user prompts, the authors evaluate 34 open-weight LLMs to isolate which features of non-native English degrade response quality. They find an asymmetry: models do not propagate surface errors like misspellings, but do mirror higher-level rhetorical and lexical features of non-native writing, producing lower-quality outputs. This pinpoints specific drivers of inequity for non-native English speakers.

entry.title: Learning from Think-Mode Advantage via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Wanqi Ren, Jianxiang Wang, Danxuan Liu, Linyi Ding, Huaixiao Tou

entry.summary: The paper studies on-policy distillation of reasoning ability from think-mode teachers, proposing a refinement of a uniform think-enabled baseline that conditions distillation on a shared privileged think trace. It identifies cases where the same privileged trace induces misleading teacher-student discrepancies across sibling student responses and designs a method to correct this.

entry.title: Compiling Learning Problems into Adaptation Programs for Language Models

author.name: Rebecca Ramnauth, Brian Scassellati

entry.summary: The paper introduces adaptation compilation, reframing where, how, and how much a model should adapt as a joint prediction and decision problem. A compiler learns from prior adaptations to predict a counterfactual response surface over candidate programs, capturing effects on acquisition, transfer, boundedness, and preservation before adaptation begins.

entry.title: Your Benchmark Is Not Saturated: Reviving Multiple-Choice Evaluation with Answer Pooling

author.name: Mohamed Eltahir, Abobaker Ahmed, Nawaf Barebood, Hussain Bu Subayt, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: AnswerPool revives saturated multiple-choice benchmarks by pooling options from N questions sharing a context and requiring the model to assign each question its answer, with no new item writing or label changes. This drops the chance of guessing a five-question group correctly from 10^-3 to 5x10^-7 while models that genuinely recognize answers retain their scores.

entry.title: Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Oliver Sieberling, Bharat Runwal, David Jin, Ryan Chin, Rameswar Panda, Yoon Kim

entry.summary: The authors generalize linear attention's matrix-valued outer-product state to a third-order tensor state, writing the triadic outer product of two keys and a value, enabling larger effective memory for constant-time recurrent inference. This extends a line of work where memory state size is the key determinant of long-context performance in RNN-style models. It is a clean architectural idea with potential relevance to efficient long-context language modeling.

entry.title: Group-Marginalized Self-Rewarding RL Drives Zero-Label Self-Evolving

author.name: Yiming Wang, Yikang Liu, Qingyuan Tian, Xingyu Chen, Zhuosheng Zhang, Zhaopeng Tu, Rui Wang

entry.summary: The paper identifies that ensemble-based self-rewarding RL assigns rewards based on a single random group-context realization (the other sampled responses), which can miss reward signals, and proposes GMAE (Group-Marginalized Advantage Estimation), which aggregates reward realizations across possible contexts into a response-level distribution of expected advantages. Experiments across eight benchmarks support label-free self-evolution of LLMs. This is a statistically principled fix to a real variance source in group-based reward methods.

entry.title: Cool the Sampler, Not the Learner: Sampling Temperature Moves the Staleness Cliff of Importance-Corrected GRPO

author.name: Taiheng Pan

entry.summary: This single-author study finds a sharp staleness cliff in importance-corrected GRPO when the sampler lags the learner: training on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and GSM8K degrades severely just before a 192-update refresh. Rather than modifying the update rule, the proposed decoupled cooling samples at temperature 0.8 while learner, reference, and importance weights stay at temperature 1, shifting the staleness cliff. It is a practical insight for asynchronous production RL systems.

entry.title: Predictive Geometry of Hidden Trajectories in Transformers

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Tatiana Petrova, Radu State

entry.summary: The paper formalizes layerwise loss-to-go functions in decoder-only transformers and shows that around successful validation trajectories, their local second-order geometry is governed by a pullback Fisher operator on hidden-state space. Its spectrum identifies output-sensitive versus prediction-null directions, yielding an observable subspace of the residual stream. This provides a principled geometric lens on what intermediate representations can influence.

entry.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI

author.name: Cheng Qian, Kunlun Zhu, Beibin Li, Zhenhailong Wang, Heng Ji

entry.summary: The paper studies test-time AI-for-AI, where a frozen Builder model learns meta-skill principles for constructing execution environments (harnesses) for a frozen Target agent from execution feedback, storing them in a reusable skill bank for unseen tasks. Full-bank meta-skills improve macro-average performance by 8.95 points over no-skill construction and 12.02 points over direct delivery across Harness-Bench and NewtonBench. This makes harness-engineering experience transferable.

entry.title: MOBA-VL: Event-Localized Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning for Real-Time MOBA Commentary

author.name: Shengyun Zhong, Xinkang Zhao, Ziyuan Chu, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: MOBA-VL is a 9B-parameter VLM for real-time esports commentary trained with event-localized multi-turn reinforcement learning, using game telemetry that records exact event timings as a supervision signal to reward turns describing key events like kills and objectives. The authors also release MOBACast, a dataset of 860 professional matches (~460 hours) with word-level timestamped commentary across three MOBA games, plus a benchmark. This addresses the gap between fluent but event-missing streaming VLMs and accurate narration.

entry.title: StereoGaussians: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from Stereo Images

author.name: Boyuan Tian, Huangying Zhan, Zhan Li, Shin-Fang Chng, Hanwen Yang, Zirui Wang, Yi Xu

entry.summary: StereoGaussians predicts a metric 3D Gaussian Splatting representation from a single calibrated stereo pair, reusing intermediate representations from frozen pretrained stereo networks and anchoring geometry with calibrated disparity. A second Gaussian layer and expanded image canvas provide capacity for disoccluded and out-of-field-of-view content, addressing nearby-view extrapolation needed in practical stereo-camera applications. This enables feed-forward reconstruction without per-scene optimization.

entry.title: SCALE: Synthetic Calibration via Agreement Labeling in Embedding Space

author.name: Wenjun Liu, Saeed Hassanpour

entry.summary: Studies calibration in computational pathology foundation models, showing calibration error is consistently higher on cases where pathologists disagree, a pattern hidden by aggregate ECE metrics. Proposes synthetic agreement calibration that improves calibration using pathologist agreement as a difficulty proxy without collecting multi-annotator labels.

entry.title: Persistent Watermarking of Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Dixi Yao, Kaiwen Chen, Tahseen Rabbani, Tian Li

entry.summary: Addresses model copyright protection for text-to-image generators by embedding trigger data that remain persistent under unauthorized reuse and modification, including prompt preprocessing, fine-tuning, and output post-processing. The work studies how to preserve ownership verification signals while maintaining normal generation capabilities.

entry.title: MindWorldBench: Evaluating Mental-State-to-Behavior Reasoning in Image-to-Video Generation

author.name: Ruiqi Li, Xuanyi Liu, Sijia Li, Haofeng Wang, Yuxin Liu, Feng Xie, Songchao Tan, Shiqi Wang, Hanwei Zhu, Yizong Wang, Chuanmin Jia, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: MindWorldBench is a benchmark of 744 prompts evaluating whether image-to-video models can generate actions conditioned on latent mental states like beliefs and desires, using Zero-Action Prompting and counterfactual design to isolate mental-state causal effects. An automated pipeline assesses video quality, commonsense plausibility, and mental-state consistency across 11 models.

entry.title: RESUME: Recurrent State Updates from Motion and Residual Signals for Efficient Video Language Modeling

author.name: Can Zhang, Xiaotian Han, Junyuan Shang, Yuchen Ding, Zhenyu Zhang, Shuohuan Wang, Dianhai Yu, Ruirui Li

entry.summary: RESUME argues that video language models should treat codec motion vectors and residuals as functions of both current primitives and a carried reference state, proposing recurrent state updates that exploit temporal-order-sensitive information discarded by symmetric pooling. This improves efficiency for long-video language modeling without exhausting token budgets.

entry.title: Learning Where to Look: Anatomical Grounding and Guided Attention for Cardiac MRI Vision-Language Models

author.name: Bangwei Guo, Xiao Chen, Boris Mailhe, Jia Yao, Yiqing Wang, Ankush Mukherjee, Yikang Liu, Zheyuan Zhang, Hang Yu, Terrence Chen, Shanhui Sun

entry.summary: This work builds anatomically grounded cardiac MRI VLMs with 128,915 grounding pairs and 42,799 clinical QA pairs across multiple CMR sequences, enabling guided attention to clinically relevant structures. It addresses the scarcity of CMR-specific localization and QA supervision.

entry.title: Enhancing Autoregressive Video Generation via Representation Adversarial Distillation

author.name: Fangyu Lin, Xingtong Ge, Lunjie Zhu, Yi Zhang, Zhening Liu, Tianhang Wang, Mengfei Li, Yumeng Zhang, Guanglu Song, Yu Liu, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Radian complements on-policy distribution matching distillation with adversarial supervision in a frozen visual foundation model's feature space to improve few-step autoregressive video generation. Sparse frame decoding during training curbs error propagation from early temporal blocks that causes detail loss and drift in streaming synthesis.

entry.title: Representation Risk in Pretrained Image Encoders

author.name: Ardyn Nordstrom, Morgan Nordstrom, Vamuyan Sesay, Matthew D. Webb

entry.summary: The paper introduces representation risk: the uncertainty arising because plausible pretrained encoders map the same images into different feature spaces and can yield sharply different downstream conclusions.
