Comparing ten frozen encoders across six applied domains, including histology, radiographs, and econometric applications, the authors show encoder choice is a consequential modeling decision rather than an implementation detail. They advocate treating encoder selection as a source of model uncertainty in applied pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond the Current Scene: Event-Referential Grasping with Active View Selection

author.name: Hyunjoon Lee, Haebeom Jung, Eunsung Cha, Daeun Lee, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Jaesung Choe, Jaesik Park

entry.summary: BeyondSCe is a zero-shot robotic grasping system for event-referential requests, where a target object is specified by its role in a past interaction rather than name or appearance, and may be occluded when the request is made. The system combines an event prior from interaction history with current scene geometry to select camera viewpoints likely to reveal the target. It uses pretrained models without task-specific training.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Guided Evolutionary Discovery of Native Neural Architectures for Spiking Sequence Modeling

author.name: Ruoyu Zhao, Jiaqi Wu, Chenyu Zhu, Zhichao Lu

entry.summary: OpenArchEvo uses large language models to evolve executable, native spiking neural network architectures for low-energy sequence modeling, moving beyond adapting ANN designs to predefined configuration spaces. This LLM-guided evolutionary architecture search aims to discover spike-native mechanisms for encoding, neuronal dynamics, and propagation.

entry.title: Coral Grow-out Robotic Assessment System (CGRAS): Scaling Coral Recruit Monitoring Through Robotics and Computer Vision

author.name: Dorian Tsai, Scarlett Raine, Emilio Olivastri, Riki Lamont, Andrew Lui, Timothy Morris, Joshua Esplin, Christopher A. Brunner, F. Mikaela Nordborg, Reginald Wardleworth, Garima Samvedi, Karen Jackel, Matthew Dunbabin, Tobias Fischer, Andrea Severati

entry.summary: CGRAS combines robotic imaging and computer vision to automate monitoring of microscopic (0.5-2mm) coral recruits grown in aquaculture for reef restoration, a task that is prohibitively labor-intensive when done manually at the tens-of-thousands scale. The system addresses a key production bottleneck in scaling coral seeding as a climate-change response technology.

entry.title: DODGER: Safety-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Robot Navigation Among Dynamic Obstacles

author.name: Sanghyuk Park, Kwanwoo Lee, Taekyung Kim, Seohyeon Lim, Yisoo Lee

entry.summary: DODGER is a safety-guided reinforcement learning framework for navigation among dynamic obstacles that executes policy-generated actions during training rollouts while using control barrier function (CBF) filtered references and corrective signals, avoiding the exploration restriction caused by only executing safety-filtered actions. This addresses a key limitation of prior CBF-based RL methods in dynamic scenes.

entry.title: RoboAssist: Interactive Human-Humanoid Planning for Long-Horizon Surgical Assistance

author.name: Jingwei Jia, Keyu Zhou, Jiewei Wang, Peisen Xu, Xingyuan Zhou, Liang Wang, Jiming Chen, Gaofeng Li, Jin Wang, Shunlei Li

entry.summary: RoboAssist is an agent-based framework for humanoid robots providing long-horizon surgical assistance, combining workflow reasoning, online task coordination, and cross-layer safety. Its asymmetric dual-track representation separates partially observed human process states from executable robot task sequences, enabling suffix-only replanning when workflows change. The work targets a demanding human-robot interaction setting with strict safety requirements.

entry.title: Dream4ACT: A Shared Visual Action Interface for Multi-Embodiment Video-Action Modeling

author.name: Xiangyu Zhu, Jin Xu, Yue Guo, Xin Wu, Yifan Sun, Xiancong Ren, Jianxin Sun, Yong Dai, Xiaozhu Ju

entry.summary: Dream4ACT is a world model for joint video-action modeling across robot embodiments that introduces action views, a shared visual action interface rendering target joint configurations from four prescribed virtual cameras. This unifies action representations of differing dimensionality and semantics across embodiments, enabling video generation model priors to be leveraged for multi-embodiment control.

entry.title: Local polynomial density ratio estimation

author.name: Hajo Holzmann, Alexander Meister

entry.summary: The authors propose a local-polynomial estimator of the ratio of two d-dimensional densities that achieves pointwise minimax optimal rates over Holder classes of arbitrary smoothness without logarithmic factors, assuming smoothness only of the ratio rather than of the individual densities. The analysis also covers support boundaries under mild geometric assumptions and includes a concentration inequality useful for classification.

entry.title: This game-playing AI is the new champ at Stratego

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: Researchers from MIT, Carnegie Mellon, NYU, and Stanford developed an AI system that decisively defeats top-ranked human players at Stratego, a two-player imperfect-information wargame long used as a strategic-reasoning benchmark. The system combines efficient training algorithms with new decision-making techniques for hidden-information settings, achieving state-of-the-art performance while being substantially cheaper and less computationally demanding to train than prior models. It also generalizes to other strategic games, suggesting applicability to real-world adversarial decision problems.

entry.title: NAQD Env: A benchmark for selective withdrawal in language agents

author.name: Mohamed Abouzahra

entry.summary: NAQD-Env is a synthetic environment testing whether language agents can selectively withdraw planned actions when evidence changes, permission is revoked, or a stop instruction arrives, suspending affected actions while preserving unaffected work. It evaluates against a deterministic reference policy over dependency structures with eleven dependency families and metrics separating attempted from permitted violations.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Algorithm-Design Agents: Escaping In-Context Evolutionary Stagnation via Population-Curated Policy Optimization

author.name: Chen Lu, Ke Xue, Siyuan Xu, Mingxuan Yuan, Chao Qian

entry.summary: This paper characterizes in-context evolutionary stagnation in LLM algorithm-design agents and proposes sample-efficient parametric self-evolution via population-curated policy optimization, letting agents learn from self-generated algorithms where domain corpora are scarce. It analytically grounds why pure in-context evolution plateaus. The approach bridges in-context and parametric adaptation for algorithm design.

entry.title: C-STRIDE: An Observation-Driven AI Digital Twin for Predicting Basin-Wide Flood Fields from Sparse Stream-Gauge Histories

author.name: Yanjie Tong, Phillip Si, Yuan Qiu, Peng Chen

entry.summary: C-STRIDE is an AI digital twin that converts sparse stream-gauge readings plus terrain and rainfall data into basin-wide water depth maps with forecasts up to a day ahead, trained on simulations from a calibrated 2D hydrodynamic model. It was evaluated on the Des Plaines River basin near Chicago and avoids costly data assimilation or hydrodynamic reruns.

entry.title: On the Complexity of Preference-Based Bandits

author.name: Ahmed Ben Yahmed (CREST, ENSAE Paris, FAIRPLAY), Marc Abeille (FAIRPLAY), Cl\'ement Calauz\`enes (FAIRPLAY)

entry.summary: This paper studies preference-based bandits with general reward function classes under the Bradley-Terry model, addressing the logistic-type challenge of the problem-dependent constant kappa. It extends the theory beyond the linear and kernelized reward models that dominated prior work, with relevance to learning from human feedback.

entry.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization

author.name: Tunyu Zhang, Hao Wang, Kai Xu, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Turbo Harness introduces a framework for adapting an automatically optimized agent harness to individual task instances rather than applying one global harness uniformly. It recycles artifacts from a completed global harness optimization run, summarizes them into a structured playbook, and trains a harness editor that leverages this prior optimization experience to generate instance-specific harnesses. This is positioned as a step toward agents that can recursively self-improve.

entry.title: What Was Said, Not What Was 'Thought': Type-6 Logic for CoT Verification

author.name: Adrian de Wynter

entry.summary: The paper introduces Type-6 logic, a dynamic epistemic logic variant with uncertainty and recurrence operators designed to model pathologies of LLM chain-of-thought reasoning such as unlicensed revision, enthymemes, and unverifiable claims. A graph-based verifier checks traces against Type-6 axioms and detects structurally unsound reasoning steps that surface-level heuristics miss.

entry.title: Prompt2Skill: Unsupervised Skill Optimization From Natural Language Instructions

author.name: Bo Ni, Li Li, Ryan A. Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Tyler Derr

entry.summary: Prompt2Skill optimizes skill artifacts for LLM agents in an unsupervised manner, using natural language instructions as the source instead of curated in-distribution training sets, addressing the cost of expert-authored skills and their mismatch with specific model versions. This extends automated skill optimization to settings where no curated training data exist yet.

entry.title: Online Evolution Strategy for Flow-Matching VLA Policies via Self-Supervised Trajectory Distribution Optimization

author.name: Gongxin Yao, Yongsheng Zhao, Jiayin Deng, Deng Liang, Han Gao, Lei Zhao, Baoping Cheng

entry.summary: Observing that Flow Matching vision-language-action models learn ill-formed action trajectory distributions where successful and failed behaviors coexist, the authors propose Online-ES. This framework uses evolution strategies with interaction feedback to refine the learned trajectory distribution online, improving robotic manipulation performance.

entry.title: Scale-Split Neural Operator for Memory- and Data-Efficient 3D Turbulence Prediction

author.name: Shaoxiang Qin, Yucheng Zhao, Zongyi Li, Liangzhu Leon Wang, Xiongye Xiao

entry.summary: ScaleSplit-NO decomposes 3D turbulence prediction into a Parent operator that predicts coarse global fields and a Child operator that predicts full-resolution local patches conditioned on the coarse forecast, so neither model processes full-resolution fields. This exploits turbulence scale structure to cut training memory and data requirements while preserving resolution.

entry.title: ReSAIL: Mitigating Collapse in Iterative Agent Self-Distillation

author.name: Shengjie Jin, Hengbo Xu, Zelong Sun, YuJie Guo, Zhiwu Lu

entry.summary: ReSAIL addresses performance collapse in iterative self-distillation for LLM agents pursuing recursive self-improvement, prioritizing informative interaction steps where privileged information most strongly changes teacher predictions and preserving PI-conditioned behavior across cycles. It is a plug-in augmentation for iterative PI-based self-distillation pipelines.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy AI for Glioma Diagnosis: A Task-Aware Evaluation of Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Gonzalo Esteban Mosquera Rojas, Sebastian R. van der Voort, Carolin M. Pirkl, Sandeep Kaushik, Marion Smits, Stefan Klein

entry.summary: This work evaluates uncertainty quantification in a multi-task deep learning framework for MRI-based glioma diagnosis covering segmentation and molecular/grade prediction, using Monte Carlo Dropout with detailed task-aware analysis of predictive, aleatoric, and epistemic uncertainty. It compares against Deep Ensembles and examines calibration, error detection, and selective prediction.

entry.title: RoboCoach: World Models as Active Coaches for Compositional Robot Skills

author.name: Jiajun Liu, Yifan Chen, Yichao Liu, Jiayi Zhang, Ruoqu Chen, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Mengdi Xu, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: RoboCoach is a world-model-guided coaching framework that uses imagined failures to decide which demonstrations to request and which skill adapters to update for long-horizon compositional manipulation. Its Route-Imagine-Diagnose-Improve loop runs reusable skill experts inside a shared action-conditioned world model with a progress judge identifying the first failing subtask.

entry.title: When a Kindergartener Solves Calculus: Measuring Capability Leakage in Role-Prompted Reasoning Models

author.name: Pakhapoom Sarapat, Saksorn Ruangtanusak, Kunat Pipatanakul, Pittawat Taveekitworachai

entry.summary: The paper introduces RoleCapBench, a curriculum-grounded benchmark measuring role-capability leakage, where role-prompted reasoning models produce convincing in-role text while secretly retaining benchmark performance far beyond the assigned role. Evaluating three open-weight reasoning models across six educational roles and four assessment levels, it finds the effect is widespread.

entry.title: WARP: A Unified Benchmark for Invisible Image Watermarking -- Robustness and Protection Against Attacks

author.name: Khaled Abud, Aleksey Yakushev, Aleksandr Akimenkov, Irina Serzhenko, Kirill Aistov, Egor Kovalev, Dmitry Obydenkov, Sergey Lavrushkin, Anastasia Antsiferova, Dmitriy Vatolin, Yury Markin, Kirill Lukianov

entry.summary: WARP is a unified benchmark evaluating robustness of invisible image watermarks across 32 recent classical, deep, and generative watermarking methods and 34 erasing techniques, spanning traditional distortions to adversarial, purification, and re-embedding attacks. It responds to regulatory pressure for marking AI-generated content and updating outdated watermarking evaluation practice.

entry.title: The Advantages of Fresh Sketching for Ridge Regression

author.name: Linkai Ma, Qilin Li, Petros Drineas

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open question in iterative randomized solvers for ridge regression: whether drawing fresh sketches at every step provably beats reusing one sketch. Fresh sketching enables error analysis along the current residual only, yielding sharper convergence guarantees for leverage-score and ridge-leverage-score sampling and motivating new residual-aware sampling rules.

entry.title: Not all solutions are created equal: An analytical dissociation of functional and representational similarity in deep linear neural networks

author.name: Lukas Braun, Erin Grant, Andrew M. Saxe

entry.summary: Using analytically tractable two-layer linear networks plus simulations in nonlinear networks, the authors show that functional similarity and representational similarity dissociate, questioning the common inference from representational comparisons (e.g., multivariate pattern analysis) to underlying function. This is foundational for neuroscience and AI comparisons of biological and artificial networks. The work clarifies when matching representations does or does not imply matching computations.

entry.title: Characterizing High Bandwidth Flash for LLM Serving

author.name: Zack Yu, Chloe Wong, Coleman Hooper, Minjae Lee, Wonjun Kang, Youngjin Cho, Michael W. Mahoney, Yakun Sophia Shao, Kurt Keutzer, Amir Gholami

entry.summary: This systems paper evaluates high-bandwidth flash (HBF) memory as a way to expand accelerator memory capacity for LLM serving, where model weights and KV caches increasingly strain memory bandwidth and capacity, especially for agentic workloads with long, repeatedly accessed contexts. The authors characterize when HBF improves serving performance and efficiency across system design and scheduling choices, while accounting for its access costs and limited write endurance.

entry.title: Riemannian Flow Models with Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction

author.name: Thomas Egg, Harry Winston Sullivan, Maya M. Martirossyan, Philipp H\"ollmer, Cheng Zeng, Adrian Roitberg, Mingjie Liu, Richard Hennig, Sapna Sarupria, Ellad B. Tadmor, Stefano Martiniani

entry.summary: The paper introduces CG-OMatG, an equivariant Riemannian flow-based generative model with a coarse-grained hierarchical representation that treats molecules as rigid bodies for molecular crystal structure prediction. It is combined with RL fine-tuning to handle polymorphism, large unit cells, and complex packing geometry that challenge existing generative CSP models.

entry.title: Advantage of Sample Complexity in Quantum PAC Learning Requires Inverse Access to State-Preparation Unitaries

author.name: Natsuto Isogai, Satoshi Yoshida, Mio Murao

entry.summary: In quantum PAC learning, this paper clarifies when quantum data can reduce sample complexity versus classical learning: the advantage from forward access alone is absent, and improvements in the accuracy parameter require access to both a state-preparation unitary and its inverse. This settles a previously open question about the necessity of inverse access.

entry.title: Learn-Then-Differentiate Gradient Estimation

author.name: Nifei Lin, Qingkai Zhang, L. Jeff Hong

entry.summary: This work develops a unified theoretical framework for learn-then-differentiate gradient estimation, where a surrogate model is fit to simulation outputs and then differentiated. It shows that accuracy guarantees for fitted models translate into gradient and higher-order derivative guarantees, with rates approaching the standard Monte Carlo rate, recovering known results for kernel-based methods as special cases.

entry.title: MADGRAV: a multilevel anomaly-detection pipeline for gravitational-wave searches applied to LIGO data

author.name: Gianluca Inguglia, Huw Haigh, Ulyana Dupletsa, Alessandro Longo

entry.summary: MADGRAV is a deep-learning pipeline of sequential convolutional networks performing anomaly detection, glitch classification, coherence testing, and signal ranking, applied to LIGO data from the third and fourth observing runs. Of surviving candidates, 48 reached significance and 47 gravitational-wave detections are reported. It demonstrates deep learning producing real scientific detections at scale in fundamental physics.

entry.title: OPTS-TTPO: Enhancing Finite-Sample Policy-Gradient Learning with Tree Search

author.name: Junyu Lu, Shichao Weng, Zhiqiang Wang, Haojie Luo, Jingfan Zhang, Yuhua Zhou, Cheng Du, Yuzhuo Zhang, Xi Li, Jinwei Du, Tiancheng Feng, Chuan Xiao, Shuyuan Zheng

entry.summary: This work studies whether on-policy parallel tree search can improve coverage of rare high-return trajectories in policy-gradient learning within a fixed budget while controlling gradient bias. The authors introduce OPTS and TTPO, which sample new suffixes from the current policy at visited states, requiring no action-distribution correction, and prove a Branch Aggregation Lemma showing branch-weighted tree statistics recover chain expectations under pre-fixed weights. This connects tree search with policy optimization in a theoretically grounded way.

entry.title: PrimeSeeker: Capability-Oriented Supervision for Deep Search Agents

author.name: Linzhi Peng, Hanting Chen, Heng Chang, Ke Cheng, Bowen Du, Weifeng Lv

entry.summary: PrimeSeeker introduces latent anchor reasoning, a primitive retrieval unit where models resolve an unnamed retrieval anchor from descriptions and transfer it into a subsequent information demand. This capability-oriented question construction aims to train deep search agents on the local skills search actually requires rather than global proxy difficulty.

entry.title: When Does Correction Become Repair? Mechanistic Auditing of Internal Interventions in Tool-Using LLMs

author.name: Jiayi Li, Ruizhe Li

entry.summary: The paper presents SAKIKO, an auditing framework that examines whether activation steering interventions in tool-using LLMs actually repair misclassified pre-execution decisions or merely displace errors. It formalizes representation repair through directional error discovery, router-conditioned intervention, and destination-resolved verification, evaluated across seven LLMs on When2Call and MetaTool. The work brings mechanistic rigor to evaluating internal interventions in agentic decision-making.

entry.title: ER-JEPA: Experience Replay Improves Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Language Models

author.name: Jingnan Pu, Zi-En Fan, Feng Lian

entry.summary: ER-JEPA augments LLM-JEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture for language models, with an episodic replay memory that stores training pairs and retrieves relevant data at each step to provide additional supervision for token prediction and representation alignment. This addresses the gap between strong view alignment and stable, accurate prediction in JEPA-style training.

entry.title: Selecting The Most Informative Tokens in Natural Language Autoencoders

author.name: Federico Torrielli, Gianluca Barmina, Andrea Blasi N\'u\~nez, Amon Rapp, Luigi Di Caro, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: This work studies which token positions auditors should explain when using natural language autoencoders to interpret model activations, analyzing 4.7 million explanations on prompt injection and concealment tasks. It finds simple chat-structure signals outperform computational signals for selecting positions, and explaining just 5% of positions retains nearly all success on three of four datasets.

entry.title: Devils in Question Relay: Source-Conditioned Relay Steering to Mitigate Hallucinations in Audio-visual Large Language Models

author.name: Yu Zhang, Pingrui Zhang, Xuefeng Bai, Pengfei Zhang, Yang Xiang, Kehai Chen

entry.summary: Studies source-confused grounding hallucination in audio-visual LLMs, where cues from an unused modality induce unsupported responses. Through path-intervention and representation analysis the authors reveal a question-relay mechanism in internal cross-modal interactions and propose source-conditioned relay steering to mitigate it.

entry.title: From Routing Signals to Selective Review: Visual regrounding in MoE VLMs

author.name: Hongzhu Guo, Mohsen Fayyaz, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: The paper identifies target-absence grounding failures in vision-language models, where models answer questions about objects that are absent, and presents the first framework using internal Mixture-of-Experts routing decisions to detect such failures before generation. They extract target-token routing probabilities from Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct and Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, train linear detectors, and selectively invoke correction tools. This offers a cheap, internal-signal-based reliability mechanism for multimodal systems.

entry.title: When Trees Are Not Enough: Learning Mixed-Topology Feature Graphs with Adaptive Graph Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Xiaozuo Shen, Yifei Cai, Tian Tan, Rui Ning, Chunsheng Xin, Hongyi Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces AG-SAE, a structure-guided sparse autoencoder training paradigm for LLM activations that treats each feature's complete parent set as an atomic structural hypothesis, allowing zero, one, or multiple parents rather than imposing tree topologies. By competing parent sets against null and alternative explanations, it identifies jointly necessary multi-parent relations while rejecting spurious ones. This advances SAE-based interpretability by enabling richer, more faithful feature relationship structures.

entry.title: CorrGRPO: Correlation-Normalized GRPO for Multi-Reward Learning

author.name: Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Haochen Shi, Yuxuan Liu, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how GRPO's within-group reward normalization behaves with multiple rewards, showing that correlated or large-scale reward components can dominate the aggregate covariance and suppress smaller reward signals. CorrGRPO normalizes using the correlation structure so each reward contributes appropriately to advantage estimates. It is a targeted fix to a practical issue in multi-objective RL post-training of reasoning models.

entry.title: Asking for What Was Never Requested: Horizontal and Vertical Proactivity in Agents

author.name: Ido Levy, Asaf Yehudai, Segev Shlomov, Asaf Adi, Leshem Choshen

entry.summary: The paper studies the content of agent proactivity, distinguishing horizontal proactivity (pursuing unstated information already identified by the context) from vertical proactivity (pursuing needs revealed only by earlier evidence). It introduces a need graph recovered from benchmark decompositions that enables scoring both proactivity types and stopping behavior from transcripts without a model-based judge, plus a method to train this behavior. This addresses an underexplored dimension of tool-using agent behavior.

entry.title: Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation

author.name: Joel Anto Paul, Litu Rout, Aditya Akella, Sanjay Shakkottai

entry.summary: The paper introduces time-based self-supervised anchoring for diffusion language models, learning latent anchors that encode persistent properties of the clean sequence (intent, structure, plan) without supervised important-token targets. A two-stage architecture uses an expensive anchor network to build a latent cache and a lightweight generator that reuses it, exploiting the observation that anchor semantics remain useful across nearby diffusion timesteps. This improves denoising speed for diffusion text generation.

entry.title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies

author.name: Hui Ren, Lei Fan, Henry Pao, Han Guo, Zeeshan Zia, Ying Chen, Alexander Schwing, Gang Hua

entry.summary: Grounded Entity Biographies (GEB) is a long-video memory framework that groups visually grounded observations of the same physical instance across clips into retrievable entity biographies, resolving identity ambiguity that chronological descriptions leave open. During question answering, the relevant biography is retrieved to connect events about a specific object across hours or days. This addresses a core failure mode in long-video understanding.

entry.title: Multidimensional Observer Model and Perceptual Dimensions of Human Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Sheng Zhao, Weikai Lin, Yuhao Zhu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-dimensional observer model representing images as distributions in a latent perceptual space, with human judgment modeled as comparison of noisy samples. Constrained by primate ventral stream neural representations and fit to large-scale behavioral data, the model matches the predictive power of existing image quality metrics while revealing the structure of human perceptual space. It finds that the perceptual spaces needed to explain quality judgment have specific dimensional structure relevant to machine vision tasks like image generation.

entry.title: Eulerian Motion Reconstruction for Water Scenery

author.name: Chuhan Chen, Yen-Chi Cheng, Ayush Saraf, Rajvi Shah, Tuotuo Li, Johannes Kopf, Chen Gao, Hung-Yu Tseng, Deva Ramanan, Matthew O'Toole, Changil Kim

entry.summary: This paper reconstructs looping 4D dynamic water scenery from a single non-looping 2D source video, renderable from novel viewpoints. Motion is represented as a 3D static Eulerian motion field that advects canonical Gaussian splats cyclically reborn at fixed periods, supervised with rendering losses, with a non-periodic time-varying residual term for stochastic real-world dynamics. The author list includes prominent graphics researchers (Deva Ramanan, Johannes Kopf, Matthew O'Toole).

entry.title: FrameMorrow: Future-guided Frame Selection with Prospective Tokens for Long-Horizon Video Generation

author.name: Bo Yin, Xiaobin Hu, Jiaqi Zhao, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: Addresses long-horizon video generation by selecting historical frames according to their relevance to future information needs rather than current content. Introduces prospective tokens, a compact representation of what will become needed, avoiding full future generation while enabling better history selection as generated sequences grow.

entry.title: FOMO: Forget the Concept, Don't Miss Out on the Scene in Selective Video Unlearning

author.name: {\L}ukasz Rudnik, Agnieszka Polowczyk, Alicja Polowczyk, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: FOMO extends concept unlearning in generative video models to motion concepts while preserving the surrounding scene, background, composition, and dynamics. It addresses the gap where existing unlearning methods target only static visual concepts and often unintentionally alter the rest of the video.

entry.title: Inline Memory Meets Reusable Skills: Memory-centric Framework for Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Zaijing Li, Rui Shao, Bing Hu, Haoyu Zhang, Dongmei Jiang, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Optimus-R formulates VLA adaptation as explicit query-skill memory tuning, inserting learnable memory tokens into the VLA prefix stream for skill extraction and retrieval, avoiding costly parameter tuning and catastrophic forgetting. The framework targets efficient adaptation of robotic manipulation policies to new tasks and domains.

entry.title: CoEvoWhen: Policy-Tool Coevolution for Ultra-Long Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Yiduo Jia, Muzhi Zhu, Jinchuan Shi, Hao Zhong, Yuling Xi, Ke Liu, Hao Chen

entry.summary: CoEvoWhen jointly evolves high-level agentic policies and executable media tools from a VLM's reasoning trajectories for ultra-long video temporal grounding, distilling reusable skills without parameter updates. An external skill updater refines orchestration of long-range image-based and fine-grained video-based observations under a limited visual budget.

entry.title: UniWAM Technical Report: Unified Mobile Manipulation via Mixed-Stream World-Action Modeling and Manipulation Anchor Pose Supervision

author.name: Wei Xue, Keliang Liu, Mingzhang Cui, Jinhua Xie, Jinjie Wei, Jianan Hou, Jingcheng Lu, Lintao Wang, Kaixiang Qiu, Yizhou Liu, Xinghai Ye, Jinghang Han, Mingcheng Li, Jie Gu, Shunli Wang, Lihua Zhang, Dingkang Yang

entry.summary: UniWAM is a unified mixed-stream world-action model for mobile manipulation with separate action encoders and output heads for navigation and manipulation on a shared backbone, enabling joint learning on independently sampled data and both independent and batch-parallel inference. It introduces manipulation anchor pose supervision to reduce reliance on costly navigation data with explicit manipulation-ready pose labels. The design addresses the differing action spaces and visual requirements of the two stages.

entry.title: TALK-Dem: Benchmarking Embodied Task Planning under Dementia-Associated Communication Patterns

author.name: Guangxin Zhao, Yiran Hu, Yuan Cao, Chenxi Jiang, Jianfei Yang, Yegang Du, Yasuyuki Taki, Yoshifumi Kitamura, Lin Gu, Zhi Zheng

entry.summary: TALK-Dem is the first benchmark evaluating LLM-driven robot task planning under dementia-associated verbal communication, with 4,800 instructions covering five patterns such as referential imprecision, object substitution, empty speech, topic drift, and intrusion. It targets a real safety-relevant gap: planners that assume clear, complete instructions may err or create physical risks when interacting with people living with dementia.

entry.title: Locomotion-Grounded Humanoid Soccer: Task-Gated Reinforcement Learning of a Multi-Directional Kicking Library

author.name: Abu Hanif Muhammad Syarubany, Jaehyun Jang, Hwanhee Kim, Kyuwon Kim, Seungyeon Ryu, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: This paper inverts the typical humanoid soccer stack by training a general command-conditioned locomotion policy first, then adding motion-guided kicking skills as task-gated layers on top, making locomotion a composition hub with O(N) composition properties. This contrasts with motion-tracking-based approaches where locomotion is only trained on the narrow command distribution induced by ball approach.

entry.title: It takes hundreds of samples to poison a model, but only a few dozen to make it believe in it.

author.name: Skdk

entry.summary: Building on Souly et al.'s finding that roughly 250 poisoned documents suffice to implant backdoors regardless of model size, this post presents mechanistic experiments on a 20M-parameter model with a constructed shortcut-versus-long-route task to explain why poisoning is not diluted by clean data. The small scale allows enumerating information transmission paths underlying the backdoor.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Diffusion Language Models with Context Selection and Target Weighting

author.name: Loay Mualem, Llu\'is Pastor-P\'erez, Vinh Tong, Andrei Manolache, Tanja Bien, Steffen Staab, Mathias Niepert

entry.summary: GoldiMask improves supervised fine-tuning of discrete diffusion language models by selecting which tokens to reveal as context via approximate maximization of a submodular objective that balances context benefit against prediction-target value, then weighting remaining targets by their dependence on the selected context and learning potential. This replaces uniform random masking, which ignores the interaction between context and target choices.

entry.title: Towards Model as a Library: Offline, Community-Sourced AI for Low-Resource African Languages

author.name: Fendji K. E. Jean Louis

entry.summary: MaaL (Model as a Library) is a software architecture packaging small, community-enrolled speech models as versioned on-device dependencies for offline structured data collection in African languages, avoiding web-scraped corpora that misrepresent dialectal variation. The design prevents generative hallucination during data collection and enrolls community vocabularies directly.

entry.title: AgBench: Agentic AI Benchmarks for Personal AI Devices

author.name: Yizhou Han, Di Wu, Dhananjay Saikumar, Blesson Varghese

entry.summary: AgBench provides a benchmark suite and open artifacts for evaluating agentic AI workloads across local, hybrid, and cloud execution on personal devices, measuring task success, latency, API cost, and data exposure. It addresses the lack of systematic tools to characterize the privacy-cost-performance trade-offs of running agents on-device. This is timely given rising concerns about cloud API costs and data leakage.

entry.title: Diversity Combining for Multi-Path LLM Reasoning

author.name: Guangsheng Yu, Litianyi Zhang, Qin Wang, Xu Wang, Mingyuan Li, Shaoxiong Ji, Ren Ping Liu, Massimo Piccardi

entry.summary: This work formalizes multi-path LLM reasoning (self-consistency) as a diversity combining problem from wireless communications, showing pairwise correlation of path correctness caps the effective sample size of the vote. GLS analysis under exchangeability shows the optimal symmetric linear combiner is uniform, theoretically supporting majority vote as a default while indicating when weighted schemes could help. It explains why self-consistency gains plateau as K grows.

entry.title: When Order Matters: First-Speaker Bias and Mitigation through Personality in Sequential Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Duofeng Xu, Bryan Hooi, Dandan Qiao

entry.summary: The paper shows sequential multi-agent debate exhibits pronounced first-speaker bias, where speaking first disproportionately determines the final answer and can negate a stronger model's reasoning advantage when it speaks last. Drawing on Big Five traits, the authors find agreeableness and extraversion prompting have trait-specific effects that can mitigate this imbalance.

entry.title: Inferring Causal Relations between Two Sequences of Events with Language Models

author.name: Nishchal Prasad, Eric Gaussier, Emilie Devijver, Alexander Obeid Guzman, Armen Aghasaryan, Gregor G\"ossler

entry.summary: This work addresses causal discovery from single observations of event sequences, a setting where standard causal discovery methods fail. It explores using language models to infer causal relations between events in sequences, extending causal AI toward settings with severely limited information.

entry.title: Trust Is Not a Score: Runtime Assurance Contracts for High-Risk AI Agents

author.name: Serhii Zabolotnii

entry.summary: The paper identifies the assurance-transition gap: benchmarks and audits describe agent performance and permissions but not how evidence should change an agent's authority mid-task. It proposes Runtime Assurance Contracts, a formal schema binding autonomy boundaries, evidence state, transition policy, human-review capacity, and non-compensatory gates, under which failed or unknown mandatory gates force escalation or stop and aggregate performance cannot authorize action.

entry.title: EHR2Trace: Auditable EHR Data Infrastructure for Patient World Models and Clinical Agents

author.name: Xinye Yang, Yuli Wang, Cheng Ting Lin, Harrison Bai

entry.summary: EHR2Trace converts electronic health records from multiple sources into traceable patient-event streams suitable for training and evaluating patient world models and clinical agents. It links events to source records, separates event time from information availability, and distinguishes medication orders, dispensing, and administration, with shared representations supporting OMOP and MEDS exports. This addresses a key data-infrastructure barrier for reliable clinical AI.

entry.title: Explicit Trajectory Diversity for RL-Based Post-Training of LLM Agents

author.name: Huaiyu Fu, Heng Cao, Hao Wang, Jian Ya, Tao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes making trajectory diversity explicit in RL-based post-training of LLM agents by defining diversity through user-specified, task-specific trajectory descriptors that map sampled trajectories to interpretable behavioral variation. This addresses the limitation that existing diversity in LLM post-training arises implicitly from stochasticity rather than targeting intended behavioral variation.

entry.title: Optimal Design for Active Preference Learning with Biased LLM Judges

author.name: Zhongman Du, Huiming Zhang, Haodong Zhu, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper incorporates LLM judge bias directly into the acquisition design for active preference learning, rather than relying on separate calibration, since active acquisition can shift the comparison distribution and expose residual judge bias. Comparisons that look informative about the reward may also reflect judge bias, and the framework jointly estimates both.

entry.title: An Uncertainty-Guided Digital Twin Framework for Online Adaptive Proton Therapy in Head and Neck Cancer: A Feasibility Study

author.name: Yizhou Wu, Ryan J. Sanford, Huiqiao Xie, Jie Ding, Shupeng Chen, Tung-Ho Wu, Ping-Hsiu Wu, Justin Roper, Jun Zhou, Minglei Kang, Bill Stokes, Sibo Tian, David S. Yu, Xiaofeng Yang, Chih-Wei Chang

entry.summary: The paper presents an uncertainty-guided digital twin framework that forecasts treatment-day anatomy for head and neck cancer patients using 302 longitudinal deformations from 88 prior patients transported via multi-atlas registration built on a pretrained CT foundation model. Contour dispersion provides uncertainty estimates to determine when online adaptive proton therapy replanning yields clinically acceptable plans.

entry.title: DAGent: Evaluate-then-Grow Planning for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Hanwen Liu, Yuanfu Sun, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: DAGent is a DAG-based multi-agent framework for deep research that replaces plan-then-patch strategies with an evaluate-then-grow approach, expanding the plan only as evidence accumulates rather than committing to a full plan upfront. This avoids committing most strongly when evidence is weakest and reduces wasted computation on poorly planned branches.

entry.title: Learning Normal Diffusion Dynamics for Backdoor Defense in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Junjian Li, Xiaolong Liu, Peng Sun, Liantao Wu, Linghan Chen, Yudong Gao, Honglong Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose Normal Diffusion Dynamics Learning (NDDL), a backdoor defense for text-to-image diffusion models based on the observation that benign diffusion trajectories exhibit structured, timestep-dependent transition patterns that backdoor attacks deviate from. This transition-dynamics perspective aims for better generalization than pattern-matching defenses.

entry.title: DiffWAM: A Fast and Efficient Navigation World Action Model

author.name: Mo Zhu, Yuze Wu, Xijie Huang, Xiao Cui, Fei Gao, Xin Zhou

entry.summary: DiffWAM is a geometry-conditioned navigation world-action model that recovers motion directly from predictive representations of a frozen video foundation model, avoiding costly future-video synthesis and geometric reconstruction. Its Grid-Motion module preserves spatial-temporal motion associations and Latent2Pose grounds them into metrically meaningful 3D camera trajectories for UAV navigation.

entry.title: Learning When and How to Intervene: A Hindsight-Distilled Sentinel for Coding Agents

author.name: Jiangrui Zhao, Chenglong Li, Meng Zhang, Xiaoting Du

entry.summary: HiSentinel trains small (0.6B and 1.7B) sentinels to choose pre-execution interventions for coding agents using hindsight distillation: a privileged teacher exploits recorded execution outcomes to make intervention judgments, which are distilled into the compact model. The goal is improving eventual task completion rather than correcting every imperfect action.

entry.title: Lasting Effects of Abstract Pretraining Beyond Perplexity

author.name: Zachary Shinnick, Hemanth Saratchandran, Damien Teney, Anton van den Hengel

entry.summary: The paper shows that a brief warm-up (as little as 1% of pretraining tokens) on abstract algorithmically generated data, specifically a stack-manipulation task requiring compositional state tracking, improves multi-hop question answering in small language models by up to 3.9 F1 on MUSIQUE with gains on related benchmarks, despite comparable language-modeling perplexity. This demonstrates capability improvements from abstract pretraining that perplexity does not capture.

entry.title: Robust Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning from Corrupted Human Feedback

author.name: Xinyi Ni, Lifeng Lai

entry.summary: The paper studies online risk-sensitive RLHF with static conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) objectives under adversarial preference-label flips, using additive linear rewards and a fixed-reference protocol with at most C flipped labels over K episodes. The proposed WSP-CVaR-RLHF combines uncertainty-weighted reward estimation with optimistic augmented-state CVaR planning and achieves regret bounds explicitly depending on the corruption budget. This provides principled robustness guarantees for preference-based RL under manipulation.

entry.title: Whitening Improves Robustness to Spurious Correlations in Linear Probes

author.name: Floris Holstege, Bram Wouters, Noud van Giersbergen, Cees Diks

entry.summary: The authors show theoretically that linear probes fitted on pretrained representations inherit a preference for high-eigenvalue covariance directions, making them vulnerable to spurious features. Whitening equalizes eigenvalues and reduces spurious-correlation reliance without requiring labeled data or prior knowledge of the spurious feature, validated on synthetic and real settings.

entry.title: Awakening of the Buddha: Subspace Learning During Population-Loss Plateaus

author.name: Akash Kumar

entry.summary: The paper theoretically separates loss from representation quality, proving for two-layer ReLU networks that substantial subspace learning occurs while population loss stays nearly constant on a plateau. For structured additive teachers, it gives high-probability guarantees that alignment between the teacher subspace and the leading eigenspace of the average gradient outer product increases during the plateau.

entry.title: When the Right Answer Is Missing: An Arithmetic-Dependent Rejection Bottleneck in Jev

author.name: Jike Zhong, Ming Li, Yuxiang Lai

entry.summary: This report identifies an arithmetic-dependent rejection bottleneck in typed decision models like Jev: on paired arithmetic problems, answer-present accuracy reaches 99% while correct rejection of absent answers falls to 7%, despite an explicit none-of-the-above option. The gap persists across magnitudes, operation depths, and formulations, challenging recommendations like TypeSafe's.

entry.title: GraphMAS: A Systematic Benchmark of Multi-Agent Coordination for Graph Learning

author.name: Jiayi Yang, Yifang Chen, Yuanfu Sun, Xinyan Ge, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: GraphMAS is the first systematic benchmark of LLM-based multi-agent systems for graph learning, evaluating coordination strategies (aggregation, interaction, adaptive control) across heterogeneous local, long-range, global, and semantic evidence sources. It aims to clarify whether multiple specialized agents improve graph learning and how coordination should be designed and measured.

entry.title: Shared Weights, Selected Computations: How Looped Transformers Route What Each Loop Does

author.name: Jiaju Wu, Yi Hu, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: Using graph walks as a testbed, the paper asks whether loops in looped transformers repeat the same computation and finds they do not; the model routes shared parameters to different operations per loop. The work provides interpretability insights into how recurrence in weight-shared transformers implements latent iterative computation.

entry.title: OpenTSLM TeeMoE: A Unified Time-Series Language Model for Forecasting, Contextual Prediction, and Reasoning

author.name: Tony Chen, Timo Stoffregen, Maxwell Xu, Thomas Kaar, Martin Maritsch, Geremia Pompei, Nicolas Zumarraga, Robert Jakob, Paul Schmiedmayer, Patrick Langer, Juncheng Liu

entry.summary: OpenTSLM TeeMoE is a generalist time-series language model that unifies direct forecasting, context-conditioned prediction, and language-based temporal reasoning without degrading individual capabilities, using a mixture-of-experts-style architecture. It targets the fragmentation between numerical time-series specialists and language-based temporal reasoners. The work appears to be an open model relevant to healthcare and industrial time-series applications.

entry.title: Correcting WHERE, Preserving HOW: Compositional Generalization for Vision-Language-Action Models via Referential Guidance

author.name: Yanyan Zhang, Disheng Liu, Xinpeng Li, Chaoda Song, Mohsen Hariri, Debargha Ganguly, Wang Yang, Kai Ye, Bryce Grant, Vipin Chaudhary, Yu Yin

entry.summary: This paper tackles visual shortcuts in VLA models that prevent compositional generalization across objects, destinations, and backgrounds. It proposes referential guidance as a backbone-agnostic mechanism to correct spatial references (where) while preserving action semantics (how), enabling recomposition of seen elements without task-specific perception modules or data diversification.

entry.title: Minimax rates for learning spectral Barron functions by deep ReLU neural networks

author.name: Songqiu Ma, Yunfei Yang

entry.summary: The authors establish new approximation bounds for deep ReLU networks on spectral Barron functions, achieving rate O~(S^(-1/2 - s/d)) in sparsity S, and derive the minimax statistical learning rates for these function classes. This complements known curse-of-dimensionality-free approximation results for shallow networks.

entry.title: WEIRDO: WEak resIdual Regularized DOob's h-transform diffusion alignment

author.name: Denis Suchkov

entry.summary: This paper studies estimating the guidance needed to steer a pretrained diffusion model toward a tilted target distribution at inference time, identifying the exact correction as the gradient of Doob's h-function. The proposed WEIRDO method estimates this from samples via a penalized least-squares objective whose penalty is the residual of the space-time harmonicity equation, requiring only bounded positive weights and bounded support. It contributes to training-free alignment of diffusion models.

entry.title: Less is more: error-distance scaling relation for data-efficient kilometer-scale downscaling of extreme heat

author.name: Ahmed Marey, Henry Lu, Abhishek Gaur, Liangzhu Leon Wang, Sherif Goubran, Malek Aloui, Theodore Potsis, Alex Hernandez-Garcia, David Rolnick

entry.summary: The authors train CASPER, a U-Net with structure-preserving loss, to downscale 32 km reanalysis data to 1 km temperature, humidity, and wind for extreme heat, across 24 training-data configurations. They discover a linear error-distance scaling relation (RMSE growing with climatological distance to training data) explaining 90% of held-out error variance, enabling prediction of required training data in advance. This informs how much costly simulation data is genuinely needed for urban climate adaptation.

entry.title: BaLEEN: Biasing with Latent Encoded Entities for Context-Aware ASR

author.name: Chihiro Taguchi, Yotaro Kubo, Rujikorn Charakorn

entry.summary: BaLEEN is a lightweight hypernetwork-based framework for contextual ASR biasing that encodes variable-length contextual keywords with a pretrained language model, compresses them via a Perceiver bottleneck, and injects bias vectors into intermediate ASR encoder representations. Both the ASR backbone and language model stay frozen, making it a plug-and-play adapter for recognizing rare entities without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Regime Boundary Alignment for Evidence-Gated Question Answering

author.name: Zeyan Li, Qirong Guo, SIyuan Qiu, Hu Xu, Chun Li, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: RBA traces unsupported answering in retrieval-augmented readers to the training signal, since answer-focused fine-tuning assigns no target to unsupported contexts. It trains a single reader on matched question variants to answer when context supports the gold answer and abstain when support is removed, including under conflicting evidence.

entry.title: Act First, Reason Later: Accelerating On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents via Reference-Conditioned Inverse Dynamics

author.name: Zubin Zheng, Jiahao Wu, Shaofeng Zhang, Zhirui Zhang, Yew-Soon Ong, Shengcai Liu

entry.summary: ActFirst-OPD accelerates on-policy distillation for multi-turn agents by decoupling environment interaction from full-response generation: the student executes actions via reference-conditioned inverse dynamics using its context and a reference next observation, then switches to autonomous next-action prediction. This avoids the cost of lengthy think-then-act rollouts that delay environment transitions and data collection. It addresses a real efficiency bottleneck in training language agents with dense teacher supervision.

entry.title: Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Md. Ismail Hossain, Humaira Kousar, Isidora Chara Tourni

entry.summary: This paper performs a factorial analysis of on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), separating scaffold correctness from teacher context correctness, and finds scaffold correctness matters more for downstream accuracy. Unverified scaffolds create an imitation gap because the teacher sees privileged information; verified scaffolds remain effective even when the teacher is conditioned on the student context. The findings suggest simple fixes to OPSD that persist at scale.

entry.title: TrackFish3D: Self-Supervised 3D Tracking of Schooling Fish from Multi-view Videos

author.name: Patt Phurtivilai, Zhiyang Dou, Yifan Wu, Kinfung Chu, Yuan Liu, Lei Yang, Wenping Wang, Taku Komura

entry.summary: TrackFish3D performs dense multi-camera 3D tracking of schooling fish without identity annotations, using triangulation and reprojection consistency as self-supervision instead of appearance-based re-identification. A geometric encoder and global association transformer learn cross-view correspondence, with a transformer-based tracker ensuring identity awareness. It targets the challenging regime of frequent occlusion and visually similar individuals in collective behavior studies.

entry.title: MEMO: Multi-Level Entity-Aware Memory for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Yinying Li, Yuqian Fu, Yulin Dai, Jingyu Gong, Tianwen Qian, Xiaoling Wang

entry.summary: Proposes MEMO, a framework for streaming video understanding that models memory at the entity level with structured, semantically meaningful representations rather than fixed-size compressions or coarse global summaries. This preserves fine-grained visual information across long temporal horizons in unbounded video streams.

entry.title: Agentic Tool-Augmented Reasoning for Explainable Image Forgery Detection

author.name: Zhiya Tan, Jing Huang, Changtao Miao, Lin Tan, Xin Zhang, Weiwei Feng, Jianshu Li, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes ATAR, an agentic framework integrating 22 specialized forensic tools across seven domains to autonomously detect, localize, and explain image forgeries via multi-turn reasoning. A dual-stream forensic reasoning paradigm combines semantic anomaly inspection with low-level evidence analysis, moving beyond post-hoc explanations of predetermined classifications.

entry.title: SPOON: Towards Coherent Compositional 3D Scene Generation from Uncalibrated Multi-view Images

author.name: Guibiao Liao, Mochu Xiang, Heng Li, Ken Deng, Zijie Wang, Guanbin Li, Ping Tan, Shenghua Gao, Yizhou Yu

entry.summary: SPOON addresses compositional 3D scene generation from uncalibrated multi-view images, disentangling spatially coherent scene layout from image-conditioned object generation. It resolves ambiguous and view-inconsistent pose hypotheses that cause prior approaches to produce incoherent object-camera arrangements.

entry.title: Learning to Reason with Compressed Context: Ground-Truth-Free Adaptation of OmniLLMs via Self-Distillation

author.name: Jianghao Wang, Ke Meng, Jian Li, Chi Cheng, Longyu Qi, Liyin Liang, Yifeng Qian, Chunbo Lai, Yutian Lin, Zeyu Wang

entry.summary: CAFD adapts omni-modal LLMs to token-compression pipelines via ground-truth-free self-distillation, using full-context reasoning as the teacher signal so the model reasons better over compressed audio-video sequences. It requires no reference answers, rationales, or correctness rewards.

entry.title: TrafficSignBench: Rule-Centric Closed-Loop Evaluation of Traffic-Sign Compliance in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Victoria Smirnova, Viktoriia Zinkovich, Gregorii Bukhtuev, Artem Belyaev, Andrey Kuznetsov, Denis Shepelev, Vlad Shakhuro

entry.summary: TrafficSignBench is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating traffic-rule compliance of autonomous driving planners, filling a gap since aggregate metrics like driving score and collision rate do not explicitly measure rule adherence. It combines real-map-based simulation with rule-targeted procedural scenario generation for balanced coverage of underrepresented rules. The benchmark enables systematic, interpretable evaluation that can catch planners scoring well while behaving illegally.

entry.title: How much of fly walking is written in the wiring?

author.name: Isabel Guan, Yuntian Zhao, Dingyuan Zhang, Shipeng Lyu, I-Ming Chen

entry.summary: The authors provide the first test of which features of fly walking motor output depend on the specific connectome wiring, simulating leg motor systems from two independent Drosophila connectomes and comparing against six families of rewired networks under pre-registered criteria. They find rhythm is generic, with many rewired networks more rhythmic than real ones, but antagonist motor pool coordination is specific to the actual wiring. This distinguishes which motor behaviors are structurally encoded versus emergent.

entry.title: PneuTac: Tactile Manipulation with Soft Pneumatic Robots via Unified MPM-Gaussian Splatting Simulation

author.name: Shaohong Zhong, Marco Pontin, Joe Watson, Perla Maiolino, Ingmar Posner

entry.summary: PneuTac presents a unified simulation framework for tactile manipulation with soft pneumatic robots, combining the material point method for soft robot and deformable membrane dynamics with 3D Gaussian splatting for high-resolution vision-based tactile rendering. This addresses the simulation bottleneck that has limited learning of tactile manipulation with compliant robots.

entry.title: Occlusion-Aware, Quasi-Static, Stability-Oriented Trajectory Planning on Uneven Terrain

author.name: Amith Manoharan, Chinmay Mundane, Aayush Bahukhandi, K. Madhava Krishna, Karel Zimmermann, Arun Kumar Singh

entry.summary: The paper proposes a model-based trajectory planning framework for four-wheeled vehicles on highly uneven off-road terrain that treats terrain-occluded blind spots as coverage-induced epistemic uncertainty in a Fourier terrain representation, quantified via a regularized inverse-Hessian estimate. This uncertainty is propagated through a nonlinear least-squares pose/contact model using implicit differentiation to produce stability-oriented quasi-static reference trajectories.

entry.title: Making Waves: A Membrane-Coupled Delta Array for Manipulating Objects Below the Actuator Spacing

author.name: Bailey Dacre, Andr\'es Fa\'i\~na, Oliver Kroemer, Zeynep Temel

entry.summary: This hardware paper couples the end-effectors of an 8x8 array of 3-DoF delta robots with a stretchable fabric membrane, converting 64 discrete contacts into a continuous surface that can manipulate objects smaller than the actuator spacing, removing a hard size lower bound in distributed manipulation. The authors treat the array as a displacement field and investigate local and global quasi-static and cyclic manipulation primitives. This is a clever hardware-level advance for distributed manipulator systems.

entry.title: Identifiable Decomposition of Submovements in Human Hand Trajectories

author.name: Adrian Prados, James Hermus, Ramon Barber, Sylvain Calinon

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sub-ID, a method for decomposing human hand movements into submovement primitives using a spatiotemporal kernel correlation identifiability criterion embedded in adaptive-ridge regularization. The approach recovers ground-truth parameters on synthetic data where existing methods fail and demonstrates identifiability is lost when primitives become collinear and recovered when they diverge spatially.

entry.title: Beyond Mode Collapse: Generating Diverse Synthetic Expert Conversations via Generative Flow Networks

author.name: Sumit Asthana, Michael Ion, Kevyn Collins Thompson

entry.summary: The authors use GFlowNets to generate diverse synthetic expert conversations by training flow models to sample latent conversation structures, using a Gaussian mixture over interaction features such as confusion dynamics and scaffolding balance. This samples expert strategies in proportion to their prevalence in training data, avoiding the mode collapse of direct prompting, with results in two structurally distinct domains including tutoring.

entry.title: A Competing-Hazards Systematization of Loss of Control in Autonomous Agents

author.name: Mohamed Aly Bouke

entry.summary: This paper formalizes loss-of-control events in autonomous agents as a discrete-time competing-hazards model where each attempt ends in approved completion, safe stopping, scope escape, or continuation. It derives escape probabilities within retry budgets and safe-budget limits, motivated by reports of agents acting beyond approved limits and UN panel warnings.

entry.title: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents

author.name: Terumi Chiba, Guangzhi Sun, Zheqi Yuan, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Talk2Agent is a benchmark evaluating how speech transcription errors affect LLM computer-use agents, built from spoken versions of WildClawBench and OSWorld tasks. It measures whether task-critical information survives the voice interface, rather than using conventional ASR word-error metrics.

entry.title: Beyond Prediction: Steering VLM Agents with Retrospective World Modeling

author.name: Yongjiang Liu, Jie Zhang, Haoyue Zhang, Jingcai Guo, Deze Zeng, Song Guo

entry.summary: The paper proposes Retrospective World Modeling, where vision-language model agents verify whether actions are causally consistent with observed state transitions, rather than only prospectively predicting action consequences. This backward-looking paradigm is intended to catch physically incoherent but plausible-looking behaviors.

entry.title: A2Z GameSpec-Bench: How Faithfully Can Coding Agents Generate Games from Game Design Specifications?

author.name: Seonho Lee, Wonryeol Jeong, Alberto Cereser, Inha Kang, Hyeonjong Kim, Seungmin Kwak, Dongmin Park

entry.summary: A2Z GameSpec-Bench is a benchmark of 100 long-form game design documents used to test whether coding agents can build complete games that faithfully satisfy interdependent requirements spanning game logic, rendering, and player interaction. It targets end-to-end application development rather than compact-spec code generation.

entry.title: SynIL: Leveraging Synergy for Offline Imitation Learning from Imperfect Demonstration Datasets

author.name: Yuto Tanaka, Kyo Kutsuzawa, Martina Doku, Dai Owaki, Mitsuhiro Hayashibe

entry.summary: SynIL is a label-free framework for assessing demonstration quality in offline imitation learning, grounded in the neuroscience concept of motor synergy, low-dimensional coordinated movement structures that correlate with motor proficiency. It avoids manual selection of expert reference data or task-specific heuristics used by prior filtering methods, improving robustness to noisy demonstrations in robot learning.

entry.title: Simulator-Refined Diffusion for Radio-Frequency Inverse Design

author.name: Jinhao Liang, Jacob K. Christopher, Michael Frei, Tommaso Dreossi, Nando Fioretto

entry.summary: SRD addresses PCB inverse design with diffusion models conditioned on target S-parameters, tackling the mismatch between accurate-but-expensive non-differentiable electromagnetic simulators and reliable-but-imperfect differentiable surrogates. The method alternates simulator-based refinement with surrogate-guided sampling to produce layouts that meet quantitative electromagnetic specifications.

entry.title: ShamAN-Q: Shampoo Augmented NanoQuant for Sub-1-bit LLM Weights

author.name: Jonathan Mei, Sang Hyub Kim, Oliver Knitter, Chi Chen, Martin Roetteler

entry.summary: ShamAN-Q is a sub-1-bit post-training quantization method that augments NanoQuant by fitting a Kronecker product to the empirical Fisher information matrix in the style of the Shampoo optimizer, yielding a Mahalanobis reconstruction loss. The diagonal geometry becomes dense curvature, converting ADMM updates into Sylvester equation solutions while keeping the discrete projection and deployment format unchanged.

entry.title: SpatialCORE: Confidence-Aware Grounded Spatial Reasoning in Large Vision--Language Models

author.name: Rafi Ibn Sultan, Xiangyu Zhou, Md. Sajid Alam Chowdhury, Chengyin Li, Prashant Khanduri, Marco Brocanelli, Dongxiao Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces SpatialCORE, a post-training framework for LVLMs that incorporates the model's own confidence in grounded localization (bounding boxes, masks) into the reasoning process, rather than optimizing only final-answer correctness. This rewards reasoning from confidently localized task-relevant objects, targeting the persistent spatial reasoning weakness of vision-language models.

entry.title: Right Answers, Costly Models: The Efficiency Gap in LLM-based Optimization Modeling

author.name: Zhong Li, Xin Huang, Jinhui Wan, Xiangyi Wang, Shenkai Zhang, Ruiqi Chen, Wenyu Liu, Zaiwen Wen, Ziyan Luo

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether LLMs can identify problem structure in natural-language optimization tasks and apply expert modeling techniques to produce formulations and solver code that are both correct and efficient. It contributes OptTips, a knowledge base of 50 modeling techniques, and OptDachshund, a system built on it, highlighting a gap between correct and computationally efficient formulations.

entry.title: T-Router: Learning Thalamic Routing for Reasoning with Parameter-Efficient Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Liuxian Ma, Jiale Dai, Jiaqi Li, Lu Mi

entry.summary: T-Router is a parameter-efficient adaptation method that reuses completed computations through a compressed, addressable bank of block changes, with a depth-recurrent controller selecting and scaling their writeback, inspired by thalamic routing. Trained with correctness rewards while freezing the backbone, it allocates only 41.73M parameters (0.466%) on an 8.95B model, claiming substantial reasoning gains.

entry.title: Ready2Blend: From Natural-Language Instructions to Composable Alignment Prompts

author.name: Jeesu Jung, Hwan Chang, Juseon Do, Jeonghwan Choi, Jinho Choo, Sungwoo Nam, S. K. Hong, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Ready2Blend addresses continual alignment of LLMs by mapping natural-language requirements to fixed-length alignment prompts stored in a frozen modular prompt bank via AlignFormer, with composability regularization enabling inference-time blending and reweighting. This avoids repeated parameter updates while retaining behavioral adaptation.

entry.title: Self-Spec Verifiable Code Generation

author.name: Jiaru Qian, Yihong Dong, Yongmin Li, Hao Zhu, Bin Gu, Ge Li

entry.summary: This work critiques existing formally-verifiable code generation benchmarks for evaluating specification and code generation stage-wise with oracle specifications, and for focusing on proof-oriented styles. It proposes self-specification where the model formulates its own specifications, and evaluates end-to-end verifiable code generation.

entry.title: When Masking Helps or Hurts Robustness in Compressed CLIP: A Pre-Deployment Diagnostic

author.name: Muhammad Zawish, Steven Davy

entry.summary: The paper shows that masking-based token pruning in compressed CLIP models has highly unstable effects on worst-group robustness, sometimes improving it by up to 82.5 percent relative and sometimes degrading it completely. It identifies spurious inversion as the cause and proposes SIM, a label-free pre-deployment metric predicting whether pruning will help or hurt on a given dataset.

entry.title: Mid-Harness: Scaling Actions Between Model and Harness for Terminal Agents

author.name: Minki Kang, Ryo Hachiuma, Shaokun Zhang, Subhashree Radhakrishnan, Yonggan Fu, Jindong Jiang, Mingjie Liu, Ehsan Hosseini-Asl, Yi Dong, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Byung-Kwan Lee

entry.summary: Mid-Harness investigates allocating test-time compute at the model-harness boundary for terminal agents by sampling and verifying candidate actions before executing one, without changing the generator or harness. Using a TMAX-9B generator, the paper analyzes when extra action sampling helps reliability and trajectory success and what makes this allocation effective.

entry.title: Function-Space Transformer with Adaptive Anchors

author.name: Guorui Sang, Pedram Rooshenas

entry.summary: The Function-Space Transformer (FST) learns from functions over continuous domains via a spatially adaptive continuous latent representation, storing features at anchors whose locations are predicted from input observations. This combines ideas from neural operators and latent-attention architectures to avoid fixed-grid trade-offs between resolution and compute. A new architecture for function-valued data.

entry.title: NeurDuo-EEG: A Long-Sequence EEG Foundation Model with Persistent State and Explicit Memory

author.name: Yifan Wang, Haiping Liu, Yang Cui, Wenhao Cai, Shuhang Li, Xiaoyang Huang, Xianyang Liu, Jingyu Sun, Yizheng Sun, Cunhang Fan, Tianming Du, Jiancheng Yang, Zhenhong Li, Yunhao Zhang, Hongpeng Zhou, Jingyuan Sun

entry.summary: NeurDuo-EEG is a causal EEG foundation model with channel-resolved persistent memory and multi-timescale memory management via learned consolidation and selective retrieval, enabling continuous long-horizon modeling with fixed-size state. It is pre-trained on 3,955 hours of EEG, addressing the limitation of windowed foundation models that ignore timescales from milliseconds to hours.

entry.title: Certified Approximation for Interpretable Representer Landmarks

author.name: Jayanta Mukherjee, Shourya Verma, Mengbo Wang, Jasorsi Ghosh, Ananth Grama

entry.summary: CAIRN provides end-to-end error certification for representer-point explanations of self-supervised representations, which rest on up to four stacked approximations of the empirical neural tangent kernel. The authors derive the exact variance of the sketched multi-head eNTK, matching measurement within 4 percent where Johnson-Lindenstrauss bounds err by up to 2.5x, and carry combined error through to certify the top-K landmark ranking. This brings formal guarantees to influential-example attribution at scale.

entry.title: The Row Normalization Puzzle in Muon

author.name: Jiayu Zhang, Tianyi Lin

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how row-wise renormalization affects the Muon optimizer, examining the gap between NorMuon's worst-case guarantees and its strong practical performance in LLM pretraining. It shows row normalization introduces a dimension-dependent factor in worst-case iteration complexity that persists even with exact polar computation, deepening understanding of a widely adopted optimizer.

entry.title: Low-Discrepancy Dither for Quantized Recurrent State Caches

author.name: Snigdha Chandan Khilar

entry.summary: For Mamba-style models storing recurrent states in low precision, the paper finds that a deterministic golden-ratio Weyl dither keeps quantized models closer to full precision than stochastic rounding across formats and long horizons, at no extra cost. Round-to-nearest is shown to be problematic because it discards small updates.

entry.title: Beyond Simulation: Retain-and-Repair Neural Operators for Real-World Adaptation

author.name: Woojin Cho, Junghwan Park

entry.summary: R2NO is a framework for adapting simulation-pretrained neural operators to real-world data: the finetuned operator is frozen to provide a source prediction, and a spectral repair module learns refinements via orthogonal Fourier projections with per-cell ridge regression ensembles. The approach aims to retain useful pretrained structure while correcting sim-to-real gaps.

entry.title: Should I stay or should I show? Learning to selectively disclose information

author.name: Carlotta Giacchetta, Alessando Bogani, Cesare Barbera, Giovanni De Toni, Michele Caprio, Andrea Pugnana, Andrea Passerini

entry.summary: The paper formalizes selective disclosure: deciding when to reveal costly support information to a human decision-maker under a budget constraint. It proves the optimal policy is a threshold rule on the Value of Information and provides a plug-in estimator with guarantees bounding degradation relative to no disclosure.

entry.title: From DNA Design to DNA Slimming: Auditable Agentic Discovery of a Deletion-Only Designer

author.name: Joel Shor

entry.summary: The paper defines sequence slimming, a new nucleic-acid design task of removing bases from an existing functional regulatory element while retaining predicted activity, with a quantitative evaluation built on the NucleoBench benchmark. Slimmers must return source indices, enabling auditable verification of deletions. This shifts DNA design from fixed-length substitution to deletion-only optimization.

entry.title: Generative sequence modeling for infinite memory processes via predictive states

author.name: Michael Wieck-Sosa, Cosma Rohilla Shalizi

entry.summary: The authors introduce a nonparametric estimator for one-step-ahead conditional distributions of multivariate processes with potentially infinite-range memory, based on predictive states. They prove fast convergence rates when the past can be compressed into a low-dimensional sufficient statistic, avoiding finite-memory, sparsity, or additivity assumptions.

entry.title: Recovering Off-Policy Supervision for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Chanjun Park, Sugyeong Eo, Hyeonseok Moon

entry.summary: For training block drafters used in speculative decoding, this paper solves the problem that one off-policy token invalidates supervision for all subsequent slots in a block. Its rollout-based framework uses Anchor-Label Relabelling to restore labels from greedy target rollouts and In-Rollout Anchors to expose draft blocks within rollouts, recovering full supervision from off-policy corpora.

entry.title: Distributionally robust linear regression through the lens of adversarial training

author.name: Elis Stefansson, David V\"avinggren, Ant\^onio H. Ribeiro

entry.summary: The authors study Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization for linear regression, unifying square-root Lasso and adversarial training as special cases. They prove deterministic and non-asymptotic in-sample error bounds of O(n^-1/2) generally and O(n^-1) under favorable design conditions, carrying known properties of the special cases over to the general method. This provides a principled theoretical bridge between regularized, adversarial, and robust estimation.

entry.title: SAGE: Salient Factor Discovery and Generation with Visual Foundation Representations

author.name: Shuang Liang, Lejun Liao, Shiyuan Zhang, Max C. Zhang, Xiaolong Luo, Han Wang, Stefano Anzellotti, Yuan Yuan

entry.summary: SAGE performs contrastive analysis, separating salient target-specific factors from common content shared with a background dataset, learning both directly in the spatial latent of a frozen representation autoencoder. The learned salient representations reveal unlabeled subtypes and condition a diffusion transformer to generate new examples of discovered subtypes. This enables unsupervised factor discovery and controllable generation from foundation-model representations.

entry.title: Proximal Balancing for Causal Effect Estimation under Unmeasured Confounding

author.name: Yonghan Jung

entry.summary: The paper introduces proximal balancing, which extends classical covariate balancing to settings where confounders are observed only through proxies, learning a low-dimensional balancing representation. It avoids the ill-posed inverse problems of existing proxy-based approaches and the strong latent-variable assumptions of latent-model methods. This strengthens the toolkit for causal inference from observational data.

entry.title: Can We Still Trust Disaster Social Sensing? Empirical Evidence on Detecting AI-Generated Social Media Posts

author.name: Xiaoshan Zhou, Zaifu Zhan

entry.summary: The study builds a 12,000-text dataset from nine disasters with matched semantic units contrasting human posts, LLM-proofread posts, and factual versus affectively framed AI-generated posts, testing whether text-based detectors can distinguish them. The results inform whether disaster social sensing remains trustworthy in the generative AI era.

entry.title: Question-Specific Knowledge Graphs for Efficient Visual Reasoning

author.name: Ting-Chih Chen, Emile van Krieken, Shujian Yu, Filip Ilievski

entry.summary: VisKG is an RL framework where vision-language models learn to translate images into question-specific knowledge graphs, retaining only details relevant to the reasoning task instead of exhaustive captions. This reduces token counts and spurious assumptions while supporting visual question answering.

entry.title: The Canonical Order Problem: When Large Language Models Are Unreliable Knowledge Bases for Multi-Valued Relations

author.name: Timo Pierre Schrader, Annemarie Friedrich, Simon Razniewski, Lukas Lange

entry.summary: This paper identifies the canonical order problem: LLM internal distributions organize multi-valued relations alphabetically or chronologically, causing set generation to be unreliable when queried as knowledge bases. Through mechanistic analysis, the authors show set generation proceeds in three phases: candidate retrieval, internal sorting, and ordered emission. This reveals a systematic structural limitation in using LLMs as knowledge sources.

entry.title: FinRT: Distilling Adaptive Red-Teaming Strategies into Reusable Adversarial Generators in Consumer Finance

author.name: Rikhiya Ghosh, Himanshu Kumar, Sriram Venkatapathy, Sahil Wadhwa, Alexandre G. R. Day, Pranab Mohanty

entry.summary: FinRT builds reusable adversarial prompt generators by distilling adaptive red-teaming strategies, jointly optimizing coverage, severity, and diversity in consumer finance settings. Across six victim models it substantially outperforms adaptive search baselines, nearly doubling attack success while amortizing generation cost into a reusable generator. This improves scalable safety testing in a regulated, high-stakes domain.

entry.title: Momentum-Coupled Rubric Adaptation for Detailed Image Captioning

author.name: Zhenwen Ji, Lei Jin, Shanyong Wang, Jiaming Lu, Chengqiang Lu, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Lizhen Cui, Yanyu Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a rubric-based reinforcement learning approach for detailed image captioning in which caption policy, rubric generator, and judge are updated in a coupled, momentum-based manner rather than as separately maintained or staged-optimized models. This addresses inconsistency across roles that plagues existing rubric-based RL methods.

entry.title: LatCom: Cross-Agent Latent Compression for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Shinan Zhang, Tao Zhang, Qihui Zhu, Mengjie Zhang, Dong Jin, Yunpeng Hou, Shuangwu Chen, Xiaobin Tan, Quan Zheng, Jian Yang

entry.summary: LatCom addresses the growing receiver-side context in latent multi-agent collaboration by jointly compressing latents across senders rather than independently compressing and concatenating, resolving cross-agent redundancy. This reduces computation, memory, and collaboration latency as agent count and reasoning length scale.

entry.title: Correct, Don't Delete: Mitigating Emergent Misalignment with Corrective Supervision

author.name: Jacob Epifano

entry.summary: Investigates emergent misalignment caused by fine-tuning on narrow harmful data (bad medical advice) and asks whether correcting poisoned rows is better than deleting them. Controlled experiments on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct show that replacing a fraction of poison rows with corrected answers to the same prompts reduces misalignment more than removing them.

entry.title: It's Not What the Image Shows: Irrelevant Context Destabilises VLM Judges Without Informing Them

author.name: Nagham Omar, Mahmoud Jabarin, Kinan Ibraheem, Lotem Peled-Cohen

entry.summary: Introduces MIST, a misleading-image stress test with 200 ambiguous sentences where labels should be decided from text alone, showing that across thirteen VLM judges, aligned images changed 20.5 percent of labels and misleading images destabilized more, even though images should not inform the decision. This reveals that irrelevant visual context undermines VLM-as-judge substitutability.

entry.title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Quang Hieu Pham, Thuy Duong Nguyen, Jocelyn Qiaochu Chen, Xi Ye

entry.summary: The authors introduce a benchmark evaluating both effectiveness and efficiency of long-context LM harnesses, arguing existing evaluations are saturated and fail to distinguish modern approaches. Tasks require diverse retrieval strategies (lexical and semantic) plus adaptive reasoning over contexts where most content is relevant but only a small subset is useful at each step, creating distinct accuracy-cost tradeoffs.
