This adapt-then-steer strategy avoids training a truck VLA from scratch while handling geometry and dynamics differences.

entry.title: LBDU-VIO: Learned Bias Dynamics and Uncertainty for Visual-Inertial Odometry with Unreliable Vision

author.name: Qizhi Guo, Junning Lyu, Defu Lin, Shaoming He

entry.summary: LBDU-VIO is a learning-augmented multi-state constraint Kalman filter for visual-inertial odometry that replaces random-walk bias assumptions with a neural ODE modeling continuous-time bias dynamics and predicts motion-adaptive IMU measurement noise covariances. These learned components improve filter robustness for aerial robots when visual information is unreliable.

entry.title: Decode-Latency Feedback Prefill: A Model-Free Controller and Its Generalization Limits

author.name: Gaurav Agarwal, Ashish Garg, Isha Singhal

entry.summary: DLFP is a model-free controller for concurrent LLM inference that resizes prefill chunks based on observed decode-latency feedback, reducing interference where prefilling a new long prompt delays tokens for requests already decoding. Implemented in vLLM and evaluated with open-loop Poisson arrivals, exact token accounting, and NVIDIA telemetry, the paper also explicitly documents its generalization limits.

entry.title: Where Scientific Search Agents Fail: Decision-Checkpoint Auditing of Exposure and Inspection Attempts

author.name: Hongmin Li, Wanli Zhao

entry.summary: This work introduces decision checkpoints that record an agent's observations and tool actions during inference, enabling attribution of failure to never encountering a target paper, failing to inspect it, or inspecting without using it. Applied to 540 AutoResearchBench Deep questions, the audit reveals that keyword search improves accuracy over raw search but also increases incorrect answers after the target was exposed. It offers a finer-grained diagnostic lens than final-answer accuracy.

entry.title: GraphCert: Bootstrap Agentic Graph Reasoning with Certified Evidence Rubrics

author.name: Weiqi Jiang, Yuchen Ying, Rui Wang, Kaixuan Chen, Bingde Hu, Shunyu Liu, Yu Wang, Tongya Zheng

entry.summary: GraphCert bootstraps training data for agentic graph reasoning using a Bootstrapped Graph Quizzer that generates graph-grounded QA pairs with certified evidence rubrics, avoiding costly manual trajectory collection and the privacy risk of exposing sensitive graph data to proprietary LLMs. It addresses supervision scalability for graph agents. The certified evidence framing supports verifiable multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Reserve-Aware Contrast Certificates for Conservative Bandits with Uncertain Baselines

author.name: Qinchuan Cheng

entry.summary: Reserve-C4B improves conservative bandits by bounding the baseline-relative contrast directly instead of separately bounding candidate and baseline rewards, which double-charges shared estimation error. It includes a reserve ledger separating evidence from permitted deficit, a prefix-refresh extension, and self-normalized confidence sets for simultaneous validity with linear rewards.

entry.title: DualCast: A Dual-Path Language Model for Bimodal Financial Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Wentao Zhao, Hongqiang Wu, Shanghang Liu, Zhaochen Zan, Yu Zhang, Biqing Huang

entry.summary: DualCast extends a frozen Qwen3-8B language model with a learned discrete financial vocabulary for forecasting across heterogeneous assets plus news. It represents return patches via summary and residual shape tokens and introduces adaptive frequency-equalizing residual vector quantization to improve codebook utilization, training only new embeddings and heads on the frozen backbone. This is an efficient approach to bimodal financial forecasting.

entry.title: Policy-Conditioned AI-Use Detection: An Evidentiary Framework for Academic Publishing

author.name: Jairo Diaz-Rodriguez, Mumin Jia

entry.summary: The authors argue that AI detection targeting whether a model wrote text is misaligned with what conferences and journals need to decide, and propose policy-conditioned AI-use detection, an evidentiary framework that treats the governing AI-use policy as an explicit input and reports calibrated hypotheses and uncertainty rather than verdicts. Benchmarks are built from reproducible workflows.

entry.title: Security-Enhanced Seed-Based Weight Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Qiuyu Ren, Sudipta Paria, Aritra Dasgupta, Swarup Bhunia

entry.summary: Seed-Q is a sensitivity-aware, seed-based weight compression framework for LLMs that uses LFSR-based pseudo-random weight generation with non-uniform bit allocation, giving more representation budget to sensitive weights without requiring side information. It targets storage, memory bandwidth, and energy costs while adding a security dimension to compression.

entry.title: Towards Universal Wasserstein Barycenters through Flow Matching

author.name: Eduardo Fernandes Montesuma

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Universal Barycenter Approximation over the Wasserstein simplex and proposes BaryFM, a flow-matching model that transports marginal measures into any weighted Wasserstein barycenter, allowing sampling from barycenters via an ODE after training. This generalizes fixed-weight barycenter computation to the whole weight simplex.

entry.title: Uncovering Uncontrolled Repetition through Residual Stream Dynamics

author.name: Yuanhe Zhang, Xinyao Zhou, Haoran Gao, Yuyao Zhang, Zhenhong Zhou, Fanyu Meng, Li Sun, Sen Su

entry.summary: Investigates how uncontrolled repetition, which can prolong LLM generation and enable resource consumption attacks, emerges in large vision-language models. The proposed Tokenwise Residual Comparison (TRC) method identifies and localizes repetition-related anomalies in residual stream dynamics during generation, extending prior feature-based analyses to earlier layers.

entry.title: CellMSA: Context Modeling for Single-Cell Representation Learning

author.name: Suyuan Zhao, Minghao Liu, Yizhen Luo, Zaiqing Nie

entry.summary: CellMSA argues that single-cell foundation models should exploit relational information across batches and cell types rather than encoding cells independently, using cross-cell consistency and variation to capture gene-gene dependencies tied to cell states. The proposed attention-based context modeling improves representation quality under sparsity and batch effects.

entry.title: HO-FL: Hybrid-Order Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Edge Devices

author.name: Qiyuan Chen, Xian Wu, Yanan Ma, Xianhao Chen

entry.summary: HO-FL hybridizes zeroth-order and first-order optimization in federated learning, training the bottom segment of a model with ZO and the top with FO so memory-constrained devices can pick their order boundary while training one global model. The convergence analysis reveals a new trade-off where favoring clients with larger FO segments improves update accuracy but underrepresents others. It tackles a practical fairness-efficiency tension in edge FL.

entry.title: HiWE: Hierarchical World Knowledge Model with Visual Keypoint Enhancement for Zero-Shot 3D Path Planning

author.name: Guoqing Ma, Mingqi Yuan, Chen Gao, Jiayu Chen, Shan Yu

entry.summary: HiWE connects visual grounding and language-based planning for robot demonstration generation through a point-based interface: a PointVLM associates task-relevant objects with image coordinates, depth lifts these into semantic 3D, and a 3DLLM planner specifies end-effector waypoints and gripper commands with a hybrid grasping module. Evaluation covers 100 tasks in a zero-shot setting.

entry.title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Time Series

author.name: Lucas Poinsignon, Jorge da Silva Gon\c{c}alves, Samuel Ruip\'erez-Campillo, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: This paper proposes generating multivariate time series via flow matching in the wavelet domain, operating on multilevel discrete wavelet coefficients to represent coarse and fine temporal structure at separate scales. The differing variances across scales induce a coarse-to-fine generative process, paired with a cross-channel modeling component.

entry.title: SEPAL: Separated Expert Pairs with Answer-Level Fusion for Reliable LLM Collaboration

author.name: Weijie Ren, Yanwen Zhang, Hao Li, Zhuolin Qi, Hengyi Zhang, Naibo Wang

entry.summary: SEPAL is a multi-agent LLM collaboration framework that assigns three private Actor-Critic teams to reasoning, evidence grounding, and verification, with role-specific training so teams develop different reasoning objectives. By keeping feedback within teams and fusing answers only at the majority-vote level, it avoids the error-coupling problem of shared discussion while retaining refinement benefits.

entry.title: Fenchel Tilting: Weighted Correction for Efficient Finetuning of Generative Models

author.name: Maksim Bobrin, Maksim Zhdanov, Dmitry Dylov

entry.summary: FTFC (Fenchel Tilt Flow Control) decouples utility optimization from generative-model fitting for adapting pretrained generative models to arbitrary utility functions. It jointly fits an effective reward and density-ratio weights on pretrained samples using variational structure and Fenchel duality, aiming to support general preferences without the usual efficiency-generalization tradeoff in fine-tuning.

entry.title: Learning Skills from Historical Action Trajectories: Action Experience Dictionary for World Action Models

author.name: Qi Lyu, Jiahua Dong, Hao Shen, Xudong Wang, Hongyuan Yu, Baichen Liu, Henghui Ding, Zhi Han, Nicu Sebe, Ivan Laptev, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Salman Khan

entry.summary: This paper proposes an Action Experience Dictionary (AED) for World Action Models, encoding historical physical action trajectories into shared embeddings to enable cross-task skill reuse in manipulation. Retrieved action embeddings guide target action prediction while suppressing interference from redundant background visual elements. Builds on the growing world-model-for-robotics line of work.

entry.title: RetroGEF: Dynamic Graph Edit Flow for Single-Step Retrosynthesis

author.name: Xiaozhuang Song, Xuemin Chen, Xinjian Zhao, Yaoyao Xu, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: RetroGEF is a flow-based generative model for single-step retrosynthesis that constructs reactants from a target molecule by adding atoms and changing bonds in the molecular graph. Crucially, it models molecular transformations and changes in graph size within a single generative process, addressing cases where reactant components absent from the product must be introduced.

entry.title: K2P: Label-Free Knowledge to Prompt Distillation

author.name: Yingchuan Zhang, Haoran Lu, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: K2P distills a stronger teacher's reasoning into reusable prompts for a frozen student without ground-truth labels, addressing the problem that agreement with unverified teacher solutions can reward shared mistakes. It synthesizes instructions from teacher solutions, refines them using paired teacher-student responses, and selects candidates on reserved questions, deploying only the frozen student and selected prompt. The work separates generation and selection roles theoretically and practically.

entry.title: RW-Flow: One-Step Generation on Compact Manifolds via Wasserstein Gradient Flows

author.name: Ualibyek Nurgulan, Seungwoo Yoo, Prin Phunyaphibarn, Minhyuk Sung

entry.summary: RW-Flow is a theoretically grounded framework for one-step generative models on compact manifolds (geospatial locations, torsion angles) built on Wasserstein gradient flows, resolving the identifiability challenge of ensuring zero velocity field implies target matching. This cuts sampling from tens or hundreds of network evaluations to one.

entry.title: How Many Samples Are Enough for Learning Across Domains?

author.name: Hong Zheng

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes criteria for per-domain sample sufficiency in multi-domain learning, deriving an inverse linear scaling law between the number of training domains and samples required per domain. The results explain when adding domains versus adding samples improves generalization under distribution shift.

entry.title: Decoupled and Distilled: Task-Adaptive LoRA-Teachers with Ensemble Knowledge Transfer for Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Hongwei Zhao (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University), Rui Liu (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University), Yansong Liu (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University), Zhiyuan Zou (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University), Yong Chen (School of Computer Science, Beijing University of Posts, Telecommunications)

entry.summary: TALON is an inference-efficient framework for few-shot class-incremental learning that allocates an independent LoRA-Teacher per incremental task, then distills the frozen ensemble into a single unified LoRA-Student. This avoids unreliable strict gradient constraints under data scarcity and the inference cost of multi-expert approaches.

entry.title: Graph Residual Conjugate Diffusion: SNR-Equalized Heat Flow for Graph Signals

author.name: Jinwei Li, Daniel Tenbrinck

entry.summary: GRCD improves diffusion models on graph-supported signals by replacing the shared diffusion clock of isotropic graph heat diffusion with a mode-dependent clock that equalizes terminal signal-to-noise ratios across graph-frequency modes. This reduces the noise range that must be traversed under a fixed sampling budget for spectrally nonuniform data like traffic and sensor signals.

entry.title: Learning to Explain While Planning: Rule-Aligned Diffusion Planning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiaxi Ye

entry.summary: The paper proposes a rule-aligned diffusion planner for autonomous driving that explicitly models driving rules rather than only fitting expert trajectory distributions, improving long-tail safety where demonstration data is scarce. It also produces rule-level explanations of when and how strongly rules influence trajectory adjustments.

entry.title: PMosFM: Preconditioned Manifold Matching for One-Step Physics-Constrained Generation

author.name: Zhangyong Liang, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: PMosFM enables one-step physics-constrained generative modeling by encoding constraints in a manifold decoder so transport is learned in intrinsic coordinates, avoiding costly iterative corrections, residual losses, or trajectory unrolling. A geometric preconditioner rescales the learning dynamics to respect the constraint manifold. This reduces both sampling and training costs for physics-constrained generation of physical fields.

entry.title: Lower Bounds for Linear-Oracle Online Learning

author.name: Mohit Sinha

entry.summary: The paper proves a conjecture by Weibel et al. that fixed-coefficient methods cannot improve on the T^(3/4) regret rate of online Frank-Wolfe on general convex sets, extending the lower bound to every deterministic learner in an oracle-only model. It constructs explicit hard instances achieving regret at least on the order of L D b^(-1/4) T^(3/4).

entry.title: A Pre-trained Variational Autoencoder for Gyrokinetic Plasma Turbulence Surrogate Modeling

author.name: Minglei Yang, Marshall Nicholson, Diego Del-Castillo-Negrete, David Hatch, Guannan Zhang

entry.summary: PreVAE-Turb fine-tunes the pre-trained VAE from Stable Diffusion for spatial compression of plasma turbulence fields, adding a physics-informed Fourier-space spectral loss, and pairs it with ConvLSTM networks for latent dynamics with an encode-decode consistency metric during autoregressive rollout. This accelerates gyrokinetic plasma turbulence simulation.

entry.title: Sharp Statistical Rates for Asynchronous TD Learning with Markovian Data

author.name: Yang Peng

entry.summary: The paper proves high-probability sup-norm last-iterate bounds for tabular temporal-difference learning from a single Markovian trajectory, achieving error epsilon with roughly H^3/(mu_min * eps^2) plus mixing-time transitions. The rates hold for both tuned constant step sizes and target-independent decreasing schedules.

entry.title: Mitigating Representation Gaps in Amortized Bayesian Inference with Auxiliary Supervision

author.name: Hans Olischl\"ager, Svenja Jedhoff, \v{S}imon Kucharsk\'y, Aayush Mishra, Stefan T. Radev, Paul B\"urkner

entry.summary: The authors propose generic auxiliary guidance losses that improve training dynamics in amortized Bayesian inference, where neural networks learn to map datasets to posterior approximations. The approach reduces avoidable representation gaps that normally require problem-specific fixes under finite simulation and compute budgets. This improves the practical reliability of simulation-based inference.

entry.title: PINNing the pion: conformal deep learning for $F_\pi(s)$ and the $(g-2)_\mu$ hadronic contribution

author.name: Mayank Goel, Subhadip Mitra, Monalisa Patra

entry.summary: The authors build a physics-informed neural network embedded in a conformal z-plane to construct the pion electromagnetic form factor from first principles, enforcing charge normalization, Schwarz reflection, analyticity, dispersion relations, Watson's theorem, and perturbative QCD asymptotics by construction or via the loss. This reduces model dependence compared to phenomenological curve fitting. The application targets the hadronic contribution to the muon g-2, a key quantity in precision particle physics.

entry.title: Efficient Expert-Parallel Communication on PCIe-Connected Consumer GPUs

author.name: Jaehwan Lee, Sangmin Lee, Chaewon Kim, Junsik Shin, Jaejin Lee

entry.summary: The paper addresses expert-parallel communication overhead for Mixture-of-Experts inference on PCIe-connected consumer GPUs, where existing EP libraries assume direct GPU-to-GPU access and NCCL's CPU-staged transfers incur redundant PCIe traffic. The authors design a communication scheme tailored to this hardware constraint, reducing inference latency as expert activation counts grow. This democratizes MoE serving on consumer hardware.

entry.title: Beyond the Context Window: An Adaptive Entropy-Based Routing Framework for Hybrid Retrieval and Long-Context Language Models

author.name: Isaac Olufadewa, Miracle Adesina, Ezekiel Oladejo, Owen Adeniyi, Fadare Fadekemi, Olamide Oso, Uthman Babatunde, Matthew Olawoyin

entry.summary: EDAR routes each query at inference time between answering from retrieved chunks and escalating to full long-context processing, using predictive entropy over the token distribution on retrieved evidence. The framework targets the trade-off between expensive long-context processing and retrieval errors from partially relevant chunks.

entry.title: FastGuide: Accelerating Reward Guidance for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Darshan Thaker, Lachlan Ewen MacDonald, Ren\'e Vidal

entry.summary: FastGuide accelerates gradient-based reward guidance for masked diffusion LLMs by adaptively hybridizing parallel and autoregressive decoding, amortizing reward model backpropagation across multiple tokens per step. This reduces the otherwise prohibitive inference-time cost of controlling diffusion LMs with reward models. It is a meaningful efficiency contribution to an emerging model class.

entry.title: Memory Consolidation Flattens the Temporal Shape of User Facts

author.name: Sugam Panthi, Muhaiminul Yeamin, Siyan Luo, Rabab Abdelfattah

entry.summary: The authors identify aspectual flattening: memory-writing systems convert temporally marked user statements like an ongoing activity into timeless facts, losing cues about whether information still holds. They introduce LAPSE, a benchmark of matched statements differing only in temporal form, showing selective flattening across 11 model configurations and deployed pipelines including mem0, Graphiti, and Letta. The lost cue demonstrably harms later retrieval and reasoning.

entry.title: VAA-CSEC: Vote-guided Advantage Allocation for Chinese Semantic Error Correction

author.name: Yitong Han, Nankai Lin, Juan Luo, Hongyan Wu, Lianxi Wang, Shengyi Jiang

entry.summary: VAA-CSEC is a multi-stage framework for Chinese semantic error correction combining CoT distillation, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning with a task-specific vote-guided reward, and self-consistency decoding, targeting over-correction and the unreliable transfer of CoT benefits to final corrections. It addresses a relatively underexplored task beyond spelling and grammar errors.

entry.title: The Rashomon Wikipedia: A Data-Perspectivist Analysis of Divergent Historical Narratives

author.name: Claudiu Creanga, Liviu P. Dinu, Anca Dinu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes cross-lingual historiographical bias in Wikipedia language editions (Romanian, Hungarian, Russian, Turkish, English) around three contested Romanian historical events, using human annotators and LLMs to classify citation stance and track narrative evolution from 2005 to 2024. It identifies citation isolation, where language editions cite largely disjoint sources and sustain divergent narratives.

entry.title: Orthogonal Yet Coupled: Decoupling Geometric Components for Model Merging

author.name: Zijing Wang, Yongkang Liu, Mingyang Wang, Ercong Nie, Mengjie Zhao, Yunpu Ma, Kang Liu, Zihan Wang, Shi Feng, Daling Wang, Hinrich Sch\"utze

entry.summary: Identifies cross-component coupling as a problem in model merging: existing methods treat task vectors as indivisible units, so geometric characteristics of one component influence how another is merged. Proposes DiGA, a disentangled geometry-aware merging framework that uses pretrained weights as a shared geometric reference to merge components separately.

entry.title: Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue

author.name: Shengbo Cai, Yuxiang Wang, Jingran Xie, Zhisheng Zhang, Shun Lei, Di Cao, Teddy Sun, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: Introduces LoopSLM, which uses looped Transformers for latent reasoning in empathetic spoken dialogue, refining hidden states with acoustic grounding at each pass rather than relying on explicit chain-of-thought that adds latency and may miss acoustic cues. Two-stage training separates learning to reason from learning to respond, narrowing the perception-reasoning gap for paralinguistic cues.

entry.title: One Threshold Does Not Fit All Languages: Language-Conditional Deferral for Reliable and Efficient Low-Resource Text Classification

author.name: Bhanu Prakash Vangala, Vangala Navya

entry.summary: Shows that split conformal prediction with a single confidence threshold pooled across languages fails to deliver its error guarantee to every language in multilingual low-resource settings, testing on MasakhaNEWS across 16 African languages. Proposes language-conditional deferral so that per-language error budgets are honored on CPU-only deployments typical of the Global South.

entry.title: Gender bias across LLMs is common and highly heterogeneous

author.name: Edoardo Bolzoni, Valerio Capraro

entry.summary: This audit examines gender bias across ten LLMs from nine vendors released between April 2025 and June 2026, using two paradigms: gender attribution of stereotyped phrases and moral judgment of abuse or torture scenarios. Results show biases are common but highly heterogeneous, with some models attributing masculine-stereotyped phrases to female writers more often than the reverse and others showing the opposite pattern. The breadth of models and vendors makes this a useful longitudinal snapshot of bias in deployed systems.

entry.title: VehicleArena: A Realistic Urban Environment for Multi-Agent Driving

author.name: Jie Yang, Jiajun Chen, Jiazheng Zhou, Mianqiu Huang, Yining Zheng, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: VehicleArena is a 3D urban-driving benchmark where LLM-controlled agents pursue independent passenger-transport objectives in a shared dynamic world, with each agent's decisions reshaping traffic flow, delays, and risk for others. Unlike prior benchmarks assuming shared goals or prescribed protocols, it targets emergent physical coupling among independently operating agents, providing 112 evaluation tasks. It addresses an underexplored gap in multi-agent LLM evaluation.

entry.title: Fisher-IRG: Fisher-Induced Local Invariant Representation Geometry across Language and Vision Models

author.name: Abdullah All Tanvir, Xin Zhong

entry.summary: Fisher-IRG defines a local metric on learned representations based on predictive sensitivity: it builds semantic-preserving and semantic-changing neighborhoods, aggregates local Fisher information, and recovers invariant directions via a contrastive generalized eigenvalue problem. The method shows that comparable Euclidean motion can have very different predictive consequences across both language and vision models. This offers a principled, modality-general lens on which representation changes actually matter.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Selective LLM Answering by Pricing Label-Free Checks

author.name: Dongyub Jude Lee, Jungseob Lee, Chanjun Park, Hyeonseok Moon, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: PriceCheck builds a compact family of decision rules from label-free checks (such as re-solving a problem), assigning each a price derived from agreement rates on correct and incorrect answers plus run cost. Prices fitted on a small class-enriched labelled set compose into predictions of a schedule's coverage and cost, and a calibration test selects a schedule meeting a stated selective-risk target. On mathematics tasks it serves about 76.1% of answers while keeping held-out selective risk below target.

entry.title: Hierarchical Compression of Vision-Language Model Benchmarks

author.name: Hyunjong Ok, Seunggu Kang, Jaeho Lee

entry.summary: The paper presents PRIMEBench, a vision-aware hierarchical framework for compressing VLM benchmarks while preserving model rankings, addressing the rising cost of multimodal evaluation. It operates in four stages including cleaning items answerable without the image, selecting category representatives, and further pruning. Benchmark compression is well studied for text LLMs but under-explored for VLMs, making this a useful methodological addition.

entry.title: AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation

author.name: Rishabh Agrawal, Hejie Cui, Shasha Li, Shanchan Wu, Sercan \"{O}. Ar{\i}k

entry.summary: AdviSD trains a small advisor model to steer a frozen frontier LLM executor with natural-language advice, using multi-turn interaction feedback for self-distillation. The paper proves that in a shared-parameter model, learning from plausible-but-ineffective corrections can hurt learning, and shows that sampling such corrections less often improves eventual performance. The method pairs outcomes with targeted distillation to improve advice quality.

entry.title: Restoring without Forgetting: Filter-Level Continual Image Restoration via Parameter-Space Integrated Gradients

author.name: Xin Feng, Jin Zhao, Yizhen Zhang, Wenjie Pei, Fanglin Chen, Guangming Lu

entry.summary: RwF is a filter-level continual adaptation framework for image restoration that avoids catastrophic forgetting when learning a stream of new tasks without revisiting past data. It uses parameter-space integrated gradients attribution to localize degradation-critical filters, then adapts to new tasks by generating task-specific filters from a filter bank via factorized low-rank transformations augmented with cross-task attention. The key observation is that task-specific knowledge concentrates in a small subset of filters separable from general content reconstruction.

entry.title: ResARC: Residual-Aware AutoRegressive Coding for Ultra-Low Bitrate Image Compression

author.name: Qin Yan, Ruixiao Dong, Yutao Xie, Li Li, Ying Chen, Kai Li, Daowen Li, Houqiang Li

entry.summary: ResARC improves progressive autoregressive image codecs by explicitly compensating for quantization residual from discrete tokenization and generation residual from imperfect suffix-token prediction at the decoder. The residual-aware design targets ultra-low bitrate compression with better reconstruction quality.

entry.title: BTC3D: Blended Tile Conditioning for Detail-Enhancing Image-to-3D Generation

author.name: Junyu Li, Qiuyu Chen, Pengcheng Wang, Shiqi Yang, Alexandra Gomez-Villa, Joost van de Weijer, Ruilin Li, Kai Wang

entry.summary: BTC3D introduces a training-free conditioning scheme for diffusion-based image-to-3D generation that preserves fine spatial detail, addressing what the authors call detail attenuation caused by globally compressed conditioning features. By avoiding retraining of large diffusion models, it offers a practical route to higher-fidelity 3D assets from detailed input images.

entry.title: Grounding with Confidence: Controllable Generative Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Jinhao Chen, Benlei Cui, Ruijian Jia, Ziheng Wang, Tianyu Wo, Pengfei Sun, Longtao Huang, Hui Xue, Yitong Yang, Haiwen Hong

entry.summary: The paper adds an explicit interval-level confidence head to generative video temporal grounding models, separating candidate generation from acceptance. Offline verifier scores and RL-time temporal-overlap labels train the head, enabling controllable selection of grounded time intervals for video search, review, and editing.

entry.title: StreamRig: Exploiting Intra-Rig Geometry for Streaming Multi-Camera Odometry

author.name: Yufei Wei, Shuhao Ye, Qi Wang, Xin Zheng, Qing Huang, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: StreamRig builds causal streaming odometry for calibrated multi-camera rigs on top of a frozen multi-view 3D foundation model, training only 74.6M parameters for feature resampling, causal attention bridging, and pose regression. A periodic re-anchoring protocol stabilizes poses over long sequences.

entry.title: DiFF: Doppler-informed Flow Matching for Human Motion Flow

author.name: Kai Wang, Mingle Zhao

entry.summary: DiFF is a generative framework for non-rigid scene flow estimation from sparse, noisy 4D millimeter-wave radar point clouds, combining Doppler-informed motion priors with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based conditional flow matching model. The approach exploits Doppler velocity cues that rigid-centric prior methods neglect, targeting privacy-preserving human motion perception for human-robot interaction. A KAN-attention mechanism provides expressive feature extraction.

entry.title: CADeT: Causal-Aware Deformation Transmission for Indirect Robotic Manipulation of Soft Tissue

author.name: Junlei Hu, Dominic Jones, Pietro Valdastri

entry.summary: CADeT integrates structural causal models with active sensing for indirect manipulation of deep-seated deformable tissue in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery, inferring a latent transmission mode and estimating a state-dependent adhesion Jacobian online. When observation ambiguity persists between decoupled and blocked modes, the system selects probing actions to improve mode distinguishability.

entry.title: Path-Following Control and Terramechanics Analysis for Planetary Rovers Under Wheel-to-Wheel Traction Asymmetry

author.name: Ryuya Matsuoka, Keisuke Takehana, Kentaro Uno, Toshinori Kuwahara, Kazuya Yoshida

entry.summary: The authors propose a model-free path-following controller for skid-steered planetary rovers on loose deformable terrain, which avoids slip-sinkage entrapment by limiting commanded velocity and correcting heading only through selective deceleration of outer wheels. The deceleration-only strategy turns outer wheels into a mechanical anchor and was validated on a four-wheel independent rover platform.

entry.title: MVP-SLAM: Multi-Camera Visual-Inertial Floorplan-Prior SLAM

author.name: Asier Bikandi-Noya, Miguel Fernandez-Cortizas, Muhammad Shaheer, Holger Voos, Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez

entry.summary: MVP-SLAM is a multi-camera visual-inertial SLAM system for indoor construction sites that uses as-planned floor plans as a metric prior to localize online and correct drift under challenging lighting and low-texture conditions. Unlike prior floor-plan methods that correct trajectories offline or require depth sensors, it performs online correction with cameras only. This matters for robust long-duration autonomy in structured but visually degraded environments.

entry.title: Magnetic based In-situ Self 3D Pose Estimation for a Modular Soft Tendon-Driven Continuum Robot via IMU-Fusion

author.name: Zheng Cao, Guo Ning Sue, Xiangyun Bu, David Quinn, Junzhe Hu, Carmel Majidi

entry.summary: This work presents an embedded pose sensing framework for continuum robots combining IMU measurements with active magnetic fields to estimate configuration without external cameras. Fusing IMU angular measurements with magnetic-field references reduces accumulated orientation error and achieves high update rates, addressing a key gap for compliant robots operating where vision is obstructed.

entry.title: GPU-Accelerated Path-Dependent Marginal Information Gain for Autonomous Exploration

author.name: Jo\~ao F\'elix Mendes, Rodrigo Ventura, Meysam Basiri

entry.summary: This paper introduces a GPU-accelerated method for computing path-dependent marginal information gain in autonomous exploration, replacing per-path voxel merging with depth-buffer representations of previous observations. Candidate rays are projected into ancestors' depth buffers to identify observation overlap, correcting the mutual-independence assumption of sampling-based planners while remaining fast.

entry.title: Partial identification with entropy regularized optimal transport

author.name: Bruno N. Costa, Florian F. Gunsilius

entry.summary: For settings where data and assumptions only identify a set containing the true parameters, this work recasts the associated (potentially infinite-dimensional) linear programs as optimal transport problems on path spaces. Entropic regularization turns them into multi-marginal entropic OT problems solvable with efficient existing algorithms.

entry.title: Learning to Route in Visual Space via Multi-Step Embedding Retrieval

author.name: Tianyu Chen, Mingyuan Zhou, Jiaxing Wu

entry.summary: The paper argues that visual agentic search is bottlenecked by single-step text-query retrievers and proposes offloading multi-step navigation directly to the retrieval tool in embedding space. It introduces VHOP, a data generation framework and benchmark with five difficulty levels testing visual matching and search planning. This could unlock more capable visual search agents.

entry.title: Coverage Before Control: Route-Instruction Grounding and Steering for Controllable Retrosynthesis

author.name: Xuemin Chen, Xiaozhuang Song, Xinjian Zhao, Yaoyao Xu, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: RIGS is a two-stage framework for instruction-conditioned retrosynthesis: Stage A trains a language projector to learn which precursor alternatives an instruction favors, and Stage B uses it to steer a frozen retrosynthesis model, enabling chemists to preserve motifs or impose preferences rather than merely recovering recorded reactions. The framework emphasizes both coverage of alternatives and controllable selection among them.

entry.title: Interpretable but Fragile? Robustness of Concept Bottlenecks under Geometric-Semantic Perturbations

author.name: Hanwei Zhang, Tianma Hu, Gaojie Jin, Xu Cheng, Ronghui Mu

entry.summary: The paper disentangles contradictory findings about concept bottleneck model robustness by arguing prior studies conflated robustness notions, and introduces a generator-based evaluation framework comparing standard classifiers and CBMs under continuous geometric perturbations in latent space versus discrete semantic interventions in concept space. This clarifies when CBMs are genuinely more or less robust.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Normalized Margins for Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Sadegh Khorasani, Petrus Mikkola, Matthias Grossglauser

entry.summary: UNM-DPO extends DPO by combining strength-dependent margins with a learned prompt-dependent scale, motivated by a heteroskedastic Bradley-Terry model that accounts for preference strength and prompt-level uncertainty in human feedback. The authors develop two objectives (advantage-only and whole-residual) that differently order margin subtraction and normalization of implicit reward differences.

entry.title: World-as-Graph: Relational World Modeling Through Latent Space Graphs

author.name: Yaqi Yang, Shuo Huang, Yujin Huang, Fucai Ke, Jiatong Han, Xin Zheng

entry.summary: WAG is a graph-based object-centric world model that introduces relational inductive bias into JEPA-style predictive representation learning. It builds time-varying latent graphs over object-centric states via relation-aware structure induction, explicitly modeling object-object relations that prior set-based object-centric world models capture only implicitly. This supports explicit relational, temporal, and dynamic memory modeling of visual scenes.

entry.title: Towards Robust Time Series Learning via Capacity-Centric Modulation

author.name: Siru Zhong, Senzhang Wang, James T. Kwok, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Capacity-Centric Modulation, a sample-adaptive regularization principle for time-series learning where sample-wise dropout probabilities along activation paths are assigned using spectral sparsity. The resulting SACM framework is task-agnostic, plugs into existing backbones without architectural redesign, and adapts regularization strength to sample reliability.

entry.title: Is Weight Tying Still Beneficial for Decoder-Only LLMs in Private Settings Under DP-SGD?

author.name: Razan El Mais, Ali Chehab, Ibrahim Issa, Razane Tajeddine

entry.summary: The paper investigates weight tying between input and output embeddings of decoder-only LLMs (GPT2, DistilGPT2) under DP-SGD fine-tuning and finds that untied embeddings consistently outperform tied ones, with gains up to 4.74 percentage points. This inverts a common design heuristic from the non-private setting. The result gives practitioners a simple, actionable configuration choice for privacy-preserving fine-tuning.

entry.title: The Detectability Gap: Hidden Heterogeneity in Hallucination Detection Across Language Models

author.name: Pranav Darshan, Pranav A, Sravan Karthick T, Minal Moharir, Ivan P. Yamshchikov

entry.summary: The paper partitions hallucinations by answer agreement into high-agreement Ghost and low-agreement Flickering regimes across four models and three QA datasets, revealing a 0.35-0.46 AUC detectability gap. Notably, the authors themselves flag strong coupling between regime-defining and evaluation statistics and treat the raw gap as a property of agreement-based detection rather than independent evidence.

entry.title: Reliable Parallel Decoding in Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zhenghao He, Bohan Liu, Guangzhi Xiong, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper analyzes when parallel token commitment is reliable in masked diffusion LMs, showing that confidence alone is insufficient: confident late-sequence predictions can fix answers before supporting computations, and downstream reliability degrades with upstream uncertainty. The authors derive commitment-order criteria using cross-layer prediction stability. This improves both quality and speed of an emerging efficient generation paradigm.

entry.title: Can Vision-Language Models Stay Helpful When Facing Implicit Risks? Intent-Privilege OPSD for Efficient Safety-Helpfulness Alignment

author.name: Haotian Deng, Wenbin Xing, Gang Xu, Tao He, Jinkai Zheng, Chun Li, Zheng Zhu, Ming Li

entry.summary: Proposes Intent-Privilege On-Policy Self-Distillation for VLM safety, using evidence-grounded intent as privileged supervision during training so models recognize cross-modal implicit risks and respond safely and usefully rather than refusing blanketly. The approach avoids large preference datasets, costly multi-rollout training, and inference-time safeguards.

entry.title: The Price of Token Boundaries: Compression Certificates and Prediction

author.name: Yuhao Du, Shunian Chen

entry.summary: The paper develops lower and upper bounds on the minimum token count achievable with and without a regular-expression pre-tokenization boundary rule, using shortest-path and vocabulary-budget formulations with an integer-programming certificate. On English Wikipedia, boundary rules increase the optimal token count by 28.3-36.8 percent, and BPE lies 2.1 percent above the constrained bound but 10.9 percent above the unrestricted one. This quantifies a previously obscured cost of pre-tokenization constraints in tokenizer design.

entry.title: GLARE: Generating Listening Heads with Appropriate Reactions

author.name: Zikai Liao, Yumin Suh, Yi Ouyang, Yi-Lun Lee, Yi-Hsuan Tsai, Zhaozheng Yin

entry.summary: GLARE addresses listener-behavior generation in dyadic conversations with a curated dataset of roughly 147 hours of paired speaker-listener videos and 64,557 event-level reaction annotations across six categories, plus evaluation metrics measuring reaction appropriateness rather than visual realism alone.

entry.title: Residual Wrench Certification and Margin-Aware Control Synthesis for Aerial Physical Interaction

author.name: Abhimanyu Khadga, Abhinav Sinha, Shashi Ranjan Kumar

entry.summary: The paper develops a task-relative framework certifying residual wrench authority of multirotors after hover and contact loading, deriving signed margins for convex reserves (Euclidean balls and ellipsoids) using convex geometry. It proposes command projection onto a tightened feasible set and structured gain synthesis with proven exponential convergence and robust ultimate boundedness within the certified tracking region.

entry.title: Examining Variation in How Guided AI Tutors Resolve Student Impasses

author.name: Bakhtawar Ahtisham, Kirk Vanacore, Alessandra Napoli, Josh Arens, Ksenia Ionova, Clayton Cohn, Shima Salehi, Rene Kizilcec

entry.summary: Using 20,462 student turns from 1,260 authentic sessions with a guided LLM chemistry tutor, the authors identify 6,630 impasse turns (conceptual errors, uncertainty, help-seeking) and simulate three tutoring conditions to study how AI tutors handle persistent impasses. The work targets the assistance dilemma: helping too early undermines productive struggle while withholding help too long causes wheel-spinning.

entry.title: ChartRevise: A Dataset and Evaluation Protocol for Exact Chart Editing via Code

author.name: Jiaxiang Tang, Yi Zhou, Chad DeLuca, Rogerio Feris, Ahmed Khalil Omran, Zhi-Li Zhang, Pengyuan Li, Ali Anwar

entry.summary: ChartRevise is a structured dataset and evaluation protocol for exact program-grounded chart editing, where a requested visual change must be realized in code without missing coupled updates or altering unrelated content. Built on the grammar of graphics, it systematically covers edit operations and verifies applicability across chart types and libraries. It fills a gap left by benchmarks that conflate request completion with edit exactness.

entry.title: Action Conditioned Bisimulation For GUI Agent Memory

author.name: Hongbo Zhang, Liuyang Song, Quanquan Li, Daqian Yang, Yan Wen, Zhengtao Yao

entry.summary: The paper defines a merge rule for GUI agent memory as action-conditioned bisimulation over the empirical predictive state graph, merging states only when shared actions lead to agreeing outcomes, explicitly ignoring observation similarity. This addresses the problem that visually similar GUI pages often behave differently. It is training-free and evaluated against an existing outcome-value memory on MiniWoB++.

entry.title: Consistent Plan-Act for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Heng-Zhuang Li, Yi-Kai Zhang, Yu Wang, Yueqing Sun, Jiayuan Zhang, Qi Gu, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: This work identifies planner-actor state mismatch, a systematic disagreement between planner and executor agents about task-relevant facts in long-horizon tasks, detected by comparing structured state assertions. The authors show that supplying agents with task-relevant state information reduces mismatch and improves coordination and task performance.

entry.title: BELIEFRAG: Making Adaptive RAG State-Aware under Evolving Evidence

author.name: Hongji Pu

entry.summary: BELIEFRAG is a closed-loop controller for adaptive retrieval-augmented generation that maintains an explicit belief state over sufficiency, reliability, conflict, uncertainty, evidence gaps, and acquisition cost, then selects among retrieval, query rewriting, verification, and answering. It targets evidence-state fragmentation where local RAG signals act as isolated triggers.

entry.title: AVERT-VLN: Abstention-aware Visual Error Recovery and Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Minrui Liu, Jingke Wang, Yuehao Huang, Hao Su, Jiajun Lv, Yukai Ma, Yong Liu

entry.summary: AVERT-VLN is a closed-loop framework for vision-and-language navigation in which a plug-in vision-language monitor detects when execution goes off track, selectively requests human corrective guidance, and reuses those interactions for offline preference learning. This reduces the need for continuous human supervision in unseen environments.

entry.title: GrammarRL: Effective Grammar-Constrained Decoding via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Gabriele Tuccio, Antonino Furnari, Aldo Gangemi, Misael Mongiov\`{\i}

entry.summary: GrammarRL is a label-free RL method that adapts language models to grammar constraints without annotated data, addressing the known trade-off where grammar-constrained decoding guarantees syntactic validity but degrades semantic quality. It uses complementary self-reward signals to outperform beam-search mitigations at lower computational cost.

entry.title: Argus: Academic Integrity in the Era of Generative AI

author.name: David Racovan, Ajay Rawat, Christopher K. May, Jeffrey A. Turkstra

entry.summary: Argus is an automated system for detecting LLM-assisted student work in undergraduate C programming assignments by combining behavioral and stylistic indicators across a student's assignment progression. Applied to six years of data from a large Purdue CS2 course, it found 45 percent of enrolled students exhibited patterns consistent with LLM-assisted coding. The work quantifies the scale of the academic integrity challenge posed by generative AI.

entry.title: Raw Imagery Impacting Your AI: Should You Care?

author.name: Adrien Dorise, Marjorie Bellizzi, St\'ephane May

entry.summary: This study quantifies how image degradation, controlled via Signal-to-Noise Ratio, Modulation Transfer Function, and Ground Sampling Distance, affects lightweight object detectors (YOLOv5s, YOLOX-S, NanoDet) applied to raw satellite imagery for onboard space applications like vessel and wildfire detection. It provides practical guidance for mission designers deciding whether onboard models can operate on unprocessed imagery instead of expensive ground-restored products.

entry.title: MM-FinEval: A Multi-Task Multimodal Benchmark for Real-World Financial Forecasting

author.name: Dong Shu, Yanguang Liu, Huopu Zhang, Saisai Hu, Haiyan Zhao, Hekun Huang, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: MM-FinEval is a multimodal benchmark for evaluating LLMs on financial forecasting from earnings conference calls, containing 2,045 S&P 500 calls from 2019 to 2022 with three input modalities and 12 financial task labels. It addresses the limitation of existing financial benchmarks that are unimodal or single-task.

entry.title: Retargeting Motions to Diverse Skeletons via Learnable Flattening

author.name: Kia-J\"ung Yang, Fabian H. Sinz, Pawe{\l} A. Pierzchlewicz

entry.summary: The paper introduces a Transformer autoencoder with a learnable flattening of skeletal graphs for cross-structural motion retargeting, producing a topology- and translation-invariant latent space that handles zero-shot transfer to unseen skeleton topologies. It integrates graph-based positional information in a way that outperforms both prior transformers and specialized geometric methods.

entry.title: Breaking Babel: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Long-Form Subtitle Translation

author.name: Haibo Jin, Xinjie Li, Najmeh Sadoughi, Yang Liu, Yibo Wang, Zhu Liu, Yuzong Liu

entry.summary: Proposes SMART, a self-evolving multi-agent system for translating long-form subtitles that requires discourse-level reasoning and consistent terminology across episodes. It builds persistent series-level memory during test-time training, routes sentences through a dynamic router and mixture-of-agents layer with verification tools, and uses a judge-refiner loop with textual criteria.

entry.title: Cascadia: A Control-Plane-Free Alternative to Hyperconverged AI Infrastructure

author.name: Matias Parij, Pawan Paudel, Tate Berenbaum, Muthaiah Venkatachalam

entry.summary: Presents Cascadia, a system for serving LLMs on fleets of commodity Intel AI PCs using CPU, integrated GPU, and NPU resources, where every node embeds ingress, scheduling, and execution without a dedicated routing control plane. Nodes form a libp2p QUIC mesh with certificate-based admission and support whole-model, replica, and pipeline-sharded serving modes including speculative decoding.

entry.title: Efficient Multi-Modal Planning with Reward-Guided Preference Optimization for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chenglin Chen, Lujia Wang, Xinhu Zheng, Jun Ma, Haoang Li

entry.summary: EMPlan is an autonomous driving trajectory planning method combining sparse anchors with an offset refinement module for efficient multi-modal trajectory prediction, trained via reward-guided fine-tuning. It aims to avoid causal confusion from imitation learning and the computational overhead of rule-based scoring while relaxing pairwise annotation requirements.

entry.title: Learning Continuous Neural Representation of Stochastic Hybrid Systems

author.name: Sangli Teng, Hang Liu, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that stochastic hybrid systems, governed by SDEs with Markov resets on guard surfaces, can be approximated by an SDE in a higher-dimensional latent space with continuous sample paths. The key technique encodes reset kernel branches with auxiliary variables, turning resets into deterministic ones enabling topological gluing of the manifold.

entry.title: Signal-Routed Temperature Scaling: Low-Capacity Risk-Conditioned Calibration for Small Validation Budgets

author.name: Wenhao Liang, Liangwei Nathan Zheng, Lin Yue, Wei Emma Zhang, Mingyu Guo, Olaf Maennel, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces SRTS-BCE, a 10-parameter, argmax-preserving calibration method that cross-fits a correctness-risk score over logit statistics and fits per-group temperatures, targeting the regime where only a few thousand validation examples are available. It reduces expected calibration error on fine-tuned CIFAR-100 with ViT-B/16 while generalizing vector-scaling approaches as a special case.

entry.title: TED:Text-Axis Evidence Decomposition for Prompted Anomaly Localization

author.name: JinYoung Kim, Geonho Kim, GiJeong Park, Geonu Lee, YoungJoon Yoo

entry.summary: The paper shows that CLIP-based anomaly detectors adapted for defect sensitivity can assign high anomaly scores to visually complex normal regions under domain shift, because local scoring conflates defect and hard-normal evidence. TED is a post-hoc scoring method that decomposes responses along text axes to determine whether evidence better supports a defect or a hard normal. It addresses a real reliability gap in industrial anomaly localization.

entry.title: From Benchmarks to Production: Transferring Time Series Anomaly Detection Methods for Electricity Production Monitoring

author.name: Nicolas Vautier, Paul Caron, Nardi Xhepi, F\'elicie Bizeul, Manel Boumghar, Christophe Degouy, Paul Boniol

entry.summary: TAMIS is a scalable, interpretable system deployed at EDF for detecting anomalies in short-term electricity production forecasts, identifying atypical intra-day patterns that signal data quality issues or operational irregularities. The paper documents the transfer of research TSAD methods into an industrial production monitoring context.

entry.title: GRPO Training Dynamics for Small Language Models

author.name: Rajat Ghosh, Vaishnavi Bhargava, Henry Wong, Aryan Singhal, Debojyoti Dutta

entry.summary: This is a systematic empirical study of GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning dynamics for small language models from 1.5B to 7B parameters under a practical single-node 8xA100 budget, spanning mathematics, coding, and science MCQ domains. It analyzes how group size affects policy convergence and training stability to improve reproducibility in resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: A Reusable Semantic Web Framework for Evidence-Grounded Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments under the EU AI Act

author.name: Faith Olopade, Delaram Golpayegani, David Lewis

entry.summary: The paper presents a Semantic Web framework consolidating fragmented evidence for EU AI Act Article 27 Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments, with a 150-record annotated corpus serialized as a SPARQL-queryable knowledge graph covering employment and public services use cases. Five demonstration scenarios surface relevant records to support credible assessments.

entry.title: Robust Transfer Learning for Paper ECG Recognition

author.name: Yinghao Xie, Zhenbang Dai, Haojun Wang, Jinyu Cai, Fabio Bonassi, Hongwu Chen, Johan Sundstr\"om, Jiawei Li, Ant\^onio H. Ribeiro

entry.summary: RobECG-CL is a rank-aware contrastive learning framework for robust paper ECG recognition that trains on progressively degraded paper ECG views built from standard 12-lead recordings. It outperforms contrastive baselines and the ECG-FM waveform foundation model in the 1% labeled setting on CODE-II and EchoNext stress tests, with validation on hospital samples.

entry.title: Zero-Compute Cross-Lingual Transferability Estimation Using Typological Feature Proxies

author.name: Dalton Raphael Harmsen, Swier Garst, Thomas van Osch, Zar\`e Palanciyan, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: This work shows that cross-lingual transfer between languages is predictable from freely available typological features alone, with a typology-only random forest scoring leave-one-language-out Spearman rho of 0.705 on a 24-language transfer matrix. It offers a zero-compute proxy for estimating transfer and probes whether high-resource language dominance reflects typology or data quantity.

entry.title: DoGBench: Can Agents Meet Expert Standards for User-Facing Documentation?

author.name: Frances Liu, Manny Silva, Paige Calvert, Ayu Adiati, Sarah Sanders

entry.summary: DoGBENCH is presented as the first benchmark for generating and maintaining real user-facing software documentation, with 292 items drawn from open source projects like Helm, PostHog, and Mautic. Agents must decide whether documentation needs an update, produce an acceptable patch in one attempt, or abstain, judged against task-specific rubrics mirroring technical writer review standards.

entry.title: Efficient Active Auditing of Multi-Group Fairness with Bias Probes

author.name: Ayoub Ajarra, Debabrota Basu

entry.summary: The paper studies property-specific auditing of black-box models for multi-group fairness, aiming to extract targeted fairness information without reconstructing the model (which risks extraction attacks) or merely estimating aggregate metrics. It introduces bias probes that efficiently identify which regions of the data distribution drive bias.

entry.title: ViTeX-Bench: Benchmarking High-Fidelity Video Scene Text Editing

author.name: Xinghao Chen, Xiangbo Gao, Jiongze Yu, Yuheng Wu, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: This paper introduces ViTEX-Bench, a benchmark for video scene text editing, the task of replacing text on surfaces in videos (storefront signs, whiteboards, product labels) while preserving scene dynamics, motion, and temporal consistency. The authors identify a gap: image scene text editing is well studied, but video variants lack paired real-video data and metrics that verify edited text remains correct over time. ViTEX-Bench addresses this with evaluation protocols for visual quality, temporal consistency, and edit locality.

entry.title: Graph Anomaly Detection as Finite-Horizon Control: Training-Free Scoring via Empirical Bayes

author.name: Fred Xu, Thomas Markovich, Florence Regol, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: EB-GAD is a training-free graph anomaly detection framework that models normality as graph-aware generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck relaxation toward a graph-filtered template, with Empirical Bayes fitting the graph precision. It decouples graph trust, spectral weighting, and score choice that are entangled in existing architectures, aiming for cheaper, more interpretable, and more stable node anomaly scores.

entry.title: JARQ: Joint Alternating Refinement for Quantization

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Sicheng Lyu, Xiao-Wen Chang

entry.summary: JARQ is a plug-in post-training quantization refinement for LLMs that alternates a joint least-squares refit of all group scales with bounded Babai proposals that move many codes of a group together, addressing the fact that group-wise quantizers leave the grid unfitted to resulting integer codes. It formulates the problem as a bilinear box-constrained mixed-integer least-squares problem with a backpropagation-free solver and monotone objective guarantees.

entry.title: Learning Chaos Without Seeing Chaos: Extrapolation of Global Dynamics in Autoregressive Transformers

author.name: Yilun Liu, Yi Zhang, Ganyu Wu, Sikuan Yan, Mengyue Wang, Alois Knoll, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: The authors study whether small autoregressive transformers trained on trajectories from restricted parameter regimes of nonlinear dynamical systems (logistic map, Lorenz, generalized Hopf) can extrapolate system dynamics to unseen parameter values. They tokenize control parameters and states as continuous sequences and evaluate closed-loop generation far outside the training distribution. The work probes the limits of learned local prediction in recovering global dynamical organization never observed during training.

entry.title: On Parameters of Nonlinear Scalar Dynamics from Video: Invariants, Calibration, and Identifiability

author.name: Wenjie Wang, Yuanyuan Wang, Zixiang Jiang, Shaoan Xie, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: The paper develops an identifiability theory for estimating physical parameters of nonlinear second-order ODEs from video observations, extending prior work that only covered linear time-invariant systems. It characterizes which parameters are uniquely identifiable versus which can only be recovered as invariants, conditioned on shared non-collapsed state maps and velocity-coverage assumptions. This grounds video-based scientific parameter estimation in formal theory.

entry.title: Shared Phase and Retention Control for Efficient Adaptive Spectral Recurrence

author.name: Wentao Wang, Hengyu Zhong, Yunhan Jiang, Jialiang An, Meng Lu

entry.summary: The paper introduces adaptive spectral recurrence where high-dimensional memory modes share a low-dimensional control signal for decay and rotation, decoupling control cost from state capacity. This improves fixed-state recurrent models that otherwise rely on static transitions, offering constant-memory inference with dynamic memory management.

entry.title: Jacobian Rank Collapse in Decision-Focused Learning

author.name: Aojie Yuan, Haiyue Zhang, Zijian Su

entry.summary: The authors characterize a failure mode of decision-focused learning where downstream-objective losses provide restricted parameter-update directions, using sparse index tracking to expose rank-one Jacobians and collinear per-example gradients. They derive spectral bounds and counterexamples, and empirically examine when this geometry affects decision quality across equity configurations.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations

author.name: Mykhailo Minin

entry.summary: This paper proposes PI-GMDH, a physics-informed method that adaptively constructs functional representations of coupled physical fields during solution rather than fixing them in advance. Candidate directions are selected using the first variation of the full physical objective and optimized via block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton steps, demonstrated on the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with a Taylor-Green benchmark.

entry.title: Mutual Equilibrium: Multimodal Representation Learning through Reciprocal Feedback

author.name: Ho-min Park, Byungkon Kang

entry.summary: MEQ is a mutual feedback architecture that refines two inputs of possibly different modalities into coupled embeddings, each reflecting information from the other, with the final output defined as a fixed point of the reciprocal interaction. The authors provide theoretical interpretation, design choices to avoid failure cases, and results on classification and visual grounding.

entry.title: MIND: Marginal-Invariant Neural Dependency Diffusion for Mixed-Type Tabular Generation

author.name: Pengfei Li, Mohammad Khalil

entry.summary: MIND is a diffusion-based generative model for mixed-type tabular data that maps heterogeneous variables into a unified latent dependency space via column-wise marginal transport, then learns cross-column relationships with a conditional diffusion model. Copula-tangent denoising and rank projection during sampling mitigate marginal shift, improving fidelity and dependency preservation across nine benchmarks.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Compression: Budgeted Transmission Allocation for Extreme Federated Learning

author.name: Pengfei Li, Mohammad Khalil

entry.summary: LBAT reframes federated learning communication under extreme uplink budgets as a resource allocation problem, estimating per-layer transmission value from local training signals and using exact byte-level dynamic programming to allocate rank and bit configurations. It outperforms uniform compression by targeting bandwidth at valuable parameter blocks.

entry.title: Fast Regularized Policy Mirror Descent with One-Step TD Updates

author.name: Qipei Chen, Wenye Li, Yule Sun, Ke Wei

entry.summary: This paper analyzes policy mirror descent coupled with a critic advanced by only a single temporal-difference update, establishing global linear convergence for finite discounted MDPs with constant actor stepsizes. It also extends results to stochastic TD-PMD with strongly convex mirror maps under off-policy sampling.

entry.title: Beyond Model Ranking: Regime Diagnosis for Distributional-Statistical Misspecification in Industrial Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Pengyu Nie, Chenglang Xu, Yaoshi Chen, Chaogan Ren, Wei Hu, Chao Yang, Jiangong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a train-deploy gap source in industrial forecasting: canonical losses embed fixed statistical priors that are systematically violated in pathological regimes like zero-inflation and skewness, producing bias that persists even with perfect temporal modeling. It proposes regime diagnosis to characterize this misspecification beyond aggregate model rankings.

entry.title: Role-Adaptive Policy Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Seonvin Cho, Soohyun Choi, Songnam Hong

entry.summary: RAPO decouples the policy's roles in critic bootstrapping versus action execution in offline RL, adapting regularization coefficients for each role separately by differentiating through candidate policy updates. Applied to TD3+BC, it separates bootstrap and execution actors with distinct penalties. This addresses a previously conflated trade-off in offline policy regularization.

entry.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis

author.name: Tian Xia, Minghao Liu, Yiqing Liang, Laixi Shi, Jiayun Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues that accuracy-based prompt optimization is ill-suited to class-imbalanced clinical diagnosis and introduces pair-level Pareto prompt optimization for multimodal LLMs targeting AUROC, modifying reflective methods like GEPA that rely on per-instance correctness matrices. This makes automated prompt optimization threshold-free and class-balance-invariant. It addresses a real gap in deploying MLLMs for diagnosis.

entry.title: Unified Optimality Conditions for Stochastic Optimal Control in the Rough Path and It\^o Frameworks

author.name: Thomas Lew

entry.summary: This paper connects Pontryagin Maximum Principle optimality conditions from Ito calculus and rough path theory via a conditional expectation relating the adjoint processes. It derives a rough stochastic PMP for adapted controls that avoids forward-backward SDEs, unifying the two classical frameworks for stochastic optimal control.

entry.title: SHIFT-Truck: A High-Fidelity Aerodynamics Dataset and Benchmark for Pickup Trucks

author.name: Riddhiman Raut, Yin Yu, Aashwin Anand Mishra, Michael Emory, Thomas Economon, Peter Lyu, Juan J. Alonso

entry.summary: SHIFT-Truck is the first high-fidelity CFD dataset and benchmark targeting pickup-truck aerodynamics, capturing the unique bed shear-layer flow absent from datasets like DrivAerML and SHIFT-SUV. It enables training neural surrogates that can predict flow features at a fraction of scale-resolved CFD cost, supporting drag reduction and EV range improvement.

entry.title: VOSSA: Voiceprint Optimization for Streaming Speech Architectures

author.name: Mu-Ruei Tseng, Waris Quamer, Ghady Nasrallah, Ricardo Gutierrez-Osuna

entry.summary: VOSSA proposes extracting speaker information from intermediate content-encoder layers with attentive statistics pooling, trained jointly with voice conversion objectives rather than relying on pretrained ASV speaker embeddings. This removes the need for a separate speaker encoder and better matches frame-level streaming generation constraints, improving over baselines across six datasets.

entry.title: Minimax Additive Regression under Unknown Dependent Designs

author.name: Baptiste Ferrere, Fabrice Gamboa, Jean-Michel Loubes

entry.summary: This paper studies additive regression under non-product, dependent random designs with dimension growing with sample size, introducing coupled smoothness classes and adapting Riesz-basis functional ANOVA constructions with dimension-free compatibility constants. It achieves matching minimax upper and lower bounds for prediction with known or unknown marginals.

entry.title: Exploring Heterogeneous Model Merging Approach for Complex Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Jiahe Fan, Si Chen, Yinghao Hou, Wenbo Xia, Ke Xu, Hong Xie, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: This work studies training-free transfer of specialist capabilities into general language models at the parameter level, without distillation or gradient updates. The authors adapt two heterogeneous merging methods, Intersection-Merge and Activate-Prune-Merge, that project a specialist donor into the recipient's shape and interpolate backbone parameters. It matters as a cheap alternative to costly training-based knowledge transfer.

entry.title: Comparison of techniques for fine-tuning open-weight models for entity extraction from radiology reports

author.name: Aawez Mansuri, Kush Mehta, Mohammadreza Chavoshi, Jahanzaib Malik, Theodorus Dapamede, Frank Li, Rohan Isaac, Beatrice Brown-Mulry, Chiratidzo Rudado Sanyika, YoungSeok Jeon, Judy W. Gichoya, Ali Emami, Hari Trivedi

entry.summary: The study examines whether a fine-tuned open-weight Gemma-3-12B can match GPT-4o for extracting intracranial hemorrhage acuity labels from head-CT radiology reports, using a 2x2 design crossing classification-head versus instruction fine-tuning with real-distilled versus synthetic training data. This addresses privacy, cost, and reproducibility concerns of relying on proprietary models in clinical NLP. Gemma-3-12B was released well before this work, so it analyzes existing models.

entry.title: Image Classifiers are Efficient Self-Supervised Video Representation Learners

author.name: Owais Iqbal, Sudipta Sarkar, Shyam Marjit, Omprakash Chakraborty, Anirban Chakraborty, Abir Das

entry.summary: VideoMSN is a decoder-free masked Siamese network framework that learns video representations by repurposing standard image ViTs on super images (grids of sampled frames), with two views masked along spatial and temporal dimensions. It avoids heavy 3D architectures and reconstruction objectives while capturing both motion and appearance cues. This offers an efficient route to self-supervised video representation learning.

entry.title: Automated Evaluation of Multi-Turn Dialogues in In-Car Conversational Assistants

author.name: Vaishnav Negi, Lev Sorokin, Soroosh Tayebi Arasteh, Andrea Stocco

entry.summary: The paper presents an automated black-box testing framework for in-car conversational assistants using closed-loop simulation with a strategy-guided user simulator, adversarial strategy manager, and two-tier LLM judge. It targets multi-turn reliability, constraint handling, context retention, and safety-critical behavior that single-turn evaluations miss.

entry.title: PACT: Pairwise-Anchored Calibrated Tuning for Single-Token Typed Decisions

author.name: Yida Lin

entry.summary: PACT introduces training objectives for single-token typed-decision models that read one-letter answer logits, exploiting contrastively curated pairs with machine-checked certificates that removing a decisive sentence makes the fact unknown. Its four loss terms, including a difference-in-differences margin invariant to shared logit offsets, require no new annotation.

entry.title: CineSubBench: Evaluating LLMs on Long-Form Narrative and Cultural Understanding from Multilingual Movie Subtitles

author.name: Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Susmoy Chakraborty, Davood Rafiei

entry.summary: CineSubBench is a benchmark of 1,012 films with complete subtitle tracks in six languages, requiring models to reconstruct characters, relationships, events, and themes from thousands of temporally ordered short utterances. It targets long-context narrative integration and culturally situated judgment, domains underexplored compared to law or medicine. This provides a demanding test of genuine long-context comprehension.

entry.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization

author.name: Jingxuan Wu, Yuzhe Yang, Yiqiao Huang, Chengzhi Liu, Qingni Wang, Chengxuan Qian, Shutong Wu, Jiawei Zhang, Xin Eric Wang

entry.summary: MemFold optimizes a fixed-budget soft memory for personalized assistants by the downstream behavior it supports rather than text reconstruction, compressing query-conditioned textual memory into latent vectors trained via on-policy optimization. This decouples retaining user information from acting on it, addressing limits of both growing text context and reconstruction-trained latent memories. It targets long-horizon personalization efficiency.

entry.title: LAURA: Knowledge Distillation for Interpretable Ambiguous Clause Identification in Legal Contracts

author.name: Amrita Singh, Aditya Joshi, Jiaojiao Jiang, Hye-young Paik

entry.summary: LAURA is a post-training framework for identifying ambiguous clauses in legal contracts while producing interpretable rationales, distinguishing harmful ambiguities from benignly flexible ones. It distills knowledge from a teacher LLM into an open-weight student model of at most 1B parameters using an IRAC-Unlearning prompting technique, then trains the student with a joint objective combining classification and rationale-generation losses. The goal is to let both legal and non-legal stakeholders act on the model's explanations.

entry.title: Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks

author.name: Zexiao Wang, Zihao Zhang, Xudong Wang, Pan Wang, Ziyi Ye, Haoyu Zhao, Zuxuan Wu, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: Chinese-Jev adapts System One decision models of the Jev family to Chinese-language tasks via a unified pipeline that converts heterogeneous Chinese annotations into probability targets over candidate options, using a lightweight encoder-only backbone for efficient inference. This fills a gap in Chinese-language decision accuracy for models that make decisions rather than generate text.

entry.title: AMU:Admission and Memory Update for Personalized Conversations---Structured Memory with SLM Guided Control

author.name: Tao Hwang, Yishi Diao

entry.summary: AMU introduces a small-language-model-guided framework for controlling what enters a user's long-term memory during personalized conversations, filtering transient requests, duplicates, and outdated states at write time. It combines structured memory filtering with storage management decisions, addressing an underexplored stage of the memory lifecycle.

entry.title: RunyaNER: Auxiliary Language Selection for Runyankore NER

author.name: Prosper Arineitwe Asiimwe, Francois Meyer, Jan Buys

entry.summary: Releases Runyankore, the first publicly available NER benchmark for the East African language Runyankore, with over 237k manually verified annotated words across 30k sentences built via a semi-automated pipeline. The authors use it to study which auxiliary language selection strategies work best for cross-lingual zero-shot and multilingual transfer in low-resource NER.

entry.title: AnthroDial: Benchmarking LLM Anthropomorphism in Autonomous Social Interaction

author.name: Wentao Liu, Xi Chen, Siyu Song, Biao Yuan, Yu Zhang, Zhou Zhuotong, Jingying Zhou, Guohao Feng, Shasha Hu, Tianfu Wang, Shangshang Yang, Haoyang Liu, Youjia Li, Xiaokun Wang, Min Ji, Ji Wang

entry.summary: Introduces AnthroDial, a unified framework for developing and evaluating anthropomorphic social agents, combining MindFlow (an asynchronous interaction harness with a dynamic Mind Buffer for autonomous communication decisions), CAPS-Eval (a theory-grounded evaluation framework), and improvement mechanisms. It targets continuous, open-ended social interaction rather than turn-taking chat.

entry.title: Retrieval Capacity of Self-Attention Under Competition

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Radu State

entry.summary: Estimates how many context tokens a language model effectively uses by retaining only highest-attention tokens per head, layer, and query and measuring negative log-likelihood increase as set size shrinks. Relatively small attention-selected sets keep NLL close to full attention, with substantial gains over random selection and structured geometric organization of selected sets.

entry.title: Layer-Informed Fine-Tuning via Three-Stage Functional Segmentation of LLMs

author.name: Junning Shao, Siwei Wang, Zhixuan Fang

entry.summary: The authors hypothesize that LLM layers exhibit structured division of labor across conceptualization, reasoning, and textualization, testing this on cross-linguistic reasoning tasks. They propose a sensitivity-analysis-based bottleneck identification mechanism to locate the most critical functional stage for a task, then use it to guide layer-informed fine-tuning. This connects mechanistic understanding to practical parameter-efficient adaptation.

entry.title: Large Language Models Exhibit Human-Like Bayesian Hypocrisy

author.name: Nykko Vitali, Mahzarin R. Banaji

entry.summary: Across five experiments with over 5,000 trials, GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet were tested on Bayesian reasoning tasks and then on their judgments of a hypothetical person giving the same judgments. The models performed near human levels on the Bayesian task with more rule-based reasoning, and exhibited hypocrisy: condemning others for offering the very same Bayesian judgments they themselves produced, echoing human findings. This is a novel window into LLM social-evaluative behavior.

entry.title: Invariant Atoms: Sparse Coordinates of Local Semantic Geometry in Language Model Representations

author.name: Muhammad Ahtesham, Xin Zhong

entry.summary: The authors propose the Invariant Atom Hypothesis: local semantic motion in LLM representations admits preferred sparse coordinates along directions stable under meaning-preserving transformations. They learn a shared semantic frame with sparse coordinates that reconstruct semantic displacements while suppressing nuisance variation, showing strong semantic-nuisance separation empirically. This contributes to understanding how meaning is geometrically organized in representations.

entry.title: VStress: Correlation-Aware Auditing and Adaptive Budget Allocation for Repeated Verifiers

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Peng Zhang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: VStress studies when repeated calls to verifiers actually add conditional information, introducing an auditable replay contract and a correlation-aware allocation policy (VStress-CA) that estimates marginal information, discounts uncertainty, normalizes by cost, and stops or abstains when calls are uninformative. It also quantifies mechanism boundaries under corruption, e.g., majority voting improving accuracy at 35% corruption but failing at 65%. The work targets principled budget control in verifier-heavy inference pipelines.

entry.title: FORUM: Frozen Outputs Reconciled Using Model Agreement for Visual Grounding

author.name: Taiyo Sato, Takamasa Sanda, Keisuke Maeda, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama, Shunya Nagashima

entry.summary: FORUM is a training-free, test-time fusion method for visual grounding with frozen multimodal LLMs, exploiting the observation that models from different data and architectures rarely fall for the same adversarial confounders. It uses agreement-based selection across distinct models plus medoid localization returning an actual member box rather than an averaged coordinate, improving robustness on benchmarks with same-category distractors and negation. It targets confident-but-wrong failures of even the largest MLLMs.

entry.title: Can a Cacheable Decision Model Follow Rules?

author.name: Dushyant Rajput (AltSlate Labs LLP), Nirdesh Chauhan (AltSlate Labs LLP), Siddharth Kosaraju (AltSlate Labs LLP)

entry.summary: Certo is a small non-generative decision model (Qwen3-4B based) that scores candidate actions and returns probabilities; the paper studies how much rule-sensitivity survives when moving from a joint state-candidate scorer to an independently encoded, cacheable scorer that is roughly 5x cheaper. The cacheable conversion drops recall@1 from 1.00 to 0.24, and a shortlist-plus-rerank rescue fails, though targeted counterfactual training partially recovers rule sensitivity. It quantifies a real cost-accuracy tradeoff in deployable decision models.

entry.title: Strike a Chord! Modal Kinetic Typography

author.name: Maham Tanveer, Jiyeon Han, Nanxuan Zhao, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces modal kinetic typography, animating vector glyphs via their natural vibration modes computed from a finite-element eigenproblem over the glyph outline, with rigid zero-energy modes applied in closed form to glyph parts. A frozen video diffusion model supervises only the modes' amplitudes and phases, producing semantically expressive yet legible letter animation while avoiding artifacts of free-form point optimization under score distillation.
