It is a creative graphics contribution combining physics and generative models.

entry.title: Curating Synthetic Data for Task-Specific Visual Perception

author.name: Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Paul Julius K\"uhn, Michael Weinmann

entry.summary: This position-style article argues that the central question for specialized vision systems is not how to generate more synthetic data but which data to generate, introducing the notion of curated synthetic data designed around a given task. It examines three complementary curation paradigms: procedural rendering with by-construction annotations, physically-based simulation encoding causal mechanisms, and a third paradigm surveyed in the text. The work frames synthetic data curation as a design problem spanning scene content, appearance, sensing, and annotations.

entry.title: AdaOcc: Adaptive 3D Occupancy Prediction for Embodied Tasks

author.name: Jinglong Wang, Yunjie Wang, Zhiyang Zhang, Jiawei He, Ye Yuan, Bo Qiu, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AdaOcc, a point-based adaptive 3D semantic occupancy prediction method for embodied scenarios that adapts to varying compute budgets, sensor setups, and observation views. It uses an adaptive geometry-guided dual-branch encoder supporting RGB inputs from variable numbers of views with estimated depth maps.

entry.title: How to Reduce Localization Ambiguity? Geometry-Semantic Constrained BEV Representation Learning for Satellite-Ground Localization

author.name: Junming Feng, Panwang Xia, Qiong Wu, Xudong Lu, Zeyu Jiao, Kun Lv, Zherong Wu, Yi Wan, Peifeng Ma, Li-Ta Hsu, Zhi Zheng

entry.summary: GeoSem-BEV improves cross-view satellite-ground localization by addressing two ambiguity sources in shared BEV spaces: geometric ambiguity from weak depth constraints along viewing directions, and descriptor ambiguity from visually similar locations lacking semantic supervision. It introduces radial depth supervision and semantic constraints to disambiguate feature placement and matching.

entry.title: COBICount: Separating Object and Background Responses for Remote Sensing Object Counting Without Training on Target Data

author.name: Junjing Zheng, Zhiyi Zhou, Ningrui Yang, Hongying Meng

entry.summary: COBICount studies source-only remote sensing object counting, where no target data is available for training or adaptation. The method separates object and background responses to improve cross-region, cross-sensor, and cross-category transfer, reducing costly data annotation requirements.

entry.title: Introduction to Computer Vision

author.name: Stan Birchfield

entry.summary: This is a code-first introductory textbook by Stan Birchfield spanning classical 2D image processing, classical 3D vision, and deep learning, organized as 44 short chapters across three parts with each topic built from first principles. It covers image arithmetic through projective geometry, structure from motion, convolutional networks, segmentation, and engineering topics like mixed-precision training.

entry.title: Hyperspectral Image Models: Technical Report

author.name: Tanishq Rachamalla, Aryan Das, Srishti Kaushik, Swalpa Kumar Roy

entry.summary: This technical report presents a modular framework unifying 55 hyperspectral image classification models across six deep learning paradigms (CNNs, ViTs, Mamba, GNNs, KANs, masked autoencoders) with standardized tensor adaptation and evaluation. It integrates 24 benchmark scenes from airborne, spaceborne, UAV, and Mars CRISM sensors.

entry.title: Beyond Missing Rates: Rethinking Incomplete Multi-View Clustering with Protocol Divergence

author.name: Haolu Liu, Xiyue Wang, Xuanting Xie, Liangjian Wen, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: This paper shows that incomplete multi-view clustering evaluations indexed only by nominal missing rate can mask large structural differences, introducing protocol divergence to quantify disparities among missing-view protocols that differ by roughly 50-fold in fully observed samples. The authors analyze support-gated reconstruction mechanisms and reveal inherent optimization pathologies. The work calls for more rigorous evaluation methodology in IMVC research.

entry.title: TSGL: Teacher-Student Graph Learning for 3DGS Compression

author.name: Matin Bani Saedi, Matthew Kyan, Gene Cheung

entry.summary: TSGL is a 3D Gaussian Splatting compression method that operates post-hoc on trained models without retraining or access to original training images. It learns signal-dependent geometry graphs over blocks of Gaussians via a teacher-student model, then applies Graph Fourier Transform to remaining attributes for compact coding. This addresses the large file sizes of 3DGS representations with millions of richly attributed primitives.

entry.title: Optimize, Learn, Refine: Whole-Body Grasping and Pick-and-Throw with a Spiral Soft Robot

author.name: Marwah Basuhai, Tingcong Liu, Ibrahim Alsarraj, Yuhao Wang, Ke Wu

entry.summary: The paper addresses whole-body grasping and pick-and-throw with a soft continuum robot via outcome-based actuation-space optimization, quantifying grasping through tip angular sweep and body-object enclosure. Because the actuation-to-outcome mapping is nonsmooth, the authors use derivative-free CMA-ES within an optimize-learn-refine pipeline, letting grasping, acceleration, and release emerge from compliant interaction without prescribed contacts.

entry.title: L1-MPPI: L1 Adaptive Model Predictive Path Integral for Agile UAV Control

author.name: Luk\'a\v{s} Kotek, Ond\v{r}ej Proch\'azka, Vojt\v{e}ch Von\'asek, Martin Saska, Robert P\v{e}ni\v{c}ka

entry.summary: L1-MPPI cascades L1 adaptive control with Model Predictive Path Integral control to improve high-speed UAV trajectory tracking under model uncertainty, payloads, and aerodynamic drag mismatch. Unlike existing MPPI UAV approaches, it incorporates low-level flight controller and motor dynamics into the MPPI model with iterative refinement.

entry.title: Yggdrasil: a Layer-First 3D Scene Graph for Real-Time Querying

author.name: Arshia Akhavan, Ermanno Bartoli, Afnan Algharbi, Alireza Hoseinpur, Iolanda Leite, Bryan Donyanavard

entry.summary: Yggdrasil is a layer-first hierarchical 3D scene graph built from generic nodes, edges, and layers, designed to be efficient for both generation and consumption so perception pipelines can meet real-time query latency budgets. It targets the underexplored consumption side of scene graphs, which current pipelines work around at a latency cost.

entry.title: FlapKAD: A Simulation Dataset of Coupled Wing Kinematics and Aerodynamic Dynamics for Flapping-Wing Aerial Vehicles

author.name: Haichuan Li

entry.summary: FlapKAD is a large simulation dataset for flapping-wing aerial vehicles with 2,000 rigid-wing flight episodes and over 720,000 time steps that synchronously record bilateral wing kinematics, aerodynamic responses, and flight states on a common clock. It is designed to overcome the scale and temporal-misalignment limitations of existing datasets and supports bidirectional sequence-prediction benchmarks.

entry.title: PhaseSync-Exo: Human Clock Anchored Reference Adaptation for Dynamic Gait Tracking

author.name: Kaijie Qi, Yuehan Wang, Kaiming Xu, Chong Li, Jiakuo Yu

entry.summary: PhaseSync-Exo is an exoskeleton gait tracking system combining a CNN-Transformer gait reconstruction module (3.24 degree MAE), amplitude-cadence retargeting with a curriculum-trained recurrent controller, and a human-clock-anchored adapter that adapts reference timing while preserving forward progression. The frozen tracking policy passed 356 of 357 amplitude-frequency trials.

entry.title: Communication-Free Distributed Multi-Robot Task Allocation under Partial Observations Using Labeled Multi-Bernoulli Filtering

author.name: Takumi Ito, Akiya Kamimura

entry.summary: This paper proposes a communication-free multi-robot task allocation method where each robot estimates neighbor positions with a Labeled Multi-Bernoulli filter and independently assigns tasks via greedy auction, continuously reallocating during execution. Monte Carlo simulations show effective decentralized coordination robust to clutter and observation noise. Communication-free coordination is valuable for swarms in degraded or denied communication environments.

entry.title: Active Mapping of Underwater Litter Using Camera-Sonar Fusion

author.name: David Rete, Patrick Boros, Lucian Busoniu

entry.summary: The paper proposes an active mapping framework for locating underwater marine litter that fuses camera and forward-looking sonar into a shared Bayesian occupancy map, solving a next-best-view optimization at each step. Viewpoints are scored by balancing exploration via voxel entropy against exploitation of likely debris locations, overcoming the limitations of either modality alone in poor-visibility underwater conditions.

entry.title: Signal Processing over Product DAGs: Causal Shifts and Filters

author.name: Sundeep Prabhakar Chepuri, Antonio G. Marques, Maulik Devmurari, Gonzalo Mateos

entry.summary: The paper develops a signal processing framework for signals indexed by the product of two directed acyclic graphs under a linear structural equation model, arising when causal relations act along two domains such as component versus manufacturing stage. The authors introduce a new DAG product under which transitive closures are factorizable, enabling efficient Fourier-type analysis without inverting product-sized matrices.

entry.title: Optimal Allocation and Volume under Surface

author.name: Kai Feng, Han Hong, Jessie Li, Wenshi Wei

entry.summary: The paper builds a framework for estimation and inference on volumes of projections of critical function sets, focusing on the convex body beneath the optimal ROC surface, using an Aumann expectation representation and Minkowski mixed volumes. It shows the volume under the ROC surface is proportional to the expectation of a symmetric U-statistic kernel and proposes a double/debiased machine learning estimator with asymptotic properties and inference procedures.

entry.title: Amortized ratio-estimation importance sampling and localized simulation-based calibration for intractable likelihoods

author.name: Umberto Picchini

entry.summary: The paper develops a sequential simulation-based Bayesian inference procedure for models with intractable likelihoods, using localized mixture-of-experts surrogates as proposals and correcting the final posterior via importance sampling with a locally amortized likelihood-to-evidence ratio estimator. It also introduces a localized variant of simulation-based calibration for diagnostics.

entry.title: Frontier models state different decision theory preferences depending on who's asking

author.name: Alex Kastner

entry.summary: The author reports that frontier models almost always endorse functional decision theory when prompted neutrally, but shift to CDT 30-100% of the time when prompts hint at an academic-philosophy provenance; similar audience-dependent shifts appear for moral realism, p-zombies, P(doom), and AGI timelines. The post frames this as user-awareness sycophancy and draws implications for interpreting attitude evaluations.

entry.title: How to give embedded evaluators the support they need: Lessons from the finance industry

author.name: gregkirczenow

entry.summary: Drawing on the author's experience as a bank model validator interacting with Federal Reserve regulators, this post offers concrete design recommendations for Dario Amodei's proposed 'embedded evaluators' at AI labs. It suggests splitting the evaluator role between strengthened internal risk teams with blocking authority and external supervisors, with embedded evaluators initially auditing risk-team effectiveness and reserving independent testing for the most critical checks. This transfers an operational governance model that has worked in finance to frontier AI oversight.

entry.title: GATE-ST: Gene-Aware Text-image Encoder for Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Lucas Ni, Jian Luo, Wentao Huang, Chao Chen

entry.summary: GATE-ST incorporates gene text descriptions into image-based prediction of spatial gene expression from slide-level images, exploiting an underexplored text-based optimization direction. This could reduce reliance on expensive, time-consuming spatial transcriptomics assays. The multimodal text-image approach is relevant to disease mechanism studies and treatment development.

entry.title: OverForge: Reasoning Through Strategies and Tactics Helps Cooperative Lifelong Adaptation

author.name: Oana Madalina Fron, Ojas Shirekar, Chirag Raman

entry.summary: OverForge is a training-free hierarchical architecture for cooperative LLM agents that separates strategic reasoning about roles and division of labor from tactical action reasoning within partner-conditioned world models, coupled by a metacognitive module that imagines consequences before committing. On OvercookedV2 it delivers 7 soups in coordination with unfamiliar partners, improving lifelong adaptation.

entry.title: Automatic estimation of verbal fluency index in people with Motor Neuron Disease using ASR alignment and pause modelling

author.name: Bahman Mirheidari, Leslie Ing, Daniel Blackburn, Sharon Abrahams, Christopher McDermott, Heidi Christensen

entry.summary: The authors build a system that automatically estimates the Verbal Fluency Index from the ECAS cognitive assessment in motor neuron disease patients, combining WhisperX ASR and Silero VAD with refined timestamping. The approach outperformed baselines built on traditional acoustic features and self-supervised embeddings on a unique MND dataset. This enables scalable cognitive-impairment monitoring in a population where speech is difficult.

entry.title: Learning Under Forgetting: Statistical Support-Selective Retention in Stochastic Training Dynamics

author.name: Fujie Gao, Zuyue Zhang, Gang Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Repeated Reinforcement with Persistent Forgetting (RPF) dynamics, a minimal theoretical framework in which recurring data patterns are reinforced while persistent forgetting attenuates learned information, treating forgetting as a selection mechanism rather than a failure mode. The theory is built in layers, deriving exposure-selective survival laws and support-dependent results in an independent-feature model.

entry.title: On the Relaxation of Conditional Independence Assumption for Image Segmentation

author.name: Zixun Wang, Ben Dai

entry.summary: The paper relaxes the restrictive Conditional Independence Assumption in RankSEG methods for direct Dice/IoU optimization by introducing a Spatially Localized Dependence structure that captures local label correlations tractably, avoiding the cubic cost of full label dependence. This improves performance in ambiguous and low-contrast segmentation scenarios.

entry.title: WinoTS: Wavelet-based Self-Distillation for Time Series Models

author.name: Noam Major, Kathy Razmadze, Yoli Shavit

entry.summary: WinoTS adapts invariance-based self-distillation, proven effective in computer vision, to time series pre-training via wavelet-based augmentations that avoid the pitfalls of cropping and jittering on temporal signals. It argues that dominant next-token and reconstruction objectives waste capacity on high-frequency noise rather than learning invariant structure.

entry.title: LEAP: Learned Block-wise Evidence Retrieval for Long Audio-Video Perception

author.name: Juyi Lin, Zhiqiang Lao, Jiali Cui, Lin Zhao, Pu Zhao, Dichang Zhang, Arman Akbari, Yu Qi, Xinru Jiang, Yanzhi Wang, Heather Yu, Liang Peng

entry.summary: LEAP tackles hour-scale audio-visual question answering by splitting recordings into fixed-duration blocks and using a lightweight localization pass to score candidate windows, then pooling and re-encoding the top windows in a bounded answer pass. This keeps peak context independent of recording duration by decoupling evidence localization from reasoning.

entry.title: Molecular Property Prediction under Structural Shift with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Jinmo Lee, Dooho Lee, Minho Jeong, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: The paper studies structural generalization in molecular property prediction and introduces MolPAIR, a training-free framework combining molecule-level and molecular-pair in-context contexts with frozen tabular foundation models. A first TFM predicts query properties from labeled examples; a second frozen TFM refines predictions using molecular-pair comparisons, improving robustness under structural shift relevant to drug discovery.

entry.title: ReSCENE: Server-Side Replay for Structural Mitigation of Catastrophic Forgetting in Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Sungmin Kang, Zhengzhong Tu, Sunwoo Lee

entry.summary: ReSCENE mitigates catastrophic forgetting in federated continual learning by having clients upload small condensed data surrogates while the server stores surrogates from past tasks and co-trains the global model on them with the current task. Temporal herding selects recent surrogates for memory efficiency, and the approach avoids burdening resource-constrained clients with anti-forgetting mechanisms. This shifts the forgetting problem from client-side constraints to a server-side structural solution.

entry.title: The Missing Coefficients: Bayesian Pairwise Merging for Model Personalization

author.name: Yaling Shen, Tongtong Wu, Siyuan Yan, Gholamreza Haffari

entry.summary: The paper addresses personalizing a shared library of reward-specialized expert models from user pairwise choices rather than explicit numerical trade-off weights. Bayesian Pairwise Merging treats unknown reward weights as latent variables, inferring a posterior from pairwise choices and reward-score differences and using the posterior mean as merge coefficients, while the posterior also characterizes ambiguity under limited feedback. This turns natural preference feedback directly into model-merging weights.

entry.title: Attention Function as an Intrinsic Inductive Bias: How Models' Behavior Diverges in Novel Contexts

author.name: Dong Gyun Kang, Megha Thukral, Kwangsoo Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Mixture of Function Attention (MoFA), a parameter-free modification fixing a ratio of softmax and sigmoid attention heads, drawing an analogy to innate priors in developmental psychology. Across GPT-2 experiments, the preset ratio has little in-distribution effect but changes behavior in weakly constrained, novel contexts.

entry.title: Network-based Spatial Context Retrieval for Open-weight LLMs: A Faithfulness Benchmark for Grounded Geographic Reasoning

author.name: Joan Perez

entry.summary: The paper presents an open pipeline that retrieves pedestrian-network-based spatial context from OpenStreetMap for open-weight LLMs, and introduces a faithfulness benchmark asking whether models reason from supplied context or override it with parametric recall. It targets grounded geographic reasoning, where models are unreliable when queried from coordinates alone.

entry.title: PEG-Tab: Sampling-Time Record Repair and Release Control for Tabular Synthesis

author.name: Pengfei Li, QinYi Liu, Mohammad Khalil

entry.summary: PEG-Tab is a post-training framework that reduces memorization (near-copy leakage) in frozen pretrained tabular generators by generating candidate alternatives per row and applying a calibrated score plus release check. It works across GReaT, CTGAN, TVAE, and TabDDPM without retraining, cutting near-copy rates across five datasets.

entry.title: Patient-Centered Treatment Planning for Chronic Multimorbidity: A Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning Framework for Preference Modeling

author.name: Nafiseh Payani, Soham Das, G. Anthony Wilson, Anahita Khojandi

entry.summary: The paper presents FAHOC, a hierarchical RL framework for treatment planning in chronic multimorbidity that models patient preference and adherence via factored intra-option policies and cooperation-aware action masking. This enables structured exploration and improved credit assignment while incorporating a patient-centered objective absent from prior computational planning work.

entry.title: A Parameter-Free Zeroth-Order Method with Covariance Matrix Adaptation and Effective Dimension

author.name: Alexander Sholokhov, Alexander Rogozin

entry.summary: POEM-CMA extends the parameter-free POEM zeroth-order optimizer with covariance matrix adaptation and an effective-dimension notion, replacing isotropic random directions with anisotropic sampling focused on informative directions. This improves black-box optimization where gradients are unavailable or expensive.

entry.title: Training-Free Affinity Fusion of Neural and Embedding-Based Speaker Diarization

author.name: Yehoshua Dissen, Joseph Keshet, Eduard Golshtein

entry.summary: TFAF integrates the speaker partition inferred by a neural diarizer into an embedding-based diarization system by conditioning local speaker representations on the neural partition, building a continuous affinity matrix fused with the acoustic affinity before global clustering. It requires no additional training, shared embedding space, or speaker-label alignment and improves accuracy in experiments.

entry.title: Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts

author.name: Guangren Wang

entry.summary: Mnemon is a memory agent that keeps conversations as raw dated records and divides memory work System-1/System-2 style: a fast decision model makes many small yes/no judgments about records in a third of a second, while an LLM handles slow query writing and answer composition. It avoids write-time rewriting into facts or graphs.

entry.title: Cognitive Expert Language Models Better Align with the Corresponding Brain Systems

author.name: Zhivar Sourati, Mengxuan Helen Wu, Nona Ghazizadeh, Jonas Kaplan, Morteza Dehghani, Samuel A. Nastase

entry.summary: The authors build expert LLM variants for six cognitive domains via prompting and fine-tuning, then test whether each domain expert better predicts brain activity in the corresponding specialized brain system during language comprehension. This challenges the one-model-fits-all approach to LLM-brain alignment studies. The work connects cognitive neuroscience with language model research in a novel way.

entry.title: The Geometry of Inference in Transformer Residual Streams

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Radu State

entry.summary: Examines how transformer residual states become specific to an eventual prediction by comparing intermediate states with their own final states and a bank of final states from other contexts, across six pretrained models. Findings show directional alignment improves with depth even when Euclidean distance to the final state changes little, and surviving candidate endpoints need not become mutually similar.

entry.title: How Many Labels Does a Language Need? Annotation Budgets and Cross-Lingual Pooling for African-Language Text Classification

author.name: Bhanu Prakash Vangala, Sowmya Guda, Navya Vangala

entry.summary: Empirically answers budgeting questions for African-language text classification across 28 language-task pairs using a fast character n-gram linear model: topic classification reaches 90 percent of full-data macro-F1 with roughly 400 labels in the median language, while sentiment keeps improving at full training size in 11 of 12 languages. Also tests how well labels from other African languages substitute for target-language labels.

entry.title: A Polyphonic Conception of AI Understanding

author.name: Matthieu Queloz, Pierre Beckmann

entry.summary: This philosophy-oriented paper argues that the question of whether AI models understand is ill-framed by a monophonic paradigm that localizes understanding in a single mechanism. Drawing on mechanistic evidence that LLM outputs arise from coalitions of parallel mechanisms, the authors propose a polyphonic conception of understanding relevant to practitioners like doctors and judges deciding when to trust model outputs. It bridges interpretability findings with practical trust decisions.

entry.title: Long-Term Memory-Guided Enhancement for Target Perception in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Zhenhong Zhou, Xuanyue Zhao, Youji Liu, Yuanhe Zhang, Xiaoyu Ma, Lianyu Hu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: LTM-AE improves target-sound perception in audio LLMs under real-world noise by using hidden-state representations from clean reference recordings as category-level long-term memory, reconstructing incoming audio tokens within that memory without any training. Inspired by human selective listening, the training-free enhancement refines audio representations inside the model. This addresses a real robustness gap for audio-language models deployed in noisy environments.

entry.title: PLRS-IC: A Dual-Calibration Framework for Chest X-Ray Vision-Language Alignment

author.name: Qixing Zhao, Jinpeng Li

entry.summary: PLRS-IC improves fine-grained chest X-ray vision-language alignment by addressing projection-induced visual mismatch between frontal and lateral radiographs and semantic overlap where instance-level contrastive objectives wrongly penalize cross-patient pairs sharing positive clinical findings. The dual-calibration framework enables zero-shot classification, grounding, and segmentation without task-specific annotations.

entry.title: Lens Flare Removal and Reconstruction

author.name: Tarun Yenamandra, Jonathon Luiten, Daniel Cremers, Nathan Matsuda

entry.summary: The authors compile a novel dataset for large lens-flare removal combining real-world data with a procedural generation pipeline and fine-tune a diffusion model to remove complex, image-filling flares. Because flares are camera artifacts rather than scene content, their removal improves downstream 3D scene reconstruction quality.

entry.title: FANVIDv2: Evaluating Video Super-Resolution by Face and Licence-Plate Recognition Under Compound Degradation

author.name: Kavitha Viswanathan, Vrinda Goel, Shlesh Gholap, Devayan Ghosh, Madhav Gupta, Dhruvi Ganatra, Sanket Potdar, Amit Sethi

entry.summary: FANVIDv2 is a benchmark that scores video super-resolution by downstream recognition of faces and license plates rather than PSNR/SSIM, using randomized compound degradations (blur, noise, compression, downsampling) instead of bicubic-only pipelines. It provides low-resolution clips with HR references for 48 public figures and 375 license-plate clips, scoring recognition inside detection pipelines.

entry.title: Super-Resolving Unseen Hyperspectral Sensors at Any Scale via Spatial Operators

author.name: Ji-Xuan He, Guohang Zhuang, Bo Junge, Tingyi Li, Lingchen, Miaomiao Cai, Yanan Qiao, Xiujin Liu, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: OmniHSR predicts band-shared spatial operators instead of spectral values, combining cross-spectral mapping and continuous operator-field reconstruction to enable cross-sensor generalization and arbitrary-scale hyperspectral super-resolution in one model without per-sensor retraining.

entry.title: Joint Supervised and Self-Supervised Training with Acquisition-Robust Techniques for Accelerated 4D Flow MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Mengyuan Xue, Bochun Mei

entry.summary: The paper improves accelerated 4D flow MRI reconstruction by combining joint supervised and self-supervised training with acquisition-robust conditioning strategies based on acceleration factors, using both magnitude and velocity data. On the CMRx4DFlow 2026 aortic dataset at 1.5T and 3T, the model reduces relative error by 38-50 percent and angular error by 7.0-8.7 degrees versus a training-matched baseline. This shortens long acquisition times needed for time-resolved blood velocity imaging.

entry.title: Drone Soccer: Learning to Manipulate with Multicopter Downwash

author.name: Neelay Joglekar, Bavin Saravanan, Yutong Wang, Varun Kandiyappan, Junyi Geng, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: This paper reframes downwash, typically treated as a disturbance, as an active manipulation tool by training an RL policy on a simplified downwash dynamics model to dribble a soccer ball with a multicopter. The policy demonstrates transfer to real drones, establishing drone soccer as a testbed for downwash-based aerial manipulation.

entry.title: AIfred: Augmented Learning through Functional Robotic Embodiment at the Desk

author.name: Gregorio Orlando, Milan Groshev, Eduardo Castell\'o Ferrer

entry.summary: AIfred is a desk-based robotic arm with an end-effector-mounted projector that places AI-generated guidance directly alongside a user's handwritten work for math, image generation, and drawing tasks. A 36-participant user study compared it against GPT-5.6 Luna on a laptop, finding comparable performance while assistance was available, with the key contribution being the physical co-location of AI guidance with the workspace.

entry.title: Sparse Planner: A Hybrid Planner for Efficient Sampling via a Conditional Variational Autoencoder

author.name: Wenguang Xu, Giovanni Lucente, Karem Mohamed, Richard Membarth

entry.summary: Sparse Planner improves sample-based motion planning for autonomous driving by learning the conditional relationship between scene context and effective trajectory parameters using a Conditional VAE, reducing the need for dense sampling. This lowers computational overhead and runtime variability in complex traffic scenarios while maintaining solution quality. Real-time, reliable trajectory planning directly affects autonomous driving safety.

entry.title: Passive Stiffness Shaping in Cable-Suspended Aerial Manipulation via Movable Compliant Anchors

author.name: Antonio Franchi, Amr Afifi

entry.summary: This work develops a gravity-aware quasi-static theory treating aerial vehicles as movable compliant anchors to predict and shape the passive Cartesian stiffness of a suspended load in cable-suspended aerial manipulation. The formulation covers arbitrary numbers of vehicles with taut cables, combining anchor compliance and transverse cable geometric compliance in series within each leg.

entry.title: Adaptive mixture variational inference for spike-and-slab regression

author.name: Hanqing Li, Yaroslav Golub, Xuewen Lu

entry.summary: This paper develops an adaptive fitting procedure for mixtures of product distributions in Gaussian spike-and-slab regression, minimizing reverse KL divergence directly on inclusion indicators and active coefficients while jointly refining component parameters and weights as the mixture grows. The analysis connects approximation accuracy to mixture size, support coverage, and within-support dependence, addressing correlated predictors that support competing sparse explanations.

entry.title: Better Deck or Different Judge? Evaluating Agentic Harness Gains in Corporate and Investment Banking

author.name: Ludovic Gibert, Matis Despujols, Andre-Louis Rochet

entry.summary: This retrospective study evaluates an agentic harness (a 27B language model plus financial calculations, templates, and validation checks) for producing investment-banking presentations, asking whether LLM-judge score gains reflect better documents or judge drift. Using shared-session text-only grading with template markers removed, five judges score the full system 20.4 to 33.6 points out of 95 above the same model generating directly.

entry.title: ChartDensity-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Numerical Data Reconstruction under Visual Density

author.name: Xinhe Wu, Yadong Jin

entry.summary: Introduces ChartDensity-Bench, a benchmark evaluating multimodal LLMs on structured numerical data reconstruction from compound scientific chart figures under controlled visual density, using charts paired with source-level ground-truth data. It fills a gap left by chart QA benchmarks that do not test precise structured reconstruction from dense figures.

entry.title: LongEmo: Towards Emotion Understanding and Reasoning in Long Videos

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Yifan Zhou, Han Wang, Jinsong Zhang, Jingyu Li, Hongbing Li, Zhejun Zhang, Chengyi Zhao, Yuquan Hao, Yitong Liu, Jiyin Li, Ruiqi Tang, Zixuan Lin, Yi Luo, Xurui Zhang, Ronghao Chen, Huacan Wang, Lei Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces LongEmoBench, a benchmark for emotion understanding and reasoning in long videos that scales from continuous scene interactions to complex episodic developments, plus LongEmo, a memory-augmented agentic framework for long-range affective reasoning. It argues that real emotions are cumulative processes shaped by past events, which current MLLMs handle poorly.

entry.title: Geometry-physics confounding impairs PDE learning across varying domains

author.name: Yinghao Cheng, Gengxiang Chen, Xu Liu, Qinglu Meng, Yixin Jing, Xiangguo Tang, Wenping Mou, Lihui Wang, Yingguang Li

entry.summary: This paper identifies geometry-physics confounding as a unified failure mechanism in learning PDE dynamics across varying geometric domains: geometric variation alters both field representation and governing operators, conflating geometric effects with intrinsic physical properties. The authors analyze how this degrades forward operator learning (data efficiency, generalization) and equation discovery (operator-library misspecification), and propose mitigation directions.

entry.title: VERA: Verifiable Feasibility Representations with Counterfactual Credit for Constrained Multi-Agent Control

author.name: Bo Yin, Dongbo Li, Hongkai Chen, Jie Liu, Guoliang Xing

entry.summary: VERA is a centralized-training, decentralized-execution framework for constrained multi-agent control that separates feasibility estimation from credit assignment, with each actor predicting a five-dimensional verifiable feasibility representation supervised by exact action-conditioned margins. A counterfactual group-relative advantage mechanism ranks candidate representation-action pairs, and execution requires only one actor pass without privileged state. In dynamic space-air-ground integrated networks, it reportedly yields large gains.

entry.title: Also Small Models Can Reasonably Self-Evaluate Their Confidence

author.name: Idil Kapikiran, Thomas Decker, Thomas Runkler

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates self-evaluation-based uncertainty quantification across language models of varying sizes on QA tasks. It finds that while accuracy drops with smaller models and specialized domains, the reliability of self-assessed confidence stays largely stable, implying the most capable model is not necessarily best at judging its own reliability.

entry.title: CNCGEN: A Dataset and Framework for Machining Process Planning and Toolpath Generation from B-rep Models

author.name: Xiaolei Zhou, Boyi Lin, Yuchao Feng, Jianwei Zheng

entry.summary: CNCGEN introduces a dataset and learning framework for generating three-axis machining process plans and toolpaths directly from B-rep CAD models, formulated around persistent manufacturing objects and evolving stock state. The dataset includes about 50k geometrically verified synthetic machining flows and 800 real CNC examples.

entry.title: CORD: Learning Reusable Degradation Representations Across Heterogeneous Physical Systems

author.name: Haibo Li, Zhiguo Zeng

entry.summary: CORD is a self-supervised pretraining framework for prognostics that combines type-specific observation interfaces with a shared degradation backbone, using intra-observation structure modeling and inter-observation dynamics modeling objectives. It is evaluated under two transfer regimes probing whether representations generalize to unseen system types and units.

entry.title: Scalable Cox Regression via Grouped Risk Sets and Sharper LogSumExp Rates

author.name: Elizaveta Iashchinskaia, Egor Gladin

entry.summary: The authors develop a softplus surrogate for stochastic LogSumExp minimization that yields unbiased single-sample gradients, proving an O(T^-1/2) rate improving prior T^-1/4 analysis and a last-iterate squared-error rate under strong convexity. Applied to Cox regression via grouped risk sets, this enables scalable survival analysis.

entry.title: Disentangling Computation in Multi-Task Neural Networks with the Green's Operator

author.name: James Hazelden

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how computation is organized and reused across tasks and time in trained recurrent networks via the finite-horizon Green's operator, which maps perturbations along a trajectory to downstream state-space responses. Matrix-free products make task-to-task and time-to-time views computationally accessible without constructing the full operator. The analysis reveals structured reuse of known computational motifs in multitask recurrent networks.

entry.title: TutlAit v1: a crowdsourced Moroccan Tamazight speech dataset with Arabic transcriptions and regional accent labels

author.name: Mohamed-Amine Chadi, Ezzahra Ait El Arbi, Ismail Khayoub, Aymane Fadili, Yassine Ennhili, Jadjigua Bouali, Hanane Inhid, Mohammed Ameksa, Hajar Mousannif

entry.summary: TutlAit v1 is a crowdsourced corpus of Moroccan Tamazight speech paired with Modern Standard Arabic transcriptions and explicit regional accent labels, collected via a purpose-built web application recruiting native speakers through social campaigns. Tamazight is an official language of Morocco yet severely under-resourced for speech technology. The dataset addresses scarcity, missing regional metadata, and uneven transcription quality in existing resources.

entry.title: Asymptotic Properties of Support Vector Machines in High-Dimension, Low-Sample-Size Settings under a Spiked Model

author.name: Yugo Nakayama

entry.summary: The paper shows that the classical geometric representation of HDLSS data breaks down under spiked covariance models, with data converging to a random configuration whose dimension equals the number of spikes. Consequently, SVM misclassification rates do not vanish, revising prior HDLSS SVM theory under realistic covariance structure.

entry.title: LLM unbranding: Erasing Commercial Identity while Preserving Generic Utility

author.name: Kajetan O\.z\'og, Alicja Wojciechowska, Dawid Malarz, Pawe{\l} Batorski, Artur Kasymov, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: This paper formally defines the novel task of LLM Unbranding: neutralizing brand-identifying language, slogans, and stylistic markers in LLM text outputs to mitigate trademark dilution, false attribution, and defamation, analogous to unbranding in image generation. It addresses the harder textual version of trade dress management where brand markers are subtler than visual logos.

entry.title: Evaluating and Benchmarking the System One Model Jev

author.name: Tobias Deu{\ss}er, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: Evaluates Jev, a commercial non-generative System One model from TypeSafe AI that returns fixed-option choices, rubric positions, or calibrated probabilities, targeting small decisions in information-access pipelines. The authors run 346,009 zero-shot requests across 37 datasets covering classification, routing, NLI, moderation, and rubric scoring to assess whether vendor calibration claims hold.

entry.title: Selecting What Matters: Semantic Compression-Guided Selective Pooling for Long-Context Embeddings

author.name: Zifeng Cheng, Jie Zheng, Zhiwei Jiang, Shuwen Wang, Fei Shen, Shiping Ge, Qing Gu

entry.summary: Proposes SCSP, a training-free framework for long-context text embeddings that uses semantic compression prompts per sentence-aware chunk to select informative tokens instead of uniform mean pooling, which dilutes salient semantics in long documents. A prompt-isolated attention mask preserves information integrity during compression-guided selection.

entry.title: Masked Swingers: Harnessing Data Augmentation to Advance Autoencoders for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Anthony Fuller, Scott C. Lowe, Daniel G. Kyrollos, Graham W. Taylor, Evan Shelhamer, James R. Green

entry.summary: Masked Swingers improves masked autoencoders by augmenting an image two ways, masking and encoding each view separately, then exchanging global CLS representations between views before decoding masked patches. This design encourages learning of view-invariant global representations within the reconstruction-based SSL framework. It combines ideas from contrastive learning with MAE-style reconstruction.

entry.title: Decoupling Spherical Reasoning from Dense Prediction for 360 Depth Estimation

author.name: Zhijie Shen, Chunyu Lin, Shuai Zheng, Feng Li, Runmin Cong, Huihui Bai, Yao Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling contextual reasoning in native spherical space from dense equirectangular prediction for panoramic depth estimation. A Fibonacci Spherical Graph lifts ERP features onto quasi-uniform spherical nodes to capture local and long-range dependencies, mitigating distortion from ERP's spatially varying stretching.

entry.title: MegaAvatar: Controllable Talking Avatar Generation

author.name: Junyao Gao, Sibo Liu, Weidong Zhang, Cairong Zhao, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: MegaAvatar is a controllable talking-avatar framework built on the existing Wan2.2-TI2V-5B video model, adding SMPL-X-derived 3D guidance rendered into dense mesh frames for body pose and head motion control, plus audio and face cross-attention modules for expression control and identity preservation. It extends beyond audio-only conditioning typical of prior talking-avatar methods.

entry.title: Front-to-Back: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Asymmetric Cross-View Vehicle Re-Identification

author.name: Moseli Mots'oehli, Thulani Babeli

entry.summary: Front2Back-ReID is a benchmark of 500 manually verified front-to-rear vehicle matches from South African recordings, evaluating seven zero-shot VLMs, four retrieval baselines, and 25 humans on matching vehicles across non-overlapping camera views. The strongest VLM reached 76.6 percent Rank-1 on crops, modestly above a reported human baseline figure, exposing both capability and geographic-bias issues.

entry.title: Local-Minimum Escaper: Programmatic Subgoal Generation for Robust Navigation in Unknown Environments

author.name: Yin Gu, Xinming Zhang, Shanze Wang, Siwei Cheng, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: LME is a programmatic hierarchical navigation framework that explicitly detects local-minimum situations in mapless unknown environments and generates interpretable subgoals using heuristic criteria to guide the robot out. This contrasts with deep RL approaches that learn recovery behaviors implicitly through reward design, offering an explicit, interpretable escape mechanism based only on local observations.

entry.title: Prediction is Better than Detection: Traffic Congestion Control using Drones

author.name: Samira Hayat, Christian Raffelsberger

entry.summary: The authors study how drone fleet size scales for traffic-jam detection and prediction in a simulated road network where drone reports drive an adaptive traffic-signal controller in closed loop, using Nagel-Schreckenberg vehicle dynamics and round-robin patrol. They find prediction outperforms mere detection and characterize detection rate, delay, and plateau effects across fleet size, traffic level, and network size. The finding that sensing-for-action changes scaling conclusions is broadly relevant to persistent monitoring deployments.

entry.title: A Mesoscopic View of Transformer Weights Through Row and Column Scale Fields

author.name: Tiexin Ding

entry.summary: This work studies the mesoscopic structure of transformer weight matrices via row and column scale fields, median-centred log-RMS profiles that together with a global scale and balanced core represent the matrix exactly. Analysis across Pythia checkpoints at four sizes and controlled runs reveals similar core magnitude profiles, and a pre-specified mixture bridge predicts pooled-shape behavior on held-out data.

entry.title: Concept-Grounded Attention: A Controlled Evaluation of Graph-Injected Attention, Temporal Versioning, and Epistemic Status

author.name: Sachin Dev Duggal, Pradyumna Swarnalatha Ramanna, Alexandros Vassiliades

entry.summary: The paper presents the Concept Lifecycle Model, representing knowledge as persistent, temporally versioned, graph-grounded entities with explicit provenance and epistemic status, plus Concept-Grounded Attention mechanisms that inject concept-graph structure into transformer self- and cross-attention. Controlled evaluations on MuSiQue and HotpotQA subsets with disabled-mechanism baselines test each component. It targets gaps in point-in-time reasoning and validated-versus-inferred knowledge distinctions.

entry.title: STRATA: Self-Learning Through Role-Aligned Tiered Agents for Real-Time Strategy Games

author.name: Xinhe Tian, Xiaoyue Zhang, Ziyou Zhang, Jiacheng Li, Xiaoqiang Jin, Qianchuan Zhao, Gaochen Cui

entry.summary: STRATA is a hierarchical LLM agent system for Red Alert that assigns role-aligned tiers for economic, production, defense, and tactical decisions, with cross-game self-learning to reduce dependence on hand-written prompts. It targets the latency problem that causes LLM planners to miss critical tactical events in real-time strategy games.

entry.title: Divide and Collapse: MAPF-Collapse via Exact Decomposition into Independent Sub-Instances

author.name: Oren Salzman

entry.summary: The paper studies MAPF-Collapse, an NP-hard post-optimization step that removes redundant moves from Multi-Agent Path Finding plans while preserving feasibility. Rather than solving a joint ILP over all agents as in prior work (Judgelight), it exploits exact decomposition into small coupled sub-instances, making cost depend on the residual coupling rather than the full instance.

entry.title: A Moving-Horizon Approximate Branch-and-Reduce Method for Deep Classification Trees

author.name: Chenxuanyin Zou, Jiayang Ren, Qiangqiang Mao, Jing Liu, Marcus Lai, Yankai Cao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a moving-horizon approximate branch-and-reduce method for training near-optimal deep classification trees on large datasets with continuous features, combining exact root-level optimization with greedy approximation of induced subtrees. This addresses the scalability limits of globally optimal decision tree methods while retaining interpretability.

entry.title: Derandomizing Dense Binary Hypervector Codebooks for Quantized Scalars

author.name: Dmitri Rachkovskij, Evgeny Osipov, Olexander Volkov, Denis Kleyko, Vaclav Snasel

entry.summary: The paper presents a transition-based derandomization framework for dense binary scalar codebooks in hyperdimensional computing, targeting similarity laws that decay exponentially or linearly with level separation. It systematically addresses deviation sources such as sampling noise and finite-capacity effects that plague randomized constructions at finite dimensionality.

entry.title: CollabFlow: Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Collaboration

author.name: Xiao Huang, Mingda Zhang, Junming Zhang, Qiang Huang, Hanwen Zhang, Yue Dai, Zijia Wang, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Introduces CollabFlow, a recursive self-improvement system for LLM multi-agent collaboration in which a trainable Collab-Director constructs agent teams, a frozen executor runs them, and each round's outcomes retrain the director. The design addresses open problems in prior work such as operator-defined collaboration topologies and error propagation through verbatim exchanges.

entry.title: RAST: Resolution-Aware Privileged Structure Transfer for Low-Resolution Audio Activity Recognition

author.name: Ji Hwan Park, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Yufei Shen, Dawei Liang, Edison Thomaz

entry.summary: Formulates the gap between high-resolution audio used in training and low-resolution audio used at deployment as a sensor-resolution privileged learning problem, motivated by privacy (speech exposure) and resource efficiency in human activity recognition. RAST transfers privileged structure from HR audio to improve LR-audio recognition models.

entry.title: DAMPER: Return-Prioritized Gradient Control for Smooth Policies

author.name: Seokmin Ko, Taewon Goo, Kihyuk Hong

entry.summary: DAMPER addresses oscillatory actions in actor-critic continuous control by combining the native actor gradient with a temporal-consistency gradient through conflict-conditioned projection and adaptive magnitude control. It explicitly prioritizes return over auxiliary smoothness objectives, avoiding the loss-balancing fragility of stacked auxiliary losses.

entry.title: Hard-Gate Candidacy in a Deployed Validator Suite

author.name: Xin Xu

entry.summary: The paper evaluates 13 validators in a deployed generative agent pipeline against 550 runtime and 350 static builds labeled by downstream outcome, reporting marginal separation with proper statistical corrections. Only two checks survive multiple-comparison correction and nine are indistinguishable from zero, offering rare empirical evidence about which deployed validators actually gate useful behavior. This is a valuable empirical audit of deployment-time validation practice.

entry.title: A Generalisation Signal Need Not Be a Model-Selection Signal

author.name: Aditya Nagarsekar, M P Ashish Bhat, Aadi Nesarkar, Vrishti Godhwani, Rahul Yedida, Aditya Challa, Danda Sravan, Snehanshu Saha

entry.summary: This paper tests whether network geometry measures, including a novel forward-only Hessian-norm proxy, can replace validation data for model selection under distribution shift in computational biology tasks. Contrary to the hypothesis, geometry does not become more useful as validation quality degrades, and augmenting validation with geometry helps some shifts while harming others, a valuable negative result for model selection practice.

entry.title: UniAE-MoE: A Unified Audio Encoder via Mixture of Experts

author.name: Shengbo Cai, Zhisheng Zhang, Zichao Nie, Jing Peng, Jingran Xie, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: UniAE-MoE is a unified audio encoder using a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to fuse representations from strong existing encoders such as those from Qwen2-Audio and Audio-Flamingo 3 for large audio language models. It employs SwiGLU with shared experts to decouple encoder networks and a two-stage instruction-tuning strategy for downstream adaptation.

entry.title: Candidate Retention for Abductive Learning

author.name: Hao-Yuan He, Yu Liu, Ming Li

entry.summary: The paper improves abductive learning—combining neural perception with symbolic reasoning—by selecting a retained subset of candidate explanations rather than picking one pseudo-label or weighting all, balancing supervision sharpness against coverage. It provides a coordinate-level bound on supervision error involving retained uncertainty, discarded model mass, and model mismatch.

entry.title: Let the Carrier Carry the Attack: Preserving the Subject in Adversarial Image Generation

author.name: Linfeng Jiang, Steven McDonagh, Yuhang Chen, Xingyu Zhao, Siddartha Khastgir, Andi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper introduces the carrier, a secondary visual element that absorbs globally normalized adversarial perturbations so targeted attacks preserve the integrity of the primary subject while maintaining attack strength. It shows carriers improve cross-model transferability and keep attacks perceptually stealthy for humans.

entry.title: Pseudo-Label-Triggered Retraining from Forecast Errors for Online Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yeryeong Kwak, Yoo-Min Jung, Jonghun Park

entry.summary: PILOT is an online retraining framework for time series forecasting that learns when to retrain directly from realized forecast-error dynamics, using pseudo-labels instead of indirect drift alarms or staleness heuristics. It targets non-stationary streams under limited deployment resources, balancing recovery of accuracy against retraining cost.

entry.title: Cluster Attention Neural Operators for Solving Parametric Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Ming Zhong, Antonio Colanera, Gianluigi Rozza, Zhenya Yan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a cluster-based attention neural operator for parametric PDE solving that improves on Transolver by avoiding lossy projection into a reduced slice space and shared attention-head weights. The design aims to retain fine spatial detail and greater model flexibility while keeping computational cost manageable.

entry.title: SCB: SpeechConversationBench for Evaluating Multi-Turn Reasoning in Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Kanpat Vesessook, Saksorn Ruangtanusak

entry.summary: SCB evaluates multi-turn spoken reasoning using 103 sharded GSM8K problems delivered full, concatenated, or incrementally across turns. Four commercial speech-to-speech systems lose 5.0-25.3 percentage points under sharded disclosure, exposing that current systems struggle when task requirements emerge across conversational turns. A focused diagnostic benchmark for speech models.

entry.title: A Data-Free Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Level-Set Interface Advection

author.name: Muhammad Akbar Khan

entry.summary: This work trains a physics-informed neural operator for level-set interface advection using only the transport residual and a geometric constraint, with no reference solutions. A spacetime Fourier backbone emits entire trajectories in one pass and initial conditions are imposed by construction, removing penalty-term competition. A methodological contribution at the intersection of neural operators and scientific computing.

entry.title: Does Text Steer Neural PDE Surrogates? A Controlled Diagnostic with OperatorCLIP

author.name: Aadi Dash, Lennon J. Shikhman, Michael Galarnyk

entry.summary: This diagnostic study asks whether text-conditioned neural PDE surrogates actually use the meaning of conditioning text, comparing an unconditioned FNO, a constant-sentence FiLM control, and contrastively aligned task text via OperatorCLIP on Darcy2D, ShallowWater2D, and compressible Navier-Stokes. Results show constant conditioning often achieves lower error, and apparent benefits of task text have substantial seed uncertainty, questioning attribution of gains to text semantics.

entry.title: Proper Scoring Rule-based Diffusion for Probabilistic Weather Forecasting

author.name: Joonhyeong Park, Giung Nam, Hyungi Lee, Kyunghyun Cho, Byoungwoo Park, Juho Lee

entry.summary: The paper improves CRPS-trained stochastic weather forecasters by introducing auxiliary conditional denoising tasks that predict the same future state from context plus corrupted versions, providing partial future information to reduce prediction ambiguity at long horizons. Built on distributional diffusion models, a single stochastic predictor learns conditional distributions of these tasks under a proper scoring rule.

entry.title: LEARN-TS: LLM-Enhanced Alignment and Reconstruction with Normality Guidance for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jahyeob Koo, Kio Yun, Byoungmo Koo, Jun-Geol Baek

entry.summary: LEARN-TS incorporates language-derived semantics into multivariate time-series anomaly detection via masked reconstruction, avoiding reliance on time-paired textual annotations that standard benchmarks do not provide. It conditions reconstruction on window-specific semantics without leaking anomaly cues, and uses a window-independent notion of normality as a complementary reference rather than an independent detector. This addresses the practical problem that reconstruction error alone often fails to distinguish anomalies from benign deviations.

entry.title: Anchoring Adversarial Trajectories to Data Manifolds: A Bilevel Transfer Optimization Framework

author.name: Yaohua Liu, Yifan Guo, Jiaxin Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes Manifold Anchored Bilevel Transfer (MABT) for improving adversarial example transferability, addressing the problem that ambient gradients drift away from the intrinsic data manifold and overfit to the surrogate. MABT anchors adversarial trajectories to the shared semantic subspace via a relaxed manifold-anchoring operator and casts transfer attack generation as distributional bilevel optimization solved with a Hessian-free linear-complexity method. This aims to produce more transferable attacks.

entry.title: Sharp Stationary Gaussian Approximation for Constant-Stepsize SGD

author.name: Junghoon Seo

entry.summary: This proves a sharp Gaussian approximation for the invariant law of constant-stepsize SGD with bounded noise from an ergodic Markov chain, achieving O(sqrt(alpha)) Wasserstein closeness for smooth strongly convex objectives. A matching lower-bound example shows third-order mixed moments drive the leading correction even under vanishing autocovariance.

entry.title: A differentiability framework for zigzag persistent homology via linear interpolation

author.name: Enrico Maria Ferrari, Clemens Bannwart, Matteo Biagetti

entry.summary: The paper develops the first differentiability framework for zigzag persistent homology, enabling topological features that evolve non-monotonically to be incorporated into learning pipelines. By assigning real-valued crossing times to diagram endpoints under linearly interpolated filtrations, it derives differentials almost everywhere under mild conditions.

entry.title: ElectrolyteFM: Unifying Electrolyte Property Prediction through Cross-Property Knowledge Learning

author.name: Jiaxin Yu, Shuo Wang, Peng Wang, Yongcai Wang, Deying Li

entry.summary: ElectrolyteFM is a unified multi-property prediction model for electrolyte formulation design that identifies property-specific features and shared cross-property knowledge. The authors analyze asymmetric transfer effects between property prediction tasks and use this to decide when joint learning helps or hurts relative to separate training.

entry.title: RiboUnmix: Learning Shared Translational Dynamics from Biased and Noisy Ribo-seq Measurements

author.name: Gabriele Martino, Denis Skibinski, Ivo L. Hofacker, Sebastian Tschiatschek

entry.summary: RiboUnmix is a probabilistic multi-dataset framework for ribosome profiling that separates shared sequence-dependent ribosome occupancy signals from experiment-specific distortions using a negative-binomial observation model. It addresses the risk that models fit technical artifacts rather than biology in Ribo-seq data.

entry.title: Markovian Dynamics Enforcer: Feasibility Preserving Correction on Learned Dynamics Manifolds

author.name: Kevin Yu, Tao Guo, Constantinos Antoniou, Panagiotis Angeloudis

entry.summary: MaDE is a post-hoc operator that corrects neural trajectory predictions by mapping proposed state transitions onto a learned feasible dynamics manifold, inferring controls and recomputing states via a physics-plus-residual completion model. It targets settings where controls are unobserved and dynamics are only partially specified, with best-effort inequality constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: Gromov-Wasserstein Distillation for Inductive Multi-View Embedding

author.name: Rafael Pereira Eufrazio, Eduardo Fernandes Montesuma, Charles Casimiro Cavalcante

entry.summary: The paper extends Gromov-Wasserstein MDS from transductive to inductive embedding via barycentric distillation: a GW-MDS teacher produces transport-based targets and a neural student learns an explicit out-of-sample mapping. It supports single-view, Mean-GWMDS, and Multi-GWMDS teachers with consensus targets.

entry.title: MANET-GNN: Learned Decentralized Optimization of Power Allocation in Multi-Channel MANETs

author.name: Tomer Alter, Nir Shlezinger, Michael Segal

entry.summary: The paper formulates decentralized transmit-power allocation in multi-hop, multi-channel wireless ad hoc networks as a constrained end-to-end throughput maximization problem spanning several traffic patterns, and trains a message-passing GNN as a distributed learned optimizer using the non-convex centralized objective as unsupervised training signal. This provides a unified learned alternative to hand-crafted distributed power control. It matters for infrastructure-less connectivity in dynamic, resource-constrained environments.

entry.title: Inference-Layer Security: Defending Against Adversarial Inference and Infrastructure Abuse

author.name: Keifer Lee

entry.summary: This technical report studies inference-layer defense for LLM-as-a-service providers against jailbreaking, denial of service, and distillation attacks. Lacking public labeled data, the authors construct a structural causal model generating labeled user-session data with coordinated multi-account campaigns and tiered label observability, then train detectors on it. It addresses an underexplored operational security layer for frontier model providers.

entry.title: From Codebase to Culprit (C2C): Reducing the Search Space for Bugs with Semantic Retrieval and Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ankur Garg, Corey Yang-Smith, Rishav Rishav, Ahmad Abdellatif, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: C2C is a bug localization framework that mirrors developer workflows by narrowing the search space across files, functions, and lines. It combines contrastively fine-tuned CodeBERT embeddings for recall-oriented retrieval with a hierarchical RL agent that progressively localizes the bug given bug-report text and stack traces.

entry.title: STEPS: Scene Text Editing with Preserved Style Using Diffusion and Contrastive Style Encoding

author.name: Nicolas Thiebaut, Nameer Hirschkind, Xiao Yu, Kyle Spence

entry.summary: STEPS is a diffusion-based architecture for scene text editing that changes textual content in images while preserving style (font, color, orientation, background). It introduces a contrastive style encoder that disentangles style from content, combined with character encodings and rendered glyphs, achieving improved style preservation over prior methods.

entry.title: RouteRec: Behavior-Guided Sparse Routing for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Junyeong Song, Jaemin Yoo

entry.summary: RouteRec is a sequential recommender that routes computation through mixture-of-experts blocks using observed session behavior, summarizing interaction tempo, item-group focus, repetition, and popularity tendency at macro, mid, and micro scopes. Behavior-derived scores select expert groups, making conditional computation interpretable and behavior-aligned.

entry.title: QuantCode Model: Specializing Language Models for Executable Algorithmic Trading Code

author.name: Alexey Chernysh, Orkhan Ekhtibarov, Dmitry Zmitrovich

entry.summary: The authors specialize language models for generating executable algorithmic trading strategies via continued pretraining on trading-framework code and supervised fine-tuning on agent-validated request-to-code pairs. They introduce QuantCode-Bench, a 400-task benchmark for Backtrader strategy generation plus a repository-level SWE-bench-like track. This provides both a domain-specialized model and an evaluation resource for a demanding code-generation niche.

entry.title: General Performance Guarantee for Human Torque Estimation-Based Task-Agnostic Assistive Exoskeleton Control

author.name: Duy Hoang, Bastien Berret, Olivier Bruneau, Laurent Fribourg

entry.summary: The authors formalize matched assistance in robotic exoskeletons as scenarios where the robot positively contributes to human movement, and develop a theoretical framework that guarantees a lower bound on the matched-assistance probability. The guarantee holds over the full torque distribution, including unseen tasks, addressing errors in human torque estimation. This brings formal safety-style guarantees to assistive robotics control.

entry.title: PassGPT+: Leveraging Linguistic Priors for Password Modeling

author.name: Rajneesh Anand, Neeraj Lakshmanan, Masoud Yari

entry.summary: PassGPT+ adapts GPT-2's linguistic priors to password modeling via character-aware tokenization, rather than training generative password models from scratch on leaked corpora. The work also introduces PassDiffusion, presented as the first absolute-diffusion-based password generative model. It offers insight into how humans construct secrets, relevant to both defensive strength estimation and attack simulation.

entry.title: Resolving the Missing Financial Data Crisis: A Generative AI Pipeline for SEC 10-K Extraction

author.name: Prisha Nair, Roee Shraga

entry.summary: This paper addresses missing financial data affecting over 70 percent of firms in structured datasets by evaluating LLM-based extraction pipelines for SEC 10-K filings, where regex and BERT methods fail on attributes buried in footnotes or nonstandard sections. The work aims to reduce bias against smaller firms in quantitative financial research.

entry.title: Concept Direction Reliability Across Languages with Different Tokenizer Fertility

author.name: Muhammad Abdullahi Said, Abass Oguntade, Elisha Komolafe, Babangida Sani, Fatima Muhammad Adam, Muhammad Sammani Sani

entry.summary: This paper measures reproducibility of extracted sentiment directions in language model representations across English, Hausa, and Yoruba, finding split-half agreement degrades sharply with poorer tokenization, from about 0.74-0.87 in English down to 0.10-0.40 in Yoruba. The language rank order holds across all model comparisons, linking tokenizer fertility to the reliability of interpretability artifacts. This cautions that steering and probing results may not transfer to low-resource languages.

entry.title: Population Fidelity: Evaluating Population Representativeness in LLMs

author.name: Neemias B. da Silva, Martin Lukk, Ali Sutani, Abhishek Moturu, Harris Yang, Daniel Silver, Matt Ratto, Thiago H. Silva

entry.summary: The paper introduces Population Fidelity, a framework evaluating how well LLM-generated survey responses represent human populations along three dimensions: group-level accuracy, between-group variation, and the structure of that variation. The authors demonstrate the framework by reanalyzing a prior machine-bias study. This addresses concerns that LLM simulations compress and misrepresent population attitudes.

entry.title: Cross-Linguistic Effects in Bilingual Phoneme BabyLMs

author.name: Nikitas Theodoropoulos, Maria Lymperaiou, Giorgos Filandrianos

entry.summary: The paper trains bilingual BabyLMs on phonemic representations of speech to better mirror how children acquire language, investigating cross-linguistic L1-L2 interactions under developmentally plausible constraints. This combines phoneme-level modeling with bilingual acquisition research to reduce the modality gap between human and machine learners.

entry.title: Co-Linguistics: AI-augmented Theory Construction in Linguistics

author.name: Emmanuel Chemla, Benjamin Spector, Alexandros Kalomoiros, Philippe Schlenker

entry.summary: A position paper proposing Co-Linguistics, the use of AI as a co-scientist to help construct and assess formal linguistic theories, rather than as a model of human linguistic ability. It argues linguistics theories are mathematically formalizable, so AI advances in mathematics could accelerate theory building, with the twist that the goal is finding the best axioms rather than proving theorems.

entry.title: Corpus-Guided Dual-Path Propagation for Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Baoxian Liu, Tong Wei

entry.summary: Proposes NexusRAG, which augments relation-free Tri-Graph retrieval with a corpus-level entity neighborhood structure built from entity co-occurrence and semantic similarity. It guides two complementary propagation paths to recover bridging evidence with low query similarity that existing query-similarity graph retrieval misses.

entry.title: Local Predictability and Collective Fidelity in LLM-Agent Societies

author.name: Igor Itkin

entry.summary: The paper examines whether compact surrogates can cheaply simulate large LLM agent societies by comparing individual predictions and collective forecasts across 9,455 published trajectories plus new opinion-dynamics experiments. Neighbor information improves individual prediction in all 16 settings, but collective gains depend on transfer conditions, and tests on 24 new statements fail to confirm earlier contrasting history effects. The findings motivate direct collective validation of simulation surrogates.

entry.title: Does a prosody-trained representation help beyond trainable fusion? A parameter-matched study with frozen HuBERT

author.name: Ki Woong Moon, Daniel Brenner

entry.summary: This paper asks whether explicit prosodic representations (F0, voicing, energy, spectral tilt) genuinely improve ASR of spontaneous speech, or whether measured gains come merely from added trainable fusion parameters. Using a parameter-matched design with a frozen HuBERT backbone across Buckeye, Switchboard, and AMI IHM, the authors find that the trainable fusion alone accounts for essentially all WER reductions, with the prosody representation contributing nearly nothing. It is a useful cautionary negative result about ablation rigor in speech representation research.

entry.title: MERGE: Multi-LLM Ensemble for Retrieval via Generative Enrichment

author.name: Tzu-I Ho, Yung-Yu Shih, Shang-Yu Su, Dongzhe Wang, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: MERGE is a two-stage query-enrichment framework for information retrieval in which three heterogeneous 7-8B open-source LLMs independently generate candidate query expansions and a larger LLM generatively synthesizes them into a single query for a retriever such as BM25. It also introduces techniques to make prompt engineering scale across the ensemble rather than requiring per-model re-engineering. This addresses the brittleness of single-LLM query enrichment.

entry.title: EmoRES-TTS: Residual-Enhanced Vector Steering for Emotional Speech Generation

author.name: Kuan-Po Huang, Haohe Liu, Puyuan Peng, Haibin Wu, Zhaoheng Ni, Hung-yi Lee, Jinwon Lee, Neha Chachra

entry.summary: EmoRES-TTS is a training-free method for emotion control in TTS that decomposes emotion steering vectors into a shared component moving speech away from neutral and a residual component directing generation toward the target emotion, replacing single global-strength steering. This improves adherence to requested emotions in frozen models without additional training or emotion-labeled data. It advances controllability of speech synthesis at low cost.

entry.title: Team MSU GenText-Forensics Challenge 2026 Technical Report

author.name: Kirill Koltsov, Aleksandr Gushchin, Dmitriy Vatolin, Anastasia Antsiferova

entry.summary: This technical report describes a solution to the ACM MM 2026 GenText-Forensics challenge on detecting and localizing document text forgery, including attacks targeting OCR and LLM pipelines. The approach combines a document tampering detector with two LoRA-adapted Qwen3-VL-32B models in a decomposed chain-of-thought pipeline that also produces human-readable forensic reports. It addresses multilingual text-image forgery detection, localization, and attack-type classification.

entry.title: Hard-Region Supervision: #1 on the Waymo Open Dataset 2D Video Panoptic Segmentation Leaderboard

author.name: Jinghan Yang

entry.summary: Describes the winning entry to the Waymo Open Dataset 2D Video Panoptic Segmentation Challenge, building on DVIS++ with a hard-region supervision scheme. The method identifies regions where the baseline makes mistakes and applies a dedicated loss and auxiliary training-time prediction head, removed at inference so architecture is unchanged.

entry.title: FLOW: Feature-Level Optimal Warping for Generalized Remote Physiological Measurement

author.name: Bo Zhao, Junzhe Cao, Dan Guo, Dongmin Huang, Wenjin Wang, Tao Tan, Yue Sun, Zitong YU

entry.summary: Presents FLOW, an optimal-transport-driven framework for domain-generalized remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) with a temporal refinement module and prototype-based cross-temporal optimal transport. It aligns temporal features flexibly across domains while preserving intrinsic physiological rhythmic patterns, improving robustness to illumination, motion, and sensor shifts.

entry.title: CamAgent: An LLM-Agent Framework for Multi-Species Camera-Trap Workflows

author.name: Yutong Deng, Qi Song, Xi Guo, Tianming Wang, Lei Bao, Jianping Ge

entry.summary: CamAgent is an autonomous LLM-agent framework that unifies fragmented camera-trap ecology workflows, interpreting natural-language ecological intents and orchestrating computer-vision tools such as SpeciesNet alongside standardized data formats. It aims to lower programming barriers for end-to-end spatiotemporal wildlife analyses from raw media archives.

entry.title: From Wrecks to Wisdom: Recovering Crash Mechanics from Real-World Multi-View Photos

author.name: Ond\v{r}ej Valach, V\'aclav Divi\v{s}, Ivan Gruber

entry.summary: This work formulates crash understanding as supervised prediction from multi-view post-crash photo sets, recovering structured targets including Collision Deformation Classification codes when key crash-record metadata is missing or corrupted. Applications span vehicle-safety analysis, injury modeling, and insurance claim triage.

entry.title: ExpandDiff: Dynamic Range Expanding Diffusion for Single-Image HDR Reconstruction

author.name: Mehmet Emre and{\i}ran, Zhuoqian Yang, Liying Lu, Mathieu Salzmann, Sabine S\"usstrunk

entry.summary: ExpandDiff is a conditional diffusion pipeline for single-image HDR reconstruction that jointly recovers clipped shadows and highlights, using Dynamic Clipping Synthesis to randomize clipping percentiles during training. A pixel-space diffusion model with spatially-adaptive normalization predicts perceptually encoded HDR through a bounded output head.

entry.title: EmAvatar: Multimodal Empathetic Response Generation via Conflict Resolution and Expressive Guidance

author.name: Xiaolin Chen, Xuemeng Song, Jinlan Fu, Weili Guan, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: EmAvatar addresses avatar-based empathetic response generation, synthesizing synchronized text, audio, and talking-face video while handling conflicting emotions across modalities. The framework performs deliberative multimodal emotion recognition that exposes inter-modal prediction conflicts and provides explicit guidance for expressive synthesis while mitigating error propagation. It targets more accurate emotion perception and better-synchronized empathetic avatars.

entry.title: Simulating Synchrony Loop Networks in the Open Source RISP Neuroprocessor

author.name: Jackson Mowry, Patrick Abbs

entry.summary: The paper implements Synchrony Loop Propagation networks, which use sophisticated heterogeneous neuron models, on the open-source RISP event-driven neuromorphic processor designed for simpler leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. This bridges experimental spiking network approaches and deployable neuromorphic hardware, addressing the limited task performance that has constrained practical SNN adoption. The work expands the reachable design space for resource-constrained neuromorphic computing.

entry.title: Draft: A Parametric Tool for Robot Design Exploration

author.name: David Nguyen, Marcelo Coelho, Sangbae Kim

entry.summary: Draft is a parametric generation tool that compiles any parametric tree of serial chains into a simulation-ready MJCF model without CAD, enabling engineers to explore morphology-control co-design tradeoffs quickly. It addresses the cost of iterating on design and control together by grounding parameters in real-world plausibility.

entry.title: Bounded Channel-Adaptive Spectral Learning for Forward-Consistent Inverse Flapping-Wing Aerodynamics

author.name: Haichuan Li

entry.summary: This paper tackles the inverse problem of recovering flapping-wing kinematics from desired aerodynamic trajectories using a bounded channel-adaptive spectral residual gated recurrent network. The method combines temporal sequence modeling with frequency-domain methods while bounding spectral augmentation to prevent inconsistent corrections across kinematic variables and prediction horizons.

entry.title: CLIPPER Beyond Shortlisting: Auditable Decision Support for Changing Municipal Micromobility Policies

author.name: Julian Teusch, J\"org Philipp M\"uller, Monika Sester

entry.summary: CLIPPER is a constraint-exact, low-latency optimizer with audit functions for municipal planners comparing shared-micromobility parking policy alternatives, developed with requirements from the City of Braunschweig. It replaces the transparent but slow full-set greedy reference (tens of seconds per alternative at city scale) with deterministic bounded candidate pools and pooled evaluation/replay for interactive what-if analysis.

entry.title: FORTE: Forecasting Occupancy for Spatiotemporal Risk-Aware Planning in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Hahjin Lee, Young J. Kim

entry.summary: FORTE is a navigation framework that improves safe movement in dynamic environments by predicting occupancy grid maps over time and exploiting their spatiotemporal evolution during planning. It introduces two concepts, spatiotemporal occupancy overlap and occupancy directivity, to better anticipate when and where collisions may occur. This addresses known shortcomings where predicted occupancy maps are generated but underused by planners.

entry.title: PhasePlan: Ordered Future-Phase Planning for Robot Brain Models

author.name: Xiaoyu Yang, Yafei Zhang, Wensheng Li, Qing Zhan, Nan Wu

entry.summary: PhasePlan improves robot brain models by predicting the task phase at each future action position from multimodal observations, with these planning representations conditioning corresponding actions to preserve temporal alignment between task progress and action generation. The planner is trained first and then frozen during action-model adaptation to keep phase planning stable.

entry.title: Rethinking Legibility in Social Robot Hallway Navigation: Impact of Intent Representation and Human Distraction

author.name: Pranav Goyal, Andrew Stratton, Christoforos Mavrogiannis

entry.summary: This HRI study investigates how the choice of intent representation and the level of human attention shape legible robot motion in dynamic, constrained hallway navigation environments. It extends legibility frameworks designed for static observers to settings where pedestrians are distracted and safety must be ensured alongside clear intent communication.

entry.title: By default, Chinese AI falls very behind

author.name: Parv Mahajan

entry.summary: A multi-part policy analysis arguing that Chinese AI capabilities will fall increasingly behind the US absent major policy shifts, and modeling Chinese government and lab incentives over the next 6-18 months, including domestic interventions, sabotage and weight-theft options, and considerations for hypothetical US-China AI treaty negotiations.

entry.title: A simple argument about capabilities externalities versus opportunity costs

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld crossposts

entry.summary: This post presents a decision-theoretic argument that AI safety projects should generally not be judged net-negative due to capabilities externalities: even if safety research leaks capability gains, a generic capability researcher would add more capability directly, and the opportunity cost of not doing alternative safety work likely dominates. The author formalizes the tradeoff faced by an altruistic actor choosing among AI interventions such as interpretability or reward-hacking studies. It is a clarifying analytical contribution to the research-timeliness debate.

entry.title: Caption-Mediated Perceived-Safety Estimation for Pedestrian Routing
