author.name: Simon Parkinson, Paloma Liu, Wei Zheng, Mohammadreza Sheikhfathollahi

entry.summary: The paper proposes an explainable pedestrian-routing approach that estimates perceived safety from street-level imagery via an explicit natural-language caption intermediate, with risk scores derived only from structured caption features so every score is inspectable. Across nine captioning conditions and five model families, caption-mediated representations reach parity with direct CLIP image embeddings while adding interpretability.

entry.title: A Time-Aware Bag-of-Receptive-Fields for Interpretable Irregular Time Series Classification

author.name: Francesco Spinnato

entry.summary: This work extends Bag-Of-Receptive-Fields (BORF), a fast deterministic interpretable transform, to irregular time series via a time-weighted normalization scheme weighting each observation by its time delta. It avoids imputation and complex opaque architectures, providing interpretable classification for healthcare, mobility, and environmental monitoring data.

entry.title: BayesNDE: Bayesian Generative Modeling for Neural Density Estimation

author.name: Chenglin Li, Qiao Liu

entry.summary: BayesNDE is a neural density estimator that learns a Bayesian generative model and evaluates densities without invertible networks or Jacobian determinants. It infers sample-specific latent posteriors to build adaptive proposals and uses bridge sampling for density evaluation, showing improved density estimation on nonlinear and multimodal synthetic data.

entry.title: Less Data, Better Timing: Student-Curriculum Coupling for VLM On-Policy Distillation in Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Jiacheng Qiu, Yunsoo Kim, Ruichen Xu, Jian Luo, Petar M. Djuri\'c, Sima Mofakham

entry.summary: The paper argues that supervision trustworthiness and supervision necessity are distinct but coupled in on-policy distillation for vision-language models, with necessity varying with the student's current competence. It introduces Student-Curriculum Coupling, which adapts the training curriculum to the student state, reducing required data for temporal video grounding.

entry.title: Kinematic signatures of impairment: Detecting alcohol intoxication in e-scooter riders using sensor data and machine learning

author.name: Rahul Rajendra Pai, Marco Dozza, Alexander Rasch, Ali Mohammadi, Marco Capuccini

entry.summary: A controlled study of 25 e-scooter riders at three blood-alcohol levels using IMU and brake/throttle sensors, extracting permutation entropy and complementary signal features for ML-based intoxication detection. Motivated by the contribution of alcohol to fatal e-scooter crashes and the limits of pre-ride screening. Real-world safety application with human-subject data collection.

entry.title: In-Distribution Imagination for Model-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mintae Kim, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: The paper proposes in-distribution imagination (IDI), a rollout control framework for model-based offline RL that estimates trajectory support in a learned representation space and adaptively truncates rollouts leaving the offline data manifold. Combined with trajectory-regularized entropy-regularized RL, IDI consistently improves performance in limited-data settings by preventing model-error-driven divergence from realistic trajectories.

entry.title: The Nixtlaverse: An Open-Source Ecosystem for Forecasting

author.name: Olivier Sprangers, Max Mergenthaler Canseco, Marco Peixeiro, Saul Caballero Ramirez, Mariana Menchero Garc\'ia, Jing-Qiang Goh, Han Wang, Nikhil Gupta, Rogelio Melo, Senbong Gee, Cristian Challu

entry.summary: The Nixtlaverse paper describes an open-source ecosystem of Python forecasting libraries built around shared long-format panel data and keyed forecast outputs, letting statistical, ML, and neural model families coexist without rewriting data pipelines. It presents this design as a case study in forecasting software engineering.

entry.title: Dynamic LoRA-Experts and Prototype-Ensemble Matching for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Hongwei Zhao (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University), Rui Liu (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University), Yansong Liu (School of Computer Science, Engineering, Beihang University)

entry.summary: DLEPEM is a two-stage rehearsal-free class-incremental learning framework that assigns a task-specific LoRA expert per incremental task and uses prototype-ensemble matching combining frozen pretrained-model prototypes with task-adaptive expert prototypes. It shows strong performance on standard and few-shot CIL benchmarks.

entry.title: Airfoil2Vec: Spectral Geometry-Conditioned Neural Surrogate Models for Airfoil Aerodynamics and a Downforce-Generating CFD Dataset

author.name: Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Flavio Savarino, Andrei Cristian Popescu, Pietro Innocenzi, Pantelis Papageorgiou, Xerxes Xian Chong

entry.summary: The paper releases a dataset of roughly 10,000 RANS simulations of subsonic flow around downforce-generating NACA airfoils aimed at automotive and motorsport regimes, and benchmarks geometry-conditioned neural surrogates including neural fields, neural ODEs, MLPs, and graph models. It proposes Airfoil2Vec, a spectral geometry encoder combining joint contour spectra with separate spectral representations. Both the dataset and encoder are openly available.

entry.title: Diffusion-2BC: Hybrid Diffusion and Regression Training for Offline Behavior Cloning in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Bruno Maciel Machado, Eric Aislan Antonelo

entry.summary: Diffusion-2BC addresses multimodal action distributions in driving behavior cloning by combining a diffusion denoising objective with an auxiliary deterministic behavior-cloning loss over a shared visual encoder; the auxiliary branch is dropped at inference. It is evaluated in the Claw environment and closed-loop CARLA navigation.

entry.title: Unapologetically Distributed: A Call for Decentralized Document Analysis

author.name: Adri\`a Molina, Oriol Ramos Terrades, Josep Llad\'os

entry.summary: This is the first comprehensive study of distributed learning in document analysis, evaluating it along task, architecture, and data axes simultaneously, arguing that federated approaches can improve out-of-distribution robustness rather than merely trading performance for privacy. The paper repositions decentralization from a necessary evil to a potential advantage in privacy-constrained settings like archives and government.

entry.title: Look What You Made Us Cluster: Hate Narrative Extraction from Reddit Discourse

author.name: Annabelle K. L. Chua, Forster J. Khoo, Joel C. R. Tan, Huey Ting Ang, Kheng Hwee Tan, Joel Y. A. Sim, Shirley W. H. Ow, Ria Mundhra, Elsie C. K. Toh, Youfeng Xu, Lynnette H. X. Ng

entry.summary: This paper presents a pipeline extracting hate narratives from Reddit as entity-evaluation pairs, using an LLM reasoning process extending aspect-based sentiment analysis to identify aspects and judgement types, followed by Leiden clustering of extracted narratives. The structured representation yields more precise and interpretable narratives than surface-level semantic approaches.

entry.title: A Proposed Rubric for Evaluating Expressed Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Model Responses

author.name: Zhangshu Joshua Jiang, Zina Ibrahim, James T. Teo

entry.summary: Proposes a multidimensional rubric for scoring free-text clinical reasoning in LLM responses to gold-standard clinical vignettes, synthesizing medical education assessment frameworks, clinical LLM benchmarks, and general LLM reasoning evaluation research. It includes behavioral anchors, applicability rules, and a groundedness category adapted from the factuality-validity-coherence-utility taxonomy.

entry.title: Better Behavioral Prediction, More Faithful Model Ablations? Evidence from Sequential Choice

author.name: Hanbo Xie

entry.summary: The paper tests whether accurate behavioral prediction implies faithful explanation via input ablations, using synthetic sequential bandit tasks with known generating policies. Comparing GRUs, Transformers, a fine-tuned LLaMA model, and cognitive models under varied reward contributions, the analysis distinguishes predictive accuracy from the validity of ablation-based explanations of behavior. This is a useful caution for cognitive science and interpretability work that equates model performance with mechanistic fidelity.

entry.title: Event-Driven Refresh and Recurrence Memory to Reduce Stale Grounding in Referring Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Abu Hanif Muhammad Syarubany, Jaehyun Jang, Siwoo Lim, Seungyeon Ryu, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: Proposes EDRRM, an enhancement to Sa2VA for referring video object segmentation that selectively re-invokes the multimodal LLM plus SAM2 pipeline only at stable change points detected by an EMA-smoothed event score. This reduces stale grounding and persistent false positives in long or dynamic videos where object composition changes.

entry.title: Invariant Shape Analysis of Surfaces with Spherical Topology

author.name: T. Shaska, M. -R. Siadat

entry.summary: The paper constructs a shape descriptor for closed 3D surfaces with spherical topology that is exactly invariant to parameterization, pose, and scale while retaining all other information, including chirality via polynomial invariants of the rotation group. It connects spherical harmonic descriptors to classical invariant theory, making mirror images distinguishable where power-spectrum and bispectrum reductions fail.

entry.title: Embodiment-aware control by inference over the operator: a simulation study

author.name: Sara Falcone

entry.summary: The Universal Embodiment Engine (UEE) is a teleoperation controller that infers the operator's sense of embodiment and visuo-proprioceptive cue weighting from implicit gaze, pupil, and task-outcome signals, then chooses bounded device settings under explicit preferences. It is grounded in predictive-processing accounts while avoiding the degenerate solution of simply removing feedback.

entry.title: Learning Global Sensitivity Indices from Observational Data: A Metamodel-Based Approach

author.name: Giulia Vannucci

entry.summary: MM-GSA extends variance-based global sensitivity analysis to observational data where designed experiments are impossible, using supervised metamodels to approximate the input-output relationship. It combines a model-agnostic Sobol index estimator with a new trigger-based structural index measuring how predictive performance depends on predictor availability.

entry.title: Continual Learning of Dynamical Systems in Recurrent Neural Networks through Recyclable Unit Gating

author.name: Sima Hashemi, Daniel Durstewitz, Georgia Koppe

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks continual learning methods (regularization, replay, parameter isolation) for continual dynamical systems reconstruction on Almost-Linear RNNs, finding isolation best but wasteful of capacity. It then introduces Continually-Recyclable Unit Gating to reuse task-specific parameters while preserving earlier dynamics. Niche but careful contribution at the intersection of continual learning and dynamical systems.

entry.title: Autoregressive Frontier Expansion: Growing Trees with Graph Machine Learning

author.name: Umer Gupta, Saku Peltonen, Martin Ritzert

entry.summary: The paper proposes Autoregressive Frontier Expansion, a generative framework that constructs tree-like branching structures (botanical trees, neurons, vessels) through iterative frontier expansion, simultaneously learning topology and geometry. It fills a gap between morphology-specific models that constrain topology and generic 3D graph generators that ignore tree structure.

entry.title: A Rank Graduation metric for Algorithmic fairness

author.name: Dalia Atif, Paolo Giudici

entry.summary: The paper proposes a rank-based fairness framework evaluating fairness through the distribution of model prediction errors rather than aggregate group-parity measures, combining Rank Graduation Fairness, an integrated AURGF measure, a centered Cramer-von Mises permutation test, and a feature-removal explainability procedure. Applied to credit-scoring-style models including logistic regression and random forests, it links fairness assessment with predictive accuracy and identifies which individuals and factors contribute to unfairness.

entry.title: Larry Caused the Car to Stop, But the Model Didn't Notice: Transformer Blindness to the M-Heuristic

author.name: Stefania Butnaru, Claudiu Creanga

entry.summary: The paper tests whether encoder transformers employ the M-Heuristic — the neo-Gricean principle that marked forms implicate marked meanings — by contrasting lexical with periphrastic causatives in an NLI framework across 188 conditions and 15 ambitransitive verbs. DeBERTa, RoBERTa, and BART show no evidence of capturing the pragmatic distinction.

entry.title: Beyond Spatial-Domain Supervision: A Relation Constrained Space for Multi-Modal Image Fusion

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Mingyu Ge, Haiyu Song, Haoran Duan

entry.summary: Proposes a relation-constrained supervision paradigm for multi-modal image fusion that moves supervision from the spatial domain to a learned relation space, using frozen pretrained representation models. This addresses the inherent misalignment of spatial-domain surrogate supervision given the absence of ground-truth fused images.

entry.title: Defining and Categorising Human-AI Interactions in Clinical Trials: A Multidimensional Human-AI Classification Approach

author.name: Sandra Woolley, Tim Collins, Khalid Khattak, Illia Chernomorets, Ariane Arevalo, Chris Richardson

entry.summary: This paper presents a multidimensional framework for classifying human-AI interactions in clinical trials along AI tasks, human-AI relationships, interaction configurations, and human groups. Fifteen trials were independently categorized by two human reviewers and six LLM classifiers, providing a structured method for consistent identification and comparison of human-AI interactions in clinical research.

entry.title: AIMS: An Agentic AI Framework for Sim-to-Real Multi-Modal ISAC

author.name: Yijie Bian, Kai Zhang, Wei Guo, Zixin Wang, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief

entry.summary: AIMS applies an agentic AI framework to sim-to-real transfer for multi-modal integrated sensing and communication in wireless networks, coordinating scene, sensing, wireless, and learning configurations to generate and adapt synthetic data for target deployments. It aims to reduce dependence on annotated real-world data that constrains scalable ISAC deployment.

entry.title: Conformal Adversarial Generative Ensemble

author.name: Ahmad Shahi, Mamehgol Yousefi, Brendon J. Woodford, Farhaan Mirza, Tapabrata Chakraborti

entry.summary: CAGE combines multiple generative forecasting models with a discriminative component that uses conformal prediction p-values from nonconformity scores to dynamically reweight ensemble members and downweight unreliable extreme forecasts. The goal is improved reliability and accuracy in time series forecasting. It unites three established techniques in a sensible pipeline.

entry.title: Colorectal Cancer Segmentation with Adaptive Augmentation and Multi-Resolution Ensemble Models

author.name: \"Umit Mert \c{C}a\u{g}lar, Alptekin Temizel

entry.summary: The paper presents an automated segmentation pipeline for whole-slide colorectal cancer histopathology images, labeling tumor grades 1-3 and normal mucosa using dense prediction transformers with various encoders, adaptive augmentation, and multi-resolution ensembles. It aims to speed up biopsy-based diagnosis and support timely clinical decisions.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Architectural Shift from Traditional to AI-Enabled Simulink Controllers

author.name: Hadiza Umar Yusuf, Khouloud Gaaloul

entry.summary: This empirical study compares traditional and AI-enabled Simulink controllers using a taxonomy of ten structural categories and nine functional roles, analyzing 62 real-world models across 8 controller types and 10 domains, plus a survey of 13 practitioners. It identifies three architectural tensions arising as AI components replace analytically derived control laws in cyber-physical systems.

entry.title: Unveiling the Value of Motion for Cinematic Camera Trajectories

author.name: Ziqi Zhou, Yujian Yuan, Laura Sevilla-Lara

entry.summary: Finds that decomposing camera trajectory representations from per-frame poses into explicit direction and speed components yields surprising benefits for trajectory-to-text alignment and text-to-trajectory generation in cinematic camera control. The paper also introduces a simple metric for evaluating trajectory-text alignment.

entry.title: BARRAC: Adaptation of an English Aspect-based Sentiment Analysis Approach for Classification Tasks in Arabic Dialects

author.name: Ali Almutairi, Gelareh Mohammadi, Imran Razzak, Aditya Joshi

entry.summary: BARRAC adapts an English aspect-based sentiment analysis framework to Arabic dialect tasks by replacing consumer-review attribute pools with Arabic linguistic markers for sentiment, sarcasm, and dialect identification, plus a two-stage training scheme. It achieves 63.93 percent mean macro-F1 across five Arabic dialect datasets, outperforming few-label baselines.

entry.title: Beyond Text: LLM-Based Dimensional Emotion Evaluation in Multimodal Dialogue

author.name: Yutong Hu, Jinho Choi

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM framework for continuous Valence-Arousal-Dominance emotion evaluation in multimodal dialogue on IEMOCAP, encoding acoustic cues as natural language descriptions. Across six models from LLaMA, GPT, and Qwen families, LoRA fine-tuned LLaMA models substantially beat prompt-engineered GPT models despite smaller scale, attributed to domain adaptation. It extends LLM emotion work from discrete categories to dimensional ratings.

entry.title: SCIC: Scope- and Codebook-Aware Instruction Conditioning for Speaker-Adapted Expressive TTS

author.name: Longyu Lu, Zongwei Du, Mengtao Xing, Zhuoqun Liu, Zifan Guan, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma

entry.summary: SCIC introduces Speaker-Relative Inline Prosody Control for long-form streaming TTS, where pitch, energy, and speed instructions apply clause-by-clause relative to the preceding clause. By analyzing Qwen3-TTS RVQ codebooks, the authors show energy concentrates in early residual codebooks while pitch accumulates deeper, informing scope- and codebook-aware conditioning for expressive synthesis.

entry.title: From Speech to Editable Concepts: Probing Emotion Recognition with Concept Bottleneck Models

author.name: Hezhao Zhang, Thomas Hain

entry.summary: This paper adapts concept bottleneck models to speech emotion recognition, using LLMs to examine how predictions depend on transcripts, acoustic descriptions, and speaker attributes. Experiments test three LLMs on CREMA-D and related datasets to improve explainability of direct-audio emotion classification.

entry.title: Parameterization method of reservoir properties for ensemble-based data assimilation using intermediate latent space of StyleGAN

author.name: Marcio A. Sampaio, Paulo H. Ranazzi, Martin J. Blunt

entry.summary: This paper applies StyleGAN intermediate latent spaces to parameterize reservoir properties for ensemble-based history matching, addressing the failure of Gaussian-assumption ensemble smoothers under complex non-Gaussian facies geology. It aims to identify which deep generative parameterization is most compatible with ensemble methods.

entry.title: Grounding Time-Series Foundation Models in Digital Twin Topology for Predictive Maintenance

author.name: Sizhe Ma, Katherine A. Flanigan, Mario Berg\'es

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks five frozen time-series foundation models on remaining useful life prediction with C-MAPSS, finding multivariate architectures substantially outperform univariate ones, and explores grounding TSFMs in digital twin topology for unseen regression tasks. It addresses the gap that TSFMs, pretrained for temporal continuation, underperform on tasks like regression in digital twin contexts.

entry.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space

author.name: Anson Y. Lam, Shuqing Li, Michael R. Lyu

entry.summary: MatLoom is a compact layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation, where programs compose alpha-masked layers with shared spatial expressions defining coverage and PBR channels. A standalone interpreter produces material maps, and parser-guided repair plus preview-based critique enable revision without task-specific fine-tuning. Supports subsequent authoring via named layer parameters.

entry.title: An Input-Frugal Deep Learning Framework for Weather-Driven National Crop-Yield Forecasting: A Case Study of Brazilian Soybean

author.name: Fernando Dupin da Cunha Mello (Stricto Sensu Department, SENAI CIMATEC University, Salvador, Bahia, Brazil), Prashant Kumar (Global Centre for Clean Air Research), Erick G. Sperandio Nascimento (Stricto Sensu Department, SENAI CIMATEC University, Salvador, Bahia, Brazil)

entry.summary: The authors present a frugal, architecture-agnostic deep learning framework for national crop-yield forecasting using only routine weather data plus two lightweight static inputs, evaluated on 20 seasons of Brazilian soybean data with leave-one-year-out cross-validation. They benchmark MLP, CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM, Transformer, and Mamba encoders against linear baselines under identical data requirements.

entry.title: Does a Shared Temperature Imply a Shared Angular Scale in Probabilistic Contrastive Learning?

author.name: Ningkang Peng, Qianfeng Yu, Jingyang Mao, Xiaoqian Peng, Tingyu Lu, Peirong Ma, Yanhui Gu

entry.summary: The paper proves that in the exact von Mises-Fisher probabilistic score used by ProCo, a shared temperature does not imply a shared similarity scale: the score retains a class-dependent leading angular gain involving the mean resultant length, which affects softmax competition, decision boundaries, and gradients. Experiments on CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist representations confirm the theory's predictions about boundary movement and gradient changes.

entry.title: EFormer: Temporally Aligned Local Correction for Continuous sEMG-Based Hand Pose Tracking

author.name: JiaCheng Ge, SiYu Zhang

entry.summary: EFormer is a residual feature-correction network built on a frozen tracking backbone for continuous hand-pose estimation from surface electromyography, addressing the indirect, drifting, and anatomy-dependent nature of sEMG signals. It combines a high-rate event branch, temporally aligned local cross-attention, causal RoPE temporal layers, and a bounded dynamically gated residual, fusing 16-channel 2 kHz sEMG with a 64-channel tracking representation. The design targets robust, wearable, camera-free motion inference.

entry.title: Argus: A Real-EKS Study of When Predicting Spot Interruptions Beats Simple Checkpointing

author.name: Angshuman Chakravertty, MD Rayyan

entry.summary: Argus is a Kubernetes operator for EC2 Spot workloads that compares predictive interruption handling against simple checkpointing for multi-node training. On a real EKS deployment with a CIFAR-10 testbed, it shows graceful SIGTERM checkpointing loses only the in-progress epoch, while an 80-trial benchmark reveals reactive protection degrades once interruptions outpace the 2-minute notice window.

entry.title: T-ARC: Topology-Aware Randomized Clustering via Distributionally Robust Stochastic Block Models

author.name: Serena Grazia De Benedictis, Andersen Ang, Nicoletta Del Buono, Flavia Esposito, Laura Selicato

entry.summary: T-ARC corrects K-means geometric bias by embedding topological information into the clustering objective, coupling a data-fidelity term with a graph-cut penalty over a latent graph modeled as a stochastic block model. The SBM parameter is optimized within a distributionally robust framework to uncover connectivity-consistent cluster structure.

entry.title: TopTimeNet: Topologically-assisted time-series classification model

author.name: Sharareh Sayyad, Sophia Bazzi

entry.summary: TopTimeNet decouples representation learning from classification for periodic-versus-chaotic time series by using a fixed, non-learned stage extracting 42-dimensional geometric and topological descriptors from Takens embeddings and persistent homology, followed by a lightweight classifier. A 1,638-parameter model matches the accuracy of a version with 33x more trainable parameters.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Checkpoint Selection for Domain Generalization

author.name: Jinshi Liu, Jiahao Li, Pan Liu, Yanfeng Li, Rui Qian, Zhao Tong, Yue Sun, Tao Tan

entry.summary: The paper observes that within a fixed training trajectory, checkpoints with near-optimal source accuracy can differ substantially in target probability quality, and proposes accuracy-constrained reliability selection that ranks near-optimal checkpoints by source reliability. This yields improved target calibration with minimal accuracy loss.

entry.title: Prototype-Rule Neurosymbolic Regularization for Rank-Constrained Tensor Neural Networks under Label Scarcity

author.name: Eftychios Protopapadakis, Konstantinos Makantasis, Konstantinos M. Giannoutakis

entry.summary: This paper augments rank-constrained tensor neural networks with differentiable prototype-rule regularization to provide an inductive bias on class geometry under limited supervision. It evaluates on four hyperspectral benchmarks with careful stratified and spatially separated folds, varying class support from 2 to 20 samples. The work targets the practical regime of low-label hyperspectral classification.

entry.title: Near-Linear Accuracy Bounds for Moreau--Yosida Unadjusted Langevin Sampling

author.name: Yuchen Xin, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: This paper establishes improved theoretical convergence guarantees for MYULA, a popular unadjusted Langevin sampling algorithm that uses Moreau-Yosida smoothing to handle non-smooth targets. The authors prove a near-linear Õ(h) invariant-measure bias bound with only logarithmic dependence on the smoothing parameter, which yields a Õ(epsilon^-1) iteration complexity to reach epsilon accuracy in Wasserstein distance for targets decomposable into a strongly convex smooth part and a Lipschitz convex part.

entry.title: Say, Echo, Do: Strategic Narratives and Revealed Positioning in Financial Markets

author.name: Ali Atiah Alzahrani

entry.summary: This paper models financial markets with three observable voices—institutional statements (Say), media repetition (Echo), and revealed positioning (Do)—using a linear-quadratic model of an informed institution that speaks and trades before a partly credulous crowd. It derives a distribution-free identity showing that when Say-Do covariance is negative, words carry negative predictive content and should be faded.

entry.title: A Width-Matched Comparison of Hybrid Quantum-Classical Self-Supervised Learning for Fingerprint Recognition

author.name: Maria S. Edwards, Kidwell Dlamini, Pin-An Lin, Wen-Hsien Hsu, Wen-Chieh Fang

entry.summary: The study inserts a quantum feature-extraction module (QuFeX) into three SSL frameworks, SimCLR, MoCo v2, and BYOL, and compares each hybrid with its classical counterpart at matched 8-feature representation width on a fingerprint dataset. This controlled design tests whether previously reported quantum SSL benefits stem from the objective or the quantum circuit itself.

entry.title: Geometric Representations of African Languages: A Regional Semantic Hub and Cultural Steering

author.name: Muhammad Abdullahi Said, Jonathan Shock

entry.summary: The authors study how Gemma 4 31B represents nine African languages, finding that transfer from English varies by language and layer, and that African languages share more aligned representational directions with each other than with control languages, suggesting a regional semantic hub. They also examine cultural steering, though some statistical conclusions are limited by dependence between language pairs. This extends interpretability analysis to understudied languages.

entry.title: Similar Choices, Different Attention: Cross-Modal Associations in Humans and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sumin Hong, Katsumi Ibaraki, Renee Shi, David Chiang, Toby Jia-Jun Li

entry.summary: The study compares humans (N=53) and vision-language models on cross-modal associations like the bouba-kiki effect, using identical stimuli and recording human eye movements alongside choices. Choice alignment appears in a few larger VLMs, but their saliency matches human gaze less closely than a center-bias baseline, suggesting models achieve similar answers through different mechanisms. This adds behavioral and attentional evidence to human-model comparisons.

entry.title: SRJudge: Empowering Large Language Models with Selective Reasoning for Fine-Grained Knowledge Concept Tagging

author.name: Zhiwei Yang, Jiahua Yang, Huiru Lin, Xing Chen, Quanlong Guan

entry.summary: SRJudge is a three-stage Select-Reason-Judge framework for assigning fine-grained knowledge concept labels to educational content, first narrowing a large candidate set with a fine-tuned small language model before LLM reasoning and judging. This decomposition addresses the high-dimensional decision space that causes LLMs to fail at selecting from many candidate concepts.

entry.title: Billiger.de Products: A Bilingual Entity Matching Benchmark

author.name: Aaron Steiner, Ksenia Elagin, Ralph Peeters, Johannes Knopp, Christian Bizer

entry.summary: Introduces a bilingual German-English entity matching benchmark from the billiger.de price comparison platform, covering thirteen product categories including hard cases like clothing and furniture, with aligned English translations preserving all pairs and splits. Multiple variants vary corner-case fraction, dev-set size, and unseen-entity fraction, following the WDC Products design.

entry.title: Auditable Long-Term Memory: A Deterministic Retrieval Chain Measured at 479/475 of 500 on LongMemEval-S

author.name: Christopher J. Chanhnourack

entry.summary: The author evaluates an auditable long-term memory system on LongMemEval-S combining hybrid retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, coverage-first packet compilation, and deterministic reasoning scaffolds, with an LLM used only as a replaceable final reader. Two passes with a Claude Opus reader score 479/500 and 475/500 under GPT-4o grading, straddling Chronos High's published 478/500. The paper honestly notes caveats including an unpinned CLI alias and a modified scoring prompt for knowledge-update rows whose effect under the official prompt is unmeasured.

entry.title: Detail in Context: A Dual-Scale Machine Learning Framework for Mycosis Fungoides Detection

author.name: Mohamed Hazem, Tarek Waleed, Omar Khaled, Nada Omar, Mahmoud Raslan, Marwa Mohamed Fawzy, Aya Fahim, Rania M. Mogawer, Ahmed Mourad, Kariman Mansour, Muhammad Rushdi

entry.summary: This paper presents a diagnostic framework for automated detection of mycosis fungoides, a rare cutaneous T-cell lymphoma often misdiagnosed early due to visual similarity to benign dermatoses. It combines a late-fusion ensemble of dual-magnification (10x and 20x) CNNs on histopathology images with a random forest classifier over 16 clinical features, evaluated on an expanded dataset of 6,267 images. The dual-scale plus clinical-feature fusion aims to distinguish MF from other lymphoproliferative skin conditions.

entry.title: Consensus-Aware Multi-Source Fusion for Reference-Guided Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Junyang Xia, Luocheng Zhang, Wenwen Pan, Chifeng Zhu, Yang Yang, Xinchun Liu, Jiajun Ding

entry.summary: Proposes a consensus-aware fusion framework for reference-guided camouflaged object detection where targets visually resemble their surroundings. It couples trainable PVTv2 queries with frozen DINOv3 features using reference-conditioned correlation, and aggregates multiple references through cross-reference consensus to handle inconsistent target cues.

entry.title: TSMD: Temporal-Stream Modality Dropout for Robust Video Highlight Detection

author.name: Bo-Yuan Cheng, Kuan-Yu Chen, Po-Han Huang, Jeng-Lin Li, Jian-Jiun Ding

entry.summary: Formulates robustness in multimodal video highlight detection along two missingness dimensions: temporal missingness of frames per modality and complete stream-level outages. Proposes Temporal-Stream Modality Dropout, combining structured missingness simulation with a joint objective including pointwise losses better aligned with the peak-driven nature of highlights than MSE.

entry.title: PCB-MC: Missing Component Analysis in Printed Circuit Boards

author.name: Betsy Villa Brochero, Ian Gibson, Estefania Talavera

entry.summary: PCB-MC is a curated dataset for detecting missing components on printed circuit boards, with footprint-level annotations across 197 board types built on the RF100 dataset, plus benchmarks of supervised and unsupervised methods with leakage-aware cross-validation splits. It highlights that supervised detectors produce high false negative rates in this unusual detection setting where absent objects must be localized.

entry.title: P-SRM: Selective Recovery of Rejected Predictions in Visual Tracking

author.name: Youbin He, Siwei Wang

entry.summary: P-SRM reassesses candidates rejected by tracking rejection mechanisms, combining spatial responses, past accepted states, and decision margins to selectively restore correctly localized predictions. Evaluations across six trackers and four datasets show consistent improvements in rejected-candidate ranking and overall tracking performance.

entry.title: An Island-Based Parallel Biased Random-Key Genetic Algorithm for the Three-Dimensional Trailer Loading Problem

author.name: A. del R\'io, L. D\'iaz, L. C. de Vicente, J. Cameselle, B. Fern\'andez

entry.summary: The authors propose an enhanced Biased Random-Key Genetic Algorithm combined with a novel island-based parallelization framework, PANGEA, to solve the NP-hard Three-Dimensional Trailer Loading Problem with heterogeneous items and complex logistical constraints. The multi-population evolutionary scheme targets large-scale industrial applications where exact optimization is impractical.

entry.title: Onboard Vision and MPC Navigation for Underwater Robots: An Open BlueROV2 Platform for Multi-Robot Experiments & Docking

author.name: Victor Nan Fernandez-Ayala, Wiktor Kowalczyk, Cezary Banaszek, Dimos V. Dimarogonas

entry.summary: The paper presents an open-source BlueROV2 platform with onboard Jetson Orin NX vision, underwater-calibrated stereo depth, and real-time object detection combined with quaternion-based estimation and nonlinear MPC for autonomous navigation and docking of underwater robots. It enables multi-robot underwater experiments with modular hardware.

entry.title: TO-mdiSPAs: Topology Optimization of multi-directional Soft Pneumatic Actuators

author.name: Swagatam Islam Sarkar, Prabhat Kumar

entry.summary: This work presents a topology optimization methodology for designing multi-directional soft pneumatic actuators that can bend in any 3D direction, using a three-field formulation for manufacturing robustness and Darcy's law with a drainage term to model design-dependent pneumatic behavior. It provides a systematic computational design tool for soft robotics. The contribution is primarily methodological within computational actuator design.

entry.title: Centralized Multi-UAV Exploration and 3D Reconstruction Using Single-UAV Planners

author.name: Jo\~ao F\'elix Mendes, Meysam Basiri, Rodrigo Ventura

entry.summary: The authors present a centralized multi-UAV exploration framework that reuses existing single-UAV sampling-based planners by maintaining a shared global TSDF map with real-time fusion of depth measurements from multiple UAVs, built on the voxblox library. This enables collaborative exploration of unknown environments while addressing consistent mapping and safe navigation.

entry.title: Accelerated Algorithm for Sparse Regularized Partial Optimal Transport

author.name: Khoa Nguyen, Dung T. Nguyen, Thong Huynh, Hoang-Hiep Nguyen-Mau, Anh Nguyen, Minh Ngoc Dinh, Juho Kannala

entry.summary: The paper proposes a penalty-based optimization framework for partial optimal transport with smooth strongly convex regularizers (quadratic, elastic net), inducing sparse transport plans with better computational efficiency than entropic approaches. It targets real-world applications where mass conservation does not hold strictly.

entry.title: GeoGAT: Bidirectional Temporal Sampling Meets Hierarchical Graph Attention for Global Video Geo-localization

author.name: Junchao Cui, Xuanzi Ma, Wenqi Shi, Hangyu Li, Biru Zhu, Chong Fu, Xiangyang Luo

entry.summary: GeoGAT tackles global video geo-localization by combining bidirectional temporal sampling (forward and offset-reversed frame sequences) with hierarchical graph attention networks to jointly predict location across city, state/province, country, and continent levels. The approach addresses shortcomings of prior methods that use one-way uniform frame sampling and independent per-hierarchy classifiers, which lose geographic cues and produce conflicting predictions, especially on multi-shot edited videos. This matters for applications like content moderation, forensics, and geospatial understanding from video.

entry.title: Prototype-guided Bilateral Alignment Multimodal Federated Learning

author.name: Tianchi Liao Tianchi_Liao, Lele Fu, Sheng Huang, Qing Hu, Hong-Ning Dai, Chuan Chen

entry.summary: MFedPBA is a multimodal federated learning framework that handles heterogeneous client architectures and imbalanced modality distributions via dual alignment: contrastive-learning-based feature-space projection and prototype-guided alignment. It aims to enable knowledge synergy under realistic, non-idealized federation conditions.

entry.title: GeoNest: Learning to Select Failure-Aware Neighborhoods for the Irregular Knapsack Problem in a Circular Container

author.name: Zhongman Du, Huiming Zhang, Linlin Yang, Sheng Xu, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: GeoNest is a failure-aware large neighborhood search framework for the 2D irregular knapsack problem in a circular container, driven by an RL-trained graph policy. It pairs failed target polygons with residual pockets and uses explanatory poses to identify blocking placed polygons, addressing the late-stage packing bottleneck in manufacturing material utilization.

entry.title: Structure vs. Chain-of-Thought: Evaluating LLM Criteria Extraction for Depression Severity

author.name: Xinkai Chen

entry.summary: This paper compares direct chain-of-thought severity rating against auditable criteria extraction followed by code-based labeling for depression assessment from social media, across two Reddit corpora, three LLM scales, and PHQ-9/BD-II questionnaires. Findings show criteria extraction only matches or beats chain-of-thought when thresholds are fitted on labeled data, with no significant gains. It offers a sobering comparison of auditability versus accuracy in clinical LLM use.

entry.title: NarrativeSteward: Coordinating Delegation, Guidance, and Verification in Agent-Assisted Interactive Narrative Authoring

author.name: Wenjin Wang, Jiazhen Lei, Yuxin Sha, Nuwa Xi, Meng Zhao, Xingxi Yin, Qi Liu, Yuliang Shen, Zixun Sun

entry.summary: NarrativeSteward is an authoring environment where AI agents organize and revise interactive narratives, with outlines, worldbuilding, and narrative graphs maintained as linked artifacts that help authors understand and guide evolving content. Agent dialogue, structural review, change records, and execution verification support local and cross-layer revision control.

entry.title: MeanVoiceFlow2: Joint Optimization of Mean Flow and Content Encoder for Fast One-Step Zero-Shot Voice Conversion

author.name: Takuhiro Kaneko, Hirokazu Kameoka, Kou Tanaka, Yuto Kondo

entry.summary: MeanVoiceFlow2 jointly optimizes a flow-based one-step voice conversion module and a computationally efficient content encoder, trained via conversion distillation from MeanVoiceFlow plus real-data reconstruction. Diffusion-GAN training with sample mixing and teacher-guided conditioning augmentation improves realism and diversity while removing the heavy content-encoder bottleneck.

entry.title: FlashDiffusion: Fused Tiled Kernel Spectral Decomposition

author.name: Julio Candanedo

entry.summary: FlashDiffusion is a matrix-free method for kernel spectral decompositions (including diffusion maps) that evaluates dense Gaussian kernel blocks in fused GPU tiles, avoiding O(N^2) memory. It couples the eigensolver to an empirical beta-flow for resolution-scale selection and uses continuation over sample size and bandwidth to warm-start expensive solves. A systems/numerical contribution to geometric learning.

entry.title: Synchronous Multi-view Neural Diffusion

author.name: Yongquan Shi, Weijun Huang, Yueyang Pi, Wendi Zhao, Yiqing Shi, Shiping Wang

entry.summary: SynMDiff proposes synchronous intra- and inter-view fusion for multi-view learning using neural diffusion, addressing the limitation that existing strategies treat within-view and across-view fusion as independent stages with conflicting structural inductive biases. By jointly evolving views and their dependencies, the method avoids information distortion and compression along intermediate fusion pathways. This yields richer multi-view representations within a broader solution space.

entry.title: QuanVI: Score-based Variational Inference via Quantum Maximally Mixed States

author.name: Yuchen Cong, Zerui Tao, Chao Li, Zhe Sun, Qibin Zhao

entry.summary: QuanVI is a quantum-inspired algorithm for score-based variational inference that replaces eigenvalue formulations with a mixed-state density-operator view and quantum tensor network parameterization. It overcomes exponential parameter scaling and eigenvector non-uniqueness that plague prior score-VI approaches based on Fisher divergence.

entry.title: Dynamics to decision: A mathematical theory of Lyapunov spectra and decision boundaries in deep classifiers

author.name: Shirin Panahi, Amirhossein Nazerian, Ali Pezeshki

entry.summary: The paper models feed-forward classifiers as finite nonautonomous discrete dynamical systems and analyzes the Finite-Time Maximum Lyapunov Exponent of data trajectories through depth. This traces how decision boundaries acquire their dynamical signature across layers, connecting decision geometry to contraction/divergence of nearby trajectories.

entry.title: Finite-Horizon Fisher Memory in Two-Sided Power-Bounded Recurrent Systems

author.name: Jeonghoon Lee (Attractor Dynamics Inc.)

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes allocation, admission, and retention in finite-horizon linear-Gaussian noisy recurrent memories, showing the trace of directional Fisher memory is horizon-invariant while non-normality redistributes information. It derives uniform 1/n lag bounds for bi-power-bounded carriers, identifies limit operators, and characterizes store-optimality versus write-optimality directions.

entry.title: DashVMC: Real-Time Discrete World Model Control in Geometry Dash

author.name: Florent Tariolle, Florian Yger

entry.summary: DashVMC learns a compact action-conditioned world model from about two hours of Geometry Dash gameplay and trains a controller via behavioral cloning plus PPO entirely in frozen-model rollouts, satisfying real-time frame constraints. Refined policies outperform BC initializations on official levels and a held-out community layout.

entry.title: CraftSPH: A high-accuracy and composable differentiable SPH solver implemented in PyTorch

author.name: Gen Matono, Shujiro Fujioka, Mayuko Nishio

entry.summary: CraftSPH is a high-accuracy, composable differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics solver implemented in PyTorch, with major operations as independent modules that can be combined flexibly, including advanced and implicit schemes. It supports continuous extension and updating of solver configurations. This fills a gap in unified differentiable SPH tooling for simulation and ML integration.

entry.title: Generalized Geometry Block Proximal Linearized Method for Multiblock Nonconvex and Nonsmooth Optimization

author.name: Weifeng Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a generalized geometry proximal linearized operator and the GGBPL method for multiblock nonconvex nonsmooth optimization, replacing standard Euclidean inner products with problem-adapted geometry for block updates. Convergence analysis and experiments indicate improved numerical efficiency over Euclidean-geometry proximal methods.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Graph Transformations for SpTRSV Optimization

author.name: Buse Y{\i}lmaz

entry.summary: This paper formulates graph transformation of sparse triangular solve dependency graphs as a reinforcement learning problem, replacing manually designed heuristics with learned transformation policies. SpTRSV is a fundamental kernel in scientific computing where data dependencies limit parallelism. RL guidance enables adaptation to different optimization objectives without hand-crafting new heuristics.

entry.title: Calibrated to Whom? Persona and Language Effects on Cultural Values in JEV

author.name: Bushra Asseri, Abdulaziz Asseri

entry.summary: This audit tests a decision-only language model, TypeSafe's JEV, on cultural values using the Values Survey Module 2013 across Saudi and American personas in English and Arabic, collecting 288,000 answers. Without personas the model resembled its own American personas, and Saudi personas reproduced 87 percent of the human Saudi-US difference in English but only 62 percent in Arabic. This quantifies calibration limits of LLMs as cross-cultural survey respondents and judges.

entry.title: Reader Proficiency Shapes Layer-wise Surprisal Profiles

author.name: Akio Hayakawa, Horacio Saggion

entry.summary: Using eye-tracking data from the MECO L2 corpus, the study shows that the layer-wise relationship between LLM surprisal and human gaze differs by reader proficiency: lower-vocabulary-proficiency readers show deeper Predictive Depth for first-pass gaze duration across 12 tested LLMs. This suggests cognitive fit of LLM representations varies with reader characteristics.

entry.title: GeoOutageBench: Benchmarking Ambiguity-aware, Ontology-grounded Geospatiotemporal KGQA for Multimodal Power Outage and Resilience Analysis

author.name: Ethan D. Frakes, Amy Kvien, Rishabh Kundu, Redad Mehdi, Van D. Tran, Vibha S. Mandayam, Kristopher O. Davis, Erika I. Barcelos, Roger H. French, Yinghui Wu, Mengjie Li

entry.summary: GeoOutageBench is a benchmark for LLM-based knowledge graph question answering over a spatiotemporal KG integrating visual, textual, and structured data from power outage records, remote sensing, weather, and domain ontologies. It provides a competency query taxonomy spanning containment, proximity, co-occurrence, multimodal evidence, and hypothetical evaluation, with configurable evaluation across difficulty levels. It targets a real applied domain (grid resilience) where existing web-KGQA benchmarks do not apply.

entry.title: When Integral Meets Decomposition: A Signal-Level Self-Supervised Feature Decompose Paradigm for Multi-Modal Image Fusion

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Jiayu Wang, Haiyu Song, Haoran Duan

entry.summary: Reformulates feature decomposition for multi-modal image fusion as a 1D signal-level self-supervised problem, separating source images into common and modality-specific features without requiring ground-truth decomposition maps. This avoids the incomplete and conflicting image-level metric losses used by prior decomposition-based fusion methods.

entry.title: A Generalizable and Explainable Framework for Synthetic Video Detection Using First-Digit Gradient Statistics

author.name: Sidharth Shanu, Gautam Kumar, Tej Singh

entry.summary: This work proposes AI-generated video detection using Sobel gradient statistics analyzed via the first-digit law (Benford-type analysis), with linear discriminant analysis for visualization and an MLP for classification. The method is generator- and scene-agnostic, offering explainability that CNN-based black-box detectors lack.

entry.title: Evolutionary foraging in grids: Intermittent search dynamics emerge in finite, depletable landscapes

author.name: Shailendra Bhandari, Alex Szorkovszky, Anis Yazidi, Pedro G. Lind

entry.summary: Using evolutionary simulations with heritable movement genomes on finite, depletable 2D landscapes (uniform or Levy-dust resources), the authors test whether evolved search trajectories follow intermittent-search or Levy-walk dynamics. Results indicate evolved search is better described by intermittent-search dynamics without imposing a prescribed step-length distribution.

entry.title: Observability Analysis and Online Calibration of Visual-Inertial-Wheel Odometry for 4WIS4WID Mobile Robots

author.name: Branimir \'Caran, Vladimir Mili\'c, Bojan \v{S}ekoranja, Bojan Jerbi\'c

entry.summary: This work presents a visual-inertial-wheel odometry framework with online calibration for four-wheel independently steered and driven robots, deriving a 2D odometry model from all wheels with rolling and no-slip constraints plus preintegration and analytical Jacobians. The observability analysis shows a drive-only model leaves steering offsets unobservable, while the redundant model restores observability and identifies additional unobservable directions.

entry.title: Non-Invasive Inspection of Water Canals Using Dronar

author.name: Michael Zielinski, Zhizhan Wang, Benjamin Dymond, Reza Razavian, Zhongwang Dou

entry.summary: The paper describes a deployable, non-invasive drone-based inspection system (Dronar) for concrete water canals in the Phoenix metro area that can inspect canal beds without draining water. It detects lining deformation, cracking, and sediment buildup that are otherwise only assessed during four-year dry-up cycles, enabling maintenance prioritization.

entry.title: A ‘Morally Binding’ White House Accord on AI Safety

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's commentary on a White House accord involving leading AI companies, assessing it as nonzero substantive progress on AI safety despite the performative framing, and flagging an expected renewed push for a state-level AI moratorium during the lame duck session. The post covers embedded evaluators, FTC activity, and the shifting regulatory landscape in characteristic analytic-newsletter style.

entry.title: Reasoning Externalization for Faithful Large Language Model Narratives of Stock Return Predictions

author.name: Sujung Kim, Seung Hwan Cho, Sangjin Park, Young-Min Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose an LLM narrative framework that translates XGBoost stock return predictions into natural language using temporal SHAP evidence and historical regime analogs. The goal is to make explainable AI outputs comprehensible to non-experts while reducing LLM errors in inferring numerical changes and feature relations.

entry.title: Completion-Aware Cross-Fidelity Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Line Bus Holding

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Qifan Zhang, Liang Zheng

entry.summary: The paper studies cross-fidelity offline-to-online RL for multi-line bus holding, where a cheap online simulator differs from the target system in transition and event-duration dynamics. It addresses a specific failure mode in which an inexpensive simulator reduces passenger time while producing incomplete passenger journeys, combining fixed target replay with simulator interaction.

entry.title: A 3GPP-Compliant Benchmark Dataset for RIS-Aided Beyond 5G Networks

author.name: Pujitha Mamillapalli, Pankaj Singh Rathour, Abhinav Kumar

entry.summary: The authors release a large-scale, 3GPP TR 38.901-compliant dataset for reconfigurable intelligent surface-aided millimeter-wave networks, spanning canonical deployment scenarios across 20 variants with diverse user densities, fading, and blockage regimes, including oracle RIS phase configurations. It fills a genuine resource gap for data-driven RIS research. Open standardized datasets often catalyze progress in applied wireless ML.

entry.title: Overview of BioASQ 2026: The fourteenth BioASQ Challenge on Large-Scale Biomedical Semantic Indexing and Question Answering

author.name: Anastasios Nentidis, Georgios Katsimpras, Anastasia Krithara, Martin Krallinger, Miguel Rodr\'iguez-Ortega, Eduard Rodriguez-L\'opez, Natalia Loukachevitch, Igor Rozhkov, Elena Tutubalina, Dimitris Dimitriadis, Vasiliki Patsiou, Grigorios Tsoumakas, George Giannakoulas, Alexandra Bekiaridou, Athanasios Samaras, Giorgio Maria Di Nunzio, Nicola Ferro, Stefano Marchesin, Marco Martinelli, Gianmaria Silvello, Georgios Paliouras

entry.summary: This is the overview paper for the fourteenth BioASQ challenge at CLEF 2026, covering six shared tasks including biomedical QA, multilingual clinical summarization, nested named entity relation extraction, and clinical coding. It summarizes the tasks, datasets, and participating systems, serving as a community resource for biomedical NLP evaluation.

entry.title: CAS II: Symmetric Partitions as Kolmogorov Models

author.name: Romie Banerjee

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops algorithmic statistics over symmetric partitions, connecting Vereshchagin's strong models to orbit partitions of group actions on strings. It establishes a Galois connection between subgroups and partitions yielding lattices of hypotheses with canonical certificates and costs, extending Kolmogorov's structure function. Single-author pure theory paper.

entry.title: Role-guided Speaker Deletion Verification in Clinical Psychiatry Speech Recordings with Audio Language Models

author.name: Joseph T Colonel, Daniel Katzman, Kelsey Kirker, Adam N Davidson, Shalaila S Haas, Cheryl Corcoran, Ren\'{e} S Kahn, Guillermo Checci, Baihan Lin

entry.summary: This paper addresses verifying that a designated speaker (clinician or patient) has been removed from multi-speaker psychiatric recordings, a compliance requirement at corpus scale where manual review is infeasible. It builds two symmetric pipelines that redact raw audio for a target role and then use audio language models to verify deletion completeness.

entry.title: How Accurate Is Accurate Enough?

author.name: Ningkang Peng, Qianfeng Yu, Jingyang Mao, Xiaoqian Peng, Yanhui Gu

entry.summary: This paper asks how accurate numerical approximations inside a learning system must be, arguing that primitive error magnitude alone is insufficient because the learning objective weights classwise errors nonuniformly depending on training state. For softmax cross-entropy, the authors characterize the coupling between class weights and numerical errors and derive exact extrema of signed loss change over pairings of fixed non-target probability and score errors.

entry.title: Generalized Residual Closure: General Learning Dynamics for Stability-Plasticity Compatibility

author.name: Dongxu Li, Yinuo Zhang, Hongyu Zhang, Feng Tian

entry.summary: The paper introduces Generalized Residual Closure, a framework modeling learning as recursive closure of future-relevant discrepancies, with two primitive modes: transformation within a representation and revision of the representation itself. It establishes a local tangent decomposition, a criterion for when representation revision is necessary, and derives necessary-and-sufficient conditions in an affine model. The aim is a general theory of stability-plasticity compatibility in persistent learning.

entry.title: Importance-Aware Feature Sparsification for Wireless Split Learning

author.name: Bumjun Kim, Yoon Huh, Wan Choi

entry.summary: ICS reduces the communication bottleneck in wireless split learning by having the server rank feature channels using Grad-CAM-based class scores computed during backpropagation, avoiding client-side overhead of task-agnostic criteria. This improves accuracy under non-i.i.d. client data while cutting transmission cost.

entry.title: Hybrid Methods for Robust Tabular Data Imputation

author.name: Jinwei Li, Michelle Bruch, Daniel Tenbrinck

entry.summary: The paper proposes NuclearForest and SoftForest, hybrid imputation methods combining low-rank initialization via Singular Value Thresholding or SoftImpute with non-iterative Random Forest refinement. The authors also prove adaptive step-size bounds and convergence for the SVT-based component.

entry.title: LARC: Low-Rank Adaptive Residual Connections for Learning in Frozen Models

author.name: Junyi Zou, Avrova Donz

entry.summary: LARC adds a low-rank learnable residual correction to frozen model representations with a slow cross-task state and a private fast state that adapts from feedback and resets. A rank-4 implementation with about 12K trainable parameters on a frozen MiniCPM substrate reduces error with two feedback-gradient steps in a selection task.

entry.title: About the Influence of Workflow Topology on Task Intensity Prediction through Graph Learning

author.name: Max Otto, Haci Ismail Aslan, Joel Witzke, Jonathan Bader, Odej Kao

entry.summary: This paper investigates how directed-acyclic-graph topology of large-scale cloud workflows affects prediction of task-level resource intensity, using graph learning methods. Accurate intensity prediction helps balance under-provisioning bottlenecks against over-provisioning costs. The work quantifies which topological signals improve prediction beyond standard task-level features.

entry.title: Component-Weighted Centroid Search for Exact Incremental BPE

author.name: Harshit Verma, Rex Ying

entry.summary: This algorithms paper improves exact incremental Byte Pair Encoding tokenization, reducing the per-append cost from O(log^2 t) to O(log t) using a component-weighted centroid search whose charges telescope over a stream. The improvement preserves BPE semantics and asymptotic space within a prior 2026 algorithmic framework. Relevant to efficient streaming tokenization for language models.

entry.title: Hyperspherical Semantic Trajectory Analysis: Mapping Technological Diffusion across Academic Preprints, Patent Signals, and Compute Scaling

author.name: Muhammad Sukri Bin Ramli

entry.summary: HSTA is an unsupervised methodology that tracks technology diffusion from 30,000 arXiv and USPTO records by projecting transformer sentence embeddings onto unit hyperspheres with Spherical K-Means and UMAP, aiming to detect breakthroughs faster than lagged productivity metrics like TFP. It links semantic trajectories to compute scaling signals.

entry.title: Bridging Semantic Gaps in RAG through Generated Context Knowledge Fusion

author.name: Xinkai Du, Chao Lv, Yalin Sun, Quanjie Han, Lei Yao, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: KASB improves retrieval-augmented generation by addressing semantic space mismatch between queries and retrieved passages, fusing generative and retrieval-based knowledge in a multistage process to enhance passage selection. It aims to improve both relevance and accuracy of the RAG pipeline.

entry.title: Which papyrus HTR is good enough? Character-error-rate tolerance of four papyrological tasks on Greek texts

author.name: Anton Repushko, Elena Chepel

entry.summary: Determines how accurate Greek papyrus handwritten text recognition must be for four downstream papyrological tasks, by algorithmically degrading editorial-layer-free ground truth from 63,846 published editions at various character error rates. This sets the first accuracy benchmarks for a domain where most texts remain unpublished and undigitized.

entry.title: Multimodal Detection of Higher-Order Behavioral Constructs: Self-Compassion in Structured Reflective Interaction

author.name: Siddhant Jain, Dimitra Tsovaltzi

entry.summary: This paper tackles computational modeling of latent psychological constructs, using self-compassion during structured reflective interviews as a case study in multimodal (speech, text, behavior over time) detection. It addresses the labeling difficulty of such constructs and their inference from temporally extended human behavior in technology-mediated training settings. The work sits at the intersection of affective computing and educational technology.

entry.title: Evaluating Multi-Task Morphological Concept Learning for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy Assessment in 3D CT

author.name: Namitha Narayanan

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether jointly learning radiologist-annotated morphological features (e.g., spiculation, lobulation) with malignancy risk from lesion-centered 3D CT volumes improves nodule malignancy classification, using LIDC-IDRI with patient-level splits and 628 reader annotations in the held-out test set. It compares multi-task concept learning against single-task baselines. This is an applied medical-imaging contribution on interpretable risk assessment.

entry.title: Perceptual Color Difference Modeling Using Machine Learning and Human Similarity Judgments

author.name: Elnara Kadyrgali, Muragul Muratbekova, Adilet Yerkin, Nuray Toganas, Ayan Igali, Malika Ziyada, Aruzhan Burambekova, Jamaladdin Hasanov, Pakizar Shamoi

entry.summary: The authors collect human similarity judgments for 2,000 systematically generated color pairs rated by seven observers on a four-point scale, then train regression models over RGB, HSI, and fuzzy linguistic color representations to predict perceived color difference. The goal is a data-driven alternative to standards like CIEDE2000 that better matches human perceptual judgments.

entry.title: DensePed-Lite: Quality-Aware Adaptive Detection for Dense Pedestrians under Occlusion

author.name: ZiAn Wang, MingZhe Liu, Chaoyi Guo, ChangChun Li, Fangming Gu

entry.summary: DensePed-Lite is a unified lightweight pedestrian detection framework for dense, heavily occluded scenes that adapts network behavior to observed feature quality rather than assuming complete information. It improves the balance of accuracy and efficiency while enforcing consistency between classification and localization quality.

entry.title: Determining Vertical Displacement of Agricultural Areas Using UAV-Photogrammetry and a Heteroscedastic Deep Learning Model

author.name: Wojciech Gruszczy\'nski, Edyta Puniach, Pawe{\l} \'Cwi\k{a}ka{\l}a, Wojciech Matwij

entry.summary: The paper applies a U-Net with heteroscedastic regression to estimate vertical ground surface displacement from UAV photogrammetry point clouds, replacing conventional ground filtering. The model predicts elevation corrections while also quantifying per-prediction uncertainty via variance estimation, reducing vegetation interference.

entry.title: Tissue Detection Determines False Positives in Diffusion-Based Histopathology Artifact Detection

author.name: Konstantinos Moutselos, Ilias Maglogiannis

entry.summary: This study shows that the usually-treated-as-neutral tissue-detection preprocessing step significantly affects false positives in one-class diffusion-based artifact detectors for whole-slide images. On 16 annotated TCGA slides, saturation-Otsu detection excluded normal tissue like adipose and alveolar parenchyma and retained marker ink, while entropy-based detection reduced false-positive rates in cross-validation. The finding elevates a routine preprocessing choice to a determinant of detector quality.

entry.title: A Two-Echelon Covering Tour Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones for Post-Disaster Relief

author.name: Dang Viet Anh Nguyen, Rajesh Piplani, Aldy Gunawan

entry.summary: The authors introduce a two-echelon covering tour vehicle routing problem for post-disaster relief, where trucks carry supplies and drones to satellites at the edge of affected areas and parallel-launched drones deliver to clustered victim locations. The formulation jointly handles satellite assignment, truck routing, and cluster assignment to minimize truck arrival times and drone delivery makespan.

entry.title: PTED: A multi-dimensional two-sample test for scientific inference and generative machine learning

author.name: Connor Stone

entry.summary: PTED is a Python implementation of an energy-distance-based permutation two-sample test that works in high dimensions and on learned feature representations, providing an exact test via permutation on energy distances. It targets the common practice of falling back on heuristics and visual inspection when comparing distributions in inference and generative modeling.

entry.title: Tristan Buckmaster Numberphile Interview Transcript

author.name: anaguma

entry.summary: A transcript of Tristan Buckmaster's Numberphile interview about the Navier-Stokes developments and his research, lightly edited with Claude Sonnet 5.5, accompanied by the poster's commentary criticizing AI labs for racing to scoop academic results and questioning whether codex-session access contributed to a proof. The interview itself covers the human and mathematical context of the drama.

entry.title: Can an AI Agent Rediscover a Blaschke-Curve Invariant?

author.name: Yunus E. Zeytuncu

entry.summary: This paper uses generalized Blaschke curves as a controlled environment for AI-assisted mathematical rediscovery, withholding the target theorem from an agent that receives numerical line-coordinate data. The agent's saved log shows rejected hypotheses and a fitted homogeneous cubic that predicts 480 lines from 80 unseen parameter values with a tiny recorded residual, though the authors carefully note the consistency checks fall short of a fully held-out test.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Complex (valued) Memories

author.name: Sathya Kamesh Bhethanabhotla, Efstratios Gavves, Andr\'e Biedenkapp

entry.summary: This work revisits unitary recurrent networks for partially observable deep RL, leveraging norm-preserving complex-valued dynamics for superior gradient flow and associative recall of long-term dependencies. It explores uRNN-based memory representations as an alternative to gated recurrence, attention, and model-based memory in RL agents.

entry.title: SCORE-LM: State-Space Radar Representations with Language Models for Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Mainak Mallick, Seung-Kyum Choi

entry.summary: SCORE-LM couples a compact scatterer-conditioned operator-response encoder with an adapted small local language model for radar hardware fault diagnosis, using self-referenced complex trajectories, physical descriptors, and a selective state-space branch trained with source-only self-supervision. On eight capture-excluded Rad-R fault recordings it achieves state-of-the-art results in a nine-model comparison, with roughly 120x fewer inference coefficients than a competing radar network. The system also produces maintenance guidance text.

entry.title: Spatial-Temporal Multi-scale Network for Screen Content Video Quality Enhancement

author.name: Ziyin Huang, Sik-Ho Tsang, Xinyuan Qin, Yui-Lam Chan, Xueling Zhou, Feiyu Chen

entry.summary: STM-Net enhances compressed screen content videos with a prior-guided spatio-temporal dispatcher routing inputs into parallel streams and bidirectional temporal feature extraction, tailored to abrupt motion and text/graphics-heavy content. It targets a domain where natural-video enhancement methods degrade due to broken temporal continuity.

entry.title: Robust LassoNet: Enhancing Feature Selection in Neural Networks via Robust Loss Functions

author.name: Daniela De Canditiis, Italia De Feis, Paola Stolfi

entry.summary: Robust LassoNet extends LassoNet by replacing the MSE loss with robust alternatives (Huber, Cauchy, Tukey's bisquare, Nonnegative Garrote) to make hierarchical-sparsity-based feature selection in neural networks resilient to outliers. The extension preserves the original optimization framework while improving stability under contamination. It targets the joint prediction and variable selection problem with noisy data.

entry.title: TTLab at Daleel 2026: STAR-Ar, Sequence Tagging for Argument Recognition in Arabic

author.name: Bhuvanesh Verma, Ali Abusaleh, Alexander Mehler

entry.summary: STAR-Ar is a BERT-BiLSTM-CRF system for Arabic argument mining, jointly performing argument discourse unit detection and classification as token-level sequence labeling for the Daleel 2026 shared task. It achieves F1 scores of 72.69 on validation and 73.7 on test data.

entry.title: BatSLAM 2.0: Sequence-Verified Sonar Place Recognition in a Robust Pose Graph

author.name: Jan Steckel

entry.summary: BatSLAM 2.0 is a sonar-only SLAM system combining an updated biomimetic binaural acoustic front-end, a sequence verifier for loop-closure candidates, and a pose graph on a high-performance factor graph framework. It addresses the inherent ambiguity of sonar place recognition (e.g., near-identical corridor echoes) and is evaluated in simulation and real environments.

entry.title: Disagreement-Regularized Imitation Learning for Image-Based Continuous Control with Gaussian and Beta Policies

author.name: Irving Giovani Bronzatti Petrazzini, Eric Aislan Antonelo

entry.summary: This controlled study evaluates whether DRIL, which converts disagreement among behavior-cloned policies into an RL reward, improves image-based continuous control in CarRacing. It systematically varies policy distributions (Gaussian vs Beta), expert types, and demonstration counts, comparing behavior cloning, best training checkpoint, and final DRIL checkpoints under deterministic and stochastic evaluation.

entry.title: Client and Training Data Selection for Computationally Efficient Synchronized Federated Learning

author.name: Muzaffer Citir, Hiroki Nishikawa, Sangyoung Park

entry.summary: The paper studies joint client and data selection to mitigate straggler delays and non-i.i.d. degradation in federated learning, particularly when client counts are small where probabilistic selection fails. It aims to improve global model convergence while maintaining participation rates.

entry.title: Cybersecurity in Edge Computing: A Trust-Aware Federated Hybrid Intrusion Detection Framework

author.name: Zawad Yalmie Sazid, Robert Abbas

entry.summary: The paper proposes TA-FHIDF, a trust-aware federated framework combining an autoencoder, 1D-CNN, and other components for intrusion detection on resource-constrained edge and IoT devices without centralizing data. It targets the enlarged attack surface created by edge computing while respecting privacy regulations. It is an applied security architecture combining established components.

entry.title: Robust and Learned Online Matching in Growing Trees

author.name: Marek Ga{\l}\k{a}zka, Hanna Wdowicka

entry.summary: This theory paper studies irrevocable maximum-cardinality matching in trees revealed by successive leaf attachments, with a misspecified or unknown growth law. The authors prove that a threshold policy loses at most twice the cumulative expected conditional total-variation error relative to an online oracle, via a unit-span property of the Bellman continuation score, and provide matching lower bounds. This is a competitive-analysis result under model misspecification.

entry.title: CredWise: A Controlled Agentic Decision-Intelligence Framework for Explainable and Auditable Credit-Risk Assessment

author.name: Aakash Kumar Tiwari

entry.summary: CredWise integrates XGBoost credit-risk prediction, probability calibration, explainability, policy retrieval, SQL analytics, and controlled agent workflows into an auditable decision-support framework, evaluated on Lending Club data with a temporal split. The calibrated model achieves ROC-AUC of 0.7109 with improved Brier score on the 2018 test set.

entry.title: Port-Hamiltonian Latent Deliberation: Mitigating the Deliberation Drift Cliff in Test-Time Compute Scaling

author.name: Zeyu Jia (School of Biomedical Engineering, Technology, Tianjin Medical University, Medical School, Tianjin University)

entry.summary: The paper identifies a Deliberation Drift Cliff in latent-space iterative reasoning, where recurrent latent models collapse when extrapolated to deeper deliberation steps, and proposes a port-Hamiltonian formulation with Lyapunov stability to resolve a trilemma among expressivity, stability, and efficiency. It reports large drops (22-62%) for unconstrained baselines at 16+ steps and claims stability for the constrained gradient-flow approach. The work applies control-theoretic structure to test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: Can We Anticipate Violence? Multimodal Learning from Pre-Incident Behavioral Cues

author.name: Sindhuja Penchala, Mohammed Yusuf Mujawar, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: The study frames short-horizon pre-incident violence risk recognition using facial appearance, aligned audio, and body-motion features from XD-Violence clips, with the incident excluded from inputs. It uses 443 samples with source-level train/test separation to probe whether behavioral cues allow anticipation rather than detection.

entry.title: Behavioral Persistence and Incomplete Functional Transfer of Co-evolved Communication in Evolutionary Robotics

author.name: Fernando Montes-Gonzalez (Universidad Veracruzana, Mexico)

entry.summary: This study evaluates direct transfer of a co-evolved communication protocol from 2D simulation to physical 3D e-puck-type robots with GRU-controlled agents performing a food-seeking task with signaling. Even after three calibration corrections, transfer was partial and asymmetric, with one agent reaching the food in only one of thirty tested seeds.

entry.title: Characterizing Questioning Patterns and Student Engagement Through Contextual Analysis of Real-Time Classroom Interactions

author.name: Rohit Sharma, Pavani Ayinampudi, Aditya B. M. V., Jinal Gupta, Prakash Hegade, Sakshi Sharma, Meenakshi V, SRS Iyengar

entry.summary: This study analyzes real-time classroom polling data read against lecture transcripts to determine a poll's instructional function (recall, comprehension, attention direction) and its relationship to student engagement, classifying questions by Bloom's taxonomy levels. It shows polling data carries richer signal than simple correctness scores.

entry.title: Context Language Models

author.name: Rulin Shao, Shannon Zejiang Shen, Junjie Oscar Yin, Yuetai Li, Minheng Wang, Hamish Ivison, Radha Poovendran, Nathan Lambert, Teng Xiao, Mike Lewis, Wen-tau Yih, Luke Zettlemoyer, Pang Wei Koh

entry.summary: Same paper — already featured in yesterday's Research roundup, Context Language Models (CLMs) natively manage their own context by treating it as a file the model can freely edit, learning what to keep in context and extending naturally to multi-agent settings with multiple context files. Built zero-shot with existing models, CLMs beat SOTA context management strategies: 11.4% higher accuracy with 21.5% fewer FLOPs on BrowseComp-Plus and large gains on long-horizon agent tasks. The author list includes prominent researchers (Zettlemoyer, Yih, Lewis, Koh, Lambert), indicating serious work.

entry.title: MASCRDM: Multi-Agent System for Compliance Risk Detection and Mitigation in Training Process of Large Language Models

author.name: Yan Zhang, Chuming Wei, Ruien Li, Yaoyao Peng, Wusheng Zhang, Guangwen Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes MASCRDM, a multi-agent system for detecting and mitigating compliance risks such as discrimination and bias during LLM training in real time, rather than filtering inputs and outputs of trained models statically. It critiques existing approaches as localized, static optimizations lacking real-time risk monitoring.

entry.title: Cycle-Aware Autoencoder with Cross-SignalConsistency for Railway Door Anomaly Detection

author.name: Ammar Bouketta, Smail Niar, Hamza Ouarnoughi, Eva Mutuzo Brindle

entry.summary: This work frames railway door condition monitoring as cycle-level unsupervised anomaly detection, treating each open-dwell-close cycle as one monitoring unit. The proposed TCAA-CS autoencoder combines dual-stream 1D-CNN branches for physical signals and logical door states with LSTM encoding, trained only on nominal cycles. It is a domain-specific applied contribution for safety-critical rail maintenance.

entry.title: Methodological Changes to the Attention ResUNet Hourly Precipitation Postprocessor

author.name: Thomas M. Hamill

entry.summary: A technical note documenting updates to a previously published Attention Residual U-Net that postprocesses GRAF deterministic forecasts into probabilistic hourly precipitation forecasts. Changes include FiLM conditioning on season and lead time collapsing 192 per-checkpoint models into one, lead-time extension from 48 to 72 hours, and new solar-hour and climatological input channels.

entry.title: Comparative study of adapting pre-trained models for driving behavior video captioning

author.name: Sayak Mallick, Philipp Geiger, Augustin Kelava

entry.summary: This report compares fine-tuning and prompting methods, including full fine-tuning, LoRA, and prompt engineering, for adapting LLMs to driving video captioning on the BDD-X dataset. Experiments use SpaceTimeGPT and VideoLLaVA, with full fine-tuning performing well on automatic metrics and sometimes surpassing baselines. It is a comparative empirical study rather than a new method.

entry.title: From Lexical Baselines to Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Structured Skill and Responsibility-Level Extraction with the SFIA Framework

author.name: Ranuga Disansa, U. S. Samarasinghe, Lasith Gunawardena

entry.summary: The paper formalizes structured extraction of (skill, responsibility-level) pairs under the SFIA framework (147 skills, seven levels) from free text, comparing five strategies from lexical baselines through agentic retrieval-augmented generation. No prior automated LLM-based SFIA extraction existed, and the task supports workforce planning. It evaluates which strategies reliably predict level alongside skill.

entry.title: A Character-Level Neural Approach to Sinhala Sandhi Splitting

author.name: Yasas Ekanayaka, Deshan Sumanathilaka

entry.summary: The authors establish the first neural benchmark for Sinhala Sandhi splitting, recovering word boundaries hidden inside phonologically merged forms. Using character-level sequence-to-sequence models on the SandhiLex dataset, their best bidirectional LSTM encoder-decoder reaches only about 68 percent exact-match on the hardest lexicalized and etymological subset. The work highlights an underserved low-resource language NLP task.

entry.title: BITEM at the NTCIR-19 R2C2 Task: Predicting Confidence from Agentic RAG Pipeline Signals

author.name: Julien Knafou, Luc Mottin, Alexandre Flament, Paul van Rijen, Esteban Gaillac, Patrick Ruch

entry.summary: This paper describes the BITEM team's system for both subtasks of the NTCIR-19 R2C2 evaluation, built around a single agentic retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. A searching-and-reading agent gathers evidence over a movie corpus under an orchestrator that admits claims only after an entailment cascade verifies them against their cited passages, and answers are released only when sufficient verified evidence exists.
